gaps.title: Glide command FIFO left enabled after a not-idle Glide/OpenGL close: every D3D triangle silently vanishes (clears still work); a D3D surface in the stale FIFO window escalates to a 2D give-up and loss of the HAL
gaps.description:
Measured on .124 today (onbox-01, hal-01, runtime-25). An OpenGL/Glide 4-chip SLI session (pid 1892, about 2 h earlier) closed on h5 Glide's not-idle path. hwcRestoreVideo therefore skipped its register restore, including cmdFifo0.baseSize = 0, and SLI went off through the kernel's display reset. cmdFifo0 stayed enabled: baseSize 0x1fe, window 0x18000-0x117000, readPtr 0x2f624 stuck.

What broke: D3D devices still created and cleared, but drew no triangle. d3dprobe scored 9/40 fullscreen at 1024x768x32 and 7/42 windowed, while the ring logged 36 triangles sent. history-01 recorded the same 32 bpp no-triangle failure before the FIFO was identified.

How it escalated: a windowed texture at 0xc0000, inside that window, made the chip read 0xa1f (CMD0 busy). The desktop PDEV's 2D engine then gave up, and the D3D HAL was not offered at all (GetDeviceCaps/CreateDevice 8876086a) until a paced mode switch triggered the miniport's busy-at-mode-set engine reset. That reset stops the FIFO fetch; with nothing else changed the same probes passed 40/40, 42/42 and 40/40.

Why nothing caught it (verified in code):
- the miniport resets only a BUSY chip at a mode set (vcrmp_hw.c voodoo_program);
- an enabled-but-idle FIFO passes the 2D idle test;
- Diag\Reset3D is default off and never ran on silicon (history-26). It refuses whenever SST_CMDFIFOEN is set and never runs at DrvAssertMode.
A D3D surface inside an enabled FIFO window is a credible freeze mechanism (inferred).

Fix (hal Phase 1, Diag\D3DSafe bit 0, default off):
- stop cmdFifo0/1 at the display reset that ends a not-idle Glide close (VcrSliOff 'display reset') and at every mode set with no exclusive owner;
- check cmdFifo0 at ContextCreate and DP2, and refuse plus request a reset when it is on;
- never place surfaces inside an enabled FIFO window.
Our own future CMDFIFO (G47) must likewise detect a foreign FIFO and drain/disarm before any direct access (perf-18). Every perf baseline must start with cmdFifo0 off and d3dprobe render at 40/40.

Not yet measured: the 16 bpp path in the stale state, and why an idle-but-enabled FIFO blocks PIO triangles but not fastfill.
evidence: ONBOX/regs/regs_after_windowed_1009.txt (0x80024=0x1fe, 0x8002c=0x2f624 on two reads, aMin 0x2f630, holeCount 0x22177)

gaps.title: Max Payne freeze (2026-10-04): the game froze, not the box; the cause is not established, no ring was saved, and every D3D title on .124 is 'blk' in readiness rounds because of it
gaps.description:
Configuration: vcrmp fda1b8c9 / vcrdd b63ea6a5 (the build before 11-08), D3D32=1, D3DBigTex=7. Max Payne 1.05 was at its menu in D3D 1280x960x32, under SafeDisc 2.51 via DAEMON Tools.

What happened:
- The default fbshot (an ExtEscape under win32k's display lock) printed nothing in 25 s.
- fbshot --probe took about 120 s at normal priority and 38 s at /high.
- wmic and WM_CLOSE did not return.
- Two probe frames taken minutes apart were pixel-identical.
- Num Lock was alive and Task Manager reachable; taskkill /f at high priority ended the game in about 3 s, and the desktop returned at 1280x1024x32@85.
No flight-recorder ring was saved.

history-04 (its own observation): the frozen frames lack the menu text the 09-29 menu frame shows. So the game had probably stopped presenting before or while the probe ran, which argues against 'the probe caused it'; a menu fade-in is the alternative.

Candidate causes, merged:
(a) a stale Glide command FIFO with D3D surfaces in its window (G01);
(b) a silent engine give-up: frozen picture, game alive (G02, ring 512 a=9);
(c) priority inversion or starvation on the display lock: the escape waits on it, the game may hold the CPU above normal priority, and the HAL's PCI PIO runs under it ('everything crawled', hal-25; H1/H2);
(d) the probe's 1.2 M uncached reads (H3);
(e) the game, SafeDisc 2.51, or a Flip-loop stall (511 a=12/13);
(f) the old build.

Renderer needs (games-11): install.reg forces 32 bpp, so it hard-depends on D3D32 (G20). It uses DXT and render targets; cube maps and bump are optional (absent, so it falls back). Only the main menu has been seen on our HAL; the tutorial level was played on the GeForce2 in 2026-08.

Today's on-box pass ran 13 probes and 4 game sessions with no hang (onbox-12), but Max Payne was excluded by rule.

Plan (history-05, hal-30), attended only:
1. Land G01 and G02 first, then cold boot with no Glide session.
2. Set LogLevel=2 and a larger LogEntries (both read at boot).
3. E0: no capture tools for 10 minutes; only agent PING/PROCLIST/WINLIST plus one early wmic for priority and threads. Then WM_CLOSE and vcrctl log; look for 512 a=9, the 513 a=2 counters and 511 a=12/13.
4. E1: fbshot --probe at /high.
5. E2: the default fbshot, last.
6. Repeat E0 three times; the freeze was seen once in about four sessions.
evidence: XEV/v56k-gametune_1001-fbshot_probe-20261004/fbab_maxpayne_probe.png, fbab_maxpayne_probehigh.png, maxpayne_gdi_screenshot.png (no menu text; identical frames)
KMD/README.md:156 (no D3D title in an unattended sweep); KMD/README.md:796
ONBOX/state/proclist_end.json, ONBOX/state/displaycfg_end.txt, ONBOX/regs/regs_end.txt, ONBOX/ring_end_decoded.txt (today's no-hang record)
LIB/MaxPayne/e2driver/e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll strings (D3DTEXOPCAPS_*, cube maps, DRV_setRenderTarget, DXT1-5, CreateVertexShader (software), 'D3D_OK stages:%d')

gaps.title: MODULATE2X/4X drawn as MODULATE on stage 0 and stage 1: the Unreal Engine 2 lightmapped world renders half-bright
gaps.description:
Measured: UT2003's own log_combo dump shows D3DTOP_MODULATE2X (op 5):
- on stage 1 in combines 1, 5 and 6;
- on stage 0 (TEXTURE x DIFFUSE) in combines 3, 10 and 12.
That is 7 of 26 logged set-ups (history-12's count).

How the HAL draws it (verified):
- color_path's default branch draws 'MODULATE, MODULATE2X/4X and the rest' as MODULATE (vcrdd_d3d.c:714);
- stage1_combine maps it to TM_TC_MULT (:862); the logged textureMode 0x800242cf carries MULT;
- TextureOpCaps 0x184f does not list it, yet ValidateTextureStageState accepts it (G15) and UE2 uses it anyway (runtime-14).

Today's first in-game frames (UT2004 botmatch, both runs, and the UT2003 flyby) show the lightmapped geometry very dark (luma 28), while the weapon, HUD and grass look right (onbox-05, hal-33). UT2004 uses the same D3DDrv path (games-02: expected, not measured on its stage sets). onbox-05 names the staged gamma (Brightness/Gamma 0.8) as a second candidate for the darkness.

Hardware: combineMode bit 31 with SST_CM_CC_OUTSHIFT_2X/4X (FBI) and SST_CM_TC_OUTSHIFT_2X/4X (TMU), as 3dfx's HAL uses (D6MT.C:649-652); Glide's grTexColorCombineExt takes the same shift.

Fix: land it with the extended combine (G12), default off behind Diag\D3DFeat, with d3dprobe mod2x/mod4x cells on stage 0 and stage 1 and a host test. Then widen TextureOpCaps.
evidence: SWP/sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt:2, 8, 60 (combine 1 'ops: s0 2 2 1 a 2 2 1 s1 5 a 2'; combine 3 'ops: s0 5 2 0 a 4 2 0')
games: Battlefield 1942 (inferred, per the HAL report's per-title list)

gaps.title: In-game blocky multi-coloured texture noise on terrain and rock meshes (UT2004, UT2003, Halo), on a path no d3dprobe test exercises
gaps.description:
Every in-game frame from today shows 4x4-block-like multi-coloured 'confetti' on terrain and many static rock meshes:
- UT2004, runs 1 and 2;
- the UT2003 flyby at 60, 90 and 120 s;
- Halo timedemo rock faces at 90 and 120 s.
Near rock faces, weapons, grass, trees, HUD and text in the same frames are clean. d3dprobe passes every texture test on the same driver (83/0 and 37/3, decodes texel-exact). The captures were taken after the engine reset (cmdFifo0 off), so G01 is not the cause.

Candidates (the sources differ; none is proven):
(1) runtime-12: XP creates every mip level in its own CreateSurface. The repo's own test docstring records seven calls for a 64x64 D3D8 texture, and ring events show '1 levels' per call. The allocator therefore packs one level per call, while the TMU samples level k at base + chain_offset(k). That holds only while the heap hands out blocks back to back, and breaks after fragmentation. Distant, minified surfaces would then sample garbage, and garbage read as DXT1 decodes to 4x4 blocks of random colour (inferred). The per-level allocation is verified in code; see G07.
(2) hal-23: mipmapped DXT and A8R8G8B8 chains were never probed, and mipchain_ext hands a chain whose levels' FOURCCs differ back to DirectDraw (unaligned, no mips). With one level per call that FOURCC fallback cannot trigger, so this specific path is unlikely (my reading of vcrdd_d3d.c:423-433). The untested multi-level DXT case remains.
(3) onbox-04: UE2's DXT1 lightmaps (UseCompressedLightmaps=True) drawn in texture stage 1, where no probe puts a DXT texture; also sub-4x4 DXT levels and terrain alpha-layer passes.
(4) combine and format gaps (hal-33).

Diagnose with a LogLevel 2 run that reads 513/19 and 513/20 ('mipmap chain ... levels ... at'), 513/21-23 and 513/7; the game rings so far wrapped before any such event survived. Add d3dprobe mipdxt1, mipdxt5, mip8888, a DXT texture in stage 1, and a fragmented-heap chain test.
evidence: ONBOX/ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt seq 24873-24938 ('mipmap chain ... 1 levels' per call)
gaps.vendor_ref: VH5/D3TXTR.C:1635-1636, 1750-1785 (whole chain reserved at the top level's call); VH5/DDFXNT.C:1224-1248

gaps.title: Mip chains: XP sends one CreateSurface per level, but the allocator packs only the levels of one call while the TMU assumes a packed chain; no whole-chain reservation, and multi-level DXT/8888 chains were never probed
gaps.description:
The TMU finds level k at base + chain offset(k), so a chain must be one block.

What the code does (verified, vcrdd_d3d.c:420-460, 547-583): VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain and mipchain_ext compute 'levels' only from p->dwSCnt and mark each call's own top MIP_TOP. On XP dwSCnt is 1 per level unless the driver answers GUID_NTPrivateDriverCaps with ATOMICSURFACECREATION. XP asked today and we declined (ring seq 24832), and the repo's own test docstring records seven calls for a 64x64 D3D8 texture. tex_view and tex_view_ext then walk the attach list and set LODMAX over levels that sit wherever the heap put them.

Consequences:
- On a fresh heap the levels happen to land back to back (d3dprobe mip and mip2048 pass); after fragmentation they do not.
- Small levels also break on padding: each block is 16-byte aligned, while a 2x2 16-bit level is 8 bytes (inferred).

hal-23 adds two points:
- no d3dprobe test builds a multi-level DXT or A8R8G8B8 chain (all use Levels=1; only R5G6B5 chains are tested);
- a chain whose levels' FOURCCs differ is handed to DirectDraw (4-byte aligned, no mips). That fallback should not trigger with one level per call (my reading).

Fix (default off): reserve the whole chain from DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT / lpSurfMore->dwMipMapCount at the top level's call and place the later levels into it, as 3dfx did, or answer ATOMICSURFACECREATION. The TMU's multi-base mode might sample separately placed levels without repacking (hw-27, inferred). Tests: a Python placement test, d3dprobe mipdxt1, mipdxt5 and mip8888, and a fragmented-heap chain test.
evidence: W2KDDK help d_grafx.chm DD_CREATESURFACEDATA (dwSCnt usually 1 on NT); DDK8/ddrawint.h:1022-1035
ONBOX/d3dprobe_textures_a_1024x768x32.txt (mip, mip2048 pass on a fresh heap)

gaps.title: Legacy DX5 texture render states (TEXTUREMAPBLEND, TEXTUREMAG/MIN, TEXTUREADDRESS/U/V, WRAPU/V, MIPMAPLODBIAS, BORDERCOLOR) and D3DTSS_ADDRESS are stored but never applied: DX5/DX6 titles draw point-sampled and MODULATE-only
gaps.description:
What the code does (verified):
- set_rs treats only TEXTUREHANDLE specially (vcrdd_d3d.c:1393-1406).
- compute_regs reads texture state only from the TSS (filters, ADDRESSU/V, MIPFILTER), so stage 0 keeps its defaults: POINT/POINT, WRAP, and MODULATE with texture alpha (ctx_defaults :1138-1146).
- D3DTSS_ADDRESS (12) is never copied to U/V (runtime-11).
- The DX5/6 caps nevertheless advertise DECAL, MODULATEALPHA, COPY, ADD and linear filtering (:2036-2043).

Who sends these states:
- Execute-buffer titles (JK, MotS and Rainbow Six use IDirect3D2 + ExecuteBuffer) pass their raw DX5 render states into DP2 (STATERENDER = RENDERSTATE).
- Microsoft's NT Permedia2 sample maps all of them onto stage 0 for every render state it receives, and so does 3dfx's NT HAL ('still used for WINNT').
- That d3dim also forwards IDirect3DDevice2/3 SetRenderState is inferred: yes.

Consequences:
- point sampling;
- MODULATEALPHA translucency lost;
- DECAL, COPY, ADD and DECALALPHA wrong;
- wrap where clamp was asked;
- DX5 MODULATE's 'vertex alpha when the texture has no alpha' rule lost.

Visual evidence (visual-06): JK, MotS and Thief II's original DX6 engine show hard texel blocks, while NewDark D3D9 Thief II on the same card is bilinear.
Disagreement: games-20/21 read JK's point sampling as JK's own option, because MotS looked 'bilinear-filtered'. visual-06 sees MotS point-sampled too. My look at RES/day/fbshots/mots_game.png at native size (crop x 940-1100, y 200-320) shows hard-edged texel blocks on a magnified wall, and the code path explains it, so visual-06 is supported.
The same engine also runs Thief Gold 1.37 and SS2.

Fix (Diag\D3DFeat), mirroring 3dfx's map (D3RSTATE.C:2851-2940):
- the legacy-MODULATE 0x7ffffffe sentinel;
- TEXTUREMAG/MIN to MAG/MIN/MIPFILTER;
- TEXTUREADDRESS(U/V) and TSS 12 to ADDRESSU/V.
Measure first with a Phase 0 counter (rs 3, 17, 18, 21, 44-46; tss 12). Testing needs a DX5/DX7 probe (G75), because d3dprobe is D3D8.
evidence: JK.EXE / JKM.EXE / RainbowSix.exe GUID scan: IDirect3D2 + ExecuteBuffer, no IDirect3D3
RES/day/fbshots/jkdf2_d3d2.png, jkdf2_d3d3.png, mots_game.png (point-sampled wall at x 940-1100, y 200-320), thief2_c2.png (DX6), thief2_d3d9_armed_4.png (bilinear)
games: D3D options of Half-Life, Descent 3, Turok 2

gaps.title: Argument modifiers D3DTA_COMPLEMENT and D3DTA_ALPHAREPLICATE are masked off before the mapping
gaps.description:
ARG_KIND(a) = a & D3DTA_SELECTMASK (verified, vcrdd_d3d.c:671) drops both modifiers in color_path and stage1_combine. The gap was known and documented as 'rare in games', and d3dprobe's DXT alpha test was rewritten so as not to depend on it. No title's set-up log has yet been checked for the modifiers (history-13).

How the hardware does them:
- COMPLEMENT: XOR the op's invert field (for example INVERT_OTHER_ONE_MINUS_X) into combineMode.
- ALPHAREPLICATE: add 1 to the select field (each select lists the RGB source, then its alpha), or swap fbzColorPath MSELECT from MRGBTMU to MATMU. It is not available as a TMU's M input.
3dfx's validator refuses a complement its op table does not allow.

This is a candidate cause of Halo's glow drawn as a square (G17, onbox-07).

Fix: with the extended combine (G12). Tests: d3dprobe areplicate and complement.
evidence: KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c:735-737 (DXT alpha pass rewritten to avoid the modifier)
gaps.hw: supported (ALPHAREPLICATE not as a TMU's M input)

gaps.title: TFACTOR: paired with a texture it becomes the diffuse colour, and only the FBI's c1 is loaded, so a TMU stage can never use it
gaps.description:
What the code does (verified):
- color_path picks 'other' = TEXTURE if either argument is the texture, otherwise TFACTOR; 'local' is always the iterated diffuse (vcrdd_d3d.c:700-716, 729-741).
- So MODULATE(TEXTURE, TFACTOR) draws texture x diffuse, and a TFACTOR alpha fade does not fade.
- compute_regs writes c0 = 0 and c1 = TEXTUREFACTOR only (:1019-1020).
- Stage 1 cannot see TFACTOR at all.

What 3dfx does on a TEXTUREFACTOR change:
- writes both TMUs' chromaKey and chromaRange; the constant alpha sits in chromaRange[31:24] with combineMode bit 30 set;
- writes the FBI's c0 and c1;
- re-sends the factor after FastFill (vendor-26).
The TMU chroma registers are reserved for TFACTOR; the texture colour key uses the FBI's chromaKey (G09).

Fix: with the extended combine (G12). Tests: d3dprobe tfactor_tex and tfactor_fade.
evidence: SPEC chromaRange register ('When combineMode[30]=1, then the chromaRange register is used to store constant color values in the texture units'); SPEC:2825, 3522

gaps.title: ValidateTextureStageState always answers 1 pass / DD_OK
Lines and points: LineCaps are a copy of the triangle caps, but every LINE and POINT opcode is parsed and skipped
gaps.description:
Verified: prim_caps(&d->dpcLineCaps) (vcrdd_d3d.c:2072) with D3DDD_LINECAPS (:2063). POINTS, LINELIST, LINESTRIP, INDEXEDLINELIST(2), INDEXEDLINESTRIP and LINELIST_IMM are all skipped 'not drawn yet' (:1690-1715). HUD lines, map overlays, beams, tracers and point particles vanish, and FILLMODE wireframe/point would route through these opcodes.

Which titles send them is unmeasured; add a per-context count (G76). Likely users (inferred): JK/MotS automap, Rainbow Six planning overlays, Red Faction HUD, Halo, UE2. Thief II already stages its pixel and square particles as disks.

How to draw them: the hardware has no line or point primitive (the spec calls lines 'special case triangles'). The 2D engine's Bresenham lines have no Z, texture or blending, so they are no use.
- Glide draws a line as a 4-vertex strip offset by +/-0.5 in the minor axis.
- 3dfx draws 1-pixel quads and 1x1 points (MaxPointSize 1, so no point sprites). Its NT geometry spans y-1..y; the Win9x tree moved it to -0.5..+0.5 for WHQL, so copy the Win9x geometry.

Fix: two-triangle quads through the existing setup unit. Tests: d3dprobe lines, points, linestrip and indexedlines.
gaps.hw: partial (no line/point primitive; drawn as triangles)

gaps.title: Halo: glow and soft sprites drawn as sharp-edged squares
Unreal Engine 2: solid-white sky and horizon areas, white polygons and striped frames
gaps.description:
Seen today:
- UT2004 run 2: the sky seen through a cave opening is white (80 s), and a white band covers most of the horizon under a correct orange sky strip (100 s).
- UT2003 flyby: terrain solid white with a cyan triangle and a striped floor (30 s), and a white wedge in the sky (120 s).
- UT2004 run 1: a striped/white early frame at 65 s (hal-33: 'horizontal stripes').
- visual-11: UT2003 at 60 s on 13256e46 (menu time) is black except a yellow-green band at y 485-492 across the full width. It may be a transition or a collapsed quad, and needs a recapture (G79).

Candidates (unverified):
- UT2003.log says 'Using w- pixel fog'. W table fog over world-unit ranges beyond the table's last entry (w 52428.8), or the fog colour, could give white; d3dprobe's fogtable test covers only w 1..8 with a blue fog colour.
- TFACTOR (G14).
- A blend mode mapped to white (G28, G29).
Halo's sky renders right.

gaps.title: UT2003/UT2004 render at 16 bpp with D16 although the staged ini says Use16bit=False and D3D32 is armed; UT2003 also drops to 640x480
gaps.description:
What the logs show:
- UT2004.log: 'Enter SetRes: 1280x960 ... back-buffer format 23 (16-bit) ... depth-buffer format 80 (16-bit)'.
- UT2003.log: 'D3D Detected: 3dfx video card', then 640x480x16@120 with D16 and software T&L.
- The ring shows UT2004's only context at 16 bpp, with no refused 32 bpp attempt before it, so the choice is made above the driver.
- Every UT frame is 565-quantised with ordered dither.

Why (the sources differ):
- Both staged D3DDrv.dll binaries contain the UTF-16 string 'D3D Detected: 3dfx video card' (checked). That supports runtime-26's reading that UE2 has a 3dfx path keyed on the vendor id; that the path forces 16-bit is inferred.
- visual-08 also named the D16-at-32 lead (G10). The absence of any refused 32 bpp ContextCreate in the ring argues against it.

UT2003's 640x480: the 11-08 sweep and today's flyby both SetRes 640x480, while [WinDrv.WindowsClient] FullscreenViewportX/Y is 1280x960. The same section sets MenuViewportX/Y = 640x480, a candidate cause (inferred).

To decide:
- Is 16 bpp acceptable? It gains most from 2PPC (G50).
- Or should a library/ini change force 32 bpp?
Settle the 3dfx path by reading what D3DDrv does when it detects the vendor id, or by testing with the vendor id masked.
evidence: LIB/UT2003/System/D3DDrv.dll and LIB/UT2004/System/D3DDrv.dll (UTF-16 'D3D Detected: 3dfx video card')

gaps.title: D3D32 and D3DBigTex are default OFF: on a fresh install seven titles cannot run, and the docs still call BigTex unproven
gaps.description:
Titles with hard dependencies:
- Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe forces 32 bpp: 'Unable to initialize graphics ... requires DirectX 8' without D3D32.
- UT2004/UT2003 need D3DBigTex: DXT1 lightmaps, DXT5 512xN fonts, A8R8G8B8 up to 1024x512. With the 256x256 Voodoo3-era HAL, UT2004's CreateTexture failed with INVALIDCALL ('Critical Error' in the 09-28 D3D32-only sweep). Their Use16bit=False asks for 32 bpp, but they actually run at 16 bpp here (G19).
- Halo needs D3D32 plus D3DBigTex=7 (a white menu without DXT2/4), and DisableRenderTargets on top.
- Thief II NewDark needs D3D32 plus D3DBigTex bits 0 and 2. Its launcher checks the registry and otherwise falls back to the DX6 display at 640x480.
- Max Payne's install.reg forces 32 bpp.
- Rainbow Six's 16-over-32 Z fix applies only with D3D32.
Without D3D32 there is no 32 bpp D3D8/9 at all, including windowed on the 32 bpp desktop: DDBD_16 only (vcrdd_d3d.c:2079).

Where the switches stand:
- D3D32 was proven on silicon on 09-28 (step 16: 40/40, 42/42, perf 84.2, H&D starts) and has been armed since.
- D3DBigTex was verified on 09-28 (4ef226e) and 11-08 (481acfd, 100/0). Today it scored 83/0, with decodes at 0 wrong texels.

Blockers before D3D32 goes default-on (history-29):
- G01 (no triangles after an unreleased Glide session);
- G10 (D16 at 32 bpp, exposed to every 32 bpp client);
- the 16 bpp stencil premise and Reset3D (G03);
- the README's LAN-party caution.
The Rainbow Six and Thief II blockers are gone. The default path's alignment and 24-bit-address bugs (G21) argue for defaulting at least part of BigTex.

Flipping a default needs a MOVED_DIAG entry with evidence and a change to test_d3d32_is_a_default_off_switch. The README's 'NOT yet on silicon' wording is in G80.
evidence: KMD/README.md:110-111 (D3D32 and D3DBigTex rows), :480-482 (UT2004 CreateTexture failed), :784-796
LIB/HiddenAndDangerous/Play Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe.bat:22 (forces 'Display bitdepth' 32); FIND:730-736

gaps.title: The default texture path (no D3DBigTex) keeps two bugs the BigTex path fixed: DirectDraw's 4-byte placement for single-level and render-target textures, and the 24-bit texBaseAddr (textures above 16 MB sampled 16 MB lower)
gaps.description:
Bug 1, placement (verified): VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain's default path takes only TEXTURE|MIPMAP chains (vcrdd_d3d.c:532-539). Single-level textures therefore keep DirectDraw's linear-heap placement on a 4-byte boundary, while texBaseAddr holds address bits 25:4 (vcr_texlod.c:32 masks 0x00fffff0); such a texture is sampled up to 12 bytes early.
- This is the UT2003 noise class that was fixed on 11-08, but only inside mipchain_ext. visual-02 shows the before and after on the BigTex path.
- Render-target textures keep DirectDraw's placement on both paths (:381-391).

Bug 2, address width: the default path writes the Voodoo3's 24-bit texBaseAddr field. On a 64 MB VSA-100 (.124's heap spans 0-27 MB), a texture placed above 16 MB is sampled 16 MB lower (README); d3dprobe texhigh shows the difference.

Another route: XP asks GUID_GetHeapAlignment at every enable, and we decline (runtime-13). Answering 16-byte start and pitch alignment for Texture, ZBuffer, FlipTarget and Offscreen surfaces could fix placement at the source (that XP honours it is inferred).

.124 has BigTex armed, so these bugs hit fresh installs and every box without the switch.

Fix: generalise mipchain_ext's single-level placement and the 26-bit base to the default path, or default BigTex on (G20). Add Python placement tests on both paths.
games: all textured D3D titles on a box without Diag\D3DBigTex
Unreal Tournament 2003 (the instance fixed on the BigTex path)

gaps.title: Z bias (D3DRENDERSTATE_ZBIAS) ignored and not reported: decals and bullet holes z-fight
gaps.description:
ZBIAS is never read (verified: no ZBIAS reference in vcrdd_d3d.c), and RasterCaps (00100191) lack it. Titles that check caps drop their bias: UE2 probes 'Supports Z biasing', and Halo has a per-card DecalZBiasValue.

Hardware: fbzMode bit 16 (FZ_ZBIAS, vcr_3dregs.h:115) adds zaColor[15:0] at 16 bpp, or zaColor[23:0] at 32 bpp, to the computed Z or 1/W.

What 3dfx did:
- ZBIAS 0..16, shifted left by 1 at 16 bpp and by 9 for a 24-bit Z;
- negated for LESS/LESSEQUAL and masked to the Z width;
- ENZBIAS always on.
Its shift follows the primary's depth rather than the Z's; do not copy that (G95).

zaColor is also FASTFILL's clear depth: VcrDd3dClear rewrites it (vcrdd_3d.c:160), so the bias must be re-sent after every clear, as 3dfx restores zaColor after its clears.

D3D9's slope-scaled bias has no register (Halo's DecalSlopeZBiasValue cannot be honoured).

Fix (Diag\D3DFeat): implement it and report ZBIAS. Test: d3dprobe zbias, where a coplanar decal at bias 1 must win.
evidence: UT2004/System/D3DDrv.dll UTF-16 strings 'D3D Driver: Supports Z biasing'
gaps.hw: supported (constant bias only; no slope-scaled bias)

gaps.title: ZENABLE = D3DZB_USEW turns depth testing OFF; the W-buffer is not implemented and WINFO is skipped
games: DX6/DX7 titles that request W-buffering (inferred: System Shock 2, Thief Gold, UE2, Halo)

gaps.title: SHADEMODE FLAT and FILLMODE wireframe/point are ignored, although COLORFLATRGB/ALPHAFLATBLEND are advertised
gaps.description:
Verified: there is no SHADEMODE reference in vcrdd_d3d.c, so every triangle is gouraud-shaded from its vertices. The flat flags in DX5 execute-buffer INDEXEDTRIANGLELIST wFlags are ignored too (:1643-1648). ShadeCaps nevertheless advertise COLORFLATRGB and ALPHAFLATBLEND (:2032-2033).

The chip has no flat-shade mode: colour always iterates from three vertices. 3dfx replicated the provoking vertex's colour on the host, and noted 'HW cannot support FLAT_SHADE and Auto Strip/Fan', so flat geometry loses strip reuse (relevant to G49).

Fix:
- in vertex(), send the provoking vertex's colour for all three vertices;
- route wireframe and point fill through the line/point path (G16).
Test: d3dprobe flatshade. Users (inferred): JK, MotS and DX5 titles.

gaps.title: Specular highlights are never drawn: SPECULARENABLE is ignored and the specular colour is used only to carry vertex fog
gaps.description:
What the code does (verified):
- the vertex specular colour is read only for the fog factor in its alpha (vcrdd_3d.c:202-209);
- SPECULARENABLE is never read;
- ShadeCaps (0x4008 as D3D8 reports them) lack SPECULARGOURAUDRGB.
Titles that check caps therefore fall back and lose their highlights: Halo (DisableSpecular), UE2 and Max Payne (inferred).

The chip has one ARGB iterator set per triangle. 3dfx's approach:
- Untextured: CLAMP888(diffuse + specular) per vertex on the host.
- Textured with non-zero specular: a second pass. It blends ONE/ONE (or the app's source factor with destination ONE), uses ZFUNC EQUAL when Z writes are on, passes iterated RGB, uses FOGADD-only fog and turns auto-strip off.
- The Win9x tree later made untextured specular two-pass as well (SPECULARFIX), because a per-vertex clamp is wrong across an edge.
- 3dfx's matrix says 'Napalm: single texture scenario only, 2-pass', and D3DTA_SPECULAR as a stage argument was refused.

A single-pass variant, loading a TMU's colour iterator through a chip-field sARGB write, is untested (inferred, low confidence; hw-41 check 3).

Fix: a per-vertex saturating add for untextured triangles and a second additive pass for textured ones; then report SPECULARGOURAUDRGB. Test: d3dprobe specular.
games: DX6-DX8 titles with lit specular materials
gaps.hw: partial (one colour iterator: host add or two passes)

gaps.title: No trilinear filtering: MIPFILTER LINEAR is drawn as nearest-level mipmapping (visible mip bands)
gaps.description:
Verified: tex_view only sets the chain's LOD range, with no TRILINEAR bit (vcrdd_d3d.c:779-786, 814-824). TextureFilterCaps 03010317 lack MIPFLINEAR and LINEARMIPLINEAR. UE2 stages UseTrilinear=True, Red Faction logs 'Trilinear filtering enabled.', and Thief II stages tex_filter_trilinear; all fall back.

Hardware: single-pass trilinear for ONE texture stage.
- textureMode[30] trilinear with tc_mselect = LOD fraction.
- TMU1 fetches the odd LODs (tLOD[18] lod_odd, [19] lod_tsplit); TMU0 fetches the even LODs and blends.
- One copy of the texture serves both TMUs (26-bit base).
- It uses both TMUs and disables 2PPC.

With two texture stages it does not fit one pass:
- 3dfx failed ValidateDevice with TOOMANYOPERATIONS ('V5 doesn't support it') unless LOD_DITHER was set (registry default 0).
- The substitute is SST_TLODDITHER, about +0.375 LOD, offset with lodbias.
- Under SLI, 3dfx added per-chip LOD bias offsets for multitexture with trilinear.
SPEC section 3.3's 'two-pass trilinear' is the stale section; section 3.5 and textureMode say single cycle (hw-40).

Fix (Diag\D3DFeat): use 3dfx's TMU0/TMU1 split tables when one stage is active, and LOD dither with two stages. Test: d3dprobe trilinear (a gradient across a mip boundary).
evidence: LIB/UT2003/System/UT2003.ini:245-265 (UseTrilinear=True); rf.exe strings 'Trilinear filtering enabled.'; LIB/Thief2/cam_ext.cfg (tex_filter_trilinear)
gaps.hw: partial (single stage only; LOD dither with two)

gaps.title: MIPMAPLODBIAS, MAXMIPLEVEL, SETTEXLOD and nearest-LOD rounding are ignored
gaps.description:
What is missing in our HAL:
- D3DTSS_MIPMAPLODBIAS and MAXMIPLEVEL are never read.
- SETTEXLOD, the managed-texture LOD clamp, is skipped by size (vcrdd_d3d.c:1563-1565).
- RasterCaps lack MIPMAPLODBIAS.
- The hardware truncates the LOD, where 3dfx added +0.5 to round to the nearest level (for point mip and for two-stage draws).
UE2 stages DefaultTexMipBias=-0.5.

Hardware:
- tLOD[17:12] holds lodbias, 4.2 signed, -8..+7.75 (Glide clamps it to -0x20..0x1f);
- tLOD[5:0] and [11:6] hold lodmin and lodmax, which serve MAXMIPLEVEL;
- the LOD-dither offset must be subtracted from the bias when dither is on.

What 3dfx did:
- converted D3D's bias with CalcBias42 and added a registry LOD_BIAS on top;
- raised LODMIN for MAXMIPLEVEL, but used stage 0's value for both TMUs (a bug its own comment admits; do not copy). F-22 Lightning 3 drove that clamp.
- never advertised MIPMAPLODBIAS, although it implemented it. SWARCH's planning-era 'No' is stale.

Fix: implement and report the cap. Test: d3dprobe lodbias.

gaps.title: Alpha channel always blends ONE/ZERO; DESTALPHA factors are unadvertised yet passed to the hardware; SRCALPHASAT is advertised but unverified
gaps.description:
What the code does (verified):
- compute_regs writes AM_ASRC(BF_ONE) | AM_ADST(BF_ZERO) whatever the blend states are (vcrdd_d3d.c:998). On a target with alpha (an A8R8G8B8 render target at 32 bpp), destination alpha receives unblended source alpha.
- blend_src/blend_dst map DESTALPHA and INVDESTALPHA to the hardware factors (:636-637, 659-660), while SrcBlendCaps 0x1f33 and DestBlendCaps 0x3f do not advertise them. An app that sets them anyway reads stale or undefined destination alpha on X8R8G8B8 and 16 bpp targets.
- SRCALPHASAT is advertised and maps to BF_SATURATE, min(As, 1-Ad), which needs destination alpha.

Hardware (hw-04, hw-22):
- At 32 bpp the alpha planes are live (fbzMode[18] clear), and alphaMode[23:16] gives the alpha channel its own factors: zero, srcA, dstA, one, 1-srcA, 1-dstA. renderMode[20] gates alpha writes.
- At 15/16 bpp the alpha-channel factors are only ZERO and ONE.
- 15 bpp has a 1-bit alpha sharing fbzMode[9]; at 16 bpp the aux buffer can serve as alpha only with depth off.

3dfx advertised DESTALPHA, INVDESTALPHA and SRCALPHASAT, then substituted ONE/ZERO on every Napalm draw (PRS 8373), and below 32 bpp also clamped the alpha factors. It never did real destination alpha (vendor-19).

Fix:
- at 32 bpp targets with alpha, take the alpha-channel factors from the app's factors;
- honour DESTALPHA only where the target has alpha, and use D3D's no-alpha substitution elsewhere;
- decide SRCALPHASAT with a d3dprobe srcalphasat test, and stop advertising it if that fails.
D3D9's separate alpha blend is a different feature, not reachable through this DDI (G91).
gaps.hw: partial (real destination alpha at 32 bpp only)

gaps.title: SRCCOLOR as a source factor and DESTCOLOR as a destination factor are mapped to ONE ('the chip cannot'), but the VSA-100's A_SAMECOLOR does exactly this
gaps.description:
Verified:
- blend_src's default case returns BF_ONE with the comment 'SRCCOLOR the chip cannot' (vcrdd_d3d.c:643);
- blend_dst's default case returns BF_ONE with 'DESTCOLOR the chip cannot' (:661);
- the caps hide them honestly: SrcBlend lacks SRCCOLOR/INVSRCCOLOR, and DestBlend lacks DESTCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR.

Napalm added A_SAMECOLOR/AOM_SAMECOLOR (alphaMode factor codes 8/9; the inverse comes with it), meaning the same pixel's colour. Only on Voodoo3 is the comment true. With 0xF (SRCALPHASAT as a source factor, colour-before-fog as a destination factor), all 13 D3D factors map. 3dfx mapped SRCCOLOR/INVSRCCOLOR (source) and DESTCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR (destination) to them and advertised the factors.

Shogo's d3d.ren checks 'Src blend SRCCOLOR'.

Fix: two mapping lines plus the caps, with d3dprobe blend-matrix cells.
evidence: SPEC:2966, 2969-2970, 2972 ('Added new alpha blending functions A_SAMECOLOR and AOM_SAMECOLOR')
Shogo/d3d.ren strings 'Src blend SRCCOLOR: %s, Dest blend SRCALPHA: %s'

gaps.title: Dithering is left on for 32 bpp targets, which the VSA-100 spec forbids
gaps.description:
Verified: compute_regs sets FZ_DITHER whenever DITHERENABLE is TRUE, at every target depth (vcrdd_d3d.c:979-980), and VcrDd3dState writes fbzMode as it is.

The spec says: 'fbzMode bit(8) must be cleared when 32-bit color rendering is selected (renderMode[1:0]=0x2)'.
- Our h5 Glide clears dither at 32 bpp (_grDitherMode: 'disable dithering when in 32bpp', checked), and at 16 bpp forces the 2x2 matrix with dither subtraction.
- 3dfx's D3D sets DITHER2x2.
The effect on silicon has not been measured.

Also:
- we use the 4x4 matrix without subtraction at 16 bpp;
- under SLI, dithering breaks at band height 1 (G51).

Fix:
- clear FZ_DITHER for 32 bpp targets;
- consider 2x2 plus subtraction at 16 bpp.
Tests: a host test, and d3dprobe at 32 bpp with dither enabled.
evidence: SPEC:3254 (bit 8 must be cleared at 32 bpp), 3213, 3268, 6244
games: 32 bpp D3D titles that enable dither: Halo, Thief II, Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe, Max Payne

gaps.title: Table fog is always W-based: a Z-unit FOGSTART/END (1.0 or less) fogs every pixel
gaps.description:
Verified: vcr_fog_table evaluates the entries at w from 1 to 52428.8 (vcr_fog.c:36-62). With start and end given in Z units, every entry comes out as full fog.

3dfx zeroed such tables: its PXLFOGLIN guard turns table fog off when start < 1 and end <= 1 (PRS 13517), and it also carried a Centipede-specific linear-fog fix.

We advertise both WFOG and FOGTABLE.

Fix (Diag\D3DFeat): add the Z-based table guard. Test: d3dprobe fogtable_z.
games: DX5-DX7 titles using table fog with Z-unit start/end (unmeasured)

gaps.title: Vertex fog is approximated through a synthetic 1/W and is off without a specular FVF; the fog unit can take iterated alpha, Z or W directly; FOGGOURAUD is not reported; the semantics of fogMode bits 3+4 are unsettled
gaps.description:
Today's method:
- vertex fog rides a synthetic 1/W chosen to land on an identity ramp table, so across a triangle the chip interpolates 1/W rather than the fog factor;
- vertex fog is off when the FVF has no specular (vcrdd_d3d.c:1358-1360);
- vcr_fog.h justifies this with 'a fog unit that only knows W'. The spec contradicts that premise (hw-16).

What the hardware offers:
- fogMode bit 3 selects iterated alpha, and bit 4 the top 8 bits of iterated Z.
- 3dfx sets both and, under a Z-buffer, sends 255 minus the specular alpha in Wfbi (sOowfbi); under a W-buffer it uses FOG_Z with the factor in Z (sVz = factor << 8).
- When fbzColorPath[28]=1, W is clamped to [0,0xff] for the fog unit.

An evidence conflict (vendor-17, hw-17): SPEC section 8.22 says bit 4 takes precedence when both bits are set, which would mean Z. That sentence looks inherited from SST-1 and contradicts both 3dfx's code and section 8.20. One d3dprobe run settles it: fogvertex with the factor in Wb and fogMode[4:3]=3, compared pixel-exact against D3D linear fog. If W does not reach the fog unit, fall back to FOG_Z, as 3dfx does under a W-buffer.

Other points:
- The current method is proven on silicon (fogvertex passes) but occupies W, so it must move once W-buffering lands (G23).
- ShadeCaps lack FOGGOURAUD although we fog per vertex; add it now.
- RANGEFOG is a dummy at 3dfx (a vertex-processing matter, inferred).
evidence: SPEC:2791 (fbzColorPath bit 28 W clamp for the fog unit), 2848-2849 (fogMode bits 3, 4), 2867, 2885 (bit 4 takes precedence), 3644, 3781
games: DX5-DX8 titles using vertex fog (Unreal-engine and Dark-engine titles, inferred)

gaps.title: MIRROR texture addressing falls back to WRAP
gaps.description:
Verified: only CLAMP sets TM_CLAMPS/T (vcrdd_d3d.c:792-795, 830-833); MIRROR and BORDER fall through to WRAP, and TextureAddressCaps are 0x15.

Hardware: tLOD[28] and [29] mirror S and T independently. Glide's GR_TEXTURECLAMP_MIRROR_EXT and 3dfx (TMIRRORS per stage) use them, and 3dfx advertised MIRROR. MIRRORONCE has no single bit (inferred). BORDER is impossible (G86).

Fix: implement and report MIRROR. Test: d3dprobe mirror.

gaps.title: Texture formats: L8, A8L8, A4L4, R3G3B2, A8R3G3B2 and the X variants (X8R8G8B8, X1R5G5B5, X4R4G4B4) are not offered; A8 cannot be offered through a DX7 DDI
gaps.description:
What we offer (verified, vcrdd_d3d.c:2081-2099): 565, 1555 and 4444 by default; D3DBigTex adds 8888 and DXT1-5 (DXT2/4 aliased to DXT3/5). On the default path tex_view accepts only 16-bit RGB.

What the TMU samples: 332, 8332, A8, I8 (= L8/Y8), AI44 (= A4L4), AI88 (= A8L8), ARGB8888 (usable as X8R8G8B8 with alpha forced to 1, inferred), FXT1 and DXT1-5. 3dfx's DX7 list carried 332, P8, 8332, L8, A8, A4L4, A8L8, AP88, 8888, DXT1-5 and FXT1.

Disagreement on A8:
- hal-21, hw-26 and vendor-11 list A8 as addable.
- runtime-07 found that the XP runtime's DDPIXELFORMAT converter (d3d8 0x6d9b6850-0x6d9b6d48, the same cases in d3d9) has no DDPF_ALPHA case, so A8 cannot reach a D3D8/9 game through a DX7 DDI. 3dfx listed A8 as DDPF_ALPHA, which the runtime would drop.
runtime-07's disassembly is the stronger evidence; A8 needs a DX8 GETFORMAT (G94). Also, on the TMU A8 returns RGB = alpha where D3D expects 0, so its colour must not be used (inferred).

Not native: R8G8B8 (convert on upload), the bump formats, and YUY2/UYVY as textures.

Who would use them:
- Halo names a8, y8, ay8, a8y8, p8-bump and x8r8g8b8 bitmap formats. It drew white rather than convert when DXT2/4 were missing, so missing formats may draw white or not at all in gameplay (inferred).
- H&D's LS3D renderer enumerates P8, A8P8, DXT and D24S8.
- UE2 adapts through SupportsTextureFormat/ConvertDXT.

Constraint: the list must stay mode-independent (runtime-22).

Fix: add the DX7 entries one at a time, each with a d3dprobe decode test (tex_l8, tex_a8l8, ...).
evidence: LIB/Halo/halo.exe strings (a8, y8, ay8, a8y8, p8, p8-bump, x8r8g8b8, a8r8g8b8, dxt1/3/5); FIND:439-441 (white menu without DXT2/4)
LIB/HiddenAndDangerous/Bin/i3d2.dll strings ('cannot build lightmap with compressed textures', 'cannot find bumpmap texture format')
gaps.hw: supported (A8 blocked by the DX7 DDI, not the chip)

gaps.title: Stencil: D24S8 is listed in the Z formats, but its stencil is never written or tested (StencilCaps 0; stencil states and D3DCLEAR_STENCIL dropped)
evidence: halo.exe strings CCW_STENCILFAIL; BF1942.exe strings SStencilEnable
games: D3D8 titles that use stencil at 32 bpp
gaps.hw: partial (32 bpp only; no two-sided stencil)

gaps.title: Render-to-texture is untested on silicon: render-target textures keep DirectDraw's placement and pitch, the runtime's PCI-id table grants no X8R8G8B8 render-target texture, and Halo runs with DisableRenderTargets
gaps.description:
Halo's FATAL dialog 105 is a render-target creation failing. The staged config.txt sets DisableRenderTargets for 0x121a:0x0009, so Halo's render-target effects are off. The cause is unmeasured; an X8R8G8B8 render target or a non-power-of-2 size is likely (runtime-06).

The runtime's role: for DX7-DDI drivers, d3d8/d3d9 take render-target texture ops and depth pairing from a 171-entry PCI-id table.
- The entry for 121a:0009 is 0x4580: R5G6B5 and A8R8G8B8 render-target textures (A8R8G8B8 only while BigTex bit 2 lists it), D16 kept as D16_LOCKABLE, and no ARBITRARY_COLOR_DEPTH.
- The registry can only switch flags off (ForceDriverFlagsOff), so an X8R8G8B8 render-target texture needs a DX8 DDI (G94).

Hardware rules (hw-13):
- colBufferAddr and a linear stride must be 16-byte aligned;
- a linear texture's rows are packed, so the target's pitch must equal width x bytes; Glide's TEXTUREBUFFER extension works exactly this way;
- the texture cache must be flushed after rendering (G37);
- under SLI a target is split across the chips, so a render-target texture needs SLI off for that target (inferred);
- 4444, 332, 8332, L8, A8, A4L4 and A8L8 cannot be 3D targets (render, then convert with the 2D engine).

Ours: render-target textures (DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE) are excluded from mipchain_ext and keep DirectDraw's placement and pitch (vcrdd_d3d.c:381-391). No d3dprobe test renders into a texture and then samples it. Thief II's d3d_disp_enable_distortionfx also wants render targets. 3dfx's heap placement was not compared with ours (vendor-40): Z in TILED_HEAP1 when fullscreen, the flip chain in TILED_HEAP2, textures linear, tile-size or 16-byte alignment.

Plan:
1. d3dprobe rtt (render, then sample) at 565 and 8888.
2. Place render-target textures 16-byte aligned with pitch = width x bytes.
3. Retry Halo without DisableRenderTargets.
evidence: XPRT/d3d8.dll 0x6d9a1700 table (file 0xb00), entry 121a:0009 at file 0xc40 = 0x4580; 0x6d9b0140-0x6d9b0234, 0x6d9b36d6-0x6d9b373f (ForceDriverFlagsOff only), 0x6d9b5872-0x6d9b5994
gaps.hw: partial (linear 565/1555/8888 targets; SLI off for that target)

gaps.title: The TMU texture cache is not flushed after a 2D-engine Blt into a texture, or after the 3D engine renders into one
gaps.description:
Verified: VcrDdD3dTexWritten is called only from Unlock (vcrdd_ddraw.c:679) and TEXBLT (vcrdd_d3d.c:1514, 1533). Two other ways of changing a texture never mark it dirty:
- Dd_Blt / clipped_blt copying into a video-memory texture with the 2D engine;
- SETRENDERTARGET rendering into a texture.
The TMU can then sample stale texels.

3dfx flushed each TMU's texture cache whenever it sent texture state: it wrote the inverted base address, then the real one. That is the same mechanism with a broader trigger; ours is fine unless a texture changes by another route (vendor-30).

Fix (Diag\D3DFeat): mark the texture dirty on a 2D Blt into it and on rendering into it. Tests: d3dprobe blt2tex and rtt.
games: titles using render-to-texture or DirectDraw texture updates

gaps.title: Palettized textures (P8/A8P8) are not offered, SETPALETTE/UPDATEPALETTE are skipped, and P8 has never been shown to draw correctly on this silicon
evidence: Shogo/d3d.ren strings ('Couldn't find suitable 8 bit texture format.', 'Selected 8 bit texture format.', 'Palette alpha'); LIB/Shogo/autoexec.cfg:21-25
RainbowSix.exe strings 'CheckForPalettized() : CreatePalette()', 'Create palette failed while loading surface (loadtex)'
games: GoldSrc titles in the D3D renderer (Half-Life, Counter-Strike)

gaps.title: A mode set never clears video memory: the old 32 bpp desktop shows as garbage at the new depth until a title's first frame, or for its whole session if it stalls
gaps.description:
Seen:
- AvP's 640x480x16 screen showed the old 1280x1024x32 desktop, misread, for its whole session (10-14).
- UT2004 showed the same at 1280x960x16 before its first frame: on 09-29 at 30 s, and today in run 1 at 45 s.

Why: IOCTL_VIDEO_SET_CURRENT_MODE masks off VIDEO_MODE_NO_ZERO_MEMORY (vcrmp.c:674), and VcrHwSetMode (vcrmp_hw.c:652-718) never clears the framebuffer. The NT contract is to zero video memory when that bit is clear (inferred, DDK).

The effect is cosmetic, but it reads as corruption to a player during loading.

Fix: a 2D fill of the visible surface at the mode set (the fill exists, vcrdd_ddraw.c:450), or at primary creation.
games: any title that stalls or loads slowly

gaps.title: STATESET is skipped while DRAWPRIMITIVES2EX is reported: DX7-interface state blocks would be applied at record time and never replayed
gaps.description:
The walker skips D3DDP2OP_STATESET by size (verified, vcrdd_d3d.c:1562) and applies recorded states immediately. Reporting DP2EX (:2069) makes vcrdd a DX7-DDI driver, from which the DX7 runtime expects state blocks to be recorded, executed, captured and deleted. That is the DDK's 'Accelerated State Management'; Microsoft's sample has D3D_STATEBLOCKS 1, and 3dfx implemented it in D7DP2.C:1366-1826.

The sources differ on which titles are exposed:
- hal-07 (inferred, low confidence) listed DX7/DX8 titles, including Halo, UT2003 and UT2004.
- runtime-19 disassembled d3d8.dll and d3d9.dll: device init sets 'emulate state blocks' when the DDI type is 5 or lower, and reads the EmulateStateBlocks registry knob only above that. So D3D8/9 never send STATESET to vcrdd; the DDI-type enumeration itself is inferred.
The disassembly supports limiting the risk to DX7-interface titles: UE1 D3DDrv and Tribes 2's OpenGL2D3D, both of which run Glide/OpenGL on .124.

Settle it by measurement: a Phase 0 STATESET counter by operation (G76), and implement only if STATESET arrives. Tests: d3dprobe stateblock (D3D8; it should never reach us) and d3d7probe stateblock.
evidence: W2KDDK/src/video/displays/3dlabs/driver/d3dhw.h:59-62; W2KDDK help d_grafx.chm 4.7.4 Accelerated State Management
games: Unreal Gold, UT 436 and Deus Ex D3DDrv (DX7 interface; dormant on .124)
per hal-07 also Halo, UT2003, UT2004 (contradicted by runtime-19)

gaps.title: The fog-table cache is never invalidated after a Glide session or a display reset
gaps.description:
pd->fog_valid and fog_loaded are reset only when a PDEV is allocated (vcrdd.h:78-79). VcrDd3dState skips the 32-write table load when they match (vcrdd_3d.c:86-98, verified).

Three events leave the cache claiming D3D's table is still loaded:
- an exclusive Glide/OpenGL session;
- its release;
- DrvAssertMode's device reset.
Table or vertex fog on the same PDEV then uses whatever table Glide left.

Fix (CPU-only): clear fog_valid in HWCSET/HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE and in DrvAssertMode. Add a Python test.
games: windowed or same-mode D3D titles with fog after an OpenGL/Glide game

gaps.title: The 4096-entry surface handle table names every mip level and can fill; lookups degrade near capacity
gaps.description:
One open-addressing table serves all processes, and name_surface enters every attached surface, mip sub-levels included.
- Large UE2-style texture sets can hit 'surface handle table full', after which textures draw untextured.
- Lookups of absent keys scan to an empty slot.
- handle_forget rebuilds the whole table on every DestroySurface.

Fix:
- stop naming mip sub-levels;
- grow the table;
- log a high-water mark (also as a Phase 0 counter, G76).

gaps.title: D3D contexts cache a PDEV pointer that a mode change frees (possible use-after-free)
games: any D3D game alt-tabbed or switching modes

gaps.title: UT2003: the grass decoration layer renders blue, and a grey checkerboard patch appears
gaps.description:
In the UT2003 flyby (60, 90 and 120 s), the Antalus grass decorations are vivid blue; they should be green-yellow. At 120 s a grey checkerboard texture also appears.

UT2004's grass on the same map renders the right colour, so this is a UT2003-specific texture or vertex-colour path. Candidates:
- a red/blue swap in one texture format;
- a material the engine could not create. The checkerboard looks like UE2's default texture (inferred).

Diagnose with log_combo and the refused-texture events (513/7) from a LogLevel 2 run.

gaps.title: UT2004 menu: a one-pixel bright line on the bottom row of the screen
gaps.description:
After the half-pixel fix:
- row 959 has mean 232.5, with 725 px at (231,231,231);
- rows 958 and 957 are 93.9 and 18.2.
Before the fix the line sat on row 958 (132.7), with row 959 uncovered.

Because it moved with the fix, it is a texture edge that is really drawn, consistent with bilinear sampling across a WRAP edge (inferred). UT2004 is D3D8, so it sends ADDRESSU/V, which the HAL honours (vcrdd_d3d.c:792-795).

It may also appear on reference hardware; compare before acting. Low confidence.

gaps.title: In-game D3D performance is very low, and its CPU/HAL split is unmeasured: UT2003 flyby 9.41 fps at 640x480x16, with 116.7 ms of a 123 ms frame inside DrawPrimitive
gaps.description:
The first D3D game numbers on vcr-kmd (onbox-09, today):
- UT2003 flyby (-benchmark), 640x480x16@120: min 2.07 / avg 9.41 fps, score 9.419. The stats CSV has 1998 frames in 245.7 s: a 122.99 ms mean frame, of which 116.73 ms is 'Hardware DrawPrimitive', at 29,362 primitives and 33,846 software-processed vertices per frame (about 240k triangles/s end to end). Present takes 0.76 ms. The ring says 'context 1 gone: 59589 DP2, 37033284 triangles'.
- UT2004 8-bot botmatch, 1280x960x16: stat fps 4 current / 6 average.
- Halo -timedemo, 1280x960: unfinished after 485 s (26.1 M triangles, 764 clears).

What existed before today:
- synthetic numbers only. d3dprobe perf (200 triangles a frame) gave 151 fps with novsync at 640x480x16 and 85.0/84.2 with vsync. It is fill-bound: only 67 of the 200 triangles have area (about 0.99 Mpix), so its tris_s field is not triangle throughput.
- the vendor stack's UT99 D3DDrv on UTbench (AmigaMerlin 3.1-R11): 69.1 fps at 1024x768x16 on 4 chips.

'Hardware DrawPrimitive' includes the runtime's software vertex processing as well as the HAL's DP2 walk and PIO, about 4 us per triangle. Attributing it to submission (G47-G49) rather than CPU vertex work is inferred, until a heavy d3dprobe perf scene (thousands of triangles a frame, --novsync) and the driver counters (G78) split it.

gaps.title: No command FIFO: every 3D register write is an uncached PIO store into chip 0's 31-entry PCI FIFO, so the CPU and the chip run one after the other, under the display lock
A status-register read before every vertex, plus 27/36/45 uncached writes per untextured/1-texture/2-texture triangle (about 5-8 us each, inferred)
Strips, fans, indexed primitives and immediate fans are sent as independent triangles, with three full vertices each
Two pixels per clock, its band height and the column band are never programmed: D3D fills at about 1 textured pixel per clock per chip
gaps.description:
What the HAL does: nothing writes combineMode (only Reset3D writes 0), and renderMode[24:22] and fbzColorPath[31:30] stay 0. Today's on-box register read: combineMode 0, renderMode 0x001e0002, fbzColorPath 0x0c002401.

How 2PPC works:
- combineMode[29] enables it for single-textured triangles, and both TMUs must hold identical state;
- leaving it needs 12 nopCMDs addressed to the TMUs only (chip field 0x6; a hardware bug), with combineMode written before any other 3D register;
- the spec recommends it at 15/16 bpp only, and at 32 bpp only at very low resolutions; it may need disabling at very high resolutions or refresh rates.

3dfx enables it by default on Napalm (band log2 2, column band 2; its 3DMark2000 comment) for single-stage and untextured draws at 15/16 bpp, and drops it for two stages and for trilinear. Our Glide enables it when one TMU suffices.

Evidence that it works on this silicon: our Glide's 4-chip fill of 1124.6 Mpix/s at 166.8 MHz is about 281 Mpix/s per chip, more than 1 px/clk allows (inferred arithmetic). d3dprobe perf's 6.6 ms frame fits the 1 px/clk model (6.9 ms), not 2 px/clk (3.9 ms).

Expected gain: up to about 1.7-2x single-texture fill (inferred). It is most valuable for the 16 bpp titles: Shogo, JK, MotS, R6, SS2, Thief Gold and UE2, which runs at 16 bpp (G19).

Fix: P2 (Diag D3D2ppc; bits for 2PPC, band and column band), with the exit sequence. Measure with a d3dprobe perf A/B at 1024x768 and 1280x1024, at 16 and 32 bpp (hw-41 check 4).

gaps.title: Direct3D renders on one VSA-100 of four (no SLI), while 3dfx's D3D defaulted to 4-chip SLI and our kernel driver already runs SLI for Glide
Logging on the drawing path: every VcrDd() call formats a message and makes an IOCTL whatever the level, and every texture bind logs a DEBUG event
gaps.description:
VcrDd() always runs vsnprintf and EngDeviceIoControl. The level is filtered only in the miniport, after the round trip, and the default LogLevel is DEBUG, so DEBUG events are also stored.

DP2 logs a DEBUG event:
- on every D3DTSS_TEXTUREMAP;
- on each TEXBLT;
- on each render-target change.
Flip, Lock and Blt each log a TRACE event that is paid for and then dropped.

At about 5-15 us per event (inferred), a title binding hundreds of textures per frame could lose several ms per frame. The events also flood the flight-recorder ring (G76).

Fix (P1): cache the miniport's level in the PDEV and return early, and count texture binds instead of logging each one. There is no register-traffic change, so it can be on by default.

gaps.title: The full state and render target are re-sent at the first triangle of every DrawPrimitives2 call and on every change; no registers are shadowed
gaps.description:
dp2walk is zeroed for every DP2 call (prepared = 0). prepare() therefore reruns compute_regs and re-sends the target (7-9 writes) plus all state (8 FBI, 4 TMU0 and 4 TMU1 writes, maybe a NOP): about 19-30 uncached writes and 2-4 status reads per call.

compute_regs itself does two handle lookups, texture LOD maths and a 64-entry log_combo scan.

Other sources of re-sends:
- TEXTUREHANDLE and TEXTUREMAP mark the context dirty even when unchanged;
- Clear and SETRENDERTARGET force a re-send;
- Clear2 re-sends the target for each rectangle.
Only the fog table is shadowed. 3dfx used per-group dirty flags and wrote state only when it changed.

Fix: P4 (Diag D3DShadow), register shadows with invalidation (which must also cover G01/G03/G41 resets).

gaps.title: Every flip makes the CPU wait for the whole engine to go idle, then writes vidDesktopStartAddr by IOCTL; there is no hardware swap queue (and a future one must cap pending swaps at 6)
gaps.description:
Today's flip:
1. Dd_Flip returns WASSTILLDRAWING, one IOCTL per retry, until the previous flip latches.
2. VcrDd2dSync then drains the whole engine.
3. The flip IOCTL follows, plus vblank and TRACE IOCTLs; completion is polled (vcrdd_ddraw.c:246-255, 315-361).
This is cheap today because the FIFO is tiny, but with a CMDFIFO it would stall the CPU for the tail of every frame. Vblank and flip-completion polls are IOCTLs, although the DLL already maps the register window (perf-13).

What 3dfx and our h5 Glide do: queue leftOverlayBuf plus swapbufferCMD in the FIFO, throttle pending swaps, and scan out through the overlay. 3dfx caps queued swaps at MAXPENDINGBUFFERS_TOAVOIDHANG = 6 ('to avoid hardware hang'; with vsync, WaitOnVsync+1, capped at 6). Our flip path allows one pending flip today, so the cap applies to P7 (vendor-27; that pass did not check our queue depth).

Fix: P7 (Diag D3DHwSwap, after P6). Preferred: the overlay swap, as our Glide does it. Fallback: leftDesktopBuf plus SST_SWAP_DESKTOP_EN, which both existing users apply only in AA.

gaps.title: Render-after-flip hazard (unverified): DP2 and Clear2 draw at once into the buffer a pending vsync'd flip is still scanning out
gaps.description:
Dd_Lock and Dd_Blt refuse the pending flip_from buffer, but DP2 and Clear2 never check it. At the same time the HAL advertises D3DDEVCAPS_CANRENDERAFTERFLIP and executes writes immediately.

If the D3D8 runtime does not wait (vcr_flip.h itself calls this 'the D3D pattern'), frame N+1's clear and first draws land in the buffer still on the CRT, for up to 11.8 ms at 85 Hz. That would show as tearing or a flash, and never in a GDI capture.

Measure first, with a P0 counter of draws into a pending flip_from. The real fix is the in-order hardware swap (G54, P7); 3dfx answers GetFlipStatus OK for 3D because its swap is queued.

gaps.title: Every DirectDraw Lock and texture upload drains the engine; Halo's Bink movies run about 10x slow (masked by -novideo)
gaps.description:
D3D8 fills managed textures by Lock plus CPU writes, not TEXBLT. What each step costs:
- Dd_Lock calls VcrDd2dSync, a full drain, on every lock, whether or not the surface is in use (vcrdd_ddraw.c:647-661).
- Each Unlock marks the texture for a TMU flush before its next use: 7 writes, including two 2D NOPs, texBaseAddr pointed away and back, a nopCMD, and one uncached texel read written back through the texture port.
- TEXBLT also drains, then memcpys into the write-combined LFB.

Halo's Bink intros were still playing 13 minutes after launch, with halo.exe at about 100% CPU. The launcher now passes -novideo whenever vcrmp runs; FINDINGS names the texture Lock path as the first suspect. Whether Bink also reads VRAM back is unverified.

3dfx downloads textures with packet 5 through the CMDFIFO, in order with the draws and with no idle wait.

Fix:
- drain only when the surface may still be in use (per-surface last-use fences);
- then packet-5 TEXBLT after P6 (P8, Diag D3DTexPkt5);
- then drop -novideo for vcrmp.
evidence: LIB/Halo/Play Halo.bat:4-6 (HALO_NOVIDEO when vcrmp is RUNNING)
games: all D3D titles at level load

gaps.title: No guard band is reported, so the D3D runtime clips every screen-edge triangle in software
gaps.description:
Verified: the extended caps compute -2048/2048 guard values and then discard them with (void)guard (vcrdd_d3d.c:2152-2162). The runtime's software clipper therefore does work the hardware could skip; the CPU cost is estimated at a few % (inferred).

Hardware: renderMode[21] (SST_RM_ENGUARDBAND) clips against clipLeftRight1/clipTopBottom1, while the rasteriser accepts coordinates in [-4k, 4k]. The left and right edges must be even.

3dfx:
- reported -200..2048 x -200..1536 with GUARDBAND_CLIPPING=1, its default;
- programmed clip1 from the viewport;
- needed a clip initialisation for Hidden & Dangerous (PRS 12728).
The clip1 registers must then become D3D-owned state (G03).

Fix: P5 (Diag D3DGuardBand), gated on a pixel-exact guard-band d3dprobe test.

gaps.title: Vertex colour goes as four floats to sRed..sAlpha, which reach the FBI only: TMU stages cannot see diffuse, and every vertex carries 3-4 extra writes
gaps.description:
What the code does (verified): vertex() writes sRed, sGreen, sBlue and sAlpha as floats and, for two stages, sOow1 = sOow0 (vcrdd_3d.c:194-200, 218). vcr_3dregs.h marks SARGB 'NOT used'.

The spec's register table lists sARGB as FBI+TREX* and sRed..sAlpha as FBI only. So the TMU combine inputs for iterated RGB and alpha (SST_CM_TC_*SELECT_IRGB/IA) are fed only by packed sARGB (inferred from the chip column). That is harmless today, but the extended combine (G12) would break diffuse-in-TMU ops, such as BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA in stage 0 or MODULATE with DIFFUSE in a TMU.

3dfx sends packed sARGB and never writes sOow1 (checked case-insensitively: no hits in D6TRI2I.C, D6STRIPI.C or D6FANI.C). Packed colour takes a single-textured vertex from 12 writes to 9, and a dual-textured one from 15 to 11. Dropping W1 assumes the setup unit takes TMU1's W from W0 when SM_W1 is clear (inferred); verify with d3dprobe tex2mod/tex2add.

A test pins the float colour (test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:171-187), so this needs a Diag switch (a P3 bit), keeping floats on the default path. The code comment records that an old gouraud failure blamed on sARGB was really the missing PARMADJUST.

gaps.title: 16 bpp DirectDraw flips on .124 measured at about half the refresh rate (42-47 flips/s at 85 Hz); unexplained
gaps.description:
The measurements:
- ddlab's 16 bpp flip runs on .124 gave 46.9 and 42.1 flips/s, against 87.4 and 86.3 at 32 bpp;
- the completion rule is not the cause, and the 16 bpp run was confounded;
- d3dprobe perf at 16 bpp with vsync held 85.0 fps.
Diag\FlipDeadline (the achieved-refresh deadline) has run on 86Box only, and stays off until counters from real titles justify it; no game's 511 a=12/13 flip counters are on record.

If the half rate is real, every 16-bit D3D title may be capped near half refresh.

Next step: the plan's step-16 per-frame counters (511/12-13) from a real title.

gaps.title: Small CPU-side performance trims: per-call FPU save and setup, IOCTLs for vblank polls, and Glide's skip-transparent-pixels alpha test
gaps.description:
Per-call overheads (perf-13):
- each DrawPrimitives2 call does EngSaveFloatingPointState/EngRestoreFloatingPointState, a memset, target_of and fvf_layout;
- each vblank or flip-completion poll is an IOCTL to the miniport, although the DLL already maps the register window and could read status itself.
Each costs a few us; trim them only once P0 shows them.

Free fill-rate win (hw-23): Glide forces alpha test GT 0 when blending SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA with Z writes off, so pixels with alpha 0 skip their read-modify-write. The same applies to our driver when the app has not enabled alpha test (inferred benefit). It must not change results.

gaps.title: DirectDraw caps under-report what the 2D engine does: no colour-key or stretch caps, DEPTHFILL refused, no overlay
gaps.description:
Verified: ddCaps = BLT | BLTCOLORFILL | READSCANLINE and dwCaps2 = FLIPNOVSYNC (vcrdd_ddraw.c:101-105).
- The 2D engine performs source colour-keyed blits (Dd_Blt handles keys), but DDCAPS_COLORKEY/DDCKEYCAPS_SRCBLT are not reported, so the runtime emulates keyed blits (inferred).
- No stretch cap is reported, so stretches run in the HEL.
- DDBLT_DEPTHFILL is not accepted.

The DirectDraw titles still rendered in the 09-29 sweep:
- RA2/Yuri and Tiberian Sun (16 bpp; TS with VideoBackBuffer=yes);
- StarCraft/BW and Warcraft II at 640x480x8 via Storm.dll.
8 bpp palettes go through DrvSetPalette. GDI cannot photograph WC2's 8 bpp surface; fbshot can.

Low risk; this is mainly CPU cost and capture limits.

Fix: report what Dd_Blt implements, checked with ddlab.

gaps.title: DOSBox output=ddraw (Descent 1/2) shows a black 640x400: one SDL DirectDraw setup call fails; overlay output falls back for lack of overlay caps
gaps.description:
The Descent DOSBox confs use output=ddraw with fullresolution=original. The 09-29 frame had mean 0.0 at 640x400, which is DOSBox's surface fallback after one SDL DirectX5 DirectDraw call failed; which call is unknown.

Tools and leads:
- ddlab sdlddraw replays the sequence, but has never run on silicon;
- the one hypothesis is the heap block at offset 0 (Diag\DdHeapFloor, G63).

Four titles use output=overlay. We advertise no overlay, so SDL falls back to software YUV (inferred); those titles PASS.

gaps.title: The DirectDraw heap starts at offset 0, which HeapVidMemAllocAligned reports as failure; the cure (Diag\DdHeapFloor) has never run on silicon, while every BigTex texture now goes through that allocator
gaps.description:
The block at offset 0 is handed out, read as a failure, and lost until the next mode set: ddlab vidmem on .124 made 120 of the 121 512 KB surfaces that fit.

Since 481acfd every BigTex-path texture is allocated through HeapVidMemAllocAligned in mipchain_ext, where a 0 return becomes DDERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY (vcrdd_d3d.c:441-446). The runtime's own second pass hides the problem from applications.

DdHeapFloor starts the heap one page up. It is host- and 86Box-tested only; no 'on' run (ddlab vidmem, sdlddraw) is on record for .124. It is also the one hypothesis for the Descent DOSBox fallback (G62).

Plan: one clean boot with DdHeapFloor=1; ddlab vidmem must then report 121 surfaces, the lowest at +4 KB.

gaps.title: dwVidMemFree is a constant equal to the total: engines that size their texture cache from the driver's free-memory report may misjudge it
gaps.description:
vcrdd_ddraw.c:109-110 sets dwVidMemTotal = dwVidMemFree = he - hs, once, at heap creation (verified). How the runtime reports free texture memory from that value is inferred.

Affected engines:
- Thief Gold's THIEF.EXE carries 'Direct3d device driver does not accurately report texture memory usage';
- the Dark engine (System Shock 2 too) checks the reported texture memory (effect inferred).

Check what the runtime returns for GetAvailableVidMem on .124, and whether the Dark engine logs that warning.
evidence: LIB/ThiefGold/THIEF.EXE strings (lgd3d d6Render.cpp; 'Direct3d device driver does not accurately report texture memory usage.'; 'Using D3D device: %s')

gaps.title: Staged game configs contradict the campaign's vsync-on and no-AA choices (UT2003/UT2004 UseVSync=False at 60 Hz, Red Faction Vsync=0, Thief II 8x MSAA)
gaps.description:
What the library stages:
- UT2003 and UT2004 stage [D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice] UseVSync=False and DesiredRefreshRate=60. The HAL honours DDFLIP_NOVSYNC via DDCAPS2_FLIPNOVSYNC, so they tear, and 60 Hz is far below the CRT's 85-120 Hz.
- Red Faction stages Vsync=0 in HKCU.
- Thief II's cam_ext.cfg stages multisampletype 8 (8x MSAA), against the user's no-AA choice. It also asks for tex_filter_mode 16 (anisotropic), trilinear, distortion FX and ATOC, which fall back (G26, G85, G36).

Fix in the library, following the staged-game loop: stage-fleetres, or per-3dfx-box FLEETRES. A driver-side force-vsync switch is an alternative.

gaps.title: Staged resolution not applied for several D3D titles: Red Faction's launcher writes HKLM while the game reads HKCU; System Shock 2 and Thief Gold stage no resolution and run at 640x480
gaps.description:
Red Faction:
- the launcher writes Resolution Width/Height/Bit Depth (1280x960x32) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction;
- the game's per-user state (UpdateRate, Vsync, 'Video Card 0') lives in HKCU;
- both 11-08 sweeps measured 640x480, and the 09-29 scan-out was 640x480x16@85.
So rf.exe very likely reads HKCU (inferred). Once fixed, its 32 bpp setting may hit G10.

System Shock 2 and Thief Gold stage no resolution: SS2 has no game_screen_size, and Play Thief Gold.bat has no FLEETRES. Both run at the engine default of 640x480.

Fix in the library, following the staged-game loop.
evidence: LIB/ThiefGold/Play Thief Gold.bat (start thief.exe, no FLEETRES)

gaps.title: Halo: only the menu and today's timedemo cutscenes have been seen, behind three workarounds (DisableRenderTargets, -novideo, an SSE2-floor override); player-controlled gameplay never checked
evidence: FIND:435-450 (FATAL 105, white menu without DXT2/4, SSE2 floor, Bink 10x slow)
LIB/Halo/halo.exe strings (DEPTHBIAS, CCW_STENCILFAIL, cube map, DisableSpecular, environment_fog, MinMaxBlendOpIsBroken, -useff, -use00, -timedemo)

gaps.title: Red Faction: the 09-29 black frame was never explained, and gameplay was never seen; in-game testing needs its disc mounted
gaps.description:
On 09-29 the scanned-out frame was black (extrema 0/0). By 11-08 the menu rendered, apparently on the same vcrdd b63ea6a5, with no recorded cause, so a regression could hide here.

The explanations differ:
- history-34: the 09-29 sweep recorded 'close keys withheld - game not focused'. On 11-08, with the game focused, a 3D object appeared at 30 s and the menu at 60 s.
- visual-05: it ran right after GLQuake in the same boot (the Glide-then-D3D correlation, G03).
- My note, unproven: the stale-FIFO mechanism found today (G01: clears work, triangles vanish) would also give a black frame after a Glide session.

What Red Faction needs:
- its hard requirements are met: MODULATE, SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, 8 MB;
- it also uses detail textures, trilinear (lost, G26), fog, GeoMod dynamic textures (the Lock path, inferred) and HUD lines (G16).
Its timedemo switches exist (-level, -timedemo, -frameratetest), but the title needs its disc mounted. D: currently holds the SoF image, and a DAEMON Tools mount is registry state the on-box run was not allowed to change.
evidence: rf.exe strings ('Your video card is missing the following features required by Red Faction', 'Texture blending mode = Modulate', 'Trilinear filtering enabled.', 'Unable to initialize DirectX 8.0 -- Device creation failed!')
REP/onbox.md (Red Faction not reached: disc mount)

gaps.title: Rainbow Six: its 16-over-32 Z fix rests on one 320x240 strip; the deployed build 95678704 has never had a full sweep, and the title has never been checked in game
evidence: SWP/sweep_1108_fixed/run.out (R6 error at 02:25); git log be58b7d (02:41:09)

gaps.title: Shogo: the main menu is not clearly evidenced on vcr-kmd (near-black 60 s frames, a black backdrop mesh)
gaps.description:
What the frames show:
- 11-08, 30 s: the SHOGO intro logo.
- 11-08, 60 s: near-black (mean 2.0, max blue 82) inside a warped light-blue border.
- 09-29: mean 1.6 at both samples.
- visual-10: the 13256e46 60 s frame shows the backdrop mesh drawn black with no text, in a boot with no Glide session.
- visual-05: the menu text on black without its backdrop, after a Glide session.
The plan nevertheless groups Shogo with titles that render their menus or intros correctly. The compat note 'client menu renders intermittently' is from the GeForce2 era.

Shogo runs at 1280x960x16 through LithTech's d3d.ren, which:
- prefers 8-bit palettized textures (G38);
- checks the SRCCOLOR source blend (G29);
- picks 1-pass or 2-pass lightmapping;
- enables env maps.

Recapture the menu and an in-game scene with fbshot --probe.
evidence: Shogo/d3d.ren strings ('Couldn't find suitable 8 bit texture format.', 'Using 1 pass lightmapping!', 'Z-test: %s, Table fog: %s, Palette alpha: %s')

gaps.title: Aliens vs Predator has never reached a D3D device on .124: the 11-12 library fix was proven on seven other boxes
gaps.description:
Every .124 run of AvP died on game data (an assertion at alt_tab.cpp:198) before it created a D3D device. Its stall left the old desktop on screen as 640x480x16 garbage (G39).

The library fix: 154 InstallShield-obfuscated files were decoded (3f3d1bd) and deployed fleet-wide (9bcb565) on 11-12. The proof lists .110, .123, .133, .143, .171, .184 and .240 reaching the menu, but not .124.

AvP is Direct3D-only: DX5/6 immediate mode through DirectDraw 6, with execute buffers. It will be the next execute-buffer title to meet the HAL; the D3DOP_EXIT handling it needs is done. It picks a palettized or a 16-bit RGB texture format; we offer no P8, so it will use 16-bit. It may use colour keys (G09).
evidence: avp.exe strings ('chosen %u-bit palettized texture format', 'AwSetD3DDevice() OK', D3DERR_EXECUTE_*)

gaps.title: Battlefield 1942 single player is blocked by SafeDisc 2.80 before Direct3D starts
