gaps.title: No D3D title has been checked in game on the current build: in-game frames exist only for JK, MotS and Thief II from 09-28 (before the fixes), and the compat DB's .124 rows are from the GeForce2 era
gaps.description:
A correction to the brief (history-07): in-game frames on vcr-kmd do exist.
- JK DF2's first level at 1280x960x16 (jkdf2_d3d2/3);
- MotS (mots_game);
- Thief II in mission through NewDark's D3D9 display at 1280x960x32 (thief2_d3d9_armed_4), and through its DX6 display at 640x480 (thief2_c2).
All are 09-28 fbshots, taken before the half-pixel, alignment and R6 fixes, and none was compared with a reference renderer. Today added in-engine UT2004, UT2003 and Halo frames (G05, G06, G17, G18).

What is still missing:
- The deployed vcrdd 95678704 has had no full sweep; only the R6 strip exists.
- No in-game frame at all for AvP, BF1942 (all three shortcuts), H&D, Red Faction, Shogo, SS2, Thief Gold, Rainbow Six or Max Payne. Halo and UT have only today's timedemo/botmatch.
- Many sweep frames show no Direct3D at all (visual-17): 8 bpp DirectDraw menus, intro videos, SafeDisc dialogs, OpenGL titles, and downscaled copies. So no frame shows or rules out lines/points, MODULATE2X (except today's dark UE2), ALPHAREPLICATE or the separate alpha factors (visual-15).
- The compat DB's D3D rows for .124 (H&D, Thief Gold, Thief II, UT2004, Shogo, JK, MotS, AvP, Red Faction) were measured on 2026-08-31 on the GeForce2 GTS and are flagged stale. Rainbow Six and UT2003 still read 'untested', and .124 is 'blk' for every D3D title in the 11-11 readiness matrix (G04).
- The longest D3D runs are JK's ~1 minute and the 30/60 s sweep samples; there has been no soak, while GL/Glide titles got 20-30 minute multiplayer soaks.
- Not reached today: Red Faction (disc), Shogo/Thief II/H&D (no direct-to-3D switch found), Max Payne (excluded by rule); JK, MotS, SS2, Thief Gold, R6, BF1942 and AvP were not tried. The 16 bpp path was untested in the stale-FIFO state, and there is no fresh-boot control for the in-game defects.
- JK and MotS exercise DX5 paths no lab test covers (history-39, G75). H&D (games-12, history-38) and Thief II (history-37) were seen in game only on the GeForce2 or before the fixes. SS2 and Thief Gold were seen only at their menus (games-17, games-18).

Plan: Phase 0 counters (G76), then one supervised in-game pass per title at LogLevel 2 harvesting log_combo, with fbshot --probe frames and recorded compat rows.
evidence: git show c6a3e93 (JK renders its first level)

gaps.title: d3dprobe misses most of the gaps: large parts of the HAL have no check, its readback window is 256x256, and its caps mode does not report several values this plan depends on
No DX5/DX7 probe: legacy render states, execute buffers, texture colour keys and DX7 state blocks have no lab test (D3D8 cannot send them)
No per-context usage counters for the gaps, and the flight-recorder ring wraps within seconds of a game starting
No host test executes the state-to-register translation
gaps.description:
The Python D3D tests are source-text assertions on particular lines (PARMADJUST, opcode cases and the like). color_path, blend_src/blend_dst, cmp, stage1_combine, fvf_layout and compute_regs live in the DDI file, whose Microsoft DDK headers are not committed, so none of them is ever executed on the host.

vcr_rtfmt.h, vcr_3dseq.h and vcr_texlod.h already show the pattern that would make them testable: Win32-free headers compiled by native tests. Moving the translation into such a header lets every combine, blend, fog and stencil fix (G05-G35) carry the project's required old-versus-fixed regression test.

gaps.title: D3D benchmark tooling and a vsync-on measurement method are missing or incomplete
Capture and sweep-verdict tooling under D3D exclusive mode: the default fbshot blocks, --probe is slow, GDI frames can be the back buffer, and the luma verdict passes garbage
gaps.description:
Capture limits:
- The default vcrctl fbshot waits on win32k's display lock under a D3D exclusive app; the rule is no vcrctl/ExtEscape while a D3D game runs.
- fbshot --probe works, but crawls when the game holds the CPU.
- lan_sweep's verdict frames are the agent's GDI SCREENSHOT. GDI reads the flip chain at the desktop offset (vcrmp_hw.c:708), so for a flip chain it may return either buffer (inferred).

Resulting false signals:
- transient single-colour or half-drawn frames: Halo all white at 60 s, Shogo's black mesh, UT2003's thin band (visual-10, visual-11);
- the luma-statistics verdict scored H&D's full-screen noise (09-28) a PASS (visual-13), and cannot catch the stale-desktop garbage of G39.

Needed:
- multi-frame recapture with fbshot --probe, a second apart;
- a frame-content check in lan_check;
- sweep verdicts that require in-game frames.

gaps.title: Documentation drift, undocumented kill switches, and verification recorded only as prose
gaps.description:
Drift:
- The README Diag table still calls D3DBigTex 'NOT yet on silicon' (verified: README.md:111 reads 'the VSA-100 texture path (2026-09-28, NOT yet on silicon)'), although 4ef226e, 481acfd and today's 83/0 verify it. tests/README.md:239 and the test_vcr_kmd_bigtex.py docstring say the same.
- Roadmap item 6 still says UT2004 dies at 256x256.
- The 'Status (2026-09-27)' section is out of date.
- The event-table text for 513 omits whats 4/7/8/10/11/13/14/21-23, which the code emits.
- The plan's 're-sweep on the fixed driver' predates the R6 fix.

Undocumented: the kill switches Diag\D3D (0 removes the HAL) and Diag\TexPortFlush are missing from the README's Diag table.

Prose-only verification: the raw d3dprobe RESULT JSON was never committed for the 09-28 BigTex runs, the 11-08 decode/big-DXT/render runs (rgb565_decode1 1024 -> 0, 42/42, 100/0), or the R6-fix render runs. Only commit messages and the plan describe them; only the 09-28 step-16 run and the 86Box runs have raw files.
evidence: git show 4ef226e; git show 76d36e7; git show 481acfd
EV/silicon/d3d32_step16/ (the only raw D3D silicon outputs before today)

gaps.title: Half-pixel centre: the pixel half is fixed and holds on silicon; the texel-centre half and Max Payne's edge are unverified
gaps.description:
Before 76d36e7/13256e46 the last column and row of full-screen D3D quads were not drawn:
- Red Faction: column 639 white in 480/480 rows, row 479 white across 640/640 pixels;
- Thief II, UT2003, UT2004, and the Thief II D3D9 mission frame;
- Max Payne: column 1279 mean luma 4.2, against 12.4 in column 1278.

The fix is xy_bias 0.5 (vcrdd_3d.c:304), matching 3dfx's PIXELCENTER=1 pixelOffset. It cleared Red Faction, Thief II and UT2004 in the 11-08 re-sweep, and today's rgb565_decode1 at 1:1 is texel-exact (0 of 1024 wrong).

Remaining:
- 3dfx also adds textureCenter[log2 size] to S/T for every texture (D3TXTR.C:804-808, 2209-2218). The passing point-sampled 1:1 decode suggests the texel half is right for point sampling; a bilinear texel-centre check is still worth a d3dprobe case (inferred).
- Max Payne has no frame on a fixed build.
- vendor-12's other points (aspect ratios above 8:1, which 3dfx stores as 8:1) are in G88.

gaps.title: Glide/OpenGL titles keep dormant Direct3D renderers that have never been exercised on .124
No hardware T&L or shaders: every D3D8/9 title uses software vertex processing on the Athlon XP
Cube maps, volume textures, DOT3, BUMPENVMAP(LUMINANCE) and PREMODULATE are impossible on the VSA-100
evidence: UT2004/System/D3DDrv.dll strings 'D3D Device: not using cubemaps'
BF1942.exe strings 'makeNormalizedHalfVectorCubeMap() Failed to create cubemap'
LIB/HiddenAndDangerous/Bin/i3d2.dll strings ('cannot find bumpmap texture format')

gaps.title: Anisotropic filtering is impossible: one bilinear footprint per TMU per pixel
gaps.description:
textureMode bits 1 and 2 choose only point or bilinear for minification and magnification, and tDetail adds only separate RGB and alpha filter selects. 3dfx reported MaxAnisotropy 1 with a dummy ANISOTROPY render-state handler, and its matrix and architecture spec both say No. Our dwMaxAnisotropy of 1 is correct.

Mitigation:
- Thief II's staged tex_filter_mode 16 (16x anisotropic) falls back (G65);
- a negative LOD bias (G27) is the only substitute: sharper, but aliased (inferred).

gaps.title: Border-colour addressing and cylindrical wrap (WRAP0-7) have no hardware; BORDER currently falls through to WRAP
gaps.description:
Border colour: textureMode's clamp forces S into [0, width) and T into [0, height), which samples the edge texel, and the TMU register set has no border colour. 3dfx commented BORDER out of its caps, and its matrix and architecture spec say 'Border Color: No'. Padding a border ring into the texture is only an approximation (inferred).

Today D3DTADDRESS_BORDER falls through to WRAP (vcrdd_d3d.c:792-795), and BORDERCOLOR is stored but never read. CLAMP would be the closer fallback (inferred).

D3DRENDERSTATE_WRAP0-7 (cylindrical wrapping) is stored and never read; there is no hardware support (inferred).

Keep D3DPTADDRESSCAPS_BORDER off.

gaps.title: AGP (non-local) texturing is impossible: the texture base is a local 26-bit address, and the 6000's chips sit on PCI-66 behind a bridge
Texture size limits: 2048x2048 maximum (TBIG), aspect ratio up to 8:1, power of two only, base 16-byte aligned
Texture repeat range is bounded by the 14.18 S/T iterators (about +/-32 repeats at our 256-texel scaling), and dwMaxTextureRepeat is reported as 0
gaps.description:
S/W and T/W iterate as 14.18 fixed point, and VcrDd3dTexScale scales the wider side to 256 texels (vcrdd_3d.c:273-287, verified). That leaves roughly +/-32 repeats before the integer part wraps (inferred arithmetic). Large tiled floors that repeat further would swim. The standard remedy is to re-base each triangle's integer texture offset on the host (inferred).

dwMaxTextureRepeat is never set, so it is reported as 0 (hal-26).

The sources disagree on 3dfx's value: hal-26 says 32768, hw-28 says 256 with TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE. Both are in D3INIT.C, chosen by TEXTURE_REPEAT_NOT_SCALED. DDFXNT95.H:70 defines it as 1, so the W2K build reported 256 with TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE (checked); hw-28 is right.

gaps.title: Stipple: only a 4x8 pattern or a rotate mode; D3D's 32x32 STIPPLEPATTERN and STIPPLEDALPHA cannot be expressed exactly
gaps.description:
fbzMode[2] enables stipple masking, and fbzMode[12] chooses either a rotating 32-bit register or a 4x8 monochrome pattern indexed by x[2:0] and y[1:0].

D3DRENDERSTATE_STIPPLEDALPHA is stored but never read. It could be approximated (inferred), and 3dfx's handler for it was a dummy. These titles rarely use stipple (inferred).

Keep D3DPRASTERCAPS_STIPPLE off.

gaps.title: BLENDOP (subtract/reverse subtract) and per-channel COLORWRITEENABLE exist in silicon, but it is unknown whether a DX7-DDI driver can expose them; MIN/MAX blend ops are impossible
gaps.description:
Hardware (checked in VINC/H3DEFS.H):
- fogMode bits 8-11 are SST_RGB_BLEND_REVERSE, SST_RGB_BLEND_SUB, SST_A_BLEND_REVERSE and SST_A_BLEND_SUB, giving (S*a)+(D*b), (S*a)-(D*b) and (D*b)-(S*a). There is no MIN or MAX.
- alphaMode bits 16-23 hold separate alpha source and destination factors, at 32 bpp.
- renderMode bits 17-20 are R/G/B/A write enables, used only at 32 bpp under fbzMode[9]. At 15/16 bpp only the masks 0x0 and 0xF can be honoured. PLANEMASK is impossible.

Disagreement:
- hal-35 lists BLENDOP and separate alpha blend as hardware limits. The register fields above show that is only partly right: only MIN/MAX are impossible.
- Whether these can reach a game through our DX7 DDI is unresolved. hal-34 infers that the D3D8 runtime reads COLORWRITEENABLE from the DX7 misc caps; vendor-21 infers that neither is reachable without a DX8 DDI (3dfx's DX8 caps left both commented out). Both views are inferred.
- D3D9 separate alpha blend is likewise unreachable through this DDI (inferred).

Today PrimitiveMiscCaps is 0x72, and no blend op is exposed. Halo carries a MinMaxBlendOpIsBroken flag.

Settle it with a d3dprobe caps check after setting the misc-cap bits in a test build (it is not known whether 16 bpp really ignores renderMode[19:17]; hw-41 check 5). Low priority.
gaps.hw: partial (subtract ops and 32 bpp channel masks; no MIN/MAX)

gaps.title: Projected texture coordinates (TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS PROJECTED) are dropped; per-TMU 1/W may make them possible, but this is unverified
gaps.description:
Ours: vertex() uses u and v only (vcrdd_3d.c:211-222), so projected coordinates are wrong. TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS is stored and never read. UE2's projectors (SetProjectorMaterial) would misproject (inferred).

Hardware: each TMU divides by its own 1/W (sWtmu0, sWtmu1), and textureMode's tclampw exists 'when projecting textures to avoid projecting behind the source of the projection'. Sending q*rhw as a TMU's W, with s*rhw and t*rhw as S and T, would give per-pixel s/q and t/q (inferred). 3dfx did not offer PROJECTED.

Caveat from the vendor reference: 3dfx's NT DP2 parsers store TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS into ADDRESSU/V, a bug fixed in the Win9x tree (G95). Do not copy it.

Verify with a d3dprobe quad where q != 1, against a CPU reference (hw-41 check 6).

gaps.title: 1555 render targets (A1R5G5B5/X1R5G5B5) are native, but not offered
gaps.description:
renderMode[1:0]=1 renders ARGB1555, and renderMode[16:15] chooses the stored alpha bit: always 0, always 1, or the MSB of the blended alpha. The 1-bit alpha shares the RGB write enable and FASTFILL with the colour planes, and destination alpha is automatic.

vcr_rt_format accepts only 565 and 8888 targets.

Low priority. It matters mainly for render-target textures (G36); which titles would choose a 1555 target is unknown.

gaps.title: DDI level: vcrdd is a DX7 (DP2EX, non-T&L) driver to D3D8/9, which works; a DX8-level DDI would add A8 textures, X8R8G8B8 render-target textures and Caps2 at a high cost
evidence: XPRT/d3d8.dll 0x6d9e8c05-0x6d9e8c32; XPRT/d3d9.dll strings 'Cannot convert vertex declaration for dx8 driver'

gaps.title: Reference-source caveats: vendor HAL bugs, guesses and per-app workarounds not to copy, and stale passages in 3dfx's own spec
gaps.description:
The 3dfx H5 source and docs are the guidance for most fixes above, and they contain material that must not be copied.

Vendor driver bugs (do not copy):
- vendor-31: all three NT DP2 texture-stage parsers store TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS into ADDRESSU/V, so a DX7 title that sets transform flags loses its wrap/clamp on 3dfx's NT driver. Win9x revision 100 fixed it.
- vendor-15: 3dfx's Z-bias shift follows the primary's depth, not the Z's.
- vendor-08: stage 0's MAXMIPLEVEL is used for both TMUs (an admitted bug).
- vendor-19: the advertised DESTALPHA/INVDESTALPHA/SRCALPHASAT were substituted with ONE/ZERO on every draw (PRS 8373).
- vendor-22: NT line geometry spans y-1..y; Win9x moved it to -0.5..+0.5 for WHQL.

Vendor guesses and caps errors:
- vendor-32: Z_ACCESS_OPT counts flips without a Z clear and changes DdLock/HandleSLIAA behaviour; it guesses the app's clear pattern. Do not copy.
- vendor-33: ZTEST is commented out of the caps though every Z function works; MIPMAPLODBIAS is implemented but never advertised; dvMaxVertexW is never assigned; DESTALPHA/INVDESTALPHA/SRCALPHASAT are advertised but substituted. In the DX8 path Caps2 is never assigned, LineCaps is 0 and MaxPointSize 1. Our caps should follow what we render.
- vendor-41: ANTIALIASSORTINDEPENDENT is delivered as SLI/AA full-scene AA (DDSCAPS2_HINTANTIALIASING); EDGEANTIALIAS is a no-op and stippled alpha a dummy. Keep the AA caps off, since the user chose no AA; our RasterCaps 00100191 already carry no AA bit.

Per-app workarounds (vendor-34): Unreal palette (PRS 14371); UT's 3-stage remap (PRS 12099, Voodoo3 only); 3DMark 2000; Armor Command ENALPHAMASK; Homeworld; F-22 Lightning 3 MAXMIPLEVEL; Centipede fog; Hidden & Dangerous clip init (PRS 12728); SpeedBusters chromaRange init; Redline Racer, G-Police, Heavy Gear II; Forsaken format order; MDK lines; Quake III via the MS wrapper. None is known to be needed now: Unreal Gold and UT 436 use Glide on .124, and H&D Deluxe is a later D3D8 engine.

Use the Win9x tree where the trees differ (vendor-35). It holds later fixes: the TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS clobber (rev 100); keeping zEnable/zWriteEnable until a Z is attached (rev 109); lines at -0.5..+0.5 (rev 9); two-pass untextured specular (rev 8, SPECULARFIX); the LOD-dither chip mask (rev 108).

Spec caveats (hw-40):
- SPEC section 3.3 calls itself 'horribly out-of-date' and is wrong on two-pass trilinear (L554), destination alpha without depth (L573) and a palette offset register (L567).
- Section 8.22's fog-bit precedence conflicts with 3dfx's code (G32).
- SWARCH's DX7 table is from the planning stage ('no LOD bias').
- D3DXLS row 147 says AGP texture memory Yes, contradicting the register spec (G87).
- From chapter 12 on, the body's chapter numbers are one higher than the table of contents.
evidence: VH5/DDFXNT.H:68-76; VH5/DDFLIP.C:183-220; VH5/D3RSTATE.C:1311-1328; VH5/DDSURF.C:1554-1573; VH5/D6DP2.C:5402-5457; VH5/DDINIT.C:886-895

gaps.title: Library titles not on .124 that have D3D paths: Wing Commander Prophecy, Rogue Squadron and Die by the Sword are Win9x-only
gaps.description:
WCProphecy (GL_00005/GL_00006.DLL import DDRAW), Rogue Squadron (Rogue Squadron.EXE imports DDRAW) and Die by the Sword (rld3d.dll) are all max_os win9x and staged for the Voodoo 2 box; the compat DB shows them absent on .124.

Their DX5/6 D3D paths matter only if one is re-staged for XP. They would then need the same execute-buffer, colour-key and 16-bit texture handling as Jedi Knight (inferred; G08, G09).

gaps.title: Not a driver defect: Jedi Knight's and MotS's 3D view sits top-aligned

gaps.notes:
I merged 284 findings from nine agents (hal 36, vendor 41, hw 41, games 39, history 50, perf 18, runtime 27, visual 17, onbox 15) into 97 gaps. Every finding id appears in at least one gap's sources; I checked that with a script. Each sources entry is a finding id, so its prefix names the agent. The full reports are in KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/reports/<source>.md.

PATH LEGEND for the evidence strings:
- WT = /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench
- KMD = WT/voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd
- EV = KMD/evidence; P1112 = EV/d3dplan_1112; ONBOX = P1112/onbox; REP = P1112/reports
- SWP = EV/d3dtune_1014 (sweep_baseline, sweep_1108, sweep_1108_fixed); LAN = EV/lan_20260929_sweep
- RES = WT/scripts/benchmarks/results/v56k_lan_192.168.1.124; PLAN = WT/docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md
- GL5 = WT/voodoo-cleanroom/build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5 (glide3/src, minihwc, incsrc); GBK = WT/scripts/3dfx/driver/nt (gbk)
- R3 = /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx; FIND = R3/FINDINGS.md
- VH5 = R3/3dfx Driver Code/H5/W2K/Src/Video/Displays/H5; W9X = R3/3dfx Driver Code/H5/Win9x/DX/D3D; VINC = R3/3dfx Driver Code/H5/INCLUDE (H3DEFS.H, H3REGS.H)
- SPEC = R3/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc (line numbers are strings-extracted text lines); SWARCH = DOCS/SW Architecture Spec.doc; D3DXLS = DOCS/D3D.XLS; PSEXT = DOCS/PS_Napalm_External v.1.06.pdf
- LIB = /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library; XEV = ~/.retro-fleet/evidence (full-size frames on the dev host)
- XPRT, DDK8, W2KDDK as defined in REP/runtime.md (XP SP3 d3d8/d3d9 disassembly; DX8 DDK headers; W2K DDK sample and docs)

CHECKED IN CODE OR FILES BY ME:
- blend_src/blend_dst map SRCCOLOR-as-source and DESTCOLOR-as-destination to BF_ONE, with 'chip cannot' comments (vcrdd_d3d.c:643, 661).
- ARG_KIND masks the argument modifiers (:671).
- MODULATE2X falls to MODULATE (:714) and to TM_TC_MULT (:862).
- TFACTOR becomes 'other' only without a texture; c0 = 0 and c1 = TFACTOR (:700-716, 1019-1020).
- FZ_DITHER is set at every depth (:979-980); depth is enabled only for D3DZB_TRUE (:986); alpha always blends ONE/ZERO (:998).
- ctx_defaults sets POINT/MODULATE/WRAP for stage 0 (:1138-1146); set_rs maps only TEXTUREHANDLE (:1393-1406); STATESET is skipped (:1562).
- Lines and points are skipped (:1690-1715) while LineCaps = TriCaps (:2072); TRANSPARENCY is advertised (:2035).
- ValidateTextureStageState always returns 1/DD_OK (:1905-1910); the guard band is discarded (:2161); MaxTextureRepeat is unset.
- DP2 and Clear2 skip draws, yet return DD_OK, when g2d_ok is clear (:1859, 1887).
- The mip allocators pack only the levels of one CreateSurface call (:420-460, 547-583). VcrDdD3dTexWritten is called only from Unlock and TEXBLT.
- DDraw caps are BLT|BLTCOLORFILL|READSCANLINE, and dwVidMemFree is constant (vcrdd_ddraw.c:101-110).
- vertex() reads status per vertex and writes float colour plus sOow1 (vcrdd_3d.c:183-221). The miniport resets only a busy chip, and Reset3D refuses with the FIFO on.
- H3DEFS.H fogMode bits 8-11 give blend subtract/reverse, and alphaMode bits 16-23 give separate alpha factors. h5 Glide clears dither at 32 bpp.
- 3dfx's colour-key history: revision 4 removed TRANSPARENCY for Napalm, revision 17 re-enabled it for WHQL, and an FBI-only key is implemented (D3INIT.C, D6DP2.C:6943).
- DDFXNT95.H:70 defines TEXTURE_REPEAT_NOT_SCALED, so the vendor's dwMaxTextureRepeat is 256.
- Both staged UE2 D3DDrv.dll files contain 'D3D Detected: 3dfx video card'. The UT2003 ini sets MenuViewport to 640x480.
- On-box rings show 'mipmap chain ... 1 levels' per call, and the repo test docstring records seven CreateSurface calls per 64x64 texture.
- RES/day/fbshots/mots_game.png at native size shows point-sampled texels on a magnified wall.

DISPUTES AND HOW I RESOLVED THEM (details in each gap):
1. MotS filtering (G08). games-20/21 say MotS is bilinear and JK's point sampling is its own option; visual-06 says both are point-sampled. visual-06 is supported by the image and the code.
2. In-game block-noise mechanism (G06/G07). hal-23 proposes the FOURCC-mismatch fallback; runtime-12 proposes per-level allocation. The code supports runtime-12's mechanism, and hal-23's specific fallback cannot trigger with one level per call. The untested multi-level DXT chains remain.
3. A8 textures (G34). hal-21, hw-26 and vendor-11 say it can be added; runtime-07's disassembly says the DX7-DDI converter has no DDPF_ALPHA case. runtime-07 is the stronger evidence.
4. BLENDOP and separate alpha (G91, G28). hal-35 calls both hardware limits. The register header shows subtract/reverse-subtract and separate alpha factors exist; only MIN/MAX and DX7-DDI reachability are limits. hal-35 is partly wrong. COLORWRITEENABLE reachability is unresolved: hal-34 says the misc caps may carry it, vendor-21 says it needs a DX8 DDI; both are inferred.
5. STATESET exposure (G40). hal-07 names D3D8 titles; runtime-19's disassembly shows D3D8/9 emulate state blocks for our DDI type, which limits the risk to DX7-interface titles.
6. MaxTextureRepeat at 3dfx (G89). hal-26 says 32768, hw-28 says 256. The compiled W2K value is 256, so hw-28 is right.
7. Red Faction's 09-29 black frame (G68). history-34 blames focus, visual-05 blames a preceding Glide session; I add the stale-FIFO mechanism as a third possibility. None is proven.
8. UE2 at 16 bpp (G19). runtime-26 suggests a 3dfx vendor path; visual-08 suggests the D16@32 lead. The DLL string supports a vendor-keyed path, and no refused 32 bpp context appears in the ring.
9. Halo's API. games reports D3D9, hal says D3D8; G67 uses games' D3D9 and notes both.
10. Colour key at 3dfx (G09). history-17's 'Napalm doesn't support texture chroma key' and vendor-23's FBI implementation are both true, at different revisions.

FINDINGS JUDGED WRONG OR SUPERSEDED (kept, with reasons):
- The brief says only menus were captured. history-07 corrects it: in-game frames exist for JK, MotS and Thief II (G73).
- The vintage lane's 'a DX=7 build means no D3D8 hardware' is wrong in general (runtime-01, G94).
- hal-35's BLENDOP and separate-alpha limits are partly wrong (see dispute 4).
- hal-26's '3dfx reported 32768' is the uncompiled branch.
- visual-12 attributed Halo's flat squares to the alignment bug, but today's frame on the fixed build shows the class persists (G17).
- games-21's 'MotS bilinear' and games-20's 'JK's own option' are not supported.
- hal-23's FOURCC fallback as the noise cause is unlikely (dispute 2).
- games-03 implies UE2 needs 32 bpp targets, but UE2 runs at 16 bpp on this PCI id. Its hard dependency is D3DBigTex (G20, G19).
- history-36 ('Halo menu only') and perf-14 ('no D3D game fps exists') are superseded by today's on-box timedemo frames and UT2003's 9.41 fps (G67, G46).

G01.approach:
The gap is real, fixable and P0. The fix is a stale-FIFO guard behind Diag\D3DSafe bit 0. It turns a Glide command FIFO off once its owner is provably gone, and reuses the already-proven VcrHwResetEngine (stop fetch, command-stream reset, GRX + FBI-FIFO + 2D reset, bounded idle wait; on silicon at 10:12 it went 0xa5f -> 0x5f, then 40/40, 42/42, 40/40).

**Correction to the proposed fix.** The display reset (IOCTL_VIDEO_RESET_DEVICE, 'SLI/AA off: display reset') is the WRONG trigger. It is also what an alt-tab or console switch away from a live fullscreen Glide game produces (vcrmp.c:677-695; the GLQuake case in FINDINGS). At that moment pid 1892 still held its 14 views; it released them 0.9 s later at 75346.471. The first provable 'orphaned' moment is the owner's unmap, or its exit without one.

**Three new facts from the evidence:**
- An enabled FIFO alone kills PIO triangles. In the fullscreen failure every surface was outside the window (0x300000/0x600000/0x900000). In the windowed run, flat and gouraud failed before the first texture reached 0xc0000.
- aMax 0xe000c, about 0xc0000 + 128 KB, is consistent with host texture writes being counted by the FIFO's hole logic. That is the escalation mechanism (inferred).
- The ring's close signature (display reset first, no HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE) matches FINDINGS' GLQuake 'mode dropped under a live Glide stream' as well as hwcRestoreVideo's not-idle path, which would still log a release. The fix therefore must not depend on which Glide path ran. Glide's close idle wait ORs all 4 chips' status, so a not-idle SLI close is plausibly common.

**Pure decision header.** New include/vcr_fifoguard.h (Win32-free) holds:
- the cmdFifo0/1 offsets (0x80020 + 0x30n, baseSize [7:0] pages-1, bit 8 EN);
- the window and overlap math;
- vcr_fifo_guard(armed, bs0, bs1, live_owners, sli_chips): NOTHING if both FIFOs are off, else UNARMED / OWNED / SLI / RESET;
- vcr_fifo_stall_recoverable (CMD0/CMD1 busy, capped at 3 per PDEV);
- vcr_fifo_quiet (FBI/TMU/2D idle with CMD bits ignored).

**Miniport (device-scope ownership, which FINDINGS asks for).**
- The existing x->procs Glide mapping table plus a liveness check that never dereferences the stored EPROCESS: PsLookupProcessByProcessId, same object, same create time, PsGetProcessExitStatus == STATUS_PENDING, then ObfDereferenceObject. All are in tools/xp_exports. Dead slots are forgotten and logged.
- VcrFifoGuard reads chip 0's FIFO, status and slaves' baseSize, decides, and on RESET calls VcrHwResetEngine(x, 0, ...). It logs event 309.
- New IOCTL_VCR_FIFO_GUARD (0xa10) and VCR_ESC_FIFO, with QUERY and GUARD ops.

**Trigger points.**
- (A) Unmap: in the display DLL after IOCTL_VCR_UNMAP_GLIDE in the HWCEXT UNMAP_MEMORY case. This catches today's case 0.9 s after the close.
- (B) Mode set: in voodoo_program, only in an else-branch after the unchanged busy reset. VcrSliOff has already run there. This covers killed clients and every fullscreen D3D/DDraw title.
- (C) D3d_ContextCreate: a stale FIFO is reset; a live owner, live SLI or a failed reset gets DDERR_SURFACEBUSY with log 513/24 instead of a silent no-draw.
- (C') DP2/Clear2 drawable term: one baseSize read per call when armed.
- (D) give_up() cold path: a CMD-busy stall on an ownerless FIFO is reset and acceleration is kept, instead of losing 2D and the D3D HAL until a mode set. VcrDdRoom and VcrDd2dSync text stays unchanged.
- Before (A)/(C)/(C'): a bounded 2D quiesce.
- After any reset: fog_valid = 0, re-learn g2d_fifo_full, and a global reset generation that makes prepare() re-send target and state.

**Deliberately not done:**
- no reset at RESET_DEVICE, DrvAssertMode, the timer or HwResetHw;
- no reset with a live mapping or live SLI;
- slaves are only read;
- Reset3D is untouched (that is G03).

**Optional, separable.** Diag\DdHeapFloor=2 starts the DirectDraw heap at 0x117000, past Glide's default Napalm FIFO (96 KB + 0xff000). That closes live-FIFO coexistence and G63's offset-0 loss.

**Tooling.**
- `vcrctl fifo [--guard]`.
- d3dprobe records cmdfifo before/after in every RESULT.
- d3dprobe_run.py flags STALE COMMAND FIFO runs instead of reporting 9/40.

**Forward requirement.** G47's own CMDFIFO must arm through this guard and register itself as an owner.

Caps do not change, there is no multipass, and the old path is unchanged when the switch is off.

G01.risk:
**Default 16 bpp path and every unarmed path: no change.** Call sites are guarded, there is no new register access, and the tests pin both.

**Armed, normal case (FIFO off).**
- Two MMIO reads at ContextCreate and unmap, and one per DP2/Clear2 call, about 1 µs each. That is about 0.02% of a UT2003 frame.
- One compare per triangle in prepare().

**Glide/OpenGL coexistence.**
- Never resets under a live mapping or live SLI.
- The residual risk is a false 'dead' verdict on a live Glide process, which would reset its stream. It is mitigated by the strict liveness test (same EPROCESS object, same create time, exit status pending), every forgotten slot being logged, and session 2 step 6.
- Behaviour change: a D3D game launched while a Glide program still holds the board now fails CreateDevice visibly, where today it drew nothing. That refusal costs the runtime's two mode switches (G11), which is rare.

**SLI state.**
- The guard refuses while sli_chips != 0.
- The reset is the same chip-0 VcrHwResetEngine the mode set already uses; slaves are only read.
- The display reset path is untouched, so an alt-tabbed SLI Glide game is not hit.

**Flip path.** VcrHwResetEngine does not reset the video unit, so scan-out and a latched flip continue. A reset in the middle of a session drops that frame's queued 3D work, and the HAL re-sends target and state via the reset generation.

**2D.** A reset can abort at most one in-flight GDI op. The bounded quiesce (CMD bits ignored) makes that unlikely, and the 2D code rewrites its full state on every op.

**Kernel code risk.** New ntoskrnl imports, which are verified present in the XP SP3 export lists. They are PASSIVE_LEVEL-only callers, and a test pins their absence from timer and reset paths.

G07.approach:
REAL and FIXABLE. The hardware is fine: VSA-100 single-base mode wants every level packed byte-exact after the top (SPEC §20 L6083-6089, texel = texbaseaddr + lod_offset + s + t*w). The fault is our allocation.

Three verified defects:
(1) SCATTER. XP sends one CreateSurface per level (dwSCnt 1; measured 7 calls for a 64x64 D3D8 texture). mipchain_ext (vcrdd_d3d.c:367-466) and VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain (:522-584) size and allocate a block per call (levels = 1) and mark each call's surface MIP_TOP. tex_view/tex_view_ext (:779-787, :814-824) then set tLOD LODMAX over every attached level, and nothing checks that a level sits at top + chain_offset(k). On a first-fit heap with holes (any game), small levels land in earlier holes and the TMU samples foreign memory below the split. That matches the minified-only block noise in UT2003/UT2004/Halo.
(2) PADDING, even on a fresh heap. Per-level blocks start 16-aligned, but an R5G6B5 2x2 level is 8 bytes, so the 1x1 level sits 8 bytes past where the TMU reads it. 3dfx removed per-level 16-byte alignment in 1999: "fixes … DCT250 mip filter tests", VH5/D3TXTR.C header rev 7.
(3) ADJACENT. A 16 bpp texture whose top is 1x1, placed 16-aligned, is sampled 8 bytes early: the absent levels sum to 0x2AAA8 and texBaseAddr drops bits 3:0. 3dfx places such a texture +8 in its block (initMipMapChain).

DESIGN: new Diag\D3DMipChain (DWORD, absent 0), read at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO like DdHeapFloor, giving positive flags VCR_INFO_F_MIPGUARD 0x8000 and VCR_INFO_F_MIPWHOLE 0x10000, copied to pd->mip_guard/mip_whole.

(0) Log-only, default ON. Events 513/11 and 513/20 add dwSCnt, the descriptor's w/h and mipcount, the surface's lpSurfMore->dwMipMapCount and whether lpAttachListFrom is set. tex_view* always compute the in-place prefix. compute_regs counts split-chain binds (shallow ≤3 / deep ≥4), logs the first 8 per context at WARN, and adds a 'context N mip' summary.

(1) Bit 0, the GUARD. New pure vcr_tex_chain_contig(kind,w0,h0,at[],pitch[],have) in vcr_texlod.[ch] returns the levels whose fpVidMem equals top + vcr_tex_chain_offset(k) and whose pitch is the TMU's. Under mip_guard, LODMAX = top + min(attached, contig) - 1. Only tLOD bits 11:6 change, only downward, and only for split chains: the registers for an in-place chain are byte-identical.

(2) Bit 1, WHOLE CHAINS = option A, as 3dfx's NT5 HAL did (DDFXNT.C:1224-1248):
- DdGetDriverInfo answers GUID_NTPrivateDriverCaps (fad16a23) with DDHAL_PRIVATECAP_ATOMICSURFACECREATION, never NOTIFYPRIMARYCREATION, and only when the D3D half is up. dxg then passes the whole chain in one call and the existing loops pack it as one block.
- New pure vcr_tex_call_levels() picks the LARGEST surface as the top (identical for dwSCnt 1) and refuses duplicates and non-halvings.
- vcr_tex_chain_pad() gives +8 for an RGB16 1x1 top, recorded as SF_PAD8; FreeMipChain frees fpVidMem-pad.
- Calls that still arrive per level (Restore) keep today's path, covered by bit 0.
No caps change: DDSCAPS_MIPMAP is already advertised.

OLD PATH (switch absent): GUID unanswered, per-call allocation and LODMAX exactly as today. Only log text and counters are added.

FALLBACK B, built only if boot C shows dwSCnt still 1 or a flip/2D regression: a descriptor-matched whole-chain reservation at the top level's call with a pending record, placing later per-level calls.

REJECTED:
- repacking at CreateSurfaceEx: it moves fpVidMem after dxg has returned the surfaces;
- tmultibaseaddr: LODs 3-8 must still be contiguous, it costs 3 more TMU writes per bind, and its TBIG behaviour is undocumented.

G07.d3dprobe_test:
All tests are explicit, never in the default list.

Common rules:
- Each level is one solid colour from a 12-entry table: distinct, 565/DXT-exact within 12, never black, white, grey or the poison 0x804020.
- Level L is drawn with POINT min/mag/mip at texel:pixel 2^(L+0.26) (floor and round agree, as in mip2048), on a quad centred at (128,128).
- The quad is W = min(192, 16*S/r) px wide, with UV extent ≤16 wraps to stay inside the 14.18 iterators. The centre pixel is read.
- Each probe is classed ok (within 12 of level L's colour), clamped (within 12 of the top's colour) or foreign. The JSON adds levels_ok, levels_clamped and levels_foreign.
- A format or size the HAL does not offer is SKIPPED.

LAYOUT MODEL (fresh heap, MANAGED, LockRect):
- mipdeep (64x64 R5G6B5, levels 0-6): pass = all ok. Today's expectation: L0-5 ok, and L6 foreign if the next block starts on the next 16 bytes. That is the first silicon measurement of the padding claim.
- mipdxt1 (256 DXT1, levels 0-5, the levels ≥8 wide): pass = all ok. TMU offsets 0, 0x8000, 0xA000, 0xA800, 0xAA00, 0xAA80. A failure here means the DXT layout model is wrong (a G06 candidate), not allocation.
- mipdxt5 (256 DXT5, levels 0-8): pass = all ok.
- mip8888 (256 A8R8G8B8, levels 0-8): pass = all ok.

ALLOCATION, fragmented heap: mipfrag (64 R5G6B5), mipfrag_dxt1, mipfrag_dxt5 and mipfrag_8888 (256).
- They run first, in their own invocation, with DEFAULT-pool textures filled by UpdateTexture (DP2 TEXBLT).
- Construction: S0 poison, H (≥ the sub-levels' sum and < the top: 64x32, 256x128 x3), S1 poison, T (exactly the top's size), P poison (≥ the whole chain: 128x64, 512x256 x3). Release H and T, then create the chain. Probe levels 0-4.
- Expected:
  - old path: the top lands in T's hole, its levels in H's, and the TMU reads them inside P → FOREIGN (the bug reproduced);
  - bit 0: CLAMPED, 0 foreign (the guard's verdict);
  - bit 1: the chain fits neither hole, is packed above P, and passes with ALL OK.
- The ring's 513/20 lines, which now carry dwSCnt, record where every level landed.

Optional: ddlab mipchain. A DX7 64x64 MIPMAP|COMPLEX texture is lost by one paced mode set and Restore()d, to see whether restore reaches CreateSurface per level.

STEP 1 - THE MODIFIER PASS INSIDE G12'S WIN32-FREE COMPILER (include/vcr_xcomb.h):

COMPLEMENT (exact rules; 3dfx used the same XOR masks, VH5/D6MT.C:504-516 and :4535-4583):
- OTHER: invert_other ^= 2 (bits [10:9], alpha [22:21]). Only from base x or 1-x; base 0-x or x-1/2 refuses.
- LOCAL in the subtract position: invert_local ^= 3 ([12:11], [24:23]). Only from base x or 1-x.
- LOCAL in the add position: invert_add_local ^= 1 (bit 13, alpha 25).
- Multiplier (M/M7): toggle REVERSE_BLEND. That is fbzColorPath bit 13/22 in the FBI, textureMode bit 17/26 in a TMU.
- This rule reproduces exactly SWARCH's "complement of arg2 unsupported" list: ADDSIGNED, ADDSIGNED2X, SUBTRACT, BLENDTEXTURE/FACTOR/CURRENTALPHA. BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA is refused too, as in the shipped table.

ALPHAREPLICATE on colour arguments only (each select lists an RGB source, then its alpha; VH5/D6MT.C:4596-4639, :5092-5160, :5252-5320):
- FBI otherselect +4, localselect +3, mselect_7 +2;
- FBI fbzColorPath MRGBTMU(5) -> MATMU(4);
- TMU otherselect, localselect and mselect_7 +1, the last only from IRGB or CR_RGB.

THE TMU M7 TEXTURE CASE (no alpha twin; 3dfx's MALOCAL/MAOTHER fallback has disputed semantics):
1. For a commutative op (MODULATE, 2X, 4X), swap the arguments so the replicated texture sits on OTHER (OTHER_TA/LOCAL_TA).
2. Otherwise use textureMode tc_mselect MALOCAL/MAOTHER only if the same TMU's alpha unit already selects that texture's alpha on the matching mux. Both readings of the semantics then agree.
3. Otherwise refuse.

- DIFFUSE or TFACTOR modifiers inside a TMU until G58 and G14 land.

G11.approach:
VERDICT. The gap is real and fixable, but the cure is not pacing at the mode set. It is a contract between the caps and ContextCreate. The D3D8 runtime sets the fullscreen mode before it creates and checks the depth buffer and before it calls our ContextCreate, so whatever fails at those steps reaches the monitor. Full design: KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G11.md.

NEW FACTS (measured):
(1) It is four timing changes in about 170 ms, not two. Every vcr-kmd mode change goes DrvAssertMode(FALSE) -> IOCTL_VIDEO_RESET_DEVICE -> VcrHwResetToVga (vcrdd.c:570-614, vcrmp.c:677-695; FINDINGS 2026-09-26). On 11-12 that was 91.1 -> 31.5 -> 43.3 -> 31.5 -> 91.1 kHz: 640x480x32 dwelt 109 ms, refusal 513/12 at 83009.956 s, revert at 83009.971 s (ring_after_probe_i_decoded.txt lines 24-105).
(2) The runtime's OWN depth-format refusal also comes after its mode set. On 86Box e7 (Voodoo3, 640x480x16 + D24S8) pid 1144 set mode 75, created the primary chain, never created a Z or called ContextCreate, and restored mode 80 321 ms later, with no driver refusal (E86 e7 vcrlog seq 3934-3991). Only back-buffer-format and no-HAL refusals are decided before the switch (86Box e3/e5: exclusive 1 -> 0 with no MODESET; .124 10:11 run). So dropping D16 from the Z list would not help: 4a9793b did that and broke the proven 16 bpp fullscreen lane, and e7 shows the runtime flaps anyway. The only flap-free rule is: every (back buffer, Z) pair the runtime accepts must draw.
(3) Two of the three ContextCreate refusals are silent: all MAX_CTX=32 contexts in use, and no FPU save area. Both return DDERR_OUTOFMEMORY unlogged (vcrdd_d3d.c:1170-1173, 1178-1181).

Reachability. After the runtime's mode set, the only ContextCreate refusal a game can reach is 513/12 for X8R8G8B8/A8R8G8B8 + D16, which the runtime matches (caps_124 zmatch 1/1, also on 09-28). 513/17 and 513/15 cannot be reached for listed modes: every vcr_timings width is a multiple of 8, and the automatic Z has the back buffer's size and pitch. CreateSurfaceEx never refuses.

APPROACH.
(A) THE CONTRACT. G10 removes the refusal, preferably the vendor's way (VH5/DDSURF.C:592-626): a 16-bit Z requested while the primary is 32 bpp gets 32-bit storage, so surf_zbits reads 32 and the existing 32/32 rule draws it. For any D3D8/9 CreateDevice the primary depth equals the back-buffer depth, since fullscreen sets the mode before creating the Z. 3dfx also dropped its own ContextCreate mismatch error (D3CONTXT.C rev 12, 2000-04-06). Caps stay unchanged: D16 stays listed at every desktop. This item pins the contract in a host matrix test: offered render depths x the vcr_rt_zlist Z formats x the runtime's MEASURED matching table x every vcr_timings mode.
(B) LOUD REFUSALS, failure path only. Log the two silent refusals as WARN 513 what 24: b=1 no free context, c=MAX_CTX; b=2 no FPU area, c=bytes; d=pid. When the render target is a flip chain (DDSCAPS_FLIP; the D3D8 fullscreen back buffer carries 0x1000601c), add a suffix to the 12/15/17/24 text: "fullscreen flip chain: its mode is already set, and the runtime will now restore the desktop - two mode changes on the monitor". The a..d fields keep their meaning. Append the what-24 text to the 513 description in vcr_events.h.
(C) TOOLS THAT REFUSE TO CAUSE RE-SYNCS, AND COUNT THEM.
 - d3dprobe caps gains zmatch.<bb>.<z>.hal: a hidden 64x64 WINDOWED device with that auto Z wherever the back buffer equals the desktop format, else null. match=1 with hal=0 is a FAIL. This exposes G10's bug with zero switches.
 - A fullscreen preflight() runs before vcr_pace_before_switch(). It is its own function, windowed only. It checks CheckDeviceFormat(DEPTHSTENCIL) (catches e7), CheckDepthStencilMatch, and the same-format windowed device (catches 11-12). A failure gives rc 3 with nothing switched. --expect-refusal is the only bypass.
 - A new render test, zpair (SETRENDERTARGET path).
 - d3dprobe_run.py: --expect-refusal requires --i-am-at-the-box and prints the switch plan; --pace defaults to 5000 for --full.
 - d3dprobe_run.py and lan_sweep.py read Diag\PhaseCount/PhaseLog (REGREAD) before and after a run. PhaseLog is 64 x {ms, code, a, b}, flushed at every phase, and survives ring wraps. Each RESULT gets mode_sets, timing_changes (2 per set), quick_resyncs (next set BEGIN < 5000 ms after the previous DONE), min_dwell_ms and reverts. More than 64 phases, or a reboot, gives "unknown", never 0. A quick revert with a refusal inside it fails the run; an app-driven re-set is recorded but does not fail. Example of the latter: the GL session's 1280x960 @60 then @85, 2.3 s apart, ring_start seq 23787/23924.
 - vcrphases.py gets mode_sets()/resyncs() and a --resyncs view.
(D) DOCS.
 - README 565-567 says "refused ... with no mode set". That is false fullscreen (e7). Also fix 474-477.
 - The vcr_rtfmt.h:187-191 comment calls the refusal free and expects the runtime to say no; the runtime says yes.
 - The test_vcr_kmd_d3dseq.c:299 premise ("safe").
 - The d3dprobe caps comment.
 - Also: the tests README rows, the plan status, and a FINDINGS entry.

NOT RECOMMENDED.

G14.approach:
The full design is at /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G14.md.

The gap is real, confirmed at e3056d1. color_path (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:676-745) always uses the iterated colour as the combine's "local". So any stage-0 op that pairs TFACTOR with the texture draws the diffuse colour in TFACTOR's place, in RGB and in alpha:
- MODULATE(TEXTURE,TFACTOR) draws texture x diffuse.
- ADD(TEXTURE,TFACTOR) draws texture + diffuse. That is WHITE when the FVF has no diffuse (vcrdd_3d.c:187).
- A TFACTOR alpha fade does not fade.
- compute_regs writes c0=0 and c1=TF (:1019-1020). CP_LOCAL_C0 and CP_ALOCAL_C0 are defined (vcr_3dregs.h:80-81) and never used.
- No TMU stage can see TFACTOR.

D3D has no cap for TFACTOR, so games never check it and never fall back. Every use is wrong today. The fix is single pass and changes no caps. It has two parts.

PART A: stage 0 on the FBI's LEGACY combine. No new register, no new write.
- The rule: in each two-argument branch of color_path (RGB and alpha), if the argument that is not "other" is TFACTOR, set fbzColorPath[4]=1 (cc_localselect = color0) and/or [6:5]=1 (cca_localselect = color0 alpha), and load c0 = TEXTUREFACTOR. SPEC L2737-2738 and L3489 define these selects; the HAL already writes c0 at every flush.
- c0 stays 0 for every other combination. c1 stays TF.
- One conflict, resolved as "never worse than today": when COLOROP is BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA (factor = a_local), the alpha path keeps the iterated local, and the conflict is counted for G15.
- 3dfx's own legacy D3D tables do exactly this:
  - VH5/D6MT.C singleStage_s0_colorOp :1046: every "Texture + Factor" entry uses SST_LOCALSELECT (MODULATE :1120/1123, ADD :1143/1146, BLENDTEXTUREALPHA :1206);
  - alphaOp :1270 uses SST_ALOCAL_C0 (:1344, :1367);
  - c0 = TF is loaded by the non-Napalm branch of D6DP2.C:7029-7036.
- The code:
  - color_path's body moves into a new Win32-free header include/vcr_d3dcomb.h as vcr_cc_stage0(...) -> {cp, c0_tfactor, tf_pair, conflict}. With the feature off it is today's function word for word.
  - color_path stays as a wrapper, so the existing PARMADJUST pin still holds.
  - compute_regs: r->c0 = c->c0_tf ? TF : 0.
  - Switch plumbing: Diag\D3DFeat bit TFACTOR (created if absent), read at boot by miniport/vcrmp.c, passed in an appended vcr_info.d3d_feat, copied to pd->d3d_feat in display/vcrdd_2d.c.
  - Part A is armed on any chip, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed can prove it first.
- What it fixes:
  - single-stage op(TEXTURE,TFACTOR) and op(TFACTOR,TEXTURE) for MODULATE, ADD, BLENDTEXTUREALPHA and BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA;
  - the alpha fade;
  - op(TF,TF);
  - the two-texture MODULATE chain (tex0*tex1*TF).
- What it leaves alone: ops drawn as MODULATE today (they get the right operand, the op stays G12/G05's) and BLEND* argument polarity (G12).

PART B: TFACTOR inside the TMUs. It is the TFACTOR column of G12's extended-combine tables. It is needed for:
- TFACTOR at stage 1 (BLENDFACTORALPHA, a stage-1 TFACTOR argument);
- stage 0 when two textures are bound and the op is not a MODULATE chain (ADD(TEX,TF) under a lightmap: the FBI fold is wrong);
- the texture-less tint stage.

Part B registers and selects:
- Both TMUs' chromaKey (0x134) and chromaRange (0x138) are loaded with TF through chip field 6 (V3D_TMU0+V3D_TMU1), never broadcast. FBI c0=c1=TF as before. This is 3dfx's flush, VH5/D6DP2.C:7014-7027.
- Selects:
  - TC_OTHERSELECT CR_RGB(6)/CR_A(7);
  - TC_LOCALSELECT CK_RGB(6)/CK_A(7);
  - tc_mselect=7 with TC_MSELECT_7 CR_RGB/CR_A;
  - TCA_OTHERSELECT CR_A(3), TCA_LOCALSELECT CK_A(3), tca_mselect 7 (chromaRange alpha);
  - extended FBI: C1_RGB/C0_RGB/MSELECT_7 C1.
- Both TMUs' combineMode keep bit 30 (DISABLE_CHROMA_SUBSTITUTION) whenever the extended combine is armed, used or not.

Part B write order and restore:
- Each flush writes the three combineModes FIRST, then the two chip-field-6 chroma writes, then c0/c1. A new vcr_3d_tmuconst_seq() in vcr_3dseq.h builds the sequence so the host test can pin it.
- Restore in ctx_free (only while the engine is ours): chroma := 0 on both TMUs, THEN TMU combineMode := 0.
- The reason: chromaRange[30:29]=3 under combineMode[30]=0 is texture chroma substitution (SPEC L3534, L3547). Those bits are TF alpha bits 6:5, so any TF alpha in 0x60-0x7f or 0xe0-0xff, including the default 0xffffffff, left in a TMU would turn substitution on for the next legacy-path or Glide client.
- Our h5 Glide does invalidate both TMUs' chroma at its default state (gsst.c:916-917 -> gtex.c:1015-1023), so the restore is defence in depth until proven otherwise.

Part B chip-field ownership: the TMU chroma registers are reserved for TFACTOR (VH5/D6DP2.C:6943). G09's texture colour key must use the FBI's chromaKey through chip field 1.

VENDOR-26 (re-upload TFACTOR after a FASTFILL) is already met by our architecture:
- the FASTFILL colour IS color1 (SPEC L3497);
- VcrDd3dClear writes c1 (:159), and clear_rects sets dirty (vcrdd_d3d.c:1419), so the next triangle re-sends everything.
- The design pins this (d3dprobe tfactor_clear plus a source test) so G53's register shadowing cannot lose it.

MEASURE FIRST (log only, default on, no register change):
- per-context counters tf_s0_tris, tf_tmu_tris and tf_conflicts (one compare per triangle, no per-draw VcrDd call);
- reported in one 513 what=24 event at ctx_free, which survives a wrapped ring;
- stage-1 arguments logged once per combination as 513 what=25.
They decide whether any staged title uses TFACTOR at all. The 11-12 rings wrapped before a single combine line survived.

PRIORITY P1: TFACTOR has no cap and no fallback; the item plausibly feeds Halo's glow square (G17, together with G13 ALPHAREPLICATE) and UE2's white sky (G18, ADD(TEX,TF) drawn as tex+white). Demote to P3 if boot 1's counters show no use.

G14.risk:
Default 16 bpp path:
- Bit off: unchanged. Every color_path input is compared exhaustively, and the refactor into a header is covered by the same test.
- Bit on: only TFACTOR-partner combinations change. None of the default 40/40 probe tests uses TFACTOR.
- The flush keeps the same eight FBI writes in the same order and the same VcrDdRoom(12); only the fbzColorPath and c0 values differ.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence:
- Part A: no new state is left behind. c0 and fbzColorPath are FBI state that Glide rewrites: c0/c1 together at its default state (gsst.c:912) and at every validation (distate.c:2467-2470).
- Part B: the real hazard. TF left in a TMU's chromaRange reads as texture chroma substitution as soon as that TMU's combineMode[30] is 0. This bites:
  - for any TF alpha in 0x60-0x7f or 0xe0-0xff, the default 0xffffffff included;
  - for a later legacy D3D path, or for a Glide client that does not rewrite TMU1's chroma.
- Part B mitigations:
  - write combineMode before chroma;
  - restore chroma=0 before combineMode=0 at ctx_free;
  - keep bit 30 set on both TMUs while armed;
  - Glide's own invalidation at its default state (gtex.c:1015-1023).
  The attended step-5 boot proves it.
- If G03's baseline writes chroma, it must follow the same order. G09 must key on the FBI through chip field 1, never broadcast.
- Part A's on-box proof needs a cold boot: a Glide-left FBI combineMode[31]=1 ignores fbzColorPath entirely (the general G03 problem).

SLI: none. D3D is chip 0 only, and the chip-field-6 writes stay inside chip 0's TMUs. A future D3D SLI (G51) replicates them by broadcast.

Flip and DirectDraw: none. FASTFILL's c1 handling is unchanged and now pinned.

Performance:
- Part A: zero extra writes.
- Part B: +2 PIO writes per flush.
- The counters cost one compare per triangle, with no logging on the draw path.
- Per-object TF changes already cost a full flush (G53).

G03.d3dprobe_test:
New explicit test 'residue' (KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c, run with --tests residue; not in the default list). It is one analytic frame in the 256x256 readback window: clear colour 0x000040, Z=1. Each check is named after the residue class that would break it:
- 'fbi combine': an untextured flat quad, diffuse 0x40a0e0, ZFUNC ALWAYS. Expect 40a0e0.
- 'tmu0 white/red/green/grey': a 64x64 R5G6B5 texture with four 32x32 cells (ffffff, ff0000, 00ff00, 808080), MODULATE x white diffuse, point sampled, 1:1. Expect each texel. This catches the TMU combine selects, TMU chroma substitution (any channel not ff is keyed under the hostile key) and 2PPC.
- 'tmu1 two-stage': stage 0 solid red, stage 1 MODULATE x solid grey 808080. Expect about 800000 (tol 16). 2PPC residue gives about 404040.
- 'depth pass' / 'depth reject': a yellow quad at z 0.25 LESSEQUAL with Z write, then a magenta quad at z 0.75 overlapping it. Expect yellow, then still yellow. This catches a stale stencil NEVER honoured at 16 bpp.
- 'row y' x24: a green band x 8..248, y 160..167, sampled at x 16/128/240 on every row. Catches SLI band residue and aaCtrl bit 30.
- 'cover' x5: a second frame with one quad over -0.5..255.5. The 4 corners and the centre must be drawn. Catches an aaCtrl primary offset or an enabled clip1.
Tolerance is 12 at 16 bpp and 8 at 32 bpp, against computed reference values.
PASS = 0 failed checks.
Three controls:
- On a clean chip it must pass at 16 and 32 bpp (the test's own control).
- After a hostile residue with bit 1 OFF, the named checks for that class must FAIL (the negative control, proving the test can fail).
- After the same residue with bit 1 ON: 0 failures.
d3dprobe cannot create Glide state, so a new glidelab mode 'residue' (cfg 0, one chip, 32 bpp with a 24/8 aux buffer) generates it deterministically and then closes CLEANLY (the FIFO goes off, keeping G01 out). The classes, selected with --leave fbi|tmu|tmuconst|stencil|all:
- fbi: grColorCombineExt with all-ZERO inputs;
- tmu: grTexColorCombineExt with ZERO inputs on both TMUs;
- tmuconst: grConstantColorValueExt 0xffffffff with a constant-colour TCCU input, which sets combineMode[30];
- stencil: stencil enabled, func NEVER, mask and wmask ff, REPLACE.
'--close abandon' is allowed only after G01. A new tools/residue_ab.py sequences, at >=5 s pacing:
- vcrctl reg checks: cmdFifo0 off, plus the R/W registers 0x2001e0/0x200110/0x2001e4/0x2001e8/0x200200/0x200204, before and after;
- d3dprobe residue as a control;
- glidelab residue;
- d3dprobe residue at 16 and 32 bpp;
- a ring pull at the end.
The post-condition: after the stencil class, stencilMode reads 0x01ffff00, and it reads 0 after a bit-1 D3D run.

G05.approach:
The gap is real, and a one-pass fix is exact for every set-up UT2003 logged.
- Combines 3/8/10/12 are single-stage MODULATE2X(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE): cp 0x0c482405, drawn tex*diffuse x1.
- Combines 1/5/6 are SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) plus a stage-1 MODULATE2X (the UE2 lightmap): TMU0 textureMode 0x800242cf with TM_TC_MULT, drawn x1.

Fix: write the VSA-100 combineMode register, with the shift added only where the D3D op asks for it.
- **Word contents.** USE_COMBINE_MODE (bit 31), DISABLE_CHROMA_SUBSTITUTION (bit 30, which the SPEC caveat requires with bit 31), mux fields that reproduce the legacy routing exactly, and OUTSHIFT x2 or x4.
  - SPEC 8.21: with bit 31 the FBI muxes c_other = {0, cp[1:0]}, c_local = {00, cp[4]}, a_other = cp[3:2], a_local = {0, cp[6:5]} move into combineMode[2:0], [5:3], [17:16] and [20:18], with identical encodings.
  - The TMU muxes always come from combineMode, and all-zero selects are the legacy routing.
  - SPEC datapath: sum, then "Modulate 1x, 2x, 4x", then "Clamp 0-FF". That is D3D's saturating MODULATE2X/4X.
- **New pure header include/vcr_combine.h.** It holds V3D_FBI 0x400 (chip field 1), vcr_cm_fbi(cp, cshift, ashift), vcr_cm_tmu(cshift, ashift), the stage decisions, vcr_cm_seq and the lazy rule.
- **Decision, in compute_regs.**
  - Stage 0 gets a shift when its COLOROP/ALPHAOP is 2X/4X on color_path's two-argument branch: none when a TEXTURE argument has no usable texture.
  - Stage 1 gets one only on the two-stage path (stage1_combine's MULT).
  - The four shifts live in vcr3d_regs.
- **Emission, in prepare().** It runs immediately before VcrDd3dTarget/VcrDd3dState; VcrDd3dState itself is untouched. The new VcrDd3dCombine writes:
  - 12 nopCMD to TMU0|TMU1 (0x1920; the SPEC's 2PPC-exit rule), before the first write of each DP2 call;
  - then FBI@0x608, TMU0@0xA08 and TMU1@0x1208, in that order, because in 2PPC a write to one TMU reaches both.
- **Lazy, bounded to one call.**
  - Writes happen only when a word is non-zero, or to put back 0 after one was.
  - D3d_DrawPrimitives2 restores 0 after walk() if a word is live.
  - An armed DP2 with no 2X/4X therefore sends today's bytes exactly, and the extended combine is never on between DDI calls.
- **Worked words:**
  - combine 3: FBI 0xC0014001;
  - combine 1: TMU0 0xC0004000;
  - 4X: 0xC0018001 / 0xC0008000;
  - stage-1 alpha 2X: TMU0 0xC4000000;
  - TMU1: always 0.
- **Caps, when armed.** TextureOpCaps 0x184f becomes 0x187f (MODULATE2X and MODULATE4X).
- **Logging.** log_combo gains " sh cc ca/tc ta"; new events 513/24 ("armed") and 513/25 (per-context shift-state counts).
- **Old path.** Switch off, Voodoo3/86Box, or armed with no 2X draw: no new write and caps unchanged.
- **Approximation, not new.** Stage-0 2X with an active stage 1 is applied after stage 1 (G12's ordering). It is exact unless stage 0 saturates, and no logged UE2 combine has that shape.
- **Sequencing.** Land this before G12, as its first increment, instead of "with G12" as the gap says. G12 needs stage reordering, packed sARGB to the TMUs (G58) and TFACTOR in the TMUs (G14); G05 needs none of those. G12, G13 and G14 then extend the same header and emission code.
- **Darkness.** The staged Brightness/Gamma 0.8 act on the RAMDAC table at scan-out, which GDI captures do not include (inferred). The measured darkness is therefore the rendering, and the A/B uses the same ini anyway.

G05.gating:
Default OFF behind HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vcrmp\Diag\D3DFeat, bit VCR_D3DFEAT_CMSHIFT.
- **Bit:** proposed 6, the Phase-3 "extended combine" slot in hal.md's plan. It needs central allocation, because three parallel branches already collided on one vcr_info.flags bit on 2026-09-28.
- **Read time:** at boot (FindAdapter), like D3D32 and D3DBigTex, so the desktop and fullscreen PDEVs report the same TextureOpCaps.
- **Hardware:** VSA-100 only (pd->napalm); combineMode does not exist on a Banshee or Voodoo3.
- **Transport:** the whole D3DFeat DWORD goes in one appended vcr_info.d3dfeat field, so the dozens of planned D3D switches never consume vcr_info.flags bits (pinned full at 0x7fff). A VCR_INFO_F_ bit at 0x8000 is the fallback if the plan prefers flags.
- **Arming:** REGWRITE ... Diag D3DFeat REG_DWORD 64, REGREAD it back, activation check, safe-reboot.py. One Diag change per clean boot.
- **Byte-identity:** with it off, nothing changes (no writes, caps 0x184f). Even when armed, the lazy rule keeps every DP2 that draws no MODULATE2X/4X byte-identical to today.
- **Not safe to land default-on yet.** It drives register state this HAL has never used on silicon: bit 31/30 words, FBI-only chip-field writes from the display driver, and 12 TMU NOPs. Graduate it in a separate commit after the supervised armed boot passes: a default mask, or a D3DFeatOff kill mask like Accel2DPattern/GdiGamma. The plan picks one convention for all D3DFeat bits.
G05.d3dprobe_test:
Five new explicit tests in tools/d3dprobe.c (named with --tests until the switch is default-on, then in the default list).
- **Method:** an analytic scene, the back buffer locked and read.
- **Expected values:** computed per channel as want = min(255, (k*t*d+127)/255), from the 565/DXT-expanded texels. Each cell also logs the x1 "old" value.
- **Tolerance:** 14 per channel. The x1, x2 and wrap answers of every cell are at least 62 apart.

The tests:
- **mod2x** (stage 0 FBI path, UT2003 combine 3: MODULATE2X(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE), alpha MODULATE; R5G6B5 checker A=808080, B=ffff00):
  1. diffuse 80: 42,41,42 -> 84,82,84;
  2. a second quad in the same frame/DP2 with plain MODULATE stays 42,41,42 (the restore);
  3. diffuse c0 saturates cell B to ff,ff,00 (x1 = c0, a wrap = 80);
  4. alpha MODULATE2X with a diffuse alpha of 40 under SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA over black: 40 -> 80;
  5. a following clear to 404040 reads 404040.
- **mod4x:** the same with x4 (diffuse 40: 21 -> 84; saturation; alpha 40 -> ff).
- **tex2mod2x** (stage 1 TMU0 path, exactly UT2003 combine 1: stage 0 SELECTARG1(TEXTURE), stage 1 MODULATE2X(TEXTURE, CURRENT), lightmap 808080):
  - cell A 44,42,44 -> 88,84,88; cell B 84,42,00 -> ff,84,00;
  - a stage-1 MODULATE quad in the same frame stays x1;
  - A4R4G4B4 lightmap alpha 4 with stage-1 alpha MODULATE2X: 44 -> 88.
- **tex2mod4x:** the same with x4 (lightmap 404040: 22 -> 88; alpha 2: 22 -> 88).
- **tex2mod2x_dxt:** DXT1 base x DXT3 lightmap at x2 (UT2003 combines 5/6), skipped without D3DBigTex bit 1. It is also the first DXT texture in stage 1, which serves G06.

Running and passing:
- **Pass:** every cell within tolerance and none skipped (d3dprobe_run.py already fails a named-but-skipped test), at fullscreen 640x480x16 (+D16), fullscreen 1024x768x32 (+D24X8) and windowed on the 32 bpp desktop, with --pace 5000.
- **Never** run --zfmt d16 at 32 bpp (G10/G11).
- **Caps:** d3dprobe caps must read TextureOpCaps 0000187f armed, 0000184f off.
- **Reference first:** validate the expected values on a fleet box whose D3D8 driver lists MODULATE2X/4X before judging our HAL.
G05.risk:
Low risk to proven paths.
- **Unchanged paths.** The switch off, the default 16 bpp lane, the 32 bpp lane, Voodoo3 and the 86Box bed, and a fresh install: no new register write, and caps unchanged. Armed but with no MODULATE2X/4X draw: byte-identical by the lazy rule. All pinned by host tests and measured in boot A.
- **Armed 2X/4X draws are new register traffic, each hazard with its mitigation:**
  - the 2PPC exit Glide can leave: 12 nopCMDs to chip field 6 before each DP2's first combineMode write (SPEC caveat; this address form has run on .124 since 09-28);
  - texture chroma substitution: bit 30 set with bit 31 (SPEC caveat);
  - the FBI word reaching the TMUs: written FBI-only (chip field 1), never broadcast;
  - a TMU0 word copied to TMU1 in 2PPC: TMU0 is written before TMU1;
  - state lingering: 0 put back at the next state flush that does not need it, and at the end of every DP2.

  The words reproduce the legacy muxes exactly.
- **Glide/OpenGL coexistence:** no new exposure. Glide's assertDefaultState re-initialises all three combineMode registers at every open (gsst.c:913-950), Napalm Glide 2 runs _grTex2ppc(FALSE) at open, and the HAL leaves 0 after every DP2. The Glide-to-D3D direction stays G01/G03's.
- **SLI:** none (chip 0, snooping off). **Flip:** none.
- **Clears:** none. FASTFILL writes color1 directly (SPEC), and a probe cell checks it.
- **Caps widening:** caps-checking titles (Halo, Thief II NewDark, H&D, Max Payne) may switch to their 2X path. Mitigation: the probe proves the path first in the same boot; fallback is to split the caps onto their own D3DFeat bit.
- **Approximation:** stage-0 2X with an active stage 1 is exact only below saturation until G12 reorders the stages; no logged UE2 combine has that shape.
- **Performance:** +12 writes per 2X DP2 and 3 per state flush while live, against ~27-45 writes per triangle; negligible.

G10.approach:
Make the pair draw; we cannot make the runtime refuse it. d3d8's built-in PCI-id table entry 121a:0009 = 0x4580 has no arbitrary-depth bit. The registry override can only switch flags off. Dropping D16 from the Z list would break the proven 16 bpp fullscreen lane (the 4a9793b lesson).

New evidence, read from the staged binary. LIB/RedFaction/rf.exe (md5 0ba3b15d64a702333a4d9a0815f782b7) hard-codes D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS.AutoDepthStencilFormat = D3DFMT_D16 (rf.exe 0x5446f6 `movl $0x50,0x1cd42d4`) for PCI vendor 0x121a (0x544756-0x54476f) at every colour depth. 3) New VcrDdD3dCreateZSurface (vcrdd_d3d.c), called first in Dd_CreateSurface (vcrdd_ddraw.c:633-645).

- vcr_3d_target_seq writes the D24X8 sequence write for write: renderMode 0x001e0002, stencilMode=stencilOp=0, auxBufferAddr = the 16-aligned base, auxBufferStride = the pitch;

5) VcrDdD3dFreeMipChain frees SF_Z32 blocks like MIP_TOP (VidMemFree, HANDLED).

(1) d16_32: a D16 bound to the device's target by SetRenderTarget, in any run (windowed or fullscreen, 16 or 32 bpp); the device keeps its own Z.

  1. GetRenderTarget, GetDepthStencilSurface (z0).
  2. Skip if CheckDepthStencilMatch(adapter, target, D16) fails.
  3. CreateDepthStencilSurface(w, h, D16).

(3) zleak: 64 times create a 1024x1024 D16 (4 MB promoted), bind, clear Z, unbind, release.

(4) zlock, informational and never gating: a D16_LOCKABLE (skip if not offered) cleared to 1.0, then LockRect.

G06.approach:
The gap is real. Its most likely cause is G07, with strong evidence but no silicon proof: mipmap chains are split in video memory.

Why (verified in code):
- XP calls DdCreateSurface once per mip level (dwSCnt=1). We do not answer GUID_NTPrivateDriverCaps, so there is no atomic creation.
- mipchain_ext (vcrdd_d3d.c:367-460) and VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain (:522-584) size and place only the surfaces of the current call. So every level gets its own 16-byte-aligned HeapVidMemAllocAligned block and is marked MIP_TOP. The "one block" claims in e74510a and README:628 are wrong.
- tex_view(_ext) (:754-824) sets tLOD LODMAX = lod + (attach-list length - 1) and never checks placement.
- The TMU reads level k at top + vcr_tex_chain_offset(k). Wherever the heap did not put the levels back to back, minified pixels read other textures' bytes or stale memory, decoded in this texture's format. That gives saturated blocky confetti, the same look as V-02.

This fits every observation:
- Near/magnified surfaces are clean (LOD 0 = the top's own block).
- Edge-on and distant faces are noisy; in Halo, triangles of one rock mesh are clean or striped depending on their angle.
- d3dprobe passes: the heap is fresh (first-fit ascending, see ring_end_decoded.txt:986-989), and only levels 0-4 are tested; every DXT/8888 test uses Levels=1.
- Halo shows it too (D3D9 reaches the same DDI).

Further evidence:
- Every 513/20 event on .124 reads "1 levels".
- In the 11-08 UT2003 menu log (sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt), three chains have other live textures inside their own level-1 slot. Example: combine 8 is 512x512 A8R8G8B8 TBIG at 0x3c21ac0 with tLOD 0x40000b08; its level-1 slot 0x3d21ac0-0x3d61ac0 holds combine 6 (0x3d2c560) and combine 5 (0x3d4f000). Combine 16 is the counter-example: in fresh space its levels 0-6 are contiguous.
- Even a fresh heap misplaces every R5G6B5 chain's 1x1 level: the 2x2 level is 8 bytes and blocks start 16-aligned, so the TMU reads +10920 where the data is at +10928 for a 64x64.
- 3dfx's XP driver avoided all this. It answered ATOMICSURFACECREATION (DDFXNT.C:1224-1248) and reserved the whole chain at the top's call from lpSurfMore->dwMipMapCount (D3TXTR.C:1635, initMipMapChain :862-955).

INVESTIGATION (one log-only build, default-on, bounded):
- (a) 513/24: each texture CreateSurface's order, descriptor, lpSurfMore->dwMipMapCount, attach-list presence and placement (first 512 after boot).
- (b) A bind-time contiguity census in tex_view(_ext) through a new pure vcr_tex_chain_contig(). It logs 513/25 once per split surface, and keeps per-context counters plus the first 8 split chains. They are re-logged in a 513/26 summary at context-gone, so they survive the ring wrap.
- (c) LogEntries=16384.

Experiments:
- E1 miptail must fail deterministically at the R5G6B5 1x1 and the 8:1 tail.
- E2 mipfrag must fail from level 1.
- E3 the per-format chains must pass on a fresh heap; a failure would be a second, layout cause.
- E4 the stage-1 DXT chain and TEXBLT tests.
- E5 the in-game census in UT2004, UT2003 and Halo must show split chains.
- E6 a guard-only boot must remove the confetti. This is the causal proof.
- E7 reservation plus guard must render exactly.
- If the census shows no splits, work through: layout (E3), stage 1 (E4), the G89 S/T range, a replay of the exact texture from 513/21-23, then the TMU cache.

FIX (Diag\D3DMipChain, read at boot; one bit per clean boot):
- F1, chain guard (bit 0). n = min(n, contiguous prefix) before LODMAX is computed. This changes only tLOD bits 13:8, and only for split chains; it is single-pass and changes no caps. A split chain samples only its in-place levels (aliasing instead of garbage).
- F2, whole-chain reservation (bit 1). New pure header include/vcr_mipres.h, used by both allocators.
  - At the top's call (dwSCnt=1, TEXTURE|MIPMAP, more than 1 level, sampleable), allocate vcr_tex_chain_offset(kind, w0, h0, levels) rounded to 16, place the top, and open a reservation in the PDEV. The key is lpDD, pid, dimensions, level count, format and descriptor.
  - Each later level call is claimed before the sampleability check and before VcrDdD3dCreateTexSurface: fpVidMem = base + chain_offset(k), lPitch as today, MIP_LEVEL, HANDLED. DXT1 levels narrower than 8 are claimed into their TMU-size slots.
  - The link is either the attach-list stamp (as 3dfx did) or the keyed record; E0 decides.
  - Any mismatch, or no room for the whole chain, falls back to today's per-level block, logged as 513/27, and the guard clamps it.
  - The top frees the block, as today.
- F2-alt (bit 2): answer NTPrivateDriverCaps with ATOMICSURFACECREATION only, and harden the list loops (largest surface = top, k<12, no duplicate k). Use it only if E0 shows out-of-order or interleaved per-level calls. It changes flip-chain creation for every app, so it needs extra 2D and flip checks.
- Bits off: allocation and registers are byte-for-byte unchanged; only the log events are added. No caps change at any setting.

ADJACENT DEFECT (file as its own gap): a single 1x1 16-bit texture is sampled 8 bytes before itself. base = (offset-174760)&~0xf; 3dfx placed 1x1 textures at block+8 (D3TXTR.C:877-881).

G06.d3dprobe_test:
All tests are explicit only, never in the default list, and SKIPPED where the HAL does not offer the format or size.

What every test shares:
- Each level is one solid colour: L0 red, L1 green, L2 blue, L3 yellow, L4 magenta, L5 cyan, L6 white, L7 ff8000, L8 8000ff. DXT levels are solid blocks: c0==c1, indices 0, DXT5 alpha 255.
- Point min, mag and mip filters.
- Levels are selected by texel:pixel ratio at LOD n+0.26, as mip2048 does.
- Quads are sized so S/W stays below 8192 (G89): 128 px up to LOD 4, 64/32 px for LOD 5-6, 16 px with u about 19 for LOD 7-8.
- The centre pixel is read back from the 256x256 window with expect() at tolerance 12.
- RESULT gives each level ok/got/want, plus a verdict: exact, clamped (a wrong level shows the last in-place level's colour) or garbage. ok means exact.

The tests:
- (1) miptail: a 64x64 R5G6B5 chain, levels 3-6, and a 256x32 8:1 chain, levels 5-8.
  - Current code: deterministic FAIL at the 1x1 and at L7/L8, on a fresh heap. The 1x1 block starts 16-aligned while the TMU reads at 2x2+8.
  - With F2: exact.
- (2) mipfrag: a fragmenter, then a chain whose lower levels land in the holes.
  - Fragmenter: DEFAULT-pool single-level textures [H1 K1 H2 K2 H3 K3 H4 K4], where H are holes of exactly the chain's L1-L4 sizes and K are 64x64 R5G6B5 keepers. The H are released.
  - Then a MANAGED 256x256 R5G6B5 chain is created, filled and PreLoaded, and levels 0-4 are drawn. Repeated with a 256x256 DXT1 chain (holes 8K/2K/512).
  - Current code: FAIL from L1 (garbage). Guard only: clamped. With F2: exact.
- (3) mipdxt1: a 256x256 DXT1 chain, levels 0-5, plus a LOD-7 quad that must show L5 (the never-sample-below-8-wide rule).
- (4) mipdxt5: a 256x256 DXT5 chain, levels 0-8, including the 4x4/2x2/1x1 units.
- (5) mip8888: a 256x256 A8R8G8B8 chain, levels 0-8.
- (6) mipaspect: 128x16 and 16x128 R5G6B5 chains (8:1, both orientations), all levels. Current code fails in the tail.
- (7) mipbigdxt: a 1024x1024 DXT1 TBIG chain, levels 0-7.
- (8) mipdxt1_s1: the DXT1 chain in stage 1 (TMU0) over a grey R5G6B5 stage 0. Both stages SELECTARG1(TEXTURE); the set-1 coordinates are scaled by a new quad_t2s helper.
- (9) mipupd: a DEFAULT-pool R5G6B5 chain filled by UpdateTexture (DP2 TEXBLT), levels 0-8.

Pass gate for F2: the whole set exact at 1024x768x32 (D24X8) and at 640x480x16. The existing render (40/40) and texture A/B sets (83/0; 37/3 runtime refusals) must not regress.

G09.risk:
- Default 16 bpp path with the bit off: none; register traffic is identical and only CPU-side counting runs.
- Bit on, D3D8/9 titles: none by construction, since D3D8/9 have no colour keys; the d3dprobe leak check pins it.
- Bit on, DX5-7 titles that do not key: none, since the AND rule stays false.
- Keyed draws: visual only and bounded to keyed textures. A wrong key either fails to kill (today's look) or kills key-coloured texels. A chroma kill is a plain pixel reject with no hang mechanism (inferred). Bilinear fringes are a known hardware limit, since the compare runs after the filter; CKEY_POINT is the A/B.
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence: Glide's open resets chroma mode, range and texture chroma (gsst.c:909-911) and writes its own key when used, so our leftover FBI values are harmless. A stale FBI chromaRange[28] from Glide is cleared by our chromaRange=0. A stale Glide combineMode[31] would re-route the compare's input; that is G03's baseline, and the reason for cold-boot tests.
- SLI: D3D is single-chip today (G51). When G51 lands, the two FBI writes must reach every chip like the other 3D writes.
- Future combine work: G14 must write TFACTOR to TMU chip fields only, because broadcast would clobber the key. G12 must keep 'other = stage-0 texel' (cc_otherselect = texture RGB) for keyed single-stage draws.
- Flip path and 2D: untouched.
- Kernel safety: only documented DD_SURFACE_LOCAL fields of a handle-table surface are read, with no new cached pointers. This sidesteps the tex_surf0 dangling risk noted for G43.
- CPU cost: 2 PIO writes per keyed state flush and one handle lookup per DP2 while COLORKEYENABLE is on.
- Residual: XP may not refresh the kernel surface local after a late SetColorKey. Late keys would then be missed until the DdSetColorKey hook follow-up.

G04.approach:
This is an investigation, not a guessed fix. The cause of the 10-04 freeze is still unproven, so no driver behaviour changes "for G04". G04 delivers four things:
- instrumentation that can watch a frozen Direct3D session without win32k's display lock;
- an attended protocol that reproduces the two leading preconditions one at a time;
- an outcome-to-fix map (the fixes are mostly G01/G02);
- the rule for lifting .124's 'blk'.
Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G04.md.

NEW EVIDENCE FOUND WHILE DESIGNING
(1) A Glide session ran just before the freeze; none ran before the clean session.
- 10-04: Max Payne (fbab_maxpayne.json, 19:54) followed a 4-chip Quake II Glide session by about 4 minutes in the same boot (EV/gametune_1001/fbshot_probe/fbab_quake2.json, 19:50: sli_chips 4, attract demo running).
- 09-29: Max Payne ran at 13:42 in the cold boot after the 13:16:55 breaker trip. No Glide session ran before it (System Shock 2 at 13:34; Serious Sam TFE and TSE at 13:46 and 13:54, after it). It did not freeze, although the same blocked default fbshot was used.
- V-05 shows the same Glide-before-D3D correlation for Red Faction, Shogo and H&D.
- onbox-01/02 measured the mechanism:
  - a not-idle Glide close leaves cmdFifo0 enabled;
  - the miniport resets the engine at a mode set only when the chip reads BUSY;
  - a host write into the FIFO window gives status 0xa1f, then 512 a=9 (the 2D give-up);
  - after that DP2/Clear2 answer DD_OK and draw nothing, while Flip continues.
(2) Glide's FIFO window (0x18000-0x117000, KMD/README.md:80-86 and :712-716) is the bottom of our DirectDraw heap. The heap starts at offset 0 and the desktop sits at the top (vcrdd_ddraw.c heap_range). So the first surfaces of every fullscreen D3D game land in it. On 10-04 the scanned-out buffer was 0x4b0000-0x960000, so an earlier Max Payne surface filled 0x0-0x4b0000, the whole window.
(3) The crawl was CPU starvation, not the display lock: wmic and taskkill take none. The /high probe was only 3x faster, which fits a runnable thread at priority >= 13 or a bus stall. 11-12's stale FIFO did not make the box crawl.
(4) A static read of the game explains no sustained hog:
- rlmfc.dll raises HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS + TIME_CRITICAL only for a 0.5 s QPC calibration, then restores both;
- sndmfc's listener thread priority is set by the game (default 0);
- MaxPayne.exe's imports are hidden by SafeDisc.
So the hog must be measured.
(5) vcrctl takes GetDC(NULL) for every command except fbshot --probe (vcrctl.c:2101-2104), including probe-mem.

Leading hypothesis: a stale cmdFifo0 (G01), then the silent give-up (G02). Runner-up: an escape caught in a priority inversion behind a game thread at priority >= 13.

INSTRUMENTATION (log-only)
A) The D3D heartbeat, Diag\D3DBeat, default OFF.
- include/vcr_beat.h: a 96-byte record, vcr_beat_due, vcr_giveup_class, and VCR_GLIDE_FIFO_LO/HI.
- vcrdd: VcrDdBeat() runs at DP2/Clear2 entry BEFORE w.drawable (vcrdd_d3d.c:1859/1887), and at Dd_Flip (DD_OK and WASSTILLDRAWING counted separately), Dd_Lock (counting Locks inside Glide's window), ContextCreate and ctx_free. It is integer-only, touches no registers and sends at most one beat per second. max_spin is recorded in VcrDdRoom/VcrDd2dSync.
- vcrmp: IOCTL_VCR_D3DBEAT (0xa10) stamps ms and boot, READS status, the cmdFifo0 block and vidDesktopStartAddr, writes Diag\Live\D3DBeat (volatile key, never flushed) and logs event 514.
- The agent's REGREAD reads it live: no child process, no display lock.
B) give_up() names its cause, default ON (error path only).
- Before g2d_ok = 0 it reads the cmdFifo0 registers and logs 512 a=10 with the class.
- It always sends a where=7 record. The miniport flushes it to Diag\D3DGiveUp and records a VcrPhase, so it survives a power cycle.
C) vcrctl:
- no DC for probe-*, threads and probe-regs;
- 'threads [--delta]' through NtQuerySystemInformation, run at REALTIME;
- 'probe-regs [--lat N] [--scan K]' through vcrprobe;
- escape commands refuse while a fresh beat shows a live D3D context.
D) tools/d3dwatch.py:
- classifies each beat;
- on a stall, a give-up or a stale FIFO, captures a bundle: threads x2, typeperf at /realtime, probe-regs x2, WINLIST;
- never sends an escape and never closes the game.
E) LogLevel 2 and LogEntries 8192.
F) Optional Diag\D3DFault: clears g2d_ok, as give_up() does.

PROTOCOL (attended; activation check, PXE hold for 00:d0:b7:40:96:a9, safe-reboot)
- Boot 1, logging only, with G01/G02 OFF:
  - S0: d3dprobe beat check;
  - E0a x2: the Max Payne menu for 10 min with thread snapshots; the second run also plays the tutorial;
  - E0b: hands-off for 12 min (crosses the screensaver timeout);
  - E1: --probe under /high, three times;
  - E2: the default fbshot escape;
  - E3: reproduce 10-04. Use glidelab abandon --cfg 5, else a Quake II console quit, else glidelab fill plus pace-kill. Confirm bit 8 of reg 80024, then run Max Payne for 10 min. Add a control run with the FIFO off (also the G03 check).
- Boot 2: G01's switch only. The same E3 must come out clean.
- Boot 3 (optional): G02's switch only.
- E-ctl (optional): the same thread snapshots of Max Payne on .133.

OUTCOME TO FIX
- E3 reproduces and Boot 2 is clean: G01 + G02, plus a heap floor above 0x117000 for G01/G63.
- A stale FIFO alone blanks the triangles: G01.
- An ENGINE_BUSY give-up with the FIFO off: G03, and dump the registers at the give-up.
- The beat stops only during E2: H-C. Keep the rule, now enforced by the escape guard.
- A game thread at priority >= 13 also runs on .133: that is how the game runs, not a freeze.
- An interrupt/DPC storm: name the driver responsible.
- flips_still rising: vcr_flip.h.
- Device lost after E0b: G02/G43.
- Nothing reproduces: close G04 as 'not reproduced on 95678704' and keep D3DBeat armed.

EXIT
Three clean E0 runs alone would still miss a 1-in-4 event 42% of the time, so closure rests on the mechanism (E3 plus Boot 2). Lifting 'blk' is the user's decision.
