G04.risk:
To proven paths: low.
- With D3DBeat off, the drawing path's register traffic is byte-identical. The always-on parts are the give-up error path (register reads plus one 15-30 ms flushed record) and user-mode vcrctl.
- With D3DBeat on, the cost is one videoprt-serialized IOCTL plus one volatile registry write per second, from the game's own thread at PASSIVE_LEVEL, and 9 register reads in the miniport. No register is written.
- Not affected:
  - the default 16 bpp path;
  - Glide/OpenGL (they make no DP2/Flip calls, so no beats);
  - SLI (untouched);
  - the flip rule (return values unchanged; test_vcr_kmd_flip.c unchanged).
- The only perturbation: the one-second beat IOCTL can add a little latency to that single DP2/Flip call.

Experiment risk: real, mitigated.
- E3 deliberately creates the stale-FIFO state. The README records that CPU writes into Glide's FIFO window once hung the engine (status 0xA5F).
- E2 deliberately sends escapes under a live D3D game.
- Expected worst case: a frozen game, recovered as on 11-12 with taskkill /f plus a paced vcrctl modeseq.
- Rare worst case: a hard hang that needs a power cycle. .124 boots from the network first and is not in never_offer. Hence the PXE hold, the activation check and a person at the box throughout.

CRT: about 20 paced switches per boot, at least 5 s apart. The D3D8 runtime's unpaceable double switch only follows a refused CreateDevice, which Max Payne at 1280x960x32 does not hit.

AA: stays off (cfg 5, SliAA 0), per the user's choice.

G16.approach:
The gap is real and fixable, and there is a second defect in the same code. Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G16.md.

THE TWO DEFECTS
(1) The gap as filed. dpcLineCaps is a copy of the triangle caps (vcrdd_d3d.c:2063, 2072), but the walker parses and skips POINTS, LINELIST, LINESTRIP, INDEXEDLINELIST(2), INDEXEDLINESTRIP and LINELIST_IMM (:1690-1715).
(2) New: LINELIST_IMM is skipped with the wrong length. The walker skips 2n inline vertices (:1690-1694). The record is a connected strip of n+1 vertices, drawn V[i] to V[i+1]. Four parsers agree:
- 3dfx W2K VH5/D6DP2.C:3732 and :3748;
- 3dfx Win9x W9X/D6DP2.C:3561 and :3577;
- the MS DDK 3dlabs sample, d3ddx6.c:1124 and :1143;
- the MS DDK s3virge sample, d3ddx6.c:1024.
For n=1 the two lengths are equal. For n>=2 the walk desyncs: either COMMAND_UNPARSED (the D3DIM fallback that crashed JK) or vertex floats executed as opcodes.

HARDWARE
There is no line or point primitive. The setup unit draws a 4-vertex strip (begin, then draw after each later vertex) as two triangles (SPEC 3.3 and 8.59/8.60). Glide (gdraw.c:831) and 3dfx (D6LINE.C, D6POINT.C) both draw lines and points this way.

STEP 0: default ON, no register write
(a) LINELIST_IMM consumes (n+1)*stride after the existing DWORD pad. A stride of 0 goes to g_parse_unknown.
(b) Per-context counters: lines and points seen and drawn, IMM count and longest n, and a 7-bit opcode-class mask. Logged as event 513: what 26 once per context at the first line/point opcode, what 24 at ctx_free.
(c) Seven explicit d3dprobe tests, plus LineCaps and MaxPointSize in caps mode.

STEP 1: drawing, behind Diag\D3DFeat bit 4 (default OFF)
- New integer header include/vcr_dp2prim.h (HAL and host test). vcr_dp2_prim_bytes() and vcr_dp2_line()/vcr_dp2_points() decode the records: LINELIST s+2i; LINESTRIP s+i; INDEXEDLINELIST absolute pairs; INDEXEDLINELIST2 start + relative pairs; INDEXEDLINESTRIP start + n+1 indices; POINTS {wCount, wVStart}. DX5 D3DOP_POINT and D3DOP_LINE records are identical to opcodes 1 and 2.
- New float header include/vcr_d3dprim.h (vcrdd_3d.c and the host test only). vcr_line_quad() uses the Win9x rev-9 geometry: x-major when |dx|>=|dy|, minor axis ±0.5 around the line, NOT the NT tree's -1..0 which draws a row high. Strip order A-,A+,B-,B+. A zero-length line is not drawn. vcr_point_quad() is a 1x1 square at ±0.5. With the existing xy_bias of 0.5, integer endpoints give exactly one pixel per column or row, on the line's own row or column; an integer point gives exactly its pixel. Ends sit at the endpoints. D3DRENDERSTATE_LASTPIXEL is ignored, as by 3dfx and the DDK samples. Reverse-direction lines draw (first, last], as 3dfx's HAL does.
- vcrdd_3d.c:
  - vertex() becomes vertex_at(pd,d,v,x,y): the same writes, order and values. vertex() calls it with p[0]+xy_bias, p[1]+xy_bias.
  - quad() sends v0 BEGIN, then v1, v2 and v3 each followed by DRAW.
  - VcrDd3dLine(a,b) = quad(a,a,b,b); every corner carries its endpoint's colour, Z, W/fog and S/T for both TMUs.
  - VcrDd3dPoint(v) = quad(v,v,v,v).
  - VcrDd3dSetupMode().
- vcrdd_d3d.c:
  - Culling: lines and points never cull, and a quad must be a strip. quads_begin() writes regs.setupMode & ~(SM_CULL|SM_CULL_NEGATIVE|SM_FAN) once per command when the context culls; quads_end() puts it back when the command ends. prepare() resets the flag after a full state send. tri() and imm_tri() are untouched (3dfx clears SST_SETUP_EN_CULLING the same way, D6LINE.C:388, D6POINT.C:131).
  - line(), line_ix() (the tri()-style bounds check) and points() each do prepare(), then quads_begin(), then the draw.
  - walk() keeps one case per opcode: NEED(vcr_dp2_prim_bytes), count, draw if w->lines_on, quads_end.
- Caps: unchanged. The copy becomes true, since lines and points use the same texture, Z, blend, alpha-test and fog state.
- Switch plumbing: miniport hwinfo reads D3DFeat & 0x10 into VCR_INFO_F_D3DLINES (0x8000) at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO, like Accel2DLine. vcrdd_2d.c sets pd->d3d_lines and logs 513 what 25. Every chip is covered, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed can prove it first.

NOT IN THIS ITEM
FILLMODE and flat lines (G24, which reuses these functions), specular (G25), cylindrical wrap (G86), point size and sprites (runtime-emulated; MaxPointSize 1), and D3D diamond-exit end pixels (would need parameter extrapolation).
G16.gating:
Two steps.

STEP 0: default ON
Covers the LINELIST_IMM record length (n+1 vertices), the per-context line/point counters and logs (513 what 24/26), and the d3dprobe tests. It writes no register:
- for n=1 the skip length is unchanged;
- for n>=2 the old length is a walker desync.
It is pinned by the native test with both values. It should ship with the next driver build whatever this item's priority.

STEP 1: drawing, default OFF behind Diag\D3DFeat bit 4 (0x10)
- Bit number per hal.md section 10 Phase 2 item 5; coordinate with the other D3DFeat designs.
- Positive flag VCR_INFO_F_D3DLINES 0x8000, read at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO like Accel2DLine. It changes no caps, so a new PDEV picks it up at the next mode change and 0 kills it without a reboot. It is still armed for proof only at a clean boot (one Diag change per boot).
- With it off, the register stream is byte-for-byte today's: the draw loops do not run, so quads_begin is never called and quads_end writes nothing; vertex() writes the same values in the same order; tri() and imm_tri() are untouched.

PROMOTION TO DEFAULT ON (absent=1, 0=kill)
After ONE supervised clean boot on .124 (boot B of the verification) in which:
- the 7 line/point tests pass at 640x480x16 and 1024x768x32;
- the 14-test default set still passes;
- one game A/B shows the element appearing.
It is a good candidate for quick promotion: the on-path only touches command streams that draw nothing today. It is not safe to land default-on blind, because it is new register traffic (cull-bit toggles, quads at screen edges).

G12.approach:
The gap is real and fixable. It is the whole legacy combine model, not one bug, as verified in vcrdd_d3d.c:
- color_path (:676-745) hard-wires other = TEXTURE/C1 and local = diffuse, so TEXTURE x TFACTOR draws TEXTURE x DIFFUSE.
- The BLEND* ops are right only with TEXTURE as arg1, and every other colour op, and every alpha op except SELECT and ADD, draws MODULATE.
- stage1_combine (:849-874) is REPLACE, PASS, ADD or MULT, run in TMU0 BEFORE stage 0's diffuse term (:947-977).
- Stage 1 is dropped when stage 0 has no texture or stage 1 has none of its own (:928).
- combineMode is never written (vcrdd_3d.c:74-129), so Glide's leftovers apply. In a TMU the selects ALWAYS come from combineMode.

The VSA-100's extended combine provides the missing operations: combineMode bit 31 in the FBI and both TMUs, computing ((A'+B')*C'+D')<<outshift with x/-x/1-x/x-1/2 inverts, iterated, texture and constant selects, and TMU chromaKey/chromaRange as constants with bit 30.

The design gives the combine a single owner: a new Win32-free header, KMD/include/vcr_combine.h, compiled by both the driver and a native test. vcr_cmb_compile(stage TSS x2, texture usability, tiers) returns:
- a verdict: EXACT, APPROX_SAT or LEGACY, plus the reason;
- the fbzColorPath combine bits, the TMU0/TMU1 textureMode combine bits, and three combineMode words;
- which stage's texture each TMU samples.

The compiler works in four steps:
1. **Normalise:** apply D3D's rules (DISABLE ends the cascade; SELECTARG2 becomes SELECTARG1; the unbound-texture convention stays as today); eliminate dead stages; fold an untextured stage 0 whose result is a single source into stage 1's CURRENT. RESULTARG, SPECULAR, TEMP, PREMODULATE, bump, DOT3, LERP and MULTIPLYADD go to LEGACY.
2. **Recipes:** each of the 20 ops becomes an A/B/C/D/shift recipe, with vendor-equivalent complement rules (G13 lives here).
3. **Route** every source through per-unit select tables.
4. **Place** each channel (colour and alpha are independent units), first fit:
   - F: FBI stage behind a TMU0 REPLACE;
   - PROD: product chain, TMU1 REPLACE + TMU0 MULT + FBI x diffuse/TFACTOR with the total shift applied last;
   - SPLIT: TMU0 forwards one texture;
   - TINT: untextured stage 1 in the FBI;
   - (bit 7) T0F, and T1T0, which is D3D's order with stage 0 in TMU1, stage 1 in TMU0 and the FBI passing through;
   - (bit 8) iterated diffuse inside the TMUs.

**Encoders** follow Glide's ext-combine mapping. For setups the legacy path already got right, the engine emits the legacy fbzColorPath/textureMode unchanged plus 'mirror' combineMode words (0xC0000000 + the FBI selects). This works because the extended encoding with zero new fields IS the legacy arithmetic. Examples:
- MODULATE2X(TEX,DIFF): cp 0x0C482405 unchanged, cm_fbi 0xC0014001.
- UT2003 world (SEL1(TEX) + MODULATE2X(TEX,CURRENT)): cp 0x0C000005 and the TMU words unchanged, cm_fbi 0xC0014001.

**Driver changes:**
- compute_regs branches only when armed, then fills r->cm_*. c0 and c1 both hold TFACTOR.
- prepare maps texture-coordinate sets by tmu0_stage/tmu1_stage.
- VcrDd3dState writes, in order: the 12 TMU NOPs (chip field 0x1800) once per epoch; combineMode with chip fields 0x400/0x800/0x1000, before all other registers; then, only when a bit-7 placement needs them, TFACTOR into the TMU chromaKey/chromaRange.
- A shared VcrDd3dForget hook (Glide exclusive set/release, DrvAssertMode(TRUE)) also serves G41.
- log_combo gains event 513/24 (shadow verdicts per tier, stage-1 args), which is log-only.
- LEGACY setups draw exactly as today, with mirror words.
- Single pass only: no driver multipass; anything not exact is LEGACY and G15 refuses it.
- TextureOpCaps stays 0x184f unarmed. Armed, it grows by proven op groups toward 3dfx's 0x001effff, only after G15. MaxTextureBlendStages stays 2.

**Staging:**
- Bit 6 alone draws 25 of UT2003's 26 logged combinations exactly. These include all 7 MODULATE2X ones (G05: world and meshes).
- Bit 7 adds the TMU-extended ops and TFACTOR in the TMUs (G14's TMU half).
- Bit 8, with G58's packed sARGB, fixes the stage order for setups whose stage 0 uses DIFFUSE, such as UT2003 combine 21 (MODULATE then BLENDCURRENTALPHA).

G12.gating:
Default OFF. Three positive bits of Diag\D3DFeat, read at boot like D3DBigTex (caps must match between the desktop and fullscreen PDEVs), VSA-100 only, and ignored on a Banshee/Voodoo3:
- bit 6 VCR_D3DF_CMB_FBI: the HAL owns combineMode; FBI ext combine plus legacy-only TMU placements;
- bit 7 VCR_D3DF_CMB_TMU: TMU ext combine and TFACTOR in the TMUs; requires 6;
- bit 8 VCR_D3DF_CMB_ITER: iterated diffuse in the TMUs; requires 6+7 and G58's packed sARGB armed, otherwise logged as ignored (513/25).

Rollout:
- One bit per supervised clean boot, in order 6, 7, 8. Each is bisectable: disarm and the previous state is the proven one.
- With all bits off the register traffic is byte-for-byte today's: compute_regs and VcrDd3dState take the unchanged branch, and TextureOpCaps stays 0x184f. This is pinned by Python and native tests.
- The only default-on part is log-only: the shadow-verdict event 513/24, computed into a local struct and pinned never to touch c->regs.

Not safe to land default-on: it adds combineMode/c0 traffic to every D3D draw and relies on partly inferred datapath arithmetic. Bits 6 and 7 become candidates for default-on in a follow-up commit after the full section-6 verification, as Accel2DPattern did. Bit 8 follows G58.

TextureOpCaps widening is a separate later step, by proven op group, only after G15's honest ValidateTextureStageState.
G12.d3dprobe_test:
A table-driven cell framework in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c:
- **Layout:** up to 64 cells per test, 24x24 quads in 32x32 cells inside the 256x256 readback window.
- **Inputs:** 8x8 managed A4R4G4B4 solid textures with values that are multiples of 0x11 (exact on the default path), point sampling, dither and fog off. Each cell sets its own TSS, TFACTOR and vertex colours.
- **Alpha:** alpha ops are read through the blender (TFACTOR white x SRCALPHA over black).
- **Reference:** include/vcr_texop_ref.h, D3D's formulas in 8-bit integers with clamping after each stage. The native test uses the same header.
- **Pass:** each cell's centre within 14 per channel at 16 bpp, or 6 at 32 bpp.
- **Diagnostics:** each cell also prints the legacy prediction. A start-up self-check asserts |want-legacy| >= 3*tol for every discriminating cell, and a --expect legacy flag turns the bit-off run into an automated negative control.

Tests (expected / legacy):
- **Tier 6:** mod2x (TEX 0x888888 x DIFF 0x606060 -> 0x666666 / legacy 0x333333; saturating cell 0xFFFFFF), mod4x (0x666666 / 0x1A1A1A), addsigned and addsigned2x (0x686868 and 0xD1D1D1 / 0x333333), subtract (0x8C8C8C, the reversed order clamps to 0), addsmooth (0xB5B5B5), blendfa, blendca, blendtapm, madd (the four MODULATE*_ADD*), blendta_rev (BLENDTEXTUREALPHA(DIFFUSE red, TEXTURE blue, a=0x44) -> (0x44,0,0xBB) / swapped), tfactor_tex (MODULATE(TEXTURE white, TFACTOR red) with green diffuse -> red / green), alphaops, stage1_mod2x (UT2003 world: SEL1(TEX 0x888888) + MODULATE2X(TEX 0x888888, CURRENT) -> 0x919191 / 0x484848), stage1_select (-> 0x00CC00 / 0x003300), tint_stage1 (-> (0xCC,0x66,0) / 0xCCCCCC), fold_stage0 (-> (0x44,0x44,0x88) / 0x8080FF).
- **Tier 7:** stage1_blendca (-> (0x77,0,0x88) / black), stage1_addsigned (0xD4D4D4 / 0x6D6D6D), stage1_addsigned2x (0x999999 / 0x242424), stage1_subtract (0x888888 / 0x363636), stage1_blendfa (TFACTOR alpha inside TMU0, -> (0xBF,0,0x40) / black).
- **Tier 8:** stage1_add (MODULATE(TEX 0x888888, DIFF 0x404040) then ADD(TEX 0x444444, CURRENT) -> 0x666666 / 0x333333, the wrong-order case), stage1_blendda, ut2003_c21.
- **Aggregates:** combine6, combine7, combine8.

G12.regression_test:
tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_combine.c (new) compiles the driver's include/vcr_combine.h and include/vcr_texop_ref.h, plus a test-only register-level model, tests/native/vcr_cmb_model.h. The model DECODES fbzColorPath+combineMode and textureMode+combineMode words, in legacy and [31]=1 form, so encoder bit errors fail. Its inferred points are written down once: clamp after the shift, X-1/2 = 128, negatives clamp to 0, TMU1's OTHER input = 0.

It asserts:

(1) The fixed AND the old-buggy value for every defect, using a transcription of today's color_path/stage1_combine, as test_vcr_kmd_d3dseq.c's old_target() does:

| case | old (legacy) | fixed (engine) |
|---|---|---|
| MODULATE2X | t*d | min(1, 2td) |
| UT2003 world | t0*t1 | 2*t0*t1 |
| stage-1 SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) | t1*d | t1 |
| BLENDTEXTUREALPHA(DIFFUSE, TEXTURE) | swapped | right |
| MODULATE(TEXTURE, TFACTOR) | t*d | t*f |
| fold | d | t1*d |
| tint | t0 | t0*f |
| alpha SUBTRACT | a1*a2 | max(0, a1-a2) |
| tier 8: MODULATE then ADD | (t0+t1)d | t0*d+t1 |

(2) Exhaustive single stage: every op x arg pair x modifier x 7 colour vectors. An EXACT verdict gives model == reference +-2; anything else gives exactly the legacy registers plus a reason. Per-tier EXACT counts are pinned.

(3) Two stages: the UT2003 log's 26 combinations as golden rows with their logged legacy words (cp c000005/c482405, TMU MULT 0x24000) and the engine words (cm_fbi 0xC0014001 for the MODULATE2X cases). Combine 21 is LEGACY at {6} and {6,7}, and EXACT at {6,7,8}.

(4) Mirror: every legacy-correct setup gives bit-identical fbz/tm, cm_tmu = 0xC0000000, cm_fbi = 0xC0000000|mirror, and a bit-exact equal model output.

(5) Robustness: 100k random and out-of-range inputs give a verdict and never an out-of-bounds read (run with sanitizers when available).

(6) tiers = 0 gives LEGACY with no combineMode.

G12.risk:
**Default 16 bpp path:** none while the bits are off. It stays byte-for-byte (pinned); only log events are added.

**Armed:**
- Every D3D draw writes three combineMode words plus c0, relying on the inferred meaning of zero fields under bit 31. The mirror rule keeps the registers of already-correct setups at legacy plus zero fields, and boot B's unchanged-matrix gate catches any difference. LEGACY setups draw exactly as today.

**Glide/OpenGL after D3D:**
- Glide's open sends the 12 NOPs and rewrites all three combineMode words (gsst.c:916-930, gtex.c:1043-1078).
- Its 2ppc exit invalidates both TMUs' chroma, which its validator rewrites before the first triangle (gtex.c:1019-1022, distate.c:1655-1666).
- The residual risk is our TFACTOR left in the TMU chromaRange, where alpha >= 0x60 sets [30:29]=3 if a later client clears bit 30 before rewriting chroma. Mitigations: the constants are loaded only when a bit-7 placement needs them; boot C tests it; AmigaMerlin's Glide behaviour is inferred.

**D3D after Glide:** improved. The 12-NOP 2ppc exit and three explicit words follow every exclusive set/release/assert. A killed client's command FIFO remains G01.

**Unaffected:**
- SLI: chip-0 3D registers only, with no chipMask/sliCtrl writes.
- The flip path: no video or swap registers are touched.

**Other:**
- CPU: one compile per state change (about 1 us, inferred), +3 MMIO writes per flush, and 12 NOPs once per epoch. Measure with d3dprobe perf --novsync and the UT2003 avgfps; add a 16-entry per-context compile cache if the cost exceeds 1%.
- Widened TextureOpCaps could steer titles onto new paths, so widening comes only after G15 and per proven op group.
- Kernel robustness: the new code is pure integer, with bounded loops and range-checked tables, and is fuzzed under sanitizers. The 86Box Voodoo3 bed cannot exercise any of it (VSA-100 only).

G08.approach:
The gap is real and fixable in a single pass. The fix is a CPU-only translation of state; it adds no register combination the HAL does not already write.

When the D3DFeat bit is on, each legacy texture state is copied onto stage 0's texture stage states as it arrives, the way Microsoft's NT Permedia2 sample does (d3dstate.c:583-740, called for every render state at :1836) and the way 3dfx's NT HAL does (D3RSTATE.C:2168-2296, 2645-2720, 2860-2945). compute_regs then builds the registers exactly as it does for every TSS-driven title.

Mapping:
- TEXTUREMAPBLEND (21):
  - DECAL/COPY: SELECTARG1(TEX) for colour and alpha.
  - MODULATE: colour MODULATE(TEX,DIFF); alpha takes a private sentinel 0x7ffffffe (the DDK's LEGACY_ALPHAOVERRIDE), stored in tss[ALPHAOP] so a later blend state or a direct ALPHAOP replaces it.
  - DECALALPHA: BLENDTEXTUREALPHA(TEX,DIFF) with alpha SELECTARG2(DIFF).
  - MODULATEALPHA: MODULATE/MODULATE.
  - ADD: ADD with alpha SELECTARG2(DIFF).
  - DECALMASK and MODULATEMASK (not advertised) map to the nearest single-stage equivalent of the DDK formula.
  - Values outside the enum are ignored.
- TEXTUREMAG (17): mapped to MAGFILTER by the named within-level filter (3dfx's rule).
- TEXTUREMIN (18): mapped to MINFILTER plus MIPFILTER; all three references agree.
- Addressing: TEXTUREADDRESS (3) goes to ADDRESSU and ADDRESSV; 44 and 45 go to U and V separately; D3DTSS_ADDRESS (12) on stage 0 or 1 is copied into that stage's 13 and 14.
- Inert mirrors: 43, 46 and 49 are copied to TSS 15, 19 and 21. Nothing reads those yet; they become live with G27/G86.
- WRAPU/V are not mapped (cylindrical wrap is G86); they are only counted.

The mapping runs on every receipt, not only on a change. XP's d3dim sends render states 1-135 raw at device creation and then sends its TSS initialisation, so a later legacy MODULATE must re-apply.

color_path resolves the sentinel through a new c->tex0_alpha, set in compute_regs. The call text `color_path(c, tex) | CP_PARMADJUST` stays exactly as the existing test pins it. Resolution:
- Texture with an alpha mask or DXT: SELECTARG1(TEXTURE), i.e. CP_ASEL_TMU.
- Otherwise: SELECTARG1(DIFFUSE), i.e. CP_ASEL_ITER.

Registers the mapping produces:
- textureMode bit 1 (MINFILTER), bit 2 (MAGFILTER), bits 6/7 (CLAMPS/T).
- tLOD LODMAX only for chains the driver packed (SF_MIP_TOP), nearest LOD.
- fbzColorPath values, as log_combo prints them:

| case | new | old |
|---|---|---|
| legacy MODULATE + R5G6B5 | 0x0c002401 | 0x0c002405 |
| MODULATEALPHA | 0x0c482405 | |
| DECAL | 0x0c000005 | |
| DECALALPHA | 0x0c007201 | |
| ADD | 0x0c004001 | |

The textureMode equivalents are 0x08241a0f (bilinear) and 0x08241ac9 (clamp).

Caps change under the same bit; both fields are DX5-7 only, and D3D8/9 do not define these bits:
- TextureBlendCaps gains DECALALPHA: 0xcb becomes 0xcf, matching 3dfx.
- TextureFilterCaps gains D3DPTFILTERCAPS_MIPLINEAR. Our caps today advertise LINEARMIPNEAREST (point texels blended between mips, which we cannot draw) and omit MIPLINEAR (bilinear plus nearest mip, exactly what the HAL draws). So a DX5 title choosing from the caps cannot select bilinear with mipmaps.

Code layout:
- New pure header include/vcr_legacy.h holds the tables, the resolver and the Phase 0 slot helpers. It returns {idx,val} pairs so the header stays free of Win32 types.
- VCR_STATIC_ASSERTs in vcrdd_d3d.c pin every constant against the DDK.
- Phase 0, log-only and default-on: per-context counters update in set_rs, the TSS handler, ContextCreate and the DP2 entry, and are logged in two events at context gone. They record:
  - a value mask and token count for render states 3/17/18/21/44/45 and TSS 12;
  - a misc mask (WRAPU/V, border colour, LOD bias, anisotropy, rs 42, colour key, override tokens rs>=256, "a legacy state after a TSS token");
  - the dwhContext value ContextCreate received;
  - the OR of DP2 flags.

New evidence gathered for this design:
- d3dim.dll 5.1.2600.0 disassembly: the DP2 device's render-state writer is 0x6d91a6d8 (vtable+0x80). The init loop 0x6d922344 sends states 1-135, then the TSS loop at 0x6d922375 runs. d3dim's own DP2 rasterizer maps the legacy states itself (0x6d9280bd, 0x6d927f66, 0x6d9277e1), which shows the mapping is the driver's job.
- MotS is an IDirect3D2 title, so its only filter channel is TEXTUREMAG/MIN. Its Display menu has no filtering option, and its frame crop is point-sampled. This supports visual-06 over games-20/21.
- No d3dprobe test samples bilinear or CLAMP: every test sets POINT and WRAP.

Old path, bit off: legacy states are stored and ignored, the caps stay 0xcb/0x17, and the register traffic is byte-for-byte that of 95678704. Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe is D3D8, so it cannot send these states and is not affected.

G08.gating:
Two parts, gated differently.

Phase 0 counters: log-only, no register write, default ON. A Python test pins that they never touch c->regs or VcrDd3d*.

The mapping itself, the legacy-MODULATE resolver and the two caps bits:
- Behind Diag\D3DFeat bit 1 (0x2), default OFF (absent = 0). The bit position follows hal.md §10 Phase 2 order; the integrator owns the final bit map.
- Read at boot, like D3D32 and D3DBigTex, so the legacy caps an app reads at the desktop equal its fullscreen PDEV's.
- Carried as a positive vcr_info flag so an older miniport never arms it.
- Decoded on every chip, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed can prove it before silicon.
- With the bit off, register traffic and caps are byte-for-byte those of 95678704. The resolver is gated too, so even an app that sends 0x7ffffffe itself changes nothing.
- Armed alone in one supervised clean boot.

The mapping is safe to graduate to default-ON afterwards. It is a pure correctness fix using register combinations the HAL already writes. Graduation would be a negative kill switch, Diag\D3DLegacyStates=0 (absent = on), the Accel2DPattern/GdiGamma pattern. Conditions:
1. The DX5/DX6 probe legacy tests pass on .124 at 640x480x16 fullscreen and on the 86Box bed.
2. The d3dprobe D3D8 default matrix is unchanged with the bit on (40/40 at 1024x768x16 and x32, plus bilinear and clamp).
3. Phase 0 shows no legacy token after a TSS token in any D3D7/8/9 context (lgc_misc 0x100 never set), so the mapping is inert there by construction.
4. JK, MotS and Thief Gold in game show no sky, HUD or translucency regression.

If condition 3 fails, scope the mapping to legacy-interface contexts and re-prove. Scope by ContextCreate's incoming dwhContext if Phase 0 shows it carries the interface version, else by EXECUTEBUFFER or a non-default legacy value.
G08.d3dprobe_test:
Two layers: D3D8 controls in d3dprobe for the path the states map onto, and G08's tests in G75's DX5/DX6 probe.

1. d3dprobe (D3D8). D3D8 cannot send legacy states, so these test the TSS path they map onto. New tests, explicit at first: `--tests bilinear,clamp`. No existing test samples bilinear or CLAMP.

`bilinear`:
- Draws a 2x2 R5G6B5 texture (column 0 black, column 1 white) over x/y 64..192 (128 px, 64 px per texel).
- Settings: MAG/MIN LINEAR, MIP NONE, WRAP, SELECTARG1, dither off, no blending.

G08.risk:
| area | risk | why / mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| default 16 bpp path, bit off | none | Register traffic and caps byte-for-byte unchanged. The counters are CPU bookkeeping, one switch per state token and never per triangle; Python tests pin this. |
| D3D8/D3D9 titles, bit on | low | They cannot set retired states, and the caps bits changed are undefined in d3d8caps.h. The only exposure is a runtime-injected legacy token after the TSS, which Phase 0 detects (bit 0x100). The d3dprobe matrix and the UT2004/Halo menus must be unchanged in boot B. |
| DX5/DX6 titles (JK, MotS, R6, Dark engine) | intended change | A wrong mode mapping would show visually. Every mode is probed against analytic values; JK, MotS and Thief Gold get a supervised in-game check. |
| mip chains | low-medium | Legacy MIP* values make these titles walk mip chains for the first time, but only chains the driver packed (SF_MIP_TOP). A packing bug (G07) could put G06-like noise on distant surfaces. legacy_min and d3dprobe mip must pass first, and the in-game check looks at distant surfaces. |
| Glide/OpenGL coexistence, SLI, flip, Clear2 | none | No new register, no sequence or timing change; chip 0 only as before. |
| stability (Max Payne class) | none added | No new memory access, FIFO use or wait. |
| performance | none | Bilinear and mip selection are single-cycle per TMU, and mipmapping can only reduce texture-cache misses. |

Do d3dim700, d3d8 or d3d9 ever put a legacy state into a D3D7/8/9 context after its TSS (lgc_misc 0x100)? d3dim700 has a render-state re-send loop over states 2-135 at 0x7394f28c whose consumer was not followed.

What stage-0 alpha does a DX5/DX6 title get when it never sets TEXTUREMAPBLEND? The runtime's TSS init sends SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) after its render-state init, but DDKHELP says the DX6 default 'matched' legacy MODULATE. An optional read-only reference run of the DX6 probe on a fleet box with a vendor WHQL driver would settle it.

DECAL's alpha for an alpha-less texture (implementations: 1.0; DDK table: vertex alpha) and ADD's alpha (implementations: vertex; DDK table: aSrc+aTex). The design follows the implementations; the probe records both.

Execute-buffer state overrides (render state >= 256, dropped at vcrdd_d3d.c:1396) and render state 42 (DX5 ALPHABLENDENABLE, retired): Phase 0 counts both. If a title uses either, implement 3dfx's override set (D6DP2.C:1338-1355) and map 42 to 27 for legacy contexts as a follow-up.

Do JK and MotS actually request bilinear? MotS's Display menu has no filtering option and its only channel is TEXTUREMAG/MIN. If Phase 0 shows NEAREST, the point sampling is the title's own choice and only the blend/address part of G08 helps them.

G02.approach:
VERDICT: real, fixable, P0. Verified in code: give_up() (vcrdd_2d.c:83-89) only logs 512 a=9 and clears g2d_ok after SPIN_CAP (:71, ~1.2 s); VcrDdRoom then fails at once (:99-100); DP2 draws nothing and returns the walk's DD_OK (vcrdd_d3d.c:1859-1860, :1869); Clear2 returns a hard-coded DD_OK (:1901); ContextCreate (:1163-1208) never reads g2d_ok; Dd_Flip keeps flipping (vcrdd_ddraw.c:315-361); recovery only at DrvEnableSurface (vcrdd.c:540) - DrvAssertMode(TRUE) does not re-init. A VcrDdRoom give-up also leaves g2d_busy=1, so the next Sync spins a second SPIN_CAP. Silicon (ONBOX 11-12): ring seq 25058 give-up (why 2, status a1f); seq 25127/25134 GetDriverInfo 7de41f80 -> 88760028; GetDeviceCaps 8876086a with no mode switch; seq 25146 the busy-at-mode-set VcrHwResetEngine cured it (0xa5f->0x5f). CORRECTION to the gap: the HAL vanished through the LIVE GetDriverInfo gate (:2136), not DrvGetDirectDrawInfo (:2058) - so the HAL returns as soon as g2d_ok does, no new PDEV needed. H4+H2 (dead engine -> game loop spins at high priority) matches every Max Payne 10-04 symptom (inferred).

DESIGN, four parts:
A. RECORD (default-on, log-only): give_up() keeps its ERROR line and g2d_ok=0 and gains a last call VcrDdEngineLost(pd,why,status), which always sends a new IOCTL_VCR_ENGINE_LOST (VCR_CTL(0xa11)). The miniport counts it (Diag\EngineLostCount, EngineLostLast = boot<<16|why<<8|result), logs event 804 VCR_EV_ENGINE_LOST and writes a flushed VcrPhase (survives ring wrap and reboot; PrevPhaseLog after a hang). No register write without bit 2.
B. RECOVER (Diag\D3DSafe bit 2, read at boot): a pure policy (new include/vcr_englost.h: vcr_el_decide - armed, not under exclusive_pid/leaving/test block, <=3 resets per 60 s, >=2 s apart) asks the miniport for the reset (VCR_EL_REQ_RESET). The miniport refuses on SLI (x->sli_chips) or a live Glide mapping (G01's liveness helper: PsLookupProcessByProcessId + same EPROCESS + create time + exit status STATUS_PENDING, all XP SP3 exports), else calls the UNCHANGED VcrHwResetEngine(x,0,"display give-up"): cmdFifo0.baseSize=0, miscInit1 bit19 CMDSTREAM_RESET, miscInit0 bits 0/1/5 (GRX, FBI FIFO, 2D), 10 us, restore, idle wait - the engine half of GPL h3InitResetAll (h3cinit.c:1308-1340); video/memory/VGA timing untouched. Display then reads only: max of 64 FIFO-free reads and <=20000 vcr_idle_run reads; re-arms (g2d_ok=1, fog_valid=0, g2d_busy=0, shared generation g_vcr_eng_resets++) only if result IDLE, 3 idle reads and the FIFO back at the INIT count. Mid-walk: prepare() compares the shared generation and re-sends target/state/TMU/fog, then continues (as G01 specifies); the call that gave up still returns FALSE (op dropped, GDI/HEL fallbacks as today). Re-arm (read-only, no write) also after a good DrvAssertMode(TRUE) mode set and a good RESTORE_MODE; leaving=1 at DrvAssertMode(FALSE)/VcrDd2dTerm so teardown give-ups are recorded, never reset. Retries (policy-gated) at ContextCreate, DP2/Clear2 entry and GetDriverInfo while lost.
C. REPORT (bit 2): while lost, DP2 (only if the walk said DD_OK) and Clear2 answer DDERR_SURFACELOST (0x887601C2); Dd_Flip of a DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE target and Dd_Blt from a 3DDEVICE source (windowed Present) answer DDERR_SURFACELOST - DirectDraw-only 2D games are never told lost; ContextCreate retries once, then refuses ONCE per loss with DDERR_CURRENTLYNOTAVAIL (the code GetDriverInfo already gives) and accepts-and-reports after that, which bounds G11's refusal mode-flap to one per loss. Walk still runs (state tracking, lpdwRStates, TEXBLT CPU copies). Logged once per context/PDEV on a new event 514 VCR_EV_DD_ENGINE.
D. TEST HOOKS (bit 7 only): escape VCR_ESC_ENGINE_FAULT (BASE+13): LIFT, SOFT (sync then give_up why 3), HARD (real 2D stall: a 64x1 transparent mono host blit given 1 of 2 dwords, then VcrDd2dSync gives up for real), BLOCK (refuse resets -> lost path), ARM_ROOM n (the n-th VcrDdRoom gives up, i.e. inside a DP2 walk; one load+branch in VcrDdRoom, field always 0 without bit 7). Counters appended to VCR_ESC_2D_STATS and vcr_info (eng_lost_total, eng_lost_last, d3dsafe); d3dprobe caps prints an engine block; d3dprobe_run.py REGREADs EngineLostCount before/after every run.
No caps change; not a rendering change (no single/multipass question). OLD PATH (bit 2 off): byte-identical register traffic and answers (DD_OK, accepted contexts, flips, HAL withheld, recovery at next PDEV) plus part A's record IOCTL and one DEBUG line. Coordination: G01 owns flag 0x8000, IOCTL 0xa10, escape +12, event 309; G02 takes 0xa11, +13, 804, 514; recommend an appended vcr_info.d3dsafe instead of per-bit VCR_INFO_F flags (siblings already collide on 0x8000/0x10000, 513/24-25, 309; G01's 512/10 collides with the existing text-punt line vcrdd_punt.c:549). G02 generalises G01's give_up hook (bit 0 + CMD-busy status, or bit 2 for any stall). Vendor reference: none usable - VH5 has no hang recovery (its FIFO wait was unbounded; the vintage lane's CFIFO.C wedge-break pretends there is room - not to copy) and answers SURFACELOST only in #ifndef WINNT code (DDSURF.C:1733-1742, DDOVL32.C:230-250), so a driver-originated SURFACELOST on XP is measured before it is trusted. THE GAP IS REAL, BUT IT AFFECTS DIFFERENT TITLES THAN LISTED.

- I read the XP SP3 runtimes (d3d8.dll / d3d9.dll 5.3.2600.5512):
  - IDirect3DDevice8::ValidateDevice = vtable slot 64 -> 0x6d9d91a0 -> DDI 0x6d9e0520/0x6d9e0f70 (d3d9: 0x4fe769f0/0x4fe79560).
  - The DDI runs the per-stage texture update and a flush before calling the driver, so our walker has the current TSS (labels inferred from the code shape; call order read).
  - It then copies dwNumPasses and returns the driver's ddrval to the app unchanged. There is no runtime-side check: our answer IS the answer.

WHO ACTUALLY ASKS (static scan of the staged binaries, calls through the ValidateDevice vtable slot):

THE RULE: answer 1 pass/D3D_OK exactly when compute_regs draws the current state as D3D defines it. Otherwise answer 0 passes and the D3DERR code of the first failing stage/channel.
- Stage count, as 3dfx (VH5/D6MT.C:3222-3253): stop at the first DISABLE colour op, or at a stage whose colour op samples TEXTURE with no texture handle.
- Exactly drawn today:
  - stage-0 colour: SELECT of {D,C,T,F}; MODULATE/ADD with at least one of {D,C}; BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA(x, D|C); BLENDTEXTUREALPHA(T, D|C);
  - stage-0 alpha: DISABLE/SELECT/MODULATE/ADD likewise;
  - modifiers: none on colour arguments; ALPHAREPLICATE allowed on alpha arguments. No SPECULAR/TEMP;
  - stage 1 is classed PASS / REPLACE / MULT / ADD, and order-checked against stage 0 per channel: REPLACE and ADD need stage 0 SELECT(T); MULT needs SELECT(T) or MODULATE(T, D|C);
  - a stage-0 BLENDTEXTUREALPHA needs stage 1 to be PASS in both channels (the factor comes from the TMU alpha).
- Error codes:
  - stage 2 enabled: TOOMANYOPERATIONS;
  - a bound texture view_of() refuses: WRONGTEXTUREFORMAT;
  - MODULATE2X/4X, ADDSIGNED, SUBTRACT, BLENDCURRENTALPHA and the rest: UNSUPPORTEDCOLOROPERATION / UNSUPPORTEDALPHAOPERATION;
  - unsupported arguments and modifiers: UNSUPPORTEDCOLORARG / UNSUPPORTEDALPHAARG.

New test 'validate'. It needs a device, so it lives in render mode, explicit at first (--tests validate). It joins the default list once bit 0 is the default. Its stage-0 MODULATE2X cell is runtime-27's 'ValidateDevice of MODULATE2X'.

Cells (about 41):
- 25 single-stage: every row of the rule table, including MODULATE2X/4X, ADDSIGNED, SUBTRACT, BLENDCURRENTALPHA, MODULATE(T,TFACTOR), reversed BLENDTEXTUREALPHA, COMPLEMENT, ALPHAREPLICATE on colour versus alpha, SPECULAR, DOTPRODUCT3, alpha DISABLE.

- 1 three-stage.

Inputs: two 64x64 A4R4G4B4 solid textures (offered on every path, alpha exact): T0 = (a66, r88, g44, bcc) and T1 = (bb, 33, aa, 55). Diffuse 0x99c08040, TFACTOR 0x7020a0e0.

For each cell:
1. Set the TSS and textures.
2. Call ValidateDevice(&n).
3. Draw quad_t2 twice: blend off, then SRCALPHA/ZERO over black, to read alpha as colour.
4. Read the centre pixel back.

Expectations:
- The expected (hr, n) comes from the same vcr_tssval.h compiled into the probe. honest and feat are read from HKLM\...\vcrmp\Diag\D3DFeat and recorded in the RESULT.
- The expected pixels come from vcr_texop_ref.h.
- Both apply only when GetAdapterIdentifier names vcrdd.dll; on any other driver the answers are reported only.

Pass criterion:
- Answers:
  - armed: every cell's (hr, n) equals vcr_tssval's;
  - unarmed: every cell is (D3D_OK, 1), which pins the old answer.
- Pixels:
  - armed: every ACCEPTED cell is within ±10 per channel at 16 bpp (±5 at 32 bpp) of the reference, blended and unblended;
  - refused cells are reported as 'approx got/ref', with no verdict. In an unarmed run they are the on-silicon evidence of the gap.
- The three-stage cell: if the stage-2 counter in vsum stays 0, the runtime does not forward stage 2. That is recorded as a runtime fact, not as a HAL failure.

RESULT gains "validate":{armed, feat, cells, answer_ok, answer_bad, render_ok, render_bad, approx}.

The gap is real and fixable, but nothing is broken on .124 today. D3D32=1 and D3DBigTex=7 have been set explicitly there since 2026-09-28, and the ring confirms both on 11-12 (513/16, 513/18). What G20 protects is the next install: a re-image of .124 (it has been re-imaged before), a REGDELETE of Services\vcrmp\Diag (which wipes every switch), or a second VSA-100 box.

**Two default flips, made in the miniport only.**
- Step 1: vcrmp.c:244 becomes `x->d3dbigtex = VcrDiagGet(L"D3DBigTex", 7)`. It has no prerequisite, and it also fixes G21 on the VSA-100.
- Step 2: vcrmp.c:238 becomes `x->d3d32 = VcrDiagGet(L"D3D32", 1)`. This waits for G10. With D3D32 off, an X8R8G8B8 back buffer is refused before the runtime's mode set. With it on and D16, our ContextCreate refuses after the mode set, so the CRT gets 4 sync changes.
- An explicit value still decides: 0 = off, and D3DBigTex 1/2/4 picks one bit.
- The vcr_info flags stay positive, and vcrdd_2d.c:453/463-466 still requires `napalm && flag`. So vcrdd.dll needs no code change and no redeploy. A Banshee/Voodoo3, the 86Box bed and any older miniport see nothing new.
- This matches 3dfx's shipped Napalm defaults: 32BPP_RENDERING is on when absent (VH5/D3INIT.C:1035-1039), and ARGB8888, DXT1-5 and 2048 are unconditional (:2169-2240, :3190-3196).

**New finding 1: the flip as written would quietly break Thief II.**
- Its staged launcher (stage-fleetres.py newdark_display_swap, giving Play Thief 2.bat:15-19) reads the Diag VALUES. With the values absent it would fall back to DX6 at 640x480.
- The generator's own note, "DELETE THIS BLOCK the day vcr-kmd offers those by default", is wrong too, because a box can still run a pre-G20 miniport where absent means off.
- Part 1: the miniport writes a VOLATILE key, Services\vcrmp\InForce, in VcrFindAdapter.
  - Values: D3D32, D3DBigTex & 7 (both only for device 0x0009, the display driver's own test), D3D, and Boot = BootCount.
  - It uses ZwCreateKey with REG_OPTION_VOLATILE. No new imports, no hardware access, logged as event 804.
  - The key vanishes at shutdown, so after a rollback it can never be misread as the old driver's state.
- Part 2: the launcher reads InForce, and falls back to the Diag values (with their old meaning) when the key is absent.

**Part 0 (now):** correct the docs that still call D3DBigTex unproven: README rows, Status and roadmap item 6, tests/README.md:239, the test docstrings, PLAN:1120, the roster note, and a FINDINGS entry.

ROOT CAUSE, found from static evidence (strong, not yet proven on silicon): X8R8G8B8. Neither a combine bug (G13/G12/G14/G28) nor a missing luminance format causes the square.

(1) The frames show an additive quad of one flat colour.
- 11-12 timedemo, 60 s: a 244x244 px square at x 620-863, y 343-586 reads (47,92,105) over the black sky. The light beam goes from (81,84,99) outside to (122,173,201) inside, which matches the additive prediction (128,176,204).
- 09-28 menu: three squares, each adding (38,53,36) to the nebula behind it.

(2) Our HAL draws a stage whose texture handle is 0 in the vertex colour.
- `vcrdd_d3d.c:690-691` and `:725-726` select the iterated colour and alpha when an op reads TEXTURE and no texture is bound.
- 3dfx's HAL does the same (`D6MT.C:4378-4409`).
- So a flat additive square is exactly an additive sprite whose texture does not exist.

(3) `halo.exe` creates every 2D bitmap in one function with no fallback.
- The function at `0x523fa0` maps the bitmap's format through a constant `.rdata` table at VA `0x65e040`.
- It calls `CreateTexture` with `D3DPOOL_MANAGED`. On failure the texture slot stays NULL.
- This table is the one that turned the menu white when DXT2/DXT4 were not listed (fixed in `4ef226e`).
- Table index 10, `x8r8g8b8`, maps to `D3DFMT_X8R8G8B8`.
- With `D3DBigTex`=7, `.124` offers every other entry; it never offers X8R8G8B8 (`vcrdd_d3d.c:2081-2097`; `pf_tmfmt` also refuses alpha mask 0).

(4) Every one of Halo's 30 maps holds 2D X8R8G8B8 bitmaps (a host-side parser of `MAPS/*.map`):
- every lens flare (`flares_generic`, `flares_generic2`, `soft flares`, weapon and vehicle flares), with full mip chains, the shape in RGB and the X byte always 255;
- Halo's own fallback textures (`rasterizer\default 2d`);
- the menu starfield and space backdrop;
- a30's dusk-sky gradient;
- the multiplayer join icons.

There are ZERO a8/y8/ay8/a8y8 bitmaps, and `halo.exe` maps those formats to -1 anyway. The luminance theory (`runtime.md` §4.5) is refuted for Halo. visual-12's alignment attribution is also wrong: an unaligned DXT read gives noise, not flat additive colour.

FIX: offer X8R8G8B8 and read its alpha as 1.
- Exposure: the runtime converts a 32-bit `DDPF_RGB` entry without alpha into `X8R8G8B8` with `OP_TEXTURE` (`runtime.md` §4.1).
- Format list: `VcrDdD3dHalInfo` appends one entry LAST, `{DDPF_RGB, 32, 0xff0000/0xff00/0xff, A 0}`, only when `pd->tex_x8`.
- Classification moves into a new Win32-free `include/vcr_texfmt.h`. X8R8G8B8 classifies as kind ARGB32, `TM_FORMAT(15)` (0xf00), `alpha_one`=1, so `ext_layout`, `mipchain_ext`, the TMU flush and sampling all accept it. TEXBLT copies by bytes per pixel and needs no change.
- `tmu_view` gains `alpha_one`. `compute_regs` applies it at its three textureMode sites:
  - one texture: `TM_TC_REPLACE|TM_TCA_ONE` (0x41000|0x24000000) instead of `TM_TCA_REPLACE` (0x08200000);
  - two textures, TMU1 (stage 0): `TM_TCA_ONE`;
  - two textures, TMU0 (stage 1's local), through `vcr_tca_alpha_one`: REPLACE becomes ONE, MULT becomes PASS, ADD becomes ONE, PASS stays PASS.
- `TM_TCA_ONE` = (1<<26)|(1<<29) is Glide's `SST_TCA_ONE` (`h3defs.h:374`). The FBI alpha select, BLENDTEXTUREALPHA, the alpha test and the blend then all read 1.0 whatever the X byte holds. RGB is untouched.
- Single pass. No other cap changes.
- With the switch off, the format list and registers are byte-for-byte unchanged.

G21.approach:
The gap is real and fixable. Most of the fix already runs on .124 every day under D3DBigTex=7.

Verified from the code and from host arithmetic (vcr_texlod.c compiled into a scratch harness):
(1) Placement. VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain's default branch (vcrdd_d3d.c:537-539) places only TEXTURE|MIPMAP surfaces. Every single-level texture lands where DirectDraw's linear heap puts it, on a 4-byte boundary; XP ignores dwTextureAlign. texBaseAddr keeps bits 25:4, so such a texture is sampled 4/8/12 bytes early, which shifts its rows by 2/4/6 texels.
Render-target textures (3DDEVICE) keep dxg's placement on both paths (:389-391). colBufferAddr also drops bits 3:0, so rendering into one writes up to 12 bytes into the surface before it (inferred from SPEC §8.40).
(2) Address width. This is worse than "16 MB lower". .124 runs the V5 6000 in its 256 MB VBIOS mode, so chip 0 has 64 MB and the heap reaches about 63 MB (ring seq 24681; the README's "27 MB" is stale).
- With the 24-bit field a texture is read at its address modulo 16 MB: 16, 32 or 48 MB low.
- A texture in the first ~170 KB of the heap, whose LOD-0 base lies "below zero", is read 16 MB high.
(3) Adjacent, the same arithmetic on both paths: a 16 bpp texture whose top is 1x1 is read 8 bytes early, because its absent levels sum to 174760, which is 8 modulo 16.
- It is the only one of 273 shapes with a non-zero phase.
- Glide shifts the data by that remainder (ditex.c:1781-1787), and 3dfx placed 1x1 textures 8 bytes in (D3TXTR.C:877-889).

The design: a new Diag\D3DTexPlace, read at boot, absent = 0.

Bit 0 is OR-ed into pd->tex_ext. Exactly four sites read tex_ext:
- the allocator, mipchain_ext;
- the view, tex_view_ext/ext_layout;
- flush_written's ext branch;
- VcrDd3dTexFlush's lin.
So the default path's 16 bpp textures up to 256 are then:
- driver-placed, 16-byte aligned, single levels included, pitch w x 2;
- sampled through the 26-bit munged texBaseAddr on a VSA-100;
- flushed with the proven write-back rule (below 16 MB only).
ext_flags becomes chip-aware, (napalm ? NAPALM : 0) | BIG. On a Banshee/Voodoo3 (the 86Box bed) the bit then gives placement only, and flags 0 equals vcr_texlod_compute field for field.
Bit 0 also adds the 1x1 phase on every path:
- vcr_tex_chain_pad(kind,w,h) is derived from the absent levels: 8 for RGB16 1x1, else 0.
- The top goes at block+8, SF_PAD8 is set, and VcrDdD3dFreeMipChain frees fpVidMem-8.
- A per-level mip call (DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT > 1) is not padded, because that is G07's contiguity problem.

Bit 1 (it implies bit 0) lets mipchain_ext also place render-target textures (DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE):
- 16-byte aligned, pitch w x bytes, which is a legal 3D target and samplable at the same time;
- G36's placement prerequisite.

No caps change: max size, the format list and FOURCC still follow tex_big/tex_dxt/tex_32. On a VSA-100, bit 0 writes the registers .124's daily BigTex=7 path writes for every 16 bpp texture up to 256 (408 size x offset cases identical, host-checked). It changes only what is mis-addressed today.

Part 0 is log-only and default-on:
- vcr_tex_read_at(kind,w,h,reg,chipflags) gives where the TMU really reads a texture's top, under the SPEC L6091 wrap rule.
- compute_regs counts the bound textures it reads elsewhere and WARNs on the first 8.
- target_of counts a target or Z that is off the 16-byte grid.
- An INFO summary at context end reports both. That measures the gap in every title.

Rejected as the primary route:
- Answering GUID_GetHeapAlignment (runtime-13): it cannot fix the address width or the 1x1 phase, that XP honours it is inferred, it moves every surface, and a 16-byte texture pitch would break 1/2/4-wide textures. It is kept as an investigation (Diag\DdHeapAlign) built only if Part 0's target counter fires or windowed odd-width targets are needed.
- Defaulting D3DBigTex on (G20): it changes caps for every title, and the Voodoo3 bed would keep the bug.
- Editing tex_view and the old branch in place: that duplicates proven code.
The design is in KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G21.md.

- the miniport maps bit 0 and bit 1 to two new positive VCR_INFO_F flags (take the next free bits; 0x8000 and 0x10000 are already claimed by other designs);
- the display sets pd->tex_place on any chip, and pd->rtt_place;
- bit 1 implies bit 0.

Off: tex_ext is exactly today's, and the default branch, tex_view, the old flush, the caps and ext_flags' value on every VSA-100 are byte-for-byte today's. test_off_the_hal_is_the_proven_one stays unchanged. With D3DTexPlace clear, D3DBigTex=7 stays the daily path byte-for-byte; arming bit 0 there adds only the 1x1 pad.

Part 0 (misaddress and off-grid counters) lands default-ON. It is log only, writes no register, and is pinned by a Python source test.

Bit 0 lands default-OFF. It is nearly safe to land default-on: on a VSA-100 its register writes equal the daily BigTex path for every 16 bpp texture up to 256 (408 cases), and it changes only what is mis-addressed today. It is not landed blind, because on a fresh install it moves every single-level texture from dxg to the HAL's single-pass allocator, which carries G63's unproven offset-0 risk.
- Graduation, after one supervised clean boot (boot B) plus the 86Box bed run: the default becomes 1 with a MOVED_DIAG entry, and 0 is then the kill switch. The flip covers every chip.

Bit 1 stays default-off until G36's render-to-texture round trip (with G37's flush) passes on silicon.

Part C (GetHeapAlignment) is not built unless Part 0's target counter fires.

One Diag change per clean boot; safe-reboot.py after an activation check.
G21.d3dprobe_test:
Four new explicit tests plus the existing texhigh. Shared rules:
- each runs in its own fullscreen invocation, first on a fresh heap;
- spacers and probes are D3DPOOL_DEFAULT textures, placed in creation order and filled by UpdateTexture (DP2 TEXBLT), because D3D8 refuses LockRect on DEFAULT textures;
- a spacer is a 2x1 R5G6B5 (4 bytes); poison is 0x804020;
- tolerance is ±12 per channel against the 565 expansion.

texalign: three instances; instance n (1..3) is n spacers, then a 32x32 R5G6B5 probe of the LCG texels from test_dxt_decode (seed 12345), drawn one texel a pixel, point sampled, MIPFILTER NONE, every texel compared.
- PASS: 0 of 1024 texels wrong in all three.
- Default path today: whatever phase p the heap starts at, the probes land at p+4, p+12 and p+8, so at least 2 of 3 are off the grid, shifted 2/4/6 texels: FAIL.

tex1x1: three instances; instance k (0..2) is k spacers, a 4x4 poison block, then a 1x1 R5G6B5 of 0x00ff00. A 64x64 quad samples it, and the centre is read.
- PASS: all three 0x00ff00.
- BigTex path today: it reads the poison 8 bytes before: FAIL. With bit 0's pad: PASS.

texhigh (exists): 20 MB of grey fills, then 64x64 cells.
- PASS: the five cells right.
- Default path: it reads 16 MB lower, into grey: FAIL. BigTex and bit 0: PASS.

texhigh40: the same with 40 MB of fills, so the probe needs address bit 25 = register bit 1.
- PASS: the five cells right; SKIPPED if fewer than 34 MB were placed.
- Default path reads 32 MB lower: FAIL. This is the first probe proof of the bit-25 munge, so far inferred from UT2003's 60 MB textures.

rtt_align (bit 1): three instances of n poison spacers, then a 64x64 R5G6B5 RENDERTARGET texture. SetRenderTarget(level 0, no Z), Clear green, a blue quad over the right half, restore the back buffer. Then sample each spacer for the first time (a cold TMU cache), and the render target's corners.
- PASS: every spacer texel still poison, and the corners as drawn.
- dxg's placement puts at least 2 of 3 off the grid and their clears overwrite the spacers: FAIL.
- Corners wrong with the spacers intact means G37/G36, not placement.

The default render list (40/40 fullscreen, 42/42 windowed) and the 11-12 texture lists must stay unchanged.
G21.regression_test:
New tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_texplace.c. It #includes common/vcr_texlod.c and is picked up by run_all.sh's glob. Each check asserts the old value and the fixed one.

the_tmu_reads_a_default_path_texture_from_somewhere_else: vcr_tex_read_at of vcr_texlod_compute's register against vcr_texlod_compute_ext(NAPALM), with VSA-100 chip flags. A 64x64 R5G6B5:
- at 0x1400000 reads 0x0400000 (old), then itself;
- at 0x2800000 reads 0x0800000, then itself, with register 0x07d8002;
- at 0x3d4f000 reads 0x0d4f000, then itself;
- at 0x0010000 reads 0x1010000 (16 MB high), then itself.

the_base_cannot_fix_placement: at 0x0100004 the texture reads 0x0100000 (−4) through both functions. A texture placed at 0x0100010 reads itself.

a_16bpp_1x1_needs_the_8_byte_phase:
- vcr_tex_chain_pad(RGB16,1,1) = 8 (old: no pad).
- At 0x0900000 it reads 0x08ffff8; at 0x0900008 it reads itself.
- A8R8G8B8 1x1 has pad 0, so 3dfx's unconditional +8 would be wrong for it.

only_the_16bpp_1x1_has_a_phase: exhaustive over 273 shapes (every kind, to 2048, aspect at most 8). Exactly one non-zero pad. For every shape, an aligned block + pad gives read_at(compute_ext(...)) equal to the texture's address. This cross-checks the new helper against the proven function.

bit_0_is_the_daily_bigtex_path_for_16bpp_textures: compute_ext with NAPALM and with NAPALM|BIG are identical for 51 RGB16 sizes x 8 offsets (408 cases).

a_voodoo3_gets_placement_only: 24-bit wrap; flags 0 equals vcr_texlod_compute.

New tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_texplace.py:
- The switch is read at boot, absent = 0, with two distinct flag bits.
- tex_ext = big|dxt|32|tex_place, and tex_place is not napalm-gated.
- tex_ext still has exactly four readers.
- The old branch still requires TEXTURE|MIPMAP: the old buggy rule, which is what "off" means. mipchain_ext requires only TEXTURE: the fix.
- The caps never read tex_place or tex_ext.
- ext_flags is chip-aware.
- The pad is applied only under tex_place and the mip-level guard, and freed only under SF_PAD8.
- The 3DDEVICE exclusion carries !pd->rtt_place.
- The Part 0 block writes no register.
- One compiled check through both views' entry points: a 64x64 at 20 MB reads 0x0400000 on the default path and 0x1400000 on the placing path.

Updates: test_vcr_kmd_bigtex.py (the tex_ext arming line and the ext_flags text, a deliberate change), and test_vcr_kmd_integration.py (NEW_DIAG D3DTexPlace=0, later MOVED_DIAG 1).
G21.risk:
Switch off: none. Registers, allocation and dxg's call pattern are today's. Part 0 adds an integer check at state recompute and at most 8 WARNs plus one INFO per context (G52 cost per context, not per draw).

Bit 0 on a VSA-100:
- Register-identical to the daily BigTex path for 16 bpp textures up to 256. It differs from today's default path only where that path is wrong.
- Every single-level texture's allocation moves from dxg to HeapVidMemAllocAligned, the same call .124 has made for every texture since 11-08.
- G63's offset-0 loss applies only to a texture that is a fresh heap's first allocation (inferred rare: titles create the flip chain and Z first). DdHeapFloor cures it.
- The write-back decision is unchanged; the old range test is reproduced (pinned).
- Allocation costs at most 12 bytes per texture, plus 8 for a 1x1.

Bit 0 on a Banshee/Voodoo3 (the 86Box bed): placement only, with the 24-bit field.

Bit 1: render-target textures become driver-allocated; the target rules are unchanged. Flip chains carry no DDSCAPS_TEXTURE, so the flip path is untouched.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence: none. There is no new register traffic, only DirectDraw-heap surfaces are affected, and exclusive Glide ownership still draws nothing.

SLI: none. D3D is chip 0 only; a future SLI D3D (G51) must replicate placed textures on every chip, unaffected by this item.

Shared code with G07 (vcr_tex_chain_pad, SF_PAD8): coordinate which switch owns the pad. The proposal is D3DTexPlace bit 0.

Residual unknown: the 26-bit munge above 32 MB is inferred from UT2003, not probed. texhigh40 settles it. If it failed, that would also be a defect of today's BigTex path.

G19.approach:
VERDICT: the gap is real, but neither symptom is a driver defect. Both are game-side policies keyed on the PCI vendor id 0x121a, which vcrdd reports correctly. They were settled by static analysis of the staged binaries: pefile + capstone on the host, cross-references of the UTF-16 log strings, and field offsets taken from Engine.dll StaticConstructor property registrations. No box was contacted.

(1) WHY 16 BPP.
- Both D3DDrv.dll builds (UT2003 md5 04c412ca…, UT2004 md5 b6bb4d87…) run a vendor detection: UT2003 0x1000f985-0x1000fdad, UT2004 0x100111b0-0x100115f5.
- For vendor 0x121a, at ANY device id, it sets an unregistered URenderDevice flag (UT2003 +0x64, UT2004 +0x70). The flag sits between Use16bitTextures and LowQualityTerrain, so no ini key can touch it. Matrox G200/G400/G550 and 36 S3 ids get the same flag; Banshee/V3 (device < 9) get more.
- SetRes then forces ColorBytes=2 (UT2003 0x1000ff48, UT2004 0x10011785). WinDrv's TryRenderDevice passes 0, so without the flag Use16bit from the ini would decide. With it, Use16bit=1, which gives R5G6B5 (23) + D16 (80).
- Use16bit=False and Diag\D3D32 therefore cannot matter: the driver is never asked for 32 bpp.
- UE2's format rules (read): back buffer 22 if 32 bpp else 23. Z is D16 only if Use16bit, otherwise D24S8 if UseStencil, otherwise D24X8. Fallbacks are D32 then D24S8; a failure is a fatal 'Error setting display mode' dialog. So UE2 NEVER pairs D16 with X8R8G8B8, and visual-08's G10 lead is refuted for UE2.
- The flag also does two more things:
  - ApplyTexModifier: env-map texgen (TCS 10/11) becomes world coords, and non-projected coords get TTF COUNT2.
  - SetShaderMaterial: the Specular/SpecularityMask layers of Shaders are cleared (inferred from code and strings).
- Epic's own switch -nodeviceid skips the detection, so the flag stays 0.

(2) WHY UT2003 RUNS AT 640x480.
- UT2003.exe (md5 1f78f4ff…) WinMain (0x1090d80d) calls AutoConfigure (0x10905ec0) whenever GIsClient && FirstRun==0.
- The staged UT2003.ini AND Default.ini carry [FirstRun] FirstRun=0. UT2004's staged inis carry 3369, so its identical code (3dfx branch at 0x10907f40) never runs.
- For vendor 0x121a, AutoConfigure writes into the in-memory config: FullScreenViewportX/Y=640/480, Projectors=False, NoDynamicLights=True (branch at 0x10906fcb). This lands after the launcher wrote 1280x960.
- On .124 (58 MB, MaxSimultaneousTextures 2) it also writes DetailTextures=False, UseTrilinear=False, SuperHighDetailActors=False and lower texture detail.
- Log signature: 'Init: D3D Device: Video memory on board: 58' (UT2003.log:23). That line is printed only by this code.
- InitEngine raises FirstRun to 2225 only in memory. A later GAMESYNC restores the library's 0, because the game rewrites the GAMERES-ledger file on exit.
- GAMERES VERIFY reads the file and can call a 640x480 run 'ok'.
- MenuViewportX/Y is ruled out:
  - XInterface GUIPage.CheckResolution uses TEMPSETRES 640x480 only below 640x480;
  - WinDrv starts from FullscreenViewportX/Y (UClient +0x68/+0x6c);
  - UT2004 has the same MenuViewport and runs 1280x960.
- history.md:599 'UT2004 at 1280x960x32' cannot have happened (G80).

PLAN.
(A) Fix the LIBRARY, a correctness fix:
- FirstRun=0 → 2225 in LIB/UT2003/System/UT2003.ini and Default.ini. This is +3 bytes, so GAMESYNC sees it. Publish via libwrite/sharewrite with per-file read-back and no generation bump.
- Effect on .124: the launcher's 1280x960 holds; the staged detail returns; colour depth stays 16 bpp.
- Effect on other boxes: the per-launch detail auto-tune stops. That matches UT2004, and it also ends the latent overrides (3dfx → 640x480; under 16 MB VRAM → 320x240 or 512x384).
- Add a WARN in validate-staged-library.py ue2_config_problems() for FirstRun 0/empty/missing in UT2003.ini, UT2004.ini or Default.ini.

(B) Keep UE2 at 16 bpp by default:
- It is Epic's path for this vendor and what a real V5 ran.
- The VSA-100's 2PPC is 15/16 bpp only (G50).
- Frame time today is DrawPrimitive-bound.
- Measure 32 bpp once with -nodeviceid (E3). Only if the user chooses it, generate a per-box launcher block ue2_vcrkmd_depth() in stage-fleetres.py, modelled on newdark_display_swap:
  - it applies when vcrmp is RUNNING and Diag\D3D32=0x1;
  - it adds -nodeviceid to the start line and writes Use16bit=False;
  - it is two-way, and is never active on a non-vcr-kmd box or a D3D32-off box, where UE2 would fatal.

(C) Add a d3dprobe 'ue2fmt' mode that replays UE2's vendor check and DetermineFormats. It creates no device and makes no mode switch.

(D) Recommend a NEW plan item for the 16 bpp image quality 3dfx shipped:
- the 2x2 dither matrix (VH5/D3RSTATE.C:3500; we use 4x4);
- overlay-promotion scan-out with the vidProcCfg[17:16] 2x2/4x4 filter and vidMaxRGBDelta 0x1F0F1F (VH5/DDFXNT.C:2552-2700), off in AA, 4x4 or point only in SLI.

Considered and rejected:
- vendor-id spoofing: the PnP identity, the runtime's 121a:0009 driver-flag table, and every other title's 3dfx path would all move;
- a D3DDrv binary patch;
- a per-box-only FirstRun fix.

G28.approach:
The gap is real, as filed. Three defects share the blend code.
(1) Targets without alpha (every 16 bpp target, and every 32 bpp flip-chain back buffer, which is X8R8G8B8 because fill_pixfmt reports no alpha mask): blend_src/blend_dst pass DESTALPHA, INVDESTALPHA and SRCALPHASAT to the chip (vcrdd_d3d.c:636-640, 659-660). The chip then reads whatever the alpha byte holds. At 32 bpp that is the last clear colour's alpha (FASTFILL stores color1[31:24], SPEC L2703) or the last source alpha. Direct3D defines it as 1.
(2) Targets with alpha (A8R8G8B8 render-target or offscreen surfaces at 32 bpp): compute_regs always writes AM_ASRC(ONE)|AM_ADST(ZERO) (:995-998), so a blended draw stores unblended source alpha.
(3) Caps: SRCALPHASAT is advertised (Src 0x1f33) and has never been checked on silicon; DESTALPHA/INVDESTALPHA are not advertised, yet the code sends them to the chip.

FIX, three parts. The whole mapping moves into a new Win32-free header, KMD/include/vcr_blend.h, executed by a host test.
(A) Default ON. On a target without alpha, the RGB factors DSTALPHA->ONE, 1-DSTALPHA->ZERO, SATURATE->ZERO. These are exactly the values of 3dfx's PRS 8373 substitution (VH5/D6DP2.C:6233-6313), which 3dfx applied on every Napalm draw at any depth. Here it is applied only where D3D says the target alpha is 1. The alpha-channel fields stay ONE/ZERO. At 16 bpp ONE/ZERO is the only legal pair (SPEC L2974-2983).
(B) Diag\D3DFeat bit DSTALPHA, default OFF, VSA-100 with rt32 only. G26.approach:
Real and fixable; no investigation needed first. For ONE textured stage the VSA-100 does trilinear in a single pass. It uses both TMUs and one copy of the chain, exactly as 3dfx's own HAL does for this chip (VH5/D6MT.C:5453-5526, the D3DTP_LINEAR row, HOME_BOTH column; VH5/D3TXTR.C:2189-2193) and as Glide does in UMA mode (GL5 gtex.c:1410-1416). For TWO textured stages there is no one-pass hardware path; 3dfx's draw path dithered the LOD instead (VH5/D6MT.C:5931-5933, 6097-6099).

When it applies:
- Exactly one textured stage has MIPFILTER = LINEAR (the runtime hands a DX7 driver D3DTFP_LINEAR = 3).
- The texture is a driver-placed chain with at least 2 sampled levels.

Register words for that case:
- TMU0 textureMode = view bits | 0x4EC76000. That is SST_TRILINEAR (bit 30), plus TC/TCA_BLEND_LODFRAC (sub_clocal, mselect 5 = LOD_frac, add_clocal), plus TC/TCA_REVERSE_BLEND. For R5G6B5 bilinear the word is 0x4EC76A0F; today it is REPLACE, 0x08241A0F.
- TMU0 tLOD = the view's tLOD, with no LOD_ODD, no TSPLIT and LOD bias 0.
- TMU1 textureMode = view bits | 0x48241000 (TRILINEAR | TC_REPLACE | TCA_REPLACE).
- TMU1 tLOD = TMU0's final tLOD | SST_LOD_ODD (bit 18). TMU1 texBaseAddr = TMU0's, so one copy serves both TMUs (tsplit = 0). tDetail = 0 on both.
- sSetupMode stays W0|ST0: the spec says S/W0, T/W0 and sWtmu0 go to all TMUs. So there are no extra per-vertex writes, and the FBI does not change.
- How the blend works (86Box model): the TMU with LOD_ODD clear fetches the even level, TMU1 the odd one, and the reverse sense flips at odd LODs. So the finer level always gets 1−f. At either end of the LOD range f = 0, so the level one past LODMAX has weight 0. Trilinear is never armed for a single-level texture.

Two textured stages with MIPFILTER LINEAR: set TLODDITHER (bit 4) and a +0.25 LOD bias (3dfx's LB_DITH) on that stage's TMU, behind its own bit. Otherwise those draws stay today's nearest.

Caps: with TRILIN armed, TextureFilterCaps gains MIPLINEAR | LINEARMIPLINEAR | MIPFLINEAR (0x03010317 -> 0x0303033F, 3dfx's value), in both the triangle and line caps. Unreal Engine 2 reads the cap: today's UT2003.log on .124 has no "Supports trilinear".

Code changes:
- New Win32-free header include/vcr_texfilt.h: vcr_tf_decide (NONE/TRI/DITHER/NEAREST), vcr_tf_single, vcr_tf_dither, vcr_tf_lodbias. The driver and the native test compile the same code. New TM_/TL_ bit names go into vcr_3dregs.h.
- tmu_view gains `levels`.
- compute_regs applies the words and derives TMU1's tLOD last, after the G27 and G33 contributors.
- vcr3d_regs gains tmu1_tri. VcrDd3dState writes the existing TMU1 block when textured1 || tmu1_tri.
- prepare clears tmu1_tri in its untextured fallback. log_combo prints tm1.
- prim_caps(c, tri) adds the cap bits.
- Per-context counters (none/tri/dither/nearest) are logged at context end. They are log-only and on by default, so they also show which titles send LINEAR without the cap.

Single pass only, no multipass. Old path: with both switch bits clear the decision yields today's words, write sequence and caps byte for byte, and tests pin this.

A MesaFX note says "Napalm can't do single-pass trilinear" (fxddtex.c:328; fxsetup.h:630 "XXX todo - GR_CMBX_LOD_FRAC?"). That is a limit of MesaFX's combine-extension path, not of the chip.

Contracts with other gaps:
- G03: TMU combineMode selects must be 0 and 2ppc off.
- G12: an FBI-placed single stage leaves TMU0 free.
- G50: trilinear forces 1 pixel per clock.
- G15: the validation answer.

G26.gating:
Default OFF, behind two positive Diag\D3DFeat bits read at boot:
- TRILIN (proposed 0x400) gives the caps and single-stage trilinear.
- LODDITHER (proposed 0x800) gives the TLODDITHER stand-in for LINEAR-mip stages that cannot get trilinear.
- The final bit numbers come from whoever lands the D3DFeat register header and the appended vcr_info.d3dfeat word first. Other designs already claim bits 0, 1, 4 and 6-8.

Where it can arm: only on two-TMU chips, the VSA-100 (device 0x0009) and the Voodoo3 (0x0004/0x0005). The Voodoo3 is included so the 86Box bed can smoke-test the armed path. A Banshee never arms.

With both bits clear, the caps (0x03010317), the TMU words and the register write sequence are today's byte for byte. A native test and a python test pin this. The per-context counters are CPU-only logging and are on by default.

It is NOT safe to land default-on now, for two reasons:
- It changes the caps, so UE2, Red Faction and NewDark change their own mip filter.
- It sets bits that no stack of ours has ever set on this silicon: TRILINEAR, the LOD_frac blend, LOD_ODD and TLODDITHER.

Proving it: one Diag change per clean boot. TRILIN alone first, then LODDITHER, each in one supervised boot with the d3dprobe tests.

Graduating to default-on (a later one-line change) requires all four:
1. The trilinear* probes pass at 640x480x16 and 1024x768x32.
2. G03's baseline has landed (TMU combineMode = 0, 2ppc off), or the after-OpenGL probe run passes.
3. G07 has landed.
4. An in-game A/B shows no new artefact.

LODDITHER graduates separately.
G26.d3dprobe_test:
New explicit tests (never in the default list). Each chain level is a solid colour cycling red, green, blue, so adjacent levels differ in exactly two channels. f is the coarser level's fraction, read from those channels and averaged over 5 pixels (centre and ±40 px). Every quad keeps |S| < 8192, the 14.18 iterator limit (G89).

The expectation follows the caps. With MIPFLINEAR reported, the D3D blend reference applies. Without it, the OLD value applies: nearest by truncation, every φ = C_k. So one build gives both the before and the after evidence. The RESULT records "mipflinear", the measured f values and the Diag\D3DFeat value.

1. trilinear. A 64x64 R5G6B5 full chain (top = absolute LOD 2) with SELECTARG1(TEXTURE), MIN/MAG LINEAR and MIP LINEAR. Constant-LOD quads [32,224)^2 with rhw 1 and uv span 3*2^(k+φ), for k = 0, 1, 2 (absolute LODs 2, 3, 4: both parities) and φ = 0, .25, .5, .75.
   - Pass, φ = 0: C_k within tolerance 16. This catches a parity or reverse-blend error, which yields C_k+1.
   - Pass, φ > 0: |f − φ| ≤ 0.15, and f(.25) < f(.5) < f(.75).
   - Old value: C_k everywhere.
2. trilinear_odd. A 128x128 chain (top at odd absolute LOD 1).
   - Magnified at ratio 0.5: must be C_0.
   - k = 0, 1 at φ = 0 and .5: as in test 1.
3. trilinear_end. Textures with Levels = 2 (LODMAX odd) and Levels = 3 (LODMAX even), drawn at ratio 8, past the chain's end. Must show the last level's colour: the nonexistent level gets weight 0.
4. trilinear_ramp. A perspective quad (rhw 1 → 0.25, u 0 → 9) whose LOD runs from about −0.4 to 3.6.
   - Along row 128: largest adjacent-pixel step ≤ 40 per channel, and the row must run from C_0 to a C_2/C_3 mix. The row is dumped to the log.
   - Old value: a step ≥ 128 (a mip band).
5. trilinear2. Stage 0 is the chain with MIP LINEAR; stage 1 is a white 8x8 texture with MODULATE.
   - LODDITHER armed: φ = 0 gives ≥ 90% C_k; φ = .5 shows both levels at ≥ 10% each, with the coarse fraction in [0.15, 0.85]. The fractions are recorded.
   - Otherwise: all C_k.
6. trilinear2048. A TBIG 2048 chain, blending across the 512/256/128 levels around the base. Skipped below MaxTexture 2048.
7. trilinear_dxt5 and trilinear_8888. Run only after G07's mipdxt/mip8888 probes pass. Skipped where the format is not offered.

Plus perf --fill --mip point|linear: 8 full-screen minified quads per frame, reporting Mpix/s. It is for the fill-cost A/B with --novsync, measurement only.
G26.regression_test:
New tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_texfilt.c compiles include/vcr_3dregs.h and include/vcr_texfilt.h, the same code the driver runs. Every case asserts both the fixed value and the old-buggy value.

1. Switch off. LINEAR on a 7-level chain decides NEAREST with today's words: tm0 = 0x08241A0F, tl0 = 0x808, no TMU1 write. POINT and NONE decide NONE.
2. TRI words. tm0 = 0x4EC76A0F, tl0 = 0x808, tm1 = 0x48241A0F, tl1 = 0x40808, base1 = base, tmu1 = 1. Also asserts tm0 != 0x08241A0F, the old nearest word.
3. The words are 3dfx's HOME_BOTH LINEAR row. The SST_ macros are rebuilt from the h3defs.h bit definitions and checked against textureModeCombineT0/T1[LINEAR][BOTH] and tLodT0/T1 (VH5/D6MT.C:5453-5526).
4. TMU1 inherits TBIG, LODMAX 11, aspect and the mirror bits, and never TSPLIT.
5. levels = 1 is never trilinear; levels = 2 is.
6. Two textured stages: NEAREST with TRILIN alone. With LODDITHER: textureMode |= 0x10, LOD bias field 0x1000, and no TRILINEAR or LOD_ODD.
7. A one-TMU chip, or a busy TMU0, falls back to DITHER or NEAREST.
8. vcr_tf_lodbias: 0x808 + 1 = 0x1808; −2 + 1 = −1 (0x3F000); clamps at −32 and +31; bits outside 17:12 untouched.
9. An exhaustive sweep: the decision is total, and returns TRI only when every TRI condition holds.

G26.risk:
Default path (switch off): none. Words, write sequence and caps are pinned equal to today's. Armed, any draw that is not a LINEAR mip on a chain also gets today's words.

Armed LINEAR-mip draws: medium. The bits have never been set on this silicon by any of our stacks, but 3dfx shipped exactly these words for this chip. The probe checks parity (even and odd top), the magnification clamp, the far-end clamp at odd and even LODMAX, and TBIG before any game.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence: medium, and of the same kind as today's two-stage path.
- A TMU's other/local selects always come from combineMode (SPEC §8.21). So a stale MesaFX combineMode, or a stale 2ppc bit (whose TMU writes reach both TMUs), corrupts trilinear just as it corrupts every TMU combine today.
- G03's baseline is a graduation precondition, and the after-OpenGL probe run checks it.
- Our TMU1 writes are ordinary per-draw state, which Glide re-programs at its next grTexSource (inferred).

SLI, the flip path and DirectDraw: untouched. D3D stays on chip 0; sliCtrl and chipMask are not written.

Stability: low. At the far clamp the second TMU reads one level past a chain's end at weight 0 — a VRAM read, as 3dfx's HAL also did (D3TXTR.C:1388-1391). There is no new FIFO or idle behaviour.

Performance:
- 4 more TMU1 writes per state change, only on single-stage LINEAR-mip draws. Today's frame is CPU/PIO-bound (116.7 of 123 ms in DrawPrimitive).
- Trilinear keeps both TMUs busy. That costs nothing at today's 1 pixel per clock, but rules out G50's 2 pixels per clock for those draws. perf --fill measures the cost.
- In game the fix is only as good as the chains (G07). A misplaced level shows on more pixels when two levels blend, so in-game judgement waits for G06/G07.

G22.approach:
The gap is real, fixable and small. Render state 47 (ZBIAS) is stored in c->rs[] and never read: compute_regs has no reference to it (checked with GNU grep -i). FZ_ZBIAS (vcr_3dregs.h:115) is never set. zaColor is written only by the clear (vcrdd_3d.c:160). RasterCaps lacks 0x4000.

New facts:
- Unreal Engine 2 already sends ZBIAS to our HAL, whatever the caps say (measured by disassembly). In both D3DDrv.dll builds (UT2004 md5 b6bb4d87, UT2003 md5 04c412ca), FD3DRenderInterface::SetZBias stores min(max(ZBias*5,0),15) in a deferred slot. The commit then calls SetRenderState(0x2f) whenever that value changed. The cap is only copied into a flag at +0x50 and printed as "Supports Z biasing". So UE2's biases of 5, 10 and 15 are drawn unbiased today.
- BF1942 calls SetRenderState(ZBIAS).
- Red Faction has no ZBIAS among its 53 SetRenderState call sites.
- Halo is D3D9 (DEPTHBIAS). Its DecalZBiasValue entries exist only for Radeons.
- The SPEC's adder sign-extends zaColor, adds and clamps. The biased depth is what gets compared and also what gets written.

Design:
1. New Win32-free header KMD/include/vcr_zbias.h: vcr_zbias_zacolor(rs_zbias, zfunc, fmt).
   - Level is clamped to 0..16; a negative LONG gives 0.
   - Magnitude is level<<1 at a 16 bpp target and level<<9 at 32 bpp: 3dfx's WinBench-tuned scale, the same fraction of the depth range in both.
   - The scale is keyed to the TARGET's 3D pixel size, the depth the engine iterates. It is NOT keyed to the desktop: 3dfx's GETPRIMARYBYTEDEPTH gave a 16 bpp target on a 32 bpp desktop 256x the bias. It is NOT keyed to the Z surface's storage either, because 16/16-in-32 is a 16-bit depth.
   - The value is negated (toward the viewer) for every ZFUNC except GREATER/GREATEREQUAL. This departs from 3dfx, who negated only LESS/LESSEQUAL, so an EQUAL pass at the same bias over a biased LESSEQUAL pass never matched.
   - The result is masked to 16 or 24 bits; 0 means off.
2. compute_regs: after the depth block, when pd->d3d_zbias and FZ_DEPTH are set and the value is non-zero, set FZ_ZBIAS, r->zaColor and r->zbias_on. vcr3d_regs gains zaColor and zbias_on.
3. VcrDd3dState: room becomes zbias_on ? 13 : 12, and zaColor is written after sSetupMode only when zbias_on. The first eight writes are unchanged.
4. No change to the clear. clear_rects already sets dirty=1 and prepared=0 after every clear (vcrdd_d3d.c:1419-1420), and every DP2 starts prepared=0, so the bias is re-sent with the state before any biased triangle. This is 3dfx's explicit zaColor restore after FastFill, obtained by construction. G47/G53 must keep this.
5. prim_caps(c, pd->d3d_zbias) adds D3DPRASTERCAPS_ZBIAS. Expected D3D8 RasterCaps armed: 00104191.
6. Log-only, default-on per-context counters zbias_max and zbias_sets, printed at "context gone", so an unarmed boot measures who sends ZBIAS.
7. Lazy: draws without a bias are byte-identical even when armed.
8. Plan B, only if the 32 bpp probe shows zaColor[23:0] is not sign-extended (sign extension is inferred from 3dfx's masks and Glide): add the bias to each vertex's sVz instead.
9. W-buffer (G23): the SPEC applies the bias to 1/W too. G23 decides the scale there.
10. Slope-scaled bias has no register.

Diag\D3DFeat bit 2 (VCR_D3DFEAT_ZBIAS, value 4), following hal.md section 10 Phase 2 numbering.
- Default OFF: absent = 0, and it is a positive bit, so an older miniport never arms it.
- Read at boot (FindAdapter), like D3D32/D3DBigTex, so the caps read at the desktop match the fullscreen PDEV.
- Carried to the display driver as the shared appended vcr_info.d3dfeat word (G05 section 4.2).
- Armed on any chip, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed can prove the 16-bit path.

Bit off: the register traffic, the waits and the caps are byte-for-byte today's. Only the log-only counters change.
Bit on: only depth-tested draws with ZBIAS != 0 change (fbzMode bit 16 plus one zaColor write). Every unbiased draw stays byte-identical.

Not safe to land default-on: non-zero zaColor has never been driven by this HAL, and at 32 bpp by nothing on the box. The cap also changes caps-checking titles' paths. After one supervised armed clean boot passes (the four probe tests at 16 and 32 bpp, the default list unchanged, UE2 no worse), it qualifies as a pure correctness fix: every changed draw is wrong today by construction. The default then flips in a separate commit, by the plan-wide D3DFeat default/kill-mask convention.

Fallback if the cap alone hurts a title: keep the drawing and move the cap to its own bit. UE2 sends ZBIAS without the cap anyway.

G22.d3dprobe_test:
Four explicit tests, never in the default list. All use untextured quad_c quads with back-buffer readback.
- Without D3DPRASTERCAPS_ZBIAS each test is SKIPPED, but still draws and logs its pixels, which records the old behaviour.
- With --noz they are skipped.
- Base depth z0=0.375. Decals sit at z0+k/65535: exact integer 16-bit LSBs, and 256.004k LSB24.

(1) zbias:
- Green base at z0 (LESSEQUAL, ZWRITE on).
- Then LESS with ZWRITE off: a red coplanar quad on the left half at ZBIAS 1, and on the right half at ZBIAS 0.
- Pass: (64,128) red (the bias-1 decal wins); (180,128) green (the control: equal depth fails LESS); (8,8) black.

(2) zbias_scale:
- Green base, then 8 strips per row, red at z0+k/65535, LESS.
- Row A at ZBIAS 1: k = 0,1,3,4,8,16,64,256. Row B at ZBIAS 16: k = 0,16,31,33,48,64,256,2048.
- Pass: a strip is red iff k < 2*ZBIAS: A = RRGGGGGG, B = RRRGGGGG.
- RESULT zbias_step = first k lost per row, expected [3,33].
- A scale keyed to the Z surface or the desktop paints every strip red; no bias paints only k=0 red.

(3) zbias_clear:
- ZBIAS 16, LESS. A priming quad flushes the biased state.
- Z-only Clear of the right half to z 0.25 (zaColor becomes 0x4000 or 0x400000).
- With no state change, red at 0.25+16/65535.
- Pass: (180,128) red. A stale zaColor or no bias leaves it black. This guards the restore-after-clear chain for G47/G53.

(4) zbias_func:
- Row B: LESSEQUAL at ZBIAS 1 writes the biased depth; then EQUAL with the left half at ZBIAS 1 and the right half at ZBIAS 0.
- Pass: row B left red, right green. This also proves the biased depth is written; 3dfx's sign rule fails it.
- Then a Z clear of row A to 0.0. Row A: GREATER base, then the left half at ZBIAS 1 and the right half at 0.
- Pass: row A left red, right green.

- at --full 1024x768x32 (D24X8);

- at --full 640x480x16 --zfmt d24x8, the 16/16-in-32 case, which must give the 16-bit pattern;
- later at --bpp 32 --zfmt d16, only once G10 lands.
Pace 5000 ms.

Reference first: run all four on an NVIDIA DX8-class fleet box. zbias must pass there; its zbias_step and its EQUAL/GREATER rows are data for the magnitude and sign choices.
