G30.approach:
The gap is real. compute_regs (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:978-980) sets fbzMode[8] (FZ_DITHER) whenever D3DRENDERSTATE_DITHERENABLE is non-zero, at every target depth. SPEC §8.25 L3254 says the bit "must be cleared when 32-bit color rendering is selected (renderMode[1:0]=0x2)". For bit 19 (dither subtraction) the same register description only says "ignored" at 32 bpp (L3268). Our h5 Glide clears bits 8, 11 and 19 at 32 bpp (G5/gglide.c:3905-3908).

What the silicon does with bit 8 at 32 bpp has never been measured, and the evidence leans towards "nothing":
- 3dfx's C model of the chip skips the whole dither and truncate stage for a 32 bpp pixel (CSIM/FBI.C:1455, "if 32bpp just skip all this crap!").
- 3dfx's shipped D3D HAL sets ENDITHER with no depth check. A case-insensitive search of H5/W2K and H5/Win9x finds no clear of the bit anywhere (VH5/D3RSTATE.C:3488-3534).

Static scan of the staged binaries (objdump, SetRenderState(26) through the vtable):
- UT2003 and UT2004 D3DDrv set dither TRUE unconditionally, but they render 16 bpp until G19.
- Halo sets FALSE.
- Red Faction sets TRUE only when its depth is 16 and the adapter is not ATI.
- Max Payne sets TRUE only when an internal field is < 3 (plausibly 16 bpp only, inferred).
- Thief II NewDark is conditional; H&D and the DX5/6 titles are unknown.
So no staged title is known to hit this today. The gap's list (Halo, Thief II, H&D, Max Payne) is the list of 32 bpp titles, not of titles that dither.

FIX (step 1):
- New Win32-free header KMD/include/vcr_dither.h with vcr_fbz_dither(fmt, enable). It returns 0 when enable is 0 or when (vcr_rt_rendermode(fmt) & 3) == RM_32BPP, and FZ_DITHER otherwise (4x4, no subtraction: the proven 16 bpp value). Keying on the renderMode value the target itself programs means G10's promoted Z (still VCR_RT_32) and G93's 1555 targets get the right answer.
- compute_regs builds r->fbzMode = FZ_RECTCLIP | FZ_RGBWRITE | vcr_fbz_dither(c->target.fmt, c->rs[DITHERENABLE]). The target is current there: it is re-read every DP2 and Clear2 call, and SETRENDERTARGET marks the state dirty. compute_regs already uses c->target.z_on.
- A once-per-context INFO event (513, next free what-code, 24) fires when a requested dither is dropped. It counts which titles send dither to a 32 bpp target.
- vcr_3dregs.h gains FZ_DITHERSUB (bit 19).
- The header also carries vcr_fbz_dither_rows() (matrix height, a hook for G51's rule that the SLI band must be at least the matrix height; CSIM/GO.C:1136-1150, SPEC L6244) and the 16 bpp reference model (vcr_dither_565). That model was written from the CSIM arithmetic and checked against it over every value and threshold: 0 mismatches.

Unchanged:
- Caps: D3DPRASTERCAPS_DITHER stays.
- Single pass; same register writes in the same order.
- Clears: fastfill never dithered.
- fogMode bit 6 (fog-factor dither, applied at every depth by CSIM and by 3dfx's HAL) stays as is.
- Dither rotation stays off: renderMode and fogMode are written whole.

Old path: with Diag\D3D32 off, the only formats are VCR_RT_16 and VCR_RT_REFUSED, for which the helper returns exactly the old bits. The register stream is byte-for-byte unchanged.

STEP 2 (optional, P3, separate change, default OFF behind Diag\D3DDither): 2x2 and/or dither subtraction at 16 bpp, the vendor look. It is not recommended as a default:
- There is no correctness reason.
- It would change the proven 16 bpp lane.
- 3dfx's 2x2 choice belonged with the overlay's 2x2 box video filter, which vcr-kmd's desktop-surface flips never use.
- Subtraction was opt-in ("Smoother") in both vendor stacks.

Correction to reports/hw.md Q17: Glide forces 2x2 but adds subtraction only with SSTH3_ALPHADITHERMODE=3. The default is 1, Optimal, with no subtraction (G5/gpci.c:1837-1846).

2. d3dprobe_run.py 192.168.1.124 render --full --res 1024x768 --bpp 16 --tests dither16,flat,gouraud --pace 5000.
3. Optionally the same at --bpp 32 with --tests dither32.
dither32 here measures what the silicon does with fbzMode[8] at 32 bpp: PASS = latent, FAIL = P1 and a prerequisite of G19. dither16 records the 16 bpp baseline (expected matrix 4x4).

Step B: swap in the new vcrdd.dll, safe-reboot.py, then repeat runs 1-3 in the clean boot. Pass requires all of:
- dither32 passes all four checks, windowed and fullscreen;
- the dither16 block and matrix are identical to step A;
- the default gate equals the KMD/evidence/silicon/d3d32_step16 baseline at 16 and 32 bpp.

Step C, informational, same boot: launch the 32 bpp D3D titles (Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe forced 32 bpp, Thief II NewDark, Max Payne, Halo) and read the agent log for 513 / what 24 to see which ones send dither to a 32 bpp target. If step A failed, capture an in-game 32 bpp gradient (sky or fog) for any title that does. The natural game scene is UT2004 at 1280x960x32 (V-08's menu backdrop, an ONS flyby sky) once G19 makes UE2 render at 32 bpp.

Evidence goes to KMD/evidence/silicon/g30_dither/; the outcome is recorded in retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md, KMD/README.md and the D3D resume point in docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md.
G30.risk:
Very low.
- Default 16 bpp lane: none. The helper returns the old bits for every non-32 target; this is pinned on the host, and on silicon by dither16 being identical before and after.
- 32 bpp lane (D3D32 armed): one bit fewer in fbzMode, with the same register writes in the same order. The image changes only if the chip honoured the bit, and then towards correct. A bit the spec requires clear cannot plausibly hang the engine, and 3dfx's retail HAL wrote both values.
- Clears: unchanged (fastfill uses its own fbzMode without dither).
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence: none. D3D writes fbzMode whole at every state emit; Glide keeps its own shadow and clears dither at 32 bpp itself.
- SLI: none today (D3D is single-chip). It also removes 32 bpp from G51's band-height-vs-matrix constraint.
- Flip path: none.
- Performance: one compare per compute_regs, nothing per triangle.
- Step 2, if ever done, would change 16 bpp pixels and is therefore behind its own default-OFF switch.
games_unblocked: None is blocked today; output changes only for D3D draws with DITHERENABLE on a 32 bpp target
Unreal Tournament 2003 and 2004 once they render at 32 bpp (G19): D3DDrv sets DITHERENABLE TRUE unconditionally, and V-08's ordered pattern on the menu backdrop must not survive on a 32 bpp frame
Thief II NewDark (flag-driven dither; to be counted on the box via the new event)
Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe (forced 32 bpp; dither use not found statically; to be counted)
Any windowed D3D client on .124's 32 bpp desktop
Not expected to affect Halo (sets dither FALSE), Red Faction (dithers only at 16 bpp, never on ATI) or, very probably, Max Payne (dithers only when an internal field < 3)
open_questions: Does the VSA-100 ignore fbzMode[8] at 32 bpp, as 3dfx's C model and its shipped HAL imply, or does it dither or quantise as the spec's 'must be cleared' hints? Step A's windowed dither32 on build 95678704 answers it with no mode switch; a FAIL raises G30 to P1 and makes it a prerequisite of G19.

Which staged titles actually send DITHERENABLE to a 32 bpp target: Thief II NewDark's flag path, H&D's LS3D renderer, and the DX5/6 titles (JK, MotS, Shogo, SS2, Thief Gold, AvP) that a static scan cannot see? The 513 / what-24 event in step C answers this.
Is Max Payne's device field [+0x10] (dither only when < 3) the bytes per pixel? The same event answers it.
Does the silicon's 16 bpp dither match the C-model arithmetic exactly? dither16 reports 'other' if not; the model then follows the chip, and the G30 old==new criterion holds either way.

Should 16 bpp move to 2x2 and/or dither subtraction (step 2, Diag\D3DDither)? Only as the user's by-eye choice; there is no correctness reason, and 3dfx's reason (the overlay's 2x2 box filter) does not apply to vcr-kmd's desktop-surface flips.
fogMode bit 6 (fog-factor dither) is left as is, since L3254 does not cover it. Is it ever visible at 32 bpp? That belongs to G31/G32.

G29.approach:
The gap is real, but today it is honest. `blend_src` and `blend_dst` (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:643, :661) draw SRCCOLOR/INVSRCCOLOR as a source factor and DESTCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR as a destination factor as ONE. The caps hide this correctly (SrcBlend 0x1f33, DestBlend 0x3f), so only a title that ignores the caps ever sees a wrong pixel.

The VSA-100 does all four natively, in one pass, with one register field:
- alphaMode RGB factor code 8 = SST_A_SAMECOLOR and 9 = SST_AOM_SAMECOLOR (VINC/H3DEFS.H:925-926). The spec's change log says the codes were added "to allow src*src and dst*dst blending".
- 3dfx's feature sheet D3D.XLS (rows 251-252, 271-272) says Napalm Yes, Voodoo3 No.
- 3dfx's own HAL maps exactly these four (VH5/D3RSTATE.C:3084-3107, :3250-3272) and adds the caps under IS_NAPALM (D3INIT.C:3132-3158). Its per-draw blend rewrite (D6DP2.C:6234-6324) leaves codes 8/9 untouched.
- Glide writes GR_BLEND_SAME_COLOR_EXT straight into the field. Our MesaFX ICD already maps GL_SRC_COLOR as a source to it and ships GL_NV_blend_square on the V5. Nobody has ever measured it on .124.
- The comment "the chip cannot" came from commit 56e0bc1, written on the 86Box Voodoo3, where it is true. The fix therefore follows pd->napalm.

The gap's game claim does not hold. No staged .124 title was found that sends these factors:
- **Shogo:** disassembly of d3d.ren shows the SRCCOLOR cap is read only by its LISTDEVICECAPS console dump (0x10013a4e). Its "Lightmap capable" check uses SrcBlend ZERO plus DestBlend SRCCOLOR, which we already advertise. Every SRCBLEND/DESTBLEND it sets is SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA or ONE/ONE.
- **Halo:** its framebuffer-blend table (.rdata 0x65dfbc/0x65dfe0/0x65e004) uses none of the four.
- **15 more renderers:** a byte scan plus disassembly of every hit found no use. The hits were zlib's zalloc(19,4), a table registration in JK/MotS, a text draw in Red Faction, or unrelated data.
- Engines that set blend state from variables (UE2, NewDark, Max Payne, LS3D) cannot be ruled out statically. Step 0's counter answers that.

The fix:
- A new Win32-free header, KMD/include/vcr_blend.h, holds vcr_blend_src, vcr_blend_dst, vcr_blend_alphamode and the caps functions vcr_blend_src_caps and vcr_blend_dst_caps. Host tests can execute it.
- vcr_3dregs.h gains BF_SAMECOLOR 8 and BF_INVSAMECOLOR 9.
- compute_regs computes alphaMode through vcr_blend_alphamode(s, d, pd->blend_same).
- prim_caps takes its words from the header for both tri and line caps: SrcBlend 0x1f33 becomes 0x1f3f, DestBlend 0x3f becomes 0x33f.
- pd->blend_same = napalm AND Diag\D3DFeat bit SAMECOLOR.
- Single pass. Same register write count. The alpha channel stays ONE/ZERO, which is G28's to change.

Two extra steps:
- **Step 0:** a log-only, default-on per-context mask of the SRCBLEND/DESTBLEND values each title asks for, logged when the context goes away. It also serves G28.
- **Step 1:** a glidelab 'blendsq' mode that proves A_SAMECOLOR on .124's silicon through our Glide, with no driver change and no reboot. If it fails, do not advertise, and withdraw NV_blend_square in the GL lane.

Priority P3: no staged title has been shown to need this. Raise it to P2 if the counter names a title. Land it together with G28: same functions, same caps words, same probe matrix.

G29.gating:
The switch is default-OFF: bit VCR_D3DFEAT_SAMECOLOR of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vcrmp\Diag\D3DFeat. Absent means off.
- It is the plan's shared D3DFeat transport (one raw word in vcr_info.d3dfeat, G05 §4.2); whichever D3DFeat item lands first creates it.
- Take the next free bit; vcr_d3dfeat.h and its one-bit-each test decide.
- It is read at boot, like D3D32 and D3DBigTex, so the blend caps an app reads at its desktop match its fullscreen device.
- VSA-100 only (pd->napalm). On a Banshee/Voodoo3, and on the 86Box bed, codes 8/9 are reserved and the bit is never honoured.

Off is byte-for-byte the proven path. For all 256 SRCBLEND x DESTBLEND pairs the alphaMode word is identical to build 95678704, and the caps stay 0x1f33/0x3f. The native test pins both against a verbatim copy of today's functions.

Armed, only the four requests change: SRCBLEND 3/4 (not BOTH*) and DESTBLEND 9/10. Register count and FIFO room are unchanged.

Not default-on on day one. Codes 8/9 have never been observed on this silicon, and the caps change can move a caps-checking title onto a path never seen on .124.

Graduation needs all of:
- the glidelab blendsq silicon check passes at cfg 0 and cfg 5;
- one supervised boot with only this Diag change passes blendsq 12/12 at 640x480x16, 1024x768x32 and windowed 32 bpp;
- the default matrices are unchanged (40/40, 40/40, 42/42).

Then flip the default in a separate commit with its own test, using the plan's D3DFeat convention (a default mask, or a D3DFeatOff kill mask). If a title regresses only from seeing the caps, split the caps onto their own bit and keep the mapping.

Arm with: REGWRITE ... Diag D3DFeat REG_DWORD <bit>, read the key back, check activation, then scripts/fleet/safe-reboot.py.
G29.d3dprobe_test:
Two new tests in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c run_test: **blendsq** and **blendsq_force**.

What they draw:
- Clear to Cd = 0x004080C0, untextured flat colour Cs = 0x80C08040, ALPHABLENDENABLE on.
- 12 cells of 40x40 at x = 24 + 64·col, y = 24 + 56·row, inside the 256x256 readback.
- Before each cell, SRCBLEND = DESTBLEND = ZERO, then the cell's pair. A factor the runtime does not forward stays ZERO and shows as "dropped".
- Eight SAMECOLOR cells (src/dst): SRCCOLOR/ZERO, INVSRCCOLOR/ZERO, SRCCOLOR/ONE, ZERO/DESTCOLOR, ZERO/INVDESTCOLOR, ONE/DESTCOLOR, SRCCOLOR/DESTCOLOR, INVSRCCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR.
- Four controls every Voodoo has: ONE/ZERO, DESTCOLOR/ZERO, ZERO/SRCCOLOR, ONE/ONE. The last three are untested today (history.md §6.1).
- The background at (8,8) is read back as the stored Cd.

Reference:
- Per channel: min(255, round(s·Fs/255 + d·Fd/255)) using the measured background, quantised like the back buffer (565 truncate and replicate, or 8888 as is).
- Tolerance 6 at 32 bpp and 12 at 16 bpp. Computed: the two plausible chip roundings differ by ≤1 at 32 bpp, and the unknown 565 destination expansion moves a cell by ≤8. Every SAMECOLOR reference is ≥41 from the pre-G29 value in some channel.
- Example 32 bpp references against the pre-G29 values:

| cell | reference | pre-G29 |
|---|---|---|
| SRCCOLOR/ZERO | 914010 | C08040 |
| ZERO/DESTCOLOR | 104091 | 4080C0 |
| SRCCOLOR/DESTCOLOR | A181A1 | FFFFFF |
| SRCCOLOR/ONE | D1C0D0 | FFFFFF |
| INVSRCCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR | 5F7F5F | FFFFFF |

- At 16 bpp, e.g. SRCCOLOR/ZERO is 944110 against C68242.

Each SAMECOLOR cell is classified ref / old / dropped / other. "old" is the pre-G29 drawing with the factor replaced by ONE.

Pass criteria:
- **blendsq** respects the caps. An advertised cell must be ref (pass/fail). An unadvertised cell is SKIPPED. The controls always run.
- **blendsq_force** draws every cell. Advertised cells are pass/fail. An unadvertised cell is a note carrying its class, so the probe stays driver-neutral.
- New `d3dprobe_run.py --expect-class blendsq_force=old|ref` makes the host fail the run on any other class.

Expected results:
- Off: blendsq gives 4 pass and 8 skipped; blendsq_force gives 4 pass and 8 class=old.
- Armed: 12/12 in both.
- d3dprobe caps: SrcBlendCaps 00001f33 and DestBlendCaps 0000003f off; 00001f3f and 0000033f armed.

Neither test joins the default list until graduation, so the recorded 40/40 and 42/42 matrices stay comparable.

The Glide twin is glidelab mode **blendsq**: same cells, colours, references and tolerance 12 at 16 bpp, read back with grLfbReadRegion. Its pass is the precondition for arming.

Rules for every step on .124: pace switches ≥5 s (onbox/d3dprobe_paced.py --pace 5000); no vcrctl while a D3D game runs; Max Payne is excluded (G04).

**Step 1: silicon, with no driver change and no reboot.**

**Boot A: the bit clear.**

**Boot B: the bit set, the only Diag change.**

G29.risk:
Very low.
- **Default 16 bpp path:** off, it is byte-for-byte unchanged in register words and caps, pinned pair by pair. Armed, only the four requests change, and those are drawn wrong today. Write count, FIFO room and performance are unchanged.
- **D3D32 path:** same as above. The alpha channel stays ONE/ZERO (G28).
- **Glide/OpenGL coexistence:** no new shared state. D3D re-sends alphaMode with the full state at the first triangle of every DP2 (G53). Glide resets its shadow alphaMode in assertDefaultState at every grSstWinOpenExt (gsst.c:889/905/953/3122). Neither side's factor 8 can leak into the other. The Step 1 Glide run carries the usual G01 ordering caveat.
- **SLI:** none. D3D runs on chip 0 only (G51), and alphaMode is a per-chip word that a future broadcast would simply copy.
- **Flip path:** untouched.
- **Banshee/Voodoo3/86Box:** never armed.
- **Main behavioural risk:** caps-checking titles may take a different path when armed. Shogo is proven not to: it only prints the cap. Boot B's sweep covers menus only, since in-game is G73. Fallback: put the caps on their own bit.
- **Hardware:** codes 8/9 only select a blender input, so they cannot leave the engine busy (inferred). Failure is caught before arming by the Glide check.
- **Step 0 counter:** one OR per state change and one event per context.

Which Diag\D3DFeat bit should SAMECOLOR take, and which graduation convention applies (a default mask, or a D3DFeatOff kill mask)? This is plan-level, shared with G05/G09/G12/G13/G14.

G25.approach:
The gap is real and verified in the source. D3DRENDERSTATE_SPECULARENABLE (29) is stored by set_rs (vcrdd_d3d.c:1393-1406) and never read; compute_regs (:921-1029) is the only consumer of rs[]. The specular DWORD is read only for its alpha, as the vertex-fog factor (vcrdd_3d.c:202-209). ShadeCaps are 0x500a (:2032-2033), which D3D8 reports as 0x4008, with no SPECULARGOURAUDRGB. The chip has one iterated colour per triangle (SPEC: sARGB 'FBI+TREX*', sRed..sBlue FBI only), so specular is either host arithmetic or a second pass, as 3dfx did.

Design: a Win32-free planner, a new KMD/include/vcr_spec.h. For each state set it picks one of three modes, computed at the END of prepare() from the words actually sent.

(1) FOLD, with no new register writes. It applies when the FBI RGB result is the iterated colour (legacy combine, RGBSEL_ITER with CC bits 0: DISABLE, SELECTARG(DIFFUSE), the texture-less fallback) or TMU/C1 plus iterated with only CC_ADD_CLOCAL (D3D ADD), and the local is iterated. vertex() then sends sat(diffuse+specular) per channel, with the alpha from the diffuse. It is exact unless a vertex saturates, and it does not copy 3dfx's CLAMP888, which loses the LSB.

(2) PASS2, for every other combine (MODULATE and the rest). Right after each lit triangle (some vertex's specular RGB != 0), VcrDd3dSpecBegin writes:
- fogMode with FOGADD (bit 1) set and FOGMULT cleared, when fog is on;
- alphaMode: blend off gives BLEND|ONE/ONE plus ASRC ZERO/ADST ONE; blend on keeps the app's source factor with RGBDST ONE and the alpha factors ZERO/ONE, so the destination alpha is untouched; the alpha-test bits are kept;
- fbzMode: when depth and Z write are on, ZFUNC EQ with Z write off and the chroma key off; otherwise unchanged;
- the FBI combineMode with its CC fields cleared, only when G05/G12 have it live;
- fbzColorPath with its RGB fields cleared (RGB = iterated, passed); the alpha fields and the texture are cleared unless the source alpha matters;
- sSetupMode without ST/W unless the texture is kept.
The texture is kept, with S/T/W re-sent, when the alpha test is on, when an SRCALPHA-family blend is on, or when 2 ppc is live. The three vertices are then sent with colour = specular RGB plus diffuse alpha and bit-identical x/y/z/W, and VcrDd3dSpecEnd restores pass 1's words, sSetupMode included.

(3) SKIP, counted. A source factor that reads the destination or the source colour (DESTCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR/DESTALPHA/INVDESTALPHA/SRCALPHASAT/SRCCOLOR), a destination factor SRCCOLOR/INVSRCCOLOR, or a colour key or stencil without the Z-write EQUAL guard. These cannot be separated additively. A source factor ZERO, ZFUNC NEVER or colour writes off need no pass at all (NONE).

Triangles whose specular RGB is zero (fog-only TL vertices) send today's stream byte for byte. Caps when armed: dwShadeCaps |= 0x200 (DX7 0x520a, D3D8 0x4208); SPECULARFLATRGB only together with G24's flat shading.

Code changes:
- vcrdd_3d.c: one vertex_at(pd,d,v,x,y,argb,tmus) writer, extending G16's, defined between vertex() and VcrDd3dTriangle so the existing python pins hold; VcrDd3dSpecBegin/End/Triangle.
- vcrdd_d3d.c: a draw3() helper used by tri()/imm_tri(); per-context counters; the prim_caps flag.
- A default-on shadow plan counts lit/fold/pass2/skip per context. It is logged once when first seen and once at context end, so boot A measures which titles use specular before anything is armed.

G25.d3dprobe_test:
13 new tests in tools/d3dprobe.c.
- Vertex types FVF_ST/FVF_ST2 (diffuse + specular + 1 or 2 texture sets); SPECULARENABLE set per test.
- Every test except the controls is SKIPPED when caps lack D3DPSHADECAPS_SPECULARGOURAUDRGB. --force runs them anyway, to record the gap on an old build.

Controls (always run):

- spec_tex_zero: spec_tex with specular ff000000 (fog alpha only). Want 800000/000080, and the ring shows pass2 0.

Untextured (FOLD):
- spec_untex: diffuse 402010 + specular 204080. Want 606090 (old 402010).
- spec_untex_sat: c0c0c0 + 808080. Want ffffff. A gouraud edge midpoint is logged as a note (D3D ff, fold df).
- spec_grad: gouraud, diffuse 0 to 800000, specular 0 to 008000. Midpoint 404000, tol 24.

Textured (PASS2):
- spec_tex: 64 checker, MODULATE(TEX, DIFF), diffuse 808080, specular 006000. Red cell 806000, blue cell 006080 (old 800000/000080).
- spec_tex_z: LESSEQUAL + Z write. A green occluder at z .25 on the left; the quad at z .5; then again at z .5 on [160,Q1).

- spec_tex_blend: clear 0000ff, SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, white texture, ALPHAOP SELECTARG1(DIFFUSE), diffuse 80ff0000, specular 00ff00. Want 80807f (old 80007f).
- spec_tex_blend_ta: as above with a solid 4444 texture (alpha 8) and texture alpha. Want 888877. A lost texture alpha gives green ff.
- spec_alphatest: Z off, alpha test GREATER 80, 4444 checker with alpha f/0, specular 008000. Opaque cell ff8000, killed cell stays 0000ff (a lost test gives 0080ff).
- spec_fogtable: red cell + specular 00c000 at rhw 1/3, linear fog 1..5 toward blue. Want 406080 (old 400080; a doubled fog colour gives blue ff).

G25.risk:
Default 16 bpp path with the bit off: none. Registers, caps and DDI answers are byte-identical; the only new code is integer counting while SPECULARENABLE is on with a specular FVF.

Bit on, unlit triangles: none. The zero-RGB fold is the identity and no pass 2 runs.

Bit on, lit triangles:
- (a) fogMode, alphaMode, fbzMode, fbzColorPath and sSetupMode (plus the FBI combineMode under G05/G12) flip before and after each pass 2. The chip consumes writes in order, and 3dfx did exactly this per triangle on VSA-100.
- (b) EQUAL needs pass 2's iterated Z bit-identical to pass 1's while sSetupMode differs in ST/W. 3dfx relied on it; spec_tex_z proves it before any game runs.
- (c) About 2x the PIO writes per lit triangle: a specular-heavy scene could lose up to half its triangle rate until G47/G49. The counters and perf --spec make that visible.

The cap change moves Halo, Max Payne and H&D onto specular paths never run on this HAL. That is the reason for default-off and the A/B frames; Max Payne stays attended-only (G04).

Glide/OpenGL coexistence: no new hazard. Pass 2 touches only registers VcrDd3dState re-sends at every DP2's first draw, and a failed restore forces a re-send. G01/G03 hazards affect pass 2 exactly as they affect pass 1.

SLI: none (D3D stays chip 0, broadcast writes). Flip path: none.

The legacy registers mean the 86Box bed exercises the same logic before silicon.

G23.approach:
VERDICT: the defect is real, but no staged title triggers it today. compute_regs enables depth only for ZENABLE == D3DZB_TRUE (vcrdd_d3d.c:986), so D3DZB_USEW draws with no depth test. WINFO is skipped by size (:1556), and WBUFFER is not in RasterCaps (live 00100191). To find out who sends USEW, I disassembled the staged binaries.
- Thief Gold (THIEF.EXE, Dark lgd3d DX6) tests D3DPRASTERCAPS_WBUFFER (0x56f919) and sets ZENABLE = 1 + flag (0x5738e3-0x573905). It sends USEW only when the cap is reported. SS2 is the same engine (inferred).
- The Unreal 1 D3DDrv (Deus Ex/Unreal Gold/UT436, dormant on .124) sets USEW only with the cap (0x1000c744-0x1000c76e).
- Red Faction's D3D init resets its W mode to Z (0x5444c1). Halo (62 sites), UE2, Max Payne: TRUE/FALSE only. DX5 titles have no USEW.
So "depth off" has no measured victim; the bug would go live only for a blind USEW or once we advertise the cap.

RUNTIME: all three XP runtimes (d3d8 0x6d9e2640, d3dim700 0x739557bf, d3dim 0x6d91af6e) build WINFO themselves from the projection matrix with one formula:
- {0,1} when _33==_34 or _33==0;
- otherwise WNear = _44 - _34*_43/_33, WFar = _44 + _34*(_44-_43)/(_33-_34). Perspective gives {Zn,Zf}; identity gives {1,1}.

STEP 0 (log only, default-on): parse WINFO (last record, float BITS stored, since the HAL is integer-only); drop it from rec_size. Count USEW sets and WINFOs per context. Two once-per-context 513 events: the first WINFO, and a depth summary at ctx_free. A WINFO sets dirty only when armed, so register traffic is unchanged.

STEP 1 (default-on): new Win32-free include/vcr_depth.h vcr_depth_bits(zenable, zfunc, zwrite, z_on, wbuf_armed, &wbuf). USEW gets FZ_DEPTH|FZ_ZFUNC|[FZ_ZAWRITE], the exact proven TRUE values; every other value is byte-for-byte today's. The Z is the runtime's sz, which software VP always computes.

STEP 2 (W-buffer, default-OFF, Diag\D3DFeat bit WBUF): single pass, native hardware.
- Depth: USEW adds FZ_WBUFFER (fbzMode bit 3); bit 21 (DEPTH_FLOAT_SEL) stays 0. The choice is per ZENABLE, never per fog or per draw, so W and Z never mix in one depth buffer. Both depths: 16-bit W at 16 bpp, 24-bit W at 32 bpp (3dfx D3D.XLS row 83).
- W range: new common/vcr_wbuf.c (FPU, host-testable). It applies 3dfx's remap (D6DP2.C:1733-1734) only when [WNear,WFar] does not fit [1,65520], so W from 1/WNear to 1/WFar maps onto [1/65520, 1]; otherwise identity (vendor parity, the identity default). Sanitized: any non-finite, non-positive or non-increasing range is identity. Vendor bug not copied: the runtimes' own {0,1} gives bW = NaN in 3dfx's formula.
- Vertex path: vertex() sends sOowfbi = rhw*aW + bW. Same registers, same order; the TMU W stays raw.
- Fog routing: a FnZTable-like table in vcr_fog.h, shared with G32.
  - Table fog + W: Wfbi remapped, table rebuilt in the chip's W domain via vcr_wbuf_eye_w = aW/(1/w_chip - bW). Identity is special-cased so vcr_fog_table stays byte-identical. Vendor bug not copied: D3FOG.C:404 applies WSCALE to a W ({0.1,1000}: the far plane read as w = 6552).
  - Vertex fog + W: FM_FOG_Z (fogMode bit 4), sVz = (255 - specular.a) * 256 at 16 bpp (the vendor's <<8, Z[27:20] of 20.12) or *65536 at 32 bpp (Z[27:20] of 28.4; the vendor's <<8 there is inferred wrong; a probe decides).
  - The fog cache key gains wbuf and winfo, both always 0 when off.
- Caps: D3DPRASTERCAPS_WBUFFER only while armed (expected RasterCaps 0x00140191).
- Arming: on every chip with the 3D engine, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed (which emulates W-buffer and FOG_Z) can pre-test 16 bpp.
- What it changes: Thief Gold and SS2 move from a 16-bit Z to the W-buffer they had on 3dfx's own driver. No D3D8/9 title changes.

G23.d3dprobe_test:
Six tests in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c. All are analytic, inside the 256x256 readback window, tolerance ±8 unless noted. usew joins the default list; the wbuffer* tests are explicit and are SKIPPED (not failed) when RasterCaps lacks WBUFFER.

1. usew (Step 1): the ztest scene with ZENABLE=USEW and consistent z/w.
   - Draws: green full quad (z .25, rhw 1/4), red full quad (z .75, rhw 1/40), blue left half (z .10, rhw 1/2), LESSEQUAL.
   - Pass: (64,128) blue, (180,128) green.
   - Today's driver 95678704 gives a red right half (depth off). Record that failing RESULT first.

2. wbuffer: z deliberately INVERTED against w, so W, Z and depth-off give three distinct pictures.
   - Draws: green (w 4, z .75), red (w 40, z .25), blue left half (w 2, z .90), then yellow at (4..28)^2 with w 60000, z .99.
   - Pass: (64,128) blue, (180,128) green, (16,16) yellow.
   - Failures: red/red means Z is in use; blue/red means depth is off; no yellow means the 1.0 clear is not farther than W 60000.

3. wbuffer_far (the 16 bpp precision gain):
   - Projection Zn 1, Zf 1000. Red quad at w 902, then green at w 900, z from the projection, ZFUNC LESS.
   - Pass: green with USEW.
   - Control: the same pair with ZENABLE TRUE must be red at 16 bpp (both z16 = 65527). At 32 bpp the control is green and the test is reported not discriminating.

4. wbuffer_near (WINFO received and applied):
   - D3DFVF_XYZ quads, perspective Zn 0.1, Zf 100. Red at view z 0.5 covers the screen; green at view z 0.2 covers screen x < 128 (computed from the projection and the back-buffer size). LESS.
   - Pass: (64,128) green, (180,128) red.
   - All red means no remap: rhw 5 and 2 both encode as W-float 0 without it (0x1009 / 0x2681 with it).

5. wbuffer_fogtable (table rebuilt in the W domain):
   - fogtable's linear fog 1..5 with XYZ geometry at view z 1, 3, 8 on fogtable's three columns. Perspective Zn 0.5, Zf 50 engages the remap. USEW.
   - Pass: ff0000, 80007f (±40), 0000ff (±12).
   - About quarter/all/all fog means the table was not rebuilt (chip W' 2.02 / 6.32 / 18.85).

6. wbuffer_fogv (vertex fog via FOG_Z), run at 16 AND 32 bpp:
   - fogvertex's three quads (specular a 255/128/0) at w 4 under USEW, then fog off and a white quad at w 2 over the upper half of the left quad, LESSEQUAL.

G24.approach:
Real and fixable, in two parts of very different weight. The gap text needs four corrections:
(1) Jedi Knight and MotS are NOT users. Their execute-buffer state block writes SHADEMODE=GOURAUD and FILLMODE=SOLID as constants (JK.EXE 0x42b916/0x42b961, JKM.EXE 0x42ead6/0x42eb21), and no other SHADEMODE write exists. A static scan names the likely users instead: the Dark engine (Thief Gold/SS2) lgd3d setter sends FLAT for a false argument (thief.exe 0x574c30); Rainbow Six uses FLAT only for a software device; BF1942 has one FLAT site but is SafeDisc-blocked; Halo and UE2 have wireframe debug paths.
(2) The 'flat flags' in INDEXEDTRIANGLELIST wFlags (STARTFLAT/ODD/EVEN) are strip CULLING hints, not shading (d3dtypes.h:1749-1755). Only EDGEENABLE1-3 matter, and only in WIREFRAME.
(3) D3D's first vertex is not the first vertex we send to the setup unit. Odd strip triangles go as (s+i+1, s+i, s+i+2), and every fan triangle goes hub-first. D3D's first vertex is s+i for strips and v[i+1] for fans, the W2K DDK triangle sequences, the same picks 3dfx's DCT-fixed code makes (D6STRIP.C pF, D6FANI.C pB).
(4) Flat shading is mandatory in every DDI (DDK D3DPRIMCAPS: 'assumed ... supports D3DSHADE_FLAT'). D3D8/9 have no flat cap bits at all, which is why the live ShadeCaps read 0x4008, and any D3D8/9 title may send FLAT without checking a cap.
The VSA-100 has no flat mode (SPEC L551, L2239-2243, L3718-3734), so 3dfx replicated the first vertex's colour on the host.

Step 0 (default ON, log-only): per-context counters for flat triangles DRAWN (not state sets), an 8-bit mask of the DP2 forms that drew them, would-be-flat triangles with the switch off, and wireframe/point-fill triangles. Events 513/27-29 (provisional numbers).

Part A, flat shading:
- A Win32-free decode helper vcr_dp2_tri(op, rec, s, i, &t) in KMD/include/vcr_dp2prim.h (G16's header). It returns today's setup order a,b,c, the walker expressions moved unchanged and pinned by a native test, plus pv, D3D's first vertex: lists 3i/wV1, strips i, fans/indexed fans/IMM i+1.
- vertex() takes a colour-source pointer cv: the diffuse ARGB, alpha included, is read from cv; the fog factor (specular alpha) stays per vertex, as D3D interpolates it.
- VcrDd3dTriangle(a,b,c,f) sends f's colour for all three vertices when f is non-NULL.
- prepare() sets w->flat = vcr_flat_on(rs[SHADEMODE], diff_off, pd->d3d_flat).
- tri() and imm_tri() pass vb+pv*stride or NULL.
- ctx_defaults gets GOURAUD/SOLID.
- Cost: zero extra register writes. Same writes, same order and count; only two vertices' colour values change. With f NULL the register stream is byte-identical.
- No caps change: COLORFLATRGB and ALPHAFLATBLEND become true.
- Rules for neighbours: G49 must keep flat triangles independent ('HW cannot support FLAT_SHADE and Auto Strip/Fan', D6TRI2I.C:767); G25 takes specular RGB from cv and its alpha from v.

Part B, FILLMODE wireframe/point (needs G16):
- Adds a colour-source arg to G16's VcrDd3dLine/VcrDd3dPoint.
- A CPU cull test: 3dfx/MS CULL_TRI, area<=0 culled by CCW; float in vcrdd_3d.c, the decision vcr_cull_drops() in the header. The cull runs before edges/points, because G16 clears the HW cull bits for quads.
- Edge flags via vcr_dp2_tri_edges: INDEXEDTRIANGLELIST wFlags>>8&7; TRIANGLEFAN_IMM dwEdgeFlags outline bits per the DDK; all other forms 7.
- Points are three per triangle; the triangle's first vertex colours edges and points under FLAT.

G27.approach:
VERDICT: three of the four parts are real gaps that the VSA-100 does natively. SETTEXLOD is NOT a gap. The W2K DDK says it is "used only for driver managed textures". Our dwCaps2 is FLIPNOVSYNC only (vcrdd_ddraw.c:105), and XP's d3d8.dll SetLOD (0x6d9fb860) sends it only for a managed texture without a runtime resource-manager object. So the runtime applies SetLOD by what it hands the driver. SETTEXLOD stays parsed, gains its own case with a counter and one WARN per context, and is never applied.

TODAY: TSS 19/20 are stored and never read. RasterCaps lacks MIPMAPLODBIAS (00100191). tLOD always carries lodbias 0, and a placed chain gets LODMIN=top, LODMAX=smallest (vcrdd_d3d.c:777-786, :814-824). The TMU picks a level by truncation, so POINT and LINEAR mip sample floor(LOD) where D3D's point mip asks for the nearest level. 3dfx added +0.5 for exactly this reason (VH5/D6MT.C:5507-5510). The existing d3dprobe mip tests deliberately use LODs where floor and round agree, so the truncation was never tested.

FIX, one integer function in common/vcr_texlod.c. It is host-tested and -mgeneral-regs-only (no FPU): vcr_tlod_lodctl(tlod, maxmip, bias_bits, round_q). It takes a texture view's tLOD and rewrites bits 17:0 only:
- LODMIN = top + min(MAXMIPLEVEL, levels below) + 0.5, clamped to LODMAX (3dfx's F-22 clamp; never LODMIN > LODMAX);
- LODBIAS = vcr_lod_bias_q(app float bits) + 0.5, clamped to -32..31 quarters (-8..+7.75);
- LODMAX unchanged; bits 18-31 (TBIG, aspect, MIRROR, lod_odd/tsplit) kept;
- a one-level tLOD (MIPFILTER NONE, unplaced or single-level textures) is returned unchanged.

vcr_lod_bias_q decodes the IEEE bits with integers. It rounds to the nearest quarter, symmetric. It clamps before masking, not after. NaN, denormals and UE2's _ftol2'd integers come out as 0, and +-inf as the field's ends.

Putting the +0.5 on LODMIN as well as on the bias keeps the min/mag filter choice at the unbiased LOD 0. The hardware magnifies when bias+LOD is clamped at LODMIN (SPEC L3857, L3931). 3dfx's bias-only rounding moved that threshold by half a level.

The single call site is view_of(): if (d3dfeat & LODCTRL && MIPFILTER > NONE) v->tLOD = vcr_tlod_lodctl(...). That covers both texture paths (default and D3DBigTex) and both stages. Each stage's own values follow its texture to the TMU that samples it (stage 0 on TMU1, stage 1 on TMU0). This avoids 3dfx's bugs:
- crossed stage biases (D6MT.C:5919-5922, :6085-6088);
- stage 0's MAXMIPLEVEL used for both TMUs (D6DP2.C:6656-6756);
- an OR instead of an add for the table bias (D6MT.C:5660);
- the CalcBias42 wrap (+7.5 becomes -8.0).
G07's guard, which lowers LODMAX inside the view, is honoured automatically.

CAPS: prim_caps(c, lodctl) adds D3DPRASTERCAPS_MIPMAPLODBIAS, so RasterCaps becomes 00102191. Nothing else changes.

MIPFILTER LINEAR uses the same +0.5 nearest stand-in until G26. round_q is G26's seam: 0 for true trilinear, or a dither-compensated count. MIPFILTER NONE leaves bias and MAXMIPLEVEL inert, as 3dfx does.

LOGGING (default-on, log only): a one-shot INFO line per distinct non-zero TSS 19/20 value per context (cap 8), plus a ctx_free summary of the LOD-state sets and SETTEXLOD counts.

EVIDENCE OF USE, from a static disassembly of the staged binaries:
- Red Faction sends stage 0 bias -0.75 always (rf.exe 0x54f400, global 0x5aa778 = 0xbf400000), and -1.5 on its detail-texture stage (0x54f2eb).
- BF1942 sends a per-stage bias from its settings.
- UT2003/UT2004 send DefaultTexMipBias -0.5 as raw bits at device set-up, but a texture-state path converts it with _ftol2 to the integer 0 (UT2004 D3DDrv 0x1001a32d).
- Halo, Max Payne, H&D, Thief, Thief II and SS2 send neither state; they get the rounding only.

Effect: half-level-softer distant textures where no bias is sent (D3D-correct, what 3dfx shipped), and correct bias where one is. No staged title is blocked: P2.
G27.gating:
Default OFF behind Diag\D3DFeat bit LODCTRL: proposed bit 10 (0x400), unclaimed by the sibling designs (0 G15, 1 G08, 4 G16, 6-8 G05/G12/G13); the integrator assigns the final number.
- The bit is read at boot by the miniport (VcrDiagGet(L"D3DFeat", 0)) and appended to vcr_info as one size-checked d3dfeat word. Whichever D3DFeat item lands first adds the word.
- It is latched at boot because it changes RasterCaps, the D3D32/D3DBigTex rule.
- It is chip-independent: the tLOD fields are identical on Banshee/Voodoo3, h3defs.h:269-270. Only VSA-100 silicon can verify it, because 86Box's LOD selection is wrong.
- With the bit off: vcr_tlod_lodctl is not called and prim_caps gets 0, so tLOD, RasterCaps and every register are byte-identical on both texture paths and every chip. The new SETTEXLOD case parses exactly the n*8 bytes rec_size did. A Python test pins this.

NOT safe to land default-on:
- it changes what every mipmapped title samples (half a level softer where no bias is sent);
- it adds a cap that games probe;
- it relies on a fractional LODMIN that 3dfx never used and that has never run on this silicon.

It IS a pure correctness fix with a d3dprobe proof. So it graduates to default-on after ONE supervised clean boot (Boot B) in which lodbias, lodscan and setlod pass and the default probe gate is unchanged.
- The graduation mechanism is the D3DFeat owner's: prefer a per-feature kill bit (e.g. Diag\D3DFeatOff) over an absent-value default, which would silently drop LODCTRL on a box that sets D3DFeat for another bit.

Default-on from the first build, log only:
- the one-shot INFO line per distinct non-zero TSS 19/20 value (cap 8 per context);
- the SETTEXLOD counter and its single WARN;
- the ctx_free summary line.
G27.d3dprobe_test:
Three explicit-only (silicon) checks in tools/d3dprobe.c. The default list stays unchanged because 86Box's LOD is wrong.

The scene:
- a 256x256 R5G6B5 D3DPOOL_MANAGED chain of 9 levels, each level one solid colour: L0 red, L1 green, L2 blue, L3 yellow, L4 magenta, L5 cyan, L6 white, L7 grey, L8 orange. 256 works on both the default and the BigTex texture paths;
- 192-px quads with uv = 0.75*2^LOD;
- LOD fractions of .15/.85, never .5. A piecewise-linear log2 puts them at 1.11 and 1.80, giving at least 0.3 of margin;
- each case is one frame, with the centre pixel (128,128) checked by expect() at tolerance 12.

(1) lodbias, judged against D3D's rules, at 16 and 32 bpp fullscreen:

| case | set-up | LOD | expect | old HAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | POINT | 1.15 | L1 | L1 (control) |
| B | POINT | 1.85 | L2 | L1 (nearest rounding) |
| B2 | LINEAR | 1.85 | L2 (judged only while MIPFLINEAR is absent) | L1 |
| C | bias -1.0 | 2.15 | L1 (flipped sign: L3) | L2 |
| D | bias +1.0 | 1.15 | L2 (flipped sign: L0) | L1 |
| E | bias -0.5 | 1.85 | L1 (Glide's -0.25 decode: L2) | L1 |
| E2 | bias +0.5 | 1.15 | L2 | L1 |
| F | MAXMIPLEVEL 2 | 0.15 | L2 | L0 |
| F2 | MAXMIPLEVEL 2, magnified | -1.0 | L2 | L0 |
| G | MAXMIPLEVEL 20 | 0.15 | L8, the smallest (never LODMIN>LODMAX) | L0 |
| H | MIPFILTER NONE + bias 2 + maxmip 2 | 1.85 | L0, both states inert | L0 |
| I1 | two stages: stage 0 bias +1, stage 1 SELECTARG2(CURRENT) | 1.15 | chain-1 L2 (stage 0's bias reaches TMU1) | chain-1 L1 |
| I2 | stage 1 SELECTARG1(TEXTURE); stage 0 bias +1, maxmip 3 | 1.15 | chain-2 L1 (no leak; 3dfx's crossed biases give L2/L3) | chain-2 L1 |
| I3 | as I2, stage 1 bias +1 | 1.15 | chain-2 L2 | chain-2 L1 |
| K | MAG LINEAR / MIN POINT, L0 a 1-texel red/blue checker | -0.25 | at least 16 of 64 row pixels are bilinear mixes: the magnification choice stays at LOD 0 (3dfx-style rounding gives 0) | mixed |
| K2 | as K | +0.25 | 0 mixes | 0 mixes |

Without the MIPMAPLODBIAS cap the bias cases (C, D, E, E2, I1, I3) still draw, but are reported skipped. d3dprobe_run counts a skipped named check as not a pass, which is correct for the old HAL.

(2) lodscan, the measurement:
- POINT, bias 0, LOD from -0.5 to 3.0 in 1/32 steps (113 frames); each centre pixel is classified to the nearest level colour.
- It reports the transitions next to D3D's [0.5, 1.5, 2.5] and the truncating [1.0, 2.0, 3.0].
- Pass: every transition within +-0.15 of D3D's, monotonic, no garbage colour.
- It can run on TODAY's build with no driver change: the first measurement of the truncation and of the silicon's LOD-approximation error.

(3) setlod:

| case | set-up | LOD | expect |
|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | SetLOD(1), MIP NONE | -1 | L1 |
| J2 | SetLOD(2), MIP POINT | 0.15 | L2 |
| J3 | SetLOD(1) + MAXMIPLEVEL 2 | 0.15 | L2, reported: does the runtime rebase MAXMIPLEVEL? |

J1 and J2 must pass on any build, proving the runtime does SetLOD; the SETTEXLOD counter must read 0.

Caps mode gains "lodbias":0|1. Optional cross-check: run lodscan, lodbias and setlod once on a vendor-driver GeForce box to confirm the reference values: rounding, bias sign, MAXMIPLEVEL as an index, case H.

G27.risk:
Default 16 bpp path and every path with the switch off: none. There is no tLOD, caps or register change; only a parse-equivalent SETTEXLOD case and capped INFO/WARN logs. A Python test pins this.

Switch on:
- Only tLOD bits 17:0 change, and only for driver-placed chains with 2 or more levels drawn with MIPFILTER > NONE.
- There is no new register, write, ordering, FIFO, flip or target change. texBaseAddr and textureMode are untouched. A wrong encoding samples the wrong level: visible and recoverable, never a hang or corruption.
- The fractional LODMIN is new on this silicon: case K verifies it, and the fallback is one line.
- Visual change: titles that send no bias get distant textures about half a level softer than today. That is D3D-correct and is what 3dfx shipped, but the user may perceive it as blurrier. Red Faction's -0.75 and UE2's raw -0.5 restore roughly today's look.
- G06/G07 exposure: smaller levels are sampled sooner, so a chain with misplaced small levels (G07) shows its garbage more. In-game arming waits for G07.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence: unchanged.
- The HAL already writes TMU0's whole tLOD (and TMU1's in two-stage draws) today; only the value differs.
- Glide rewrites tLOD from its shadow in grTexSource before it textures (inferred), so no bias leaks into Glide.
- MesaFX's own -0.25 bias never reaches D3D.

SLI: none today, since D3D is single-chip. Under G51 the same tLOD goes to all chips; 3dfx's per-chip bias trick needs AA, which is off.

Flip path: untouched.

Performance: neutral to slightly positive (smaller levels sooner); a game's negative bias costs a little (MesaFX's sharper bias measured up to 9% in GPU-bound RtCW on this board). D3D is transport-bound today, so it is unlikely to show.

Caps: reporting MIPMAPLODBIAS may switch a game (UE2 'Supports LOD biasing') onto a bias path, which then works.

Is a fractional LODMIN (4.2) honoured for the min/mag filter choice, as SPEC L3857/L3931 imply (probe case K)? If not, fall back to 3dfx's integer LODMIN, accepting a half-level shift of the threshold when MAG != MIN filter.

Which MIPMAPLODBIAS value does UE2 actually send in game: raw -0.5 at device set-up, or _ftol2 -> 0.0 per texture state (UT2004 D3DDrv 0x1001a32d)? The Boot A lodstate log answers it.
Does XP's D3D8 runtime forward D3DTSS_MIPMAPLODBIAS to a HAL that does not report the cap? Boot A's probe bias cases plus the log answer it.
After SetLOD, does the runtime rebase MAXMIPLEVEL for its smaller device copy (setlod J3)? The HAL cannot correct it if not; no staged title is known to combine the two.

The W2K DDK help reverses the bias sign and calls MAXMIPLEVEL '2^n'; the headers, 3dfx, Glide and the hardware disagree. Probe cases C/D/F/G and a vendor-driver run settle it.

Does the DX7 runtime (d3dim700, DX6/DX7 titles) ever send SETTEXLOD to a non-managing driver? d3d8.dll does not; the new counter will show it for the others.

G18.approach:
VERDICT: the gap is real. One dominant cause was identified from the staged game data, and the driver can fix it. It is a texture-aspect refusal, not fog, TFACTOR or blending.

THE CAUSE
- DM-Antalus is the map of both staged UE2 test scenes: the UT2003 flyby and the UT2004 botmatch/statfps runs. Its sky is a six-face BSP sky box (brush Polys29, identical in LIB/UT2003 and LIB/UT2004, md5-checked):
  - three walls use AntalusTextures.sky.antalusB0000, an 8x512 DXT5 vertical gradient, (198,128,93) at the top to (231,219,206) at the bottom, 10 levels, clamped;
  - the fourth wall is the 1024x512 planet panel antalusB0001;
  - the ceiling is antalusB0321, 8x8, solid (198,128,93);
  - the floor is cp_white1 (UT2004; white by design) or the Cloudcombine combiner (UT2003 level model);
  - an OB_Modulate cloud dome (Shader cloudsky2) sits over all of it.
- The VSA-100 TMU samples at most 8:1. The failure chain:
  - mipchain_ext leaves the 64:1 texture to DirectDraw (vcrdd_d3d.c:416-417);
  - ext_layout -> vcr_texlod_compute_ext refuses it at draw time (common/vcr_texlod.c:105);
  - compute_regs draws untextured (:932-944, color_path :690) with the 0xFFFFFFFF default diffuse (vcrdd_3d.c:187).
- So three walls are pure white.

THE EVIDENCE
- The white is exactly (255,255,255): 64.2% of the UT2003 frame at 30 s, 36.8% of UT2004 statfps at 100 s.
- At 100 s the orange strip is the ceiling. Its straight edge is the ceiling/wall edge, and everything below it is white.
- UT2004 botmatch at 65 s shows the 565 dither of exactly (198,128,93), B0321's colour. So the sky box is drawn with these textures.
- Fog is ruled out by the map data:
  - the zones fog toward (118,105,65) over 2000-9000 units, inside the W table;
  - the sky zone has no distance fog.
- 3dfx's own W2K HAL stored textures above 8:1 as 8:1 and stretched them at TEXBLT and Unlock (AspectRatioGT8, VH5/D3TXTR.C:1788-1885, :2645-2680, :4012-4100; DDSURF.C:2072-2087), while reporting MaxTextureAspectRatio 8. Our MesaFX ICD rescales the same way (fxddtex.c:676-735). So G88's aspect limit can be hidden by the driver.
- Scope: the staged UT2003 has 11 textures above 8:1 and UT2004 25: the Antalus sky, rope in Tokara Forest, UT2004 menu strips (very likely the flat menu band at S08F 60 s y 218-256: ScrollSmall 1024x32 is 40 px tall at 1280), the ULogo scan, Onslaught beams, fonts and gradients.

NOT THIS ITEM
- Stripes, the cyan triangle and the striped floor: G06/G07.
- visual-11: a thin band on black, no white. Likely a menu transition; recapture under G79.
- TFACTOR and blend factors: not needed to explain the white (G14/G28/G29).

THE DESIGN
- **Part A (default-on, log-only).**
  - a WARN at creation for every texture above 8:1, logged as "expanded" or "drawn UNTEXTURED";
  - stage-1 refusals logged (they are silent today, :928);
  - refused-bind counts in the context-end summary.
- **Part B (the fix, Diag\D3DFeat bit ASPECT, default off):** a driver-owned, packed, 16-byte-aligned 8:1 shadow chain per texture above 8:1. The application's surface stays as DirectDraw placed it, so Lock and TEXBLT are untouched.
  - New pure module include/vcr_texaspect.h + common/vcr_texaspect.c: vcr_tex_aspect_plan gives W'=max(w,big/8), H'=max(h,big/8) and per-level k; expansion is nearest-neighbour replication along the narrow axis.
  - 16/32-bit: texels are replicated.
  - DXT1/3/5: lossless, with no decode. Each output block comes from one source block: endpoints are copied and only the 2/3/4-bit index fields are rebuilt, unlike 3dfx's decode/re-encode.
  - Lifetime: allocated in Dd_CreateSurface (top level only, via DDSCAPS2_MIPMAPSUBLEVEL) with HeapVidMemAllocAligned. A descriptor sits in lpGbl->dwReserved1 with SF_ASPECT in dwReserved1. Freed in Dd_DestroySurface, which stays not-handled.
  - Refresh: at bind, view_of -> aspect_view re-expands when any level is SF_DIRTY or the shadow is unfilled, under VcrDd2dSync, then VcrDd3dTexFlush. flush_written defers to it.
  - The TMU view is the existing tex_view(_ext), refactored to explicit geometry and given the shadow as a placed chain (aspect 3, TBIG, 26-bit base, existing filter/clamp/LOD rules). v->w/h = W'/H', so the S/T scale maps u 0..1 across the stretched texture: exact for WRAP and CLAMP.
  - No new registers or fields, single pass.
  - Caps: MaxTextureAspectRatio stays 8 unless E1 shows the runtime refusing creation.
  - On the default path, a shadow at or above 16 MB is refused until G21 lands.
- **Part C (contingency, Diag\D3DDebugTint, debug-only):** refused textures draw magenta through c0 and CP_LOCAL_C0.

THE INVESTIGATION LEFT
- **E1:** LogLevel 2 on the deployed build (shared with G05/G12/G14's measurement boot). Expect 513/7 with c=0x00080200 (8x512). An outcome table in G18.md maps each other result.
- **E2:** a B1/B3 A/B on the camera-deterministic UT2003 flyby.
- **E3:** the tint, only if white survives.
G18.gating:
- **Part A (log-only): default-on.**
  - It adds the creation WARN for textures above 8:1, the stage-1 refusal log and the context-end refusal counts.
  - It writes no registers. Its cost is one IOCTL per over-aspect texture creation (a few per title, at precache) plus one summary event per context.
  - A Python source test pins that the draw path is unchanged.
- **Part B (the shadow): default OFF**, behind Diag\D3DFeat bit VCR_D3DFEAT_ASPECT, read at boot. The shared D3DFeat plumbing is created by whichever item lands first.
  - With the bit off, no shadow is allocated and SF_ASPECT is never set, so view_of runs today's code and every register write is byte-identical.
  - It is not safe to land default-on yet: it allocates video memory and programs texBaseAddr/tLOD values no silicon run has used. 8:1 DXT, 8:1 TBIG and 8:1 A8R8G8B8 have never been probed (the widest tested is 4:1).
  - It graduates to default-on after the supervised B3 boot passes (aspect probes, default and BigTex lists unchanged, the UT2003 flyby A/B) and a D3D title sweep (G73) with it armed shows no regression.
- **Part C (Diag\D3DDebugTint): debug-only**, default 0, never graduates.
- **One Diag change per clean boot:** E1 = LogLevel 2; B1 = the new build alone; B3 = ASPECT; B4 = the tint, only if needed.

G18.risk:
**Low to the proven paths.**
- With ASPECT off, only logging differs: Part A is pinned, and no register value changes.
- With it on, only textures above 8:1 change, and today those draw white.

**The one shared-code change** is refactoring tex_view/tex_view_ext to take explicit geometry. It is guarded by the existing texlod native tests and a Python assertion that both views read the surface's own geometry when it is not a shadow.

**Video memory.**
- Shadows are small: 43,792 B for the Antalus strip, about 175 KB for the menu strips and rope, about 700 KB per 2048x32 Onslaught beam. That is about 3 MB as an upper bound, never resident at once.
- The shadow is allocated before DirectDraw places the application's surface, so a nearly full heap can make the creation fail. The runtime would then evict and retry (inferred).
- A failed allocation, or a block at heap offset 0 (G63), falls back to today's refusal, logged.

**Coherency.**
- The refresh is a CPU write into video memory after VcrDd2dSync, then the existing TMU flush: the TEXBLT rules.
- A 2D-engine Blt into an over-aspect texture is not flagged dirty (G37, inherited).
- On the default path without D3DBigTex, a shadow at or above 16 MB would be sampled 16 MB lower (G21), so it is refused until G21 lands.

**Lifetime.** If dxg ever drops a texture without DestroySurface at a mode change, the descriptor leaks and the heap is rebuilt beneath it. This is the same open question as G43/R4 for mip chains.

**Untouched:** Glide/OpenGL coexistence (the shadow is a D3D-session DirectDraw-heap block, and Glide owns the board exclusively), SLI (D3D is chip 0 only), the flip path.

**Narrow-axis filtering** is coarser than true bilinear (replicated texels), as 3dfx and MesaFX ship it. It is invisible for the Antalus strip, which is constant across its narrow axis.

**First-time silicon:** 8:1 DXT, 8:1 TBIG and 8:1 A8R8G8B8. The aspect* probes cover them before any game run.

G32.approach:
The gap is real, and large for big fog gradients.

**Today's path.** Vertex fog sends a synthetic 1/W per vertex that lands on a ramp fog table (vcr_fog.h:10-14, vcrdd_3d.c:202-209, vcr_fog.c:75-92). The value is exact at each vertex: on silicon `fogvertex` passes 3/3 at 16 and 32 bpp (onbox 640x480x16 7b007b, 1024x768x32_clean 7f007f). But the chip interpolates 1/W, and the table index is logarithmic in 1/W. On a triangle running from no fog to full fog, the midpoint fog alpha is about 16/255 instead of 128, and at t=7/8 it is 49 instead of 223. Moderate gradients are wrong too: 0.2->0.6 gives 0.262 at the midpoint instead of 0.40.

**What the hardware offers.** fogMode[4:3] is the fog-alpha source mux (SPEC L2848-2849, L2885). W[39:32] is wired to the fog unit (fbzColorPath bit-28 text, L2791-2798). 3dfx routes Z-buffered and Z-less vertex fog as fogMode ENFOGGING|FOG_Z|FOG_ALPHA|FOG_DITHER = 0x59, with Wb = (float)(255 - specular alpha) (VH5/D3FOG.C:215-222; D6TRI2I.C:904-906). That code is H3-era: it was written in 1998 for Banshee/Voodoo3 and branched for Napalm (W9X/D3FOG.C:58,91,117). The 86Box setup unit makes W = sWb*2^32 (voodoo_setup.c:187-199).

**Design: a single pass, with no new register traffic beyond the source bits.**
- New header include/vcr_fogsrc.h, integer only and host-tested:
  - VCR_FOGV_NONE/RAMP(=1)/W/Z;
  - vcr_fogv_source(armed, depth_is_w): Z if depth_is_w (G23 only), else W if armed, else RAMP;
  - vcr_fogv_mode: RAMP 0x41, W 0x59, Z 0x51;
  - vcr_fogv_amount(sa) = 255 - sa.
- vcr_3dregs.h gains FM_ALPHA (1<<3), FM_Z (1<<4), FM_FOGADD and FM_FOGMULT.
- compute_regs (vcrdd_d3d.c:1013-1016): c->fog_vertex = vcr_fogv_source(pd->fog_iter, 0) and r->fogMode = vcr_fogv_mode(...). Table fog is unchanged.
- prepare: d.fog_vertex = spec_off ? c->fog_vertex : NONE. The no-specular rule is kept.
- vertex(): a new branch before the untouched ramp branch. For VCR_FOGV_W it writes sOowfbi = (float)(255 - sa), with the same writes in the same order.
- VcrDd3dState: the fog table is loaded only when !(fogMode & (FM_ALPHA|FM_Z)). For the W source the cached table stays valid, and vertex fog no longer depends on G41's stale table cache.
- fbzColorPath bit 28 stays 0, as 3dfx left it. The values stay in [0,255], and the wrap rule maps -eps to 0 and 256 to 0xff.
- TMU W is unaffected: SM_W0/SM_W1 plus sOow0/sOow1 override the broadcast Wb.

**Caps.** ShadeCaps gains FOGGOURAUD|FOGFLAT only when armed; D3D8 then reads 00084008. The caps ride the switch because DX5/DX6 pickers test FOGGOURAUD: H&D's igraph2.dll names it, and AvP prints it. Advertising it on the ramp path could switch a title into the approximation.

**Instrumentation, default-on.** Per-context counters for vertex-fogged triangles, vertex fog dropped for want of a specular, and table-fogged triangles. They are logged at context gone under a new event 513 'what', plus an armed event.

**For G23.** Under a W-buffer, vertex fog moves to the Z carrier: fogMode 0x51, sVz = (255 - sa) << 8 at 16 bpp, << 16 at 32 bpp (28.4, inferred). 3dfx's constant << 8 would fog nothing at 32 bpp. This lands with G23 and is host-tested now.

**The bits 3+4 conflict (S1).** It is settled by one d3dprobe draw. The fog factor goes in Wb, the depth is a constant z=0.25 (Z[27:20] = 0x3f at both depths) and the diffuse alpha is a constant 0xC0, so W, Z-precedence and alpha-precedence each predict a different colour.
- Outcome W: the design stands.
- Outcome Z or alpha: disarm. Keep the ramp for Z-buffered draws, use the Z carrier only where Z is free (no depth test or write, or G23's W-buffer), and do not use FOG_ALPHA.

**RANGEFOG** stays the runtime's job.

G32.d3dprobe_test:
All four tests use pretransformed vertices with FOGENABLE, FOGCOLOR 0xff0000ff and FOGTABLEMODE/FOGVERTEXMODE NONE (the factor is the specular alpha). References are computed analytically. Tolerance is 12 per channel at 16 bpp and 5 at 32 bpp.

**1) fogvgrad** (explicit until graduation). This is both the S1 experiment and the exactness proof.
- Draw A: quad x 32..224, y 32..112, z 0.25, rhw 1, diffuse 0xc0ff0000 (alpha 0xC0), specular alpha 0xff at the left and 0x00 at the right. Checks at y=72, x = 32, 56, ..., 200, 222.
- Draw B: triangle (32,128) sa ff, (224,128) sa ff, (128,224) sa 00. Checks at x=128, y = 140..212 step 12.
- Want: R = round(255(1-t)), G = 0, B = round(255t). For example x=128 gives 800080 and x=200 gives 2000df.
- Pass: 16/16, with RESULT "fog_source":"exact".
- The probe classifies the source:
  - z: constant ~bf0040 (Z[27:20] = 0x3f at both depths);
  - alpha: constant ~3f00c0;
  - ramp: the old curve, ~ee0011 at x=128 and ~cd0032 at x=200;
  - otherwise unknown.
- It FAILS on today's path; that is expected, and Boot A records the old curve on silicon.

**2) fogvgrad_tex.** Draw A again with a white 64x64 R5G6B5 texture, MODULATE(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE), point filter. 9 checks with the same wants.

- Quad rhw 1.0 at the left and 0.25 at the right, u 0->1, SELECTARG1(TEXTURE), point filter, vertex fog on with sa 0xff (Wb = 0 armed, 1.0 on the ramp path).
- Checks at y=44 and the perspective-correct cell centres x ~72, 124, 156, 177, 193, 204, 213, 221.

- table LINEAR 1..5 at rhw 1/3: want 80007f, tol 40;
- vertex sa 0x40: want 4000bf;
- the same table at rhw 1/8: want 0000ff (a cache hit after a W draw, or a reload after the ramp);
- vertex fog with an FVF lacking specular: report-only, none = ff0000 or full = 0000ff.

G31.approach:
REAL and fixable. A host prototype built against the real vcr_fog.c confirms the bug: for LINEAR 0.2..0.8, and for D3D's default 0..1, the W-indexed table has 64 of 64 entries at 255, so every pixel is the fog colour.

3dfx's answer (PXLFOGLIN, VH5/D3FOG.C:376-395, PRS 13517 for Centipede) was to zero the table, i.e. no fog. Fix: take 3dfx's exact test but draw D3D's Z-based fog correctly with the registers we already use.
- Detection: LINEAR only, start < 1.0 && end <= 1.0; 1.0/1.0 stays W, the WHQL W-fog exclusion 3dfx added 04/04/00. It is an integer-only predicate on the float bit patterns, vcr_fog_zrange_bits in vcr_fog.h, because the HAL is built -mgeneral-regs-only.
- When it fires, each vertex sends sOowfbi = vcr_fog_z_oow(sz) = 1 - (1 - 5/2^18)*sz. This is affine in device z, so the setup unit iterates it exactly as it iterates Z.
- The same 64-entry table is built at the z each entry stands for: z_i = (1 - 1/w_i)/(1 - 5/2^18), via a new vcr_fog_table_z using the same LINEAR/EXP/EXP2 formulas. VCR_FOG_ZINDEX is or'd into fog_table[0], which is the cache key.
- Deltas are saturated to 0..63 by a new vcr_fog_reg_sat. SPEC section 8.46 says a step "cannot exceed 63", and today's '& 0xff' wraps 64 to 0. A Z table needs this: LINEAR 0.25..0.75 has steps of 64, and a wrapped delta reads 64 instead of 127.5 at the midpoint.
- Single pass. fogMode stays 0x41 (ENFOGGING|FOG_DITHER). Same registers, order and write counts. vcr_fog_table and vcr_fog_reg are untouched.
- Code changes: compute_regs sets c->fog_z, prepare copies it into vcr3d_draw, vertex() gets one else-if branch, VcrDd3dState gets two dispatches.
- Caps unchanged. Keep WFOG; never add ZFOG.

Accuracy, from a host model of the SPEC 8.22 lookup (index from 1/W, blend linear in 1/W): LINEAR Z fog is within 1/255 when start/end fall on entries, and up to about 13/255 near a kink that falls between entries (W tables have the same limit). The predicate had 0 mismatches against real float compares over 2M random pairs.

All checks use untextured red quads (0xffff0000) with fog colour blue, FOGTABLEMODE LINEAR and FOGVERTEXMODE NONE. Expected colours are computed in the probe as a = clamp((z-start)/(end-start)), want = ((255-round(255a))<<16) | round(255a). Tolerance is 12 per channel at 32 bpp and 16 at 16 bpp. Both tests are explicit (--tests) until promotion, and the RESULT records Diag\D3DFeat.

fogtable_z (the units): six 32x128 quads at x0 = 8+40i, y 64..192, sampled at (x0+16, 128). rhw is constant within each quad, so a W index cannot separate them.
- z 0.10, start 0.2, end 0.8: ff0000.
- z 0.50, same range: 7f0080.
- z 0.65, same range: 4000bf.
- z 0.90, same range: 0000ff.
- z 0.50, start 0.999, end 1.0: ff0000 (a Z range; end <= 1 is inclusive).
- z 0.50, rhw 0.5, start = end = 1.0: 0000ff (NOT a Z range; it stays W, 3dfx's WHQL exclusion).
Pass is 6/6. The old build or bit off fails 4 (everything blue). A 3dfx-style zeroed table would fail 3.

LINEAR 0.25..0.75; both kinks fall on table entries 2 and 8. Columns at y = 128, x = 56, 80, 92, 104, 128, 152, 176, 200 expect ff0000, ff0000, df0020, bf0040, 7f0080, 4000bf, 0000ff, 0000ff.

G33.approach:
The gap is real and the fix is small. It is one pass and costs no CPU, but no staged .124 title has been shown to need it, so it is P3.

TODAY: tex_view and tex_view_ext (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:792-795, 830-833) map only D3DTADDRESS_CLAMP, to textureMode TM_CLAMPS/T (bits 6/7). MIRROR, BORDER, D3D8's MIRRORONCE and any other value draw as WRAP. The caps honestly omit MIRROR (TextureAddressCaps 0x15, prim_caps :2044-2045).

HARDWARE: tLOD bit 28 (tmirrors) and bit 29 (tmirrort) (SPEC 8.77 L3927-3928). They are identical on Banshee/Voodoo3 (GL5 h3 h3defs.h:281-282, gtex.c:645-661, TEXMIRROR in diget.c:679).
- 3dfx's chip simulator H5/CSIM/TREX.C (:738-788, :840-865, :1322-1344) and diag model DIAGS/TREX/SSTTEX.C:1354-1395 define the semantics. The mirror happens per axis at the selected level's own size (TBIG included). The two bilinear taps are mirrored separately, so a seam blends the edge texel with itself. This is exactly D3D MIRROR.
- Mirror and clamp together are a different mode: outside [0, 2*size) the TMU returns texel 0. That matches no D3D mode, so the mapping never sets both on one axis.
- 3dfx shipped MIRROR in tri and line caps (VH5/D3INIT.C:2874, 3084). The single-stage bits go in a common tLOD word that is ORed into both TMUs (VH5/D6MT.C:5692-5702; D6DP2.C:6521, 6588). With two textures, stage 0 goes to tLODT1 and stage 1 to tLODT0 (D6MT.C:5936-5946, 6102-6111).
- 86Box mirrors one fixed coordinate bit before its bilinear offset (86B voodoo_render.c:306-313). It is right only for square, point-sampled textures.

DESIGN:
(1) vcr_3dregs.h gains TL_MIRRORS (1<<28) and TL_MIRRORT (1<<29).
(2) New pure header include/vcr_texaddr.h with vcr_tex_address(u, v, flags), returning {tm, tlod}:
- CLAMP sets the textureMode clamp bit, as today.
- MIRROR, and MIRRORONCE (exact for |u|<=1, never advertised), set the tLOD mirror bit, but only with VCR_TADDR_F_MIRROR.
- BORDER (left to G86) and every other value stay wrap.
- Clamp and mirror are exclusive by construction.
(3) vcrdd_d3d.c gets one helper, tex_address(pd, tss, v), which ORs the result into v->textureMode/v->tLOD. tex_view gains a pd parameter. Both views replace their four CLAMP lines with the call.
- compute_regs is unchanged: the bits ride in v0/v1 to whichever TMU samples the stage (:952, :955, :963).
- VcrDd3dState already writes the whole tLOD at every state send (vcrdd_3d.c:115, 123).
- Static asserts pin the enum values against d3dtypes.h.
- log_combo hashes the mirror bits.
(4) Caps: after prim_caps (:2071-2072), add D3DPTADDRESSCAPS_MIRROR to dpcTriCaps and dpcLineCaps only when pd->tex_mirror is set. D3D8/9 then report 0x17. prim_caps itself is untouched.
(5) Plumbing: one positive Diag\D3DFeat bit, VCR_D3DFEAT_MIRROR (next free bit; provisionally 14, 0x4000), read at boot by the miniport. VcrDd2dInit sets pd->tex_mirror on every chip, after zeroing it before the IOCTL. Event 513 logs "armed". This uses the shared convention of G05/G08/G26/G28/G29; G33 creates the plumbing if it lands first.
(6) Log-only, default-on counter: a per-context addr_seen bitmask, ORed in the DP2 TSS walk for ADDRESSU/V on stages 0 and 1 (bit = value), printed once in ctx_free's event 2. One pass over the titles turns the unknowns into fact. It moves into G76's block if that lands first.

OFF PATH: byte-for-byte unchanged, both register stream and caps. ON: only a stage that asks for 2 or 5 changes, and only in tLOD bits 28/29.

INVARIANTS handed to other gaps:
- G26/G50: a stage split across both TMUs carries the mirror bits on both.
- G51: per-chip tLOD writes derive from r->tLOD.
- G53: tLOD is compared whole, and the shadow is dropped after any Glide session.
- G86: BORDER is a one-line change in the same function.
- G08: it feeds DX5/DX6 MIRROR into ADDRESSU/V.
- G15: never refuse address modes.

The gap's "Halo, UT2004" was an inference and is refuted for their engine code.

G33.gating:
Default OFF, behind one positive Diag\D3DFeat bit, VCR_D3DFEAT_MIRROR (next free bit when it lands; provisionally bit 14, 0x4000). The miniport reads it at boot. The caps and the drawing sit behind the same bit: caps without drawing would lie, and drawing without caps helps no known title. The bit applies on every chip, because Banshee/Voodoo3 have the same tLOD bits.

With the bit off, the register stream and the caps are byte-for-byte today's. A native test proves this for every value; a Python test proves it for the call sites and the caps.

It is proven by one supervised clean boot with this bit as the only Diag change. In that boot, d3dprobe mirror and mirror_ext must pass at 640x480x16, 1024x768x32 and windowed, and the onbox regression set must be unchanged.

After that boot it is SAFE to graduate to default-ON, through the plan's shared D3DFeat default/kill-mask convention. With the bit off nothing changes, and with it on only requests that are drawn wrongly today change.

It is not safe to land default-on before silicon. The caps change would move any caps-checking title onto a path that has never run on this card.

Fallback if a caps-checking title gets worse: keep the drawing and withdraw the cap (one if).

G33.risk:
Low, confined to MIRROR requests.

Default 16 bpp path: unchanged with the bit off. The register stream and caps are byte-for-byte identical, pinned by native tests over every value, by Python call-site and caps tests, and by Boot A's probe. With the bit on, only a stage whose ADDRESSU/V is 2 or 5 changes, and only in tLOD bits 28/29. There is no new register, write, pass or per-vertex work.

Caps change: a caps-checking title could switch to a mirror path. The scanned staged titles do not use MIRROR, and Halo tests only the BORDER bit. Boot B watches for this, and the fallback is to withdraw the cap and keep the drawing.

Silicon: these bits have never run on this card. A wrong mirror would still be a texel lookup inside the same level, because the result is masked to the level (CSIM TREX.C:851, 1332). There is no out-of-texture address and no hang mechanism. TBIG and DXT with mirror are unproven; mirror_ext E5/E6 cover them.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence: no new shared state. The HAL writes the whole tLOD at every textured state send (vcrdd_3d.c:115, 123). Glide's window open re-asserts CLAMP/CLAMP on both TMUs, which clears the mirror bits (GL5 gsst.c:989, 1011 -> gtex.c:1121).

SLI: untouched. D3D runs on chip 0, and no SLI register is written. Future per-chip tLOD writes must start from r->tLOD.

Flip path and 2D engine: untouched. The texture-port flush is unaffected, because addressing bits do not change host writes.

The 86Box bed models mirror inaccurately for non-square textures and bilinear seams; its E1/E2 failures are not HAL bugs.

G35.approach:
The gap is real and fixable, at 32 bpp only, in one pass. Every claim was checked in the code:
- D24S8 is listed (vcrdd_d3d.c:2204-2212) and reaches D3D8 as D3DFMT_D24S8.
- dwStencilCaps is never set (the extended caps are memset, :2150-2172).
- compute_regs (:921-1029) never reads rs[52..59].
- clear_rects (:1408-1421) builds `what` from TARGET and ZBUFFER only; the stencil value (DP2 CLEAR offset 12, Clear2 dwFillStencil) is never read.
- 32 bpp targets write stencilMode = stencilOp = 0 (vcr_3dseq.h:56-77).

No staged title is shown to need stencil:
- Halo's CCW_STENCIL* strings sit in a full D3D9 render-state name table (D3DX); the only Halo hint is the global `rasterizer_stencil_mask`.
- Max Payne has a getStencilMask(D3DFORMAT) helper.
- BF1942 is blocked by DRM (G72).
- UT2003/2004 are staged UseStencil=False.
- H&D only dumps the caps.
- The other D3D titles show no stencil strings.
Hence P3; escalate to P1 if the counters show a staged title using stencil.

DESIGN. Two default-OFF bits of Diag\D3DFeat, read at boot, VSA-100 with D3D32 only: STENCIL (provisional bit 14, 0x4000) and STENCILCAPS (bit 15, 0x8000, needs STENCIL).

(1) New Win32-free header include/vcr_stencil.h. Register layout, from SPEC 8.27/8.28 and VH5/H3DEFS.H:143-186:
- stencilMode = ref[7:0] | mask[15:8] | wmask[23:16] | ENABLE[24] | func[27:25], with func = D3DCMP-1;
- stencilOp = fail[3:0] | zfail[7:4] | zpass[11:8], each op = D3DSTENCILOP-1 (the spec says the order was changed to match D3D);
- the test is (ref&mask) func (dst&mask), with ref on the left, as in D3D;
- disabled or not live = the pair 0/0, never the enable bit alone. With enable clear the chip does ALWAYS + REPLACE under the write mask (3dfx PRS 12972);
- vcr_stencil_zbits accepts only our listed layout (DDPF_STENCILBUFFER, 8 bits, mask 0xff000000);
- the clear mode is 0x00ff0000|value.

(2) target_of: new vcr3d_target.z_stencil = 8 when z_on, the target is 32 bpp and the Z has that layout.

(3) compute_regs: when STENCILENABLE is set and the stencil is live (armed, 32 bpp, z_on, 8 bits), fill the new vcr3d_regs.st_live, stencilMode and stencilOp. VcrDd3dState writes the pair LAST, with its own VcrDdRoom(2), so every existing FIFO count is unchanged. prepare() always sends the target before the state, so stencil goes 0/0 then live, and a disable falls back to the target's 0/0.

(4) The target sequence gains st16: when armed, the 0/0 pair is written at 16 bpp too (9 writes, identical to 4a9793b's sequence). This stops our own live stencil from leaking into a later 16 bpp context through the unproven 16 bpp premise. 3dfx's NT HAL wrote DISABLE/0 at every depth on every state send. Glide resets stencil at its window open (gsst.c:956).

(5) Clears:
- the DP2 CLEAR passes rd(p+12) and Clear2 passes dwFillStencil;
- VCR3D_CLEAR_STENCIL is set only when armed and the target has stencil bits;
- the clear writes move into vcr_3dseq.h helpers (vcr_3d_clear_head/_tail): stencilMode = 0x00ff0000|value before the FASTFILLs, and 0 after the clip restore;
- a stencil-only clear uses fbzMode 0x001;
- the value never goes into zaColor (its [31:24] is alpha; G22 owns [23:0]).
FASTFILL has no per-bit stencil mask (SPEC 21.4). D3D's Clear writes all bits, as 3dfx's FastFill does (D7DP2.C:862-874), so the 2D byte-mask path is not needed. Stencil writes follow the stencil write mask, not fbzMode[10], so ZWRITEENABLE FALSE keeps shadow-volume ops working.

(6) ctx_defaults sets D3D's stencil defaults (KEEP, ALWAYS, masks 0xffffffff).

(7) Caps: dwStencilCaps = 0xff (KEEP..DECR) only with STENCILCAPS. Never TWOSIDED: there is one stencilOp, so two-sided stencil is impossible in one pass. Stencil at 16 bpp is a hardware limit.

(8) Step 0, log-only on every build (G76's counter carried here): per-context counts of STENCILENABLE, live, stencil clears asked and done, ops/funcs seen, and TWOSIDEDSTENCILMODE set. They are logged at ctx_free, plus a ContextCreate line naming the Z's stencil fields.

OLD PATH. With D3DFeat absent: no new register write, the same VcrDdRoom counts, caps 0 and the same Z list. Only CPU counters and two log lines are added.
G35.risk:
Off (default): none to the proven paths. Register writes, FIFO waits, caps and the Z list are byte-for-byte today's, pinned by test_vcr_kmd_d3dseq.c with st16=0 and by the new clear-head/tail tests. Only CPU counters and two log lines at context create and free are added.

Armed:
- 16 bpp default path: +2 writes of 0 (stencilMode/stencilOp) per target setup. These are the values 3dfx's NT HAL wrote on every state send; boots B and C re-run the 16 bpp lists.
- 32 bpp: unchanged unless a title enables stencil on D24S8; a title that set stencil states believing them ignored now has them honoured, which is correct D3D.
- Clears: +2 writes only for a stencil clear. FASTFILL's stencil write on SDRAM is unproven (Glide uses an aux-as-colour trick there); F1/F7 decide it, with Glide's trick as the fallback.
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence: Glide's window open writes stencilMode 0 and our next target writes 0/0 at any depth, so no stencil state crosses APIs.
- SLI: none (D3D is chip 0, no sliCtrl/chipMask writes); a future G51 must route stencil fills through the 2D path because of the FASTFILL SLI bugs.
- Flip path: none.
- Caps: only with STENCILCAPS, and a title may take a stencil path never run here (watched in boot C).
Code risks:
- if NT's D24S8 surface lacks DDPF_STENCILBUFFER, stencil stays off (safe; the log names the fields);
- G53's future register shadowing must treat stencilMode/stencilOp as written by the target, the state and the clear.

Halo (only if the step-0 counters show it enabling stencil once STENCILCAPS is reported; hint: rasterizer_stencil_mask)
Max Payne (P_D3D::getStencilMask in e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll; use unmeasured; supervised runs only, G04)
