open_questions: Does XP's D3D8 runtime pass D3DCLEAR_STENCIL (and the stencil render states) to a DX7 HAL whose StencilCaps is 0? Inferred yes for the states, unknown for the clear; boot B's outcome table answers it.

Does a Windows D3D driver's Clear honour D3DRS_STENCILWRITEMASK? The design follows 3dfx's FastFill (it does not; Wine is recalled as doing the same); d3dprobe stencil_clearmask on a GeForce reference box settles it.

Does the native FASTFILL stencil write (stencilMode wmask + ref) work on .124's SDRAM? Glide's SDRAM path avoids it with an aux-as-colour fill (gglide.c:2314-2422); 3dfx's D3D HAL used the native fill. d3dprobe F1/F7 decide it; the fallback is Glide's trick.
Does any staged title use stencil once caps are reported (Halo rasterizer_stencil_mask, Max Payne getStencilMask)? Boot C counters answer it and decide whether this stays P3.
Plan-level: the D3DFeat bit numbers (14/15 provisional), the transport (appended vcr_info.d3dfeat word vs per-feature flags), and how a D3DFeat bit graduates to default-on.
Merge boots B and C to save a reboot? That breaks the one-Diag-change-per-boot rule, so it is the user's call.
Should D24S8 stay listed while STENCIL is off? Recommended yes (apps that name it would otherwise find no 24-bit Z), as vcr_rtfmt.h argues today.

Two-sided stencil (D3D9) could in principle be emulated per triangle by switching stencilOp on winding; it is not proposed, because no staged title needs it and it is unclear whether a DX7-DDI driver can advertise D3DSTENCILCAPS_TWOSIDED or receive render states 185-189.

G39.approach:
The gap is real, fixable and small. The DDK contract is not merely inferred: the NTDDVDEO.H that 3dfx shipped (W2K/Src/Video/Inc/NTDDVDEO.H:618-623) says a clear VIDEO_MODE_NO_ZERO_MEMORY bit means "zero video memory at the set mode". Our display DLL never sets the bit (vcrdd.c:472), and neither half of the driver clears anything. VcrHwSetMode only programs registers, and the miniport maps no frame buffer beyond the cursor page.

There is a vendor reference, although the gap says none. 3dfx's own display driver clears the desktop right after every mode set: bAssertModeHardware(TRUE) calls vClearDesktopSurface (VH5 ENABLE.C:1371-1373, MISC.C:195-215), which is one 2D RECTFILL with colorFore 0 and ROP 0xCC. Its miniport, with DMT_ENABLED forced (H3.H:62, H3.C:859), clears nothing either. In 3dfx's own stack the display driver owns the clear.

The defect has already cost a misdiagnosis. On 10-14 the user reported "the half life game is all garbled" from AvP's stale screen (PLAN:200-206).

Every application mode switch on vcr-kmd builds a new PDEV and goes through DrvEnableSurface (ring_after_probe_i lines 26-76). A same-mode reset is only DrvAssertMode. The desktop sits at the top of memory, so a smaller new primary lies wholly inside the old desktop: AvP's 640x480x16 shows old rows 904-1023 (307,200 of 307,200 pixels stale) and UT2004's 1280x960x16 shows rows 544-1023.

Fix, a single pass:
- **New function.** VcrDd2dClearPrimary(pd) in vcrdd_2d.c, called in DrvEnableSurface right after VcrDd2dInit (vcrdd.c:540).
- **What it writes.** One VcrDd2dFill of the visible primary (off = pjScreen - pvRamBase, pitch lDelta, 0,0,cx,cy, colour 0), then VcrDd2dSync, so the call returns only when the fill is done. These are the proven nine 2D writes: clip0 0/0x1fff1fff, dstBaseAddr = desktop offset (e.g. 0x03f6a000), dstFormat = stride | bppcode<<16 (0x00030500 at 640x480x16, 0x00051400 at 1280x1024x32), commandEx 0, colorFore 0, dstSize (cy<<16)|cx, dstXY 0, command 0xCC000105. SPEC §7.2.6-7.2.9 and L6495 confirm 13-bit sizes, a 14-bit stride and a 26-bit base, so one fill covers every listed mode, up to 1920x1440x32.
- **Cost.** About 2-8 ms per mode change (inferred; event 512/12 measures it).
- **CPU fallback.** Rows of zeros, only where there is no engine by design: no register window (the VM bed) or Diag\Accel2D=0.
- **Wedged engine.** An engine that is present but unusable (FIFO read full, give-up) is never written (SKIP).
- **Decision logic.** It lives in a new Win32-free include/vcr_modeclear.h: vcr_modeclear_how and vcr_modeclear_one_fill.
- **Plumbing.** Diag\ModeClear is read in fill_info at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO and sets the positive flag VCR_INFO_F_MODECLEAR on the next free bit. VcrDd2dInit sets pd->mode_clear from it. Event 512, sub-code 12 (how, offset, us) is added.
- **What does not change.** The miniport mask at vcrmp.c:674 stays; it only gets a comment pointing at the display-side clear. Caps do not change. DP2, Clear2, textures, flips, DrvAssertMode and RESTORE_MODE are untouched.

Deliberately not taken, for the reasons in §4.6:
- a miniport clear (no frame-buffer mapping; it would also run at Glide's release);
- a clear at primary creation (misses some switches; would clear a windowed client's live desktop);
- the vendor's whole-heap clear (runs over Glide's FIFO window);
- a clear at DrvAssertMode(TRUE) or Glide's release (where an alt-tabbed Glide stream resumes);
- an asynchronous fill;
- a 3D fastfill.

Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G39.md.
G39.gating:
The new switch is Diag\ModeClear (DWORD). Absent or 0 is OFF when it lands. It is read at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO, i.e. at every new PDEV, so arming it needs no reboot: the next switch to a different mode picks it up. A same-mode CDS_RESET does not. It is a positive flag, so an older miniport never arms it and an older DLL ignores it.

With the switch off, VcrDd2dClearPrimary returns on its first line, before any read, write or log. DrvEnableSurface's register traffic and memory writes are then today's, byte for byte. It is registered in NEW_DIAG as "ModeClear": "0".

It is a pure correctness fix on a proven primitive, but it should not land default-on blind. It adds 2D traffic at every mode change, including the boot's first DrvEnableSurface and every Glide/OpenGL switch-in. So per the project rule it gets one supervised clean boot (one Diag change in that boot). After that boot, a separate commit moves the default to VcrDiagGet(L"ModeClear", 1), with 0 as the kill switch. That commit moves the entry to MOVED_DIAG with the evidence path and updates the README row to "default ON since <date>", as Accel2DPattern did on 2026-09-28. The user decides that move.

Deploying it means swapping both vcrmp.sys and vcrdd.dll (the flag lives in the miniport) via deploy_box.py, after its activation preflight, then safe-reboot.py. Make no other Diag change in that boot.
G39.d3dprobe_test:
A new d3dprobe mode, `d3dprobe modeclear [--res WxH] [--bpp 16|32] [--pace MS]`. It is fullscreen by definition and driver-agnostic, and it draws nothing.

1. Refuse if WxHxbpp equals the desktop mode: there is no mode change to test.
2. Seed the screen. A topmost popup covers the whole desktop and erases it with RGB(0x5A,0xC3,0xA5). At a 32 bpp desktop that is the dword 0x005AC3A5, and its 16-bit halves 0xC3A5 and 0x005A are both non-black. Do GdiFlush and wait 300 ms. GetPixel(GetDC(NULL)) must then read the seed at the 4 corners and the centre, or the run ends with an error and no switch.
3. Stop erasing: WM_ERASEBKGND returns 1 and WM_PAINT only validates. Call ShowCursor(FALSE).
4. Make a paced CreateDevice: fullscreen HAL, WxH, R5G6B5/X8R8G8B8, 1 back buffer, FLIP, no depth buffer (this keeps G10 out).
5. With no Clear and no Present, CreateImageSurface(A8R8G8B8), GetFrontBuffer, LockRect. Count nonblack (RGB != 0), first_nonblack and seedlike. Read again after 500 ms. If GetFrontBuffer fails, fall back to a GDI BitBlt and report "readvia":"gdi".
6. Release the device (paced).

PASS: nonblack == 0 and nonblack_500ms == 0.

G39.regression_test:
**tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_modeclear.c** (new). It includes include/vcr_modeclear.h and common/vcr_modes.c, so it runs the code the driver runs.
- **off_writes_nothing (the old path).** vcr_modeclear_how(0, ...) is VCR_MC_OFF for all 16 input combinations.
- **an_engine_clears_with_one_fill.** how(1,1,0,1,1) is VCR_MC_ENGINE.
- **No engine by design.** No register window or Diag\Accel2D=0 gives VCR_MC_CPU.
- **a_wedged_engine_is_never_written.** how(1,1,0,0,1) is VCR_MC_SKIP, never CPU.
- **Every listed mode.** For every vcr_timings[] entry × {8,16,32} that vcr_mode_check accepts, at 64 MB and 32 MB per chip:
  - vcr_desktop_offset gives an offset for which vcr_modeclear_one_fill is 1;
  - the cleared range lies inside VRAM;
  - the cursor page [off-0x1000, off) lies outside it;
  - it starts at or above Glide's reserved 0x118000.
- **Refusals.** Stride 0x4000 or an unaligned offset gives 0, so the CPU path is used, never a partial engine fill.
- **the_stale_desktop_avp_and_ut2004_saw (old-buggy vs fixed).** From the 1280x1024x32 desktop at 0x3b00000:
  - AvP's 640x480x16 primary [0x3f6a000,0x4000000) is 614,400 B of old rows 904-1023, so 307,200 pixels are stale without the clear;
  - UT2004's 1280x960x16 [0x3da8000,0x4000000) is 2,457,600 B of rows 544-1023, so 1,228,800 pixels are stale;
  - with the clear (cleared range == new primary) both are 0.

**tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_modeclear.py** (new, the wiring):
- In DrvEnableSurface, VcrDd2dInit(pd); comes before VcrDd2dClearPrimary(pd);, which comes before return hs;.
- The clear appears in neither DrvAssertMode nor vcrdd_escape.c.
- Its first statement returns on !pd->mode_clear, before any VcrDd2dFill, VcrDd2dSync, memset or VcrDd. This pins the old path.
- The fill is VcrDd2dFill(pd, off, pd->lDelta, bpp, 0, 0, cx, cy, 0) followed by VcrDd2dSync. memset appears only under VCR_MC_CPU.
- VcrDd2dInit zeroes mode_clear before IOCTL_VCR_INFO and sets it only from VCR_INFO_F_MODECLEAR.
- fill_info contains (VcrDiagGet(L"ModeClear", 0) ? VCR_INFO_F_MODECLEAR : 0).
- SET_CURRENT_MODE still masks VIDEO_MODE_NO_ZERO_MEMORY, and VcrHwSetMode/voodoo_program gain no frame-buffer write.

G39.on_box_verification:
**Off silicon first:**
1. Run `bash tests/run_all.sh`, build, and run check_imports.py on vcrmp.sys and vcrdd.dll. There should be no new imports: memset and EngQueryPerformanceCounter are already used.
2. On the 86Box Voodoo3 bed (port 19920; 86Box clears nothing, so it reproduces the defect), run `d3dprobe modeclear` at 640x480x16 with the switch absent (expect FAIL) and then armed (expect 0). Check the ddlab flip front field the same way. Then run the bed's usual gdilab, ddlab and d3dprobe render.
3. On the QEMU bed (CPU branch), boot once armed: the ring shows 512/12 how=2 and the desktop comes up. QEMU clears VRAM itself, so this only proves the code runs.

**Silicon (.124): one supervised clean boot.** Conditions:

- A person watches the CRT.
- Pace switches at least 5 s apart (d3dprobe_paced.py, --pace 5000).
- Run vcrctl only at the desktop.
- Dismiss the screensaver first.
- Run no Glide/OpenGL before the D3D steps (G01 confound).

Steps:

2. Run `modeclear` at 640x480x16 with the switch absent. Expect FAIL with nonblack ≈ 307,200: the silicon old-path reference. If it passes, the D3D8 runtime clears the front buffer itself, and the ddlab front field becomes the discriminating check.
3. Arm ModeClear=1 (REGWRITE, then REGREAD back). This is the boot's one Diag change.
4. Run `modeclear` at 640x480x16, 1280x960x16 and 1024x768x32. Expect PASS (0 and 0). The ring should show 512/12 how=1 at every switch with its µs, and no 512/9.
5. Run the regression set and expect the 11-12 counts:

6. Make three paced desktop mode changes. Each time the desktop must repaint fully and the hardware cursor must stay visible.
7. Launch the UT2004 botmatch (staged, 1280x960x16). Its 45 s GDI frame must be black or game content, not the doubled-icon desktop of ONBOX/games/UT2004_botmatch/UT2004_botmatch_045s.png.
8. Run AvP (640x480x16) with frames at 30/60 s. They must be black if it still stalls (G71) or its own picture, never the garbled desktop.
9. Last, one Quake II run on our ICD + Glide (4-chip SLI). It must render and return to the desktop, with 512/12 before HWCSETEXCLUSIVE and at the return, and no give-up.

G39.risk:
Off, there is none: the function returns before anything, and DrvEnableSurface is byte-for-byte today's. Armed, the risk is very low:
- **Default 16 bpp D3D path.** Only DrvEnableSurface changes, before any D3D context exists on the PDEV. The HAL code, caps, DP2, Clear2, textures and flips are untouched.
- **Glide/OpenGL coexistence.** The fill is chip 0 only, through the PCI FIFO. It covers only the top-of-memory primary, never Glide's command-FIFO window, so a stale cmdFifo0 (G01) is not touched. It is waited for before DrvEnableSurface returns, and GETLINEARADDR and HWCSETEXCLUSIVE sync again. It never runs at DrvAssertMode, RESTORE_MODE or HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE, so no live, alt-tabbed or killed Glide stream is written under. A Glide switch-in pays a few ms.
- **SLI.** It runs after the mode set's VcrSliOff, and SLI is enabled only by Glide after HWCSETEXCLUSIVE.
- **Flip path.** The fill completes before DirectDraw is enabled on the PDEV, and the scan-out offset is the primary it clears.
- **Boot.** It is a bounded fill and sync: at worst a give-up (acceleration off, logged), never a hang. BootAttempts and Diag\Disable still cover the boot.
- **Cursor.** Its page lies one page under the desktop, outside the range, and the native test pins that.
- **Wedged chip.** SKIP writes nothing.
- **Timing.** About 2-8 ms per mode change (inferred); G11's refused CreateDevice pays it twice.
- **Measurement (intended).** Titles that never present give black sweep frames instead of plausible garbage, so AvP's baseline changes. Do not read that as a regression.

open_questions: Does XP's D3D8 runtime clear the front buffer itself at CreateDevice? UT2004's 45 s frame says no, but only if UT2004 had created its device by then. The first silicon run with the switch absent settles it; if the runtime does clear, the ddlab flip front field becomes the discriminating check.
How long does the VSA-100 2D engine take to fill a 1280x1024x32 primary? The estimate of 2-8 ms assumes about 1 pixel per clock (inferred). The 512/12 event measures it.

Should DrvAssertMode(TRUE) and Glide's release also clear, as 3dfx's bAssertModeHardware does? Not without evidence of a defect there: GDI repaints on both paths, and DrvAssertMode(TRUE) is where an alt-tabbed Glide game resumes its stream. If it is ever wanted, it should be a second value of the switch, default off.

Should the DirectDraw heap also be cleared, like the vendor's cxMemory x cyMemory fill? Only if a title is seen flipping an undrawn back buffer. It would cost several fills, run over Glide's FIFO window, and take about 10x longer.

Which VCR_INFO_F_* bit? 0x8000 is free today but is proposed by eight sibling designs (G01, G04-G09, G16). The integrator assigns it, and the tests pin the name. It belongs in flags, not in a D3D feature word.
DOSBox output=ddraw (Descent 1/2, G62): its unused borders should turn black instead of stale. That is unrelated to G62's failing setup call, but the frames will change.
When does the default move to ON? After the supervised boot passes, by the user's decision.

G37.approach:
REAL and fixable; three holes plus one hazard the fix must avoid, all verified by reading the code. Full design: KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G37.md.

The four problems:
- (1) A handled Dd_Blt into a video-memory texture is never marked dirty. This covers the 2D-engine copy and fill, clipped_blt, and Dd_Blt's own CPU memset/memmove fallbacks (vcrdd_ddraw.c:510-520, 546-557), which write video memory with no Unlock.
- (2) Rendering into a texture is never marked: triangles, DP2 CLEAR and Clear2 fastfills into a TEXTURE|3DDEVICE target.
- (3) NEW, dirty while not bound. prepare() checks dirty flags only when the global g_tex_writes moved, and only for the textures bound at that moment (vcrdd_d3d.c:1327-1335). Untextured draws write no TMU register (vcrdd_3d.c:113-130), so TMU0 keeps the old base. A texture written while unbound and then rebound writes the SAME texBaseAddr, which does not flush. SPEC 20.3 L6187 says the flush is "by changing the value of texBaseAddr", and Glide's gtexdl.c:1650-1662 says "legal to source once and download over and over". This hole also affects today's CPU writers (TEXBLT, Unlock).
- (4) Hazard. VcrDd3dTexFlush's texture-port write-back reads texel 0 with the CPU and does not wait for the engine (vcrdd_3d.c:263-267). Once engine writes are marked, that read could fetch the pre-write dword and write it back over the new texels.

Why only the cache needs fixing: miscInit1 bits 16/17 (default 0, SPEC L5836-5837) make 3D wait for pending 2D and the reverse, so memory ordering is the hardware's job. Only the TMU cache needs software.

What 3dfx did: it flushed both TMUs at every texture-state send (D6DP2.C:6709-6714, 6762-6767), and SetRenderTarget forced a full re-send (D7DP2.C:138). A 2D Blt only set BltToTxtrInFifo for the Lock drain (DDBLT32.C:444-450, DDSURF.C:1612-1620).

Why we do not copy that rule: on our PIO transport it would add about 14 uncached writes per state send (G47/G48/G53), and the TMU would refetch every texel after each flush. It stays only as a debug bit.

86Box: its decoded cache is invalidated only by texture-port, CMDFIFO packet-5 and agpMove writes (voodoo_texture.c:641-651). So the old path fails deterministically on the bed, and the one-dword port write-back is what makes the fix visible there.

THE FIX:
(a) New VcrDdD3dTexEngineWritten(pd, s, who):
- returns at once for anything that is not a video-memory texture, so the back buffer, primary and flip chain never reach the rest;
- always counts;
- when armed, sets SF_DIRTY|SF_ENGINE (new surface flag 0x10) and bumps g_tex_writes.
It is called at four places:
- before pd->dd_blts++ in clipped_blt (ddraw.c:463) and Dd_Blt (:562), the only two HANDLED+DD_OK exits; the flip-pending WASSTILLDRAWING exit is not marked;
- at SETRENDERTARGET for the OLD target when it changes (d3d.c:1735, before c->rt = rt), so a mark lands inside the same DP2 walk;
- for the current target at the end of D3d_DrawPrimitives2 (after walk, :1867) and of D3d_Clear2. This covers multi-context rendering and DX7 devices created on a texture.

(b) flush_written ORs SF_DIRTY|SF_ENGINE over the levels and clears both. When vcr_texcoh_plan(fl, !no_texport && addr != ~0) returns SYNC, it calls VcrDd2dSync before the unchanged VcrDd3dTexFlush, so the engine's write lands before the CPU read-back. There is no sync on the VSA-100 path where no write-back happens: 32-bit, DXT, TBIG or above 16 MB. There, the flip plus the flush's own 2D-NOP pixel flush (SPEC rule 1) is enough.

(c) Dirty-at-bind. In prepare's state-send path, after compute_regs and before VcrDd3dState, when armed, flush_written runs on tex_surf0/1. It costs only a level walk when nothing is dirty. The counter path at :1327 is unchanged.

(d) Always-on observation with no hardware access: g_tex_blt2d and per-context rt_away, appended to the existing "context gone" INFO text (no tool parses it). Armed only: a rate-limited event 513/30 (provisional), the first 16 per boot.

(e) New Win32-free include/vcr_texcoh.h with vcr_texcoh_mark(who, vidmem_texture, armed) and vcr_texcoh_plan(levels_or, writeback_reads). Compile-time checks pin SF_DIRTY == VCR_TC_DIRTY and SF_ENGINE == VCR_TC_ENGINE.

What does not change:
- Caps: none. Single pass. No new register field.
- Unarmed: no flag set, no counter move, no dirty-at-bind, no sync. The flush runs for exactly today's textures at today's points; only the context-gone log text gains two numbers.

Optional debug bit TEXFLUSHALL (3dfx's rule): a base flip with no write-back (VcrDd3dTexFlush(base, ~0)) at every state send, for each textured TMU. It is silicon-only and never graduates. It validates TEXCOH and gives G06/G17/G18 a one-boot cache-staleness A/B.

G37.gating:
Switch: Diag\D3DFeat bit 5 (0x20, VCR_D3DFEAT_TEXCOH). This follows hal.md §10's Phase 2 numbering: bits 0-4 are G15/G08/G22/G25/G16, and G21 took the alignment half onto D3DTexPlace, so bit 5 is free. The plan owner fixes the number in include/vcr_d3dfeat.h.
- Default OFF: a positive flag, absent = off, read at boot through the shared vcr_info.d3dfeat word.
- NOT napalm-gated: the cache rule is the same on Banshee, Voodoo3 and VSA-100, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed can prove it first.
- With the bit off, the proven path is unchanged in register traffic, allocation and flush points. The only difference is two counters appended to the existing context-gone log text.
- Arming: REGWRITE HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vcrmp\Diag D3DFeat REG_DWORD 32 (ORed into existing bits). Read it back with REGREAD on the KEY. Then the activation check and safe-reboot.py. One Diag change per clean boot.

Safe to land default-on? Not on day one, but it is the strongest graduation candidate in Phase 2:
- for: it is a pure correctness fix that reuses the flush sequence running on .124 since 09-26, at new trigger points, and changes no caps;
- against: the only new silicon action is a status-read VcrDd2dSync inside the DP2 walk, before an engine-written texture's write-back.
- Graduation: flip the default in its own commit with its test after supervised boot B passes, using the plan's shared D3DFeat convention (a default mask or a D3DFeatOff kill mask). TEXCOH then becomes a kill switch.
- The debug bit TEXFLUSHALL (provisionally bit 31) is diagnosis only. It is never combined with another change and never graduates.
G37.d3dprobe_test:
New explicit tests in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c, not in the default list until graduation.

Shared rules:
- Textures are 16x16 R5G6B5, small enough to fit the TMU cache whole (inferred).
- The quad covers [32,224), so each texel is 12 px. Sampling is SELECTARG1 TEXTURE, POINT/POINT/NONE, CLAMP.
- Probe texels: all of row 0 (texels 0..7 at y = 38, x = 38..122), because the flush's write-back lands at texel (fpVidMem&15)/2 of row 0; plus (8,7) and (14,14).
- References: red 0xf800 -> 0xff0000, green 0x07e0 -> 0x00ff00, ±12 per channel.
- Round 1 is the cold read. A texel wrong there is reported 'placement' (G21/G36) and excluded from the verdict.
- Round 3 is ground truth: CopyRects of the tested texture into a fresh, never-sampled DEFAULT texture F, sampled cold.
- Verdict per texel:
  - ok: round 2 = round 3 = green;
  - stale: round 2 red, round 3 green. This is G37.
  - stale_wb: only row-0 texels stale. The write-back raced the engine, so the sync is missing.
  - premise: round 3 not green.

The tests:
- blt2tex (hole 1): D, a DEFAULT texture filled red by UpdateTexture. S, a 16x16 R5G6B5 CreateRenderTarget SURFACE cleared green. A surface source cannot travel as TEXBLT, only as DdBlt. R1: sample D -> red. R2: CopyRects(S -> D level 0), which is Dd_Blt on the 2D engine, then the same quad with D still set and no SetTexture call -> must be green.
- rtt_clear (hole 2): T, a 16x16 R5G6B5 D3DUSAGE_RENDERTARGET texture (SKIPPED if CheckDeviceFormat or CreateTexture refuses). R1: SetRenderTarget(T0, NULL), Clear red, back to BB/ZS, sample -> red; otherwise verdict 'rtt_base' and stop. R2: with T still set, Clear green into T (3D fastfill), back, sample -> green.
- rtt_draw (holes 2+3): like rtt_clear, but R2 draws an untextured green quad into T. After switching back it draws an untextured blue quad on the back buffer at (0,0)-(24,24) BEFORE SetTexture(0,T). That draw consumes the write counter with nothing bound, so the sample needs dirty-at-bind -> must be green.
- texblt_unbound (hole 3, CPU writer). In one scene:
  1. SetTexture(0, NULL);
  2. untextured quad;
  3. UpdateTexture(green sysmem -> D), a TEXBLT that is already marked today;
  4. untextured quad;
  5. SetTexture(0, D);
  6. sample -> green.
- rtt_clear8888 (silicon with D3DBigTex bit 2): rtt_clear with an A8R8G8B8 render-target texture at 32 bpp. This is the flush with no write-back and no sync.

Pass criterion: every judged texel 'ok'.

The old-path reference is part of the evidence. With the bit off on the 86Box bed, all four portable tests must FAIL 'stale', deterministically. If blt2tex passes unarmed there, CopyRects did not reach Dd_Blt: a probe premise failure, not a G37 result.

- No vcrctl or ExtEscape tool while a D3D program runs; read the ring after the probe exits.

- 0. 86Box Voodoo3 bed, new vcrdd.dll, D3DFeat absent: d3dprobe render --full --res 640x480 --bpp 16 --tests blt2tex,rtt_clear,rtt_draw,texblt_unbound. All must FAIL 'stale' (rtt_* SKIPPED if the runtime grants 121a:0005 no R5G6B5 render-target texture); the default list passes as before.

  - The default lists must be unchanged and perf within ±1% of A.

  - First read the always-on counters (rt_away, g_tex_blt2d in the context-gone lines) from an unarmed boot-A session of every staged D3D title.
  - Then compare A/B frames only for titles whose counters move. Likely candidates: Thief II NewDark D3D9 with d3d_disp_enable_distortionfx (a water/distortion scene at 1280x960x32 fullscreen) and Max Payne bullet-time (supervised only, G04).

Max Payne - DRV_setRenderTarget / bullet-time effects (inferred; supervised only, G04)
UT2003 / UT2004 - UE2 render-target and scripted textures (inferred)
DX6/DX7 titles that DirectDraw-Blt a video-memory surface into a texture, or update a texture during untextured draws (unmeasured; the always-on counters name them)
open_questions: Does writing the SAME texBaseAddr value flush the VSA-100 texture cache? SPEC says 'changing' and Glide implies not; boot A measures it. If it does, today's per-DP2 state re-send masks holes 1-3 on silicon until G53's shadowing removes those writes, so G37 should land before G53.

Does D3D8 CopyRects from a render-target SURFACE into a DEFAULT texture reach DdBlt (the 2D engine)? It should, because TEXBLT cannot carry a non-texture source (inferred). The bed's unarmed blt2tex FAIL and the armed 513/30 who=1 line confirm the route.

Is the texture-port write-back, and therefore the sync, needed on silicon at all? It exists for 86Box's cache. Dropping it for engine-written textures on the VSA-100 would save the drain but make the bed and silicon run different code. That is for G46/G47 to decide with measurements.

G41.approach:
VERDICT. The defect is real in the code, but the gap's headline trigger cannot happen with our stack.

The defect:
- pd->fog_valid/fog_loaded (vcrdd.h:78-79) are reset only because the PDEV is allocated zeroed (vcrdd.c:397).
- VcrDd3dState (vcrdd_3d.c:86-101) skips the 32-register load whenever the key matches.
- No event ever clears the cache.

Why the trigger is unreachable:
- XP builds a new PDEV at every mode change and frees the old one within about 60 ms: ring_start_decoded.txt lines 49-99. Across all evidence: 38 DrvEnablePDEV, 37 DrvDisablePDEV, and 93/93 DrvAssertMode calls with bEnable=FALSE.
- Our Glide always changes the mode, even at the desktop's resolution: 3dfx's 'DDraw communication hack' asks for 8 bpp then (glide3x/h5/minihwc/win_mode.c:200,220-234), and vcr-kmd lists 8 bpp modes.
- So every Glide/OpenGL session runs on a PDEV of its own (ring lines 316-369 and 914-964), and the PDEV D3D uses afterwards is new.
- The table can only be reloaded by a drawable DP2 (prepare() is the only VcrDd3dState caller, vcrdd_d3d.c:1361, and it requires !exclusive_pid).

What is reachable:
- Today: lab escapes (vcrctl reset-engine, reg pokes) on a live desktop PDEV.
- Re-asserted PDEVs (fast user switching, full-screen console): never recorded.
- Tomorrow: G01/G02 same-PDEV engine resets.
- Latent: a load cut off by a FIFO give-up leaves fog_valid=1 with the OLD key over a half-written table. G02's same-PDEV recovery makes that reachable.
- Not a G18 (UE2 white sky) candidate.

DESIGN. CPU-only. Caps, register fields and register values are unchanged, single pass.

- vcr_fogc_need(c, fog_on, key): fog off never loads; a new key reloads.
- vcr_fogc_begin(c): valid=0, called BEFORE the first fogTable write.
- vcr_fogc_done(c, key): key, valid=1, loads++, called after the 32nd write.
- vcr_fogc_forget(c, why).
- Reasons: GLIDE_MAP, GLIDE_OWN, GLIDE_RLS, GLIDE_UNMAP, ASSERT_OFF, ASSERT_ON, ENG_RESET, REG_POKE.

VCR_PDEV and vcr3d_regs:
- vcr_fogcache fogc replaces the two fields.
- Add ULONG serial (a per-session ++g_pdev_serial in DrvEnablePDEV).
- vcr3d_regs.fog_table becomes vcr_u32[4] (same width on ILP32).
- vcrdd.h gets static inline VcrDdFogForget(pd, why). It logs 513 what 40 at DEBUG, only when a VALID table is dropped.

VcrDd3dState rewrite:
- vcr_fogc_need(&pd->fogc, r->fogMode & FM_ENABLE, r->fog_table), then begin, the same 32 writes `(e1<<24)|(d1<<16)|(e0<<8)|d0` to fogTable 0x160-0x1dc with the same VcrDdRoom(8) waits, then done.
- The chip sees the identical write stream; only the moment the CPU flag changes moves.

Forget points (vendor rule VH5/HWCEXT.C:1302-1310: Glide executing => SC_FOGALL dirty; also D6DP2.C:6372-6377, DDSLIBLT.C:2125-2130, DDFXNT.C:2445-2449/2496-2501):
1. hwc() GETLINEARADDR on success.
2. HWCSETEXCLUSIVE, after exclusive_pid=pid. This alone covers every Glide session, including killed ones.
3. HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE, after the non-owner refusal block (left textually unchanged) and before IOCTL_VCR_RESTORE_MODE.
4. UNMAP_MEMORY.
5. DrvAssertMode, as the first statement, for both directions.
6. DrvEscape VCR_ESC_RESET_ENGINE, always.
7. VCR_ESC_REG, on an accepted MMIO32 write (flags read before the IOCTL).
- G01/G02 call VcrDdFogForget(pd, VCR_FOGC_ENG_RESET) instead of writing pd->fog_valid=0.
- G51 must forget at SLI entry/exit and broadcast the load.

Instrumentation:
- 513 what 41 PDEV summary at DrvDisableSurface.
- VCR_ESC_DD_STATS answers slots 4-7 (serial, loads, forgets, last_why) to callers asking for 32 bytes. The 16-byte answer and its pinned text are unchanged.
- vcrctl info adds a second 32-byte query.

OLD PATH. On every flow recorded on .124 the register writes are byte-for-byte identical:
- every forget there hits an already-invalid cache (a Glide PDEV) or a PDEV about to be freed;
- a forget can at worst add one 32-write load, the same one the first fogged draw of every new PDEV makes.

RECOMMENDATION. Land default-on in G01's or G03's commit, P3.

New explicit tests 'fogcache' (vertex fog, the constant RAMP key) and 'fogcache_table' (LINEAR start 1 / end 5). Not in the default list, because each costs one paced same-mode switch.

Helper: a new 'vcrctl fogpoison' command (tools/vcrctl.c), reusing hwc_open/hwc()/hwc_close and the pace gate as 'sliaa off' does. It does exactly what a fogging Glide client does to the chip:

Each test:
1. Pass 1 draws an unfogged red control strip (x16-240, y208-240) and fogvertex's three quads, red fogged toward blue (FOGCOLOR 0xff0000ff); it reads back and checks with expect().

4. Treats as SKIPPED (inconclusive, which fails an explicit --tests run): a missing or failed helper, TestCooperativeLevel != D3D_OK (the PDEV changed), or a changed stats serial.
5. Pass 2 repeats the same draws, so the same key is the first fogged draw after the poison. A control strip that is not red (±12) skips the fog checks as 'D3D not drawing after the HWC session (G01/G03), not a fog-cache verdict'.

| 'no fog' | 0xff0000 ±12 | 0x0000ff |
| 'half fog' | 0x80007f ±40 | 0x0000ff |
| 'all fog' | 0x0000ff ±12 | 0x0000ff (cannot discriminate) |
| control | 0xff0000 ±12 | 0xff0000 |

G36.approach:
The gap has two halves, and they have different answers. Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G36.md.

(1) Render-to-texture on our HAL is real, untested and fixable. Two defects are verified by reading the code.
- PLACEMENT. A render-target texture (TEXTURE|3DDEVICE) is excluded from mipchain_ext (vcrdd_d3d.c:389-391), so dxg's linear heap places it on a 4-byte boundary. colBufferAddr and texBaseAddr both drop address bits 3:0, and target_of checks only the pitch.
  - The engine then renders up to 12 bytes into the surface in front of it. The TMU samples from the same truncated base, so the round trip looks right, while the CPU and 2D blitter see the image shifted.
  - The fix is G21's Diag\D3DTexPlace bit 1 (16-byte start, pitch = w x bytes). No new code here; G36 supplies the proof.
- COHERENCY. Rendering never marks a texture written, so the TMU cache can serve stale texels (SPEC 20.3). Two traps in the existing flush:
  - Its texture-port write-back re-writes the first dword from a CPU LFB read, which is not ordered after the queued rendering. A naive mark would therefore corrupt texels (0,0) and (1,0).
  - prepare() only flushes when the global write counter moves, so a dirty texture bound later with an unchanged texBaseAddr is never flushed. This hole affects CPU uploads too.
- Part B (G37's 3D half, specified here; behind G37's switch or Diag\D3DRtt bit 0, default off):
  - Pure header vcr_rtt.h (mark / writeback / needs_idle).
  - SF_RT3D flag. rt_leave() marks the old target when SETRENDERTARGET switches away from a texture that was drawn or cleared, and in ctx_free.
  - flush_written passes ~0 (no port write-back) for 3D-written textures on a VSA-100, and idles then keeps the write-back on a Banshee/Voodoo3 (the 86Box bed).
  - Flush-on-bind after compute_regs. A one-WARN feedback watch.
- Part 0 (log-only, default on): a census of render-target textures — one INFO line per creation in name_surface (size, format, off-grid, pitch), the first 8 texture targets per context, and a context-end summary that survives the ring wrap.

(2) Halo cannot get its render targets from any fix inside the DX7 DDI. This is verified statically from halo.exe 1.10 (md5 b7aa8f68).
- The creation function 0x52ca20 creates 8 render-target textures and raises FATAL 105 (Strings.dll: 'video driver is known to have serious issues') at the first CreateTexture failure (0x52cb57).
- Five of them are X8R8G8B8 (128x128 x3, 64x64 x2). Two are A8R8G8B8 at back-buffer size and half size, i.e. 1280x960 non-pow2 on .124, unless alpha render targets are off.
- XP's d3d9.dll (verified: table entry 121a:0009 = 0x4580 at file 0x1410; per-format flag tests at 0x4fdfbe19; CheckDeviceFormat's single-entry op lookup at 0x4fdf8c22) never grants a DX7 driver an X8R8G8B8 render-target texture. Only ForceDriverFlagsOff exists.
- So the plan's step 3 (retry Halo without DisableRenderTargets) reproduces FATAL 105 whatever the HAL does. Do not spend a supervised boot on it.
- Routes: G94 (DX8-level DDI with its own format ops), or a Halo-local d3d9.dll shim mapping X8R8G8B8 render targets to A8R8G8B8 on 121a:0009 only. Either needs DisableAlphaRenderTargets staged in place of DisableRenderTargets. This is the user's decision.

Part C (tools):
- d3dprobe rtt* tests and caps 'rtformats'.
- A new d3d9probe (LoadLibrary, no -ld3d9) with caps9, halort9 (Halo's exact slot table replayed windowed with a 1280x960 back buffer, so no mode switch) and rtt9.
- An optional game-local d3d9/d3d8 'spy' only if the census needs it.

No caps change in any part. With every switch off, the driver is byte-for-byte today's apart from the Part 0 log lines.

G34.approach:
The gap is real, and every format except A8 is fixable in one pass. However, no staged .124 title is measured to need any format left in G34, so it is P3. The one format a staged title is shown to miss is X8R8G8B8, which is owned by G17 (D3DBigTex bit 3).

EVIDENCE (read this session)
(a) Halo needs none of G34's remaining formats. halo.exe's bitmap->D3DFORMAT table (VA 0x65e040) maps a8/y8/ay8/a8y8/p8-bump to -1, i.e. no texture on any card. A tag-index scan of all 30 Halo maps finds 0 monochrome bitmaps, 2 p8-bump and 1,419 2D x8r8g8b8 bitmaps (lens flares, sky stars, rasterizer default 2d, bump maps). This refutes the A8/Y8 reading in games.md/runtime.md.
(b) UE2's D3DDrv calls CheckDeviceFormat only for DXT1/3/5, A8R8G8B8 and R5G6B5.
(c) Max Payne and Thief II load through D3DX "closest format" helpers, so offering more formats changes their choices rather than fixing anything.
(d) H&D's LS3D has its own converter for every D3D8 format: a candidate consumer and a candidate regression.
(e) Shogo picks its 8-bit format only with DDPF_PALETTEINDEXED8 (P8 = G38). AvP takes the first enumerated format with enough colour depth.
(f) The XP d3d8/d3d9 converter (d3d8 0x6d9b6850, d3d9 0x4fe05d7f) compares dwFlags for EQUALITY and checks exact masks:
  - L8 = 0x20000/8/L ff -> 50
  - A4L4 = 0x20001/8/L 0f A f0 -> 52
  - A8L8 = 0x20001/16/L ff A ff00 -> 51
  - R3G3B2 = 0x40/8/e0,1c,03 -> 27
  - A8R3G3B2 = 0x41/16/A ff00 -> 29
  - X1R5G5B5 = 0x40/16/7c00 -> 24
  - X4R4G4B4 = 0x40/16/f00 -> 30
  - DDPF_ALPHA has no case and is dropped.
  The op builder appends display-mode entries separately, and its lookup (0x6d9ac790) needs both the format and the op bits, so texture-only entries cannot trip its validation.
(g) TMU formats (SPEC 8.76; h3defs): RGB332=0, I8=3 (alpha 0xff, i.e. D3D L8), AI44=4, ARGB8332=8, AI88=13.
  - AI88 is alpha-high: MesaFX packs AL88 as (a<<8)|l for Glide's AI88.
  - The AI44 nibble order is inferred (alpha high); a probe settles it.
  - Glide's offsets are texel-exact and 8-bit rows are w bytes, including 1-wide levels (xtexdl_def.c).

DESIGN
1. A new switch, Diag\D3DTexFmt (bits: 0 = X1R5G5B5+X4R4G4B4, 1 = A8L8, 2 = L8+A4L4, 3 = A8R3G3B2+R3G3B2). It is read once at boot, VSA-100 only, and honoured only with the D3DBigTex texture path (tex_ext).
   - NOT new D3DBigTex bits: the Thief II launcher tests D3DBigTex with findstr "0x[57df]$", which fails for any value >= 0x10 and would silently drop that title to DX6 at 640x480.
   - Transport: an appended vcr_info.d3d_texfmt field, the same pattern as G05's d3dfeat. VcrDd2dInit must memset info before the IOCTL.
2. Formats are appended to the DX7 list through G17's vcr_texfmt_list, never reordered: ... X8R8G8B8 (G17) | X1555, X4444 | A8L8 | L8, A4L4 | A8R332, R332.
   - g_texfmt grows to 17. There is a texfmt_lum helper, and 8-bit RGB332 needs dwRGBBitCount 8.
   - No cap bits change. The list stays mode-independent.
3. Classification in G17's vcr_texfmt_classify (equality on dwFlags) gives kind, tmfmt and alpha_one. Unarmed, every result is today's.
   - It adds vcr_texfmt_has_alpha (for G08) and vcr_texfmt_port_ok.
   - New TF codes go in vcr_3dregs.h.
4. The X formats reuse G17's alpha_one: TMU TCA = TM_TCA_ONE 0x24000000 instead of TM_TCA_REPLACE 0x08200000, and vcr_tca_alpha_one handles stage 1.
5. A new storage kind, VCR_TEXK_B8, in vcr_texlod (level bytes w*h, pitch w, NAPALM only, TBIG unchanged), plus a vcr_tex_row_bytes helper replacing two ternaries in mipchain_ext.
6. TexBaseAddr phase. The TMU drops bits 3:0, so an 8-bit 1x1 top must sit 4 bytes past a 16-byte boundary, and a 2x1 or 1x2 top 8 bytes (345-shape check; G21 covers only RGB16 1x1 = 8).
   - Use G21's vcr_tex_chain_pad, but store the pad as a 4-bit count (SF_PAD, bits 11:8) rather than G21's SF_PAD8, and have VcrDdD3dFreeMipChain subtract it.
   - Without G21, apply the pad to B8 only.
7. TEXBLT needs no change (luminance bit count is the same union field).
   - flush_written keeps the texture-port write-back only for formats 10/11/12.
   - Dd_Blt: while tex_fmt is armed, a texture whose own bit count differs from the desktop's goes to the HEL. surf_bytespp otherwise uses the desktop depth when HASPIXELFORMAT is clear, which would overrun an L8 texture 2-4x.
8. Phase 0 (log only, default on): 513/41 logs the first texture of each format per process; 513/42 logs texture formats CanCreateSurface sees that the HAL cannot sample. This measures DX5-7 demand and who switches after arming.
9. A8 is not offered: D3D8/9 cannot see it, no title needs it, and the TMU returns RGB = a. 3dfx's own DX7 A8 (DDPF_ALPHA) fell through to its 565 default. The only route is G94 with the TMU's RGB zeroed (SST_TC_ZERO).

SEQUENCE: Phase 0 now; bits 0-1 after G17 (cheap); bit 2 only for a measured consumer or for parity; bit 3 only for a measured consumer.

G34.gating:
The new switch is Diag\D3DTexFmt (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vcrmp\Diag), DWORD. Absent = 0 = off.
- Bit 0: X1R5G5B5 + X4R4G4B4.
- Bit 1: A8L8.
- Bit 2: L8 + A4L4.
- Bit 3: A8R3G3B2 + R3G3B2.

How it is read and honoured:
- Read once at boot in FindAdapter, beside D3DBigTex: the list must be identical at the desktop and the fullscreen PDEV.
- Masked & 0xf, and 0 on anything but a VSA-100.
- Honoured only when the VSA-100 texture path is on (pd->tex_ext, i.e. any D3DBigTex bit; G20 makes D3DBigTex=7 the default and stays below bit 3).
- It deliberately does not extend D3DBigTex: the staged Thief II launcher's findstr "0x[57df]$" treats any D3DBigTex value >= 0x10 as off and falls back to DX6 at 640x480.

Off-state guarantees:
- With the switch absent, the texture list, classification, registers and placement are byte-for-byte today's, pinned by the native list test.
- The Blt guard is inactive.
- The default path (no D3DBigTex) is never touched.

Arming:
- One bit per supervised clean boot: activation check, REGWRITE plus read-back, then safe-reboot.py.

Not safe to land default-on:
- Offering a format changes what H&D (LS3D), Max Payne and Thief II (D3DX) and DX5/6 enumerators may choose.
- B8 storage, AI44 and AI88 have never run on this silicon.
- Even once proven, the bits stay opt-in unless a consumer is measured.
- Bit 3 (the quality-reducing 3-3-2 pair) is not to be armed without a measured consumer.

Safe to land default-on now:
- the Phase-0 log events (no register traffic, not on the drawing path);
- the new d3dprobe tests and caps rows (explicit-only);
- the refactors: vcr_tex_row_bytes, the vcr_info memset, and the SF_PAD count (pads written only for B8 or under G21's bit).
G34.d3dprobe_test:
Caps mode: add rows texX1555, texX4444, texA8L8, texL8, texA4L4, texA8R332, texR332 and texA8 to d3dprobe.c fm[] (G17 adds texX8888). Expected:
- switch absent: all new rows 0, everything else equal to caps_124.txt;
- each armed bit turns on exactly its rows;
- texA8 is 0 in every boot, which documents the DX7-DDI limit.

Render tests (group @texfmt). Each runs at --full 640x480x16, --full 1024x768x32 and windowed on the 32 bpp desktop. Each FAILS when named but skipped ("format not offered", rule 2991448), which is the old value.

Decode tests: generalise test_dxt_decode's raw-565 mode. Fill a DXD x DXD texture with LCG-random texels and draw one texel a pixel (point, MIPFILTER NONE). Pass 0 is RGB via SELECTARG1(TEXTURE); pass 1 is alpha as white diffuse x texture alpha, blended SRCALPHA/ZERO onto black. Every texel is compared within +/-12. PASS = 0 wrong in both passes.
- x1555_decode1: RGB is 5->8 replication; pass 1 must be ALL white. The old/unforced value is about half black.
- x4444_decode1: RGB is 4->8; all white.
- a8l8_decode1: RGB (lo,lo,lo), alpha = high byte. A byte swap fails.
- l8_decode1: RGB (L,L,L), all white.
- a4l4_decode1: RGB lo nibble x17, alpha hi nibble x17. A nibble swap fails, which settles the AI44 order.
- a8r332_decode1 and r332_decode1: RGB {r,r,r[2:1]}, {g,g,g[2:1]}, b x 0x55; alpha is the high byte, or white.

l8_phase:
- Three instances, each: k spacer 4x4 L8, a 4x4 L8 poison (0x00), a 1x1 L8 0xC0 and a 2x1 L8 (0x40, 0xC0), sampled by 32x32 quads (point, WRAP).
- Expected: c0c0c0 at the 1x1's centre, 404040 / c0c0c0 at the 2x1's halves.
- Without the 4/8-byte phase pad the TMU reads the poison (000000): FAIL.

mipl8 and mipa8l8: a 64x64 full chain with a distinct grey per level, drawn at 192/32/16 px with point mips, expecting levels 0/1/2 as the existing mip test does. Only levels down to 4x4 are asserted until G07.

l8_2048_decode: a 2048x2048 L8 texture, decode window at the far corner (TBIG + 8-bit + 26-bit base).

l8_upd and l8_copy: cells_copied with an L8 grey checker, via UpdateTexture (DP2 TEXBLT at 1 byte a texel) and via CopyRects (DdBlt), expecting the checker greys. l8_copy at 32 bpp proves the Blt HEL guard: without it the 2D engine copies 4 bytes a texel.

G34.on_box_verification:
On .124, supervised, one Diag change per clean boot.

Preconditions:
- G17's plumbing is in the build, and G01's FIFO reset;
- activation check, then deploy (vcrdd.dll + vcrmp.sys) and safe-reboot.py;
- no vcrctl/ExtEscape while a D3D title runs;
- probe mode switches paced >= 5 s;
- Max Payne only with a person watching (G04).

Boot A: new DLL and miniport, D3DTexFmt absent (D3D32=1, D3DBigTex=7).
- Probes: d3dprobe caps must equal caps_124.txt plus all-zero new rows. The default render list must score 40/40 at 640x480x16, 40/40 at 1024x768x32 and 42/42 windowed. @bigtex must be unchanged, and @texfmt must FAIL as skipped (the old value).
- Attended titles: Halo menu + -timedemo, UT2004 menu, Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe profile screen + one mission load, Thief II one mission, Jedi Knight one level, Shogo menu, Max Payne menu.
- The ring's 513/41 lines list each title's texture formats today. 513/42 and 513/7 list any off-list format a DX5-7 title creates or binds. That is Phase 0's measurement and the baseline frames.

Boot B (D3DTexFmt=1): the texX1555/texX4444 caps rows are 1, x1555_decode1 and x4444_decode1 PASS at all three modes, and nothing else changes. Re-run the titles; any title whose 513/41 now shows X1R5G5B5/X4R4G4B4 gets its frame compared with A's.

Boot C (=2): a8l8_decode1 and mipa8l8 PASS. Compare H&D and JK/MotS frames: DX5 choosers could misread a luminance entry as RGB.

Boot D (=4): l8_decode1, a4l4_decode1, l8_phase, mipl8, l8_2048_decode, l8_upd and l8_copy all PASS at all three modes, and the ring shows no extra 513/10 out-of-memory. Max Payne menu attended, since its D3DX loader may now pick L8.

Boot E (=8), only for a measured consumer: r332_decode1 and a8r332_decode1 PASS. AvP, once G71 lets it reach a device: A/B its "chosen %u-bit ... texture format" log; it must keep a 16-bit format.

No game scene is expected to change, since no consumer is known, so the game runs are no-regression checks.
- If Phase 0 shows a DX5/6 title creating L8/A8L8/A4L4/332 textures that are refused today (drawn untextured), that title's own scene, fullscreen at its staged mode, becomes the proof for the matching bit, and G34's priority rises.
- If an armed boot changes a working title's frame, that bit stays opt-in and the finding is recorded in the README.
G34.risk:
Proven paths:
- The fresh-install default 16 bpp path (no D3DBigTex) is untouched: tex_fmt is forced to 0, and tex_view and DirectDraw placement stay as they are.
- D3DBigTex=7 with D3DTexFmt absent is byte-for-byte today's list, classification, registers and placement. Only two deduplicated INFO log events are added at CreateSurface/CanCreateSurface, outside the drawing path.
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence, SLI and the flip path: no new registers. The changes are textureMode format codes and TCA bits inside the existing writes; no combineMode, chipMask, sliCtrl or flip code.

Main risk when armed: behaviour change, not crashes, in titles that work today and choose formats themselves:
- H&D's LS3D converter;
- Max Payne's and Thief II's D3DX "closest format" loaders;
- DX5/6 best-match enumerators (AvP could take RGB332 for 256-colour art; JK/MotS could misread luminance entries as RGB).
Mitigations: an append-only list (first-match choosers unchanged), one bit per boot, 513/41 naming exactly who switched, and bit 3 never armed without a consumer.

Memory-safety hazards the design closes, each pinned by a test:
- Dd_Blt's surf_bytespp falls back to the desktop depth for textures, so an engine blit would overrun an 8-bit texture 2-4x. Closed by a HEL guard.
- Freeing a padded tiny 8-bit texture without subtracting the pad corrupts DirectDraw's heap. Closed by a 4-bit SF_PAD count rather than G21's SF_PAD8.
- The texture-port write-back on unproven formats. Restricted to formats 10/11/12.

Avoided by design: the Thief II launcher's findstr "0x[57df]$" would turn D3DBigTex >= 0x10 into "off", hence the separate D3DTexFmt switch.

Silicon unknowns, each settled by a decode test before any game runs with its bit: AI44 nibble order, AI88, B8 layout. B8 mip chains lose their last 1-2 levels until G07, as 16-bit chains do today. Any boot that runs Max Payne must be attended (G04).
games_unblocked: none measured - Halo's only missing format is X8R8G8B8 (1,419 2D bitmaps across its 30 maps), owned by G17
candidate, unmeasured: Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe (LS3D converter covers every D3D8 format)
candidate, unmeasured: DX5/DX6 titles that Phase 0 (513/42, 513/7) finds creating off-list texture formats
open_questions: AI44 nibble order on the VSA-100: alpha in bits 7:4 is inferred from the spec naming and 3dfx's direct A4L4->AI44 mapping; a4l4_decode1 decides.

Does NT set DDRAWISURF_HASPIXELFORMAT on DX6-created textures? If not, Dd_Blt's surf_bytespp desktop-depth fallback also mis-blits today's 16 bpp textures at a 32 bpp desktop - a latent issue outside G34 (G56/G61's area); the 513/42 event can log dwFlags to answer it.

Does any staged title actually ask for these formats? Phase 0 answers it for DX5-7 titles. D3D8/9 titles refused inside the runtime are invisible to the HAL; only an optional API-level d3d8/d3d9 logging proxy would see them. Build it only if a decision depends on it.

Will Hidden and Dangerous (LS3D), Max Payne (D3DXCreateTextureFromFileInMemoryEx) or Thief II (D3DXLoadSurfaceFromSurface) switch to newly offered formats, and does the switch look the same? Boots B-D answer it.
Pad encoding: G21 proposes a single SF_PAD8 bit, while G34 needs a 4-bit count (4 and 8). G07, G21 and G34 should agree on the count before the first of them lands.
Switch transport: an appended vcr_info.d3d_texfmt field (the same pattern as G05's d3dfeat, with VcrDd2dInit zeroing info) or four positive VCR_INFO_F_* bits in an increasingly crowded flags word?

Does the DX6 runtime (d3dim.dll) validate a bound texture's format against the enumerated list? If it does, off-list X1R5G5B5/X4R4G4B4 surfaces - today sampled with their undefined X bits as alpha - cannot occur in DX6 titles.
A8 is reachable for D3D8/9 only through a DX8-level DDI (G94); if that is ever built, the TMU colour combine must zero RGB (SST_TC_ZERO) because the TMU's A8 returns RGB = alpha.

G43.approach:
VERDICT: the headline claim does not hold, and the gap's proposed fix (re-derive pd from c->ddlcl->lpGbl->dhpdev on every call) should NOT be built.

Why the claim fails:
- Microsoft's W2K DDK, section 2.3.3 "Supporting Multiple PDEVs" (local copy w2kddk/help/d_grafx.chm), says a driver instance that owns a Direct3D object is only disabled by DrvAssertMode(FALSE). It is kept until its last D3D object is destroyed, or brought back with DrvAssertMode(TRUE) when the mode returns. Only then do DrvDisableDirectDraw, DrvDisableSurface and DrvDisablePDEV run.
- Seven teardowns already recorded on .124 follow that order: RING09 seq 9033-9039 and 9346-9420; the onbox ring_after_probes; the UT2004 run killed by pid; UT2003; Halo. In all seven, ContextDestroy comes before DrvDisablePDEV of the context's own PDEV. One PDEV was kept inactive for 27.7 s under a live context.

Why the proposed fix is harmful:
- In 4 of the 7 runs, ContextDestroy arrives after DestroyDDLocal, so re-deriving would read a local the driver has already been told is going away.
- If XP re-points a local's global at the new PDEV, re-deriving would aim a context whose surfaces are lost at the active PDEV's memory.

What is real:
- R1, the open stability question: in 3 of 7 runs (the UT2003 and Halo exits, and RING09 seq B), DestroyDDLocal arrives after DrvDisablePDEV. Dd_DestroyDDLocal then reads pd->flip, and may write it through flip_stats_log, of whatever pDDLcl->lpGbl->dhpdev names. Whether that is the freed PDEV is unknown.
- R2: a context can live on a kept-but-inactive PDEV. DP2, Clear2, TEXBLT and ctx_free never check whether their PDEV owns the screen. TEXBLT does not even check w->drawable. The Glide-owner check reads the inactive PDEV's exclusive_pid, which is 0.
- R3: three borrowed pointers are never cleared:
  - tex_surf0/1 (VcrDdD3dSurfaceGone does not clear them);
  - pvmList (DrvDisableDirectDraw does not clear it);
  - ddlcl after DestroyDDLocal.
- R4: it is unmeasured whether a mip chain is freed before its DirectDraw heap is torn down.
- R5: alt-tab was never run. A DX5/6/7 context that survives a surface loss has rt/zb cleared at the loss.

DESIGN, part 1: a new Win32-free header include/vcr_d3dlife.h, host-tested.
- A live-PDEV registry: up to 16 entries holding the pointer, a generation number and an active flag. Entries are only compared, never dereferenced. If the registry is full it answers UNKNOWN and every guard behaves as today.
- A dead-heap set.
- Verdict functions: may_read, may_hw, heap_may_free, and ctx_verdict (DRAW, DRAW_LOGGED, LOST or BAD).

DESIGN, part 2: default-on glue. No register write and no answer changes on any path where the contract holds.
- Registry calls: DrvEnablePDEV registers the PDEV. DrvEnableSurface and DrvAssertMode set the active flag. DrvDisableSurface and DrvDisablePDEV first run VcrDdD3dPdevGone, then DrvDisablePDEV unregisters the PDEV before EngFreeMem.
- VcrDdD3dPdevGone orphans any context that still names the PDEV, which should never happen. It logs ERROR, clears pd/rt/zb/tex_surf, and keeps the slot reserved until the runtime's own ContextDestroy, so a reused slot cannot answer to a stale handle.
- ctx_of returns NULL for an orphan, so the call answers D3DNTHAL_CONTEXT_BAD. ContextDestroy finds orphans through a new ctx_slot_of.
- ctx_free calls VcrDd2dSync only when the PDEV is active, as the DDK rule requires. This changes nothing on all 7 runs, where g2d_busy was 0.
- Dd_DestroyDDLocal calls VcrDdFlipLocalGone only if the PDEV is live. It always logs local, global and dhpdev with their liveness, and marks that local's contexts ddlcl_gone.
- DrvDisableDirectDraw clears pvmList and marks the PDEV's heap dead.
- VcrDdD3dFreeMipChain skips VidMemFree for a dead heap (ERROR) and counts frees made at a loss (DDRAWISURF_INVALID).
- VcrDdD3dSurfaceGone also clears tex_surf0/1.
- DP2 and Clear2 check the registry once per lifecycle epoch, and log once when the local's dhpdev differs from c->pd (the global-swap detector).
- Instrumentation:
  - event 515 VCR_EV_DD_LIFE, what codes 1-12, rare events only;
  - VCR_ESC_D3D_LIFE (VCR_ESC_BASE + 14), returning counters that survive the ring wrap;
  - vcrctl d3dlife, read only after the D3D program exits.
- No caps change and no register change.

DESIGN, part 3: Diag\D3DSafe bit 4 (value 16), default off.
- An inactive PDEV never draws. DP2 parses the stream so state is kept, writes no register, skips TEXBLT and answers DDERR_SURFACELOST. It shares G02's "answer lost" helper.
- rt/zb are kept by handle and resolved again after a loss, as the DDK recommends.

INVESTIGATION. Run on the 86Box bed first, then one supervised .124 boot:
- T1: baseline teardown.
- T2: the new d3dprobe lost mode (minimize, restore, Reset).
- T3: release while lost.
- T4: kill while lost.
- T5: kill while active.
- T6: windowed device plus an external mode switch.
- T7: alt-tab in a DX5/6 title (Mysteries of the Sith or Thief Gold).
- DV: T2-T5 again with Driver Verifier special pool on vcrdd.dll, if XP accepts it.

Outcomes:

| outcome | action |
|---|---|
| 1. the contract holds | keep the guards as hardening; drop to P2 |
| 2. 515/9: DestroyDDLocal names a freed PDEV | a real use-after-free; P0 |
| 3. 515/7: a context outlives its PDEV | P0 |
| 4. 515/8: drawing calls on an inactive PDEV | arm bit 4 |
| 5. black frame after alt-tab | arm the rt/zb-by-handle fix |
| 6. 515/10: chain freed after its heap died | P0 |

Vendor reference: 3dfx's own HAL caches ppdev in the context too (D3CONTXT.C:342-343,404; SETUP_PPDEV in every DP2). It relies on the same contract.

G43.gating:
This item has two halves with different gates.

DEFAULT-ON half, allowed under the "proven path byte-for-byte unchanged" convention. It covers the registry, the guards, the orphan scrub, the ctx_free hardware gate, the DestroyDDLocal liveness check, clearing pvmList and tex_surf, the dead-heap skip, event 515 and the counters escape.
- On every path where the contract holds it adds only pointer bookkeeping and logs: no register write and no answer changes. That covers all seven sequences recorded on .124.
- The only new answers are:
  - D3DNTHAL_CONTEXT_BAD for an orphaned context, which without this change would be a dereference of NULL or of freed memory;
  - a refused ContextCreate on a PDEV that is not live, which cannot occur.
- The registry fails open: if it is full it answers UNKNOWN, and every guard then behaves as today.
- It is safe to land default-on once:
  - the host tests pass (they replay the seven real sequences);
  - d3dprobe render plus the new lost mode pass on the 86Box bed;
  - render passes on .124 at 640x480x16 and 1024x768x32.

BEHAVIOURAL half: Diag\D3DSafe bit 4 (value 16), default OFF, absent = off. Bits 0-3 and 7 are taken by G01, G03, G02, G10 and G02's test bit. The miniport reads the switch at boot beside D3D32/Reset3D, and the display DLL learns it through vcr_info.d3dsafe (G02) or flag 0x8000<<4 (G03). It covers two things:
- An inactive PDEV never draws: parse only, no register write, TEXBLT skipped, DDERR_SURFACELOST.
- rt/zb are re-bound by handle after a loss.

With the bit off, 515/8 is only a detector. Arm it only if the investigation shows Outcome 4 (drawing on an inactive PDEV) or Outcome 5 (black after an alt-tab). It is proven on the bed first, then in one supervised clean boot with that single Diag change.
G43.d3dprobe_test:
New mode `d3dprobe lost [--full] [--res WxH] [--bpp 16|32] [--pace MS] [--tests clear,tex[,mip]] [--release-while-lost] [--hold-lost S] [--external]`.

Sequence:
1. Create the device fullscreen (mode switch 1, paced through vcr_pace_before_switch/after_switch). Create managed textures: tex is a 64x64 checker; mip is the existing chain, whose video-memory copy is our mip-chain block. Draw and read back against the same analytic references `render` uses: the exact clear colour, the checker texels, and level colours by texel:pixel ratio for mip (silicon only; 86Box samples level 0).
2. Lose the device (mode switch 2). Take the pace gate, then ShowWindow(SW_MINIMIZE); the runtime gives the desktop back. Focus loss does not end the run here. Expect TestCooperativeLevel = D3DERR_DEVICELOST (88760868), Present = D3DERR_DEVICELOST, and a DrawPrimitiveUP that returns.
3. With --release-while-lost: release the device here and end.
4. Restore (mode switch 3, paced). ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE) and SetForegroundWindow, pump until TestCooperativeLevel = D3DERR_DEVICENOTRESET (88760869, at most 10 s), then Reset (paced). Redraw and read back the same tests.
5. Release (mode switch 4, paced).

RESULT line: {mode:lost, before, after, lost_hr, notreset_hr, reset_hr, switches:4}.

Pass criterion:
- every check passes both before and after, pixel-exact against the references;

G40.approach:
VERDICT: G40 is NOT a real defect on .124 (XP SP3). No runtime on that OS ever sends D3DDP2OP_STATESET to vcrdd, so the hal-07 "over-promise" does not exist. Priority P3. The code path is real: rec_size skips opcode 39 by size (vcrdd_d3d.c:1562) and RENDERSTATE/TSS records are applied at once (:1585-1611, set_rs :1393-1406). But a forwarding runtime is needed to reach it, and there is none.

STATIC EVIDENCE (new for d3dim700; d3d8/d3d9 re-checked byte for byte)
1. D3D8/D3D9 emulate state blocks for any DDI type <= 5.
   - d3d8 0x6d9e8c05/0x6d9e8c32: cmpl $5,0x28; jle -> emulate=1.
   - d3d9 0x4fe6fc25/0x4fe6fc5a: the same.
   - EmulateStateBlocks (string at d3d8 0x6d9a949c) is read only above 5.
   - vcrdd is DX7-level (no GETDRIVERINFO2), so its DDI type is <= 5.
2. d3dim700 5.03.2600.5512 (md5 56adb11f), the DX7 runtime that runtime-19 called "the exception":
   - Its DDI-4 (DP2EX, vtable 0x739486f8) and DDI-5 (T&L) device classes do contain a STATESET emitter: WriteStateSetToDevice 0x73956583 (BEGIN at 0x7395661e, END at 0x73956673) and helper 0x7395157e for EXECUTE/CAPTURE/DELETE. The DDI-3 version is `ret 4`.
   - Every emission is gated on the state set's driver buffer being non-empty (0x739565a9; 0x739524c5, 0x739521b1, 0x73952528).
   - A recorded state goes into that buffer only if bit 31 of CStateSets::m_dwFlags is set (testb $0x80,0x5f(%ecx) at 0x739521f4; and $0x80000000 at 0x7395245d).
   - m_dwFlags is copied once, by Init 0x7395140c, from the device's runtime-flags word +0x1a6c (push 0x1a6c(%ebx) at 0x7394bb94).
   - Nothing sets bit 31 of +0x1a6c. All 65 writes in the disassembly were enumerated, and a raw byte scan of every encoding that could set it (81/1, 83/1 imm8, 80/1 on +0x1a6f, C7/0, 0F BA/5) found zero hits. The scan's positive control was found exactly once: bit 30 at 0x73956d0d, in the T&L Init. Objects come from LocalAlloc(LMEM_ZEROINIT), and there is no registry knob.
   - So d3dim700 always emulates. While recording, SetRenderState and SetTextureStageState return without reaching the driver (0x7394f928, 0x7394fc18). ApplyStateBlock (0x73950bc5 -> 0x7394f470 -> CStateSet::Execute 0x739517b6) replays the block as ordinary RENDERSTATE/TEXTURESTAGESTATE records, which the walker already applies.
3. d3dim.dll (DX6 interfaces) has no state blocks at all. No staged title ships its own runtime DLL (case-insensitive find).
4. Who uses state blocks:
   - UE1 D3DDrv (Unreal Gold, UT436, Deus Ex): zero Apply/Capture/Delete/Create call sites.
   - Tribes 2 OpenGL2D3D.dll: 27 ApplyStateBlock calls on its device global 0x437080. It is the only staged renderer that uses them, and it is dormant on .124 (runs OpenGL).
   - D3D8/9 titles (Halo, UT2003/2004, ...) are emulated before the DDI.

DESIGN
Step 0, land default-ON (log-only; register traffic and parse alignment unchanged):
- New Win32-free include/vcr_dp2stateset.h:
  - vcr_ss_count tallies 12-byte records by operation (BEGIN/END/DELETE/EXECUTE/CAPTURE/other) and keeps the first {op, handle, type};
  - vcr_ss_pack16 packs two counts into one event field, saturating.
- vcrdd_d3d.c:
  - add vcr_ss_tally ss to vcr_d3dctx;
  - give walk() an explicit case D3DNTDP2OP_STATESET: NEED(n*12), count, skip, never apply;
  - drop STATESET from rec_size;
  - the first record per context raises one WARN, 513/25 (op, handle, sbType): "the runtime is not emulating state blocks";
  - ctx_free ALWAYS emits INFO 513/24 with the six counts packed into b/c/d, as its own event because the "context gone" text is at the 96-character limit. If G76's per-context counter record lands first, the counts become a row of it instead.
- vcr_events.h: document 24/25.
- Caps: no change. DRAWPRIMITIVES2EX must stay: it selects d3dim700's DX7 device class and our D3D8/9 DDI type, so dropping it would change everything and fix nothing. Setting EmulateStateBlocks on the box is not a fix: it is never read at DDI <= 5.
- What each outcome means:
  - all counters 0 and the probes pass: close G40 as not a defect;
  - a 513/25 appears: the box runs another runtime build; md5 it, re-run the scan, build Step 1;
  - pixels fail with 0 STATESET: another gap (G01, blend, ...), not G40.

Step 1, PARKED (build only if Step 0 ever counts a STATESET), default-OFF behind Diag\D3DFeat bit SBLK:
- include/vcr_stateblk.h holds per-context blocks: RS mask and values for 256 states, TSS stages 0/1 including TEXTUREMAP. The table is capped at 1024 handles; handle 0 is refused.
- While recording, RS/TSS records are stored, not applied, and lpdwRStates is not mirrored (as Microsoft's sample does).
- EXECUTE replays through set_rs and the TSS path. CAPTURE reads c->rs[], c->tss*[] and the texture handles. DELETE frees the block. Context destroy frees every block.
- A nested BEGIN or stray END is logged and the walk continues; the batch is never aborted.
- Vendor behaviour NOT to copy:
  - 3dfx's Capture writes 0 for every state it keeps no field for (D7DP2.C:2046-2057);
  - its block table has an off-by-one: it grows when handle > [0] but finds only handle < [0] (:2237 vs :2202);
  - it aborts the whole DP2 batch on a STATESET error (D6DP2.C:4236-4245, 4972-4980).

Docs: README Findings, the plan's G40 row, FINDINGS.md. runtime-19's "DX7 is the exception" is superseded by this design.

Step 0 is safe to land default-ON:
- It is log-only. No register write is added or changed, and the D3D-visible behaviour is identical: opcode 39 is still consumed as n*12 bytes under the same NEED bound, and nothing is applied.
- It adds one INFO event per context lifetime, plus a WARN that fires only if the static analysis is wrong.
- It is pinned by the native and Python tests.
- It rides on the next vcrdd.dll deploy (ideally with G76's counters) with no Diag change.

Step 1 (record/execute/capture/delete) is PARKED:
- It is built only if Step 0 ever counts a STATESET.
- It then lands default-OFF behind Diag\D3DFeat bit SBLK, read at boot and cached in the PDEV like D3D32/D3DBigTex.
- With the bit clear, Step 0's skip stays byte-for-byte unchanged.
- It is proven in one supervised clean boot.

Step 0 carries effectively no risk to proven paths:
- No register write is added or changed. The default 16 bpp D3D sequence, D3D32, Glide/OpenGL coexistence, SLI state and the flip path are untouched.

The evidence test depends on the share: it skips loudly when the share is absent, and it fails by design when the fleet image's runtime changes.

Step 1 (parked) has one real risk: a stuck record mode (BEGIN with no END) would swallow later RS/TSS records, and frames would draw with stale state. Mitigations:
- END, ContextCreate and ContextDestroy clear it;
- a draw while recording is counted and logged;
- the block table is capped;
- it is default-OFF and proven one clean boot at a time.

G46.approach:
The gap is real and the evidence on file cannot close it, so this is an investigation in four stages. Each stage runs only if the one before leaves the question open, and each outcome is mapped to the fix that follows from it.

S0 is done in this design: a host re-analysis of the committed UT2003 stats CSV and ring.
- DrawPrimitive is 94.9% of the frame. The game outside D3D costs only 6.3 ms of 123.
- Each submitted primitive costs 3.75 µs (median). Primitives alone explain the frame time with R² 0.953.
- 18,586 triangles a frame reach the HAL (63% of the 29,362 submitted) in 29.9 DP2 calls. That bounds the HAL at 6.28 µs per triangle, which fits the PIO model of 36-45 uncached writes plus 3 status reads per triangle.
- The CSV cannot split runtime from HAL: primitives and software-processed vertices correlate at 0.994.
- The driver kept no frame count for any game: all four sessions logged 'flips of 0', because the flip counters count vsync'd flips only.
- UT2004 run 1 at 1280x960 shows about 2x the cost per HAL triangle. Its frame count is inferred, so fill may be a large share at high resolution. The split differs per title and per resolution.
- Logging costs at most about 0.8 ms a frame (from the ring's sequence numbers), so G52 is not the bottleneck.

S1 needs no driver change. A new user-mode lab tool, cputimes.exe, samples the game thread's kernel and user time once a second (GetProcessTimes/GetThreadTimes/GetSystemTimes; query rights only, no escape, no display lock). It runs during the UT2003 flyby (with the game's own CSV), the UT2004 stat-fps botmatch and Halo. The HAL's DP2/Clear2/Flip/Lock run in the calling thread in kernel mode, and the D3D8 runtime's software vertex processing runs in user mode, so this gives the HAL-versus-runtime split directly. A host tool, ue2stats.py, reproduces the S0 numbers and joins them with cputimes and the ring.

S2 adds Diag\D3DStats, default off, log-only. It is the counter set the gap assigns to G78, written as a pure header, vcr_d3dperf.h, in the pattern of vcr_flip.h.
- Frames: every successful Flip, NOVSYNC included, plus a Blt to the primary.
- Triangles by DP2 op (TRIANGLEFAN_IMM measures runtime clipping, for G57) and by stage count.
- Writes, computed from the formulas so vcrdd_3d.c stays untouched.
- VcrDdRoom calls and extra spins (the chip-busy waits); VcrDd2dSync waits.
- compute_regs calls, state and target re-sends, texture flushes, log IOCTLs, and draws into a pending flip_from (for G55).
- A cpuid-serialised TSC at the DDI entry points, calibrated against QPC, and per-frame histograms of frame time and HAL share. The HAL share is also the display-lock hold share, which links to G04.
- Six reads of chip 0's statistics registers after the existing Flip drain (VSA-100 only): fbiPixelsIn/ChromaFail/ZfuncFail/AfuncFail/PixelsOut at 0x14c-0x15c and fbiTrianglesOut at 0x25c, accumulated 24-bit wrap-aware.
- The totals are logged once per session as a new 5xx event at the points the flip counters already use. They can also ride G04's heartbeat for live REGREAD.

S2 also adds d3dprobe perf modes (code owned by G74/G78, specified here), each with an analytic verification frame:
- setup: tiny 2-pixel quads, list/strip/fan/ilist, 0/1/2 textures. Gives µs per triangle and the effective write and read costs.
- fill: full-screen layers. Gives px/clk, and checks Σ fbiPixelsIn against W×H×L.
- xform and clip: the runtime's per-vertex and per-clipped-triangle cost.
- game: a fixed UE2-like 20K-triangle frame, the before/after benchmark for G47-G51.

The S2 session also runs:
- resolution scaling: the UT2003 flyby at 640x480 and 1024x768 via a setres exec file, and UT2004 at 1280x960 and 640x480;
- UT99 436 D3DDrv UTbench against the vendor HAL's 70.35/69.5/69.11 fps;
- a 60 s breadth pass over every D3D title, ranking them as HAL-bound, fill-bound or fine.

Analysis. A new tool, d3dperf.py, builds the split table, reconciles three measures and applies a decision table:
- The three measures are S1's kernel time, D3DStats' HAL time, and the counts times the unit costs. They must agree within 10%. If they do not, build the vendor's PCI_NULL/PCI_NOP levels (values 2 and 3) before choosing a fix.
- Transport-bound means kernel ≥70% and writes+reads ≥60% of HAL time, with few spins. Do G48 credit room checks and G58 packed colour / no duplicate sOow1 first (model: −30-45% of HAL time, UT2003 9.4→~13-17 fps). Then G47 CMDFIFO (model: ~30-45 fps) if the S3 ceiling is ≥3x today's fps. G49 only if the continuable share is ≥30%.
- Chip-bound means spins ≥25% or time that grows with resolution. Do G50 2PPC, then G47 for overlap, then G51 SLI for 1280x960 titles.
- Runtime-bound means user ≥50% with a low ceiling. Do G57 if fan_imm ≥5% of HAL triangles; otherwise it is a hardware limit (G83).
- Smaller shares go to G53 (state ≥10%), G52 (log ≥2%), G56/G54 (drains ≥5%) and G55 (draws into a pending flip).
- A what-if model predicts each fix's frame time from the measured counts before it is built.

Expected outcome (inferred): UT2003 at 640x480 is transport-bound; 1280x960 titles add a large fill-wait share.

Nothing changes on a fresh install or on the proven path: both switches are absent by default, and the emitter and register sequences are pinned by tests.

G46.gating:
Tools (cputimes.exe, ue2stats.py, d3dperf.py, optional procprof.exe):
- user mode or host only, query rights only, no escape and no display lock, so no gating is needed.

Diag\D3DStats:
- Default OFF (absent = 0). Read at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO, as Accel2DText and DdHeapFloor are, so a game's own mode switch picks it up.
- It travels in a new appended vcr_info.d3d_perf field, not the flag word, because bit 0x8000 is already claimed by five designs. The DLL honours it only when info.size covers the field, so an older miniport means off.
- Log-only: it adds no register write. Its only hardware access is six reads of chip 0's statistics registers per frame, after Dd_Flip's existing drain, VSA-100 only, never while a Glide owner holds the chip.
- Off, it costs one predictable branch per DDI call plus an integer add at VcrDdRoom/VcrDd2dSync return: no cpuid/rdtsc, no register read, no event.
- Bit 0 may become default ON after one supervised boot shows:
  - d3dprobe render 40/40 at 16 and 32 bpp (windowed 42/42);
  - the overhead A/B within 1%;
  - the counters equal to the analytic workloads.
  Bit 1 (fine timing) stays off.

Diag\D3DPerfTest:
- Diagnostic only, never default.
- Read at boot (beside D3DBigTex), and only value 1 is accepted.
- The miniport writes it back to 0 (flushed) at the same boot, so a forgotten arm costs one boot of undrawn D3D at most.
- WARN lines at boot, at VcrDd2dInit and at every ContextCreate.
- d3dprobe render visibly fails its triangle checks while it is armed.

General:
- One Diag change per clean boot: S2 arms D3DStats once for the session; S3 is its own boot.
- Activation check plus safe-reboot.py for every reboot.

Proven path:
- byte-for-byte unchanged: vcrdd_3d.c is untouched, and the register sequences and emitter bodies are pinned by tests.

Not applicable:
- This is not a behaviour fix, so there is nothing to land default-on beyond the instrumentation above.
G46.d3dprobe_test:
New d3dprobe perf modes (code owned by G74/G78, specified in G46 §3.5). All run with --full --novsync. Each runs a timed loop and then one verification frame, read back against analytic values, so a run that drew nothing never reports a speed. Today's scene stays the default as --mode classic.

1. perf --mode setup --prim list|strip|fan|ilist --tex 0|1|2 --tris 20000
   - Draws: tiny 2x1-pixel quads, (x-0.5,y-0.5)-(x+1.5,y+0.5) in XYZRHW, from a static SYSTEMMEM vertex buffer. Clipping off, Z off, cull none.
   - Reports: µs per triangle and triangles/s.
   - Pass: lit pixels == 2 x quads exactly. With D3DStats on, the ring's triangle count must equal frames x triangles per frame, and status reads must be ≥ 3 x triangles (today's formula).
   - The slope across 27/36/45 writes gives the effective write cost; the intercept, with S3, gives the read cost.

2. perf --mode fill --layers L (0, 1, 8) --tex 0|1|2 [--blend]
   - Reports: Mpix/s and px/clk (core clock read before the run, never during).
   - Pass: every pixel equals the last layer's colour, and with D3DStats on, Σ fbiPixelsIn over the timed frames == W x H x L x frames. L=0 measures the clears' own contribution. This analytic reference settles the counters' width and meaning.

3. perf --mode xform [--light 0..8] and perf --mode clip
   - xform: the same cells as untransformed XYZ under software vertex processing. clip: cells straddling the viewport edge.
   - Reports: the runtime's µs per vertex and µs per clipped triangle.
   - Pass: the same lit-pixel count as setup for xform; for clip, the inside part lit and the outside dark.

4. perf --mode game
   - Draws: a fixed UE2-like frame of about 20K indexed triangles in 30 DrawIndexedPrimitive calls, 2 stages, Z on, about 400 state and 60 texture changes.
   - Pass: 16 probe pixels equal their analytic colours.
   - Its fps is the standing before/after benchmark for G47-G51.

Also:
- Overhead A/B: classic and game fps with D3DStats=1 must be ≥99% of the unarmed boot's.
- With D3DPerfTest=1: d3dprobe render must FAIL its triangle checks while the clears pass, which proves the switch is live.

G46.risk:
Low. When off: both switches are absent by default, so a fresh install and the proven 16 bpp path get no new register traffic and no new read; only one predictable branch per DDI call and an integer add at VcrDdRoom/VcrDd2dSync return. vcrdd_3d.c is untouched and pinned by tests.

D3DStats when armed:
- Its only hardware access is six statistics reads of chip 0 per frame, after Dd_Flip's existing drain. That delays the start-address write by about 6-12 µs, well inside a refresh, and the vsync completion rule is unchanged.
- The reads are skipped while a Glide owner holds the chip, and a Glide game never calls Dd_Flip, so Glide/OpenGL coexistence is unaffected.
- D3D stays single-chip, so the SLI state is untouched.
- Perturbation: about 70 cpuid/rdtsc pairs a frame. The fine mode costs about 3-5% and is used only for calibration.

D3DPerfTest:
- When armed, D3D draws only clears. It clears itself at the boot that honours it, and logs WARN everywhere, so a forgotten arm costs one boot at most.

G44.approach:
VERDICT (host analysis of the staged game data, reproducible script in the design's Appendix A). The gap is real, but it is not specific to UT2003 and it is not a texture-format swap. The checkerboard is not UE2's default texture either.

(1) The grass is the same object in both games.
- Both DM-Antalus maps have one deco layer, TowerStatic.Rock.TowerDecoGrassA (28 triangles). The flyby stats CSV confirms it: 84-236 decorations a frame at exactly 28 triangles each, in 1978 of 1998 frames.
- Its material is TowerTerrain.General.TowerGrassFinalBlend: AlphaBlend, AlphaTest, AlphaRef 57, TwoSided.
- The texture is General.TowerGrass, a 512x512 DXT3 with 10 levels (NormalLOD 1).
- TowerTerrain.utx is byte-identical in UT2003 and UT2004 (md5 7ac4cc2c...). So no format swap can make the two games differ.

(2) The blue pixels cannot be TowerGrass texels under any combine.
- Decoded, the roughly 89,000 alpha>57 texels on levels 0-6 are yellow-green, mean about (85,105,42). None has blue above red or green, and blue's p99 is 57-123.
- The frames show about (49,79,149). MODULATE (the HAL draws 2X/4X as 1x) cannot lift blue above the texel's own. ADD cannot lower red.
- The quads are about 70-90% covered by diagonal stripes in texture space, while TowerGrass covers 25-34% as blades. So the TMU reads bytes that are not this texture at the LOD in use.

(3) The UT2004 "control" was captured at a different LOD.
- UT2003 ran at 640x480 (G19's auto-configuration) with a flying camera: near quads about 60-120 px for the 256 level, so the TMU samples level 1-2.
- UT2004's only grass frame is a bot standing in the clump at 1280x960: magnified, level 0.
- Level 0 is the only level that is always its own block.

(4) Engine.DefaultTexture is a 128x128 P8 of grey-green bubbles, not a checkerboard. The wedge is a periodic grey tiling with a period of about 12 px: a tiled small mip level read from the wrong place, or real content (catwalks).

LEADING HYPOTHESIS H1: this is G06's confetti / G07's split mip chains, seen through UT2003's 640x480. Two alternatives remain: H6 (the wrong surface is bound, handle table G42) and H7 (a DXT3 chain is mis-laid out or decoded at LOD 1 or more; never tested). The combine (G05/G12-G14), texture coordinates, fog and the cache (G37) are excluded.

- E1, log-only instrumentation in G06's Boot 0: log_combo gains 513/28 (fog, TFACTOR, cull, TEXCOORDINDEX/TTFF raw, stage-1 args) and 513/29 (FVF, offsets and the first vertex, sampled once in tri()/imm_tri()). combo_seen grows 64->128. At LogLevel 2 with LogEntries 16384:
