G54.approach:
VERDICT: real, small today, and the frame-boundary serialiser once the CMDFIFO (P6/G47) lands.

TODAY (read): a vsync'd Dd_Flip does VcrDd2dSync (a full idle wait; today about one triangle, because the PCI FIFO holds 31 writes), then three IOCTLs: the flip (the miniport writes vidDesktopStartAddr), a TRACE log line and a vblank read. Each DDERR_WASSTILLDRAWING retry is another IOCTL (vcrdd_ddraw.c:330-361, 246-255; vcrmp_dd.c:65-80). That is about 20-50 us a frame (inferred). After P6 the drain would wait for the whole GPU tail and leave frame time at about CPU+GPU instead of max(CPU,GPU).

FIX: 3dfx's and our Glide's hardware swap on the OVERLAY layer (VH5/DDFLIP.C:394,441-446; GL5 gglide.c:2812-2828).

PROMOTION (miniport, at the first hardware flip of a fullscreen 3D primary chain): a new IOCTL_VCR_DDOVERLAY (proposed 0xa12).
- Preconditions, one refusal reason each: no SLI, no exclusive owner, chip 0 cfgInitEnable bit 17 clear, cmdFifo0 off (G01), status[30:28]==0, chip idle.
- Saves every register it will touch.
- Loads leftOverlayBuf = the current front by an immediate swap, verified with vidCurrOverlayStartAddr (I/O 0xfc).
- Programs the overlay as 3dfx's Promote_PrimaryToOverlay does (VH5/DDFXNT.C:2552-2697): stride[29:16] = pitch, start coords 0, end coords ((h-1)<<12)|(w-1), dudx/dvdy 0, fetch width (w*Bpp)<<19.
- At vblank, in one write: vidProcCfg desktop off, overlay on, linear, RGB565U or RGB32U, filter POINT (pixel-identical to today's desktop output); cursor, 2X and VP bits kept.
- dramInit1 bit 11 per chain: off for 2 surfaces; on for 3 or more only with Diag bit 2. This is 3dfx's rule (VH5/DDSURF.C:371-393), and Glide can leave the bit set.
- Refused (old path): half mode, 2X mode, 8 bpp, w*Bpp>8191, pitch>0x3fff, unaligned address.

DEMOTION (idempotent): bounded wait for the count to reach 0 (engine reset on a stall), vidDesktopStartAddr = the GDI primary, then restore vidProcCfg (at vblank), the overlay registers and dramInit1.
- The DLL demotes at FlipToGDISurface, SetExclusiveMode(0), DestroySurface of a chain member, DestroyDDLocal, DrvDisableDirectDraw, DrvAssertMode(FALSE), HWCSETEXCLUSIVE and a 2D give-up.
- The miniport also demotes on its own at RESET_DEVICE, every mode set, HWCSETEXCLUSIVE and the bugcheck callback, so no missed DLL hook can leave the overlay up.

PER FLIP (DLL, new branch at the top of Dd_Flip; the rest of Dd_Flip is today's code byte for byte):
- one status read through pjRegs; if status[30:28]+1 > cap, return WASSTILLDRAWING (never spin under the display lock; 3dfx's unbounded spin was the .143 3DMark freeze);
- VcrDdRoom(4), then leftOverlayBuf=target, direct swapBufferPend=0, swapbufferCMD = 0x001 vsync / 0x000 NOVSYNC (interval 0, bits 9/10 clear), nopCMD=0 (SPEC 5493-5494 order; Glide's V5 NOP);
- no VcrDd2dSync, no IOCTL, no per-flip log.
- Cap = outstanding swaps including the new one: default 2, 1-6 from Diag bits 4-6, hard max 6 (MAXPENDINGBUFFERS_TOAVOIDHANG, VH5/D3GLOBAL.H:749).
- flip_done becomes count==0 (one register read). GetFlipStatus: CANFLIP = may queue; ISFLIPDONE = DD_OK, as 3dfx answers 3D apps. Lock of a chain surface returns WASSTILLDRAWING while the count is above 0. Blt is unchanged (FIFO-ordered).

ORDERING: the VSA-100 blocks the command processor at a vsync'd swap when dramInit1 bit 11 is clear (SPEC 5492, 3960). Rendering after the flip therefore waits in the chip, which closes the render-after-flip hazard (G55), and CANRENDERAFTERFLIP becomes honest. Consequence: correct double buffering quantises a vsync'd frame rate that sits between 1 and 2 refreshes. Today's driver avoids that only by drawing into the scanned-out buffer. Measure per title; triple buffering is the remedy.

MEASUREMENT: fbiSwapHistory (3D 0x258) gives an exact vsyncs-per-frame histogram, sampled when idle, every 8 flips (feeds G78).

STALL: no progress for 500 ms with swaps pending -> ERROR log, engine reset, demote, broken (old path) until the next PDEV.

SELF-TEST (Diag bit 7, test boots only): a sentinel pixel of the on-screen target, read while a flip is pending around the first clear after a flip. It measures G55 on the old path and proves the ordering on the new one.

STAGES:
- S0 (0x80): measure today's flip cost and G55.
- S1 (0x08): bounded miniport probe ops on an idle desktop settle the spec's contradiction on who increments status[30:28] (SPEC 3956 vs 3959/5493), plus underflow, the fence, history reads, the overlay recipe and reset recovery.
- P7a (0x01): the hardware swap over today's PCI FIFO; mostly correctness and hygiene, small fps gain.
- P7b: the same three registers as CMDFIFO packets after G47 (swapBufferPend stays direct; fence and bump before return). This is the CPU/GPU overlap payoff.

REJECTED:
- desktop-layer swap (leftDesktopBuf + SST_SWAP_DESKTOP_EN) as primary: AA-only use, needs vidScreenSize bit 23, A0 erratum, no SLI path;
- spinning in Flip on the count;
- Glide's FIFO-position counting as primary (kept as the fallback);
- a fence-only fix (it keeps the drain);
- a hidden driver-side third buffer (open question).

Caps: none added. Single pass. DirectDraw 2D chains (no DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE) never take the new path.

G54.gating:
New Diag\D3DHwSwap (DWORD), read at boot, VSA-100 only. Absent = 0 = today's flip path for every flip, byte for byte.

Bits:
- 0: hardware swap for fullscreen 3D primary chains (overlay scan-out, P7a; P7b is selected automatically when G47's ring is live).
- 2: honour triple buffering (dramInit1 bit 11 for chains of 3 or more surfaces).
- 3: miniport probe ops only (S1 experiments; no flip-path change).
- 4-6: maximum outstanding swaps (0 = default 2; 1-6; 7 is clamped to 6).
- 7: ordering self-test (test boots only, reads only).

It reaches the DLL as an appended vcr_info.d3dhwswap field, not a flag bit, because sibling designs collide on 0x8000/0x10000.

Boot sequence, one Diag change per clean boot via safe-reboot.py after the activation check: S0 0x80 -> S1 0x08 (user at the box) -> P7a 0x81 for tests, 0x01 for games -> P7b (D3DCmdFifo already proven, plus 0x01).

NOT safe to land default-on: it moves the scan-out layer, programs video registers (vidProcCfg, overlay geometry, dramInit1) and changes frame pacing. Correct double buffering quantises vsync'd titles that sit between 1 and 2 refreshes per frame. The default flip comes only after P7a and P7b pass with 0 stalls and 0 verify mismatches, the per-title pacing is measured, and the user agrees (with triple-buffer settings in the staged configs where titles offer them, G65).

G54.risk:
Default 16 bpp path and all DirectDraw 2D titles: none while off. When armed, 2D chains still take the old path. When armed:

(a) A swap that never completes blocks the shared PCI FIFO, so GDI's 2D stalls too. Bounded by SPIN_CAP and a 500 ms progress-based stall rule, then engine reset (E8 must prove it clears the swap), demote and fallback for the PDEV. A stuck vsync wait could come from SLI's swap algorithm (bit 17) left set, so promotion refuses it (E7).

(b) A missed demote leaves the last game frame on the overlay over the desktop. It looks like a hang to a remote operator, but the box is alive and the next mode change recovers it. The miniport's own hooks at RESET_DEVICE, mode set, HWCSETEXCLUSIVE and bugcheck make this a backstop-only case.

(c) P7a moves the vsync wait from Flip retries (lock released) into the first DP2/Clear/Lock after a flip (VcrDdRoom/VcrDd2dSync under the display lock, up to one refresh). Texture Locks right after Present also wait a vsync until P8 fences (G56). Measured by counters; P7b removes most of it.

(d) Frame pacing: correct double buffering quantises vsync'd titles between 1 and 2 refreshes per frame (e.g. ~83 fps with tearing today -> 42.5 fps). This is correct behaviour, but a visible fps drop; it needs per-title measurement and triple buffering where offered.

(e) Glide/OpenGL coexistence: promotion is refused with an exclusive owner, SLI or a live cmdFifo0. dramInit1 bit 11 and the overlay registers are restored at demote. Glide reprograms both at open.

(f) Spec ambiguity on the pending count could freeze the throttle (double count) or wrap it. No code relies on it before S1.

(g) Hardware cursor visibility with the desktop layer off is unknown.

Monitor: no mode or timing change; the overlay toggles at vblank, so at most one blip at session start and end. Tools: GDI/agent screenshots stay blind as today; fbshot's linear-overlay decode must be confirmed once.

G53.approach:
VERDICT: the gap is real, and fixable as a default-OFF performance switch. Full design: KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G53.md.

WHAT HAPPENS TODAY. Every DP2 call starts with prepared = 0 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1835). So the first triangle reruns compute_regs and re-sends the whole target and state:
- VcrDd3dTarget: 6, 7 or 9 writes.
- VcrDd3dState: 8 FBI writes, 4 TMU0, 4 TMU1, and a nop for DXT.
- In total 15-26 uncached writes and 2-4 status reads (58 writes with a fog reload).
- The same happens after every state change. TEXTUREHANDLE (:1400-1405) and TEXTUREMAP (:1600-1604) set dirty even when the handle is unchanged.
- Every clear forces it again (:1419-1420), and Clear2 re-sends the target per rectangle (:1890-1899).

Something the perf report did not note: 11 (16 bpp) or 13 (32 bpp) of those writes are SPEC 'sync' registers (L2225: "flush the data pipeline before loading the register"). They are fbzMode, fogColor, c0, c1, renderMode, the stencil pair, the colour/aux buffer address and stride, and the clip. So every DP2 call and every texture bind also drains the pixel pipeline, while a pure bind only needs TMU registers, all non-sync.

Today the cost is small. Inferred from the 11-12 rings: 30-43 DP2 calls per frame, and at most 42-129 binds per frame, come to ~0.2-0.5 ms per frame. That is under 1% of UT2003's 123 ms frame, which the triangle path dominates. It is 2-10% once G47-G49 bring frames to 15-25 ms.

FIX: Diag\D3DShadow, read at boot, any chip, default OFF.

(1) KMD/include/vcr_3dshadow.h (new, Win32-free, host-tested). It holds a per-PDEV write-through record of chip 0's 3D registers:
- an explicit table of 22 registers / 26 slots, each with the SPEC 'Chip' kind:
  - FBI-only;
  - FBI+TREX% (fbzColorPath);
  - per-TMU TREX* (textureMode/tLOD/tDetail/texBaseAddr), decoded from chip field bits 13:10 (0 = FBI and both TMUs, 0x800 TMU0, 0x1000 TMU1).
- the functions note, need, filter (order kept), forget, taint and audit.
- Commands, vertex and parameter registers, and the fog table (which keeps G41's keyed cache) are never recorded or skipped.
- Values are compared whole, which is G33's 'compare tLOD whole'.
- Built-in rules for later items:
  - SPEC L6236's 2PPC rule: TMU writes reach both TMUs (for G50);
  - a chipMask without chip 0 forgets everything (for G03).

(2) vcrdd_3d.c gets a recording writer, w3r: the same single store as w3, then vcr_sh_note when armed.
- Target, state, clear (fbzMode/c1/zaColor/clip) and texture flush (all three texBaseAddr writes) use it. Vertices, commands and the fog table keep w3.
- So every writer describes itself, with no list of who clobbers what:
  - the clear's c1/fbzMode/zaColor/clip (G14/G22/G35's constraints) hold by construction;
  - the flush's chip-field-0 texBaseAddr is recorded on BOTH TMUs. In two-stage mode TMU0 is then re-written exactly as today's full re-send does.

(3) Bit 0 (skip). VcrDd3dTarget/VcrDd3dState branch early into target_sh/state_sh. The proven bodies stay below unchanged, apart from w3 -> w3r.
- The shadowed path builds the same write lists from new pure builders in vcr_3dseq.h (vcr3d_regs moves there; vcr_3d_state_fbi_seq/_tmu_seq).
- It filters them against the record and emits them with Reset3D's chunked VcrDdRoom: k = 0 costs no status read.
- The DXT nop is sent only when a TMU write follows. That still covers Glide's transition rule (gtex.c:2978-2983).
- A CALL BARRIER keeps the old path's first write per call. The first target emission of each DP2/Clear2 call always issues the sequence's first write (renderMode; colBufferAddr on a V3), because it is not known whether a 3D sync register orders an in-flight 2D blit (SPEC §20.3 needs a 2D NOP for the other direction). Cost: ~30-43 writes per frame.
- Precise binds: TEXTUREMAP/TEXTUREHANDLE set dirty only on a changed handle. TEXTUREHANDLE compares against c->tex_handle, the binding it aliases with TSS TEXTUREMAP, not rs[] (the RS 5 -> TSS 7 -> RS 5 case).
- Unchanged on purpose:
  - compute_regs at every call;
  - target_of at every call;
  - prepare()'s per-call FVF edits;
  - clear_rects' dirty + prepared = 0 (G22's chain).

(4) Forget points, VcrDd3dForget = vcr_sh_forget + G41's VcrDdFogForget:
- GETLINEARADDR and GET_SLAVE_REGS TAINT the PDEV: a user-mode Glide writer exists, so the PDEV never skips again. That is always Glide's own PDEV (G41 Fact 2).
- HWCSETEXCLUSIVE.
- HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE, before RESTORE_MODE.
- The end of VcrDdGlideReset3d: its wr() at vcrdd_2d.c:422 is the one unrecorded 3D writer.
- UNMAP_MEMORY.
- SLI_AA_REQUEST, which vcrctl sliaa sends outside a session.
- DrvAssertMode, both directions.
- VCR_ESC_RESET_ENGINE.
- A successful VCR_ESC_REG MMIO write.
- give_up().
- VcrDd2dInit.
- G01/G02's resets, instead of fog_valid = 0.
- PCI, CLOCK (pllCtrl1 only), SNAPSHOT (reads only) and the rest are classified 'no 3D write', and a test pins the split.
- XP gives every mode change and every Glide session a new zeroed PDEV, so cross-API cases start empty.

(5) Bit 1 (audit). Today's writes unchanged, plus at every DP2/Clear2 call a VcrDd2dSync and a read-back of the 15 readable recorded registers against the record. A mismatch logs 513/46 once and forgets the slot. On silicon these registers already read back what D3D wrote (regs_after_windowed_1009).

G53.risk:
With the switch off: none to proven paths. Register traffic is byte-for-byte (stores, order and VcrDdRoom checks), pinned by Python and native tests. CPU cost: one not-taken branch per state write (not per vertex), the forget calls (PDEV fields) and a few counter adds per state change.

With it on:
- Default 16 bpp lane: fewer writes; covered by matrix M at 16 bpp.
- D3D32/BigTex lane: the DXT nop is now sent only when a TMU write follows. That is still a superset of Glide's switch-to-compressed rule.
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence:
  - Glide never runs on a D3D PDEV (a new PDEV per Glide session, G41 Facts 1-2);
  - every Glide escape forgets, and a mapped PDEV is tainted;
  - the Q3 step in boots A and B checks it.
- SLI: none today (D3D draws on chip 0 only); G51 must forget around SLI.
- Flip path: none. Flips write no 3D register, the target is still read at every call, and shadow_frames checks it.
- 2D/DirectDraw ordering: the call barrier keeps the old first-write per call, because it is unproven whether a 3D sync register orders an in-flight 2D blit.

G56.approach:
VERDICT: the drain is real but nearly free on today's transport, and it is NOT what makes Halo's intros slow.

1. Why the drain is cheap.
   - VcrDd2dSync returns at once when nothing was queued since the last sync (vcrdd_2d.c:121-122).
   - Every Dd_Flip drains before it flips (vcrdd_ddraw.c:334), so a Lock between a Present and the next draw costs nothing.
   - A mid-frame Lock waits only for what the 31-entry PCI FIFO holds: 1-2 triangles or one clear, plus 3 status reads.
   - Uploads are rare in every game measured on this HAL. The per-context 'texture flushes' counter reads UT2003 42 (245 s), UT2004 63, Halo timedemo 77 (ONBOX ring lines).
   - The 7-write TMU flush costs a few µs and is required by SPEC §20.3. It stays.

2. Why Halo is slow: a software stretch. Read from the staged halo.exe (md5 b7aa8f68, movie function 0x43ed20-0x43f003):
   - Setup: CreateOffscreenPlainSurface(640, 480, X8R8G8B8, DEFAULT) and GetRenderTarget(0).
   - Each frame: LockRect(flags 0); BinkCopyToBuffer (32-bit, writes only); UnlockRect; StretchRect(→ the 1280x960 back buffer, D3DTEXF_NONE); Present (0x518180 → vtable +0x44).
   - Our Dd_Blt hands every stretch back (vcrdd_ddraw.c:529-532), yet the 09-28 frames show the movie stretched 2x. So the runtime stretched on the CPU, reading video memory through the write-combined user view (vcrmp_dd.c:28-29). Uncached reads (inferred).
   - No engine work is queued in that loop, so its Locks never wait.
   - The rate fits: 1109 intro frames (37 s from the Bink headers); 09-28 screenshot times bound Bungie + Gearbox to 0.48-0.67 s a frame (14-20x slow). That fits 0.3-1.2 M uncached reads a frame, not the Lock.

PART A (investigation, no driver behaviour change):
- E1 `d3d9probe movie9`: Halo's loop call for call, each phase QPC-timed, picture verified via GetRenderTargetData. Run at 1280x960 and at 640x480 (same-size = our 2D copy).
- E1b `vramread9`: sequential and 2x2-repeat reads give t_read.
- E2 Halo itself without -novideo at -vidmode 1280x960 vs 640x480 (150 s cap, WM_CLOSE).
- E3 one TRACE ring slice: the Blt flags and the Lock pattern; it shows whether d3d9 even sends the stretch to DdBlt.
- E4 counters in G46's D3DStats: Locks by kind, waits, Blt hand-backs by reason x source-in-VRAM. These also check the Bink/Smacker paths of RF, BF1942, AvP, R6, Shogo, SS2, Thief Gold and Max Payne.
- Outcomes: if the stretch dominates, the Halo fix is G61's 2D screen-to-screen stretch blt (SPEC §7.3.2; vendor DDBLT32.C:1267-1270, caps DDINIT.C:256/339-342). If the Lock is ≥ 10 ms, find what was queued.

PART B (the scoped-wait fix): new Win32-free header include/vcr_inflight.h.
- The set: up to 16 [lo,hi) video-memory spans tagged R/W, an overflow flag, an epoch, and g2d_ops_at_idle.
- vcr_infl_must_wait(lo, hi, cpu_writes) waits on any of:
  - overflow;
  - an unknown size;
  - a 2D op since idle (the existing g2d_ops counter, so vcrdd_2d.c's ops are untouched);
  - any overlapping span with cpu_writes or W.
- Spans are noted in vcrdd_d3d.c:
  - prepare() after Target+State, and again when the epoch changes: target W, Z W, each bound texture's TMU span R (vcr_tex_chain_offset / mip_offset of all levels — G07-safe);
  - clear_rects: target and Z W;
  - flush_written: the texture W.
- VcrDd2dSync empties the set after its idle loop (one line).
- Dd_Lock, after the unchanged flip_from check:
  - a system-memory surface returns NOTHANDLED with no sync;
  - a non-conflicting span skips;
  - otherwise the unchanged VcrDd2dSync.
- TEXBLT's two syncs use the same rule, per level.
- Under a Glide owner (exclusive_pid), the old full drain.
- It never relaxes WAR, RAW, 2D, unknown size or overflow. It is stricter than 3dfx's own DdLock, which skipped the WAR wait (VH5/DDSURF.C:1614-1620).
- The gain on PIO is small and measured first in shadow mode. It is needed for G47: a CMDFIFO drain stalls a whole frame.

PART C (after G47, Diag D3DTexPkt5):
- TEXBLT as packet 5 (LFB space first, the vendor TEXPORT form 0x3a00000 as fallback), ≤0x4000 dwords per packet, sfence per chunk.
- The SPEC §20.3 flush (2D NOP, inverted texBaseAddr, nopCMD, rewrite, 2D NOP) in the FIFO.
- Lock fences by FIFO serial: a 2D-NOP pixel flush plus a packet-5 LFB write of a serial to a reserved dword. readPtr alone is not completion.
- PIO texture-port writes were considered and rejected: 27-90 MB/s against a WC memcpy.

The record the gap and both reports rest on (games-32, history-28) stops when the README/FINDINGS paragraph was written (d0e6af7, 09-27 00:43). Three later silicon results appear in no doc:
(1) SIL/vcrkmd-v5-7.jsonl (09-27 21:48): the same battery order as the 09-26 runs (16 bpp first, the only depth change, 60 frames), same monitor, same 800x600@85. Result: 87.4 flips/s, first-to-last 86.1, slow_frames 0, max frame 14.6 ms.
(2) SIL/vcrkmd-256-1.jsonl (09-27 23:10): 102.6 / 101.3 flips/s at 100 Hz.
(3) ONBOX/ring_after_probes_decoded.txt:192-193 (11-12, build 95678704): D3D8 perf at 640x480x16@85 with vsync made 85.1 fps. 511/12 logged "flips 300: retrace 297, deadline 2, pending 1"; 511/13 logged 262,965 reads, longest 1228 us. These are the first silicon flip counters, and they are healthy.

The 42.1 and 46.9 runs (v5-2, v5-6) used 09-26 builds and a ddlab without per-frame timing. Their flip rule is code-identical to today's. The rule bounds a DDLOCK_WAIT spinner at about 1/1.125 of the refresh or better, for any poll cadence and either flag sense, so those runs lost 0.50-0.65 s outside the rule. The data cannot say whether that was one stall or every frame. v5-2 also measured vblank_hz 87.6 (85.0 everywhere else), which suggests its timing was disturbed.

VENDOR FINDING (G59 depends on it; it is not G59's cause): every 3dfx display driver XORs status[6] with the vsync polarity from Misc Output bit 7. That covers the H5 drivers for W2K, NT4 and Win9x (VH5/DDFLIP.C:1031-1069, DDFXNT.C:654-656) and the Mac Avenger driver ("positive sync, trigger on rising edge"). Our miniport reads "clear = retrace" at every mode, as Glide and 86Box do. The desktop mode 1280x1024@85 and 800x600, 1024x768 and 1280x960 at 85 Hz all have positive vsync. If the vendor is right, our in_vblank is inverted at those modes. That leaves the flip rate unchanged, but it inverts GetScanLine, TESTVB and GetRasterStatus, and a flip written inside the sync pulse completes one frame early.

PLAN:
(a) Correct the docs: README:669-682 and 797-799, FINDINGS, PLAN step 16, tests/README:248.
(b) E1, one session on the deployed build, 16 paced switches, no Diag change, no reboot:
- ddlab vbduty on the desktop (no switch) to settle the polarity question;
- the exact 09-26 cell first, then 600-frame runs in both orders at 800x600 16 and 32 bpp, 640x480x16 (negative vsync) and 1280x960x16 (positive vsync, 35 us pulse);
- d3dprobe vsync at 640x480x16 and 1280x960x16;
- read the ring after each run. Outcomes map to a decision table in the design (stall, missed pulses, a second retrace, the vendor polarity model, a flag that covers the whole blank).
(c) Logging-only counters in vcr_flip.h, logged as 511 a=15/16: NOVSYNC presents; a 6-bucket histogram of present-to-present time in nominal frames; waits and total wait time. The owner is now named for NOVSYNC presents too, so another process's teardown can no longer cut a live NOVSYNC session. These counters let any session, a game included, show whether it is limited by the driver, limited by the game, or has no vsync.
(d) E2: real 16 bpp titles with vsync on (JK/MotS/Shogo at 1280x960x16, R6/SS2/Thief Gold/AvP at 640x480x16), riding on G73's sweep. That boot sets Diag\LogEntries=16384, because the 1024-entry ring is overwritten by each game's own CreateSurfaceEx teardown. That is why no game counters exist today.

CONTINGENT, only on that evidence: F2a FlipDeadline A/B (exists); F2b direct status read (G60); F2c complete flips on the chip's swap-pending count (swapBufferPend + swapbufferCMD at vsync), as the vendor does (G54); F-P polarity-correct sense behind a new Diag\VblankSense, default off, to be filed as its own P2 item if E1 confirms the vendor's model.

G59.d3dprobe_test:
Name: d3dprobe vsync (test key vsync_rate), a new fullscreen mode: d3dprobe vsync [--res WxH] [--bpp 16|32] [--frames N] [--hz N] [--work-us N].

Device: D3DSWAPEFFECT_FLIP with 1 back buffer; FullScreen_PresentationInterval = D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_ONE; FullScreen_RefreshRateInHz = --hz (default 85).

Raster measurement first: 0.5 s of polling IDirect3DDevice8::GetRasterStatus, which goes through the HAL's GetScanLine. This gives raster_hz (the median period between InVBlank rising edges) and invb_duty.

Then 600 frames, each:
- a target-only Clear that alternates two colours;
- one 64x64 checker-textured quad (2 triangles, MODULATE);
- Present, with a QPC stamp after each Present.

RESULT fields: present_hz, present_hz_first_last, raster_hz, ratio, first/max/min frame ms, slow (>1.5 R), two_frame (1.5-2.5 R), fast (<0.5 R), invb_duty, sense, work_us.

PASS (work 0):
- 0.98 <= ratio <= 1.02 against the measured raster rate. Reference values: the 11-12 d3dprobe perf made 85.1 fps at 85 Hz (ratio 1.00); the v5-7 ddlab made 86.1 flips/s first-to-last at vblank_hz 85.0 (ratio 1.013).
- slow + two_frame <= 3 of 600.
- fast <= 1.
- raster_hz within 1% of the nominal rate; otherwise the result is "inconclusive".
- At 16 bpp, and at 32 bpp where D3D32 is armed (otherwise skipped): |ratio16 - ratio32| <= 0.02.

Run at 640x480x16@85 (negative vsync) and 1280x960x16@85 (positive vsync, 35 us pulse).

Reported but not gated until F-P is decided: sense = pulse (<2%), blank (2-10%), inverted (>90%).

Informational: --work-us 12353 (1.05 R) should give about 0.889 R with FlipDeadline off and >= 0.94 R with it on. That is the PLAN step-16 A/B, run on the D3D path.

Companion check, ddlab vbduty (no mode switch): the GetVerticalBlankStatus duty plus GetScanLine samples on the desktop.
G59.on_box_verification:
E1 on .124: deployed 95678704, Diag unchanged with FlipDeadline read back absent, box idle, no Glide session since boot (or cmdFifo0 read off, per G01). 16 paced switches, about 12 minutes, no reboot.

Steps:
0. Fetch the ring as a baseline (vcrlog.py fetch).
1. ddlab vbduty on the 1280x1024x32@85 desktop (positive vsync, no switch). A duty of about 0.28% means our sense is right; about 99.7% means the vendor's polarity model holds (inverted here); about 4.5% means the flag covers the whole blank.
2. The 09-26 cell as the first fullscreen run: ddlab_run.py 192.168.1.124 flip --res 800x600 --bpp 16 --frames 60, then --bpp 32.
3. 600-frame runs in reverse order: 800x600x32, then 800x600x16.
4. 640x480x16 for 600 frames (negative vsync) and 1280x960x16 for 600 frames (positive vsync).
5. d3dprobe vsync at 640x480x16 and 1280x960x16, 600 frames each.
6. Read the ring after each run: 511/12-13, and 511/15-16 once deployed.

PASS, which closes G59 as not reproduced:
- every 16 bpp run at >= 0.98 of the measured refresh first-to-last;
- slow_frames <= 0.5%;
- the 60-frame 09-26 cell at >= 83 flips/s;
- 511/12 by_retrace >= 95% for the ddlab spinner;
- 16 bpp within 2% of 32 bpp.

IN GAME: after the counters ship with the next vcrdd.dll deploy, on G73's sweep boot with Diag\LogEntries=16384:
- Jedi Knight DF2 in a level at 1280x960x16@85 (positive vsync, the shortest pulse);
- Rainbow Six at 640x480x16@85 (the negative-vsync control).

Run each for 2 minutes or more, exit cleanly, and fetch the ring right after. Expect 511/12 retrace + deadline = flips. The 511/16 '~1' bucket should dominate if the game holds 85; if it does not, the slower buckets should show waits ~0 (the game's own frame time). The '~2' bucket must never dominate with waits ~ flips (that would mean the driver is limiting).

G51.approach:
Verdict: the gap is real and fixable, and it is the largest fill item in the stack. Glide measured 330.2 Mpix/s on one chip and 1124.6 on four (EV/glidelab/vcrkmd-paced-2.jsonl:1,4). But it buys nothing today. The first D3D game numbers are transport-bound, not fill-bound: UT2003 flyby spends 116.7 ms of a 123 ms frame in DrawPrimitive at 640x480x16, and UT2004 runs 4-6 fps at 1280x960 (onbox/session_log.md). So this is last and supervised (P9), after G46/G78 measurement, G47 CMDFIFO, G48/G49, G50 2PPC and G54 swap queue.

Shape: only the proven Glide cfg-5 shape. 4 chips, SLI, AA off, analog, Glide's per-mode band (8/2/32/16/4 lines at 640x480/800x600/1024x768/1280x960/1600x1200), so packed height = h/4. It is programmed by the kernel's existing vcr_sli_set_ex(io, req, 0), which ran Quake II 4-chip at every mode at 16 and 32 bpp. The request is built with dwChips = glide_chips and aaEn = sampleHigh = 0, by construction.

Memory: our desktop/heap are linear, and DirectDraw rotates the chain's blocks every flip (the GDI desktop block becomes a render target). So D3D renders the fullscreen flip chain into PRIVATE packed TILED buffers P(B), one per chain block, plus P(Z). They are allocated from DirectDraw's heap with HeapVidMemAllocAligned (as mipchain_ext does), shown by the VIDEO OVERLAY (desktop off, overlay tiled; register values copied from Glide's cfg-5 golden), and flipped with leftOverlayBuf + swapbufferCMD. Completion is swap-pending = 0 on every chip. Everything else stays linear and is replicated by memBase1 snooping.

Per render target (VH5/D6DP2.C:6027-6081), via the new vcr_d3dsli_target_prefix in VcrDd3dTarget, emitted after G03's baseline:
- chain target: chipMask=1/sliCtrl=s0 .. chipMask=8/sliCtrl=s3, then chipMask=ALL, with the kernel's vcr_sli_slictrl words (e.g. 0x060F0030..0x060F3030 for 16-line bands);
- any other target: sliCtrl=0, so render-to-texture is rendered whole by every chip;
- colBufferStride/auxBufferStride = 0x8000|tiles.

Clears: a full-target clear writes sliCtrl=0, clip bottom = Hp, fastfill, then the prefix again (VH5/D7DP2.C:883-940). All four chips fill in parallel, which avoids the FASTFILL SLI speed bug. Partial clears are plain fastfill under SLI.

Textures: replicated lazily at bind by an SLI generation stamp (read + write back through the linear lower half). The TMU flush and texture-port write-back go through the broadcast transport.

Lock/Blt/GetDC of chain blocks: resolve P(B)->B through the SLI tiled aperture, placed in the UPPER half of memBase1 with lfbMemoryTileCompare (TileCompare = 32 MB | bit 15, TileCtrl base T chosen so every chain buffer's aperture lies in [32,64) MB; vendor SLI_HwPtrToLfbPtr maths, pure function vcr_d3dsli_layout). The desktop and heap keep their linear addresses. Upload on Unlock. More than 8 resolves in 2 s demotes the session to one chip. A full-surface COLORFILL becomes an SLI clear; any other chain Blt demotes.

Transport (experiment E1 decides; SPEC L5426 contradicts the vendor's practice):
- T-A: snooped memBase0 PIO with all-chip credit room/idle checks over slave register VAs (new IOCTL_VCR_SLI_REGS);
- T-B: G47's CMDFIFO with per-chip readPtr room (VH5/CFIFO.C:266-391).

Kernel (new IOCTL_VCR_D3DSLI):
- enable = the cfg-5 request; then per chip, save and write both lfbMemoryConfig halves and copy the master's CLUT; flushed Diag\D3DSliLive=1;
- disable = per-chip lfbMemoryConfig restore, then VcrSliOff;
- VcrSliOff with owner D3D also restores lfbMemoryConfig (protects Glide's later SLI LFB access);
- a boot guard disarms D3DSli after a death with D3DSliLive=1.

Promotion is in D3d_ContextCreate. Eligible only if: exclusive, a primary flip chain of 2+ buffers, screen-sized, 16/32 bpp, no doublescan, no Glide owner, the engine alive, no stale CMDFIFO on any chip, band legal, layout feasible, allocation OK.

Demotion from: DrvAssertMode(FALSE), DrvDisableDirectDraw, SetExclusiveMode(0), FlipToGDISurface, DestroySurface of a chain block, the last ContextDestroy/DestroyDDLocal, HWCSETEXCLUSIVE, an engine give-up, and the lock policy. A demoted context stays single-chip.

Stages: S1 (bit 0) = the whole machinery on one chip; S2 (bit 1) = four chips; bit 2 = fast clears; S3 = band tuning. No caps change; single pass; with the switch absent the register traffic is byte-identical. Not done: AA, 2-chip SLI, windowed SLI, 2D-engine SLI blits, per-chip LOD bias (needs G26), a tiled GDI desktop. Interim with no driver change: stage the fill-heavy 32 bpp titles at 1024x768. G51.d3dprobe_test:
New explicit tests in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c (never in the default gate). Full-frame readback (lifts G74's 256x256 window), dither off, exact match for flat colours, +-1 where interpolated. RESULT reports bad_rows and bad_per_chip, owner = (y >> band) & 3, computed in the probe with no escape.

- slibands: every scanline y drawn as a 1-px quad of colour C(y) = 565 (R5 = y&31, G6 = (y>>5)&63, B5 = 21), unique per row below 2048 at both depths. Then a full-screen top->bottom gouraud quad. Pass: 0 bad rows at x = 1, w/2, w-2; gradient continuous across band edges.
- slitex: a 256x256 texture whose rows encode v, MANAGED (TEXBLT) and DEFAULT via UpdateTexture, sampled full-screen point; then rewritten (Lock/Unlock) and redrawn. Pass: every row correct before and after (catches stale slave copies and unflushed slave TMUs).
- slirtt: stripes rendered into a 256x256 render-target texture, then sampled full-screen. Pass: every row correct (catches sliCtrl not 0 on a non-chain target). SKIPPED if no RT texture is offered (G36).
- sliclear: a full clear; partial clears straddling bands and chips (y 37..136); a Z-only full clear followed by a LESS test. Pass: every row computed; the Z test leaves the first colour everywhere.
- sliz: near-then-far and far-then-near full-screen quads, LESSEQUAL. Pass: the near colour on every row.
- slilock: draw, Lock, write colour K into rows 100-163, Unlock, Present, Lock again. Pass: rows 100-163 = K and every other row its stripe (resolve and upload).
- perf --mode fill (G78): 8 full-screen textured quads per frame, novsync diagnostic and vsync. Pass: S2 >= 3.0x S1 Mpix/s at 1280x960x16; the Glide reference is 3.4x.
G51.risk:
Default 16 bpp path: none. With the switch absent no code runs, and the register traffic is byte-identical (pinned by tests).

Box stability:
- Every SLI/AA wedge on record was an AA configuration or an AA LFB read. The non-AA cfg-5 shape has run clean under Glide at every mode.
- New exposure:
  - overlay promotion from a DirectDraw context;
  - the lfbMemoryTileCompare split (shipped by 3dfx, ENABLE_NAPALM_SLI_EXTRA_LINEAR_HEAP=1, never run by us);
  - non-AA SLI LFB reads through it;
  - all-chip room checks. A missed one could overflow a slave FIFO (inferred: lost writes or a hang), which G02 must surface.
- Mitigations: supervision, flushed phases, the D3DSliLive auto-disarm.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence:
- The miniport SLI state is shared. D3D refuses promotion while a Glide owner exists, demotes at HWCSETEXCLUSIVE, and the owner is logged.
- Glide's cfg-5 path is not changed (same function, flags 0).
- The real hazard is a slave lfbMemoryConfig left with TileCompare bit 15. It would misplace Glide's later SLI LFB accesses. It is closed by a per-chip restore in every exit path, including VcrSliOff at mode set and display reset (pinned by a mock test).

SLI state: the teardown is the same VcrSliOff every mode set already runs.

Flip path: the desktop flip is unchanged when not promoted. The overlay swap is new (G54 + the overlay target).

Monitor: no new mode switch; layers change, timing does not. Slave video processors are cycled at the enable, as at every Glide SLI open.

Memory: 0.6-7.8 MB per chip of private chain buffers on top of DirectDraw's chain. An allocation failure keeps the title single-chip, never broken.

Visible behaviour changes while promoted:
- the hardware cursor is hidden;
- lock-heavy titles drop to one chip after about 8 resolves.

Performance risk: no gain where frames are CPU, software-T&L or setup bound (every chip sets up every triangle).

Is the tile-compare translation relative to TileCtrl, as the vendor's SLI_HwPtrToLfbPtr implies? Do SLI LFB reads work above a TileCompare at 32 MB on .124 (E4)?
Are UT2003/2004, Halo, Thief II and H&D fill-bound once G47-G50 land, or bound by software T&L on the Athlon XP 2400+ (E2)? A CPU-bound title gains nothing.

G55.approach:
Measure first, then fix in the driver. Full design: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G55.md

FACTS (today)
- Dd_Flip (vcrdd_ddraw.c:315-361) drains the engine, writes vidDesktopStartAddr directly through IOCTL_VCR_DDFLIP (vcrmp_dd.c:65-80), sets pd->flip_from (:358) and returns at once. The chip latches the new address at the next vsync, up to 11.76 ms later at 85 Hz.
- XP re-targets rendering with SETRENDERTARGET (test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:7-13), so the next frame's Clear2 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1416) and DP2 triangles (prepare(), :1361) write at once into the buffer still being scanned out.
- Only Lock (:652-657) and Blt (:500-504) honour flip_from, although vcrdd.h:94 says "not to be drawn on yet".
- CANRENDERAFTERFLIP is advertised (:2068). hal.md:221 rated it OK, but only for the pre-flip drain.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY REAL
- 3dfx's own HAL gets this right because its hardware is in order. It queues swapbufferCMD in the command FIFO (VH5/DDFLIP.C:257-297, 394-447), and SPEC §8.83.4 (L4060) says a vsync'd SWAPBUFFER blocks the command processor in double-buffer mode. That is why its GetFlipStatus answers OK for 3D (DDFLIP.C:701-718).
- Both Microsoft W2K DDK sample D3D drivers handle it in the driver, and neither reports the cap.
  - S3 ViRGE: DP2 returns the flip status when the render target is the flipped-from surface (s3virge/d3ddx6.c:153-166), and Clear spins (:2006-2009).
  - Permedia 2: the flip is queued in the input FIFO as SuspendUntilFrameBlank (3dlabs/driver/dd.c:451-458).
- What could hide it: the D3D8 runtime might wait itself, through GetFlipStatus (one wrapper in d3d8.dll, callback slot 0x4c, callers not traced) or a back-buffer Lock throttle.
- No flicker has been reported, but no in-game D3D scene has been watched.
- Visibility model: a fast frame (draws done inside the 0.55 ms back porch) is invisible. A GPU-bound frame shows a partly drawn picture on most refreshes. Neither GDI nor fbshot can see it.

INVESTIGATION
Shared infrastructure:
- New pure-logic header include/vcr_raf.h.
- One hook just before the first colour write of each DP2 (prepare(), before VcrDd3dTarget) and each colour Clear (clear_rects()). The pre-test needs no I/O: flip pending AND target == flip_from.
- Per flip it counts candidates, latched, hazard, certain (line witness), beam third, first-draw delay, and the GetFlipStatus/Lock calls in between (does the runtime wait?). Logged as 511 a=15/16 with the existing per-session flip counters.

Experiments:
- E0: `d3dprobe raster` (GetRasterStatus loop). Is vidCurrentLine a monotonic line counter on the VSA-100 (SPEC L4609)? No driver change needed.
- E1: counters plus `d3dprobe raf`, then UT2004 (D3D8), Halo (D3D9), Thief Gold (d3dim DX6) and Jedi Knight/MotS (DX5). Hazards on about every frame of --bb 1 means real. Zero hazards with GetFlipStatus/Lock calls at least once per frame means the runtime waits: close G55 as P3.
- E2 (optional): drop the cap, to see whether the runtime keys a wait on it. Information only, never the fix.
- E3: the user at the CRT, `raf --gap-us 5000`. A dark band over the top ~40 % is the hazard; uniform grey is the fix.
- E4 (optional): the vidCurrDesktopStartAddr read (SPEC L6609: write bit 31 to IO 0xfc, then read 0xfc). Would give an exact latch witness, and the first silicon test of vcr_flip.h's assumption.

FIX F1 (primary; the S3 pattern, no register write)
- In the hook, VcrDdFlipGuard waits in place until the latch. It polls status[6] directly from pjRegs (about 1 µs, catching the 35-69 µs pulse) and feeds vcr_flip_poll.
- Never early, and bounded by the flip deadline (13.24 ms at 85 Hz).
- Why wait in place and not return WASSTILLDRAWING: the target changes inside the stream, and the S3 sample also spins in Clear.
- Witness: W3, vidCurrentLine (L_now < L_flip, or a retrace seen, or elapsed ≥ a frame means latched), once E0 proves it. Otherwise today's rule, whose over-wait on frames that already missed a refresh is measured.
- NOVSYNC flips, windowed presents and triple-buffered chains are untouched.
- The caps do not change: the fix makes the cap true.
- Cost: the honest double-buffer rate. In the 18 ms GPU-frame model at 85 Hz, 55.6 fps (with corrupted frames) becomes 42.5 fps. Triple buffering (G65) gets the overlap back.

ALTERNATIVE F2 (the vendor/Permedia pattern; becomes G54's first half)
- After a vsync'd flip: VcrDdRoom(2), a direct write of 0 to swapPending (3D 0x24c), then swapbufferCMD (3D 0x128) = WAIT_ON_VSYNC|DONT_SWAP = 0x201. Bits 10:9 = 01: "count decremented, no video swaps occur" (SPEC L2720).
- Read back: status[30:28] must be ≥ 1, or the fence did not take.
- The command processor then blocks until the retrace (L4060), so every later draw is ordered behind the latch.
- status[30:28] == 0 becomes an exact flip-completion witness (the vendor's FXGETFLIPSTATUS).
- Preconditions: VSA-100; vsync; no Glide owner; cmdFifo0 off (G01); dramInit1[11] clear (triple-buffer mode does not block, L2724); no stale swap count; DPMS off.
- Stuck-fence watchdog: deadline plus one frame, then disarm and log.
- Pre-write pulse avoidance closes the vsync-start race.
- Costs: every Lock/TEXBLT drain waits for the vsync (the vendor's documented side effect), 2D work is held for up to a refresh, and the 2D DirectDraw titles are affected.
- Silicon only: 86Box ignores bits 9/10 and skips the vsync wait when its FIFO is full.
G55.gating:
New DWORD Diag\D3DFlipOrder. Absent or 0 is today's driver byte for byte: no new read, write, IOCTL or wait, and the same caps.
- It is read at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO and reaches the DLL as an appended vcr_info.d3d_flip_order field, read only when info.size covers it.
- It uses no flag-word bit, because 0x8000 is already claimed by other designs.
- One value per clean boot.

Bits:
- 0x01: counters only (reads, plus one witness sample per candidate).
- 0x02: F1 guard.
- 0x04: F2 fence. Exclusive with 0x02; if both are set, only 0x01 is kept.
- 0x08: the fence's swap count decides flip completion (only with 0x04).
- 0x10: experiment E2, withdraw CANRENDERAFTERFLIP. Never left armed.
- 0x20: W3, trust vidCurrentLine as a witness (only after E0 passes on that box).
- 0x40: experiment E4, the IO 0xfc select read in the miniport (a register write).

Default-on path:
- 0x01 may become default-on after boot A shows d3dprobe render 40/40 and perf within 1 % (the flip counters' precedent).
- F1 (0x02, with 0x20 if E0 passed) is safe to land default-on once proven. It is a pure correctness fix that changes no register write; its only effect is waiting, bounded by the flip deadline. Proof: E1 confirms the gap; one supervised boot with d3dprobe raf hazards 0 and E3 uniform grey; then the D3D title sweep with no hang.
- F2 (0x04/0x08) stays off and is folded into G54.

G55.risk:
Default path: none. With D3DFlipOrder absent the driver is byte for byte today's (no new read, write, IOCTL or wait; same caps); the tests pin it.

F1 (primary):
- Waiting only; the register stream is identical, so it cannot mis-draw or wedge the chip.
- A stall of up to one refresh inside DP2/Clear2 holds win32k's display lock. It is bounded by the flip deadline: 13.24 ms at 85 Hz, 18.75 ms at 60 Hz.
- Without the line witness, frames that already missed a refresh can be pushed one more refresh late. This is measured, and pinned by the host test.
- GPU-bound double-buffered titles drop to the honest double-buffer rate (model: 55.6 → 42.5 fps at 18 ms GPU frames and 85 Hz). The old rate showed corrupted frames.
- Untouched: NOVSYNC flips (the perf battery), windowed Blt-present, triple-buffered chains, DirectDraw-only titles, Glide/OpenGL, and SLI (no register access at all).

F2 (alternative):
- Two extra 3D writes per vsync'd flip on chip 0.
- Blocks the whole command processor, 2D and GDI included, for up to a refresh.
- Every Lock/TEXBLT/DrvAssertMode drain waits for the vsync; this hurts upload-heavy titles (Halo Bink, G56).
- Depends on dramInit1[11]: a 3-buffer Glide open can leave it set, and the fence is then refused and logged.
- A fence that never retires (no vsync) wedges the FIFO until SPIN_CAP gives up. DPMS is pre-checked; G02 makes the give-up visible.
- Possible one-frame-early release if vidDesktopStartAddr latches at vsync start and the write lands in the pulse. Mitigated by pre-write pulse avoidance; G54's leftDesktopBuf + SST_SWAP_DESKTOP_EN removes it.
- The 2D DirectDraw titles receive fences too.
- Glide/SLI: never written while exclusive_pid is set or cmdFifo0 is on. It leaves only fbiSwapHistory and the retrace counter changed. A stale chipMask (G03) shows as fence_untaken.
- The 86Box bed cannot validate it, because it ignores bits 9/10 and skips the vsync wait when its FIFO is full.
open_questions: Does XP's D3D8 runtime (and d3dim/d3dim700 for the DX5-DX7 titles) wait for the flip before Clear2/DP2? It could do so through GetFlipStatus (d3d8.dll callback slot 0x4c, callers not traced) or a back-buffer Lock throttle; E1's raf_gfs/raf_locks counters answer it. If it does, G55 is not a defect (P3). If it does not, promote the fix to P0.
Does any runtime key a wait on D3DDEVCAPS_CANRENDERAFTERFLIP (E2)? The DDK samples suggest it does not.
Is vidCurrentLine monotonic through active display on the VSA-100, and what does it read in the blank (E0)? This decides whether F1 gets an exact witness.

On this silicon, does a DONT_SWAP|WAIT_ON_VSYNC swapbufferCMD (0x201) block the command processor in double-buffer mode? Does it release at the start or the end of the retrace, relative to vidDesktopStartAddr's latch? This is the F2 race.
Is dramInit1[11] (triple buffer enable) ever left set on .124 after a Glide session? Read it before and after a 3-buffer Glide open.
Does vidCurrDesktopStartAddr (IO 0xfc, bit-31 select, SPEC rev 1.11) exist on this VSA-100 revision, and does writing 0 restore the overlay read that fbshot relies on (E4)?

Which staged titles present with a single back buffer, i.e. carry the hazard? Should G65 stage triple buffering (e.g. UE2 UseTripleBuffering) where the engine offers it, to recover the frame rate correct double buffering costs?
Does the D3D8 runtime retry a DP2 that returns DDERR_WASSTILLDRAWING (the S3 sample's pattern)? F1 does not need it; recorded for G54.

G58.approach:
VERDICT: the gap is real and fixable. It has two halves.
(1) Latent correctness. vertex() (KMD/display/vcrdd_3d.c:197-200) sends diffuse as four floats to sRed..sAlpha, which SPEC's register table lists as FBI-only (L2361-2364). Only packed sARGB is FBI+TREX* (L2360). So a TMU combine that selects iterated RGB/alpha can never see D3D's diffuse. No pixel is wrong today, because no TMU stage of ours selects iterated colour. It becomes wrong the moment G12 bit 8 does.
(2) Performance. Each vertex carries 3 extra colour writes, and a 2-stage vertex also carries a duplicate sOow1 (:218) that 3dfx never sends.

THE EVIDENCE IS STRONGER THAN THE GAP ASSUMED. Three sources:
(a) Packed sARGB already ran through THIS HAL on THIS silicon. Battery evidence/silicon/vcrkmd-v5-2 (2026-09-26 12:12) used the sARGB build; v5-3 (12:23) used the float build. Both ran before PARMADJUST. They failed the same 2 gouraud checks with byte-identical values (fffb00/ff00ff) and passed the same 34, including tex2mod/tex2add. The cause was PARMADJUST (commit d716d6f), not the transport.
(b) Our own OpenGL stack on .124 sends packed colour, and no per-TMU W, in every frame.
   - MesaFX defaults to FX_PACKEDCOLOR 1 (fxglidew.h:41-42, fxglidew.c:128-133), and our Glide then sets packet-3 bit 28 (gglide.c:5777, 6259).
   - Q0/Q1 are disabled (fxglidew.c:139-144), and a W hint is given only for projective formats (fxvbtmp.h:370-380). So _grUpdateParamIndex sets up neither W0 nor W1 (gglide.c:4558-4630), and both TMUs take W from Wb.
(c) SPEC says it outright. The packet-3 words are "Wbroadcast", "W0 Tmu 0 & Tmu1 W" and "W1 Tmu 1 W" (L4875-4879), and the register table has "sWtmu0 TREX0 & TREX1 W" (L2367). The vendor HAL always sends the raw D3DCOLOR to sARGB (D6TRI2I.C:1133-1134; PK3 packed=1, FIFOMGR.H:91-93), and never sets SST_SETUP_W1 (every hit clears it; D6MT.C:6013 sets ST1 only).

DESIGN.
- Two bits of Diag\D3DFastSetup. This is perf.md P3's switch, using G48's bit table and plumbing; whichever item lands first creates the plumbing. The DWORD is read at boot and carried whole in an appended vcr_info.d3d_fastsetup word. VcrDd2dInit must memset info before the IOCTL. pd->d3d_fast = g2d_ok ? word & VCR_FS_IMPLEMENTED : 0.
  - Bit 0 (0x01) VCR_FS_PACKED: one w3(V3D_SARGB, raw D3DCOLOR). D3DCOLOR is sARGB's own layout (SPEC 8.61).
  - Bit 4 (0x10) VCR_FS_W1SHARE: SM_W1 cleared and no sOow1 when W0 is set up and no TMU needs its own W.
  - Optional Part C, bit 7 (0x80) VCR_FS_PRUNE: Glide's own _grUpdateParamIndex rules, which G48 handed to this designer.
    * TMUs take W from Wb, i.e. W0/W1 are not set up, when the Wfbi sent equals rhw (no vertex-fog ramp, no W remap).
    * No Z when no depth test, depth write or Z-sourced fog/alpha reads it.
    * No Wfbi when the draw is untextured with no fog and no W-buffer.
    * It never drops a parameter a unit reads. vcr_vtx_facts is that contract, and G23/G31/G32/G92/G12 must extend it when they add a reader.
- ONE OWNER: a new integer, Win32-free header KMD/include/vcr_vtxplan.h.
  - vcr_vtx_setup(sm, fast, facts) turns compute_regs' sSetupMode into the bits a draw really sets up.
  - vcr_vtx_words(sm, packed) gives the dwords per vertex.
  - vcr_vtx_layout(sm, packed, reg[]) gives the registers, in packet-3 order (SPEC L4867-4882).
  - vcr_vtx_pk3_bits(sm, packed) gives packet-3 mask [21:10] and bit 28, for G47.
- prepare() (vcrdd_d3d.c:1322-1365) applies vcr_vtx_setup right before VcrDd3dState and sets w->d.sm/packed/vwords. vcr3d_draw gains these ULONG fields.
- vertex() writes exactly what d->sm says, packed or floats per d->packed, with room d->vwords+1. The sSetupMode the chip is given and the payload it gets therefore cannot disagree, on the direct path or in G47's packet 3.
- SWITCH OFF: byte-for-byte today's writes. With fast=0, vcr_vtx_setup is the identity, and prepare() already keeps d.textured <=> W0|ST0 and d.textured1 <=> W1|ST1.
- No caps change; single pass.
- A per-context payload counter (setup words / triangles, logged at ctx_free as a second event) gives on-box proof of what was actually sent.

EFFECT. Writes per triangle (0/1/2 stages, commands included):
- today: 27/36/45
- bit 0: 18/27/36
- bits 0+4: 18/27/33
- Part C: 15/24/30 with depth on; 12/21/27 with depth off.
Model: -9 to -18% of HAL bus time per triangle before G48. UT2003 flyby: 8.1 fps becomes about 8.6-11 fps from this alone (model); G46 pairs it with G48. It also unblocks G12 bit 8 (diffuse in TMUs, UT2003 combine 21), G13's diffuse modifiers, G25's TMU-iterator experiment, and G47's packed packet 3.

Fallback, ready: if tex2persp_fogv shows TMU1 takes Wb rather than W0 under vertex fog, W1SHARE gains '&& wfbi_is_rhw'. That is one line plus its native test.

Colour pruning (dropping sARGB when no unit reads iterated colour) is left to G12's combine compiler.

The full design is in KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G58.md.

G58.gating:
DEFAULT OFF at landing. Behind Diag\D3DFastSetup bits 0x01 (packed sARGB), 0x10 (TMU1 W from W0) and, optionally, 0x80 (Glide's parameter pruning).
- The bits are positive and read at boot (G48's convention).
- They are chip-generic, so the 86Box Voodoo3 bed can try bit 0; it is advisory for bits 4 and 7.

OFF PATH: register traffic stays byte-for-byte today's. A frozen-sequence native test, the Python pins and boot A's 40/40 prove it. The only off-path code changes are an identity call in prepare(), vertex() keyed on d->sm (equivalent by construction) and VcrDd2dInit's memset.

PROOF: one Diag change per clean boot. A = baseline, B = +0x01, C = +0x10, D (optional) = +0x80, each on top of whatever D3DFastSetup value G48 has already proven.

NOT safe to land default-on: it changes every vertex's bus traffic, and the project rule wants a supervised silicon proof first. It is, however, the best-evidenced change in the performance lane:
- v5-2 and v5-3 were identical on silicon;
- MesaFX/Glide run packed colour with inherited TMU W on .124 every frame;
- the vendor HAL and SPEC agree.

GRADUATION:
- Bits 0 and 4 can graduate to default-on in the commit after boots B and C pass, with their test change.
- Proposed convention for this word: absent = VCR_FS_DEFAULT (0x11), present = exactly its bits, 0 = the proven float path. This is the Accel2DPattern precedent; the choice is plan-level.
- Bit 7 graduates separately after boot D.

Host check of the geometry: 92 samples checked, 34 skipped near cell edges; 28 discriminate against an affine sampler and 26 against a TMU stuck at the fog-ramp Wb.

1) texpersp
   - Draws: quad [32,224)^2, left edge rhw 1.0, right edge rhw 0.25, u 0->1 left to right, v 0->1 top to bottom; checker(64, red, blue) with 8x8-texel cells, one level, point sampling, stage 0 SELECTARG1(TEXTURE); new helper quad_tp.
   - Reference: columns px = Q0+2..Q1-3 step 3, rows 45 and 69. t = (px-32)/192, u = 0.25t/(1-0.75t), s = 64u; skip a sample within 1 texel of a cell edge; expected red if (floor(s/8) + row) is even, else blue; tolerance 12.
   - Pass: 0 mismatches, plus a CPU self-check of at least 10 samples that discriminate against the affine model. RESULT reports checked/skipped/mismatches/discriminating.
   - Proves: perspective texturing on TMU0 (the first such check d3dprobe has), and TMU0 taking W from Wb under bit 7.
2) tex2persp
   - Draws: the same quad with two stages. The checker is stage 0, which TMU1 samples in our HAL; stage 1 is a solid white texture with MODULATE(TEXTURE, CURRENT).
   - Pass: the same parity scan with tolerance 16, 0 mismatches.
   - Proves: TMU1's W with SM_W1 clear (bit 4).
3) tex2persp_fogv
   - Draws: tex2persp plus vertex fog (FOGTABLEMODE NONE, specular alpha 0xff = no fog, fog colour green). Our HAL then sends Wfbi = the fog ramp's 1.0 while W0 = rhw.
   - Pass: identical to tex2persp, and no green anywhere.
   - Proves: TMU1 takes W0, not Wb; bit 7 keeps W0 under vertex fog.
4) iterexact
   - Draws: frame 1, the 4-colour gouraud quad (red/green/blue/white corners, Z and dither off); frame 2, two white bands blended SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA over black, alpha falling 255->0 in one and rising 0->255 in the other.
   - Reference: every one of the 36,864 pixels per frame against the analytic plane of its triangle (strip diagonal x+y=256; on the diagonal either triangle is accepted), quantised as the readback expands it; tolerance 9 at 16 bpp, 2 at 32 bpp.
   - Pass: 0 bad pixels. RESULT adds maxerr and a CRC32 of each frame's quad region.
   - Proves: packed = float colour, pixel-exact. The host compares boot B's CRC with boot A's: equal is expected (bytes 0-255 are exact floats).
5) zprune
   - Draws: frame 1, green full quad (depth on, z 0.3) then a red left half with ZENABLE FALSE at z 0.9; frame 2, the same, then a blue left half (depth on, z 0.2) and a white right half (depth on, z 0.6).
   - Pass: frame 1 (64,128) red and (180,128) green; frame 2 (64,128) blue and (180,128) green.
   - Proves: Z is set up again after a pruned, depth-off triangle (bit 7).

The existing default list (including tex2mod, tex2add, fogtable, fogvertex) still runs in every boot. Single-test sessions also check the HAL's payload counter: --tests tex2mod must log exactly 90/72/66/60 setup words for 0/0x01/0x11/0x91.
G58.risk:
Default 16 bpp path / fresh installs (bits absent): no traffic change. Writes stay byte-for-byte, pinned by the frozen native sequence, the Python pins and boot A. The off-path code is restructured, not changed in effect: vertex() is keyed on d->sm, which is equivalent because prepare() already keeps d.textured <=> W0|ST0 and d.textured1 <=> W1|ST1 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1340-1356).

Armed with a wrong rule: wrong pixels, never a hang. A direct register write cannot desynchronise the engine. The new probes name the parameter at fault: W0 -> texpersp, W1 -> tex2persp(_fogv), Z -> zprune, colour -> iterexact. Under G47's packet 3, the one-owner header rules out a header that disagrees with its payload.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence:
- The TMU colour latch now holds D3D's last colour. This is harmless: Glide and MesaFX send colour whenever a combine of theirs reads it (gglide.c:4507-4525).
- A stale Glide TMU combineMode that selects ITRGB (G03) would now see D3D's diffuse instead of a stale colour. That is G03's bug either way.
- G01's stale cmdFifo0 stops triangles on both paths alike. Verify from a clean boot.

SLI: none. D3D is chip 0 only with snooping off; a future G51 broadcast of sARGB is an ordinary FBI+TREX write.
Flip path: untouched.
2PPC (G50): no conflict; sARGB and W0 are broadcast anyway.
CPU: slightly less work. Four fewer x87 int->float conversions per vertex; the integer rule runs once per state change.

Part C prunes only parameters nothing reads. The PARMADJUST double-correction note (SPEC L2769) therefore affects only values no unit uses, and the facts contract must be extended by any later reader (G23/G31/G32/G92/G12).

86Box may disagree with silicon on W inheritance: the bed is advisory for bits 4 and 7.

Residual unknown: whether TMU1 takes W0 or Wb under vertex fog (U3). Settled by tex2persp_fogv; the fallback rule is ready.
games_unblocked: UT2003 (performance: about 18.5K HAL triangles a frame, two-stage lightmapped world; and, through G12 bit 8, combine 21 BLENDCURRENTALPHA, which needs diffuse inside a TMU)
Halo (performance: 26M triangles in one timedemo session)
every Direct3D title on .124 (fewer uncached bus writes per vertex; no pixel changes by design)
open_questions: U4: do the TMUs see iterated colour ONLY through sARGB, as the SPEC chip column implies? G12 bit 8's probe cells or the optional 'glidelab itrgb' experiment (float vs PARGB layout, TMU0 combine = ITRGB) settle it. If floats also reach the TMUs, G12 bit 8 need not wait for G58 and G58 is purely a performance change.
U3: with vertex fog (Wfbi = fog-ramp 1/W != rhw), does TMU1 take W0 or Wb when SM_W1 is clear? tex2persp_fogv decides; the fallback rule (W1 sharing only when wfbi_is_rhw) is ready.

Graduation convention for the multi-bit D3DFastSetup word: 'absent = default mask, present = exact bits, 0 = proven path', or a separate kill mask? This is plan-level, shared with G48/G49 and G05's D3DFeat question.

Colour pruning: dropping sARGB when no combine unit reads iterated colour/alpha would save one more word on SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) geometry such as UT2003's BSP world. It needs a 'needs iterated' output from G12's combine compiler. Owner: G12 or a later G58 follow-up?
Part C (bit 7, Glide's parameter pruning): keep it in G58 or give it its own gap id? It shares only the header and the switch.
Is the packed path's iterated colour bit-identical to the float path's (iterexact CRC, boot A vs boot B)? Expected yes, because bytes 0-255 are exact floats. If not, how large is the LSB difference?

Does a shorter vertex also shorten the setup unit's per-triangle time (7 or 16 clocks with subpixel correction, SPEC L2767), or only the bus? The perf --mode setup deltas divided by the change in writes will show it.
Final DD_D3D event codes for the arming and payload lines, and confirmation of bit numbers 0/4/7. G48's table reserves 0 and 4; 7 is the first free bit after G48's 5 and 6.

G60.approach:
G60 holds three items of very different weight. Design file: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G60.md

(1) PER-CALL SETUP IS REAL BUT NEGLIGIBLE. Each D3d_DrawPrimitives2 call (vcrdd_d3d.c:1821-1871) and D3d_Clear2 call (:1873-1900) does:
- EngSave/RestoreFloatingPointState (:1861/:1868);
- a memset of the ~112-byte dp2walk (:1835);
- target_of (:1852);
- fvf_layout (:1837).
That is about 0.5-1.5 us a call (inferred). At UT2003's 29.9 DP2 + 2 Clear2 calls a frame (G46) it comes to at most ~50 us a frame: 0.04% of a 123 ms frame and under 0.5% of an 85 Hz frame. The FPU bracket is a correctness requirement (the x87 code in vcrdd_3d.c/vcr_fog.c runs in the game thread's FPU context) and stays. 3dfx's NT HAL never saves the FPU state (0 hits, case-insensitive, over H5/W2K), but that is not evidence that dxg saves it for us. B1 is decided by measurement (M2, G46 fine mode: prologue, epilogue and the FPU pair bracketed). It is expected to close with no code change. Only if prologue+epilogue >= 1% of a 60-85 fps title's frame time: first a target_of fast path keyed on rt/zb fpVidMem/pitch/size, then field-by-field init instead of the memset. Never the FPU bracket.

(2) THE VBLANK IOCTL IS REAL, AND THE RING SHOWS IT. Every retrace read is IOCTL_VCR_VBLANK (vcrdd_ddraw.c:147-151 -> vcrmp_dd.c:81-103, which reads chip 0 status and vidCurrentLine). d3dprobe perf vsync at 640x480x16 made 262,965 reads for 300 flips (876 a flip) (ONBOX/ring_after_probes_decoded.txt:192-193). Single reads took 1,078-2,615 us; the vsync pulse they must catch is ~33-44 us at the staged 85 Hz modes (inferred). The 1024x768x32 run had 15/300 flips completed by deadline.
- B2 VBDIRECT: a new pure header include/vcr_vblank.h holds vcr_vb_in_retrace(status) = !(status & VCR_STATUS_VRETRACE), shared by the miniport handler and the DLL so the old inverted reading cannot return. New vblank_now(pd,v,line) reads *(pjRegs+VCR_R_STATUS), plus *(pjRegs+0x94)&0x7ff for GetScanLine, through the register window the DLL already maps (vcrdd_2d.c:480); without pjRegs (BOCHS/VM) it falls back to the IOCTL. flip_sample gains a poll argument: flip_done's polls (Flip-pending, GetFlipStatus, Blt/Lock of flip_from), WaitForVerticalBlank and GetScanLine read directly. Dd_Flip's one post-write sample keeps the IOCTL: it carries refresh_mhz for Diag\FlipDeadline and stays after the write. The flip rule, the flip IOCTL and every answer are unchanged. The WaitForVerticalBlank bound of 200000 reads becomes ~0.2-0.4 s instead of ~2 s, still more than 10 frames at >= 50 Hz.
- B3 VBSNOOP (optional; only if M1 shows D3D-pattern deadline flips): vcr_flip_snoop(s,in_vblank) in vcr_flip.h, fed by the status reads VcrDdRoom/VcrDd2dSync already make before every vertex. It runs only while a vsync'd flip is pending, adds no register read, and gives the same never-early argument as a poll. It catches the pulse while the app renders through it, so a title at 1.0-1.125 refreshes a frame flips at 1/r instead of the nominal rule's 0.889 cap. Superseded by G54.

(3) GLIDE'S ALPHA-TEST SKIP (B4 ASKIP) IS REAL SILICON BEHAVIOUR.
- What SPEC guarantees: a pixel failing the alpha test writes nothing to colour, alpha, depth or stencil, and fbiAfuncFail counts it (SPEC 8.23.1 L2913, L3667).
- The exactness argument: with A_s=0, RGB is unchanged iff the source factor is ZERO/SRCALPHA/SATURATE and the destination factor is ONE/INVSRCALPHA. The alpha channel, only where the target format defines it (DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS: never the X8R8G8B8 flip chain, whose X byte is undefined), needs ADST in {ONE, INVSRCALPHA}. Also required: Z writes off (FZ_ZAWRITE clear), no stencil writes, blend op ADD (fogMode[11:8]=0), and the app's own test off.
- New pure header include/vcr_askip.h: vcr_askip(alphaMode,fbzMode,fogMode,rt_alpha,stencil_writes) returns alphaMode with AM_ATEST|AM_AFUNC(4) and the ref cleared, or the input unchanged.
- Call site: compute_regs, under `if (c->pd->askip)`, after fogMode and before log_combo (:1027), so the logged am shows it. rt_alpha is a new vcr3d_target field set in target_of (or G28's VCR_BL_RT_ALPHA).
- Example: SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA goes 0x00045110 -> 0x00045119.
- Single pass, no caps change. Per-context counters plus a 513 INFO line at context destroy make it visible.
- The only differences from today, both toward the D3D reference: the undefined X byte of an X8R8G8B8 target is kept instead of zeroed, and 16 bpp dither drift on alpha-0 pixels disappears (inferred from MAME's blender model; the probe measures it).
- Its gain is unproven and is measured FIRST on today's driver (M3). The app's own ALPHATESTENABLE/GREATER/ref 0 programs exactly B4's register value, so a d3dprobe fill A/B of --atest gt0 vs always needs no driver change. UE2 already sets GREATER 0 itself on 8 of 12 blended UT2003 menu combines (am 45119/44119); B4 would cover the 3 logged as 45110.

MEASUREMENT FIRST. M1 adds log-only flip counters to vcr_flip.h: sum_poll (mean read), by_deadline split into deadline_polling vs deadline_idle, and by_snoop, logged as a new 511 line. M2 is per-call timing. M3 is the alpha-skip A/B. A decision table maps the numbers to B1-B4 (§3 of the design). With the switch absent, register traffic, IOCTL traffic and existing log lines are unchanged.

The gap is real but small. P3 overall: B1 most likely closes as 'measured, no change'.
G60.gating:
One new registry value, HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vcrmp\Diag\D3DTrim (DWORD). It is absent/0 by default, which means all off:
- bit 0 (1) VBDIRECT;
- bit 1 (2) VBSNOOP;
- bit 2 (4) ASKIP.

How it is read and transported:
- The miniport reads it at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO, in fill_info's per-INFO block (vcrmp.c:447-466, like DdHeapFloor), so a mode change picks it up and =0 is a kill switch without a reboot.
- The raw DWORD is appended to vcr_info as d3d_trim, which avoids the flag bit 0x8000 that five sibling designs already claim. If the integrator has created one appended D3D word (G46 d3d_perf, G05 d3dfeat), these become bits 16-18 of it instead.
- VcrDd2dInit zeroes info before the IOCTL and reads the field only when info.size covers it, so an older miniport means off.
- vb_direct and vb_snoop are set only when pjRegs is mapped (the Voodoo backend). askip is set on any chip: alphaMode is the same on Banshee, Voodoo3 and VSA-100, so the 86Box bed can exercise it first.

With D3DTrim absent, compute_regs' alphaMode, the IOCTL sequence, every register access and every existing log line are byte for byte today's. The Python tests pin both branches.

M1's new 511 flip-pacing line is log-only, with no hardware access. Like the existing flip counters it may land default-on.

Proof and promotion:
- One bit per supervised clean boot.
- A bit graduates to default-on (the miniport ORs a default mask, D3DTrim=0 becomes the kill switch, the Accel2DPattern precedent) only after its proof boot passes and one more ordinary session shows no regression.
- ASKIP additionally needs M3 to show a fill gain.
- None of it is safe to land default-on at first. It changes register values (ASKIP) and flip-completion timing (VBDIRECT/VBSNOOP) on paths that are proven today.
G60.d3dprobe_test:
NEW TEST `askip` (render mode, explicit, not in the default list). Run it at 16 bpp (R5G6B5+D16) and 32 bpp (X8R8G8B8+D24X8). It runs, and must pass, on today's driver too.

Setup:
- Texture: a 64x64 A4R4G4B4. Columns 0-31 have alpha 0 with a bright RGB (0xF0F); columns 32-63 have alpha 1-15.
- It is drawn over [Q0,Q1)=[32,224) at 3 px a texel, point-sampled, inside the 256x256 readback.
- It sits on an opaque gouraud background (0x204060 -> 0xc0a080).

Four renderings per case, each a fresh frame read back:
- BG: the background alone.
- A: the case state, with no alpha test.
- B: A plus ALPHATESTENABLE with ALPHAFUNC ALWAYS. The skip cannot apply, so this is today's result.
- C: A plus GREATER, ref 0. This is exactly B4's register value.

Cases:
1. SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, dither off.
2. The same with dither on.
3. SRCALPHA/ONE, dither on.
4. ZERO/INVSRCALPHA, dither on.
5. SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA bilinear over a 0|1 alpha-texel edge: interpolated alphas 1-16, the GREATER 0 boundary.
6. ONE/INVSRCALPHA (premultiplied, not eligible).
7. SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA with Z test and Z write on at z=0.3, then an opaque green quad at z=0.6.

Pass criteria, tolerance 0 on the expanded readback:
- P1 (cases 1-4): A==B on every pixel with texel alpha>0.
- P2 (cases 1-4): C==BG on every alpha-0 pixel. This is SPEC 8.23.1 on silicon.
- P3 (cases 1-5): A==B everywhere or A==C everywhere. Case 5 also requires B==C wherever C!=BG.
- Case 6: A==B everywhere.
- Case 7: the alpha-0 region == BG. Z was written and green is hidden, which proves the skip never applies with Z writes on.
- RESULT reports drift_old (B!=BG on alpha-0 pixels), drift_new (A!=BG there) and engaged (1 when A==C!=B, 0 when A==B!=C, else unknown). Engagement is confirmed by the per-context 513 'alpha-test skip on N of M state sets' line, or by G46's fbiAfuncFail.

PERF OPTIONS on G74/G78's `perf --mode fill`:
- --blend sa|add;
- --alpha0 PCT (a 256x256 A4R4G4B4 texture: the left PCT% of columns alpha 0, the rest 8/15, point-sampled);
- --atest off|gt0|always.

Reference value: with D3DStats on, sum(fbiAfuncFail) per frame == W*H*layers*PCT%. The Mpix/s A/B of gt0 vs always (identical colour math) is the measured value of the skip.

A Python source test pins the seven cases, the three states and tolerance 0 in d3dprobe.c.
G60.on_box_verification:
Rules that apply to every boot on .124, supervised:
- Read LICSTATUS/wpa before every reboot, and reboot only through scripts/fleet/safe-reboot.py.
- Deploy by swapping vcrdd.dll, plus vcrmp.sys for the D3DTrim read.
- One D3DTrim bit per clean boot: REGWRITE, then read it back.
- Never run vcrctl or ExtEscape while a D3D title runs. Fetch the ring (vcrlog.py) only after the title exits.
- Space mode switches at least 5 s apart (d3dprobe --pace 5000).
- Every session starts from a clean engine (G01: cold boot or vcrctl modeseq, cmdFifo0 off, d3dprobe render 40/40).

BOOT 0, measurement only (the G60 build with D3DTrim absent; can share G46's S2 boot):
- d3dprobe render 40/40 at 640x480x16 and 1024x768x32.
- M1: ddlab flip 300 frames at 1024x768x16@85, and d3dprobe perf --full vsync at 640x480x16, 1024x768x32 and 1280x960x16. Record the new 511 line: mean read, deadline polling/idle.

BOOT A, D3DTrim=4 (ASKIP), only if M3 showed >= 5% gain:

- askip passes with engaged 1 or unknown, and the 513 skip line shows skips > 0.
- M3 again: atest off within 2% of gt0, and faster than always.
- In game: Halo -novideo -vidmode 1280,960,85 -timedemo and the UT2004 DM-Antalus botmatch at 1280x960. Take screenshots at the same times as ONBOX/games, and require glow, smoke, HUD and text to be unchanged. Read each title's skip share from its 513 line.

BOOT B, D3DTrim=1 (VBDIRECT):
- ddlab flip/vblank/GetScanLine: flips/s no lower than Boot 0, fast frames 0, scanline ranges unchanged.
- d3dprobe perf vsync at the three modes: mean read <= 3 us, longest read and deadline_polling no higher than Boot 0, fps >= 85.1 / 84.4.

BOOT C, D3DTrim=2 (VBSNOOP), only if M1 showed deadline_idle >= 2%:

Afterwards: update the KMD README Diag table, tests/README.md, FINDINGS.md and the v56k plan's status table, then graduate bits per the gating rule.
G60.risk:
With D3DTrim absent: none. The default 16 bpp path and every armed path keep today's register and IOCTL traffic, pinned by the Python tests. M1 adds one log-only line at session end.

ASKIP:
- The failure mode would be an admitted combination that is not neutral on silicon, making transparent-looking pixels vanish or change.
- Guards: the rule is derived from SPEC 8.23 semantics; premultiplied and colour-factor modes are excluded; a host exhaustive blender-model test and the tolerance-0 askip probe check it; it is default-off with a per-PDEV kill switch.
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence is unaffected: only the D3D alphaMode is written, and Glide programs its own.
- SLI is unaffected (D3D is single-chip).
- Future inputs: G35 must pass stencil_writes, G91 must keep fogMode[11:8] an input, and G28 widens the rule to alpha targets.

VBDIRECT:
- It only reads, from the register the DLL already polls before every vertex, with the polarity helper shared with the miniport.
- DirectDraw is disabled across mode sets, and pjRegs is unmapped only after DrvDisableDirectDraw. A status read has no side effect, even under Glide exclusive mode.
- The flip rule and the flip IOCTL are unchanged. Dd_Flip's post-write sample keeps the IOCTL for refresh_mhz.

VBSNOOP:
- It completes flips sooner, but never before the latch, under the same single silicon assumption the polls rest on (status[6] does not rise before the latch).
- Denser sampling makes a false assumption more visible, as tearing or skipped frames. Boot C's ddlab fast-frame count and screenshots check for that.
- It is interim until G47/G54.

B1: no change is expected. The FPU bracket is never removed. The only hazardous candidate, the target_of fast path, would have to keep reading the surface on every call (the existing invariant).
games_unblocked: none - G60 stops no staged title
possible (inferred, to be measured): Halo, UT2003, UT2004, Max Payne, Red Faction - fewer frame-buffer read-modify-writes on alpha-blended particles/sprites once fill-bound (B4)

every vsync-flipping title (Thief Gold/II, System Shock 2, Jedi Knight/MotS, Shogo, Rainbow Six, Hidden and Dangerous, Halo, UT2003/UT2004; DirectDraw: StarCraft, Red Alert 2/Yuri's Revenge, Tiberian Sun, Warcraft II) - cheaper, non-blocking flip polls (B2) and fewer deadline-completed flips (B3)
open_questions: Does XP's DirectX kernel already save the FPU state around D3D DDI calls? 3dfx's NT HAL never calls EngSaveFloatingPointState. Not worth settling: our pair costs ~1 us a call, and removing it is unsafe either way.

Is status[6] only the vsync pulse (~33-44 us at 85 Hz, as 86Box models it) or the whole vertical blank (~0.4 ms) on the VSA-100? A host-launched direct-read loop (not during a game) measuring the bit-6-clear width would settle how often polls can miss it, and so B2/B3's value.
Why do single vblank reads take 1.08-2.6 ms: videoprt request serialisation, DPCs or preemption? Only B2's A/B separates the first from the rest; G54 is the fix if it is preemption.
Does the VSA-100 blender re-dither an unchanged 16 bpp destination (MAME's model says one LSB at some dither positions)? askip's drift_old answers it.
Does an alpha-test-failed pixel actually save time on this chip at 1 px/clk (Z may still be read; the pipeline may not be memory-bound)? M3 answers it; re-measure after G50 (2PPC).

X-byte policy: is the principled rule acceptable (X8R8G8B8's undefined X byte means 32 bpp flip-chain targets are eligible today), or should the strict rule (no byte may differ except dither) make every 32 bpp target wait for G28?
Where should the switch bits live: vcr_info.d3d_trim, G46's d3d_perf, or G05's d3dfeat? One appended word for all D3D switches would be cleaner; the integrator decides.
Should B3 (retrace snoop) stay here or move to G54/G59? It touches the flip rule G59 is measuring, and must never be armed in a G59 measurement boot.
Is deadline/9 the right cut between 'polling' and 'idle' deadline completions under the achieved-rate rule (Diag\FlipDeadline=1), where a frame is 32/33 of the deadline?

G63.approach:
VERDICT: real and fixable, and most of the cure already exists. Correction to the gap: no listed fullscreen title (UT2003, UT2004, Halo) can hit the single-pass failure; for them the cost is heap capacity.

MECHANISM (DDK-documented, measured on .124):
- HeapVidMemAllocAligned returns 0 for failure (W2K DDK d_grafx.chm, gdifncs_8dnr.htm). A heap whose fpStart is 0 hands its first block out AT 0. That block is allocated, read as a failure, and lost until the next mode set.
- DirectDraw survives this because its heap manager makes two passes (DDK ddraw_10dj.htm, section 3.3.2.1). The driver's own allocators (mipchain_ext, vcrdd_d3d.c:437-447; VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain, :558-568) make one pass and answer DDERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY.

EVIDENCE:
- ddlab vidmem, 09-27: 120 of 121 surfaces.
- New, from the 11-12 rings: at fullscreen 1024x768x32 the heap was 0-3cff000 and the back buffer landed at 0x300000, exactly its own size; Z at 0x600000, textures from 0x900000. 3 MB of the heap was never used. The windowed run shows the same at 256 KB (target 0x40000). The flip chain is always a game's first allocation and gets the second pass.
- Cost per mode set = the back buffer: 0.6 MB at 640x480x16, 4.7 MB at the staged 1280x960x32, 7.3 MB at 1600x1200x32. The heap is 59-62 MB.
- The single-pass failure needs a driver-placed block (any texture with D3DBigTex, any mipmap chain) as the FIRST allocation of a fresh heap. It has never been shown on silicon.

VENDOR: 3dfx's NT H5 driver never starts its heap at 0. Its CMDFIFO sits at the bottom (512 KB default), then the cursor, then ddLinearHeapStart = ulScreenOffset (VH5/ENABLE.C:1074-1077, 1240-1254, 1284, 1319, 2307-2308; DDINIT.C:1148). Our h5 Glide keeps everything above its FIFO window 0x18000-0x117000.

The deployed binaries already carry the switch: LIVE vcrmp.sys fda1b8c9 contains 'DdHeapFloor', and vcrdd.dll 95678704 contains the floor log text.

PHASE A, the investigation (no driver change):
- Build two lab tools: ddlab 'texfirst' (makes the single-pass failure on demand) and d3dprobe 'heapfill'. Rebuild out/ddlab.exe, which predates sdlddraw.
- Run one supervised clean boot: control runs, then REGWRITE DdHeapFloor=1 (the one Diag change), then the armed runs. Every number is registered in advance:
  - ddlab vidmem on the 1280x1024x32 desktop: 116 (lowest +512 KB) becomes 117 (+4 KB).
  - The 1024x768x32 ContextCreate target: 0x300000 becomes 0x1000.
  - heapfill slack: 3,272,704 becomes 122,880.
  - texfirst hr1: 8876017c becomes DD_OK at 0x1000.

PHASE B, the driver change:
(1) vcr_ddheap.h gets a value table, vcr_dd_heap_floor(diag, napalm):
   - 0 = today's layout;
   - any non-zero value = one page (0x1000);
   - bit 1 on a VSA-100 = VCR_DD_HEAP_GLIDE_FLOOR 0x118000. That is above Glide's FIFO window plus a guard page, equals the miniport's caps.fb_reserved, and is above the largest base-before-texture (0x55550), so no texBaseAddr can wrap. G01 section 3.5 proposed it, and G47's ring needs it.
   - Plus vcr_dd_heap_retry(heap_start) = (heap_start == 0).
(2) Miniport fill_info reads DdHeapFloor once. It sets F_DDHEAPFLOOR for any non-zero value (old DLLs still get the page floor) and a new positive flag F_DDHEAPGLIDE for bit 1.
(3) VcrDd2dInit stores the floor in bytes, after pd->napalm is set. heap_range passes it through; the INFO line names the value.
(4) One allocator, VcrDdHeapAlloc16(pd, vm, bytes), with 16/16 alignment:
   - it retries HeapVidMemAllocAligned once when the answer is 0 and vm->fpStart == 0, and counts zero answers and recoveries;
   - it becomes the only HeapVidMemAllocAligned call site in display/. mipchain_ext and VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain use it now; G07, G10, G18, G21 and G36 must use it.
(5) VCR_ESC_DD_STATS is appended with heap start/end and the two counters; vcrctl info prints them.

Old path (switch absent): heap from 0, byte for byte. Every allocation that succeeds first time is unchanged. Only a 0 answer on a heap at 0 is retried. No register is touched. Not a multipass or combine change.

PHASE C: silicon for the retry (floor explicitly 0: texfirst DD_OK at 0x2000) and for value 2 (target 0x118000, vidmem 115, heapfill slack 28,672).

- it makes the unmeasured TMU base wrap unreachable;
