G63.risk:
Default 16 bpp path:
- with the switch absent, nothing changes except the retry in the failure path;
- armed, every surface moves down by the lost block's size, so more textures sit below 16 MB. That only helps G21's 24-bit texBaseAddr bug.

Texture base wrap:
- value 1 lets a small texture sit below its 256-level offset (under 0x2AAA8 for 16-bit, 0x55550 for 32-bit) when the first allocations are tiny, such as a small window. That is the same class as today's windowed case.
- the default path's 24-bit field then samples 16 MB high on a 64 MB VSA-100, and the texture-port write-back is silently skipped (vcrdd_3d.c:263 'addr >= lin').
- the 26-bit TMU wrap is unmeasured. Value 2 rules all of this out by construction.

Glide/OpenGL coexistence: value 1 moves a fullscreen back buffer and Z into Glide's FIFO window 0x18000-0x117000, where today's lost block often covers it. Host writes there under a stale FIFO escalate to a 2D give-up (G01). Both sessions start from a cold boot, and value 2 is the promotion target because it removes the exposure, including the 11-12 windowed one.

SLI/AA state: none. The heap is chip 0's DirectDraw bookkeeping and no register is written.

Flip path: back buffers move to 0x1000 or 0x118000, both 4 KB-aligned, and flip completion is address-free. Whether vidDesktopStartAddr needs more than 16-byte alignment for linear scan-out is unmeasured; ddlab flip, d3dprobe perf and the fullscreen matrix cover it.

VGA pad [0, 0x18000): value 1 puts live surfaces there (inferred harmless: a VGA or console switch is a mode change that loses every surface).

Capacity: value 2 costs 1.09 MB. That is a net loss against today of 0.51 MB at 640x480x16 and 0.18 MB at 800x600x16, and a net gain at every larger first allocation (+3.6 MB at 1280x960x32).

Diag\DesktopOffset pinned below 0x119000 with value 2 leaves no heap, so DirectDraw falls back to the HEL. It is a debug override, unset on .124.

A switch read at every mode change could miss a desktop PDEV that XP reuses. Phase A checks the ring's heap line and forces a paced modeseq if needed.

G64.approach:
NOT A DRIVER DEFECT. Set P3 and change no driver code. The constant is correct, and the runtime never reads it for the call the Dark engine makes. Static analysis settles this.

(1) What Thief Gold reads (THIEF.EXE md5 8dd515df, lgd3d d6Sts_s.cpp):
- At init (0x5736d7-0x5737e7) it picks a texture pool from D3DDEVICEDESC.dwDevCaps. With our HAL that is local video memory: TEXTUREVIDEOMEMORY is set, TEXTURENONLOCALVIDMEM is not.
- The helper at 0x576cd0 calls IDirectDraw4::GetAvailableVidMem with caps 0x14005000 (TEXTURE|VIDEOMEMORY|ALLOCONLOAD|LOCALVIDMEM) and keeps only the free count.
- 0x574140 reads that free count before and after it loads a texture whose memory cost it has not recorded yet.
- If the count did not drop, 0x574297 calls the engine's level-3 ERROR path. That shows MessageBoxA "ERROR: Direct3d device driver does not accurately report texture memory usage" at exit and calls exit(1). It is FATAL, not a warning.
- Retail Thief II has the same check. NewDark removed it. SS2's copy is inside the SafeDisc-encrypted ICD (inferred).

(2) Where XP SP3 gets the number (dxg.sys md5 ac728056, DXG table entry 0x1c = DxDdGetAvailDriverMemory at 0x16350):
- dxg walks every heap that is not VIDMEM_HEAPDISABLED and whose ddsCapsAlt does not exclude the requested caps.
- Free = free-list bytes + discardable allocated blocks. Total = free + non-discardable allocated blocks.
- If a driver registered GetAvailDriverMemory, dxg ADDS that driver's figures to its own sums.
- DD_HALINFO.ddCaps.dwVidMemFree is never read on this path.
- linVidMemAlloc (0x1212e) marks a block discardable only when the caller passes SURFACEALIGN_DISCARDABLE.

(3) Our HAL already meets that rule:
- Every video-memory texture comes from that heap. Either the runtime places it, or mipchain_ext / VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain call HeapVidMemAllocAligned on pd->pvmList.
- We pass a memset vcr_surfalign, so dwFlags = 0 and every block is non-discardable.
- We answer no GUID_MiscellaneousCallbacks, so dxg adds nothing.
- So free memory drops by each texture's block size, and Thief's check passes.
- dwVidMemTotal == dwVidMemFree == he-hs is exactly true when DrvGetDirectDrawInfo runs, because dxg builds the heap after that call.
- The archived numbers agree. In the 86Box V3 bed, free sits below total by exactly one surface (960,000 B and 131,072 B, the G63 offset-0 losses). UT2003 on .124 logs "Video memory on board: 58" = 61,861,888 B, the heap at a 1280x1024x32 desktop.

Trap to write down: the same fatal message appears when the D3D HAL is missing (G01/G02). With no video-memory texture pool, 0x574140 has nothing to measure. So on .124, check the 3D engine's give-up before suspecting memory accounting.

G61.risk:
With the switch absent: none. Caps, the Dd_Blt/clipped_blt bodies and all register traffic are byte-for-byte today's; only counters are added. Step 0 is log-only.

Armed, the risks are:
1. A runtime sends a claimed class with a flag we did not foresee (D3D9 StretchRect's flags are unmeasured) and gets E_NOTIMPL. Mitigations: flag normalization; every decline counted and logged as a WARN with its flags; Step 0 and G56 E3 show the flags before arming.
2. A new cap switches on code paths in titles. A stretch cap may enable StretchRect effects or render targets in Thief II NewDark or Halo (G36 is unverified on silicon); a COLORKEY cap may change SDL or game sprite paths. Mitigations: per-title frame comparison between boot A and boot B; the bits can be armed separately.
3. Keyed blits move from the HEL to the engine and may differ in the 32 bpp top byte or with range keys. Mitigations: the engine's rule is SPEC's and the CPU copies it; ddlab compares against an HEL twin; only single keys are claimed.
4. The CPU fallback runs in kernel mode under the display lock. After an engine give-up, or for a same-surface overlapping stretch, a large blit can stall GDI for up to about 1 s (the HEL's cost, now under the lock). FORCECPU is lab-only.
5. The 16/16 depth-fill layout choice (live context, else the attach list) could be wrong. No known title DEPTHFILLs a D24 at 16 bpp, unless JK picks a D24 (open question). The layout is logged and ddlab zfill_1616 pins the attach case.

Proven paths:
- The default 16 bpp D3D path, the D3D caps, TEXBLT, Clear2, the flip, vblank, Glide/OpenGL coexistence (engine used only when !exclusive_pid) and SLI are untouched.
- VcrDd2dCopy and VcrDd2dFill are not edited. The stretch leaves srcSize, bresError=0 and clip1 behind, which no other command reads.
- 2D and 3D order themselves (miscInit1 bits 16/17 = 0).

New engine command never run on silicon: screen-to-screen stretch (command 2). It is bounded by VcrDdRoom, and the bed control proves it first.

G62.approach:
The gap is real, but its cause is not established, so the design is an investigation with a fix for each possible outcome. Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G62.md.

What the record shows:
- Of four recorded Descent DOSBox runs on .124, three dropped to DOSBox's 640x400 surface fallback: 09-28 02:47, 09-28 06:57 and 09-29 00:05. One took the ddraw path at 640x480 and showed the Interplay logo (09-28 06:53). All four used the same conf and binaries; the sweep called all four PASS.
- Every failing run had a 4-chip OpenGL/Glide session one to three titles earlier.

What this reading adds:
1. Only output=ddraw puts a surface in the DirectDraw heap. The surface and overlay outputs make the same fullscreen SDL_SetVideoMode(640x480) call and only lock the primary. Carmageddon runs the identical DOSBox.exe (md5 33294e0a) and SDL.dll 1.2.13 (52726f9e) with overlay and passed, once right after a Glide session; so did Daggerfall. The suspect steps are therefore the ddraw-only ones: the hardware blit surface and its per-frame use.
2. The heap's first block is lost at offset 0; this was measured three times on silicon. So DOSBox's 640x400x32 blit surface (0xFA000 bytes) should land at 0xFA000-0x1F3FFF. Its first 46 rows then sit inside h5 Glide's default command-FIFO window [0x18000,0x117000) (minihwc.c:2566-2592). A not-idle 4-chip GL close leaves that FIFO enabled, and host writes into the window make the chip busy (G01; ONBOX 11-12). 3dfx's own driver reserves its FIFO below the heaps (VH5/ENABLE.C:2128-2143).
3. Our HAL returns almost no errors on SDL's path. The failing call is therefore most likely an answer from the runtime or Windows that depends on machine state. DOSBox can name it: -noconsole writes its log to stdout.txt, and the window title shows the running program and its cycles. Neither has been read yet.
4. No setup step is known to fail because of an enabled FIFO; the window is written only frame by frame, after setup.

The hypotheses:
- H1: the stale FIFO / post-GL state.
- H2: the lost first block (DdHeapFloor).
- H3: SetDisplayMode refused, followed by SDL's windowed retry.
- H4: the runtime's primary fails SDL's checks.
- H5: a hand-over race between back-to-back titles.
- H6, a separate question: the DOS program makes no progress in the fallback.

The investigation, all as tools with no driver change:
- T1: extend ddlab sdlddraw with --windowed-first (DOSBox's first windowed SetVideoMode), --setsize N (one GFX_SetSize per DOS video-mode change) and --no-pitch, and report the blit surface's offset.
- T2: a new host runner, tools/dosbox_ddraw_run.py. It reads cmdFifo0 and the status register before and after each run, launches the exact shortcut or a -noconsole copy under C:\vcr, samples WINLIST, PROCLIST, DISPLAYCFG and SCREENSHOT at T+15 and T+45, closes DOSBox, fetches the ring, and fetches stdout.txt with DOWNLOAD. It enforces at most 8 launches per boot, 30 s apart.
- T3, only if needed: a diagnostic SDL 1.2.13 DLL that logs SDL_SetError.

Session A (current build, no Diag change, supervised):
- From a cold boot, run Descent and ddlab sdlddraw in the clean state.
- Create the post-GL state (Quake III 4-chip quit; if cmdFifo0 stays off, d2x-rebirth closed the sweep's way), read cmdFifo0, then run Descent and ddlab again.
- Cure A/B: vcrctl reset-engine (or a paced modeseq), then Descent.

Session B, only if H2 is still open: DdHeapFloor=1 on its own clean boot. Under H2 the post-GL run passes; under H1 it fails, because the blit surface moves deeper into the window.

Session C, only if no step is named: LogLevel=TRACE with LogEntries=16384, plus the diagnostic SDL.

The design has an outcome table mapping each result to a fix:
- F1 (H1): G01's stale-FIFO guard for the state, plus a new value Diag\DdHeapFloor=2 that starts the heap at 0x117000, above Glide's default FIFO window. That costs 1.1 MB and also cures the offset-0 loss. It touches vcr_ddheap.h (VCR_DD_HEAP_FLOOR_GLIDE and vcr_dd_heap_floor_bytes), heap_range, a second vcr_info flag in fill_info, and VcrDd2dInit.
- F2 (H2): the DdHeapFloor floor; the decision belongs to G63.
- F3 (H3): an emulation of SDL's EnumModes2 against our mode-list order, then fix the mode list or pick_mode.
- F4 (H4): the primary or surface description after a mode change.
- F5 (H5): a settle step in lan_sweep; the driver is then not at fault.
- F6 (H6): depends on what the title and CPU readings show.
- The overlay half needs no change: SDL's software YUV path renders. A real YUV overlay is G61's.

G62.d3dprobe_test:
None: this path is DirectDraw only, and D3D is not involved. The lab check is ddlab sdlddraw.

The run, in two states (clean, and post-GL with cmdFifo0 read ON first):
ddlab_run.py 192.168.1.124 sdlddraw --res 640x480 --bpp 32 --src 640x400 --frames 120 --windowed-first --setsize 2

What it draws: a frame-numbered pattern written into the 640x400 video-memory blit surface. Each frame it is stretched onto the 640x480 primary and read back row by row (sdl_row_ok).

Pass: RESULT "dosbox":"ddraw", bad_rows 0, lock_fail 0, blt_fail 0, fill_bad 0, blit_in "video". The reference is the 06:53 frame: 640x480, a 320x200 picture with columns doubled and rows repeated two or three times.

The host also computes blit_off = 0x3ED4000 + blit_from_primary. Expected values:
- default layout: 0xFA000, overlapping Glide's FIFO window [0x18000,0x117000) by 0x1D000;
- DdHeapFloor=1: 0x1000, overlapping by 0xE3000;
- DdHeapFloor=2: 0x117000, no overlap.
Any other value falsifies the lost-first-block model.

The fallback path must work too: --direct --res 640x400 --bpp 32 --frames 120 must give "dosbox":"surface" with bad_rows 0.
G62.risk:
The investigation changes no code and no default.

On-box risks:
1. The 1998 CRT. A fallback run can make two mode switches in quick succession that no tool can pace (640x480, then 640x400). DOSBox launches are capped at 8 per boot, at least 30 s apart; ddlab is paced by vcr_pace.
2. The post-GL state can escalate. Writes into an enabled FIFO window make the chip execute whatever the pixels decode to. On 11-12 that meant CMD0 busy within about 1 s, a 2D give-up, and the D3D HAL lost for that PDEV; hal.md calls it a credible freeze mechanism. Mitigations:
   - a person stays near the box for steps A6-A9;
   - stop at the first sign of a wedge;
   - recover with one paced vcrctl modeseq (proven 11-12), or a cold boot through safe-reboot.py after the activation check.
3. vcrctl reset-engine has never run on silicon without a new PDEV (G01 fact 8). Run it with nothing else on the engine, with modeseq as the fallback.
4. No vcrctl or vcrlog runs while DOSBox runs, because both take the display lock.
5. The library tree is never touched. The -noconsole and diagnostic-SDL runs use a copy under C:\vcr; GAMESYNC never deletes, so anything written under C:\Games would stay.
6. Session B's DdHeapFloor=1 is unproven and moves every DirectDraw and D3D allocation, so the d3dprobe matrix runs in that boot too. That run is G63's proof as well.

F1 when armed: every heap surface moves up 1.1 MB, including D3D targets, Z, textures, mip chains and flip back buffers.
- The proven paths are unchanged while it is off: floor 0, byte for byte.
- On the default path without D3DBigTex, the move pushes a few more textures above 16 MB, where G21's 24-bit texBaseAddr bug samples them 16 MB lower. .124 runs D3DBigTex=7, so the deployed setup is not affected; a fresh install is. Prove F1 with BigTex off as well, or land it after G21.
- Glide never uses the DirectDraw heap, SLI is untouched, and the flip path is covered by ddlab flip and d3dprobe fullscreen.
open_questions: Which SDL call fails, and with which HRESULT? The core question; Session A's DOSBox log, ring and ddlab replay should name it.

Is cmdFifo0 enabled at DOSBox's start in the failing state? Did the one passing run (06:53, after Unreal's forced Glide hang and Warcraft II's mode set) have it off? Only controlled states can answer this now.

Why does the DOS program show nothing for 70 s after the fallback, when MOO2 and Warcraft run the same surface output fine? Is it stuck before DESCENTR, crawling at low cycles, or are its frames lost?
Does XP's runtime make its second heap pass for an IDirectDraw2 surface created with DDSD_PITCH | DDSD_PIXELFORMAT? The ddlab vidmem proof used DX7 surfaces without them.
Is Redneck Rampage Route 66's 640x400 under aspect=true (overlay, 09-28 03:03) its own VESA mode, or the same fallback?
Does the DOSBox Status Window console (AllocConsole) take part through focus? Compare the exact launcher with -noconsole.
Dd_GetBltStatus can answer WASSTILLDRAWING for as long as g2d_busy is set and the chip is CMD0-busy from a stale FIFO. It is not shown to matter here; does it belong to G01/G02?
If the cause proves to be harness timing (H5), should the staged Descent confs leave output=ddraw? Recommended no: fix the driver or the harness, not every box's library tree.

G69.approach:
G69 is a needs-investigation gap. It is real, and bigger than "one 320x240 strip". No new driver behaviour is proposed.

(1) What the 11-08 strip proves.
- It proves only that CreateDevice succeeds with D3D32 armed.
- R6's intro is Smacker through DirectDraw Lock, and its 640x480 menu is very likely DirectDraw: .123's compat row records it as `ddraw`, and the cursor has no key-colour box although our HAL draws no texture key.
- So no R6 triangle has been seen on vcr-kmd, and the 16-over-32 Z (be58b7d: aux stride = the 32-bit Z's 4-byte pitch, depth 0..0xffff) has never depth-tested a pixel.

(2) New static evidence (RainbowSix.exe and its data, read on the host). R6 is DX5 D3DApp: it takes the deepest Z from dwDeviceZBufferBitDepth (DDBD_16|DDBD_32 with rt32). It draws with IDirect3DDevice2 SetRenderState + DrawPrimitive/DrawIndexedPrimitive, never execute buffers. In game it is certain to hit:
- Texture colour key (G09).
  - Surface::SetTransparentValue = SetColorKey(DDCKEY_SRCBLT) at VA 0x46ad9a.
  - It has a COLORKEYENABLE setter at VA 0x47ab62/74.
  - data/texture/Sherman.CXP keys 294 materials: glass, tree lines, chain-link, railings, effects, map icons, and the HUD reticle (key 0,0,0).
- Lines (G16).
  - Its only DrawIndexedPrimitive(LINELIST, LVERTEX) wrapper (VA 0x474140) is called 6x from one class.
  - That class sits next to the stair/ladder map-icon loader, so it is very likely the planning map's floor plans and team paths (inferred). The DP2 walker skips them.
- Legacy states (G08): setters for TEXTUREMAG/MIN (1-6), TEXTUREMAPBLEND (1-8), WRAPU/V.
- Also: SPECULARENABLE (G25), STIPPLEENABLE (G90), and vertex fog only (G32; no FOGTABLEMODE setter).
- R6 has its own screenshot: VA 0x404d50 writes ShermanScreenShot%d.BMP by Locking the surface. It is case VK 0x71 (F2) of its key switch (VK reading inferred). That gives a capture with no GDI back-buffer ambiguity and no vcrctl.
- 3dfx's own V5 driver did the same Z trick at attach ("16bpp render target, 32bpp zbuffer: silently substitute 16bpp", VH5/DDSURF.C:2243-2260). R6 clears through IDirect3DViewport2::Clear (VA 0x4712e6), i.e. our Clear2/DP2 CLEAR, never a DirectDraw depth fill. So the pairing itself is likely fine.

(3) The investigation.
- Preconditions: a cold boot with no Glide/OpenGL session (G01); the activation check plus safe-reboot.py; LogLevel 2 and LogEntries 8192 set before the boot (logging only; shared with G04 Boot 1); every new D3D bit off.
- Phase 0: the lab test z16in32 in G75's DX5 probe, before launching R6.
- Phase 1, session A, 640x480x16, staged:
  - intro and menu, then F2;
  - menu-only exit, then ring_A0: did the shell draw triangles?
  - Training > Fire and Movement > shooting range (keyed tree line): action phase, GDI x3 plus F2, turn to the trees, quick menu;
  - campaign M01: planning map (lines and icons), PREVIEW, action phase with the default plan;
  - after exit: ring_A1, Sherman.log, the F2 BMPs, the REGREAD of R6's key.
  - Check P: SoftwareOnly 0, a ContextCreate with fmt 16, and thousands of HAL triangles; otherwise the frames are R6's software fallback.
- Session B: 800x600x16 (R6's HIGH; Z pitch 3200), attended and last (G43 path).
- Session C: reference frames, from R6 FORCE SOFTWARE on .124 or from .133/.123.
- Optional session D: D3D32-off control.
- Then the 13-shortcut D3D re-sweep 95678704 never had, minus Max Payne and AvP, and read every frame (G79).
- Evidence goes to EV/silicon/r6_ingame_<date>/, then `compat.py record` (runs/verified/failed with the gap list).
- Phase 2 (after G76): counters for COLORKEYENABLE with a keyed texture, lines by opcode, and the legacy state values.
- Phase 3: R6 scenes become the A/B proof for G09, G16 and G08.

(4) An outcome table maps each result to a gap: A works; A' the shell is DirectDraw; B1/B2/B3 G01/G02/a Z dropped at re-target; C a 32-bit-word clear (vendor DDBLT32.C fix, G61); D a regression; E a freeze (G04); G/H/I/J/K: G09/G16/G08/G32/G59; P software fallback.

(5) Optional log-only line: 513 INFO once per context, "16 bpp target over a 32-bit Z, aux stride N". It makes the path visible in every ring with byte-identical register traffic.

(6) Likely fixes are owned by G09, G16 and G08 (plus G32/G25). Library follow-up after proof: VideoResolution 800x600 (G66). If confirmed, escalate G09 to P0, and G16 to P0 for R6.

G69.d3dprobe_test:
D3D8's d3dprobe cannot reach this pair: the runtime refuses R5G6B5+D24X8 with 8876086a before the driver is asked (caps zmatch 0). So the test is `z16in32` in G75's DX5/DX6 legacy probe (tools/d3d7probe.c), driven through R6's own interfaces (IDirect3D2 / IDirect3DDevice2, via d3dim.dll).

Setup, as R6 does it:
- At the 32 bpp desktop, EnumDevices and record the HAL dwDeviceZBufferBitDepth: 0x500 expected with D3D32, 0x400 without. Take the deepest.
- One paced SetDisplayMode to 640x480x16, then a primary flip chain with one back buffer.
- Create the Z with DDSD_ZBUFFERBITDEPTH = the chosen depth in VIDEOMEMORY, AddAttachedSurface it, and record its pitch: 2560 expected at 32, 1280 at 16.
- CreateDevice(IID_IDirect3DHALDevice), then a 640x480 viewport.
- State: dither off, Z on, ZWRITE on, LESSEQUAL, no texture.

Each test runs Viewport2::Clear(TARGET|ZBUFFER), then DrawPrimitive(TRIANGLELIST, TLVERTEX), then a Lock of the back buffer, then a Flip. Consecutive tests therefore draw into alternate buffers after a re-target.

Tests and pass criteria (565, exact):
- `zclear_far`: a full-screen red quad at z 0.999. All 640 pixels of row 240 and all 480 of column 320 must read 0xF800.
- `zorder_nearfirst`: green z 0.25 over (100..300)², then red z 0.75 over (200..400)². Expect (250,250)=0x07E0, (350,350)=0xF800, (150,150)=0x07E0, (450,450)=0.
- `zorder_farfirst`: the same quads in the other order. Expect (250,250)=0x07E0.
- `zcolumns`: a z 0.5 quad, then red at z 0.75 over it. All 640 pixels of row 100 must keep the z 0.5 colour; this catches a 32-bit-word clear over the 16-bit rows.
- Record-only:
  - `zprecision`: proves 16-bit depth.
  - `zlayout`: Lock the Z; bytes 0..1279 of row 0 should read 0xFFBD x640.

Old-buggy reference: on b63ea6a5/13256e46 with D3D32=1, CreateDevice is refused (ring 513/12 "16 bpp target with a 32-bit Z"), so every test FAILS with device:refused.

G66.approach:
The gap is real for all three titles. Both of its inferences are now settled by reading the staged binaries (pefile/capstone on the read-only mount), and one of them is wrong in a way that matters.

1) RED FACTION READS HKCU AND HAS NEVER READ HKLM (read).
- rf.exe md5 0ba3b15d64a702333a4d9a0815f782b7. Its vsdk registry wrapper starts every lookup at HKEY_CURRENT_USER (mov ebp,0x80000001 at VA 0x52b2b3).
- The five video reads at 0x4b1480-0x4b14f5 pass a NULL subkey: Resolution Bit Depth (default 16), Width (640), Height (480), Backbuffer Format (-1) and Selected Video Card. A NULL subkey keeps that root and the base path Software\Volition\Red Faction.
- Only a subkey that starts with "hkey" can select another root; the HKLM constant appears only in that name parser, at 0x52b43e.
- Both writers use HKLM: the launcher (Play Red Faction.bat:55-59, rendered from provisioning/discmount/specs/RedFaction.json fleetres_block) and GAMERES (gameres.h:1041-1043). So every box runs rf.exe's defaults, 640x480x16. That matches the 11-08 sweeps, the 09-29 scan-out and every compat row that records a mode.

2) RED FACTION'S STAGED 32 BPP WOULD STOP IT STARTING ON .124 (read + measured).
- For vendor 0x121a, rf.exe hard-codes AutoDepthStencilFormat = D16 at any depth (0x544756 -> 0x5446f6). At 32 bpp it asks for an A8R8G8B8 back buffer (0x5446a1).
- vcr-kmd refuses 32-bit colour over a 16-bit Z (vcr_rt_format; vcrdd_d3d.c:1195). That is G10, measured 11-12 as CreateDevice 8876086c.

- New stage-fleetres.py redfaction_mode():

  - FLEETRES -reg HKCU writes Resolution Width %FR_W%, Height %FR_H%, Bit Depth %RF_BPP%;

- The RF spec's fleetres_block becomes exactly CALL + that block; a test pins the two together. Regenerate the launcher with make-mount-launcher.py through libwrite.
- gameres.h: the two width/height rows move to HKCU, and the Bit Depth row is deleted. The agent cannot see the display driver, and a second writer with a constant 32 would both fight the launcher and break .124.
- The two halves are safe in either landing order. The stale HKLM values are inert.

3) THIEF GOLD AND SYSTEM SHOCK 2 ARE NOT "INCAPABLE" (read).
- The PER-TITLE-STATUS row and gameres.h gr_incapable[] are wrong. Vanilla THIEF.EXE (md5 8dd515df..., Thief 1.37) reads "%sscreen_size/depth/flags" with prefix "" for the default (menu) mode (0x415caa) and "game_" for the in-game mode (0x410836, 0x4fd135). G65.approach:
VERDICT: half real, a quarter inert, a quarter wrong. Full design: KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G65.md.

(1) UT2003/UT2004 UseVSync=False: REAL, read in the staged binaries.
- D3DDrv sets FullScreen_PresentationInterval = UseVSync ? D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_ONE : IMMEDIATE.
  - UT2003 D3DDrv 2225 (md5 04c412ca): field +0x40e8, code 0x100103a1-c7.
  - UT2004 D3DDrv 3369 (md5 b6bb4d87): field +0x4120, code 0x10011b7a-9e.
- The runtime turns IMMEDIATE into DDFLIP_NOVSYNC, which vcr-kmd honours (vcrdd_ddraw.c:102-105, 324-333).

(2) DesiredRefreshRate=60 "runs them at 60 Hz": WRONG.
- D3DDrv uses DesiredRefreshRate only when it is >60 or OverrideDesktopRefreshRate=True (D03 0x100100b7-e0, D04 0x10011909-30). At 60 it passes FullScreen_RefreshRateInHz=0 (RATE_DEFAULT).
- The XP D3D8 runtime's default on .124 was the desktop's 85 Hz in every measured case: ring 'mode 144: 640x480x32@85' and 'mode 153: 1024x768x32@85' for d3dprobe devices, which set no rate.
- Above 60, D3DDrv takes an EXACT match or else the first (lowest, inferred) rate of the mode.
- So DesiredRefreshRate must NOT be written. UE2's log 'Best-match display mode ...@120' is the matched list entry, not the scan rate.

(3) Red Faction Vsync=0: REAL, read.
- rf.exe (md5 0ba3b15d) reads Vsync at 0x544634 into the present interval.
- Its registry layer (0x52b2a0: root 0x80000001, base 'Software\Volition\Red Faction') reads HKCU ONLY.
- By-product: its resolution keys are HKCU too, so the launcher's and GAMERES's HKLM writes are dead. That settles G66/G10's open question.

An evidence gap, and a real one. A HAL regression cannot be hiding in it. This is an investigation design plus host tooling only; nothing in the kernel or HAL changes.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS (new facts from this reading)
- F1. The D3D HAL did not change between the two runs. `git diff --stat bfdf2cd 76d36e7^` lists no file under `display/` or `common/` between the 09-29 build and the first 11-08 fix; only miniport SLI/AA, fbshot and log files changed. - F2. The black frame was painted black. A mode set leaves the old desktop in VRAM (AvP S00; UT2004's 09-29 30 s frame). A 640x480 frame that is exactly 0/0 in GDI at 30 s and 60 s and in the scan-out at ~40 s was therefore written black, by D3D Clear or by GDI erasing RF's popup. For more than 60 s nothing RF draws became visible.
- F3. Everything RF shows is a D3D triangle. Bink movies go `CreateImageSurface` 640x480 (0x52048e) → `LockRect` / `BinkCopyToBuffer` / `UnlockRect` → `CopyRects` into a texture (0x5206e3) → textured quads. The menu and the "Insert Red Faction CD #2" text are in-engine. So two causes fit F2 exactly:
  - G01: a stale `cmdFifo0`, where PIO triangles are lost and fastfill works (measured 11-12);

- F4. history-34's "game not focused" is a sweep artifact. Before `lan_sweep` `fe2a23c` (10-03), the focus was checked only after the sweep's own WM_CLOSE. On 11-08 the per-sample foreground shows RF focused at 30 s and 60 s.

  - Shogo after RTCW MP: text but no 3D backdrop.

- F7. rf.exe reads its video settings from HKCU, not HKLM:

  - defaults are 16/640/480/-1 (0x4b1480-0x4b14d5);
  - `Vsync` is read the same way.

  The launcher's HKLM FLEETRES writes are dead, which is why RF runs at 640x480x16. This answers the open hive question in G66 and G10.
- F8. The device RF asks for:

G68.d3dprobe_test:
Three additions. All are explicit (never in the default list) and analytic (readback compared with values computed in d3dprobe). Point sampling, `DITHERENABLE` FALSE, `ZFUNC` ALWAYS. Run with `d3dprobe render --app redfaction --bpp 16 --res 640x480`. The `--app redfaction` preset is RF's exact device: full screen, FLIP, `LOCKABLE_BACKBUFFER`, D16, R5G6B5 at 16 bpp / A8R8G8B8 at 32 bpp, `PresentationInterval` ONE. The 32 bpp form is refused by the runner until G10 is reported, so the runtime's unpaced double switch (G11) is never provoked by accident.

(1) `lockbb`: CPU writes into the lockable back buffer, then 3D on top. RF asks for a lockable back buffer, and d3dprobe today only ever locks it READONLY.
- Steps: clear black → `LockRect` (flags 0) → write block K (x16-79, y16-79, R5G6B5 0xFC00) and block W (x96-127, y16-47, white) → `UnlockRect` → draw an untextured quad Q (x48-111, y32-63, diffuse 0,0,255, alpha 0x80, SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA) → read back.
- Pass (8-bit expanded RGB; exact cells tolerance 4, blended cells tolerance 12):

  | pixel | content | expected |
  |---|---|---|
  | (20,20) | K | (255,130,0) |
  | (60,40) | K + Q | ~(127,65,128) |
  | (88,40) | Q over black | ~(0,0,128) |
  | (104,40) | Q over W | ~(127,127,255) |
  | (120,20) | W | (255,255,255) |
  | (200,200) | untouched | 0 |

- Old-bug signatures:
  - K or W black: the CPU write was lost behind a late clear.
  - (60,40) = (0,0,128): the blend read a stale destination.
  - (60,40), (88,40) and (104,40) unchanged: triangles lost. That is the G01 stale-FIFO state, so the test doubles as its canary.
- At 32 bpp (only after G10), tolerance is 3 for exact cells and 4 for blended cells.

(2) `rgb565_256_recopy`: RF's Bink path, copied twice into one texture.
- Steps:
  1. `CreateImageSurface` 640x480 R5G6B5 (system memory), filled with pattern A (32-texel red 0xF800 / blue 0x001F cells).
  2. `CopyRects` the source rect (192,112)-(448,368) into a 256x256 R5G6B5 DEFAULT texture.
  3. Draw at 1:1 with the half-pixel-correct quad and read back.
  4. Refill the image surface with pattern B (green 0x07E0 / white), `CopyRects` into the SAME texture, draw and read back.
- Pass: all 64 cell centres equal A after step 3 and B after step 4 (tolerance 4).
- Old-bug signature: any cell still A after B was copied, i.e. a stale TMU cache after a Blt into a texture (G37).
- The copy and draw time is logged for G56.

(3) `caps` gains an "rf" object. No device and no mode switch:
- `fs_565_565` = `CheckDeviceType(HAL, R5G6B5, R5G6B5, FALSE)`. Must be 1.
- `fs_x8_a8` = `CheckDeviceType(HAL, X8R8G8B8, A8R8G8B8, FALSE)`: measured.
- `zmatch_a8_d16` = `CheckDepthStencilMatch(HAL, X8R8G8B8, A8R8G8B8, D16)`: expected 1. This is the runtime "match" G10 is about.

The 32 bpp answers are reported with `g10_open` until the box reports G10's capability.

G67.approach:
An investigation. No driver behaviour changes in this item. Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G67.md.

(1) Static facts settled before any box time (addresses in the design; Appendix A re-derives them):
(a) Which renderer .124 runs.
- Halo reads IDirect3D9::GetDeviceCaps(HAL) into 0x7c10c0 (0x516b86/0x516b94). Its renderer selector at 0x516810 picks table 0x51fd80 (legacy, single-stream, fixed function) whenever caps.MaxStreams (+0xBC = 0x7c117c) <= 1. Otherwise it picks 0x51f3e0 (shaders, PS >= 1.1) or 0x51fad0.
- -use00 only writes MaxStreams := 1 (0x516ca8). -useff, UseFixedFunction, SafeMode and -safemode force PS 0.
- XP SP3 d3d9.dll's legacy caps builder writes MaxStreams 0, VS 0xfffe0000 and PS 0xffff0000 (0x4fdfb2fc-0x4fdfb44b). The VS/PS values are the ones our HAL reports, so .124 already runs Halo's most basic renderer and timedemo.txt will print 'Shader=Fixed Function' (printer at 0x4c71c7). The link between that builder and our HAL is inferred; caps9 --halo measures it.
- So no switch or config flag can pin a 'safer shader path' for 0x121a:0x0009. The remaining levers are the video options, DisableSpecular, the resolution and -noSSE.
- A reference box launched with -use00 runs the same legacy renderer on a vendor driver.
(b) SSE2. All 395 SSE2-class instructions in halo.exe are behind a CPU check:
- the static CRT's __sse2_available at 0x723a20, set only after CPUID.1:EDX bit 26 and tested at each routine entry;
- D3DX9's PSGP tables, where IsProcessorFeaturePresent(3DNow) comes first, so an Athlon XP gets the 3DNow! table;
- a SEH-guarded xorpd probe.
The requires.json '/arch:SSE2 build' premise is refuted for the exe; the DLLs were counted only. Halo also has its own -noSSE switch.
(c) The white 60 s frame is not Halo's art. The reference menu (.139) has a dark space backdrop, while .124's backdrop is white. G17 lists the menu starfield as X8R8G8B8, a format never offered, so it is drawn untextured. The no-logo frame is that pass caught in the back buffer by GDI (G79). That is two defects, not 'the animated menu'. 'Recapture with fbshot --probe' is dropped, because it is a vcrctl tool under a running D3D game.
(d) The three workarounds are explained by sibling designs:
- DisableRenderTargets: not liftable inside the DX7 DDI (G36);
- -novideo: a software stretch (G56; dropping it is G56 Part D, after G61);
- the SSE2 floor: (b).

(2) Instruments:
- d3d9spy: a game-local, log-only D3D9 interposer. It is copied as C:\Games\Halo\d3d9.dll for one run and never staged; Halo loads d3d9.dll by bare name.
  - It exports the same 14 names as XP's d3d9.dll and not DisableD3DSpy. It hooks by vtable patching.
  - It logs the caps, every CheckDeviceFormat and Create* call with its HRESULT, the CreateDevice/Reset parameters (incl. PresentationInterval and depth format), a census of render, stage and sampler states, draws by primitive type including lines and points, ValidateDevice, and per-second frame times.
  - Optional in-process captures: LockRect of a lockable back buffer before Present, at frame numbers or on Scroll Lock. Only then does the spy alter a call, ORing the lockable flag.
  - It is G36's E7 spy, and its hook layer can later host G36's shim as a separate binary.
- d3d9probe capture9 and caps9 --halo.
- Ring settings for the session boot: LogLevel 2 and LogEntries 16384.
- G76 counters and G04's d3dwatch, if landed.
- Halo's own timedemo.txt, debug.txt and ExitFlag, plus Dr. Watson.
- References: .110 and .240, each with -use00 and with the default renderer.

(3) Protocol:
- Phase 1 (no .124): validate the spy against d3d9probe; capture the menu; run the timedemo twice (Frames and determinism); MP spawn views.
- Phase 2: one supervised clean boot on .124 (no Glide earlier, cmdFifo0 checked, a person present). caps9 and capture9, then the menu with the spy. Then 30-40 min in a real Blood Gulch game: haloded on .123 with sv_public 0, .124 joining with -connect and its own key -8, a person playing a 15-scene checklist mapped to gap ids. Then a complete timedemo, then a deliberate alt-tab and mode change, then cleanup.
- Phase 3: repeat after G17 and G06/G07 land.
- Phase 4 decisions:
  - drop sse2 from requires.json if the soak is clean;
  - DisableRenderTargets stays;
  - -novideo goes via G56 Part D;
  - .124 moves from blk to MP in the readiness matrix and lanparty_titles.json.

Outcome-to-owner table: X8 failures → G17; DEPTHBIAS → G22/G94; stage ops → G05/G12/G13/G14; specular → G25; stencil → G35; lines and points → G16; fps → G46-G51; freeze → G04/G02; #UD → floor stays, retry with -noSSE.

G67.risk:
To proven paths: none, because no driver code changes. This covers the default 16 bpp path, Glide/OpenGL coexistence, SLI and flip code.

Session risks:
1. Stale Glide state (G01). A Glide or OpenGL title earlier in the boot makes every triangle vanish and can escalate to a 2D give-up and loss of the HAL. Guarded by a clean boot and the cmdFifo0 check.
2. An unexplained D3D freeze (G04). A person stays present; no vcrctl or escape runs under the game; GDI SCREENSHOT is proven under Halo.
3. A leftover spy d3d9.dll in C:\Games\Halo. GAMESYNC never deletes, so it would ride every later launch. Guarded by a refuse-to-start-if-present check, deletion verified with DIRLIST, and the spy logging its own md5.
4. Spy bugs crash Halo, not the box (user mode). R0 on .110 and capture9 on .124 validate the spy first.
5. Captures drain the engine through Lock. They are rare (max 120) and bounded on disk.
6. The deliberate alt-tab and mode change touch G43's possible use-after-free and the never-tested lost-device path. They run last, are supervised, and are skipped if anything earlier was unstable.
7. CRT mode switches. Halo makes two per launch; capture9's fullscreen variants are paced 5 s apart; no refused Z/target pair is probed fullscreen (G11).
8. MP. One key per player (.124 uses -8, distinct from the other boxes), sv_public 0 is required, and .123 may be in use by another session (fall back to .145).

G70.approach:
An evidence-gap investigation. It changes no driver behaviour and delivers capture tooling, a lab test and a protocol. Full design: voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G70.md.

FINDINGS FROM THIS READING (static work on the staged binaries plus every archived frame, measured):
(a) The post-OpenGL frames (09-29 and 10-01: menu text on black, or all black) match G01's on-box signature exactly.
- Shogo's menu text is drawn by DirectDraw blits. CShell v3 sends 'OptimizeSurfaces 1' only from its launcher-flag table (EnableOptSurf). Our DirectDraw HAL reports no colour-key caps (vcrdd_ddraw.c:101), so the HEL draws the text with the CPU (inferred).
- The cloth backdrop is Direct3D triangles.
- A stale Glide FIFO drops PIO triangles while clears and 2D still work, which leaves exactly 'text on black'. That half belongs to G01/G03, and Shogo becomes their game-level witness.
(b) GDI frames of Shogo's menu are unreliable on every driver.
- The 08-31 per-box frames from other vendors' cards show the same menu complete on 2 boxes, backdrop-only on 3 and title-only on 1. The compat note 'client menu renders intermittently' is this.
- A GDI read returns whichever flip-chain buffer sits at the GDI primary. On our slow PIO HAL that is often a back buffer caught mid-cloth (inferred). The S08F 60 s black-mesh frame (no text, cloth at the borders only) fits that artefact and fits a real defect equally well.
(c) Shogo has its own trustworthy capture: F8.
- Client.exe 2.2 window procedure 0x4036a0, WM_KEYUP VK_F8 at 0x403b2e: writes Screenshot<N>.bmp in its working directory.
- d3d.ren 0x10016760 writes it from the back buffer, locked with DDLOCK_WAIT, between frames: a complete frame with its 2D text. No vcrctl and no escape are involved, and the key arrives as a window message, so UIKEY reaches it.
(d) There are two direct in-game routes:
- '+runworld worlds\01_Ambush' (the CShell runworld variable and its first mission name);
- the readiness '+Connect 192.168.1.132' join to shogo-server (MCA_12FLOZ, proven on 7 boxes on 11-11, whose frames are references).
(e) Other facts that shape the protocol:
- LithTech tears down its renderer on WM_ACTIVATEAPP focus loss ('Losing focus..', 0x4036fb; 'alwaysfocused').
- Every polygon is its own DrawPrimitive(TRIANGLEFAN, FVF 0x1c4/0x244, DONOTCLIP).
- S08 and S08F both predate be58b7d, so Shogo's Z pick may now differ.

HYPOTHESES for the black-mesh frame:
- H1: a GDI back-buffer read mid-frame.
- H2: the game's own transition.
- H3: a texture defect on the driver-placement path that 13256e46 made universal. Sub-cases: (a) single-pass allocation refused (G63); (b) the upload route; (c) a silent TEXBLT with an unresolved handle (vcrdd_d3d.c:1508); (d) a stale TMU cache (G37).
- H4: a renderer rebuild after a focus round trip.
- H5: render-after-flip (G55: DP2/Clear2 draw into the buffer still being scanned out, while Lock and Blt refuse).
- H6: post-Glide residue (G01/G03).
- H7: silent drops (the tri() index-range skip, !drawable).
Each has a distinct signature across four instruments:
- F8 frames (primary);
- a classified GDI burst (measures H1);
- a person at the CRT (the only direct view of scan-out without vcrctl, and the H5 detector);
- the flight recorder at LogEntries=16384, fetched only after the game exits (513/1-2 contexts and counts, 513/7, 9, 10, 13, 14, 20, 511/12-13 flips, 512/9), plus error.log via '+ErrorLog 1 +AlwaysFlushLog 1'.

G70.d3dprobe_test:
Name: menugrid, plus menugrid2. Explicit tests. Modes: 640x480x16, 1280x960x16 (Shogo's mode), 1024x768x32, and windowed on the 32 bpp desktop.

What menugrid draws, over 8 frames with phase k/8:
- Clear to black and Z 1.0.
- Texture: 32x32 R5G6B5, MANAGED, one level. Texel (i,j) = 565(R=i, G=2j+1, B=(i^j)&31), unique per cell and never black.
- Grid: 24x18 cells covering the target. Vertex (i,j) at x = i*W/24 + 0.2*(W/24)*sin 2pi(j/18+phase), y = j*H/18 + 0.2*(H/18)*sin 2pi(i/24+phase). Boundary vertices are pushed 0.75 cell outward.
- Clipping: the probe clips each cell to the target itself (Sutherland-Hodgman), as LithTech does. Interior cells are 4-vertex fans; edge cells are 3-8-vertex fans.
- Drawing: one DrawPrimitiveUP(D3DPT_TRIANGLEFAN) per cell, with Shogo's FVF 0x1c4 (XYZRHW|DIFFUSE|SPECULAR|TEX1).
- Vertices: rhw 1, z 0.5, white diffuse. All vertices of a cell carry texel (i,j)'s centre as UV, so the expected colour is independent of the warp.
- State: point filter, MODULATE(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE), dither off, Z LESSEQUAL with writes on, cull none, D3DRS_CLIPPING FALSE.

menugrid2 draws the same grid twice per frame:
- pass 1: untextured, black diffuse, Z writes on;
- pass 2: textured, ZFUNC EQUAL, Z writes off, SRCBLEND ONE / DESTBLEND ONE.
This covers multipass rendering and ONE/ONE over a full-screen mesh.

Readback: on the last frame, before Present. A new readback_points() locks the whole back buffer; today's readback stops at the top-left 256x256. It reads one point per cell, at the centroid of the clipped polygon.

Pass criterion: all 432 centroids equal their texel's colour (expanded as d3dprobe's expand() does), within the existing 'tex' test's tolerance. Failures are listed per cell and split into 'clear colour (black)', the S08F signature, and 'other'.

Reference values: the texel table in KMD/tools/d3dprobe_grid.h, which the native test compiles.

Expected result: a pass on the current build. A failure at 1280x960 but not at 640x480 would point at target size or placement, not at Shogo.

Conditional follow-up, only on outcome O4 (black cloth without a WARN that disappears with D3DBigTex=0): texchurn.
- 64 rounds of create, LockRect fill and release of mixed-size MANAGED 565/4444/1555 textures, single-level and 3-level.
- The newest 8 are drawn as quads and read back.
- Pass: every quad reads its fill colour, and the ring holds no 513/10.

G74.approach:
The gap is real and fixable as tooling alone. Reading d3dprobe.c in full shows the tool has a bigger problem than its coverage list: five ways for a check that never ran to come out green.
(a) An unknown --tests name is only logged (d3dprobe.c:1240-1241), so `--tests mipdxt1` is a 0-check run with rc 0. The runner fails only SKIPPED names.
(b) The list is copied into char[512] (:1538), so a long list is cut silently.
(c) A test whose BeginScene fails returns with no entry.
(d) A failed back-buffer lock leaves the previous frame in g_px, and the next checks compare it (:300-343).
(e) `present` records nothing in fullscreen.
On top of that, the 16 KB RESULT buffer built with msvcrt _vsnprintf (which returns -1 on truncation) makes any run of more than about 170 checks unparsable, so big suites cannot be run.

Plan, in five phases. Nothing in vcrdd.dll or vcrmp.sys changes.

A. Framework and runner (lands first).
- An X-macro test registry in a new Win32-free tools/d3dprobe_core.h. Suites: @core = today's default list byte for byte, plus @tex11, @g74, @whole, @known and @Gnn. Planned names are refused with their owner. Every name is validated before Direct3DCreate8. A test that records no check fails. --deadline ends a run before the agent's tree kill.
- Outcome model, generalising G12's cell framework: ok / xfail (pixel equals the owning gap's predicted legacy value) / fail / skip / na / note. --fixed and --expect legacy are supported, and a self-check requires |want - legacy| >= 3 x tol.
- Reference values in a new include/vcr_d3dref.h, beside G12's vcr_texop_ref.h: blend, compare, fog, address, the bilinear texel-centre models, the fill rule, D16 quantisation and the cell pattern. It also carries vcr_legacy_* models of today's HAL.
- Readback: the same LockRect call, copying any window (`--origin tl|br|X,Y`) or the whole target, with alpha kept. It also reads lockable render targets, D16_LOCKABLE Z and GetFrontBuffer surfaces. Out-of-window and stale-frame checks fail. Whole-target diffs report bad row and column runs. BMP dumps are written.
- `--wsize` gives windowed whole-target runs with no mode switch.
- One paced create_device() helper; `--device-per-test` (windowed only).
- RESULT schema 2: a growable buffer, old keys unchanged, plus diag and opened_hz.
- The *_def tests become na (D3D8 locks a DEFAULT-pool texture only with DYNAMIC), and a new def_lock check records the runtime's refusal.
- Runner: --pace defaults to 5000 and is also fed into execw_budget (the 11-12 paced wrapper did not raise the budget). Also --hz with exact gating, a mode table pinned against the probe's, a screensaver preflight, a refused-pair guard (a windowed devcaps check before any fullscreen --zfmt), --ring (the driver's 513 events; unexpected refusals fail the run), --save with the driver md5, and --before glide-abandon (attended only).

B. caps v2 and devcaps.
- caps v2 prints every D3DCAPS8 field and the formats and usages runtime-27 lists, plus hal_windowed. It is compared against a committed caps golden.
- devcaps uses a windowed device and makes no mode switch: GetAvailableTextureMem delta (G64), render-target and dynamic creates, and real Z pairs. D16 at 32 bpp shows as xfail G10 without the double switch.

C. This item's own checks of implemented but unchecked behaviour: selfcheck, wclear, wgrad, wz, wtex, clearrect, atest, blendmx (implemented pairs only), zfunc, zwrite, zread, address, bilinear (classifies G81), repeat (G89), fogexp/exp2, vbib (VB/IB and the XYZ path), presentfs, placesweep and def_lock. It also lands G49's cull_prims and clipfan unchanged.
- Optional C2 lands the owners' single-frame known-gap cells as xfail, with their specified legacy values: mod2x, stage1_*, tfactor_tex, areplicate, usew, lines/points, mirror, d16_32.
- Every other proposed test is registered as PLANNED under its owner.

D. perf --mode: classic stays unchanged; setup and fill are added per G46 section 3.5. Every mode ends with a verification frame and reports the CPU user/kernel split and work_ms.

E. Optional: D3D9 inside the same exe through a dynamically loaded d3d9.dll (`--api 9`), for Halo and NewDark questions and rtt9.

G74.d3dprobe_test:
wgrad (whole-target coordinate grid), preceded in every non-default suite by selfcheck.

wgrad:
- What it draws: the frame is cleared to 0xff00ff, a colour no cell can have at 63 columns or fewer. The whole target (fullscreen at its mode, or windowed with --wsize WxH) is then covered by 32x32-pixel cells. Each cell is one flat untextured quad at integer coordinates, with Z, dither, blend and fog off. Under D3D8's integer pixel centres and the top-left rule, each pixel belongs to exactly one cell.
- Reference, vcr_ref_cell_rgb(cx,cy): R5 = cx & 31, G6 = cy & 63, B5 = ((cx>>5)&1)<<4 | ((cx^cy)&15), expanded as expand() expands 565. These values are exact at 16 and 32 bpp. Examples: cell (39,29) = 0x3975d6; cell (0,0) = 0x000000.
- Pass criterion: 0 mismatched pixels over the whole target, tolerance 0. The single entry reports of, bad, bbox, the first 8 bad pixels, and the bad row and column runs (signatures for SLI bands, 2PPC column pairs, pitch errors and lost lower halves).
- Old-buggy equivalent (the tool's own): the 256x256 window covered 64 of 1200 cells at 1280x960 and 64 of 768 at 1024x768.

Sibling whole-target checks:
- wz: full-target Z checkerboard over a z=0.5 layer. Even cells are green, odd cells red.
- wtex: a 256x256 random R5G6B5 texture tiled 1:1 over the target, with 0 wrong texels.
- wclear: clear to 0x08fba5 plus four 0xff00ff corner rects.

selfcheck: a planted wrong value must yield fail and a planted legacy value must yield xfail; an out-of-window pixel must be flagged; the window and full-target reads must agree.

G71.d3dprobe_test:
New explicit test 'avpstate', named with --tests and not in the default list, so the 40/42 counts stay comparable. It is run at 640x480x16 (AvP's mode) and at 1024x768x32, and on a GeForce box as the reference driver. It checks the D3D8-expressible half of AvP's pipeline with AvP's own vertex format.

Setup:
- Vertices: D3DFVF_TLVERTEX = XYZRHW|DIFFUSE|SPECULAR|TEX1 (0x1c4, stride 32). Specular is 0x00404040 with D3DRS_SPECULARENABLE FALSE, so every cell also proves that fvf_layout finds the texture coordinates after the specular slot and that a disabled specular adds nothing.
- Texture: a 64x64 R5G6B5, solid white, point-sampled.
- Stage 0: COLOROP MODULATE(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE) and ALPHAOP SELECTARG2(DIFFUSE), which is DX5 legacy MODULATE for a texture without alpha and the combine G08 maps it to. Stage 1 is DISABLE.
- Inputs: clear 0x406080; diffuse 0x80c0a040, so S = (c0,a0,40) and As = 0x80.
- Reference: D is read back from an untouched reference cell, which cancels 565 quantisation of the clear.

Eight 24x24 cells (32 bpp example values in brackets):
1. off: blend disabled, S [c0a040].
2. normal_valpha: SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, S*As + D*(1-As) [808060].
3. normal_talpha: the same blend with ALPHAOP SELECTARG1(TEXTURE), S [c0a040]. An RGB565 texel's alpha is 1.0; this is what AvP gets today without G08.
4. glowing: SRCALPHA/ONE, D + S*As [a0b0a0].
5. colour: ZERO/SRCCOLOR, D*S/255 [303c20].
6. invcolour: ZERO/INVSRCCOLOR, D*(255-S)/255 [102460].
7. darkening: INVDESTCOLOR/ZERO, S*(255-D)/255 [906420].
8. justsetz: ZERO/ONE with Z write at z 0.2, then an opaque red quad at z 0.5 with LESSEQUAL. Expect D [406080]; skipped under --noz.

Pass criterion: every channel within 16 at 16 bpp and within 6 at 32 bpp of the value computed from D3D's blend equation. Expected today: PASS. A failed cell means that blend factor is wrong on silicon, a G71 finding in blend_src/blend_dst that would hit AvP's matching translucency mode.

Culling is deliberately excluded: AvP sends CULLMODE NONE in hardware mode (avp.exe 0x4cf36c, mode set at 0x4dc831).

G75.approach:
The gap is real, and it can be closed with tooling and no driver change.

**What exists today.**
- d3dprobe is Direct3D 8 only: Direct3DCreate8 at d3dprobe.c:1307, linked with -ld3d8, and out/d3dprobe.exe imports d3d8.dll.
- So no lab test reaches any HAL path that only a DirectX 3-7 client uses:
  - D3DOP_EXIT (vcrdd_d3d.c:1773-1782);
  - op 3 with wFlags;
  - TEXTUREHANDLE;
  - the legacy states;
  - COLORKEYENABLE;
  - STATESET;
  - execute-buffer POINT/LINE;
  - TEXBLT from Load;
  - SETRENDERTARGET from DX7;
  - parse-unknown;
  - the legacy caps.
- The c6a3e93 EXIT fix that let Jedi Knight run is pinned only by a source grep.

**The plan's wording is half wrong.** A DX7 probe cannot send the legacy states. I read XP SP3's runtimes in disassembly (d3dim700 md5 56adb11f, d3dim md5 79e4ec1d, extracted from the fleet image):

- **F1. d3dim700 refuses the retired states.**
  - It has a 51-entry retired-state table at 0x739482a8: 1, 3, 5, 6, 11-13, 17, 18, 21, 31, 32, 39, 43-46, 49, 51 and 64-95.
  - IDirect3DDevice7::SetRenderState (0x7394f8c9, in all four device vtables) goes through the internal setter 0x73951237. For these states it stores the value in the runtime's array, then returns E_INVALIDARG 0x80070057 without emitting a token.
  - The legacy tests G08 needs must therefore use the DX6 runtime, d3dim.dll. A GUID scan shows it alone carries IDirect3D/2/3, Device/2/3, ExecuteBuffer and Texture/2.

- **F2. d3dim forwards every state 1-255 raw, but drops unchanged values.**
  - SetRenderState (0x6d921737) drops a value equal to its stored copy when device field +0xf50 >= 2. That field is likely the interface version (inferred).
  - SetTextureStageState (0x6d91b516) always drops an unchanged value.
  - So tests use forced delivery: set a different value first.
  - G08's legacy_order, as written, would be filtered and would fail against a correct HAL. It is re-sequenced here.

- **F3. Device7::SetRenderTarget depends on the device class.**
  - Via vtable +0x118 it either emits a DP2 SETRENDERTARGET (0x29), or destroys and re-creates the driver context (0x7394f2bf, with dwhContext=3 on input).
  - One class then re-sends render states 2-135 with no retired filter and no TSS (0x7394f28c). That is the only way a DX7 context could carry TEXTUREMAPBLEND, G08's hazard. d7_retarget settles which class vcrdd gets.

- **F4. ContextCreate's input dwhContext.** d3dim700 passes 3. d3dim passes [device+4]-1 at one site and 0 at another.

- **F5. A Microsoft reference with no 3D hardware.** Both runtimes carry the RGB software rasterizer, a no-hardware, no-mode-switch reference. Together with the 86Box bed's in-box 3dfx DX7 driver, that gives two independent checks of the probe's expected values.

**Design: one probe, two families.**
- `tools/d3d7probe.c`:
  - `dx7` family: IDirect3DDevice7 on d3dim700 (colour keys, state blocks, Load/TEXBLT, primitives and culling, SetRenderTarget).
  - `legacy` family: Device3, Device2 and Device1 execute buffers on d3dim (texture handles, legacy states, D3DOP_EXIT, edge flags, lines and points).
  - A `caps` mode: EnumDevices for IDirect3D7 and IDirect3D3.
- Render targets: offscreen by default (no mode switch, which also gives a candidate 16 bpp lane on the 32 bpp desktop), or `--full` (two switches paced by vcr_pace.h), or `--device rgb`.
- A fresh device per test, so each HAL context has a known interface and test.
- Readback by Lock, which drains the engine. Analytic per-pixel expected values, as d3dprobe uses.
- Each check is graded ok / old / bad against want and old values, with old_kind NONE, PINNED or EITHER.
- A canary stop (clear passes, no triangle drawn = G01/G02) and a per-step flushed log.
- `tools/d3d7probe_ref.h`: Win32-free. It holds the references, the execute-buffer encoder (with the OP_NOP for QWORD alignment and EXIT last) and the catalogue.
- `tools/d3d7probe_run.py`:
  - Before the run (read-only): `vcrctl info` for the armed flags, log_next_seq and exclusive_pid; and the G01 stale-cmdFifo0 refusal.
  - `--expect spec|old|auto`. In auto mode an armed fix must read want and an unarmed one must read old.
  - After the run: reads the ring (`vcrctl log`) and attributes 513/1 and 513/2 per test. That gives triangle counts and unparsed=0 for the exec tests.
  - Exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3.
- Caps goldens in `KMD/golden`.
- 30 core tests. The tests of G08, G09, G16, G24, G38, G15, G10, G37, G40 and G42 drop into the same frame.

**The driver and its old path.**
- G75 changes no driver byte, no caps and no register traffic. The old path stays byte-for-byte.
- The fixes this probe verifies keep their own default-off gating.

G78.approach:
The gap is real. With vsync on, every number the stack produces either stops at the refresh rate or does not exist:
- All four game sessions on 11-12 logged "flips of 0": the flip counters only count vsync'd flips, and the games flipped NOVSYNC.
- A game's flip-counter lines are logged at the first end point (exclusive end or mode off). In a game's teardown that point comes before about 1,000 DEBUG CreateSurfaceEx entries, and the ring holds 1,024, so the lines are gone before anyone fetches the ring. The d3dprobe rings kept theirs because its teardown is short.
- The refresh actually used is recorded nowhere. The gate printed 120 Hz and the runtime chose 85. UT2003 picked 640x480x16@120 against an ini of 60. UT2004 logs no refresh at all.
- No per-frame work time exists.
- Perf scenes are specified in five dialects across eight designs. The one scene that is built is fill-bound and checks nothing.
- The UT2004, Halo and UE1 benchmark routes do not end by themselves.

G78 delivers six parts:

**A. The frame record (driver).** A new pure-logic header, KMD/include/vcr_frames.h, holds a per-PDEV record of each present.
- **Per frame:** I (present-to-present), V and W.
  - V is the vsync wait: time inside "wait spans", opened when any flip_done() check answers "still drawing" (Flip, GetFlipStatus, Lock or Blt) and closed when one answers "done".
  - W = I − V: game, runtime, HAL and the drain inside the flip.
  - F is the cost inside the successful Flip call.
- **Histograms:** W/T in 1/32 T steps (68 bins), plus V and F histograms. Quantiles are reported as the upper bin edge, in ‰ of T.
- **L (refreshes per shown frame, 0 = superseded):** taken from a vsync clock built from the samples the flip path already takes. It detects the pulse sense from the duty cycle, anchors on in-pulse samples, and bootstraps the period inside a 1/64 trust band. L is exact when the phase is known; otherwise an expected-value estimate. The on-time rate and the 1/2/3+ histogram come from L.
- **Segments:** a 4 s gap with no present closes a segment. This separates menu, load and gameplay, and lets one d3dprobe device carry a whole sweep.
- **Also recorded:** milestones (ms to present 100/500/1k/2k/5k), the mode and the refresh used.
- **Logging:** the record is frozen at exclusive end or mode off, and emitted at DrvDisableDirectDraw, the owner's DestroyDDLocal, or the next session. Those points come after the teardown flood in all four game rings. Output is 8 INFO lines per segment under a new event, VCR_EV_DD_FRAMES.
- **Unchanged:** vcr_flip.h, the IOCTL sequence, every register access and every ddRVal. The only addition is at most one QPC per present.
- **Rules for the siblings:**
  - G46's HAL share uses the same frame boundary and excludes V.
  - G54's swap throttle counts as F, not V.
  - G59's 511 a=15/16 lines and `d3dprobe vsync` are folded in here.

**A'. Diag\D3DNoVsync.** Treats every DirectDraw flip as NOVSYNC (the vendor's SWAPINTERVAL/WaitOnVsync). Read at boot, written back to 0 at once, and a WARN is logged. Diagnostic only.

**B. The d3dprobe perf framework.**
- One grammar, with alias rows for each sibling dialect.
- RESULT schema perf_v 1: pid, hz_req, opened_hz from GetDisplayMode, client frame-time histogram, verify, and kpi = null unless the verification frame passes.
- `--hz` gates exactly that rate. `--pace` is folded in.
- All scenes are built from their owners' specs: classic (the loop byte for byte), setup, fill, state, upload, xform/clip/game, overlap. The new flip scene is G59's `vsync` extended with a `--work-sweep` that checks part A against the probe's own clock.

**C. glidelab tris.** Packet-3 triangle rate through grDrawVertexArrayContiguous, with the same geometry as `setup` and an exact lit-pixel check. This is G47's ceiling.

**D. d3dbench.py, d3dbench.json and framestats.py.** A harness built from the 11-12 gamerun.py.
- **Protocol:**
  - quiesce first, and dismiss the screensaver;
  - check `vcrctl reg 80024` == 0 before each run (until G01 lands);
  - a vcrctl mark anchors host time to the ring;
  - no SCREENSHOT or escape in the timed window;
  - games end by console exit or WM_CLOSE by pid, never a kill by image name;
  - the ring is fetched after exit;
  - 1 warm-up run plus 3 timed runs, median and range;
  - every row carries a stack label.
- **Recipes:** ut99-d3d (v56k_bench UT99Bench; vendor reference 70.35/69.5/69.11 fps), UT2003 flyby and botmatch, UT2004 botmatch (stat fps plus console exit), Halo timedemo (300 s cap, milestones), scripted segments, Red Faction timedemo (needs its disc).
- **Ledger:** EV/d3dbench/results.jsonl.
- **Verdict ladder (vsync on):**
  - holds: on time ≥ 99 % and W p95 ≤ 0.9 T;
  - judder: on time 90-99 %;
  - below: capacity and the L histogram;
  - invalid: novsync presents in a vsync-on run, a wrong mode, a focus loss, or a failed verify.

**E. 3DMark2000 Pro and 2001 SE.** Installed in the build VM and staged as library titles. Runs on .124 are supervised, one fresh process per run.

**hw-41 checks:** S4 (2PPC gain) and S7 (SLI scaling) run in G50's and G51's boots, using perf --mode fill plus `glidelab fill` as the ceiling, and the frame record at 1280x960 for the user-visible answer.

G78.gating:
**Part A, the frame record: default ON**, with a kill switch Diag\FrameStats = 0 (absent = 1).
- It is read at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO and carried as a negative bit, so an older miniport means on.
- The precedents are Accel2DPattern, GdiGamma, CoreClock and the 511/12-13 flip counters.
- This is allowed because the proven path stays byte for byte:
  - it is log-only, with no register access and no IOCTL on the drawing or flip path;
  - vcr_flip.h is untouched, so no completion answer can change;
  - the ordered call list and the ddRVal of Dd_Flip, Lock, Blt and GetFlipStatus are pinned by a test;
  - the only addition is at most one QPC per present.
- If the reviewer reads the rule strictly, the first supervised boot can ship with FrameStats = 0; the code is identical either way.

**Part A', Diag\D3DNoVsync: default OFF and self-clearing.**
- The miniport reads it at boot and writes it back to 0 at once, flushed, so an arm lasts one boot.
- It logs a WARN at boot, and every frame record says "NOVSYNC FORCED".
- Diagnostic only; never a default.

**Parts B-D (d3dprobe framework, glidelab tris, d3dbench, framestats):** user-mode and host tools.
- The classic d3dprobe loop is kept byte for byte.
- Every scene must pass its verification frame before it reports a speed.

**Part E, the 3DMark titles:** staged in the library; runs on .124 are supervised, and only after G02 has made a give-up visible.

**Rules for every run:**
- one Diag change per clean boot;
- a driver deploy = swap the binaries, check activation, then safe-reboot.py;
- the stale-FIFO gate (no D3D run after a Glide session until a clean modeseq or a cold boot) until G01 lands.
G78.d3dprobe_test:
**Test:** `perf --mode flip` (alias `vsync`, test key `frame_accounting`).

**Runs:**
- at 640x480x16@85 (negative vsync) and 1280x960x16@85 (positive vsync);
- one fullscreen device for the whole sweep: --hz 85, PresentationInterval ONE, --warmup 60 --frames 600;
- --work-sweep 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 1.05, 1.5 and 2.5 refreshes;
- one --novsync run at 640x480x16.

**What it draws, each frame:**
- a target clear alternating two colours;
- one 64x64 checker quad (the texture is set once, so no per-frame DEBUG event);
- a QPC busy-wait of w x T after Present.

Before the sweep, G59's 0.5 s GetRasterStatus window gives raster_hz and the duty. Between levels the probe makes no Present for 5 s, so the driver closes one segment per level. A verification frame at the end checks the quad's texels and the clear pixels. The host fetches the ring after the probe exits and runs `framestats.py --against`, matched by pid.

**Pass criteria:**

G77.approach:
The gap is real and fixable. The work is a pure refactor plus a test harness; it changes no register word, caps bit, event or Diag default.

STATE OF THE TREE
- The D3D state-to-register translation (blend_src/dst, cmp, color_path, stage1_combine, tex_view/tex_view_ext/view_of with pf_kind/pf_tmfmt, compute_regs, fvf_layout and prepare's coordinate-set binding; KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:270-362, 630-1029, 1254-1284, 1337-1363) lives in the DDI file. That file needs vcrdd.h and Microsoft's uncommitted d3dnthal.h, so the host only grep-tests it (test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:189-201 and others).
- The mapping has been unchanged since 7d2779b (09-28). HEAD's display/include files are identical to be58b7d, the source of vcrdd.dll 95678704.
- Its only recorded outputs are the words log_combo logged on silicon:
  - ONBOX/ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt seq 24863-24944 (d3dprobe, 11-12);
  - UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt (26 UT2003 set-ups, 11-08).

THE MOVE (step 1, one commit)
- Today's code moves unchanged into four Win32-free, integer-only headers, in the vcr_rtfmt.h / vcr_3dseq.h / vcr_texlod.h pattern:
  - include/vcr_d3denum.h: about 170 VCR_ + exact d3dtypes.h names (DX7 DDI numbering);
  - include/vcr_cmb_legacy.h: vcr_cmb_color_path and vcr_cmb_stage1 (G15's name for the legacy combine);
  - include/vcr_blend.h: vcr_blend_src/dst and vcr_blend_alphamode(s, d, flags) (G28/G29's name; flags 0 = today);
  - include/vcr_d3dstate.h: vcr_d3d_cmp, vcr_d3d_sampling, vcr_d3d_view(texdesc, tss, texpath, view), vcr_d3d_stage1_on, vcr_d3d_regs(in, regs, out), vcr_d3d_fvf_layout, vcr_d3d_bind_sets, and the DX7 caps words (MISC 0x72, RASTER 0x1001b1, SRCBLEND 0x1f33, DESTBLEND 0x3f, SHADE 0x500a, TEXTURE 0xf, TEXFILTER 0x03010317, TEXADDRESS 0x15, TEXOP 0x184f, ...).
- vcr3d_regs moves to include/vcr_3dseq.h with vcr_u32 fields (G53's chosen home).
- The HAL keeps only:
  - handle lookups;
  - texdesc_of(), which copies DD_SURFACE_LOCAL fields and walks the mip chain to 12;
  - the lazy stage-1 view;
  - the refusal log and log_combo;
  - the float calls (VcrDd3dTexScale and the others).
- The HAL's rs/tss/tss1 arrays become vcr_u32, asserted the same size as DWORD.
- prim_caps and the extended caps assign the header constants.
- A static-assert block, VCR_D3D_SAME(x) as typedef char vcr_same_##x[(VCR_##x == (x)) ? 1 : -1], proves every number equal to the DDK's in every HAL_DDI build. Both pastes keep a macro name unexpanded.

BYTE-FOR-BYTE RULES THE MOVE KEEPS
- TMU fields and fog_table stay untouched when unused.
- min(levels, 9) on the default path, 12 on the VSA-100 path.
- has_pixfmt's NT rule; the FOURCC flag kept apart from the code.
- No memset, float, long or library call in a header.
- Scale sizes are always written; they are never read unless textured.
- fvf_layout's undefined TEXCOUNT 9-15 case is refused in a separate follow-up commit. A valid runtime cannot reach it.

THE HARNESS (step 2)
- The oracle: tests/native/ref/vcrdd_d3d_be58b7d.c, verbatim line ranges of be58b7d's vcrdd_d3d.c. It is generated from git by extract_be58b7d.py and compiled against a names-only fake DDI.
- tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_d3dstate.c asserts header == oracle at feat = 0:
  - colour and alpha halves and stage 1 exhaustively;
  - the blend × alpha-test matrix, views over every texture path, fvf and bind;
  - 200k random whole states compared struct for struct from a shared sentinel.
- It also reproduces the 34 silicon-logged set-ups, pins a gap ledger of today's wrong words with gap ids, and checks caps against the translation.
- tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_d3dstate.py guards the architecture:
  - the HAL composes no register word;
  - every VCR_ number is asserted against the DDK;
  - the oracle matches the git object;
  - 12 one-line mutants each fail the native test, among them the pre-d716d6f fbzColorPath without PARMADJUST;
  - the headers compile -mgeneral-regs-only.
- The existing text assertions are re-pointed to stronger behavioural ones.

LATER ITEMS
- vcr_d3d_regs is the one place each word is composed. Each item extends its slot behind its Diag\D3DFeat bit, which arrives through in.feat (0 until an item adds D3DFeat).
- The oracle test therefore keeps feat = 0 write-for-write build 95678704 for G05, G08, G09, G12-G15 and G22-G35 at once.
- An item that later deletes its off path must mark its inputs in ref_differs_by_design() and update its ledger row.

ON SILICON (steps 4-5)
- d3dprobe statemap (53 cells, using vcr_texop_ref.h, shared with G12/G15) proves that the box computes the words the host executes, through the ring's 513/21-22 events.
- At the same time it pins each op's, argument's and factor's ideal or documented-degradation pixel.

Rejected alternatives:
- building the whole DDI file on the host against a fake DDI (a second copy of Microsoft's interface for changing code);
- a Diag switch between two identical copies of the translation;
- a hand-transcribed oracle.

Games unblocked: none directly. This is tooling, and it carries the regression tests of the fixes that do unblock games (G05 UT2003/UT2004, G12-G14, G17 Halo, G22-G35).

G81.approach:
INVESTIGATED HERE FROM FRAMES ALREADY ON DISK. Verdict: no driver change. The gap is real only as an evidence gap, and most of it is now closed.

(1) MAX PAYNE'S EDGE WAS THE PIXEL HALF AND NOTHING ELSE.
- Compared .124's pre-fix 10-04 frame (HOSTEV/fbab_maxpayne_probe.png, md5 744e9f85, build b63ea6a5) with the NVIDIA reference of the same menu at the same 1280x960: /home/voidsstr/lan-proof/box133/maxpayne_menu_1280x960_nodialog.png, .133 GeForce4 Ti, md5 44a2658d.
- Our frame is the reference displaced by exactly (+0.50, +0.50) px. On the text-free right half the MAD is 0.16 luma at that shift, against 0.33-0.40 at ±0.125 px and 4.8 unshifted. The parabolic refinement is (+0.498, +0.493).
- The per-row model "ours = ref half a pixel on" fits columns 1278/1279 with MAD < 0.1 luma. It also fits the picture's top and bottom rows: 13.0 = (17.3+8.7)/2, 4.4 = 8.7/2, 16.8, 5.6, 3.3, 10.1.
- IMPORTANT: on NVIDIA, Max Payne's own column 1279 is exactly half its neighbour (8.7 vs 17.3, median ratio 0.500). So the fixed build's target is the reference, NOT "column 1279 equals column 1278"; that naive check would fail a correct HAL.

(2) THE TEXEL HALF NEEDS NO OFFSET.
- The same fit bounds any texel-centre error on TMU0 bilinear at 32 bpp to about 0.01 px.
- G45 found the same on DXT5 at 16 bpp (about 0.05 texel).
- rgb565/dxt1/dxt5_decode1 and dxt5_big_c (TBIG) are texel-exact at 1:1 point.
- 3dfx's textureCenter[log2 size] = 1/2^(slog+1) is added AFTER the x256 scale (VH5/D6TRI2I.C:958-984). It is therefore a 1/512-texel tie-break nudge (2^aspect/512 on the narrow side), not the "half a texel" their 1998 log claims. Copying it as a real half texel would re-create the decode1 failure everywhere.

(3) MORE FINDINGS.
- 11-08 pairs: Red Faction and H&D moved exactly (+0.5, +0.5) px.
- Thief II's pre-fix frame equals post-fix shifted one whole pixel for 89.6 % of pixels exactly: point-sampled 1:1 UI, decode1's texel (x+1, y+1) signature in a game.
- No post-fix frame lost a first column or row.
- Four of the five G81 titles draw D3D-correct (-0.5) quads. Max Payne's backdrop is probably naive 0..W, so its column 0 is a silicon tie-rule reading.
- 3dfx's later Win9x HAL ships pixelOffset = 0.5 + 1/32 (W9X/D3RSTATE.C:3851-3855, RETAIL .COD:8645), with no log entry. On paper it equals rounding if the setup unit truncates (86Box's model), and it breaks every exact edge if the unit rounds half-up.
- MesaFX on the same chip uses 0 xy offset and no texel term, which is consistent with ours.

(4) WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN ON SILICON, AND IS DESIGNED HERE AS MEASUREMENTS:
- Q1: the fill rule for a pixel centre exactly on an edge. The 0.5 bias puts every integer D3D edge there. This is also G16 open question 3.
- Q2: the setup unit's float-to-12.4 conversion.
- Q3: point sampling exactly on a texel edge (naive 0..W quads after the 11-08 fix). This is where the vendor nudge matters.
- Q4: the sub-texel centre on TMU1, on TBIG levels and on DXT1 in stage 1.
- Q5: bilinear weight precision.

(5) DELIVERABLES (default; no driver behaviour change):
- the d3dprobe centre family (texc1, texc_naive, texc_phase/_t, texc_phase_tmu1/_tmu0b/_big/_dxt1/_dxt1_tmu0b, pixedge, pixsnap);
- reference functions in G74's vcr_d3dref.h (G81 creates it if G74 has not landed);
- host and native regression tests;
- the Max Payne confirmation capture, inside G04's attended Boot 1 E0a;
- documentation: the plan status, a FINDINGS.md entry (clean-room lane), the README d3dprobe list, and a tests/README row.

(6) CONDITIONAL CORRECTIONS. Only on measured evidence, each default OFF behind Diag\D3DCentre (a DWORD read at boot like D3DBigTex, passed through vcr_info). None is expected.

G93.approach:
VERDICT: the hardware claim is right, and the plan's wording hides a correctness hole that exists today. renderMode[1:0]=1 renders ARGB1555 (SPEC L3291/L3304). renderMode[16:15] picks the stored alpha bit: 0 forces 0, 1 forces 1, 2 stores the MSB of the alpha after alpha blending (L3294/L3308). At 15 bpp the 1-bit destination alpha is automatic, fbzMode[18] must stay clear, the bit is written whenever RGB is (fbzMode[9]), fbzMode[10] is the 16-bit depth buffer, FASTFILL stores zaColor[31] in mode 2, and the alpha-channel factors are ZERO/ONE only (SPEC §21.5 L6229-6232, L2696-2699, L2974-2983).

TODAY: target_of (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1047-1085) classifies a target by bit count only (surf_bpp). Every 16-bit target becomes VCR_RT_16 and is drawn as 565 with renderMode 0x001e0000, whether it is A1R5G5B5, X1R5G5B5 or A4R4G4B4. Example: a grey 0x808080 clear stores 0x8410, which a 1555 reader sees as alpha 1, colour (8,0,132). Nothing refuses it or logs it. The vendor HALs: 3dfx Win9x had the same bug; 3dfx NT detects red mask 0x7c00 (VH5/D3GLOBAL.H:836/873) but never sets [16:15], so its 1555 targets always stored alpha 0, and it still drew 4444 as 565. Neither of those is copied.

WHO CAN REACH IT. D3D8/9 titles never can through a DX7 DDI. The runtime PCI table entry 121a:0009 is 0x4580 (I re-read it in d3d8.dll at offset 0xc40 and d3d9.dll at 0x1410). Its per-format code (d3d8 0x6d9af2e7-0x6d9af319) needs flag 0x800 (A1R5G5B5) or 0x2000 (X1R5G5B5), and both are absent; the registry can only clear flags. No display mode is 15 bpp (vcr_modes.c:162-166), so no back buffer is ever 555. Only a DX3-7 app that renders into a 555 surface it created itself (an RT texture or an off-screen 3DDEVICE surface) reaches it. A case-insensitive string scan of the staged DX5-7 binaries finds no render-target strings, so no staged title is known to use one.

G93.gating:
The switch is one bit of the shared Diag\D3DFeat word, RT15. It defaults to OFF, is a positive bit, and is read at boot into the appended vcr_info.d3dfeat (DSN/G05.md §4.2 recipe). It applies to the VSA-100 only (pd->rt15 = napalm && bit). The proposed position is bit 16 (0x10000), above the 0-15 that earlier designs claim; the integrator assigns the final number. If no D3DFeat item has landed yet, this one lands the plumbing by that recipe.

With the bit off:
- vcr_rt_format_layout returns its input, vcr_3d_target_seq15 is unreachable, and vcr_rt_fill_za returns zv for 16/32 bpp. Every register write and every ContextCreate/SETRENDERTARGET/Clear2 answer is today's, byte for byte.
- The one always-on addition is a once-per-(context, surface) log record for 16-bit targets that are not 565. A proven 565/8888 run never produces it: no register write and no extra event on the proven path.
- Caps are unchanged in both states. The bit is declared not caps-relevant, so G75's caps golden ignores it.

NOT safe to land default-on:
- renderMode[16:15]=2 has never been set by any 3dfx software (Glide or either vendor HAL), so it is unproven silicon.
- Armed, the bit changes an answer an application gets: a 4444 or other 16-bit target is refused.

Proving it: arm the bit alone, one Diag change, in one supervised clean boot after an activation check and safe-reboot.py.

Graduation (absent = on) needs two things:
- the hosted d3d7probe set passes on silicon;
- the always-on layout record has run through one fullscreen D3D sweep of the DX5-7 titles.

If that record shows a title creating a 4444/other target, graduate the 1555 half first and decide the refusal with that title in front of you.

Readback is Lock after EndScene, checked at the centres of 96x96 quads, so a target placed off the 16-byte grid (G36) cannot move a check point out of its quad. Tests, with pass values; "old" is today's 565 encoding:
1. d7_rt565_ctl, R5G6B5 control.
   - Scene: clear 0x808080; quads 0x808080, 0x00ff00, 0xff0000, 0x0000ff.
   - Pass: 8410; 8410, 07e0, f800, 001f. Identical with RT15 armed and off.
2. d7_rt1555, A1R5G5B5.

   - Pass: clear c210; quads 4210, 4210, c210, 83e0. This proves the MSB alpha mode.
   - Old: 8410; 8410, 8410, 8410, 07e0 (pinned).
3. d7_rt1555_clr0: clear 0x7f00ff00.

4. d7_rtx555, X1R5G5B5, the same scene.

5. d7_rt1555_blend: SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA of 0x80ff0000 over 0x404040.
   - Pass: colour (0x9f,0x20,0x20) within ±1 LSB at 5 bits; stored alpha bit 1.
6. d7_rt4444.
   - Armed: CreateDevice returns DDERR_INVALIDPIXELFORMAT 0x88760091, plus the ring's layout-refused record.

Pass criterion: exact 16-bit words for clears and flat quads, ±1 LSB for the blend, ±8 for the sampled colours. Grades are ok/old/bad.

G93.risk:
Low to the proven paths.
- Default 16 bpp D3D: no change. With the bit off, vcr_rt_format_layout is the identity, vcr_3d_target_seq is not edited, and vcr_rt_fill_za returns zv for 16/32 bpp. A 565 target never reaches the new log record. Pinned by the native tests and by d7_rt565_ctl.
- 16 bpp D3D with the bit armed: 565 is recognised by its masks whatever the flags, and a surface with no masks keeps today's answer (refuse only on positive evidence). The d3dprobe 16/32 bpp 40/40 runs repeat in the armed boot.
- 32 bpp D3D: never touches the layout code.
- Glide/OpenGL coexistence: none. Both sides write renderMode whole (Glide's _grRenderMode writes from its own shadow), and the 15 bpp sequence also zeroes stencilMode/stencilOp.
- SLI state: none. D3D renders single-chip, and the writes are chip-0 broadcast like the existing sequences.
- Flip path: none. There is no 15 bpp display mode, so no flip chain is ever 1555.
- Memory: 15 bpp has 565's 2-byte geometry and 16-bit aux buffer, so it adds no new out-of-bounds risk. The off-16-byte-grid placement hazard of render targets is G21/G36's and exists today.

Real risks, all confined to the armed bit:
1. The MSB alpha mode (renderMode[16:15]=2) has never been set by Glide or either 3dfx HAL, so its silicon behaviour is unknown. The lab checks all three values first, supervised, and first-time paths run last. If MSB fails, ship X1R5G5B5 (forced 1) and refuse A1R5G5B5.
2. A DX5-7 app whose 4444/other 16-bit target 'worked' with wrong colours now gets CreateDevice refused. The bit is default OFF, and the always-on record names any such title before graduation.
3. The 1-bit alpha cannot reproduce D3D's blended-alpha formula. That is a format limit (ZERO/ONE alpha factors at 15 bpp), documented.
open_questions: Does any staged DX5-7 title, or a dormant D3D renderer of a Glide/OpenGL title, create a non-565 16-bit render target? A static scan of 14 binaries found no render-target strings (weak evidence). The always-on layout record answers it on the next sweep; if one does, the priority rises to P2.
Does renderMode[16:15]=2 really store the alpha MSB on VSA-100 silicon? No 3dfx software (Glide, NT or Win9x HAL) ever set it. If it does not, ship X1R5G5B5 only and refuse A1R5G5B5.
With alpha blending disabled (alphaMode[4]=0), is the stored MSB the colour path's alpha, as SPEC L3308 reads? d7_rt1555 quads A-D answer it.

Does d3dim700/d3dim pass a 555 3DDEVICE surface to ContextCreate (inferred: they check only the DDBD bit depth)? Does dxg accept a 16-bit 3D off-screen surface on the 32 bpp desktop (G75's offscreen16), and does SetRenderTarget across 565/1555 work, or does it need a second device?

Should an armed driver also refuse 4444/other TEXTURE|3DDEVICE surfaces at Dd_CanCreateSurface, as 3dfx did, so apps learn it at creation? Not in this item, because it would also refuse surfaces that are never drawn to.
X1R5G5B5's stored bit: forced 1 was chosen (D3D's alpha-1.0 rule; opaque when sampled as ARGB1555). Revisit only if a title is found that reads it.
Is .124's own d3d8.dll/d3d9.dll identical to the fleet image's copy that was read (table 0x4580)? d3dprobe caps' RT-format rows confirm it on the box.
Should the same layout check extend to 32-bit targets with non-ARGB masks (BGR 8888)? No DX7 enumeration offers one, so it is left out.
