G91.approach:
VERDICT: G91 cannot be fixed through the current (DX7) DDI. I settled this offline by disassembling the XP SP3 runtimes (d3d8.dll and d3d9.dll 5.3.2600.5512, md5 f099b129... and 0607cbc6..., the same files REP/runtime.md read). The hardware half of the gap is right.

HARDWARE (confirmed):
- fogMode[8]/[9] (RGB) and [10]/[11] (alpha) give S*a + D*b, S*a - D*b and D*b - S*a (SPEC §8.22 L2853-2856, §8.23.2 L2924-2946).
- Negative results clamp to 0 in 3dfx's chip model (CSIM/FBI.C:1410-1440). The SPEC says nothing, so blendop quad 3 checks it on silicon.
- MIN and MAX do not exist.
- renderMode[20:17] masks R/G/B/A at 32 bpp only (L3295-3312). fbzMode[9] masks all of RGB at every depth (L3256).
- So on R5G6B5 and X8R8G8B8 targets the masks 0x0, 0x7, 0x8 and 0xF are exact through fbzMode[9] alone. Only partial RGB masks at 16 bpp cannot be done.

RUNTIMES (the decisive evidence):
- Caps pass through. d3d8 copies the DX7 dpcTriCaps.dwMiscCaps into PrimitiveMiscCaps (0x6d9aeb01-04) and clears only MASKPLANES and CONFORMANT (and $0xfffffff6 at 0x6d9af0b7). d3d9 does the same (0x4fdfb231, 0x4fdfb822).
- So COLORWRITEENABLE (0x80) and BLENDOP (0x800) set in our caps WOULD be reported. The gap's proposed experiment (set the bits, read d3dprobe caps) would show 0x8f2: a false positive.
- The states never arrive. IDirect3DDevice8::SetRenderState (0x6d9d2940, CD3DHal slot 50) calls the setter in slot 98 (0x6d9d4890). That setter stores the value and calls the DDI only when the state is below m_dwMaxRenderState (cmp 0x390 at 0x6d9d499a).
- That limit is DDI->GetMaxRenderState() = 0x88 (136, D3DRENDERSTATE_CLIPPING) for the DX6 and DX7 DDI classes (d3d8 0x6d9e2110; d3d9 0x4fe79010, gate at 0x4fe678e6).
- So COLORWRITEENABLE (168), BLENDOP (171) and D3D9's SEPARATEALPHABLEND* (206-209) never reach a DX6/DX7 driver. DX8 and DX9 DDIs get them (d3d8 below 172, or 256 with a flag; d3d9 below 256).
- The reports: hal-35's reason ("hardware limit") is wrong, since only MIN/MAX are impossible, but its conclusion (don't claim them) is right. hal-34 is half right: the runtime reads the cap but drops the state. vendor-21 is right.

DECISION:
- The caps stay 0x72. Advertising the bits would be a lie: an application that tests them would get techniques silently drawn as ADD with full writes.
- Rejected: reading lpdwRStates at DP2 time. A DP2 buffer holds many draws, so the last value set would apply to the whole batch.
- Rejected: PLANEMASK. The runtimes never translate COLORWRITEENABLE into it.

LANDS NOW (effort S, diagnostics only, default-on):
- A comment in prim_caps plus a host guard test: 0x72 passes, 0x8f2 is refused, and the HAL still has no GETDRIVERINFO2.
- A new context-summary event 24 in the HAL: the highest render state received and the number at or above 136. This proves the drop on silicon at the next deploy.
- d3dprobe tests blendop and cwmask. Today they report "dropped" and skip. They become pass/fail once the states arrive.
- Errata appended to the reports and README.

FOR G94 (specified in the design §6):
- vcr_blendop.h: SUB sets fogMode 0xa00, REVSUB 0xf00 (the alpha op follows the RGB op).
- MIN becomes S*D (src A_COLOR / dst ZERO; alpha DSTA / ZERO). MAX becomes S + D*(1-S) (ONE / AOM_COLOR; alpha ONE / 1-SRCA). Both are exact when an operand is 0 or 1, and are off by at most 1/4.
- vcr_cw_map: nothing to write clears FZ_RGBWRITE. A partial mask at 32 bpp sets renderMode[20:17] = mask<<17 (a sync register, shadowed). At 16 bpp a partial mask draws all channels and is counted.
- ctx_defaults must set rs[168] = 0xF and rs[171] = ADD. Today's memset leaves 0, which would blank every draw.
- Clear must restore renderMode, because the mask must not affect Clear.
- One renderMode composer, shared with G50 (2ppc band) and G57 (guard band).
- Caps: advertise COLORWRITEENABLE. Honour BLENDOP but never advertise it, since MIN/MAX are approximations.

HALO:
- halo.exe calls SetRenderState(COLORWRITEENABLE) at 63 sites (0xF x9, 0x7 x43, 0x8 x5, 0x0 x4) and SetRenderState(BLENDOP) at 54 sites. It never reads PrimitiveMiscCaps.
- It uses REVSUBTRACT for its "subtract" framebuffer blend and its darken screen flash, and MIN/MAX for component min/max and the min/max flashes (blend tables at 0x65dfbc, 0x65dfe0, 0x65e004).
- On .124 today, "subtract" and "darken" draw as ADD and brighten instead of darkening.
- Its depth-only and alpha-only passes would also write colour, if they run on the fixed-function path. One alpha-only pass is PS-1.1-gated (G28); the gating of the rest is unknown.
- MinMaxBlendOpIsBroken (config keyword, sets 0x722b7c) changes only the MIN/MAX uses.
- How much of this shows in gameplay is measured inside G67. The result feeds G94's priority.

Two new tests go after 'blend' in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c. Both draw 48x48 untextured quads (quad_c) and read back with expect(), tolerance 6 at 32 bpp and 10 at 16 bpp.

G89.approach:
Verdict: the limit is real, but the gap states it 4x too small, and its cap half is a plain caps bug. The full design is in voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G89.md.

1) The range. 14.18 is only the format of the integer MMIO registers (startS/startT/dSdX, SPEC L2244-2245, L2568). vcr-kmd never writes those. It writes the setup unit's float registers sS/W0, sT/W0, sS/Wtmu1, sT/Wtmu1 (vcrdd_3d.c:213-220).
- 3dfx's own Napalm C simulator states the internal format: S/W, T/W and 1/W are 48-bit signed 16.32 (H5/CSIM/H3SIM.H:40-57).
- The setup unit converts each float to 32 fraction bits and masks it to 48 bits, so it wraps (CSIM/SETUP.C:550-561, 660-705). The span iterators are masked the same way (CSIM/GO.C:239-244).
- The TREX bit model agrees: TREXFUNC.H:402/410 says "16.32 signed".
- So the true limit is |S/W| < 32768, i.e. |u| x rhw < 128 at our 256 scale (not +/-32). rhw above 2 is fine, because W is 16.32 too.
- Beyond the limit the value wraps mod 65536. That is invisible whenever 256/rhw is a whole number, so every 2D/HUD quad at rhw 1 is immune. Perspective triangles show depth-banded, shifted but correctly coloured texture.
- The Napalm LOD unit computes the true perspective derivative, (d(S/W) - S*dW)*W (CSIM/LOD.C:58-73; TREXFUNC.C lod_calc_sq_term). An integer offset therefore does not move the mip level. 86Box/MAME omit that term and never wrap, so the 86Box bed cannot show the limit.
- Precision: the TMU normalises S/W to a 20-bit mantissa, so the texel error is of the order of |S| x 2^-19. That is about 1/8 texel at |u| = 256, and x8 on 2048-wide textures.

2) The cap. 3dfx reported dwMaxTextureRepeat 256 + D3DPTEXTURECAPS_TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE, which is exactly the 16.32 range.
- W2K: VH5/D3INIT.C:2824-2826, 3027-3029, 3204-3210, with DDFXNT95.H:70.
- Win9x retail: STBPERF.INC:85 "Per Gary Tarolli"; RETAIL/D3INIT.COD:6699 and 6786 store 256 at offset 36.
- So hw-28 is right, and hal-26's 32768 is the unused #else branch. We report 0 and no flag (vcrdd_d3d.c:2034-2035, 2150-2173).

3) Which titles could exceed it: none is known to.
- The 11-12 confetti is multi-coloured, which points at foreign memory (G06/G07), not at a wrap.
- Candidates: Halo (detail maps, small near plane) and BF1942 LAN (terrain detail); Max Payne and Red Faction are also possible. UE2 is unlikely (rhw <= 1).

Plan:
- Step 0, census (log-only, default-on). st_scan() in VcrDd3dTriangle counts per-context max |S/W|, |S| and rhw, plus over-8k/16k/32k, clamp, invisible-wrap and precision buckets. It logs 513/STCENSUS at ctx_free and 513/STFIRST once. It writes no register.
- Step 1, measure on silicon with four d3dprobe tests: texrepeat, texrepeat_span, texrepeat_lod, texrepeat_prec. A native-tested oracle predicts the 16.32 and 14.18 outcomes.
- F0: report 256 + TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE in prim_caps and the extended caps. Default-on, no switch, in the first HAL build after E1 confirms the number (64 if E1 measures 14.18).
- F1, only if the in-game census finds at-risk WRAP triangles in a staged title, behind Diag\D3DFeat bit STREBASE (default OFF):
  - per triangle and per rebasable axis, subtract an integer k (a multiple of 2 for MIRROR/G33);
  - the rebasable mask comes from the TMU's own TM_CLAMPS/TM_CLAMPT bits; CLAMP axes are never touched;
  - k comes from a q-weighted minimax over the three vertices, and is chosen only when the old |S/W| >= 16384 or |S| crosses the precision threshold;
  - pure header KMD/include/vcr_strebase.h. vertex() keeps today's expression textually on the NULL branch (G45/G81 pin it);
  - this is exact for WRAP and LOD-neutral. A rebased triangle is never strip-continued (G49).
- F2, per-triangle W normalisation: rejected, because W is 16.32. Revived only if E1's rhw > 2 cells fail.
- Also rejected: triangle splitting, per-batch offsets, always-rebase, reporting 32768, and leaving 0.

Priority P2: caps hygiene plus a cheap investigation that rides the planned instrumentation boot. It becomes P1 if the census finds a staged title over the limit on a WRAP axis.

- Step 0 census: default-on, no switch. It is log-only: no register write and no changed answer, so the proven 16 bpp path's register traffic stays byte for byte (hal.md section 10 Phase 0 category, pinned by a Python test).
- d3dprobe tests: explicit only, never in the default list.
- F0 (dwMaxTextureRepeat 256 + TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE): safe to land default-on without a switch. It is a report-only correctness fix whose number E1 measures on silicon and that 3dfx shipped on this chip family. It lands in the first HAL build after E1 and is verified by d3dprobe caps plus texrepeat/texrepeat_span in that build's deploy boot. If E1 has not run, it stays 0. If E1 measures the 14.18 behaviour, report 64.
- F1 rebase: default OFF behind Diag\D3DFeat bit STREBASE (bit number assigned by the integrator; siblings already propose bits 0-10).
  - It is read once at boot in VcrFindAdapter, carried in vcr_info.d3dfeat (G05's carrier), set in pd->st_rebase, and logged as 513/STARMED.
  - It is built only if the in-game census finds at-risk WRAP triangles in a staged title.
  - It is proven in one supervised clean boot where setting STREBASE is the only Diag change, then graduates to default-on as a per-feature kill bit.

G89.d3dprobe_test:
Four new tests, plus one caps field. All four fit the 256x256 readback window and are compared against analytic ideal-WRAP values. A native-tested oracle (vcr_ref_st_hw) predicts what the 16.32 and 14.18 iterators would show, so cells are classified (ideal, wrap16, wrap14, sat, other); predicted G89 failures are xfail, not plain FAIL.

(1) texrepeat (E1): about 45 cells of 128x8 px, each with constant rhw q and u from k to k+1, on a 256x256 R5G6B5 texture with 16 colour bands in u (or in v), point sampled. There are 16 band-centre samples per cell. Groups:
- A: q=1, k up to 1000 and down to -129. Expected ideal: the wrap is invisible.
- B: q=0.75, k=0/40/43/169/170/171/200/-171/-172/342/2000. Expected: ideal below |S/W| 32768. Beyond it, one wrap reads band (i-5) mod 16. Cell 170 straddles and shows the in-cell accumulator wrap at band 11. Under 14.18 the first wrap appears already at k=43, and k=171 reads (i+5) (two wraps).
- C: q=0.6.
- D: q=2/3/16/40, which checks that rhw > 2 works.
- E: the T axis.
- F: TMU1 in two-stage mode, guarded by a k=0 reference cell.
Pass: every sample equals its band colour (tolerance 12). Result fields: limit_sw, mode, w_path.

(2) texrepeat_span (E2): 256x8 px cells with 32-128 repeats on a red/blue half texture, sampled at the quarter points. Rows: centred [-32,32] at q=0.75 (ideal); [150,214] and [1000,1064] at q=0.75 (xfail now, ideal with F1); [-64,64] at q=1 and [-16,16] at q=3 (ideal); [-64,64] at q=3 (unfixable even with F1, counted).

(3) texrepeat_lod (E3): a 9-level solid-colour mip chain on two perspective quads side by side, k=0 against k=24 (frame 2: k=100). Pass: the level read in each of 30 rows is equal left and right (at most 2 rows off by one level). This tests the Napalm LOD's offset invariance.

(4) texrepeat_prec (E3b): magnified 1-texel bands (8 px per texel) at k=0..3000 with |S/W| held at 16384. Pass: centre and edge samples exact. On today's HAL this is a precision note (edges predicted to miss from k of about 130-400); with F1 it must be exact.

(5) caps: prints MaxTextureRepeat. Expected 0 / TextureCaps 00004007 today, 256 / 00004047 after F0.

G89.risk:
Low.
- Default 16 bpp path: the census adds CPU-only reads and counters inside the existing FPU bracket, with no register traffic change. F0 changes two caps only. F1 off is byte-identical; F1 on is byte-identical for every triangle below the thresholds, which covers the whole default d3dprobe gate.
- No effect on Glide/OpenGL coexistence, SLI state, the flip path or the miniport. No new hardware access, wait or allocation.
- FPU rule kept: all float work stays in vcrdd_3d.c, vcrdd_d3d.c computes only an integer mask, and the census struct is ULONG-only.
- Specific risks:
  - A wrong-axis rebase would shift a CLAMP texture. Prevented because the mask comes from the TMU's own TM_CLAMPS/T bits, pinned by native and Python tests.
  - Caps visible to applications: no staged title is known to branch on MaxTextureRepeat (Halo only dumps it); covered by the boot A' menu pass.
  - Interaction with G49 strips: rebased triangles are never continued.
  - G45's source test pins vertex()'s expression; it is kept textually on the NULL branch.
- Cost: about 30 x87 operations per textured triangle for the census and about 40 more per at-risk axis for F1, negligible against 27-45 uncached PCI writes.
- Residual uncertainty: CSIM and TREXFUNC are 3dfx's models, not silicon. E1 confirms the range before F0 lands.

Halo (candidate: detail maps on near surfaces, small near plane)
Max Payne, Red Faction (candidates: close cameras, large tiled or Geo-Mod surfaces)

What rhw and |u| do the staged titles actually send (Halo's near plane, BF1942 terrain detail coordinates, Max Payne's close cameras)? Only the in-game census (E4) answers; until then F1 is designed but not built.

Is the TMU's 20-bit-mantissa precision loss at large |u| (texrepeat_prec) visible in any title? The census s_risk counter, then a frame check, decides whether VCR_ST_S_RISK is needed or should be lowered.
Should F0 wait for E1 (this design says yes) or land on 3dfx's shipped precedent of 256 + TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE?
The vendor's undocumented 'continuation WRAP bug' (no autostrip above S/W 257, VH5/D6TRI2I.C:986-995) belongs to G49. F1 sidesteps it by never continuing a rebased triangle.

G92.approach:
THE GAP IS REAL ON THE HAL SIDE. What it costs today is not measured, and the design measures it first.

HAL side:
- vertex() sends each TMU W = rhw, S = s*scale*rhw and T = t*scale*rhw (KMD/display/vcrdd_3d.c:210-221). It never reads a 3rd or 4th coordinate.
- D3DTSS_TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS is stored by the generic TSS case (vcrdd_d3d.c:1591-1609) and read nowhere.
- D3DPTEXTURECAPS_PROJECTED is not advertised (TextureCaps 00004007).

What today's picture depends on is what XP's d3d8.dll (5.03.2600.5512, software VP) hands a DX7 HAL for a projected stage. Three possibilities:
- (a) It divides per vertex. The DX8.1/DX9 SDK say so; that is inferred, quoted from memory. Result: correct at the vertices, warped inside triangles.
- (b) It passes (s,t,q) + PROJECTED. Result: drawn unprojected, wrong everywhere.
- (c) It strips q.

NEW MEASURED EVIDENCE from UE2 (objdump of LIB/UT2004/System/D3DDrv.dll b6bb4d87... and LIB/UT2003/System/D3DDrv.dll 04c412ca...):
- FD3DRenderInterface::SetProjectorMaterial sets every projector stage to TexCoordIndex 0x20000 (TCI_CAMERASPACEPOSITION) + COUNT3 + a texture matrix, then ORs in 0x100 (PROJECTED) from a projector-material flag.
  - UT2004: 0x1000459d-0x100045f7 and 0x100052c3-0x10005319.
  - UT2003: 0x100035ec-0x10003646 and 0x100042e5-0x10004332.
- It never tests D3DPTEXTURECAPS_PROJECTED. DeviceCaps8 is at +0x4194, so TextureCaps is at +0x41d0. That field is read once, at 0x10010bae, testing only CUBEMAP 0x800 and MIPCUBEMAP 0x10000.
- The staged ini files set Projectors=True and (UT2003) bPlayerShadows=True.

HARDWARE:
- Each TMU divides its iterated S/W and T/W by its OWN iterated 1/W:
  - sWtmu0 is "TREX0 & TREX1 W";
  - sWtmu1 is "TREX1 only W" (SPEC L2367, L2370, 8.68-8.73).
- tclampw "is used when projecting textures" (L3859).
- Our MesaFX + h5 Glide already implement exactly this mapping for OpenGL q: tmu oow = oow*q (MFX/fxvbtmp.h:204-226, GL5/fxcmd.h:1606-1631). It has never been shown on silicon.
- 3dfx never offered PROJECTED (D3INIT.C:3037, 3469).
- Their NT DP2 stores TTFF into ADDRESSU/V (D6DP2.C:1508-1511, D7DP2.C:1620-1623/1750-1753). Win9x revision 100 fixed that. Do not copy it.

INVESTIGATION (U1-U6):
- U1, the runtime's behaviour: d3dprobe ptex_xform/ptex_texgen plus HAL counters, first on the 86Box Voodoo3 bed (same d3d8.dll), then on .124.
- U2, which titles send it, and U6, how much q varies per triangle: Part A counters in any in-game session.
- U3, does the VSA-100 divide by W0/W1 and not by Wb: ptex/ptex2/ptex2b on .124. This also proves or breaks today's textured vertex fog, which already relies on W0 != Wb.
- U4, range: ptex_range.
- U5, cap side-effects: boot C.

DESIGN, three parts, no new register, no new sSetupMode bit.

PART A (log-only, default ON):
- Per-context counters by kind: divided / not divided (switch off) / pre-divided by the runtime / 1-D / bad q.
- Per-triangle q-ratio buckets (<1.01, <1.1, <2, >=2).
- One INFO event the first time each shape appears; two events at ctx_free when non-zero.
- Census key tex.transform.projected (G73/G76).

PART B (Diag\D3DFeat bit PTEX, default OFF):
- New Win32-free integer header include/vcr_ptex.h: vcr_ptex_kind(ttff, set floats, &qidx).
  - PROJECTED + a set that carries the COUNT-th element gives DIVIDE.
  - A set too short gives PREDIVIDED: never divide twice.
  - COUNT1/2 gives 1D, not handled.
- New common/vcr_ptex.c, built with x87 like vcr_fog.c and natively by the test:
  - vcr_ptex_scale(qa,qb,qc) returns k, a per-triangle power of two with max|q|*k in (1/2,1]. It is exact in IEEE arithmetic and keeps the TMU W at or below the triangle's own rhw, the range the proven path already sends. It returns 0 for a NaN, 0 or out-of-range q, and that triangle is drawn as today.
  - vcr_ptex_vertex() gives W = q*k*rhw, S = s*scale*rhw*k, T = t*scale*rhw*k. The per-pixel S/W is then D3D's own (sum lambda rho s)/(sum lambda rho q) for any k. q=1 with k=1 is bit-identical to today.
- fvf_layout keeps each set's float count (set_n).
- prepare() decides per TMU at the place where it already picks the set: TMU0 samples stage 1 with two stages, TMU1 samples stage 0. So the decision follows G12's map.
- VcrDd3dTriangle computes k per projected TMU.
- vertex() gets a projected branch beside today's three writes, which stay verbatim. Same registers, write order and VcrDdRoom counts.
- SM_W1 stays set for two stages, and G58's tmu_own_w must be set for projected draws.
- TM_CLAMPW stays on (S=T=0 behind the projector). LOD is invariant under k.
- Fallback if U3 fails (the TMU ignores W0/W1): the same switch does a CPU per-vertex divide (W = rhw, S = s/q...). That matches the runtime's documented fallback quality.

PART C (D3DFeat bit PTEXCAPS, default OFF, needs PTEX): D3DPTEXTURECAPS_PROJECTED is added to dpcTriCaps/dpcLineCaps after prim_caps (vcrdd_d3d.c:2071-2072). D3D8 then reports TextureCaps 00004407, and under (a) the runtime hands the raw (s,t,q) to Part B.

Provisional bits 20/21 (0x100000/0x200000), read at boot through the D3DFeat transport (G05). Chip-generic, so the Voodoo3 bed runs it.
G92.gating:
PART A (counters and logging only): default ON. It writes no register and changes no register value; it adds integer work per state change, one increment per triangle, and three float reads per triangle that carries q.

PART B (per-pixel divide): default OFF behind Diag\D3DFeat bit PTEX, provisionally bit 20 (0x100000).

PART C (D3DPTEXTURECAPS_PROJECTED): default OFF behind bit PTEXCAPS, provisionally bit 21 (0x200000). It is ignored without PTEX.

How the bits are read:
- Both are read at boot by the miniport (the D3DFeat word designed in G05; whichever D3DFeat item lands first creates vcr_d3dfeat.h and the appended vcr_info.d3dfeat).
- They are reported by an INFO event at VcrDd2dInit.
- They are chip-generic: the Voodoo3 86Box bed can run them, and only .124 arms them.

With both bits clear:
- vertex() runs its unprojected branch, which keeps today's three writes per TMU verbatim.
- d->ptex = 0, and the caps are unchanged.
- So every register value, write count and write order is byte-for-byte today's. This is pinned by the native test q1_is_todays_values_bit_for_bit plus the Python verbatim-branch test, and re-run in boot A.

With PTEX set, only triangles whose sampled set carries q under PROJECTED change; those are wrong or per-vertex today.

Graduation:
- One supervised clean boot per bit, one Diag change per boot.
- Boot B (PTEX): every ptex probe verdict perpixel, and ptex_q1 pixel-identical.
- Boot C (PTEXCAPS): runtime-path probes perpixel, and no title regresses.
- After that, a follow-up commit makes them default-on with the plan's kill-bit convention.

Not safe to land default-on now: the per-TMU W behaviour (W0 different from Wb, W1 different from W0) is unproven on silicon.

If U1 shows a double divide with PTEX on and the cap off, Part B is tied to Part C: it divides only while the cap is advertised.
G92.d3dprobe_test:
New d3dprobe tests in KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c. They run on the explicit list only, never in the default gate.

TEXTURES
- RAMP: 32x32 R5G6B5 where every texel names itself. Red = its column (5 bits), green = 2 x its row, blue = 0.
- PLAIN: blue = its column, red = green = 0.
- Both are point-sampled, CLAMP, no mip.
- Read-back is exact: 565 at 16 bpp; R8>>3 and G8>>3 at 32 bpp.

GEOMETRY
- A band x 32..224, y 96..160 (inside the 256x256 window), drawn as a strip.
- Left vertices (s,t,q) = (0, 0.5, 1); right vertices (4, 2, 4). So s/q runs 0->1 and t/q = 0.5.

CLASSIFIER
- The probe predicts four hypotheses from the vertex values:
  - perpixel = (sum lambda rho s)/(sum lambda rho q);
  - pervertex (the runtime divided);
  - unprojected (q ignored: today's HAL);
  - tmu_w_ignored (the TMU divided by Wb).
- It samples px {52,80,128,176} at y {112,144}, with a +-1 texel tolerance (G81).
- Predicted (col,row) for ptex:

  | px | perpixel | pervertex | unprojected | tmu_w_ignored |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 52 | (10,16) | (3,16) | (13,21) | (3,5) |
  | 80 | (18,16) | (8,16) | (31,28) | (8,7) |
  | 128 | (25,16) | (16,16) | (31,31) | (16,10) |
  | 176 | (29,16) | (24,16) | (31,31) | (24,13) |

- Every pair is >= 3 apart at every sample used.

THE TESTS

| test | what it draws | pass |
|---|---|---|
| ptex | XYZRHW + TEXCOORDSIZE3, TTFF COUNT3\|PROJECTED | verdict perpixel |
| ptex_persp | rhw 1 -> 0.25 (perspective plus projection); px 52 excluded | perpixel |
| ptex_range | s, t, q x1000 (k = 2^-12) | perpixel |
| ptex_q1 | q = 1 under PROJECTED vs the same band with a 2-float set | 0 differing pixels over the 192x64 band |
| ptex2 | stage 0 RAMP projected on TMU1 + stage 1 PLAIN ADD on TMU0 | red/green perpixel, blue = floor(f*32) (3, 8, 16, 24) |
| ptex2b | stage 1 projected on TMU0 + stage 0 PLAIN on TMU1 | the same; blue warps if TMU1 took W0 |
| ptex_xform | untransformed XYZ through the runtime's software T&L, orthographic 1:1 projection, identity texture matrix, COUNT3\|PROJECTED | see below |
| ptex_texgen | UE2's shape: TCI_CAMERASPACEPOSITION plus a texture matrix mapping camera x to the band's (s,t,q) | see below |

ptex_xform and ptex_texgen:
- Without the cap, perpixel or pervertex passes (pervertex is the documented runtime fallback).
- With the cap, only perpixel passes.

RULES
- The pretransformed tests are SKIPPED without D3DPTEXTURECAPS_PROJECTED unless --force-ptex is given (also passed through by d3dprobe_run.py).
- Today's driver fails forced ptex with verdict unprojected: the old-buggy value.
- Every RESULT entry records the verdict and the sampled (col,row) pairs, so it also documents the runtime's behaviour (U1).

G94.approach:
VERDICT: do not build a DX8-level DDI (MaxStreams >= 1). I disassembled the XP SP3 d3d8, d3d9, ddraw and dxg.sys binaries (statically, host only). They show that most of the claimed "DX8 gains" are either reachable from the DX7 DDI or not needed:
- Caps2 (DYNAMICTEXTURES, FULLSCREENGAMMA, CANRENDERWINDOWED) is copied from DirectDraw's ddCaps.dwCaps2 in the DX7 path (d3d8 0x6d9b4deb-0x6d9b4e29). GetDeviceCaps keeps those bits (mask 0x220a0002, at 0x6d9ada09). CANRENDERWINDOWED is ORed in by the runtime itself.
- PresentationIntervals is recomputed by the runtime from Caps2 in both paths (DDCAPS2_FLIPINTERVAL gives TWO/THREE/FOUR, FLIPNOVSYNC gives IMMEDIATE; 0x6d9ada42-0x6d9ada62).
- MaxPointSize must be 0 below the DX8 DDI, and the VSA-100 has no point sprites.
- A8 is not needed: G17 showed halo.exe maps a8/y8/ay8/a8y8 to no D3D format.
- DXVERSION is 0x802 from d3d8 and 0x902 from both ddraw and d3d9, so it identifies the runtime DLL, not the application.

A full DX8 DDI would add only BLENDOP subtract and COLORWRITEENABLE on this silicon. The runtime's "DX7 shape" check (d3d8 0x6d9ac340, d3d9 0x4fdf6d3c) rejects both bits for any MaxStreams-0 driver, and no staged title is known to need either. 3dfx's NT DX8 path could never have run even when compiled: NTSpecificInit sets dwFlags = GETDRIVERINFOSET only (VH5/DDINIT.C:1643-1645).

WHAT ONLY GetDriverInfo2 GIVES is the format-operation list: X8R8G8B8 render-target textures (Halo: 5 of its 8 targets, G36), A8 textures, and our own Z ops. This does NOT need the DX8 DDI:
- GetDDIType (d3d8 0x6d9ee320, d3d9 0x4fe0fc80) assigns DX8 type 6 only when D3DCAPS8.MaxStreams != 0.
- With MaxStreams = 0 the DDI factory builds today's DX6/DX7 object. The DX7 token stream stays, state blocks stay emulated (type <= 5), and there are no VB/IB handles.
- A list with any DDPF_D3DFORMAT entry replaces both the legacy converter and the PCI-id table (0x6d9af100 -> 0x6d9af1b0).

DESIGN, the "GDI2 hybrid", default OFF:
- **Step 1 (bit GDI2, identity):**
  - DrvGetDirectDrawInfo adds DDHALINFO_GETDRIVERINFO2, but only when the D3D half was published.
  - VcrDdD3dDriverInfo answers GUID f828169c with dwMagic 0xFFFFFFFF: DXVERSION (logged per pid), GETD3DCAPS8 (exactly 0xd4 bytes), GETFORMATCOUNT (0x18) and GETFORMAT (0x34, bounds-checked). Every other type (0x10-0x13, 0x18/0x19, 0x21-0x23) and every stereo query is left unanswered.
  - The caps8 builder runs a port of the runtime's own synthesis (d3d8 0x6d9aeaf0) on the DX7 structures vcrdd already publishes; the ExtendedCaps block is factored into ext_caps(). So the app-visible D3DCAPS8 is identical to today's.
  - MaxStreams is 0, MaxPointSize 0.0, VS/PS 0xfffe0000/0xffff0000, MaxVertexIndex 0xffff.
  - Caps2 = ddCaps.dwCaps2 (it must carry DDCAPS2_FLIPNOVSYNC or PRESENT_INTERVAL_IMMEDIATE is lost). Caps3 = dwSVCaps.
  - The identity format list reproduces the legacy builder plus the 121a:0009 table (0x4580): R5G6B5 TEXTURE|OFFSCREEN_RT|SAME_FORMAT_RT|DISPLAYMODE|3DACCEL; A1R5G5B5/A4R4G4B4 TEXTURE; A8R8G8B8 TEXTURE|OFFSCREEN_RT (tex_32); X8R8G8B8 SAME_FORMAT_RT plus DISPLAYMODE|3DACCEL (rt32) plus TEXTURE (G17's tex_x8); DXT1-5 TEXTURE; D16_LOCKABLE / X8D24 / S8D24 ZSTENCIL. It is mode-independent (never pd->bpp).
- **Step 2 (bit RTX8):** X8R8G8B8 gains OFFSCREEN_RENDERTARGET, only with rt32 and tex_x8. A render-target op is never put on a format outside {565, X8R8G8B8, A8R8G8B8}.
- A new Win32-free header KMD/include/vcr_gdi2.h holds layout-identical structures, because raising DIRECT3D_VERSION to reach the DDK's own breaks the DX7 types (15 errors). It also holds the builders, the copy-length rule and the shape oracle.
- The copy length must use the GDI2 header's dwExpectedSize, not the outer one: dxg passes 0x18 there, and dxg copies dwActualSize bytes back unbounded. Reusing answer() would hand the process 0xbc bytes of kernel stack. Clamp to the bytes written and to <= 0x400.

Single pass, no register traffic. The old path is byte-for-byte unchanged with both bits clear.

- G91: answered no (the shape check).

Chain 12 (256x256 DXT5 at 0x3bb7000) ends at 0x3bc7000, and combine 9 starts at 0x3bc8570: a gap of 5488 bytes, exactly its levels 2-8. Caveat: the 'two 1' rows (combines 1, 5, 6, 21) log stage 1's tLOD and base against stage 0's address (log_combo is called at display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1027 with stage 0's t, while r->tLOD is v1's), so their levels cannot be read from that log.

Games list overstated. BF1942 never reaches Direct3D on .124: SafeDisc 2.80 in Mods\bf1942\Mod.dll stops the client first (reports/games.md:415-418; compat.py status --box .124: BF1942 'deployed failed'). 'games_unblocked' is also the wrong frame: UT2003, UT2004 and Halo already run, and G07 changes how they render.

'Every mipmapped DX6-DX8 title' is refuted on two counts. (1) DX5 legacy-state titles (JK DF2, MotS, any title that filters through D3DRENDERSTATE_TEXTUREMIN) never walk a chain today. ctx_defaults zeroes tss (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1129), the walk needs TSS MIPFILTER > D3DTFP_NONE (:779, :814), and legacy TEXTUREMIN is not mapped until G08 (G08.md:514). (2) Thief II, NewDark D3D9 with mipmaps and trilinear requested, D3D32 and BigTex armed, rendered a mission with no visible confetti on 09-28 (scripts/benchmarks/results/v56k_lan_192.168.1.124/day/fbshots/thief2_d3d9_armed_4.png). Impact is per engine (heap churn), not universal.

The padding sub-issue cannot explain the observed confetti. DXT1 (8x4 units), DXT3/5 (4x4 units) and square A8R8G8B8 levels are 16-byte multiples down to the last sampled level (common/vcr_texlod.c:40-57; DXT1 sampling is limited to levels at least 8 wide, :68-75). Per-level 16-aligned blocks therefore misplace only the RGB16 1x1 level and some non-square tails. UT2003/UT2004/Halo worlds are DXT/8888 (11-08 combos: fmt 20, DXT1, DXT5). That part is P2 hygiene, relevant to RGB16-heavy titles (Red Faction at 640x480x16, the default path, DX5/6 titles after G08).

The guard's 'byte-identical on the proven path' claim is false (§5, and the gating text: 'every d3dprobe check that passes today writes the same registers'). d3dprobe 'mip' (tools/d3dprobe.c:993, 64x64 R5G6B5 full chain) and 'mip2048' (:823, 2048 R5G6B5 full chain) end in a 1x1 level. Per-level 16-byte placement can never put that level at the TMU's +0x2AA8: start alignment is 16 (vcrdd_d3d.c:439, :560), and G07's own §7 case expects '-> 6'. Bit 0 therefore lowers LODMAX by one on every full RGB16 chain on both paths, as G06 §4.1 correctly says. The checked levels still pass, but the default-on rationale rests on a wrong premise.

The default (non-BigTex) path is never verified on silicon. .124 keeps D3DBigTex=7 in every boot, so view_of (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:840-843) always takes tex_view_ext, and the 86Box bed's LOD is wrong (d3dprobe.c:47-49). Yet bit 0 changes tex_view too (§4.1 'any card') and is proposed for default-on, which is what a fresh install runs.

The census misclassifies padding splits. 'Shallow <= 3 / deep >= 4' by level index counts the deterministic 1x1 padding split of a small RGB16 chain as shallow, scatter-like: an 8x8 chain's 1x1 is level 3. Every full RGB16 chain also produces a split, so 'the first 8 per context at WARN' can fill with padding cases and hide the scatter ones.

problems: Bit 0 is not register-neutral, contrary to G07.md §5 L178 ('every passing d3dprobe check today writes the same registers'). In a per-level R5G6B5 full chain, the 2x2 level is 8 bytes, so the TMU expects the 1x1 level at top + chain_offset, an address that is 8 mod 16. No 16-aligned block (vcrdd_d3d.c:439-441, 560-562) can sit there, whatever the heap state. Bit 0 therefore lowers LODMAX on every full R5G6B5 chain, and on the tails of non-square chains. d3dprobe mip (d3dprobe.c:993, 7 levels) goes from LODMAX 8 to 7, and mip2048 (:823, 12 levels) from 11 to 10. Their probed levels still pass, but the registers change. The default render list (d3dprobe.c:1247) has no mip test, so '40/40 unchanged' proves nothing about the guard. G06.md §4.1 states this correctly.

The default-on census mixes up the fixed padding split with scatter (G07.md §4.0 L94; §9 row 1). On a fresh heap, a full R5G6B5 chain whose top is 8x8 or 4x4 already splits at level 3 or 2, which the design counts as 'shallow'. An 8:1 chain splits at its last two levels. So the reading 'mostly shallow, therefore G07 causes G06' can come from padding alone. The census also counts binds, not chains, so 8 binds of one texture can use up the whole 8-per-context WARN budget.

The probe verdict 'clamped = within 12 of the TOP's colour' (G07.md §6 L194) misfiles a guard clamp below level 1. Under bit 0, mipdeep L6 shows level 5's colour and is scored 'foreign', the same verdict as reading garbage.

The regression plan (§7) says only two existing tests are affected, and that both pass unchanged. It misses these pinned proven-path tests:
- tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_bigtex.py:80-81 asserts 'return pd->tex_ext ? tex_view_ext(pd, tss, s, v) : tex_view(tss, s, v);' and func(D3D,'static BOOL tex_view(const DWORD *tss'). G07.md:123 adds a VCR_PDEV* parameter to tex_view, so this test fails.
- bigtex.py:123-124 and test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:120-121 pin the exact allocator lines (HeapVidMemAllocAligned(vm, total|mip_offset(...), ...) and fpVidMem = base + ...). The pad's 'total + pad' and 'base + pad' rewrite those lines.

Bit 1's set-up has no reference implementation, and the design misjudges its main risk. The design says 'we still return NOTHANDLED' for the other surfaces, as if that path were known to work. Only the texture-only path is known to work.
- 3dfx's NT5 HAL answers ATOMICSURFACECREATION|NOTIFYPRIMARYCREATION (VH5/DDFXNT.C:1236-1245). It allocates every surface itself and returns HANDLED (VH5/DDSURF.C:785-815, 966, 1150-1158). Texture lists go through lplpSList[0] plus an attach-list walk at creation (DDSURF.C:363; D3TXTR.C:862-950).
- Microsoft's 3dlabs sample sets NOTIFYPRIMARYCREATION only and asserts dwSCnt==1 (w2kddk 3dlabs/driver/dd.c:1709, ddsurf.c:309).
- The DDK documents ATOMIC for 'a complex flipping chain'.
No driver we can read has tested ATOMIC alone with NOTHANDLED for multi-surface lists (flip chains, Z, DXT surfaces that VcrDdD3dCreateTexSurface sends back as DDHAL_PLEASEALLOC_BLOCKSIZE, vcrdd_d3d.c:473-505). The same holds for a primary chain without NOTIFYPRIMARY. A dxg misstep there hits every DirectDraw and D3D application on the box, so it is a stability risk.

The 1x1 pad (defect 3) is bundled into the riskiest bit, although it has nothing to do with the call pattern.
- On the BigTex path, which .124 has armed, every single-level 1x1 R5G6B5/1555/4444 texture is read 8 bytes early today: texBaseAddr is truncated (vcr_texlod.c:137-138) and the block is 16-aligned (vcrdd_d3d.c:439-441).
- No d3dprobe test creates a 1x1 texture. mipdeep covers only a chain's 1x1 level.
- On the default path, 1x1 textures are placed by DirectDraw at 4-byte alignment, because VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain needs DDSCAPS_MIPMAP (vcrdd_d3d.c:537; truncation at vcr_texlod.c:32). They are misread the same way, and that is outside this design.

When vcr_tex_call_levels returns 0, the whole call is declined (G07.md §4.3.2). The call then returns NOTHANDLED and the textures get DirectDraw's 4-byte placement (vcrdd_d3d.c:381-388). Under bit 1, a multi-surface texture list that is not a mip chain, such as a DX7 texture flip chain, would lose the 16-byte placement it gets today with one surface per call. The helper itself is needed, because the old loop would alias equal-size surfaces onto one block, but its failure path is wrong.

The plan conflicts with other designs on names, bits and events.
- G06.md §4.1-4.2 defines the same Diag\D3DMipChain, with bit 1 = whole-chain RESERVATION at the top level's call (option B). It also uses dwReserved1 flag 0x8 as SF_SPLIT, where G07 uses 0x8 as SF_PAD8.
- VCR_INFO_F_MIPGUARD 0x8000 collides with G01's VCR_INFO_F_FIFOGUARD 0x8000 (G01 is a G07 dependency) and with G05, G08 and G16.
- 0x10000 collides with G03 (G63.md:322).
- G06 also claims events 513/24-27.

Option A is chosen over B before any data, although the §4.0 creation log measures exactly B's preconditions in boot A: dwSCnt, the descriptor's w/h/mipcount, lpSurfMore->dwMipMapCount and the attach state. B leaves dxg's call pattern untouched for every non-texture surface, so it is the option that could become default-on for fresh installs. The repo already records 'DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT 7 on each' call (tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:111).

The evidence is mislabelled. The .124 ring entries cited (ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt seq 24873-24938) are single-level textures: CreateSurface caps 0x5000, no DDSCAPS_MIPMAP, dwSCnt 1. They show first-fit placement only. No .124 ring records how a multi-level chain was created. The per-level claim rests on the DDK text plus an 86Box measurement kept only in a docstring; no ring is saved under evidence/86box_v3.

The README Finding at vcr-kmd/README.md:628-631 still says 'a mipmap chain is one block', in the same breath as 'XP creates every level with its own CreateSurface'. The design only adds a Diag row and leaves the wrong Finding in place.
The on-box boots run several 'd3dprobe render --full' passes in a row, each switching mode in and out, without the 5 s pacing wrapper used on 11-12 (onbox/d3dprobe_paced.py --pace 5000).

The cost claim of 'up to 12 pointer compares' per bind is understated. vcr_tex_chain_offset(k) loops over k levels (vcr_texlod.c:111-117), so calling it once per level is O(n^2) per bind. The real cost is still trivial.

problems: D3DFeat bit collision: G13 provisionally takes bit 7 (0x80) for 'argmod' (designs/G13.md:373). G12 already assigns bit 6 = VCR_D3DF_CMB_FBI, bit 7 = VCR_D3DF_CMB_TMU and bit 8 = VCR_D3DF_CMB_ITER (designs/G12.md:51-53), and G15 records both claims side by side (designs/G15.md:273). Arming 'argmod' as specified would arm G12's TMU tier instead.

Ownership and architecture contradict G12. G12's bit 6 already runs 'every single-stage op and modifier' in the FBI (G12.md:51). Its compiler takes the raw arguments, carrying its own COMPLEMENT/ALPHAREPLICATE constants (G12.md:166). It routes aX and applies per-slot complement rules, and it says 'The engine *is* G13's implementation' (G12.md:214-240). G13's contract instead has G12 compile modifier-blind ('selector bits only', G13.md:247) and has a post-pass edit the words through an XC_IN_* routing record that G12 never produces. Names differ too: vcr_xcomb.h / vcr_xc_compile / pd->xc_on versus G12's vcr_combine.h / vcr_cmb_compile / pd->cmb_fbi. G13 section 4.2.7's row 'extended on, argmod off: masked' is false for G12 as designed. G13's exhaustive sweep (b) duplicates G12's native sweep (G12.md:456).

Plumbing conflict. G13 adds VCR_INFO_F_XC_ARGMOD on 'the next free bit (0x8000 or above)' (G13.md:312). The last used vcr_info.flags bit is 0x4000 (KMD/include/vcr_ioctl.h:139), and G08 and G16 also claim 0x8000. G12 and G15 instead append one whole 'vcr_u32 d3dfeat' word to vcr_info (G12.md:342; G15.md:268-273).

ALPHAREPLICATE as a post-pass over a modifier-blind, per-channel-independent placement (G12.md:256) is unsound. An alpha 'twin' (FBI TA/MATMU, TMU OTHER_TA/MAOTHER) carries whatever the producing unit's alpha path emits. Case 1: G12's own SPLIT worked case (G12.md:301) is TMU0 TC REPLACE / TCA PASS = 0x00041000 with FBI cc_other TRGB and cca_other TA, so FBI TA is stage 0's texel alpha. Stage-1 SELECTARG1(TEXTURE|ALPHAREPLICATE) compiled into that shape and then '+4'-ed (G13.md:265-271) draws t0.a instead of t1.a, and the result is still called exact. Case 2: stage-1 CURRENT|ALPHAREPLICATE in TMU0 below bit 8, when stage 0's ALPHAOP uses DIFFUSE, gives OTHER_TA = t0.a where D3D wants t0.a x d.a. That is the same reason G12 puts UT2003 combo 21 at bit 8 (G12.md:58, 93). G13 checks provenance only for MALOCAL/MAOTHER (section 4.2.4 rule 2). Cells A7/A8 use SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) on both stage-0 channels, so they cannot catch either case. G12's dead-stage rule (G12.md:207) must also count a colour-channel CURRENT|ALPHAREPLICATE as a read of stage 0's alpha.

G12's legacy-mirror encodings are not covered. G12 keeps today's registers for set-ups the legacy path already draws right (G12.md:143-156): MODULATE(T,D) = 0x0C482405 with M = CLOCAL (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:715), and ADD via ADD_CLOCAL (vcrdd_d3d.c:705-706). With a modifier-blind compile, cell A3 MODULATE(TEX, DIFF|AREP) reaches G13 with DIFFUSE on M via CLOCAL. G13's FBI M twin table has only MRGBTMU->MATMU (G13.md:270), so A3 is refused, contradicting A3's expected 'ok'. Mapping CLOCAL->ALOCAL would read the alpha unit's local select (G12.md:140). C4's register pin 'invert_local 2 vs 1' (G13.md section 7a) assumes a SUB_CLOCAL form of ADD that the mirror encoding does not use.

ADDSIGNED conflict with G12, and refusal set pinned to policy, not hardware. G12 accepts arg2-COMPLEMENT of ADDSIGNED/ADDSIGNED2X by moving the complemented Y to A (1-x) and X to B (x-1/2) (G12.md:221). That is exact and always routable, because the other/local select sets are symmetric (H5/INCLUDE/H3DEFS.H:396-415, 477-496). G13 requires refusal (cell C9r, G13.md:447) and pins 'refusal set equals SWARCH's list ... and nothing else' (G13.md:490). SWARCH's list is 3dfx's driver policy, not a hardware limit. SUBTRACT(X,~Y) = clamp((X-1/2)+(Y-1/2)) and BLEND*ALPHA(X,~Y) = ((X-1/2)+(Y-1/2))*a + (1-Y) are also encodable with invert_other and invert_local both X_MINUS_HALF (H3DEFS.H:427, 433). That is inferred, within +-1 LSB, and unprobed. It matters because Max Payne's vocabulary is exactly ADDSIGNED plus ~TEXTURE.

Swap/complement order is unspecified. Section 4.2.4 swaps arguments between OTHER and M7 (G13.md:276); section 4.2.2 XORs invert_other or toggles REVERSE per position. If the XOR runs before the swap, MODULATE(TEXTURE|COMPLEMENT, CURRENT|ALPHAREPLICATE) in TMU0 becomes (1-a_cur)*tex instead of a_cur*(1-tex).

The XC_IN_* record cannot tell an RGB position from an alpha position. Recipes that place aX on C or D (MODULATEALPHA_ADDCOLOR, MODULATECOLOR_ADDALPHA, MODULATEINVALPHA_ADDCOLOR: G12.md:226-229; the vendor's AUX mux at VH5/D6MT.C:675-681) would be refused by the rule 'a select already on an alpha ... refuses' (G13.md:271). 3dfx '+N'-ed only the main mux (D6MT.C:4596-4639, ArgVal & ARG1_MUX). Impact is low: these ops are not in today's TextureOpCaps 0x184f.

Cell A10's 'must refuse' expectation (ALPHAOP SELECTARG2(DIFFUSE), G13.md:458) is wrong below bit 8. DIFFUSE cannot enter TMU0's TCA, so tca_localselect stays at 0 = LOCAL_TA (H3DEFS.H:533). Rule 2 is then satisfied and both MALOCAL readings deliver t1.a, so accepting is correct. The 'forced' MALOCAL-semantics probe of open question 2 (G13.md:612) needs bit 8 / G58.
Plan B can never be armed: 'the same argmod bit gates it' (G13.md:361), but argmod is honoured only with pd->xc_on (G13.md:376), and Plan B exists for exactly the case where G12 has not landed.

Validation wording conflicts with G15 and with G13 itself. Section 4.3 says that with argmod off 'every modifier on an argument that is read is refused' (G13.md:337). G15 allows ALPHAREPLICATE on an alpha argument (G15.md:171); today's HAL already draws that correctly, and G13 section 2 says it must stay so.

The Halo de-ranking is not supported by the frame. Halo_timedemo_060s.png shows a flat (47,92,105) square with stars showing through; for example (198,242,255) = 151 + (47,92,105) per channel. That fits an additive blend, where alpha plays no part. An ignored ALPHAREPLICATE on a white-RGB, alpha-shaped glow texture would give exactly this uniform square. So 'shape gone from both colour and alpha, G13 not the likeliest' (G13.md:41) is not evidence either way.

Max Payne evidence is understated: the design calls it 'inferred' (G13.md:601). MaxPayne/e2driver/e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll on the share carries its material log's own name tables: arguments TEXTURE, CURRENT, DIFFUSE, TFACTOR and '~TEXTURE'; ops DISABLE, SELECTARG1/2, ADD, ADDSIGNED, MODULATE and BLENDTEXTUREALPHA. That makes it the best-evidenced COMPLEMENT user on the staged list, yet no d3dprobe cell covers ~TEXTURE under ADDSIGNED or BLENDTEXTUREALPHA, or as arg2 of ADD.

corrections: Fold G13's register work into G12's compiler (vcr_combine.h / vcr_cmb_compile): resolve modifiers inside recipe, routing and placement (G12.md sections 3.3-3.5), with one owner, one header and one native sweep. Add a provenance rule to placement. An alpha twin of a TMU output (FBI TA/MATMU; TMU OTHER_TA/MAOTHER/MALOCAL) is exact only if the producing unit's alpha path, as placed for the alpha channel, delivers exactly that argument's D3D alpha. Otherwise re-place (for example, TEXTURE|ALPHAREPLICATE via TMU0 TC otherselect LOCAL_TA, forwarded by the FBI) or refuse. In liveness, a colour-channel CURRENT|ALPHAREPLICATE (and BLENDCURRENTALPHA) keeps stage 0's alpha alive.

Keep as designed (verified): the gap is real and nothing else handles it. Supporting facts: ARG_KIND masks at vcrdd_d3d.c:671, while the raw TSS are stored at :1605. Validate always answers 1 pass / DD_OK (:1905-1910). The silicon DXT alpha-pass failure is recorded at PLAN:124-128 and d3dprobe.c:735-737. UT2003's 26 stage-0 set-ups carry no 0x10/0x20 bits. No D3D cap describes the modifiers. Hardware encodings check out: the select/invert/outshift fields and the +4/+3/+2/+1 twins match H3DEFS.H:396-535, and the REVERSE bits are 13/22 (FBI) and 17/26 (TMU). The spec confirms that TMU muxes always come from combineMode and that bit 30 is required. 3dfx used the same XOR masks and +N edits (D6MT.C:504-516, 4535-4639, 5092-5160), and Glide's grTexColorCombineExt drives the same fields for our ICD. Proven paths stay unchanged while G12 is off. P2 priority is right.

problems: The Halo glow is the wrong target. G13's gap text still names it as a candidate cause, and the on-box acceptance step expects the crystal glow to 'show its radial falloff' (designs/G13.md:543-545). G17 already accounts for that artefact: the frame shows a flat additive quad of +(47,92,105), and the X8R8G8B8 lens-flare bitmap fails CreateTexture, so the sprite is drawn untextured (designs/G17.md §1, §2.1-2.3). A G13 A/B judged on the glow would show 'no change' and would be read as 'G13 does nothing'.

The impact is understated, and the evidence was obtainable without box time. I decrypted Halo's SHADERS/fx.bin, all 1,017,261 bytes: it is TEA in ECB; the key is built at halo.exe 0x51999a-0x5199b2, decrypted by 0x6182b0 through the wrapper 0x618350, and the body's MD5 equals its 33-byte hex trailer. It holds 122 D3DX fx_2_0 effects. Their ps_0_0 techniques carry 75 modifier assignments in 72 technique-passes across 21 effects: TEXTURE|AREP 57, DIFFUSE|AREP 12, TFACTOR|AREP 3, DIFFUSE|COMP|AREP 2, TEXTURE|COMP|AREP 1. There is no pure COMPLEMENT, and the 'fallback' techniques carry none. 54 of these are shader_model (object) techniques, effects 117-121. Their pass 1 is MODULATE(TEXTURE|ALPHAREPLICATE, TFACTOR) with ALPHAOP SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) and SRCBLEND ZERO / DESTBLEND SRCCOLOR; these are the only 54 multiply-blend passes in the file. shader_environment's ps_0_0 (effect 116) carries none.

Halo really runs those techniques on .124, independent of G67's legacy renderer choice. halo.exe builds the object technique handles at init (0x526990-0x526cc0) through 0x530120, which formats '%s_ps_%d_%d' (VA 0x66f028) from the device's PixelShaderVersion, 0.0 on .124. The model draw calls SetTechnique on them (0x5275a0-0x52767e, effects 117, 118 and 120 at 0x69e2b0, 0x69e2d0 and 0x69e310). 0x530120 returns the _ps_0_0 handle even when ValidateTechnique fails, because 0.0 is the last version it tries. G13.md:76-78 and :337-341 overclaim: honest validation (G15) cannot steer Halo's objects away from the modifier. Only the generic effects selected at 0x52f780 ('ps_%d_%d', then TDefault_no_ps, then FindNextValidTechnique at 0x52f88d) would fall to 'fallback'.

UE2 uses both modifiers, as code in D3DDrv.dll rather than as a reading of Engine.u class names. The material-stage field map comes from UT2003's copy routine (0x10012f49-0x1001304f) into the deferred setter 0x100169b0: stride 0x84, COLORARG1 +0x58, ALPHAARG1 +0x64. Inside FD3DRenderInterface::SetProjectorMaterial, COLORARG1 is set to DIFFUSE|AREP or TEXTURE|AREP at UT2003 0x10003a49, 0x10003f40, 0x10004109, 0x100047ac and 0x10004984 (UT2004: 0x10004a24, 0x10004f24, 0x100050ed, 0x10005799, 0x10005971). One of them is MODULATE(DIFFUSE|AREP, TEXTURE), selected by a 3-way projector-blend switch. In HandleCombinedMaterial (inverted mask, AO_* ops), ALPHAARG1 is set to TEXTURE|COMP or CURRENT|COMP at UT2003 0x1000a46d, 0x1000ae00, 0x1000af18, 0x1000b07d and 0x1000b1b6 (UT2004: 0x1000ca3d-0x1000d79c). Projectors=True and Decals=True in both staged INIs (LIB/UT2003/System/UT2003.ini:108,111; LIB/UT2004/System/UT2004.ini:147,150). UE2 never calls IDirect3DDevice8::ValidateDevice (no vtable+0x100 call in either D3DDrv.dll), so G15 cannot help UE2 either.

Other titles. H&D Deluxe's i3d2.dll 0x100993da sets stage 0 to SELECTARG1(TEXTURE|COMPLEMENT), then draws a 2-triangle XYZRHW DrawPrimitiveUP strip (a screen-space effect of unknown purpose). Red Faction (63 direct SetTextureStageState argument calls) and Thief Gold (64) carry no modifier. AvP and Rainbow Six make no TSS argument calls. Max Payne, Shogo and Thief II could not be decided statically: their calls go through a state cache or a wrapper. G13.md's 'Max Payne (inferred)' therefore stays unknown.

'No modifier in UT2003's 26 set-ups' (G13.md:37-38) is not evidence of absence. That log was taken at UT2003's menu, in the 11-08 menu sweep (KMD/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108/run.out 01:08:04; docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:142-150), not in gameplay.

The design duplicates G12, and the two collide. G12 already owns modifiers: 'The engine *is* G13's implementation ... G13's modifiers live in the routing' (designs/G12.md:240, :544), and it assigns Diag\D3DFeat bit 7 to VCR_D3DF_CMB_TMU (designs/G12.md:51). G13 instead post-edits words that G12 'compiles with the selector bits only', calls the header include/vcr_xcomb.h where G12 says vcr_combine.h, and takes bit 7 for 'argmod' (G13.md:233-249, :307, :373-375). That gives two owners for the same combineMode fields and a bit-number clash.

Plan A and Plan B are ranked backwards for the evidenced need. Every stage-0 set-up the titles actually use fits the legacy fbzColorPath combine the HAL already writes, with no combineMode and no G12 or G03:
- Halo's detail pass: CP_RGBSEL_C1 | CP_CC_M(CC_M_ATMU) | CP_CC_REVERSE. c1 is already TEXTUREFACTOR (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1020).
- UE2's projector fade: Plan B's own row, RGBSEL_TMU | M(ALOCAL) | REVERSE (G13.md:353).
- UE2's alpha SELECTARG1(TEXTURE|COMP): CP_CCA_INVERT (G13.md:358).
- H&D: CP_CC_INVERT (G13.md:350).
A stage-1 TEXTURE|AREP would use the legacy TMU tc_mselect ALOCAL, i.e. TM_TC_MULT with mselect 3 (KMD/include/vcr_3dregs.h:172). As written, the design delays an S-effort fix behind G12 (effort L) and nine dependencies (G13.md:588-594).

G13 alone leaves Halo's dominant set-up wrong. color_path routes MODULATE(TEXTURE, TFACTOR) as texture × iterated diffuse: the texture wins the 'other' mux and local is hard-wired to diffuse (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:697-716). The pass needs G14's TFACTOR fix in the same encoding, but G13 lists G14 only as a soft dependency for TMU cases. Separately, Plan B's c0=0xffffffff trick for SELECTARG1(TEXTURE|AREP) (G13.md:357) contends with G14 Part A's c0=TFACTOR.

Halo's texture-less stage-1 fade effects (fx.bin effects 83-101: MODULATE, LERP or MULTIPLYADD on DIFFUSE|AREP) are dropped whole by compute_regs, because `two` requires tex_handle1 (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:927-929). G13 cannot change them without G12. These effects are selected by 0x52f780, so G15's honest refusal sending them to 'fallback' is the cheaper route.

The test plan misses the case that matters.
- No d3dprobe cell covers MODULATE(TEXTURE|AREP, TFACTOR) under a ZERO/SRCCOLOR multiply blend. That is Halo's 54 passes; A3 and A5 do not exercise TFACTOR beside a texture.
- The UE2 acceptance uses the 9 fps flyby, whose frames are dominated by block noise and dark lightmaps. A modifier change cannot be judged there.

I recomputed a sample of the cell values (A2, A3, A6, A7, A8, C1-C4, C6-C10) with D3D's 8-bit formula, and they are correct.

It does not steer the shader_model techniques, because 0x530120 ignores validation at PS 0.0, and UE2 never validates. G13-L together with G14 is the only driver-side fix for those. Add these d3dprobe cells, with values computed by the same 8-bit D3D formula:
- `halo_detail`: stage 0 MODULATE(TEXTURE|AREP, TFACTOR), ALPHAOP SELECTARG1(TEXTURE), SRCBLEND ZERO / DESTBLEND SRCCOLOR over a known clear colour. This one cell exercises both G13 and G14.

Replace the on-box game acceptance. For Halo, compare a shader_model scene with the bit off and on at the same frame: the timedemo's 180 s escape-pod frame, or a supervised Blood Gulch spawn view with a Warthog and bipeds, judged on object tint and luminance. problems: Gap confirmed in deployed code. The only place the miniport turns cmdFifo0 off is VcrHwResetEngine (KMD/miniport/vcrmp_hw.c:190). It runs only on a BUSY chip at a mode set (:571-572) or on request (vcrmp.c:866). VcrDd2dSync tests only bit 9 and the PCI FIFO count (vcrdd_2d.c:113-130). Reset3D refuses when SST_CMDFIFOEN is set (vcr_3dseq.h:172-183). VcrSliOff never touches CMDAGP (grep -i basesize miniport/*.c finds only :190). The on-box sequence is real: pid 1892's display reset at 75345.579, the desktop mode set with no busy reset, then the unmap at 75346.471 (ring_start_decoded.txt).

(C') misses the third drawable site. SETRENDERTARGET recomputes w->drawable at KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1748-1749 without the new term. The design patches only :1859 (DP2) and :1887 (Clear2) and keeps the count==2 pin (tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:465-466). So when a DP2 batch is blocked as OWNED or SLI, any SETRENDERTARGET later in the same stream turns drawing back on under a live owner's FIFO.

The decision and the cure disagree on cmdFifo1. vcr_fifo_guard returns RESET when only cmdFifo1 is on (the design's own test 4). But VcrHwResetEngine writes only VCR_CMD_BASESIZE0 (vcrmp_hw.c:190), fifo_blocked reads only cmdFifo0, and the d3dprobe pass checks only size0. That case therefore 'resets' and stays enabled. RESET success is also judged by VcrHwResetEngine's status-idle return, not by re-reading baseSize.

Event-code collision with existing code. '512 a=10' is already the text-punt event (KMD/display/vcrdd_punt.c:549; vcr_events.h:74). Other designs also claim 513/24-25, event 309, VCR_INFO_F 0x8000 and the D3DSafe carrier: G05.md:268-269, G07.md:103, G09.md:188, G10.md:137/236, G11.md:257, summarised in G02.md:330-334.

Causality is overclaimed. Fact 2 ('an enabled FIFO alone stops PIO triangles') and 'the cure is proven' are not isolated. The only cure observed was VcrHwResetEngine on a BUSY chip (0xa5f) followed by a full mode set: miscInit0=0 (vcrmp_hw.c:612), a new PDEV and VcrDd2dInit. The GRX reset may also clear other Glide 3D state. The stale dump's chipMask (0x200214=0, while Glide writes 0xFFFFFFFF, h3defs.h:711) and sSetupMode (0x200260=0) cannot be interpreted without a clean-state read. The stale state at 16 bpp is unmeasured (onbox.md:297), and UT2003/UT2004 run at 16 bpp on this box.

The reproduction plan may not reach the G01 state. A client killed mid-frame leaves the chip BUSY (KMD/README.md:719-723), and the existing busy-at-mode-set reset (event 308) clears that at the next mode set, including win32k's mode restore at process exit. So E1/E2 and session-2 steps 3-4 can end up testing the already-handled case and waiting for a 309 that never comes. Also, the mode restore for a killed DirectDraw-exclusive owner may run before its ExitStatus marks it dead: (B) then reads OWNED and the reset moves to (C).

'No reset at DrvAssertMode' is only a text pin. The (D) give_up hook is reachable through VcrDd2dSync from DrvAssertMode(FALSE) just before RESET_DEVICE (vcrdd.c:613), VcrDd2dTerm (vcrdd_2d.c:509), ctx_free (vcrdd_d3d.c:1217) and GETLINEARADDR (vcrdd_escape.c:102). In those paths the owner check is the only protection.

The vendor reference is missing. 3dfx's own driver turns cmdFifo0 off at EVERY DrvAssertMode(FALSE) (ENABLE.C:1382, CmdFifo0Disable, before RESET_DEVICE at :1392) and tells Glide its context is lost (hwcSetContextDWORD, ENABLE.C:1378). The gap's display-reset trigger is the vendor's design. It is unsafe in our lane only because vcr-kmd does not implement the context DWORD: vcrdd_escape.c:252 falls to the default case, and our Glide then uses dummyContextDWORD (minihwc.c:9793/9825).

Fact 10 ('Glide arms only chip 0') is inaccurate for SLI. Glide polls each slave's cmdFifo0.readPtrL (glide3/src/fifo.c:1285-1346), and the miniport maps each slave's CMDAGP page to Glide (vcrmp_map.c:86). So after an unclean SLI close, chips 1-3 very likely keep enabled FIFOs. That is harmless to 1-chip D3D with snoop off, but it is not 'unread'.

Two liveness and QUERY edge cases. STATUS_PENDING == 259 == STILL_ACTIVE, so a Glide process whose exit code is 259 stays 'alive' forever: OWNED, and D3D is refused while the FIFO is on. The 'read-only' QUERY op calls VcrGlideLiveOwners, which forgets slots and logs 406, so it changes state even with D3DSafe=0.

The display DLL does not see resets the miniport starts. A (B) reset at IOCTL_VCR_RESTORE_MODE, sent from HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE (vcrdd_escape.c:164), leaves pd->fog_valid=1 (vcrdd_3d.c:87-98). Only resets the display DLL starts invalidate it. Separately, the prepare() reset generation is only needed for (D) in the middle of a DP2, because w is memset at every DP2 and Clear2 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1835/1882).
corrections: Compute the FIFO verdict once per DP2/Clear2 into the walker (e.g. w.fifo_ok). AND it into all three drawable sites, including SETRENDERTARGET at vcrdd_d3d.c:1748. Update the test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:465-466 pins to match.

Make the cure match the decision. Either drop cmdFifo1 from vcr_fifo_guard and its tests, or have VcrFifoGuard also write cmdFifo1.baseSize=0 (CMDAGP+0x54). Have fifo_blocked read both registers. After any reset, re-read both baseSize words and report RESET_FAILED unless bit 8 is clear in both (post-condition, not return value).

Allocate the codes at integration. Use a dedicated display event (e.g. G02's 514) instead of 512/10, which is taken by vcrdd_punt.c:549. Use one D3DSafe carrier (vcr_info.d3dsafe, or 0x10000<<bit), not flag 0x8000. Check IOCTL 0xa10 and VCR_ESC_BASE+12 against G02 and the other designs.

Mark fact 2 and 'cure proven' as inferred. Run E2 (stale state at 16 and 32 bpp) and E3 before claiming 'every D3D title'. For E3: read chipMask/sSetupMode/stats in both the clean and the stale state, then write only cmdFifo0.baseSize=0 and re-probe. Keep the full VcrHwResetEngine as the cure until E3 says otherwise.

Make the stale state deterministic. Read status (0x0) and 0x80024 immediately before every probe and label each run as busy or idle-enabled. Produce idle-enabled with an orphan glidelab that grFinish()es, then unmaps or exits without grSstWinClose. In session 2, pass on FIFO off + 40/40 + 42/42 and accept 308 or 309 (mode set or context) as the explaining event.

Say in the design that (D) can fire inside DrvAssertMode(FALSE), DrvDisableSurface, ctx_free and GETLINEARADDR, and that only the owner check guards those paths. Either skip STALL recovery on teardown paths or pin that behaviour in a test.

Cite the vendor model: FIFO off at every DrvAssertMode(FALSE) plus hwcSetContextDWORD (ENABLE.C:1378-1392). Record that implementing HWCEXT_CONTEXT_DWORD_NT, which Glide already asks for (minihwc.c:9780-9796), would let vcr-kmd use the vendor's simpler trigger. Keep the ownership guard until then.

Liveness: also require !PsGetProcessExitProcessCalled(ep), which XP exports (tools/xp_exports/ntoskrnl.exe.txt:865), so an exit code of 259 is not read as alive. Make QUERY count owners without forgetting slots.

Have the miniport publish a reset counter (in vcr_info or the guard result) that the display DLL compares before loading the fog table or preparing state. Kernel-initiated (B) resets then also invalidate fog_valid and bump the generation.

Close open question 8 from source. User processes get the register BAR only through IOCTL_VCR_MAP_GLIDE: QUERY_PUBLIC_ACCESS_RANGES refuses user mappings at vcrmp.c:734, and SHARE_VIDEO_MEMORY maps only the LFB. So every process that can enable cmdFifo0 is in x->procs. Correct fact 10 to say the slaves' FIFOs are live in SLI.

Make the (C) refusal before the context slot is allocated. Otherwise mirror target_refused's cleanup (EngFreeMem of fpu plus the memset, vcrdd_d3d.c:1177/1192-1194) so a refused ContextCreate does not leak.

problems: Wrong producer. The ring of pid 1892's close has no HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE and no 'SLI/AA off: Glide asked' (onbox/ring_start_decoded.txt:866-987). That rules out hwcRestoreVideo's not-idle path: both of its exits reach hwcRestoreVideo_release -> hwcReleaseDisplay -> HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE (build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/minihwc/minihwc.c:6015, 6315-6322, 4473-4500). vcrdd always logs that escape and answers it with RESTORE_MODE (vcr-kmd/display/vcrdd_escape.c:134-170). problems: Event-code collision. Part B logs the two silent refusals as 513 what 24 and ships them 'in the next vcrdd.dll build, which is G10's' (G11.md:137-148, :274). G10 gives 513/24 another meaning: promoted-Z placement and out-of-vidmem; it also takes 513/25 for the Z lock (designs/G10.md:180, :189, :235-236). G01 (G01.md:170-171), G03 (G03.md:244), G09 (G09.md:206-207), G13 (G13.md:177-194), G15, G22 and G44 claim 513/24 as well. G02.md:334 lists the overlap and moved to its own event 514. vcr_events.h:75 has one description string per event, so one binary emitting 513/24 with two meanings makes the ring undecodable.

The flip-chain suffix can never reach the ring. Ring messages are capped at VCR_LOG_MSG_LEN 96: include/vcr_log.h:32, vcr_ioctl.h:179, display/vcrdd_log.c:35 (vsnprintf into r.msg) and common/vcr_log.c:59 (copies 95 chars). The 513/12 text as emitted is already 87 chars (ring_after_probe_i_decoded.txt:85), so only 8 of the suffix's ~143 chars would survive. The 513/17 text is ~128 chars and is truncated today. The proposed source test 'target_refused carries the flip-chain suffix' would pass while the ring never shows the suffix. The HAL's own precedent is a second event (vcrdd_d3d.c:904: 'two events: a ring message holds 95 characters'). Editing the 12 format literal also breaks the pin at test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:277.

The suffix would be false in two common cases. (1) target_refused() is shared with SETRENDERTARGET (vcrdd_d3d.c:1739); a refusal there on a flip-chain back buffer causes no revert. (2) DX5-7 titles also render into DDSCAPS_FLIP back buffers but set the mode themselves, and their runtime does not restore it; that covers most staged .124 D3D titles (Thief, SS2, JK/MotS, Shogo, R6, AvP). Our ContextCreate overwrites p->dwhContext without reading it (vcrdd_d3d.c:1198). 3dfx reads the creating interface version from that field on entry (VH5/D3CONTXT.C:356-357: '0=DX3, 1=DX5, 2=DX6, 3=DX7, 4=DX8'); that this holds on the NT path is unconfirmed.

The d3dprobe preflight and the caps 'hal' devices contradict four pinned tests the design does not mention. (1) test_vcr_kmd_monitor_safety.py:364-373 requires every IDirect3D8_CreateDevice and IDirect3DDevice8_Release site, in ANY d3dprobe function, to sit between vcr_pace_before_switch() and vcr_pace_after_*. The design's new rule, 'preflight has no vcr_pace_ call', is its exact negation. (2) and (3) :385-386 allow CreateDevice only in main and Release only in release_device. (4) test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:652-653 asserts 'caps makes no device and switches nothing' ('CreateDevice' not in caps). The design reasoned only about :393-411. release_device() (d3dprobe.c:194-204) paces whenever g_full is set, so the preflight, which runs on the fullscreen path, cannot reuse it either.

caps would stop being device-free. silicon_battery.py:275 runs 'd3dprobe caps' as its first D3D step, lab_run.py:76 defaults d3dprobe to caps, and d3dprobe_run.py:108 refuses --noz with caps because 'caps creates no device'. Each caps call would create up to three windowed devices on the desktop PDEV, with surfaces low in the heap. If a stale Glide FIFO is on, they land inside its window (G01; session_log.md:9), and the only guard is step 1a of the on-box plan. The new per-cell key reuses the name 'hal', which is already the top-level GetDeviceCaps HRESULT (test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:649, 'one key per name'). G10 step 2 also expects caps output to stay identical to caps_124.txt.

rc 3 is taken: it already means Direct3DCreate8 failed (d3dprobe.c:1307-1310). d3dprobe_run.py never sees the exit code anyway: it runs 'cmd /c start /wait' under EXECW and parses the RESULT line (d3dprobe_run.py:153-175).

lan_sweep.py is not a D3D sweep. It runs every desktop shortcut, Glide and OpenGL included, and health-checks Glide after each title (lan_sweep.py:2-22); the D3D runs used --only (:394). PhaseLog's 64 slots (vcrmp_log.c:39) are shared with SLI milestones (vcrmp_multi.c:111-112, :359). The 11-12 OpenGL 4-chip session alone wrote 40 phases (ring_start_decoded.txt seq 23786-24536). A Glide title that opens the board twice overflows 64 slots, and the design's 'over 64 = unknown and FAIL' rule then fails it for something it did not do.

Torn read. VcrPhase writes PhaseCount and PhaseLog as separate registry values, count first (vcrmp_log.c:152-157). A REGREAD landing between the two pairs the new count with the old blob, for example right after a title exits while XP is still restoring the desktop.

'reverts' cannot be computed from the specified data. MODESET_BEGIN records only the target mode (vcrmp_hw.c:670). The 4-phase 11-12 test window cannot yield reverts=1 unless the mode before the window is supplied, and the test spec does not supply it.

The FLAP (refusal) class depends on the 513 refusal still being in the ring, but a running game wraps the 1024-entry ring within seconds (session_log.md:17, 'Ring wrapped'; G76). Open question 3 asks about titles that are refused, retry another Z format, then run. In exactly that case the 513/12 is overwritten before lan_sweep fetches the ring. The title is filed as 'app re-set' and passes, so the measurement misses the event it exists to find.

problems: GAP CONFIRMED at e3056d1, and Part A's mechanism holds. color_path picks 'other' = TEXTURE, then TFACTOR(c1), then DIFFUSE, and the local is always the iterated colour (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:698-716, alpha :733-740). compute_regs writes c0=0 and c1=TF (:1019-1020). CP_LOCAL_C0 and CP_ALOCAL_C0 (KMD/include/vcr_3dregs.h:80-81) are never used. c0 is written only by VcrDd3dState (vcrdd_3d.c:83), every flush, inside the same VcrDdRoom(12), so with the bit off the words are byte-identical. On the hardware side: fbzColorPath[4] / [6:5]=1 select color0 when combineMode[31]=0 (avenger_spec L2737-2738 and the MUX table after L2826). Supporting evidence the design misses, which closes most of its open question 4: 3dfx's own Napalm Glide uses exactly this path on VSA-100. Its triangle clear builds fbzColorPath with GR_COMBINE_LOCAL_CONSTANT<<SST_LOCALSELECT_SHIFT and clears the FBI's combineMode[31] (retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/glide3/src/gglide.c:1275-1290, :1326-1331); the legacy grColorCombine ORs local<<SST_LOCALSELECT_SHIFT (gglide.c:3480, alpha :801), and validation clears USE_COMBINE_MODE (distate.c:1945-1970).

The helper cannot implement the design's own table. vcr_cc_stage0(op,a1,a2,aop,b1,b2,tex,feat) (G14.md:198) takes no `two` and no stage-1 op, and color_path only receives `tex` (vcrdd_d3d.c:977; `two` is a local at :928). Yet the §3.1 table (G14.md:181) says 'two textures with a non-MODULATE stage-0 TFACTOR op: unchanged'. As specified, Part A folds stage-0 ADD(TEX,TF) under a stage-1 lightmap into (tex0*tex1)+TF = 0xc44040, which is the very value G14's own probe tfactor_s0_add (G14.md:409) calls wrong. The 'exhaustive' native test (G14.md:425-433) never varies `two` or the stage-1 ops, so it cannot catch this. tf_tmu_tris also needs `two`.

The D3DFeat transport is not default-OFF-safe. VcrDd2dInit reads into an uninitialised stack `vcr_info info` (KMD/display/vcrdd_2d.c:436, IOCTL :443) and never checks info.size. The miniport returns only min(OutputBufferLength, its own sizeof) bytes (KMD/miniport/vcrmp.c:789-797, Information=info at :891). So an appended d3d_feat read from an older miniport is stack garbage, and random feature bits get armed: for example when vcrdd.dll is swapped alone, or when vcrmp.sys is rolled back. Today the display driver reads no appended field at all, so the 'established extension' covers only older tools. G12.md:342's claim that the shorter struct 'reads as 0' is false. The existing bit-field switch D3DBigTex travels as positive VCR_INFO_F_* flags precisely because 'an older miniport never sets them' (vcrmp.c:447-449; vcrdd_2d.c:452). The sibling designs also disagree: d3d_feat vs d3dfeat, appended field vs flags, and G08's VCR_INFO_F_D3DLEGACY and G16's VCR_INFO_F_D3DLINES both take 0x8000. test_vcr_kmd_abi.c pins the flag bits (:118-139) but not vcr_info's size or offsets.

c0 has three proposed owners. G13's legacy fallback for SELECTARG1(TEXTURE|ALPHAREPLICATE) sets CP_LOCAL_C0 with c0=0xffffffff, on the claim that 'c0 is otherwise unused' (G13.md:357). G12 sets c0=c1=TF whenever it is armed (G12.md:313). G14 sets c0=TF when it selects a TF partner. With G13 and G14 both armed, an RGB SELECTARG1(TEXTURE|AREP) plus an alpha TFACTOR partner needs c0.rgb=white and c0.a=TF.a. A whole-word 'c0 = TF' rule then draws texture alpha x TF.rgb.

Part B duplicates G12's bit 7 (VCR_D3DF_CMB_TMU, G12.md:52, :131-132, :327) with a conflicting discipline. G14 writes the TMU chroma pair on every flush (+2 PIO, G14.md:254-263). G12 shadows it (pd->tmuc_valid) and invalidates through VcrDd3dForget (G12.md:327-337). G14's ctx_free restore (chroma=0, then TMU combineMode=0; G14.md:294-301) never clears G12's shadow, so a surviving context's TMU-stage TFACTOR reads as 0. G14's justification that every DP2 re-sends the full state (G14.md:300-301) stops being true as soon as G12's or G53's shadowing lands. The probe name tfactor_tex is also defined two different ways: G12.md:415 (white texture x TF 0xFF0000) and G14.md:400.

The chroma hazard analysis rests on the spec alone and covers one direction only. (a) avenger_spec L3547 says chromaRange[30:29]=3 enables substitution, but h3defs.h:988-990 names bit 29 SST_ENCHROMAKEY_TMU and bit 30 SST_ENCOLORSUBSTITUTION. Our shipping Glide's GR_TEXCHROMA_ENABLE_EXT ('substitute with black') sets only bits 28|29 (retro3dfx-glide/.../h5/glide3/src/gtex.c:3333-3337). So TF alphas with bits 5:4 set (0x30-0x3f, 0x70-0x7f, 0xb0-0xbf, 0xf0-0xff) also arm it, not only the 0x60-0x7f and 0xe0-0xff stated at G14.md:278-282. With TF=0xffffffff in both registers (all-exclusive, union, range [ff,ff]) nearly every texel is keyed. (b) The same hazard exists today in the other direction. Reset3D writes combineMode=0 by broadcast and never zeroes chroma (KMD/include/vcr_3dseq.h:192). MesaFX's GL_BLEND texenv (retro3dfx-gl/.../glide/fxsetup.h:282-291, grConstantColorValueExt) makes Glide load the constant into the TMU chromaKey/chromaRange under combineMode[30]=1 (distate.c:1655-1672). After such a GL session, Reset3D, or any G03 baseline that clears combineMode, leaves that constant live as a chroma key for the D3D legacy path. G14.md:305-306 treats this only as 'if G03 adds chroma writes'.

Part A's effect in the field also depends on G03, not only Part B's. MesaFX on Napalm takes the extended-combine path (retro3dfx-gl/.../glide/fxsetup.c:1465, grColorCombineExt), which leaves the FBI's combineMode[31]=1. With that bit set, fbzColorPath[4] and [6:5] are ignored (spec MUX table). So after any OpenGL or Glide session in the same boot, Part A changes nothing until G03 lands. The cold-boot rule covers the probes, not players.

The tfactor_clear probe is not independent of the switch. Its quad C, MODULATE(TEXTURE,TFACTOR) expecting 0x300000 (G14.md:408), needs Part A. So on the bit-off runs (86Box step 1 and .124 boot 1: 'the five Part-A tests fail ... everything else passes', G14.md:500-506) it fails as a sixth test, and the acceptance criterion is wrong as written. Separately, every DP2 call memsets the walk, so `prepared` restarts at 0 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1835). When the runtime sends the clear through Clear2, quad B therefore guards only future register shadowing (G53), not the dirty flag at :1419.

Event-code and switch-bit collisions. 513 what 24 is also claimed by G01 (G01.md:170), G10 (:180, :235), G11 (:137), G15 (:266) and G16 (:106). 'what 25' is claimed by G01, G10 and G16. G14 also needs a third code for its 'armed' line, and G16 already claims 26. D3DFeat bit 10 is claimed by both G27 and G31, and G14 picks no bit at all.

Overstated or unconfirmed claims about games. 'Every use is wrong today' (G14.md:24-26, :573) is false: SELECTARG(TFACTOR) and op(TFACTOR, DIFFUSE) are already right (vcrdd_d3d.c:693-694, :699-703). The only TFACTOR use ever measured on .124, UT2003's menu combine 7 = SELECTARG1(TFACTOR) (evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt:20), is correct today. Halo's TFACTOR/TEXTUREFACTOR strings (halo.exe 0x23e58c, 0x23ecd8) belong to the D3DX effect-parser token tables, which is not evidence of use. UE2 is better supported: D3DDrv.dll in both UT2003 and UT2004 carries the UTF-16 stage-printer strings 'tfactor(%u,%u,%u,%u)' and '%s * tfactor.a(%u) + %s * (1 - tfactor.a(%u))'. That makes TFACTOR operands plausible, but also BLENDFACTORALPHA, which Part A leaves drawn as MODULATE.

Modifiers. Part A keys on ARG_KIND (vcrdd_d3d.c:671), which drops COMPLEMENT and ALPHAREPLICATE. A TFACTOR|AREP or TFACTOR|COMPLEMENT partner therefore also flips to c0, and the bit-on exhaustive test (G14.md:430-433) would bless tex x TF.rgb for the Halo-glow hypothesis case, which needs tex x TF.a.

Minor measurement defects. tf_conflicts is counted per compute_regs, but prepare() can run compute_regs twice in one flush (vcrdd_d3d.c:1329-1336). Event 25 (stage-1 arguments, 'once per combination') under-reports, because log_combo's hash covers the stage-1 ops but not their arguments (:888-890).
corrections: Pass `two` and stage 1's COLOROP and ALPHAOP into vcr_cc_stage0. With two textures, apply the c0 fold only when stage 0 and stage 1 are both MODULATE, the only exact case. Otherwise keep today's word and count it, as the §3.1 table promises. Extend the native exhaustive test over two in {0,1} x the stage-1 ops, and assert tfactor_s0_add's value with Part A on and Part B off.

Make the switch transport default-OFF-safe. Either memset(&info, 0, sizeof info) in VcrDd2dInit before IOCTL_VCR_INFO and read d3d_feat only when info.size >= offsetof(vcr_info, d3d_feat)+4, or use positive VCR_INFO_F_* flags as D3DBigTex does. Pin vcr_info's size and offsets as append-only in tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_abi.c. Settle one name and one transport for every D3DFeat design, and resolve the double use of 0x8000 by G08 and G16.

Give c0 a single owner: the shared helper returns per-channel demands (rgb, alpha) and composes c0 = (alpha<<24)|rgb. When two demands for the same channel differ, as with G13's white and G14's TF, refuse and count it.

Drop Part B from G14 and make it the TFACTOR column of G12's bit 7. G14's rules become acceptance criteria on G12: chroma is written only after the combineMode words that carry bit 30, and only through chip field 6. Any write that clears a TMU's combineMode[30] (the ctx_free restore, Reset3D, G03's baseline) first zeroes that TMU's chromaKey and chromaRange, then calls VcrDd3dForget so tmuc_valid is cleared. Rename or merge the probes so tfactor_tex has a single definition.

HAZARD THE DESIGN MISSES: its zero TMU words re-arm texture chroma substitution.
- G05 always writes TMU1 = 0 (G05.md 3.2). It writes TMU0 = 0 whenever only the FBI needs a shift, and it restores 0/0/0 at every DP2 end (3.4). All of these clear bit 30.
- SPEC 8.21: 'When chromaRange[30:29]=0x3 and combineMode[30]=0, then texture chroma substitution is enabled'.
- Glide sets TMU bit 30 whenever it uses a constant colour (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/glide3/src/gtex.c:1931-1932). It then loads TMU chromaKey and chromaRange with that colour (distate.c:1655-1667), so the colour's alpha bits 6:5 land in chromaRange[30:29]. A clean close does not reset TMU combineMode (G03.md:56, 62-71).
- Our own MesaFX ICD loads such a colour for GL_BLEND texenv and GL_CONSTANT combines (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/build/retro3dfx-gl/src/mesa/drivers/glide/fxsetup.h:254-295, 68-114).
- After such a GL session, the first armed 2X DP2 leaves substitution armed for every later textured D3D draw in that boot. The risk table (G05.md 8) checks bit 30 only on the non-zero words.
- So G03 is a hard dependency, not a 'soft' one. Likelihood is low (the env-colour alpha must have bits 6:5 = 11), but it is new behaviour G05 introduces.

The FBI shift survives prepare()'s texture drop.
- The shift is decided in compute_regs using its tex flag.
- prepare() later drops texturing when the vertex lacks the texcoord set (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1351-1355). It clears regs.textured and CP_TEXTURE but keeps RGBSEL_TMU.
- The design guards only the TMU word (c->regs.textured ? vcr_cm_tmu(..) : 0, G05.md 3.4). The FBI word still carries the shift, so the draw becomes 2x of an undefined TMU colour. This is an edge case.

The restore does not leave 'the state the proven HAL leaves' (G05.md 3.4).
- The proven HAL never writes combineMode. Only Reset3D does, and it is default off (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/include/vcr_3dseq.h:193).

- A non-2X DP2 sends identical bytes, but the chip state under them differs. Boot B's 'default matrices identical to boot A' proves this only if the matrices run AFTER the 2X tests and after a GL title.

Today that state is dormant, because the HAL never writes combineMode. G05 writes TMU0 and TMU1 = 0 for FBI-only 2X states and on every restore, and never clears chromaRange.
