The 'must land before G66' argument (designs/G10.md:40 and :463-466) is already handled by G66 itself. designs/G66.md:59 and its §4.1 and §4.5 choose RF's depth per box: 16 wherever vcrmp runs, until G10 is proven. By G10's own rule (G10.md:466) that caps G10 at P1. G20 (G20.md:600) and G36 (G36.md:714) apply 'no staged title stopped today, so not P0' to themselves.

RF's real 32 bpp request is A8R8G8B8 + D16. The X8R8G8B8 + D16 that was measured is a different request. rf.exe 0x544664-0x5446b5 takes BackBufferFormat from gr_init's 10th argument, which is HKCU 'Resolution Backbuffer Format' ([0x5a127c], default -1, read at 0x4b14c9-0x4b14d7). When that value is negative, 32 bpp gives A8R8G8B8 (21). G10 §2 (G10.md:100) misreads 0x544694 as 'a matching adapter mode's format'. G66's hand-off keeps the value pinned at -1. d3dprobe always builds X8R8G8B8 at --bpp 32 (KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c:1423), and caps checks only CheckDeviceType(X8,X8) and (565,565) (d3dprobe.c:1378). RF's exact shape has never been probed.

A static read suggests the runtime refuses RF's back buffer on this PCI id whatever the Z format. In XP SP3 d3d8.dll (md5 f099b129), IDirect3D8::CheckDeviceType (0x6d9ad340, vtable slot at file offset 0x8e4) accepts a back buffer that differs from the display format only if it is the display format's alpha twin and carries D3DFORMAT_OP 0x100 (0x6d9ad44f-0x6d9ad499). The legacy op builder ORs in 0x8 instead of 0x100 when PCI flag 0x4000 is set (0x6d9af18a-0x6d9af19a, 0x6d9af319). The 121a:0009 entry is 0x4580, which includes 0x4000 (reports/runtime.md §4.3). So CheckDeviceType(X8R8G8B8, A8R8G8B8, fullscreen) is very likely NOTAVAILABLE on .124. Whether CreateDevice applies the same test was not traced. G10's 'unblocks Red Faction at its staged 32 bpp' is therefore unproven, and may be false unless the back-buffer format is also pinned.

Battlefield 1942 is not at risk on .124. SafeDisc 2.80 in Mods\bf1942\Mod.dll stops its client before Direct3D (LIB/BF1942/README-FLEET.txt hardware result; reports/games.md:415-418). Its staged Video.con sets no depth buffer (Profiles/Default/Video.con: `game.setGameDisplayMode 800 600 32 0`). BF1942.exe picks its depth buffer by enumeration ('no depthbuffer supported by the videocard', '16bit/24:8 bit/32bit depth buffer'). Listing it is speculation.

The other exposure paths have no staged consumer. (b) Windowed: every staged title runs fullscreen. (d) DX6/7 Z attach at 32 bpp: Shogo (autoexec.cfg:21 screendepth 16), SS2 and Thief Gold (game_screen_depth 16), and JK, MotS, R6 and AvP all run at 16 bpp. Thief II's DX6 path runs only with D3D32 off, where G10 does nothing. UE2 forces 16 bpp on vendor 0x121a (UT2004 D3DDrv.dll vendor branch at 0x10011265; UT2003.log:102-103). The 32 bpp titles that do run (Max Payne, H&D, Halo, Thief II) already create devices with a 24-bit Z. objdump finds zero `$0x121a` immediates in e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll, igraph2.dll and i3d2.dll.

Case (c), SetRenderTarget, is the one plausible real consumer, and it was not measured. It is not silent: vcrdd_d3d.c:1739 logs 513/12 'SETRENDERTARGET (not drawn)'. Max Payne at 32 bpp builds render-target textures, each with its own 'texture zbuffer' (e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll strings: P_ZBufferFormat, setRenderTargetFormat). Whether that Z is D16 is unknown. G36's census (E6) or one in-game ring would settle it.

Fresh installs are not exposed. With Diag\D3D32 absent, rt32 is 0 and vcr_rt_format(0,32,*) is REFUSED (include/vcr_rtfmt.h:84-86), so the promotion is inert and a 32 bpp device is refused before the mode set (G20.md:143). G10 matters only after G20 step 2. There its value is avoiding the CRT double switch (G11, P2) for titles that pick D16 at 32 bpp, and no staged title does.

The verification plan swaps both binaries and arms the Diag bit in one boot (G10.md §6 Deploy steps 1-4). The new vcrdd.dll and vcrmp.sys are never run on silicon with the bit off before it is armed. That includes the unrelated miniport changes since fda1b8c9, such as 1667afa. A regression could not be attributed to one change.

The ring signals the pass criteria rely on clash with sibling designs. G10 claims 513 what 24/25 (§4.5) and flag 0x80000 (§4.1). G01 (G01.md:170-171), G03 (G03.md:244-247) and G11 (G11.md:137) also claim 513/24-25, and G02.md:334 already lists that clash. G03 maps D3DSafe bit 3 to 0x40000 (G03.md:239-240). Until codes are reserved, '513/24 per promoted Z', '513/25 fires once' and 'flags carry 0x80000' are ambiguous.

Step 8 (RF at 32 bpp) launches through the staged launcher and also writes HKLM, which rf.exe never reads (0x52b2b3). Once G66 lands, that launcher writes HKCU 'Resolution Bit Depth' per box (16 on vcrmp boxes) and silently overrides the session's 32. In-game play is optional ('if G68'), yet on .124 the mount launcher already reaches the menu, which needs CD #2 (LIB/RedFaction/README-DISC.txt). The 24-bit-Z benefit shows only in 3D scenes, not in RF's 2D menu.
Nothing tests a killed process holding a promoted Z, although G10.md:442 claims that lifecycle is covered. zleak and the RF run never kill a process that holds an SF_Z32 block.
corrections: Re-rank G10 to P2. It is caps hygiene (the runtime promises a pair the HAL refuses) and it enables G20 step 2. Raise it to P1 only on evidence: an in-game ring from a staged title with 513/12 '32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z' (c=0x10), from the G36 E6 census or a G68/G04 session; or G20 step 2 being scheduled; or the user asking for Red Faction at 32 bpp.

Restate the title list. Red Faction is affected only if raised to 32 bpp on .124, which G66 deliberately does not do. Drop BF1942: its client is DRM-blocked and it picks its depth buffer by enumeration. Mark the windowed and DX6/7 cases as tooling-only, with no staged consumer.

Before building anything, extend d3dprobe caps, which needs no device and no mode switch. Add CheckDeviceType(HAL, X8R8G8B8, A8R8G8B8, FALSE) and CheckDepthStencilMatch(X8R8G8B8 adapter, A8R8G8B8 target, D16 and D24X8), add `--bbfmt a8r8g8b8` to render, and run both on the current build. If A8R8G8B8 is refused, G66 §4.5's hand-off must also write HKCU 'Resolution Backbuffer Format'=22 (X8R8G8B8) whenever it sets RF_BPP=32. rf.exe uses that value as is (0x544664-0x54469f), so RF then asks for exactly the shape G10's d3dprobe test proves. The hand-off should also check the deployed driver build, not only the Diag registry bits.
Correct G10 §2: 0x544694 consumes HKCU 'Resolution Backbuffer Format' (gr_init's 10th argument, default -1), not an adapter-mode match. RF asks for A8R8G8B8 + D16 at 32 bpp unless that value is set.

Split the silicon proof into two boots. Boot A: the new vcrmp.sys and vcrdd.dll with D3DSafe absent. Its caps must match caps_124.txt byte for byte, the 8876086c and 513/12 refusal must still appear, the 16 and 32 bpp controls must reach 40/40 and windowed 42/42. Boot B: D3DSafe=8 alone. Run boot A on G01's miniport build and boot B in G20's planned boot C to avoid extra reboots.

Reserve the 513 what codes, or a dedicated event id as G02 proposes with 514, and one D3DSafe bit-to-flag convention across G01, G02, G03, G10 and G11 before the first of them lands. Update G10's native and Python tests and its on-box pass criteria to the reserved values.

Make Red Faction in game a gating step. Launch rf.exe directly after the mount (not through a G66-era launcher), write HKCU only, and record 'Resolution Backbuffer Format' for each run: 22 is G10's shape, absent is RF's native A8R8G8B8. Play one level and run -timedemo at 16 and at 32 bpp, so the 32 bpp quality gain can be weighed against the one-chip fill cost.
Add a killed-process check: start d3dprobe holding a promoted 1024x1024 D16, kill it by pid, then zleak must still create 64/64. That proves process teardown frees the SF_Z32 block.

problems: RED FACTION'S REQUEST IS MISREAD (rf.exe md5 0ba3b15d). G10 section 2 says the 32 bpp back-buffer format comes from 'a matching adapter mode's format (0x544694)'. It does not. Arg 4 of 0x5444b0 (0x2c(%esp), used at 0x544664 and 0x544694) is the registry value 'Resolution Backbuffer Format': string 0x5a1534, read at 0x4b14c9-0x4b14d7 with default 0xffffffff into 0x5a127c, then passed by 0x4b1121 -> 0x50b960 arg 9 -> 0x50bcba. The staged tree never writes that value (install.reg; Play Red Faction.bat:56-58 writes only Width/Height/Bit Depth). So at its staged 32 bpp, RF asks for BackBufferFormat A8R8G8B8 (21) with D16, not X8R8G8B8 with D16. d3dprobe can only ask for X8R8G8B8 at 32 bpp (tools/d3dprobe.c:1423), and caps/zmatch never test A8R8G8B8 (d3dprobe.c:1348-1349). The planned '40/40 at --bpp 32 --zfmt d16' therefore does not exercise Red Faction's pairing.

UNSTATED DEPENDENCY ON D3DBigTex BIT 2. Read from XP SP3 d3d8.dll 5.3.2600.5512 (md5 f099b129): CheckDeviceType (0x6d9ad340) accepts an alpha back buffer over an X8R8G8B8 mode only if A8R8G8B8 carries D3DFORMAT_OP_SAME_FORMAT_UP_TO_ALPHA_RENDERTARGET, 0x100 (0x6d9ad453-0x6d9ad497). For a DX7 driver that op comes only from a LISTED A8R8G8B8 texture format plus table flag 0x400. Flag 0x4000 makes it OFFSCREEN_RENDERTARGET (0x6d9af18a-0x6d9af19f, 0x6d9af2fb-0x6d9af319), and a post-pass ORs in 0x110 (0x6d9af6c1-0x6d9af6cc). Our A8R8G8B8 entry exists only with Diag\D3DBigTex bit 2 (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:2087-2091). So RF at 32 bpp needs G10 AND bit 2. Without bit 2 (a fresh install, even after G20) the runtime refuses it (8876086a) whatever G10 does. The claimed 'fresh installs once G20 flips D3D32' benefit for RF is overstated. (Traced in CheckDeviceType; CreateDevice's own copy of that check was not traced.)

THE RUNTIME RULE IS VISIBLE, AND THE DESIGN SAYS IT IS NOT (sections 1 and 3). d3d8 CheckDepthStencilMatch (0x6d9ad790) sets 'depth must match' only in three cases: D16_LOCKABLE (0x6d9ad897); stencil formats, via 0x6d9abce0 (0x48-0x4b, 0x4e, 0x4f); and D24X8/D32 when the SDK version is above 120 (0x6d9ad8bc-0x6d9ad8cf). ZSTENCIL_WITH_ARBITRARY clears it (0x6d9ad917-0x6d9ad922). Plain D16 never has to match. Consequences: (a) zlock binds a D16_LOCKABLE to a 32 bpp target, which this rule refuses; if SetRenderTarget applies the same check (unconfirmed) zlock cannot produce the expected 24-bit words. (b) No D3D8 application can lock a promoted D16 in 32/32 use (D16 is not lockable; D16_LOCKABLE must match), so the 513/25 lock hazard is DX5-7 only. (c) DX8.0 titles get R5G6B5 + D24X8 past the runtime: Red Faction calls Direct3DCreate8(0x78) at rf.exe 0x54454e. 'D3D8 refuses the reverse pair itself' is true only for SDK > 120; be58b7d is what covers SDK-120 titles.

THE STEP-2 FILL RULE IS WRONG FOR A LAYOUT THE DESIGN KEEPS. Section 4.7 fills every SF_Z32 Z at bpp 4 with (d<<8)|(d>>8). A promoted D16 behind a 16 bpp target is used as 16/16-in-32: pixel x is the 16-bit unit at byte 2x of the row (include/vcr_rtfmt.h:70-78, :82; design sections 4.3 and 7). There, an MSB-replicated word gives odd pixels W>>16 = 0x00FF for the common 0xFFFF clear. 3dfx's (c<<16)|c (VH5/DDBLT32.C:948) is right for every d in that layout, and for 0 and 0xFFFF in 32/32. The planned native assertion that '3dfx's word copy is NOT the value' pins a rule that ignores the layout.

THE HEL DEPTH-FILL DEFECT IS WORSE THAN STATED, AND THE PLAN CANNOT SEE IT. With the D16 label kept and lPitch 4w, a HEL Blt(DDBLT_DEPTHFILL) in 32/32 use writes 2w bytes of each 4w row. Pixels 0..w/2-1 get d|(d<<16); pixels w/2..w-1 keep the previous frame's depth, so the RIGHT HALF of the screen renders against stale Z. That is a P0-class render defect for any DX5-7 title that clears Z with Blt at 32 bpp with a D16 (the HAL caps lack BLTDEPTHFILL, display/vcrdd_ddraw.c:101; the HEL caps f4c08241 have it). Step 2 is conditional on 513/25, but the on-box plan runs only d3dprobe, ddlab and Red Faction. Red Faction is D3D8 and cannot DirectDraw-Blt, so no run could show 513/25 before default-on.

THE LABEL DECISION IS ARGUED ONE-SIDEDLY. Section 4.2 rejects 3dfx's relabel because a HEL fill of 0xFFFF would write 0x0000FFFF. The kept D16 label is also wrong in 32/32 (previous item). The relabel to 32 / 0x00FFFFFF (VH5/DDSURF.C:619-627) has three advantages: it gives a correct fill to applications that derive dwFillDepth from the Z mask; it fixes the section 4.8 item 3 SRCCOPY case; and it would satisfy a d3dim700 depth-pairing check, if one exists (open question 4). Section 3 also misdescribes 3dfx: FX_ORIGINALLY_Z16 is set only at AddAttachedSurface (DDSURF.C:2346), so the (c<<16)|c patch (DDBLT32.C:940-948) never applies to the create-time promotion G10 copies. 3dfx relied on the relabel there.

THE ON-BOX PLAN HAS GAPS. (a) Step 4 runs '--tests d16_32,zprec,zleak' without --zfmt d16. The windowed default Z is D24X8 (d3dprobe.c:1433-1446), so zprec passes on the old build too and proves nothing about the promotion. (b) Nothing tests the one previously working case that changes: a D16 made in a 32 bpp mode behind a 16 bpp target, now 16/16-in-32, which one Rainbow Six frame is the only silicon proof of. (c) No D3DSafe=8 sweep covers the 32 bpp D3D titles that run today: H&D Deluxe (forced 32 bpp), Thief II NewDark (32), Max Payne (1280x960x32), Halo, and AvP. A title that today tries D16 at 32 bpp and falls back would silently take the new path.

ALLOCATION FAILURE REGRESSES A WORKING CASE. VcrDdD3dCreateZSurface returns DDERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY when the 4*w*h block does not fit. Today a D16 made at 32 bpp for a 16 bpp target gets a 2*w*h block from DirectDraw and draws 16/16. Under memory pressure it would now fail to be created at all.

THE dwSCnt==1 GATE MISSES ATOMIC RESTORES, SILENTLY. W2K DDK section 3.3.1.3 (Lost Surfaces and Atomic Restoration): when CreateSurfaceEx is exported, as ours is (vcrdd_d3d.c:2220-2222), DirectDraw restores complex surfaces in ONE CreateSurface call. A 16-bit Z inside a multi-surface create is then left unpromoted and refused at the next SETRENDERTARGET after an alt-tab or mode switch, i.e. the title stops drawing. The proposed 513/12 hint ('this D16 was made in a 16 bpp mode') also mislabels this case, a Z too wide for the stride field, and a system-memory Z.

COORDINATION CONFLICTS. G03.md:238-240 already assigns G10 bit 3 = 0x40000 under its 0x8000<<bit convention; G10 proposes 0x10000<<bit = 0x80000. Events 513/24 and 513/25 are also claimed by G01, G03, G05, G11, G12 and G16 (G15.md:266). Step 2 advertises DDCAPS_BLTDEPTHFILL in 32 bpp PDEVs only, a mode-dependent cap that contradicts the design's own 'caps stay mode-independent' (runtime-22) constraint.

P0 IS NOT SUPPORTED BY THE TASK'S DEFINITIONS. No staged .124 title is stopped today; the gap itself says 'No title run so far hits it'. RF runs at 640x480x16 because G66's values never land, and UE2 forces 16 bpp on 3dfx: UT2004 D3DDrv.dll 0x10011265-0x10011292 sets a flag for vendor 0x121a, which matches UT2004.log's 16-bit back buffer despite Use16bit=False. G10 is a prerequisite for G66's 32 bpp Red Faction and for G20, which makes it P1.

NOT A DEFECT, confirmed for the record. The refusal is real on silicon: CreateDevice 8876086c with ring 513/12, vcr_rtfmt.h:84-85 -> vcrdd_d3d.c:1189-1196. rf.exe hard-codes D16 for vendor 0x121a at both depths (0x544756-0x54476f -> 0x5446f6). The VSA-100 can store a D16 as a 24+8 aux word: renderMode[1:0] is the only pixel-size field (H3DEFS.H:126-130); auxBufferAddr is 16-byte aligned with a [25:4] address, so all 64 MB per chip are reachable; the linear stride is [13:0]; depth is 24-bit at 32 bpp (h5 Glide diget.c:792-797). Downstream code already follows t->fmt: vcr_3dseq.h:56-78, vcrdd_3d.c:153 and :292. With the bit off, every proven path is unchanged. The mip-chain lifecycle precedent matches the DDK: at a mode change, DdDestroySurface is called for every surface under the driver's control (ddraw_08br).
corrections: Fix section 2: arg 4 is rf.exe's 'Resolution Backbuffer Format' (default -1), so at 32 bpp Red Faction asks for A8R8G8B8 + D16. For .124, have G66 stage 'Resolution Backbuffer Format' = 22 (X8R8G8B8) together with Bit Depth 32: that is the exact pair d3dprobe proves. Otherwise write down that RF at 32 bpp also needs Diag\D3DBigTex bit 2, and carry that dependency into G20.

Extend d3dprobe with a fullscreen '--bbfmt a8r8g8b8' option. Add CheckDeviceType(X8R8G8B8 display, A8R8G8B8 back buffer, fullscreen) and an A8R8G8B8 zmatch row to 'caps'. Run 'render --full --bpp 32 --bbfmt a8r8g8b8 --zfmt d16', Red Faction's exact request, before step 8.

Replace 'the rule is not visible' with the rule read from d3d8.dll: a depth match is required only for D16_LOCKABLE, stencil formats, and D24X8/D32 at SDK > 120; plain D16 never. Rewrite the falsified comments with it: vcr_rtfmt.h:21-25 and :189-191, vcrdd_d3d.c:2182-2186, d3dprobe.c:1343-1346 (keeping the pinned substring) and d3dprobe.c:1430-1432. State that SDK-120 titles (Red Faction) also reach the HAL with R5G6B5 + D24X8, so be58b7d and its tests must stay.

zlock: record the SetRenderTarget HRESULT, and measure the lock pitch on an UNBOUND D16_LOCKABLE created in the 32 bpp mode (it is promoted either way). State that a D3D8 application cannot lock a promoted D16 in 32/32 use, so 513/25 is a DX5-7 signal.

Run zprec with --zfmt d16, or have it bind its own D16, so the old build cannot pass it. Add a d16_rtt16 check: in a 32 bpp mode, a promoted D16 bound with an R5G6B5 render-target texture (the runtime grants that format by table flag 0x100), the ztest scene, read back through a textured quad. That covers the changed 16/16-in-32 case.

Step 2 (with G61): make the depth fill layout-aware. Keep in dwReserved1 the format of the last target that target_of accepted with this Z. Fill (d<<8)|(d>>8) for 32/32 and (d<<16)|d for 16/16-in-32; before any bind, use 32/32. Write 0xFFFFFFFF for d = 0xFFFF, which is right in both layouts. Replace the 'word copy is NOT the value' assertion with per-layout assertions.

Before default-on, run a supervised D3DSafe=8 sweep of every D3D title that runs at 32 bpp today (H&D Deluxe, Thief II, Max Payne attended, Halo) plus AvP and any DX5-7 title at 32 bpp. Record 513/24 per title, require zero 513/25 (or step 2 landed), and compare in-game frames with a bit-off sweep. Make this a hard gate for default-on and for G20.

Revisit the label after G75's DX7 probe. If d3dim700 compares Z and render-target depths, or any staged DX5-7 title HEL-fills its Z, prefer 3dfx's relabel (32-bit, 0x00FFFFFF, plus an originally-Z16 flag). Correct section 3: 3dfx's (c<<16)|c patch covers only attach-time promotions.
On allocation failure, return 0 so DirectDraw places the D16 at 16 bits as it does today, and log WARN 513/24 b=0 'not promoted: no room'. Do not answer DDERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY.

Walk every surface in lplpSList instead of gating on dwSCnt==1, or at least log a WARN when a 16-bit video-memory Z in a 32 bpp PDEV is left unpromoted. Make the 513/12 hint name the actual reason: not promoted, made in a 16 bpp mode, not in video memory, or too wide.

Take the D3DSafe bit-to-flag value and the 513 event numbers from one integrator table (G03 already gives G10 bit 3 = 0x40000). Either make step 2's DDCAPS_BLTDEPTHFILL mode-independent, or justify the exception to runtime-22 in writing.

Set the priority to P1: a prerequisite for G66's 32 bpp Red Faction and for G20. It becomes P0 only if G66 lands first, so keep the design's rule that G66 stages RF at 16 bpp on .124 until G10 is proven.

problems: G06 duplicates G07 and defines the same switch incompatibly. KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G06.md:382-404 reads Diag\D3DMipChain once at FindAdapter, with bit 1 = keyed reservation (VCR_INFO_F_MIPRESERVE 0x10000), bit 2 = ATOMIC (0x20000), and target default 3 = guard + reservation. designs/G07.md:100-106 reads the same switch at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO, with bit 1 = ATOMIC (MIPWHOLE 0x10000) and 'Deployed value: 3' = guard + ATOMIC, so value 3 means two different things. Both designs create tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_mipchain.c with different cases (G06.md:440-476, G07.md:239) and use overlapping d3dprobe names (mipfrag). They estimate effort as L and M (G06.md:582, G07.md:326). The same fix is ranked P0 (G06.md:610, G07.md:343) and P2 (reports/runtime.md:552). Flags 0x8000/0x10000 are also claimed by G09 (G09.md:188) and G16 (per G24.md:221). G06 lists G07 as a dependency, which is circular.

The ring evidence for 'one level per CreateSurface' is mis-cited. The '1 levels' 513/20 events that the gap cites (onbox/ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt:102-167, seq 24873-24938) and that G06.md:86-92 cites (ring_end_decoded.txt:941-1006) are single-level textures from d3dprobe's checker() (KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c:385, Levels=1: 64x64, 256x256, 16x16), not the levels of a chain. No .124 ring has ever recorded a mip chain being created. The per-level claim rests on the DDK text, the refused fad16a23 query (onbox/ring_after_modeseq_decoded.txt:44) and an 86Box-bed measurement quoted in tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:106-114. That is plausible, but it is not a silicon measurement.

Impact beyond three titles is speculation, and one entry is wrong. Only UT2004, UT2003 and Halo have in-game frames. reports/onbox.md:282 (§8) lists no in-game attempt for JK/MotS, SS2, Thief Gold, R6, BF1942 or AvP; Max Payne was not launched and Red Faction was not run. G06.md:608 calls Max Payne, Red Faction, BF1942 LAN, H&D Deluxe and Thief II NewDark 'likely' without a frame, log line or ring event. 'The UE1 D3DDrv renderers' are not .124's staged path: FLEETRES sets FR_UE1DEV to GlideDrv where GlideRender=1, which is .124 (provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c:798-802; scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py:602). UE1 on the V5 6000 is also recorded on GlideDrv (retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md:164).

games_unblocked overstates the payoff. The same frames carry other defects: darkness (onbox-05), white sky (onbox-06), the Halo glow square (onbox-07), and blue grass plus a checkerboard (onbox-08/G44). The titles also run at 4-6 fps (UT2004, 1280x960x16) and 9.4 fps (UT2003, 640x480x16), and Halo's timedemo did not finish in 485 s (reports/onbox.md:233, §5). G06 alone unblocks none of them; it removes one defect from three titles.

The cheap fix is held behind the expensive one. F1 (the guard) alone removes the garbage, changes LODMAX only on split chains, and is S effort. G06 nevertheless keeps it default-off until Boot 2 and a full D3D sweep at value 3 (G06.md:399-404), which puts it behind the L-effort reservation. G07.md:176-180 already argues that the guard is safe to make default-on after one supervised boot.

The costlier whole-chain mechanism is made primary. G06 picks the keyed reservation (G06.md:290-345). It needs cross-call PDEV state and claim/close/fallback logic, and it depends on four unmeasured facts about dxg's call order (G06.md:636-642, open question 1). ATOMICSURFACECREATION is the documented NT mechanism. 3dfx's NT5 HAL for this chip answers it (VH5/DDFXNT.C:1223-1250, checked here), and the existing list loops already take lists (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:423-460). Its global effect on flip chains can be tested in the same boot (G07.md:72-73).

The visual pass bar cannot be measured like-for-like. G06.md:182 and :528 require '5 per mille or less in the same regions', but the baseline frames come from runs whose camera does not repeat. Both UT2004 runs used attractcam=true with 8 bots (onbox/README.md:40, 44), so the camera follows bots. The 513/24 creation record may never see a game. It is capped at the first 512 texture creations after boot (G06.md:193-195). With D3DBigTex=7 armed, pd->tex_ext is set (KMD/display/vcrdd_2d.c:466), and VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain returns through mipchain_ext immediately (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:532-533). The perf no-regression gate is in the wrong place. Only UT2003's 640x480 flyby fps is gated (G06.md:531-532). problems: The per-level evidence the design cites from the rings is misread. Every CreateSurface event in ONBOX/ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt:102-167 and ring_end_decoded.txt:941-1006 has caps 0x00005000 (TEXTURE|VIDEOMEMORY), with no DDSCAPS_MIPMAP (0x00400000). The '1 levels' 513/20 lines therefore belong to single-level textures that take mipchain_ext's 'every texture' path (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:383-390). No decoded ring anywhere in KMD/evidence holds a CreateSurface with the MIPMAP bit, so no mip chain's placement was ever logged on .124, and the §2.2 claim 'every 513/20 reads 1 levels' proves nothing. The per-level claim actually rests on three other sources: the 86Box docstring (WT/tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py:106-114), the DDK, and XP's GUID fad16a23 query being declined (ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt:61, ddRVal 88760028).

F2 (§4.2) opens the reservation only at the top level's call and claims the LATER calls. If UE2's levels arrive before the top, which is what the 11-08 layout implies under the bottom-up allocator the probe ring shows, F2 claims nothing:
- it opens a whole-chain block that stays empty (about 1/3 extra memory per chain until a mismatch closes it);
- every chain stays split, so F2 fixes nothing in the three target titles.
'The top frees the block' also has no defined owner for members placed before the top.

F2's open condition, '(and COMPLEX, if E0 confirms only the top level carries it)', would disable F2 for every D3D8 and D3D9 texture. The bound tops in S08/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt carry caps 0x10405000 (LOCALVIDMEM|MIPMAP|VIDEOMEMORY|TEXTURE), with no DDSCAPS_COMPLEX (0x8) on the kernel surface-local. mipchain_ext never clears that bit (vcrdd_d3d.c:458-459), so the top simply does not carry it.

The instrumentation cannot answer E0's key question: the GAME's per-level call order.
- 513/24 is DEBUG and capped at the first 512 creations after boot, and every boot runs the d3dprobe mip set first.
- At the default LogLevel (DEBUG, miniport/vcrmp_log.c:279), a game's per-draw 513/14 events (vcrdd_d3d.c:1603) and its roughly 1000 exit destroy notices, 513/3 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1936), wrap even a 16384-entry ring before `vcrlog fetch`. In the 11-12 game rings these notices are 1008-1013 of the 1025 entries.
- At LogLevel 2, a DEBUG event is dropped altogether.
- Only the 513/26 summary survives, and it says nothing about order.

The §3.1(b) census counts contiguity over the attach-walk n BEFORE vcr_tex_chain_usable is applied (tex_view_ext, vcrdd_d3d.c:817-819). DXT1 levels narrower than 8 are refused by mipchain_ext (common/vcr_texlod.c:109) and placed by DirectDraw through VcrDdD3dCreateTexSurface as NOTHANDLED (vcrdd_d3d.c:473-505), so they are never at top + offset. Every full DXT1 chain would therefore be logged and counted as 'split' even when all of its sampled levels are in place. E5's expected 'split > 0 on DXT' becomes true by construction.

The design keeps 'the first 8 split chains in the context' and re-logs them in ctx_free (vcrdd_d3d.c:1210). At application exit the textures are destroyed before the context: in the 11-12 rings, about 1000 destroy notices precede 'context 1 gone'. If those records hold DD_SURFACE_LOCAL pointers, the default-ON summary dereferences freed kernel memory, which risks a bugcheck. The design does not say to store values only.

G06 and G07 cannot both land as written.
- Both define Diag\D3DMipChain with flag 0x10000, but bit 1 means 'whole-chain reservation' here and ATOMICSURFACECREATION (MIPWHOLE) in G07 §4.1/§4.3.
- The switch is read at FindAdapter here, and at every IOCTL_VCR_INFO in G07.
- G06's default-ON SF_SPLIT = 0x8 is G07's SF_PAD8 = 0x8, in the same dwReserved1 flag word (vcrdd_d3d.c:205-212). G07's VcrDdD3dFreeMipChain frees fpVidMem - 8 when that bit is set, so a split-flagged top would be passed to VidMemFree at a non-block address: heap corruption or a leak.

The default path is never exercised on the box. Every proposed on-box run has D3DBigTex=7 armed, so pd->tex_ext sends all chains to mipchain_ext and tex_view_ext (vcrdd_d3d.c:532-533, :842). F1 and F2 also change the default path (VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain :522-584, tex_view :754-799), and the plan flips that path's default to 3, but no run tests it. The '640x480x16' runs with D3DBigTex armed are still the ext path, not the 'proven 16 bpp path'.

Text errors:
- §4.1 says the guard changes 'tLOD bits 13:8 (LODMAX)'. LODMAX is bits 11:6, in 4.2 format (KMD/include/vcr_3dregs.h:179; mask 0x3f<<6 at vcrdd_d3d.c:785/823; H5 INCLUDE/H3DEFS.H:678-679 SST_LODMAX_SHIFT 6). Bits 13:12 belong to LODBIAS. The worked tLOD values themselves are right.
- §2.3 says 'all of them MIP_TOP', but combines 10, 20, 22 and 24 read 'mip 76630004': they were placed by DirectDraw.
- §2.4 omits that non-square A8R8G8B8 chains also misplace their 1x1, after an 8-byte 2x1 level.

The F2 record is keyed on the address of p->lpDDSurfaceDesc. That is dxg's kernel copy of the descriptor: the next creation may reuse the same address, and separate calls may each get a different one. The match should use the descriptor's contents instead.

The proposed lab reproduction does not model the game. mipfrag models hole fragmentation with a MANAGED chain, the very path d3dprobe already shows placing levels correctly, so it can pass or fail without saying anything about the in-game cause. Only mipupd exercises a DEFAULT-pool chain, and only for R5G6B5. No test reproduces UE2's levels-below-top layout.
corrections:
Rewrite §2.2-§2.3 on the corrected evidence:
- In UE2 the split is systematic: each chain's levels sit just below its own top. Ten of the logged chains are provably split at level 1. Fragmentation is a secondary mechanism.
- Drop the '1 levels' ring citation and the combine-16 counter-example.
- Name the real sources of the per-level claim: the 86Box docstring, the DDK, the declined fad16a23 query, and the 11-08 tLOD values.

Make F2 order-independent.
- At the first texture call whose shared descriptor has DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT > 1, open a record sized vcr_tex_chain_offset(kind, desc.dwWidth, desc.dwHeight, count), rounded to 16.
- Place THAT surface at base + offset(k), with k = log2(descriptor side / surface side). Claim the remaining levels in any order.
- Free the block when the record's last member is destroyed (a refcount), not only on the top's destroy.
- Alternatively, promote F2-alt (ATOMICSURFACECREATION, G07's choice). It is order-independent by construction, and the existing loops already compute k by size. Run it with §4.3's 2D/flip checks.

Drop the DDSCAPS_COMPLEX condition. Tell a top from a sublevel by comparing the descriptor's and the surface's dimensions, and by DDSCAPS2_MIPMAPSUBLEVEL (lpSurfMore->ddsCapsEx.dwCaps2 & 0x10000). Log dwCaps2 in 513/24.
Compute the census over min(n, vcr_tex_chain_usable(...)) only, and report DXT1 levels narrower than 8 separately. Otherwise every DXT1 chain counts as split.

In the per-context split list, store values only: w, h, kind, top address, first misplaced k, expected address and actual address. Never store DD_SURFACE_LOCAL pointers, because those surfaces are freed before ctx_free.

Before making 3 the default, add a boot with D3DBigTex absent. Run mip, miptail, mipfrag and mipupd on the default path at 640x480x16 (VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain/tex_view). Also run the 86Box Voodoo3 bed.

Record the guard-only boot's fps separately. With nearly every UE2 and Halo chain split at level 1, F1 makes them sample LOD 0 everywhere, which puts more pressure on the texture cache. A drop there is not a regression of F2. Also correct the text: LODMAX is tLOD bits 11:6, not every 513/23 entry was MIP_TOP, and non-square 8888 tails are misplaced too.

Keep as designed. Verified from source:
- The reservation's layout is right for VSA-100. The TMU reads level k at base + the sum of the natural level sizes (H5 GLIDE3/SRC/DITEX.C:834-1003; the 'hw is still going to use the complete size computation' note at :1348-1356), with DXT1 in 8x4 units. The vendor rounds only the total (D3TXTR.C:3877).
- The design's numbers check out: 43728, 10928 and 1398112 bytes; tLOD 0x40000b08 -> 0x40000208, 0x808 -> 0x708 and 0x700800 -> 0x700600; L7 at 21856 vs 21848.
- F1 only lowers LODMAX, which gives the register shape MIPFILTER NONE already uses, so it is safe on VSA-100 and Voodoo3.
- The adjacent 1x1 defect is real: vcr_texlod.c:32 rounds the base down, where Glide (DITEX.C:1354-1356) and the vendor (D3TXTR.C:3763, 878-881) round toward the texture.

Renumber before integration. Use an IOCTL from 0xa12 up (0xa10 is G01's, 0xa11 G02's), a free 51x event (not 514), a new 512 'what' code (10 is used at KMD/display/vcrdd_punt.c:549), and a VCR_INFO flag other than 0x8000. Fix the test assertions to match.
Keep D3DBeat default-off after closure and require it off for every timed or benchmark run ('arm one, run, disarm', KMD/README.md:96). Do not leave it armed on .124 for supervised sessions.

Interim no-code mitigation for attended Max Payne runs and any supervised D3D round on .124: run the D3D titles before any Glide/OpenGL title in a boot, or, when 'vcrctl reg 80024' shows bit 8 with no live Glide client, run 'vcrctl reset-engine' first. That command calls VcrHwResetEngine, which stops the FIFO fetch first (KMD/miniport/vcrmp_hw.c:181-201). Proving it works without a mode set is G01's E2.

No renderer fallback exists for Max Payne: it is D3D8 only (e2driver/e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll). For E0, a per-box launcher A/B at 16 bpp ('Display Bits Per Pixel', LIB/MaxPayne/install.reg:21) is a cheap discriminator for whether the Diag-gated 32 bpp path (G20) is involved. It is not a fix.

problems: REFUTED, the design's main new evidence (G04.md section 1.2(2)): it says the first surfaces of every fullscreen D3D game land inside Glide's FIFO window, and that an earlier Max Payne surface filled 0x0-0x4b0000. In fact offset 0 is DirectDraw's 'no memory' answer. The first block of a heap that starts at 0 is handed out at 0, read as a failure, and never used until the next mode set (KMD/include/vcr_ddheap.h:14-26). The 11-12 evidence agrees. The fullscreen 1024x768x32 device had its target at 0x300000, Z at 0x600000 and textures at 0x900000, with nothing below (ONBOX/ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt:82,102; session_log.md 10:07: 'the fullscreen 1024x768 ones (0x300000+) do not'). The windowed device's target sat at 0x40000, which is its own size. On 10-04 the scan-out at 0x4b0000 is the back buffer placed at exactly its own size; the other flip buffer is the GDI primary at 0x3b50000. Sibling designs G79.md section 0.2 and G01.md:43 say the same. So at Max Payne's 1280x960x32, Glide's window [0x18000,0x117000) lies inside the never-used block [0,0x4b0000). No Lock, TEXBLT or Blt of Max Payne's can write there.

The leading-hypothesis chain (H-A2 then H-B: a CPU write into the window, CMD0 busy, then the silent 512 a=9 give-up) is therefore not open to Max Payne's own surfaces at its staged mode. Only H-A1 is: an enabled but idle stale FIFO loses triangles while fastfill clears and 2D/CPU writes survive (the 11-12 10:02 run). The 10-04 frame shows art and cursor but no menu text (history-04). That is H-A1's picture if the art and cursor come through Blt/CPU paths. Yet the E3 table in section 4.4 calls outcome (ii) 'the 10-04 shape' and outcome (i) only 'H-A1'. Exposure to the window is real only where the first heap request is under 0x117000 bytes: fullscreen 640x480x16 (0x96000) or 800x600x16 (0xEA600), or any windowed device. It also becomes real for every fullscreen title once Diag\DdHeapFloor=1 removes the lost block, because the back buffer then starts at 0x1000.

The locks_in_glide_fifo counter is attached only to Dd_Lock (display/vcrdd_ddraw.c:647). The driver's own CPU writes into video memory bypass it:
- the TEXBLT memcpy through pvRamBase (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1441-1448, 1487-1494), which is how D3D8 managed textures are uploaded;
- Dd_Blt's software fill/copy fallback (vcrdd_ddraw.c:515-521, 553-556), which runs whenever the 2D engine refuses, for example after a give-up.
So open question 2 ('if it never Locks there, H-A2 cannot happen') does not follow.

LogLevel 2 drops the placement lines the design relies on. Event 513 a=20 (mip-chain placement) is VCR_LV_DEBUG (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:461), and the miniport drops anything above LogLevel (miniport/vcrmp_log.c:326; the default is 3, at :279). At LogLevel 2 only these survive: 513 a=1, the ContextCreate target and Z (vcrdd_d3d.c:1202), and 513 a=23, the textures of the first 64 combos (vcrdd_d3d.c:915).

VcrBeat's ZwCreateKey and ZwSetValueKey run in the game's own DP2/Flip thread while win32k's display lock is held: EngDeviceIoControl goes through videoprt's device mutex to VcrStartIO (miniport/vcrmp.c:637). If that registry write waits on the configuration manager, for example behind a hive flush, the frame and everything queued on the display lock wait too (inferred, not measured). That is exactly the perturbation the experiment must avoid. Also, an INFO 514 event every second fills a default 1024-entry ring in about 17 minutes, and section 6 keeps D3DBeat armed after closure.

VCR_GLIDE_FIFO_LO/HI hard-code 0x18000/0x117000. That is only the default: h5 Glide moves its FIFO with FX_GLIDE_FIFOEXTRA (the 96 KB pad) and FX_GLIDE_V3FIFO (placement below fbOffset) (build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/minihwc/minihwc.c:2563-2617). The record in section 3.1 has no baseAddr or aMax field, although the miniport reads both. The proposed 'heap floor above 0x117000' has the same weakness.

The recovery step and the control run do not clear the H-A1 state. 'vcrctl modeseq' resets the engine only when the chip reads BUSY (miniport/vcrmp_hw.c:571-572); on 11-12 it worked only because the chip sat at 0xa5f. After an E3 outcome (i), the FIFO is enabled but idle, so modeseq leaves cmdFifo0 on. That contaminates the 'FIFO off' control run and the next session.

E3 method 1 is not a kill. glidelab abandon calls ExitProcess, and glide3x's DLL_PROCESS_DETACH then runs grGlideShutdown (tools/glidelab.c:1326-1333; glide3/src/gpci.c:1954-1956). That leads to hwcRestoreVideo, which disables cmdFifo0 when the board is idle (minihwc.c:6016-6017) and leaves it on only on the not-idle path (minihwc.c:5986-6013). Method 2, a 4-chip Quake II session ended by a console quit, matches 10-04 most closely, though how the 10-04 session was closed is not recorded. Neither method is guaranteed to leave the FIFO on.

vcrprobe.sys is demand-start and is left STOPPED (evidence/gametune_1001/fbshot_probe/README.md:86-87). probe-regs, fbshot --probe and d3dwatch's freeze bundle all depend on it. The protocol in section 4.2 never says to run 'sc start vcrprobe' before the game starts, and under a CPU hog the service start would itself crawl.

E0a is no longer free of measurement tools: threads and typeperf run at REALTIME, and probe-regs --scan runs at 2 and 5 minutes. So it loses history-05's acquittal ('a freeze here means the tools are acquitted'). E2 has no decision value: section 5 maps H-C to 'keep the rule ... nothing to fix on the drawing path', while E2 risks a vcrctl parked in the kernel (FIND:127). With the new guard in place E2 would also need --force, which section 4.4 omits.

Section 1.2(3) rests on unconfirmed inferences. The claim that 'the 11-12 stale-FIFO state did not make the box crawl' compares nothing: on 11-12 no D3D program was running in the stale state while responsiveness was timed (session_log.md 10:02-10:12). wmic and XP's taskkill may both go through WMI (inferred), which would be a shared dependency rather than proof of CPU starvation. The design also omits counter-evidence to H-C: the agent's GDI SCREENSHOT completed during the 10-04 freeze (fbshot_probe/README.md:59-60), and a GDI read of the screen takes the same display lock (inferred). So the lock could be taken at that point.

The 'threads' command, as specified, will print kernel32's start thunk for every Win32 thread. On XP, SYSTEM_THREAD_INFORMATION.StartAddress is ETHREAD.StartAddress (BaseThreadStartThunk); the real routine is in Win32StartAddress (inferred). Without it, section 5's question 'is the spin in our flip loop?' can only be answered from the kernel/user time split.

Ownership is duplicated and the dependencies run in a circle:
- G79 depends on G04 (G79.md:9-10) and builds the no-DC rule and the escape guard itself (G79.md:267-273), while G04 lists G79 as a dependency for the same thing and puts the same vcrctl.c changes in its own file list.
- Diag\D3DFault (section 3.6) duplicates G02's part D fault injection (G02.md:86).
- D3DFault's own text contradicts itself: 'read at boot' versus 'read at the next beat'. The second is a Diag change in mid-boot.
- D3DFault would also need a NEW_DIAG entry (tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_integration.py:76), which section 7.3 leaves out.

Smaller defects:
- Section 8 says the only always-on changes are the give-up path and vcrctl. But the max_spin bookkeeping is added, ungated, to VcrDdRoom, which runs before every vertex (vcrdd_3d.c:188), and to VcrDd2dSync.
- The classifier's STALE_CMDFIFO class requires status bit 11. A stale FIFO that has already executed garbage and left the 3D engine busy reads 0x21f with baseSize 0x1fe, and would be filed as ENGINE_BUSY.
- The 96-byte record cannot hold the 28 or so dwords listed without packing fields into bytes.

Priority: what G04 delivers is measurement plus an attended protocol, which is P1 on this scale. The cure for the mechanism the evidence supports (H-A1) is G01. Also, the 'blk' that G04 gates comes from a rule about capture tools ('do not point either path at a Direct3D title', fbshot_probe/README.md:78-79). docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md:82-83 reads it more broadly, as 'no D3D title unattended'.

Improve the threads command. For each thread, add Win32StartAddress (OpenThread plus NtQueryInformationThread class 9), mapped to a module through a Toolhelp module snapshot. Optionally take three EIP samples (GetThreadContext with CONTEXT_CONTROL). Run it at HIGH/15 like G79's reads unless REALTIME is shown to be needed.

The original rule is about capture tools under D3D titles, so non-Max-Payne D3D titles could rejoin readiness rounds once G01 is armed and a pre-flight 'vcrctl reg 80024 = 0' passes, with captures limited to GDI SCREENSHOT.

problems: The trigger is overstated as 'any OpenGL or Glide title'. A legacy Glide client actually CLEARS this residue: grColorCombine/grAlphaCombine call grDisable(GR_COMBINEEXT_MODE) (build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/glide3/src/distate.c:516, :577), and validation then rewrites the FBI combineMode with bit 31 and every select cleared (distate.c:1945-1970; TMUs: gtex.c:1204-1229). Field evidence from the 10-01 baseline: UT2003 and UT2004 drew their menu and a lit, textured 3D model straight after 'Unreal Tournament - 3dfx Voodoo' (legacy Glide), although ~35 GL/Glide titles had run earlier in that boot (vcr-kmd/evidence/gametune_1001/sweep_baseline/sweep.log:90-97; ~/.retro-fleet/evidence/v56k-gametune_1001-sweep_baseline-20261001_192225/Unreal_Tournament_2004_60s.png). The real trigger is 'the last 3D client used Glide's COMBINE extension', which is every MesaFX OpenGL title on .124 (fxapi.c:575, fxglidew.c:238; no staged launcher sets MESA_FX_IGNORE_CMBEXT).

The effect is understated as intermittent (G03.md section 0 item 1: 'depends on what the GL title drew last').
- Both FBI combines MesaFX ever sets pass b=GR_CMBX_ZERO (build/retro3dfx-gl/src/mesa/drivers/glide/fxsetup.h:574-583 textured passthrough, :828-837 untextured). That is cc_localselect=ZERO with combineMode bit 31 set.
- With bit 31 set, c_local comes from combineMode (SPEC section 8.21 table; 3dfx CSIM H5/CSIM/FBI.C:711-757, where ZERO gives 0).
- The HAL's MODULATE is other x c_local (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:714-716).
- So after ANY cleanly closed MesaFX title, every D3D MODULATE draw (lit geometry, vertex-coloured text, and alpha too) comes out black. Only texture-only or diffuse-only draws depend on the last GL state.
- Inferred link: Glide's _grCCExtcombineMode has no source in either tree.
- One open check: Thief II's NewDark menu rendered correctly on 09-29 with TFC (MesaFX) as the last 3D client. That fits only if its 2D menu draws texture-only.

The source report misreads the evidence, and G03 inherits its 'correlation only' framing.

- Every visual-05 failure had a MesaFX title as the last 3D client:
