problems: The gap is confirmed in source, and the mechanism is stronger than G03.md argues. On Napalm, MesaFX always sets the FBI combine to 'pass A' with local = ZERO (MFX fxsetup.h:572-593 textured, :828-838 untextured). COMBINE is advertised in NAPALM_EXT_STR (GL5 diget.c:883). GL5 gglide.c:5111/5132/5173 encode that as c_localselect ZERO | INVERT_LOCAL_X | USE_COMBINE_MODE. A clean close never clears it (gsst.c:3295-3303), and _grTex2ppc returns early when 2PPC is already off (gtex.c:1010). The HAL's MODULATE is CC_M(CLOCAL)|REVERSE (KMD display/vcrdd_d3d.c:714-715). By SPEC L2827-2834, every lit textured D3D surface therefore computes texture x 0 = black after any MesaFX title, until reboot. The design's P0 instead leans on visual-05, which G01 explains equally well: under a stale FIFO, clears and DirectDraw blits still land, so Shogo's text proves nothing.

The only silicon data point after an OpenGL session contradicts that prediction, unless the busy reset clears combineMode. pid 1892 was an OpenGL (MesaFX) 4-chip client (OPENGL_GETINFO, onbox/ring_start_decoded.txt:237). Its display-reset end only reprograms video: vcrmp.c:693-694 -> VcrHwResetToVga rewrites the boot miscInit0, with no reset pulse. Yet d3dprobe read 'modulate' 800000 and 'flat' 00ff00 at 10:12:32 (onbox/d3dprobe_render_1024x768x32_clean.txt). That was right after 'engine reset (busy at mode set)' (VcrHwResetEngine: GRX + FBI-FIFO + 2D + command-stream reset, vcrmp_hw.c:181-200). So, inferred: that reset restores combineMode, and open Q3 is probably 'yes'. The A/B plan has no control for it: any busy reset between the GL close and the D3D run erases the residue being tested.

G03.md:568 and §7 describe G01's fix as 'cmdFifo0.baseSize = 0 with no core reset'. G01.md:34, :49 and :130 make the full VcrHwResetEngine its cure. If Q3 is 'yes', G01 also clears the residue on the not-idle path, and G03's distinct job is the clean-close path (FIFO off, no reset). The design never says this.
The boot-1 game A/B is marked 'optional' (G03.md:522), yet it is the only title-level test that separates G03 from G01. A boot-2 pass on its own cannot show the baseline was needed.

Test 4 (G03.md:389-392), and test 1's rule that TMU chromaRange must come before combineMode (G03.md:356), encode something that is not a requirement. Substitution acts only on pixels, and no pixel is processed between two register writes: combineMode is pipelined ('No' sync, SPEC L2344) and chromaRange is sync (L2317). Also, under the design's own model routing (chip field 0 -> FBI+TMU0+TMU1, SPEC L2206), a broadcast 'FBI chroma off' clears the TMU copies too. The 'old/buggy' case therefore fails only if that write is FBI-only, so the test hard-codes open Q1's unknown as a fact.

Test 5 (G03.md:393-395) counts only chip-field-6 nopCMDs as the 2PPC exit. SPEC L2840 objects to FBI-including NOPs for performance only, and chip field 0 reaches both TMUs. The model would therefore wrongly fail the pinned Reset3D sequence (include/vcr_3dseq.h:185-198).

baseline() sets w->based = 1 before VcrDd3dBaseline succeeds (G03.md:184-187). Under G01(D)/G02's recoverable give-up ('the stalled op is dropped; the next op works'), a half-written baseline is never retried within that call. Target and state writes do retry, through w->prepared (vcrdd_d3d.c:1335-1363). Later triangles then draw on a stale combineMode.

Flag and event allocations collide. VCR_INFO_F 0x10000 is also claimed by G07. G10 proposes 0x10000<<bit (G10.md:137), which puts bit 1 at 0x20000, not 0x10000. 513 what 24/25 are claimed by G01, G05, G10, G11 and G14 (tabulated at G02.md:330-334; vcr_events.h:75 ends at 23). The existing flag-uniqueness test does not check what-codes.

The boot-1 'stencil' class (G03.md:469) injects enable + func NEVER + wmask ff + REPLACE x3 into a 16 bpp target. SPEC L3358 says stencil works only at 32 bpp, and 3dfx masks SST_STENCIL_ENABLE below 32 bpp (VH5 D6DP2.C:5459-5463). If the chip honours the enable, a REPLACE under wmask ff on a 16-bit aux buffer writes to an undefined place. That is an avoidable hazard on the box, because a state that writes nothing can answer whether the test is honoured.

About 15 of the 22 writes (chipMask, sliCtrl, 12 NOPs, aaCtrl) get no silicon negative control. The clean-close glidelab classes cannot leave chipMask/sliCtrl/aaCtrl/2PPC residue, because gsst.c:3295-3303 restores them, and '--close abandon' waits for G01. So 'row y' and 'cover' (G03.md:438-439) can only pass, and that half of the sequence is tested for no-harm only.

The verification load is understated and the perf gate is blind where the cost would land. The step list implies about 30 paced CRT switches in boot 1 and 55-60 in boot 2 (8 per residue class, plus matrix, perf and game A/B), not '~30 each' (G03.md:582). The ±1% perf gate uses d3dprobe (1-3 DP2 calls per frame) and UT2003 (~35). It cannot see a per-DP2 cost on DX5 execute-buffer titles (JK DF2, MotS), whose DP2 rate is unmeasured, and it has no measured noise floor.
The change makes two comments false: include/vcr_3dregs.h:47 (sliCtrl written 'only ... in the Reset3D reset') and include/vcr_3dseq.h:18-20 (the 2PPC NOPs 'here are broadcast').

The SLI-safety argument (G03.md:565) rests on the PDEV-scoped exclusive_pid (display/vcrdd.c:589-591). retro-3dfx FINDINGS.md:93-97 shows that ownership is lost across a PDEV swap while a Glide stream keeps running (a GLQuake in-game mode change). In that window the per-call chipMask/sliCtrl/combineMode writes would land under the live stream. Low likelihood, but not listed.

The trigger is overstated. Native Glide titles that use the legacy grColorCombine/grTexCombine clear bit 31 and every select/invert field themselves (GL5 distate.c:1946-1965, gtex.c:1205-1225). The combine residue is specific to MesaFX and other users of the COMBINE extension; TMU constant colour and stencil residue can come from others.
corrections: Adopt the 22-write sequence as designed; every field checks out. Sources: SPEC L2206, L2311-2347, L2825-2840, L3437-3444, L3482; H3DEFS.H:395-536 (combineMode 0 is legacy: INVERT_LOCAL 0 = ZERO_MINUS_X, the legacy subtract); CSIM CCU.C:68-300 with FBI.C:636 (the invert/outshift fields act on the FBI even with bit 31 clear, so the whole register must be zeroed, not just bit 31); TREX.C:1474-1690 (the TMU selects always come from combineMode); Glide gtex.c:1050 (12 TMU-only NOPs); vendor D6DP2.C:6418-6446 and 6107-6129.

Rest P0 on the source prediction, and test it first in boot 1 with bit 1 OFF: one MesaFX frame followed by a clean close (Quake III, or a one-quad GL program) must make the existing d3dprobe 'modulate' and 'flat' checks fail. If they pass, G03 drops to P1.

Make the boot-1 game A/B mandatory. Gate every post-GL D3D step on two conditions: cmdFifo0 reads off, AND the ring shows no 'engine reset (busy at mode set)' or reset-engine since the GL close. Add an explicit open-Q3 step: residue, then vcrctl reset-engine, then d3dprobe with bit 1 off.

Correct G03 §6/§7: G01's cure is VcrHwResetEngine. State that G03's unique coverage is the clean-close path, and that if G01 adopts the lighter stop-fetch cure (its E3), G03 must be armed together with it.
Set w->based only after VcrDd3dBaseline returns TRUE, so a failed baseline is retried at the next prepare(), the same way target and state are.

Fix the tests. Drop or relabel the 'chroma before combineMode' order rule. Parameterise test 4's register model on open Q1, and require substitution off at the end in both settings. Let test 5 accept broadcast NOPs as a valid, slower 2PPC exit.

Settle the D3DSafe plumbing once for G01/G02/G03/G05/G07/G10/G11/G14 before any of them lands: either G02's vcr_info.d3dsafe field or one reserved bit map, plus one event-code range. Extend the duplicate check to 513 what-codes.
Answer the 16 bpp stencil question first with a state that writes nothing: enable, func NEVER, ops KEEP, wmask 0. Use the REPLACE/wmask ff class only if that state is ignored, and only supervised.
State plainly that the chipMask, sliCtrl, aaCtrl and 2PPC writes are tested for no-harm only until G01's abandon class exists. Keep 'row y' and 'cover' as positive controls only.

Cut the CRT mode switches. Run the 32 bpp residue checks windowed on the 1280x1024x32 desktop, which needs no switch. Do one fullscreen 16 bpp run per class, and fold the control run into the bit-off run.

Before default-on, measure DP2 calls per frame for JK DF2 and MotS from the context-gone counters, and include one of them in the perf A/B. Measure d3dprobe perf noise over at least 3 runs before relying on a ±1% gate.
Flip the default on only after G01 has landed, together with G41 for the fog-table residue. Landing the switch default-off needs neither.
In the same commit, update vcr_3dregs.h:47 and vcr_3dseq.h:18-20. Narrow 'unblocks' to D3D titles run after an OpenGL (MesaFX) title in the same boot.

Strengthen the hal-02 correction with two facts from the 11-12 dump. At 10:09 chipMask read 0 while D3D clears were landing (3/3), so the read is provably not the register value. The stencilMode/stencilOp reads of 0 were the 32 bpp D3D target's own writes (vcr_3dseq.h:66-69). The dump says nothing about Glide residue.

Lower the stated 'power-on combineMode' risk. Legacy Glide titles already run on silicon with combineMode's select/invert fields at 0 and bit 31 clear (distate.c:1946-1965). The post-reset 40/40 also ran on the reset value (inferred).

Record, as a follow-up outside this fix, the residue that stays uncovered: TMU1's texture registers remain foreign for single-stage draws. Colour is safe, because TMU0 REPLACE ignores c_other, but Glide parks an idle TMU on a tiny texture to avoid fetch thrash (gtex.c:1426, 1950).
Add the PDEV-swap case (FINDINGS.md:93-97) to the SLI risk row.

problems: Almost all of the measured impact belongs to G05, not G12. Of UT2003's 26 logged set-ups, 8 are drawn wrong. Seven of those are MODULATE2X, which is G05's whole scope (KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G05.md:20-43). The only measured set-up that only G12 fixes is combine 21 (MODULATE(T,D) then BLENDCURRENTALPHA). It needs bit 8 (KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/designs/G12.md:93), which needs G58, itself P2 (G58.md:72). Nothing shows what combine 21 draws or that it is visible.

Even for UE2, the G12-specific exposure in gameplay is unmeasured. KMD/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt came from a one-off build during the 11-08 menu chase (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:143-149), so it shows the menu's backdrop scene, not play. The 11-12 in-game runs used LogLevel 3, and the rings kept zero 513/21-23 lines (KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/onbox/games/*/ring_decoded.txt: 0 'combine' matches; reports/onbox.md:259 notes the ring wraps within seconds).

The title list is wrong both ways. BF1942 cannot reach D3D on .124: SafeDisc 2.80 blocks the client (docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md:376), and the host shortcut runs BF1942_w32ded.exe (KMD/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108/run.out:3). 'LithTech titles' (G12.md:549) is also unsupported: Shogo's d3d.ren is IDirect3DDevice2, with no TSS multitexture (G15.md section 3 table). The field name 'games_unblocked' overstates the effect, because G12 unblocks no title; every effect is a quality change.

Two listed titles already have their own fallback, so G12 is not what fixes them. Max Payne's e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll validates every material and splits it into passes on refusal: its strings include 'trying separate stages', 'newPass: hardware didn't support needed operations' and 'D3D_OK stages:%d' (G15.md:82). Halo picks its technique through D3DX validation (G15.md:83). For both, G15 Part B (an honest Validate) is the cheaper fix, and G12 would only save passes. G12 even cites 'D3D_OK stages:%d' as evidence of exposure, but it is evidence of the fallback.

The candidates with real static evidence are missing from G12's list and from its boot-A run (G12.md:491, 549): (a) Red Faction never calls ValidateDevice and has 220 SetTextureStageState sites (G15.md table), so G15 cannot rescue it; it is the main non-validating, unmeasured title besides UE2. (b) Thief II NewDark mode 5 (stage-1 alpha) and mode 6 (stage-1 BLENDTEXTUREALPHA after MODULATE(T,D)), and Thief Gold mode 4, are set-ups the legacy path draws wrong (G15.md:93-108).

'Prerequisite for G15 and G50' (G12.md:545, 551) is contradicted by both designs. G15.md:498 says 'G12 is not needed to land this item', and G50.md:944-952 lists no G12 dependency. Neither of those items is P0, so the 'prerequisite for P0 work' clause cannot raise G12 to P1 either.

The schedule is inverted. G12.md:544 and 551 take G05 over ('implement it here rather than as a separate patch'). The P0 fix for the dark UE2 world would then wait for the L-sized engine: about 800 lines of vcr_combine.h, a 900-line model and test, and a 500-line probe framework (G12.md:527-535). G05 fixes the same 7 set-ups at effort M and recommends landing first (G05.md:38-43). The two designs also collide on Diag\D3DFeat bit 6 (G05.md:36, 313; G12 section 4) and on event 513/24 (G05.md:268; G12.md:353).

The exposure measurement undercounts exactly what it is meant to find. log_combo keys each set-up by texture format and size and keeps only 64 per context (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:73, 885-899). In a gameplay context those slots fill with shape variants of common ops, so a rare op that appears later is never logged. G12's shadow-verdict event inherits this limit (G12.md:353). LogLevel and LogEntries are read only at DriverEntry (KMD/miniport/vcrmp_log.c:279-283), so the boot-A plan must set them before that boot.

The G01 precondition is too weak. 'No killed Glide client' (G12.md:486) is not enough: onbox-01 showed that a Glide close that was not a kill (the not-idle path) also leaves cmdFifo0 enabled and erases every D3D triangle (reports/onbox.md:29). Boot B's Quake II run followed by combine6 (G12.md:497) can then fail for G01's reason, and the failure would be blamed on the combine.

The in-game acceptance check cannot fail cleanly. Frames at wall-clock 30/60/90/120 s and a whole-frame luma of 28 (G12.md:495-496) do not line up across boots, given load time and 9.4 fps (reports/onbox.md:237). They are also dominated by the white sky and horizon (G18), block noise (G06), blue grass (G44) and the 16 bpp that UE2 forces on 0x121a (reports/runtime.md:540). Judging 'about twice as bright' by eye cannot separate a G12 change from those.

The caps widening (G12.md:365-380) has no staged beneficiary. UE2 and Red Faction use ops whether or not the caps list them, and never validate. Max Payne's cap checks cover only ops already advertised, plus BUMPENVMAP, which the hardware cannot do (e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll strings). The validating titles go through ValidateDevice. Widening can therefore only steer caps-checking titles onto untested paths, which makes it P3.

The stale-combineMode hazard (Glide leftovers changing today's TMU combines; the V-05 correlation) is fixed by G03's P0 baseline (G03.md:297, 600; hal.md Phase 1 bit 1). It is not a reason to schedule G12 early. On ordering: UE2 runs at 4-9 fps (reports/onbox.md:58, 237), so within the P2 tier the measured performance items should come before G12's unmeasured remainder.
corrections: Split the priorities. The MODULATE2X slice is P0, but it should land first, alone, through G05's design (effort M). G12's remainder (stage order, stage-1 ops, TFACTOR and argument routing, fold/tint/split) is P2. Bits 7 and 8 and the caps widening are P3 until measured. Promote a slice of G12 to P1 for one title only when an op-keyed in-game log shows that title drawing a G12-only set-up in a common scene, and the title is one that does not validate (UT2003, UT2004, Red Faction, H&D, SS2).

Build G12's compiler on top of G05's header and emission code, as G05.md:38-43 proposes. Keep G05's pinned BLENDCURRENTALPHA test as the point where G12 changes behaviour on purpose. Settle in the plan who owns Diag\D3DFeat bit 6 and event 513/24: for example, bit 6 stays G05's shift and G12's tiers take the next free bits, and G12's shadow verdicts go into G15 Part A's log_combo verdict field rather than a new 513/24.

Measure before building. Schedule one supervised fresh boot with no Glide or OpenGL since power-on and cmdFifo0 read off. Use the deployed vcrdd 95678704, with LogLevel=2 and LogEntries=16384 set before that boot. In that boot, run the following in game, fetching the ring after each: the UT2003 flyby, the UT2004 botmatch, Red Faction's first level, H&D, Thief II and Thief Gold missions, SS2, the Halo timedemo, and Max Payne attended. Add one small default-on, log-only summary per context of (stage, colour op, alpha op, argument kinds with modifiers) seen, keyed by op and not by texture shape. Merge it with hal.md Phase 0 T3, runtime.md section 13 and G15 Part A. Size G12 from that table.

Rewrite the title list as 'titles whose rendering changes', in tiers. Measured: UT2003 (menu scene). Inferred: UT2004 (same D3DDrv). Static candidates: Red Faction (never validates), Thief II (NewDark modes 5/6), Thief Gold (mode 4), and SS2 and H&D (undetermined). Titles that draw their own fallback once G15 Part B is armed: Max Payne and Halo. Remove BF1942 (SafeDisc client, dedicated-server host) and 'LithTech' (Shogo is DX5 IDirect3DDevice2). Drop the 'prerequisite for G15 and G50' claim.

Use the cheaper fix wherever one exists. For Max Payne and Halo, G15 Part B (honest Validate). For NewDark's fatal mode-6 validation, a staged per-box `d3d_disp_forcevalid 1` written by stage-fleetres (G15 contingency b), not bit 8 plus G58. For Red Faction, the in-game 'Detail textures disabled' option (rf.exe strings) can be staged if the measurement shows its detail stage is the set-up drawn wrong.

Fix the verification preconditions. Either land G01 first, or run a read-only `vcrctl reg` check that cmdFifo0.baseSize has its enable bit clear before every D3D run. Repeat that check after boot B's Quake II step and before combine6. A failure with the FIFO enabled is G01's failure, not G12's.

Make the in-game check falsifiable. Use matched frames from the fixed-step `-benchmark` flyby, chosen by content rather than by wall clock, and take the same frames on an NVIDIA fleet box as the reference. Compare region luma ratios: pass at 1.6x or more on lightmapped wall and floor patches, with HUD, sky and unlit patches within 5 %. Exclude regions with noise or white areas. The d3dprobe mod2x and stage1_mod2x cells stay the binding proof.

Cover the other set-ups that have evidence. Add NewDark modes 4-7 and Thief Gold modes 0-4, as G15.md:93-108 decodes them, as golden rows in test_vcr_kmd_combine.c and as d3dprobe cells. Add Thief II and Thief Gold mission frames to boots A and B. Widen TextureOpCaps for an op group only after a staged title is measured to check that cap and take a worse path without it. Until then, keep 0x184f even when armed.

problems: CONFIRMED, gap real as deployed: out/vcrdd.dll md5 95678704f3e9586381a73c15e5b1bce0 (= the .124 build) is built from HEAD (481acfd; its 'combine %u ops' string is present). Its only 0x208 immediate is the Reset3D builder (vcr_3dseq.h:193, default off). VcrDd3dState never writes combineMode (vcrdd_3d.c:74-129). `two` requires a stage-0 texture plus a stage-1 handle (vcrdd_d3d.c:928). stage1_combine runs in TMU0 before the FBI applies stage 0's op (:947-956, :977). 2X/4X and the rest fall to MODULATE (:714-716, :738-740, :862, :871-872). Caps are 0x184f (:2165-2168) against the vendor's 20 ops (VH5/D3INIT.C:3262-3291). UT2003 combine 21 = MODULATE then BLENDCURRENTALPHA (sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt:59-61).

CONFIRMED, hardware model sound: (a) TMU selects 'always come from combineMode' (spec, combineMode MUX section). (b) The 12-NOP chipField=0x6 exit is required before clearing bit 29. (c) The PIO chip field selects the FBI alone with 0x1 (spec address map; SST_CHIP n*0x400, h3defs.h:2087). (d) chromaKey/chromaRange carry the constant alpha in [31:24]. (e) The vendor builds define NEW_CCU (W2K/BUILD/STBPERF.INC:49, Win9x/DX/D3D/MAKEFILE:307). (f) The vendor sets USE|DISABLE_CHROMA on all three units even for untextured draws (D6MT.C:4412-4414, 4891-4893). (g) It writes them per unit before every other register (D6DP2.C:6436-6446), and puts TFACTOR in the TMU chroma at chip 6 and in c0/c1 (D6DP2.C:7019-7026). (h) It keys the FBI chroma alone while bit 30 is set everywhere (D6DP2.C:6943), which largely settles open question 8. The 'mirror words' premise of bit 6 is vendor-shipped practice.

D3DFeat bit collision. G12 claims bits 6/7/8 (G12.md:51-53). G05 claims bit 6 for CMSHIFT (G05.md:36). G13 claims bit 7 for argmod (G13.md:373-374); G15.md:273 already lists 'G12 bits 6-8, G13 bit 7'. G12 also proposes reusing G05's bit with much broader semantics: combineMode on every draw, every op in the FBI, plus PROD/SPLIT/TINT/FOLD. If G05 proves bit 6 on silicon first, that would void the proof.

Event sub-code collision. G12 takes 513/24 for shadow verdicts (G12.md:353) and 513/25 for 'bit 8 ignored' (G12.md:347). The same codes are claimed by G03 (G03.md:222, 244), G05 (G05.md:269, 297) and G09 (G09.md:206-207), and per G02.md:334 by G01, G11 and G14 as well. G02 had already flagged this. Today's HAL uses 513/1-23.

The TMU-constant cache goes stale. G12 clears cm_primed/tmuc_valid only at SETEXCLUSIVE, RLSEXCLUSIVE and DrvAssertMode(TRUE) (G12.md:333-336). G41's forget list (G41.md:227-238) also covers VCR_ESC_REG (vcrdd_escape.c:311), VCR_ESC_RESET_ENGINE (:323), GETLINEARADDR (:101), UNMAP (:203) and DrvAssertMode(FALSE). Worse, G03's D3DSafe baseline zeroes the TMU chromaRange on EVERY DrawPrimitives2/Clear2 (G03.md:93, :157), and G12 explicitly leaves 'chroma' with G03 (G12.md:541). Its write 20, labelled 'FBI', is broadcast (G03.md:162) and also hits both TMUs. With D3DSafe bit 1 plus the TMU tier armed, tmuc_valid keeps claiming TFACTOR is loaded while CR_RGB/CR_A read 0, so every TFACTOR-in-TMU placement draws with a zero constant.

The 'byte-for-byte with bits off' claim (G12.md:361) conflicts with the shared VcrDd3dForget clearing fog_valid 'for G41' (G12.md:333). On a re-asserted PDEV that re-sends the 32-word fog table on the default path. Two incompatible hooks are also designed: G41's VcrDdFogForget(pd, why) with pd->fogc (G41.md:191-196), and G12's VcrDd3dForget(pd).

Unflagged hardware inference. G12 routes CURRENT.a and TEXTURE.a into a TMU's C input via MAOTHER/MALOCAL (G12.md:130, 136) and asserts that TC and TCA are independent (G12.md:256). Per the spec MUX table, the FBI's a_other/a_local ARE the alpha unit's select outputs (combineMode[17:16]/[20:18]); the design avoids that only in the FBI (G12.md:139-141). Whether a TMU's MAOTHER/MALOCAL read raw texel alphas or the TCA mux outputs is not in the spec. Glide's naming (gtex.c:1803-1811) and the vendor tables assume raw. Every tier-7 cell uses default TCA selects, so a coupling would pass every probe and break the first title whose stage-1 alpha op uses non-default selects.

Dead-stage rule (G12.md:207: 'The same holds for alpha') lacks cross-channel edges. Stage 0's ALPHA stays live whenever stage 1's COLOUR reads CURRENT alpha (BLENDCURRENTALPHA, CURRENT|ALPHAREPLICATE), even if stage 1's alpha op ignores CURRENT. Those references do not keep stage 0's colour alive. Example: stage-1 colour BLENDCURRENTALPHA with alpha SELECTARG1(TEXTURE); a per-channel implementation would drop the needed alpha.

OTHER is routed into TMU0 with TMU1 unprogrammed. The design forbids OTHER only in TMU1 (G12.md:141). In every one-texture placement (F, TINT, T0F), however, TMU0's OTHER is TMU1's stale output, because TMU1 is written only when r->textured1 (vcrdd_3d.c:119-126). TINT's row offers TMU0 'REPLACE/MULT/ADD' (G12.md:263); MULT/ADD there read garbage. T1T0 also allows a texture-less TMU1 but says nothing of its LOD/base; Glide forces an unused TMU to 1x1 (distate.c:1596).

Keyed draws and the mirror test both need canonical ordering. The recipe table puts arg1 in A/cc_other (G12.md:219, 226), so MODULATE(DIFFUSE,TEXTURE) and MODULATEALPHA_ADDCOLOR(TEXTURE,DIFFUSE) select DIFFUSE as c_other. G09 requires c_other = texture RGB for chroma-keyed draws (G09.md:382), and legacy always puts TEXTURE in other (vcrdd_d3d.c:700-705). The design's own mirror assertion (bit-identical fbz for legacy-correct setups, G12.md:458; worked word 0x0C482405 at G12.md:296, which uses CC_M CLOCAL) contradicts its routing table's '7 + m7 IRGB' for C=DIFFUSE (G12.md:127). vcr_cmb_in has no 'keyed' input.

The measured payoff beyond G05 is one combination behind the riskiest tier. Bit 6's '25/26 UT2003 combos' are the 18 already right plus G05's 7, and the 3 world combos rest on stage-1 arguments that were never logged (G12.md:88). The only measured gain over G05 is combine 21, which needs bit 8 plus G58. Every other title in games_unblocked is inferred. That does not yet justify an L-effort engine of ~2,400 lines of kernel and test code.

The default-on shadow verdict (G12.md:60-62, 351-357) runs vcr_cmb_compile at 3 tiers inside log_combo on every default install. Register traffic is unchanged, but this is new kernel code on the default path of a display driver, and VcrDd cannot check the log level (vcrdd_log.c:20-38 always issues the IOCTL). The measurement needs only the stage-1 arguments that log_combo omits today (vcrdd_d3d.c:908-913).

Compile cost. compute_regs runs at every DP2 call's first triangle and on every texture bind: TEXTUREHANDLE (vcrdd_d3d.c:1400-1402) and TEXTUREMAP (:1600-1602) mark the context dirty even when the handle is unchanged, and UE2 binds hundreds of textures per frame. The compile's inputs (the TSS and which textures are usable) do not depend on which texture is bound, yet the cache is deferred to 'if > 1%' (G12.md:519).

Sanitizer claim. tests/run_all.sh:64 compiles every native test with fixed flags (-std=c11 -O0 -g -Wall). '-fsanitize=address,undefined' (G12.md:459) therefore needs its own runner, and run_all.sh is a shared index file under the CLAUDE.md guardrails.

Gap-summary inaccuracies. (1) The risk text 'alpha >= 0x60 sets [30:29]=3' is wrong: chromaRange[30:29] are bits 6:5 of TFACTOR's alpha, so the condition is (alpha & 0x60) == 0x60 (0x60-0x7F, 0xE0-0xFF); 0x80 does not arm substitution. G12.md:515's 0xFF test is correct. (2) 'BLEND*ALPHA right only with TEXTURE as arg1' is imprecise. BLEND*(TFACTOR, DIFFUSE/CURRENT) is also right (other = C1, local = iterated, vcrdd_d3d.c:700-713), and (TEXTURE, TFACTOR) is wrong (local is still diffuse).
corrections: Land G05 first, on its own D3DFeat bit, as the P0 slice (MODULATE2X/4X via the FBI and TMU0 OUTSHIFT, as G05.md:39-45 proposes). Build G12 as an extension of G05's header and emission, on NEW bits; never re-purpose a bit already proven on silicon. Publish one central D3DFeat allocation table (G05, G08, G12, G13, G16) before any of them lands.
Allocate the display event sub-codes centrally, or give the combine engine its own event id (G02 proposes 514 for engine events). No design may use 513/24-25 without that table.

Make G12's first step measurement only: extend log_combo, default-on and log-only, to record both stages' full TSS. That means every ARG with its COMPLEMENT/ALPHAREPLICATE bits, TEXCOORDINDEX, and TSS 26-28 if they arrive. Run UT2003/UT2004, Halo, Max Payne (attended), Red Faction, H&D and BF1942, then compute the verdicts on the host with the same vcr_combine.h compiled natively. Scope bits 7/8 to the combinations actually measured. Keep the kernel shadow compile out of the default build, or put it behind its own Diag bit.

Use ONE forget hook: G41's, at all of G41.md:227-238's points, plus the G01/G02 resets. G12 only adds cm_primed and tmuc_valid to it. The fog_valid behaviour change ships under G41's own default-on justification, so G12 keeps its byte-for-byte claim.

Resolve chroma ownership with G03. When the TMU tier is armed, either G03's baseline skips the TMU chromaRange write, or G03's baseline calls the forget hook so that tmuc_valid drops and G12 reloads TFACTOR after it. G03's write 20 must use the FBI chip field (0x400+0x138), not broadcast. Add a d3dprobe cell with D3DSafe bit 1 plus the TMU tier armed and a TFACTOR-in-TMU0 recipe drawn across two DP2 calls.

Model the TMU a_other/a_local coupling conservatively until silicon settles it. Allow tc_mselect MAOTHER/MALOCAL (and add_alocal) only when the same TMU's TCA other/local select is OTHER_TA/LOCAL_TA; otherwise move the alpha op or return LEGACY. Add a tier-7 cell beside stage1_blendca whose stage-1 alpha op is SELECTARG1(TFACTOR) or SELECTARG1(DIFFUSE), so the TCA other select is non-default, and a matching native-model switch.

Define liveness per channel with cross-channel edges. Stage-0 alpha is live if stage-1 alpha reads CURRENT OR stage-1 colour reads CURRENT alpha (BLENDCURRENTALPHA, CURRENT|ALPHAREPLICATE). Stage-0 colour is live only if stage-1 colour reads CURRENT RGB. The final stage's alpha is always live (blend/test). Pin each edge in the native test.

Add the routing rule 'never route OTHER_* in TMU0 unless this draw programs TMU1', and restrict TINT/T0F at tier 6 to TMU0 REPLACE. A texture-less TMU1 in T1T0 gets its LOD forced to 1x1 and a known-valid base, as Glide does (distate.c:1596).

Canonicalise commutative ops (MODULATE*, ADD, the MODULATE*_ADD* operand that is a texture) so TEXTURE sits in A/cc_other. Use the CLOCAL encoding wherever the legacy shape exists, so the mirror test can hold. Add 'keyed' to vcr_cmb_in: when FZ_CHROMAKEY is set, c_other must route TRGB or the verdict is LEGACY (legacy already keeps the texel in other).
Key a per-context compile cache on the combine-relevant TSS words plus texture/coordinate usability from day one, so texture binds that do not change the combine never recompile.
Run the sanitizer fuzz from its own script (e.g. tests/native/run_sanitized.sh), not by editing the shared run_all.sh flags.

Correct the gap summary: the substitution condition is (TFACTOR alpha & 0x60) == 0x60, and BLEND*ALPHA is right for (TEXTURE or TFACTOR, DIFFUSE/CURRENT) and wrong otherwise. Record open question 8 as answered by vendor practice (D6DP2.C:6943 together with D6MT.C:4412-4414), pending one probe.

problems: The code gap is real, but the gap's stated symptom is not. TRANSPARENCY is advertised (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:2034-2035), and nothing in the 3D path reads COLORKEYENABLE, HASCKEYSRCBLT or ddckCKSrcBlt; FZ_CHROMAKEY and V3D_CHROMAKEY are defined but unused (include/vcr_3dregs.h:32,107), all confirmed by grep. D3D8 drops the cap, so caps_124.txt TextureCaps 0x4007 can neither confirm nor refute it. I checked visual-07 myself: in fbshots/thief2_c2.png brightened 8x, the tree, the polygonal bushes and also the iron fence bars are correct cut-outs filled flat (0,0,8). An ignored key under a flat fill would show solid quads, so this transparency comes from alpha and the design's re-attribution is right. No captured frame of any staged title shows a key failure.

Late keys most likely never reach the driver. Point 2 of the design's §2.1 key test reads only DD_SURFACE_LOCAL.dwFlags and ddckCKSrcBlt, but our DirectDraw HAL registers no SetColorKey callback (display/vcrdd_ddraw.c:722-724). Microsoft's NT sample registers DdSetColorKey precisely to refresh texture keys after creation (w2kddk 3dlabs/driver/d3d.c:2195-2235, dd.c:1412-1413). AvP, the design's lead title, emits 'setting the colour key' after 'creating destination direct draw surface' and 'loading texture into destination' (avp.exe string order), so it keys an existing texture. Deferring the hook to Q1 risks a v1 that keys nothing in AvP.

Creation-time keys are also unproven through the kernel flags. Our own HAL documents that NT's kernel DD_SURFACE_LOCAL.dwFlags does not mirror the user-mode flags: HASPIXELFORMAT was absent on a texture that carries a pixel format (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:162-169). So the probe's base 'colorkey' case (DDSD_CKSRCBLT) is not a guaranteed pass. The design also ignores a direct source it already has: Dd_CreateSurface is hooked and runs for textures (display/vcrdd_ddraw.c:633-643), with the app's DDSURFACEDESC in hand.

The bit-off measurement has a blind spot. With no hook, a title that keys after creation is counted as NO_KEY, so boot A cannot 'decide which titles key' (§2.4, §6 step 3) and cannot safely drive the P0/P1 escalation. It is also internally inconsistent: §2.1 and §2.4 do not count NO_STATE ('the app did not ask'), yet Q2 is to be 'settled by ck_why[NO_STATE] with keyed textures bound'.

ckey_recheck is redundant, and its premise is false. Every DP2 call does memset(&w,0,...) (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1835), so prepared=0 and the first prepare() always reruns compute_regs (:1335-1336). compute_regs already reads the live surface through handle_get (:924). A key changed between DP2 calls is picked up with no extra code, so test_dp2_rechecks_the_bound_textures_key would pin dead code.

The Q1 fallback ('store the key per handle entry') would be silently erased. handle_ent holds only {ddlcl, handle, surf} (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:76-80), and handle_forget rebuilds the whole table through handle_set(l,h,s) on every surface destroy (:95, :134-145). Any added key field is dropped for every surviving texture whenever any surface goes away.

The probe exercises the wrong runtime for the target titles. d3d7probe drives IDirect3DDevice7 on d3dim700, while JK, MotS, Rainbow Six, AvP, Thief Gold, SS2 and Shogo run on d3dim.dll (G75.md:46-50). Per G75 §2.3 F2, d3dim drops a SetRenderState equal to its stored copy. Whether COLORKEYENABLE ever reaches us therefore depends on d3dim's initial RS41 against our ctx_defaults FALSE (vcrdd_d3d.c:1128). This makes Q2 wider than execute buffers: runtime.md:76 lists Rainbow Six as IDirect3D2 + ExecuteBuffer, and Device2/3 are exposed too. The design plans to settle it from game counters only.

The plumbing collides with sibling designs. VCR_INFO_F 0x8000 is also proposed by G08 and G16 (G15.md:273), and G12/G14/G15 instead append a d3dfeat word to vcr_info. hal.md files the colour key as Phase 3 (D3DFeat bits 6+). Event codes 513/2x are claimed by about 19 sibling designs. G03 also adds V3D_CHROMARANGE plus a broadcast FBI chromaRange=0, and proposes a test that compute_regs never sets FZ_CHROMAKEY (G03.md:416); that test directly contradicts G09.

Weak evidence is used for the exclusions. 'THIEF.EXE and Shogo hold no colour-key string' proves nothing: SetColorKey is a COM vtable call and COLORKEYENABLE is the number 41, neither of which leaves a string. Shogo's D3D path is d3d.ren, not Shogo.exe, and d3d.ren has no string either. One real counter-datum is available: the MotS D3D crawl (d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108_fixed/.../Jedi_Knight_Mysteries_of_the_Sith_60s.png) shows stars between glyphs at sky density (0.0141 against 0.0136). Its text background is not drawn opaque, so that scene does not depend on a texture key.

The verification plan has gaps. The 86Box bed ignores the chip field for chromaKey and does not implement chromaRange at all (86box/voodoo_reg.c:80-82, 605-609), so a bed pass proves the compare logic but not the 0x400 routing. On silicon, PIO chip-field decode is shown only for TMU0 against TMU1 (tex2mod/tex2add pass, onbox/d3dprobe_render_640x480x16.txt). The FBI field (0x400) is plausible but has never been exercised. Boot B checks no 2D DirectDraw title, although an armed hook changes the DirectDraw callback table that the keyed sprites of RA2, StarCraft and Tiberian Sun go through.

Filter precision is untested at saturated key channels. colorkey_filter uses only magenta (0xFF channels). If the VSA-100 bilinear filter loses an LSB on 0xFF, keyed interiors would survive under LINEAR, and nothing in the plan tells that apart from edge fringes. 86Box's exact >>8 filter cannot reveal it.
corrections: Keep the hardware recipe as designed; it checks out against the spec and the vendor. fbzMode[1] (SPEC L3205/L3224); chromaKey RGB in [23:0], alpha ignored (L3520-3527); FBI-only write at 0x534 and chromaRange=0 at 0x538 (bit 28 off; [30:29] are TMU-only, L3546-3547); 3dfx's FIFO chip mask 0x1 on Napalm (VH5/D6DP2.C:6936-6958). The MSB-replication vectors match VH5/D3TRI.H:231 and D3GLOBAL.H:987-992. The single-stage and rgbsel==TMU guards are correct. Room(n+4) in VcrDd3dState is sufficient. With the bit off the register traffic is byte-identical.

Move the DdSetColorKey surface callback (DDHAL_SURFCB32_SETCOLORKEY) into v1, registered only while the CKEY bit is armed. It handles DDCKEY_SRCBLT on video-memory textures, storing the low and high values, and returns HANDLED with DD_OK for everything else (the MS sample pattern, d3d.c:2195-2235). Also capture DDSD_CKSRCBLT keys from lpDDSurfaceDesc in Dd_CreateSurface (vcrdd_ddraw.c:633-643). Keep the surface-local read only as a fallback, and log all three sources at CreateSurfaceEx so the probe shows which one XP actually fills. Add vcrdd_ddraw.c to the file list.

If keys are stored in handle_ent, make handle_forget copy whole entries instead of calling handle_set(l,h,s) (vcrdd_d3d.c:134-145). Add a test that one texture's key survives another surface being destroyed.

Drop ckey_recheck and test_dp2_rechecks_the_bound_textures_key. Instead pin the invariant G09 relies on: every DP2 call's first draw reruns compute_regs from the live handle (vcrdd_d3d.c:1835 + 1335-1336).

Fix the counters. Count NO_STATE whenever a keyed texture is bound, and log each RS41 arrival with its value; Q2 needs both. Write into the plan that bit-off counters cannot see late keys, so a NO_KEY result must never lower the priority. If exposure has to be measured before arming, add a separate record-only hook bit.

Settle Q2 and G75's F2 by probe, not by game counters. Add legacy-family cases to d3d7probe on d3dim.dll: Device3 and Device2 with COLORKEYENABLE set TRUE, never set, and set TRUE twice; plus an execute-buffer (v1) device that never sets it. After each exits, read RS41 arrivals and keyed results from the ring. If d3dim's stored default is TRUE, match it in ctx_defaults for d3dim contexts behind the same bit; the AND rule bounds the effect to keyed textures.

Use the shared D3DFeat word proposed by G12/G14/G15, with a Phase-3 bit from hal.md, not VCR_INFO_F 0x8000/0x10000. Take the 513 event codes from a single allocation table. When G03 lands, change its 'compute_regs never sets FZ_CHROMAKEY' test (G03.md:416) to 'only when keyed'.

Strengthen boot B. Add ddlab's keyed-blit test and one keyed-sprite 2D DirectDraw title (StarCraft or RA2) as no-regression checks for the armed hook. Keep the d3dprobe 40/40 leak check in the same boot; it also shows TMU state is intact after FBI-only writes. Optionally, after the probe exits (never during a D3D run), read fbiChromaFail (0x150, SPEC L3657-3661) as a register-level post-condition: non-zero when armed, unchanged with the bit off.

Add a black-key (0x0000) twin to colorkey_filter beside the magenta one. If interiors fail only with 0xFF channels, the remedy is an FBI chromaRange inclusive band [key-1, key] per channel in intersection mode (SPEC L3530-3546), rather than forcing point sampling.

Restate the title evidence. AvP: strong, since its loader sets the key after the texture is loaded and its caps dump checks TRANSPARENCY; but it is untestable until G71. Rainbow Six: moderate, from a 'colorkey' material keyword plus Surface::SetTransparentValue. JK, MotS, Thief Gold, SS2 and Shogo: unknown, not 'no evidence'; the MotS crawl does not depend on a key. H&D: confirmed D3D8 (igraph2.dll loads Direct3DCreate8). Keep visual-07 re-routed to G12/G14/G32; the fence bars show the same alpha cut-out pattern.

Do not treat an 86Box pass as evidence for the 0x400 routing, and do not flip the bit default-on without a silicon run that shows keyed pixels killed by FBI-only writes at both 640x480x16 and 1024x768x32.

problems: THE KEY NEVER REACHES THE SURFACE THE HAL READS. This is the biggest problem. Rainbow Six and AvP set their keys with IDirectDrawSurface::SetColorKey after the surface is created. XP SP3 ddraw.dll 5.3.2600.5512 (md5 a340cd71) handles that call in DD_Surface_SetColorKey at 0x7376ddbf. When DDCAPS_COLORKEY is missing from both ddBothCaps (gbl+0x484, tested at 0x7376de8e) and the driver's ddCaps (gbl+0x10, at 0x7377a765), the call goes to the HEL (gbl+0x194, at 0x7377a79a). ddraw then calls HELDDSurface.SetColorKey (callbacks+0x150, at 0x7377a85b), not the kernel thunk HALDDSurface.SetColorKey (+0xd0, at 0x7376df76). Even on the hardware path, ddraw skips the driver call when cbDDSurfaceCallbacks.SetColorKey (+0x50) is NULL (0x7376df8b). Hardware-path validation also requires the driver's dwCKeyCaps to include DDCKEYCAPS_SRCBLT (0x7377a6bb). SetColorKey never calls DdCreateSurfaceObject to re-sync the kernel surface; its only callers are at 0x737824a4, 0x73783ad0, 0x7378ba49 and 0x73790d22. d3dim.dll copies the user-mode key into its own stage state at 0x6d9294ed, and no DP2 token carries the key to the driver. Our HAL reports dwCaps = BLT|BLTCOLORFILL|READSCANLINE, dwCKeyCaps 0, and no DDHAL_SURFCB32_SETCOLORKEY (vcrdd_ddraw.c:101, 722-724). So compute_regs' check of t->dwFlags & DDRAWISURF_HASCKEYSRCBLT would stay 0 for both real users, and the bit-on boot would key nothing. The design's Q1 fallback, a DdSetColorKey hook on its own, would never be called either.

THE MEASUREMENT CANNOT SEE THE GAP. The boot-A counters (513/24-25, design 2.4 and 6.3) are meant to show which titles key textures. Under today's caps they would log Rainbow Six and AvP as COLORKEYENABLE on with VCR_CK_NO_KEY. The plan would read that as 'these titles do not key', keep G09 at P1 or drop it, and never escalate. That is wrong for Rainbow Six, whose data file shows it keys hundreds of textures (next item).

RAINBOW SIX IS CONFIRMED, WITH EVIDENCE STRONGER THAN THE DESIGN'S 'LIKELY'. LIB/RainbowSix/data/texture/Sherman.CXP (md5 e011c33b) declares 294 colour-keyed materials, covering the training levels, all 16 missions, weapons, special effects and map icons. Examples by line: glass (2-12), treeline (22), fire-escape grill (39), M16 sight (377), blood (390), bullet hole (392), muzzle flash (396), aiming reticle (405-406), shadow (407), map icons (410). RainbowSix.exe (md5 c92073e4) parses the 'colorkey' token at 0x478e24. Surface::SetTransparentValue calls SetColorKey(DDCKEY_SRCBLT) with low = high (0x46ad70-0x46ad9a). The Renderer toggles COLORKEYENABLE through IDirect3DDevice2::SetRenderState at vtable 0x5c (0x47ab45-0x47ab77). Rainbow Six is staged and deployed on .124 with SoftwareOnly=0 (D3D). An ignored key in these common scenes is P0 under the definitions, not 'P1 pending counters'.

THE TITLE LIST IS MOSTLY WRONG. Four of the listed titles are not affected, and Thief Gold, System Shock 2 and the Thief II DX6 path are unlikely ones.
- Jedi Knight and Mysteries of the Sith call SetColorKey on a texture only when the device lacks D3DPTEXTURECAPS_ALPHA. JK.EXE tests device+0x10 at 0x42a7fa-0x42a839, and sets that field to (dwTextureCaps>>2)&1 at 0x42be4e-0x42be59. JKM.EXE does the same at 0x42d9ca-0x42da09 and 0x42f00e-0x42f019. We advertise ALPHA (vcrdd_d3d.c:2034-2035), so both use alpha texels and are not affected.
- Shogo's d3d.ren has no SetColorKey call and never sets render state 41. Its only push $0x29 (0x1003a2e3) is a caps-table read.
- Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe is D3D8, which has no colour keys.
- Thief Gold is not proven keyless by the absence of a string. Its lgd3d state code sets COLORKEYENABLE through IDirect3DDevice3::SetRenderState from a per-texture flag (THIEF.EXE 0x574ee6-0x574f52, 0x57540b-0x575478). But lgd3d's own texture CreateSurface calls carry no DDSD_CKSRCBLT (dwFlags 0x1007 at 0x5743d7 and 0x574427), and no SetColorKey call lies in the lgd3d range. The 8x-brightened thief2_c2.png shows the alpha cut-outs working. Keyed draws are therefore unlikely there.

AVP DEPENDS ON THE KEY ENTIRELY, BUT CANNOT BE TESTED YET.
- Its texture-format callback (avp.exe 0x4dc612) rejects every format with DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS, ALPHA or FOURCC (test $0x7 at 0x4dc6db). On our HAL its only 3D format is therefore RGB565.
- Its loader calls SetColorKey(DDCKEY_SRCBLT) on every image that has a transparent colour (0x5178b0-0x5178ca).
- It never writes COLORKEYENABLE or ALPHATESTENABLE. XP's d3dim.dll 5.1.2600.0 starts COLORKEYENABLE as TRUE for version-1 HAL and Ref devices: the decision is at 0x6d9136ac-0x6d9136d0, the push at 0x6d9138a2-0x6d9138ab, after the state cache is filled with -1 at 0x6d9136de; the HAL flag is set at 0x6d9184a8. The colour key is therefore AvP's only cut-out mechanism.
- AvP has never reached a D3D device on any box, and .124 is excluded (G71).
- The design's claim that the advertised cap steers AvP's loader is unsupported. 'Does %s support texture transparency' sits in a table-driven caps dump with no code reference. AvP reads dwTextureFilterCaps (0x851f7c, at 0x4fa60f) from the device description, never dwTextureCaps.

THE PROBE TESTS THE WRONG RUNTIME AND THE WRONG PATTERN. G09 puts the colour-key cases only in d3d7probe's DX7 mode (d3dim700). The real users run on d3dim.dll: Rainbow Six through IDirect3DDevice2, AvP through a version-1 execute-buffer device that relies on the runtime's TRUE default. The base 'colorkey' case keys at creation (DDSD_CKSRCBLT), which neither title does, so it can pass while both titles still fail. 'colorkey_default' expects K drawn, which is wrong for a version-1 HAL device.

THE Q2 SUB-BIT IS UNNEEDED. Defaulting COLORKEYENABLE to TRUE for D3DOP_EXIT contexts duplicates what d3dim.dll already sends for version-1 devices.

Q7 (colour-space keys) and Q8 (withdraw TRANSPARENCY) are moot: Rainbow Six and AvP pass single keys, Rainbow Six never reads the cap (its enum callback 0x498060 reads only PERSPECTIVE, at 0x49818f), and AvP rejects every alpha format. No caps-only fix or staged-config fix exists. Rainbow Six's only workaround is SoftwareOnly=1 (DevicePicker, install.reg), a degraded per-box stopgap.

BILINEAR FRINGES ARE NOT OPTIONAL FOR RAINBOW SIX. Today the HAL point-samples everything because the legacy TEXTUREMAG/MIN states are ignored (G08), so an exact FBI key looks clean. Once G08 honours the LINEAR filtering these titles ask for, the FBI compare runs after filtering and leaves halos in the key colour. Rainbow Six uses many non-black keys: 96 128 144, 64 160 32, 224 224 160 and 240 232 216.

THE RISK TABLE'S 'NONE' DOES NOT HOLD. The DirectDraw prerequisite that is actually needed is DDCAPS_COLORKEY plus DDCKEYCAPS_SRCBLT. It moves every source-keyed video-memory Blt from the HEL to our engine: JK, MotS, Rainbow Six and AvP all issue such blits for their UI (G61 section 2.4). Per G61, a claimed cap that answers NOTHANDLED returns E_NOTIMPL with no HEL fallback.

There is also a G38 coupling. AvP's callback accepts PALETTEINDEXED8, and Rainbow Six's loadtex has a palette path. If P8 lands default-on, both titles may switch to palette-index keys, which G09 v1 refuses.
corrections:
Re-scope the affected titles:
- Rainbow Six: confirmed. Cite Sherman.CXP and the RainbowSix.exe addresses.
- AvP: near-certain, after G71.
- Thief Gold, System Shock 2, the Thief II DX6 path: measure only.
- Jedi Knight DF2, MotS, Shogo, Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe: remove from the affected and unblocked lists.
- Drop 'Dark-engine foliage' from the gap title and keep the visual-07 re-attribution.

Run the colour-key suite in G75's legacy mode on d3dim.dll as well as in DX7 mode:
- (a) IDirect3DDevice2 with SetRenderState(41, TRUE), then Lock, fill, and SetColorKey after creation. This is Rainbow Six's pattern.
- (b) A version-1 HAL execute-buffer device that never sends state 41, with the key set after creation. This is AvP's pattern; expect K keyed.
In both:
- assert SetColorKey's HRESULT and the GetColorKey readback;
- make the late-key case the pass criterion and keep the create-time case only as a control;
- fix colorkey_default's expectation per device version.
Drop the Q2 EXIT-default sub-bit. Instead, count the runtime's initial RENDERSTATE(41,1) on version-1 contexts to confirm that d3dim.dll's default reaches DP2. Delete Q7 and Q8, or mark them P3.

Set priority P0, driven by Rainbow Six: its defect in common scenes is established statically. AvP joins once G71 lands. The DirectDraw key-delivery work is part of this P0 fix, or its P1 prerequisite. Do not make escalation depend on counters that cannot see late keys.
Add a G38 coordination rule: no P8 texture format default-on until palette-index keys are handled. Otherwise AvP and Rainbow Six may move onto keyed P8 textures that G09 refuses.

Add DirectDraw regression coverage for the caps change. Run ddlab's HEL-twin keyed-blit cases, and check the keyed UI blits of JK, MotS, Rainbow Six and AvP in game. Confirm that the DirectDraw-only titles are unaffected: G61 reports RA2/YR as emulation-only and StarCraft/WC2 as plain copies.

problems: UNCONFIRMED, the second defect (LINELIST_IMM skip length). The design's 'four independent parsers' are one lineage. VH5/D6DP2.C:3732,3748 and W9X/D6DP2.C:3561,3577 are the same code. 3dfx's DP2 parser copies Microsoft's DX6 sample macros verbatim, comment included ('This MUST be done by the driver even on free builds...': VH5/D6DP2.C:835-856 vs DDK/3dlabs/driver/d3ddx6.c:53-71). 3dlabs and s3virge are one Microsoft template. Both DDK samples' own comments say 'Draw a set of lines specified by pairs of vertices' (3dlabs d3ddx6.c:1110-1116, s3virge d3ddx6.c:991-997), while their code reads n+1 (:1124/:1143, s3virge :1024). This repo's fxD3D HAL reads 2n and a host test pins it (scripts/3dfx/d3dhal/d3dhal_dp2real.c:495-507, test/test_dp2real.c:186-187). Nothing measures whether XP's runtime ever sends n>=2. For n=1 the change is a no-op. If the runtime sends pairs, Step 0 creates the very desync it claims to remove.

Step 0 changes default-path parsing (vcrdd_d3d.c:1690-1694) without silicon proof. That goes against the project rule (default-OFF, or byte-identical, until proven). 'Ship with the next driver build regardless' bundles an unproven behaviour change into another item's proof build. The lineclip sentinel cannot tell old from new: it also passes on today's driver unless an n>=2 IMM actually arrives. Its strip leaves the viewport only once, so it may never produce one.

Latent bounds hole. NEED (vcrdd_d3d.c:1570) casts (end - p) to ULONG. The DWORD alignment at :1682 (TRIANGLEFAN_IMM, which draws today) and :1691 (LINELIST_IMM) can move p up to 2 bytes past end in a truncated stream. After that every NEED passes, and the vertex loop reads past dwCommandLength in kernel mode. Design 4.1(a) ('pad exactly as today, then NEED((n+1)*stride)') keeps this hole, and Step 1 adds a second reader. Design 4.2's NEED(vcr_dp2_prim_bytes(op,n,stride,pad)) would close it. The two sections disagree.

LASTPIXEL. Design 4.2 calls [first,last) 'D3D's half-open rule'. The headers define LASTPIXEL TRUE as 'last-pixel on lines' (dx8ddk/inc/d3d8types.h:327, xpddk/inc/crt/d3dtypes.h:1198), and the documented runtime default is TRUE (from DirectX docs; not found in a local file). So default D3D draws both ends. With this geometry, as with 3dfx's (D3RSTATE.C:4016 'Not supported'), a closed clockwise rectangle LINESTRIP misses its bottom-right corner pixel, and every reversed segment drops its first pixel. Vendor parity is acceptable; the text is wrong.

The probe is blind to half-pixel geometry errors. Every line in design section 7 has integer endpoints. A +0.5 error, such as quad() going through vertex() so xy_bias is added twice, moves the minor-axis edges onto pixel centres. Under a top-left tie the expected row still lights and the rows at ±1 stay black, so the test passes on a broken driver. The silicon tie rule is itself unmeasured: d3dprobe samples Q0+1 and Q1+1, never the edge pixel (tools/d3dprobe.c:933-934). The Python list does not pin that quad() calls vertex_at.

The points test may never reach the HAL. That XP's d3d8 sends size-1 points as DP2 POINTS to a DX7 DDI is inferred (runtime.md:482). If the runtime handles them itself, the lit checks pass on today's driver and the 'old-buggy = 000000' expectation is wrong. The line and point tests do not consult the new counters, so a pass does not prove the HAL drew anything.

Numbering collisions across the plan. VCR_INFO_F 0x8000 is free in today's vcr_ioctl.h:109-143, but it is also claimed by G01 FIFOGUARD (G01.md:61, the D3D precondition that lands first), G02:91, G05:336, G07:103 and G08:283. Event 513 sub-codes 24-26 are also claimed by G01/G03/G05/G09/G10/G11/G12/G14/G22 (G02.md:334, G24.md:114, G10.md:235-236). D3DFeat bit 4 does match hal.md Phase 2 item 5.

The perf follow-up (section 4.2 cost note, open question 8: skip parameter writes on repeated corners) is contraindicated by the hardware spec, not merely untested. SPEC (avenger_spec.doc text L2769, section 21.3 L6221): with fbzColorPath bit 26 PARMADJUST set, 'the host must pass down new starting parameter information for each new triangle', otherwise the start parameters are subpixel-corrected twice. Our HAL always sets PARMADJUST (test_the_colour_path_always_carries_parmadjust).

The gap text says 'FILLMODE wireframe/point would route through these opcodes'. That is wrong: FILLMODE arrives as triangle opcodes plus a render state, and the driver draws the edges (DDK 3dlabs d3ddx6.c:789-866; VH5/D6STRIPI.C:287,419). The design itself correctly leaves this to G24.

Promotion requires 'one game A/B shows the element appearing'. If the Phase-0 counters find no staged title that sends lines or points (the P2 premise), that criterion cannot be met. The design does not say what happens then.

NOT A PROBLEM, verified: deployed vcrdd.dll 95678704 equals out/vcrdd.dll, built 2026-11-08 02:33 after the last vcrdd_d3d.c commit 481acfd with no uncommitted display changes, so :1690-1715, :2063 and :2072 are what .124 runs. SM_FAN/CULL/CULL_NEGATIVE (bits 16/17/18) match INC/H3DEFS.H:982-985 and SPEC section 8.59 (L3718-3733). The BEGIN-then-DRAW strip matches section 8.60. JK DF2 and MotS are refuted as users. Thief Gold: the point path is real, but the plan names the wrong content. There are no pixel particles. LIB/ThiefGold/DARK.GAM's P$ParticleG holds 208 groups (187 disks, 13 scaled bitmaps, 8 squares), and none of the 17 missions holds a pixel-type group. Points come from the star sky instead. SKYMODE=1 ('Stars'; enum {Textures, Stars} at THIEF.EXE 0x5e8f28) is set in 15 of 17 missions, all but miss1 and miss3. The chain: the frame loop calls the star code when sky mode == 1 (0x433036-0x433081). In D3D mode (flag 0x6fcf04, set at 0x43b040 after 'Using D3D device') 0x444140 installs pixel hook 0x4440c0. That leads to lgd3d_draw_point 0x56edf0, then renderer vtable slot 0x24 (0x5723b0), then the batch flush at 0x5723a1: IDirect3DDevice3::DrawPrimitive(D3DPT_POINTLIST, FVF 0x1c4, ..., D3DDP_DONOTCLIP). That arrives as DP2 POINTS, which vcrdd_d3d.c:1695-1698 skips. Expected on .124: no stars in outdoor night scenes in 15 of 17 missions. G16 never mentions stars. Thief Gold's D3D device draws only fans, lists and points (0x5700f9, 0x57127c, 0x5723a1, 0x572b4f, 0x572bf3, 0x572c6f); it draws no lines.

For n=1, 2n equals n+1, so today's walk never desyncs. The 'COMMAND_UNPARSED / JK-crash' risk and the reason given for shipping Step 0 ('fixes a walker desync', G16.md §1 item 2 and §11) do not hold here. The on-box UT2003, UT2004 and Halo sessions all logged 0 unparsed (reports/onbox.md §6).

problems: GAP CONFIRMED, WITH THE DESIGN'S CORRECTION: the code reads as the gap says. give_up() only logs and clears g2d_ok (KMD/display/vcrdd_2d.c:83-89). The DP2 walk is gated by w.drawable (vcrdd_d3d.c:1859-1860) and DP2 returns the walk's DD_OK (:1869). Clear2 hard-codes DD_OK (:1901). ContextCreate never reads g2d_ok (:1163-1208). Dd_Flip never checks it (vcrdd_ddraw.c:315-361). DrvAssertMode(TRUE) does not re-initialise (vcrdd.c:574-606). The HAL disappeared through the LIVE GetDriverInfo gate (vcrdd_d3d.c:2136; ring seq 25127/25134 7de41f80 -> 88760028; no new 511 a=1 line), not through DrvGetDirectDrawInfo (:2058). So the gap text's mechanism is wrong and the design's correction is right.

NEW CORRECTNESS HAZARD FROM PART B (verified in code and on the box): texture placement turns off while g2d_ok=0. mipchain_ext returns 0 (vcrdd_d3d.c:378), and so does VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain (:534), so DirectDraw places the texture itself. The 10:03 ring shows it: before the give-up, seq 25051 'mipmap chain 64x64 ... at c0000'; after it, the texture CreateSurfaces (seq 25062, 25073, 25087, 25089) have no 513/20 line. Once part B re-arms g2d_ok, any texture created in the lost window keeps the runtime's placement. That can mean a 4-byte-aligned base (no alignment check in vcr_texlod_compute_ext, common/vcr_texlod.c:94-134: the 481acfd noise) or a mip chain not packed the way ext_layout and the TMU assume. TEXBLT copies into next_mip levels (vcrdd_d3d.c:1532-1545). Part C's own flow (lost -> Reset accepted while lost -> the app re-creates DEFAULT/managed textures) produces exactly these textures. Every d3dprobe test in the design draws flat quads, so none can catch this.

THE CONTEXTCREATE REFUSAL CONFLICTS WITH G11: 'refuse once per loss' is the post-mode-set refusal that G11 shows flaps the CRT. G11 §1-§2 and ring_after_probe_i record about 4 sync changes in ~170 ms, with the revert made INSIDE the runtime's failed call. The verification plan provokes this refusal on purpose on .124's 1998 CRT (fullscreen lost_report, 'Reset #1 must FAIL'). It relies on --pace 5000, but d3dprobe's pacing cannot pace a revert the runtime makes inside its own call (G11 §1). The 11-12 session deliberately chose not to repeat such a refusal (session_log 10:01:28 'Not repeated').

GATING DOES NOT ADD UP. (a) Parts B and C share bit 2, yet the promotion plan makes B (recovery) default-on and holds C (report) back. With one bit that is impossible. (b) Boot C 'D3DSafe=4 for daily use' arms C for the DX5-7 titles (JK DF2, MotS, Thief Gold/II, SS2, Shogo, AvP, Rainbow Six, H&D) before their reaction is measured; the design itself says that needs G75. (c) Part A lands default-on, against the project's default-off rule. Its default arm (RECORD with bit 2 off) never runs on .124 silicon: boot A has no give-up and bit 7 off, and boot B takes the RESET arm. So the risk section's 'boot A proves it' is false.

THE SPIN BOUND DEPENDS ON WALL-CLOCK TIME: vcr_el_decide's 2 s gap keeps one DDI call to two SPIN_CAP spins only while one spin (vcrdd_2d.c:71, 2,000,000 status reads, ~1.2 s on .124) is under 2 s. Where status reads are slower (the 86Box bed), each re-wedge finds the gap expired. One call can then make 3 resets and 4 spins under the display lock before the 60 s window stops it.

THE SILICON PROOF IS NARROWER THAN CLAIMED. Both recoveries on record are the busy-at-mode-set reset (miniport/vcrmp_hw.c:571-572) of a chip that was only waiting on Glide's command FIFO: status a1f = SST_BUSY|SST_CMD0_BUSY with FBI/TMU/2D idle, cmdFifo0 baseSize 0x1fe, readPtr stuck at 0x2f624 (onbox/regs/regs_after_windowed_1009.txt). Each was followed by a full mode set (voodoo_program rewrites miscInit0=0 and lfbMemoryConfig, vcrmp_hw.c:611-612) and a fresh PDEV (VcrDd2dInit). Three cases have never run on silicon: a same-PDEV re-arm with no mode set, a reset of an engine that is actively rasterising, and a 3D-pipeline wedge. ARM_ROOM/lost_midframe on .124 is the first two of these, yet only lost_hard is flagged as a first.

A VENDOR PRECEDENT WAS MISSED: 3dfx's GPL h5 Glide has a mid-session idle-timeout recovery ('Hardware timeout on idle, resetting...', present since the initial SourceForge checkin; ours at build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/minihwc/minihwc.c:2781-2810). It asserts miscInit0 GRX|2D (with BIT(30) RAWLFB swizzle cleared) and miscInit1 CMDSTREAM, waits 1000 status reads, then restores. It does NOT use SST_FBI_FIFO_RESET, which VcrHwResetEngine takes from the init-time h3InitResetAll. Our SLIAA-GUARD (:2767-2779) skips it on a multi-chip SLI/AA board because the slaves snoop the master's init registers. The design says 'Vendor reference: none usable'.

THE FAULT-INJECTION COUNTDOWN IS NOT CONFINED TO THE WALK: ARM_ROOM is decremented by every VcrDdRoom on the PDEV, not only the DP2 walk's. On .124 GDI copies and fills use the engine by default (Accel2D=1; vcrdd_punt.c:60, :99 -> VcrDd2dCopy/Fill -> VcrDdRoom). In the windowed lost_midframe run, desktop GDI work between the escape and frame B can consume the countdown, so the give-up lands in a GDI op and the quad-index expectations become nondeterministic.

LOSS STATE IS PER PDEV, BUT THE HARDWARE AND THE RESET GENERATION ARE DEVICE-WIDE: pd->el (lost, refusal count, 3/60 s budget) and fog_valid live in each PDEV. In fullscreen lost_report, a refused Reset may revert the mode (the G11 pattern) and destroy the PDEV that held the loss. The LIFT escape then lands on whatever PDEV the window DC maps to, and Reset #2 can pass on a fresh PDEV (VcrDd2dInit sets g2d_ok=1) for the wrong reason. Budgets also add up across PDEVs, and another PDEV's fog_valid stays stale after a reset.

SCOPE: the realistic failure after a Glide/OpenGL session (onbox 10:02 fullscreen: cmdFifo0 enabled but idle, every triangle missing, clears passing, NO give-up logged) never reaches give_up. G02 therefore neither records nor heals it; only G01 does. A stale exclusive_pid also gives DD_OK with nothing drawn (w.drawable requires !exclusive_pid, vcrdd_d3d.c:1859, :1887), and G02 leaves that path silent. G02 does not make D3D failure non-silent in general, and G01 is a HARD dependency for most of the games_unblocked list, not a soft one.

THE RE-ARM TEST CAN BE FOOLED SILENTLY: vcr_el_rearm_ok checks only idle and the PCI FIFO count, so a reset that changes a 3D register the HAL never writes would leave D3D silent again with g2d_ok=1. The 3D registers ARE readable: regs_after_windowed_1009 shows 0x200104 = 0c002401, matching the ring's 'combine 2: cp c002401', and colBuffer/aux = 0x40000/0x80000 = the context's target and Z. chipMask/sliCtrl/aaCtrl/combineMode (0x200208-0x200214) read 0 at the wedge. The post-reset dumps (regs_after_modeseq_1012, regs_after_games_1039) never read 0x2002xx. Open question 8 could have been answered by one read-only dump and was not; the post-reset 40/40 cannot separate the cmdFifo cure from any chipMask effect.

TEXTURE CACHE NOT RE-FLUSHED: the generation re-send in prepare() does not repeat a texture-cache flush that the reset discarded. flush_written runs only when g_tex_writes changed (vcrdd_d3d.c:1327-1334), and c->tex_writes_seen was updated before the VcrDd3dTexFlush that went into the FIFO (vcrdd_3d.c:253-270).

PRIORITY P0 IS OVERSTATED. No staged title has been shown to hit a give-up. The 11-12 in-game runs (UT2004 twice, UT2003, Halo) logged none; the only give-up on record was the windowed probe after a not-idle Glide close (G01's class); H4 is one of six Max Payne hypotheses (history.md §4.4). Part A is not required for G04 either. history §4.5 step 0 already sets LogLevel=2. 512/9 is an ERROR entry, and log_combo is capped at 64 per context (vcrdd_d3d.c:894-899), so the ring keeps it. H4 leaves the box alive to read the ring.

UNVERIFIED LOCKING AND AN UNGUARDED RESET PATH: the design rejects work-item resets because they lack the display lock. Its GetDriverInfo retry site needs the same lock, and nothing shows that dxg holds it around DdGetDriverInfo. Separately, the existing VCR_ESC_RESET_ENGINE -> IOCTL_VCR_RESET_ENGINE path (vcrdd_escape.c:323-324, vcrmp.c:865-867) resets the engine with no SLI, live-Glide or exclusive check. G02 builds these guards only for its new path.
corrections: Placement: remove the live-g2d_ok condition from mipchain_ext (vcrdd_d3d.c:378) and VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain (:534). Gate placement on a per-PDEV 'D3D HAL offered' flag set in VcrDdD3dHalInfo instead. Placement is CPU-only heap bookkeeping (HeapVidMemAllocAligned, no register writes), so a loss must not change it. Add a d3dprobe check: after BLOCK, create a mip-chained and an odd-sized texture; after LIFT and recovery, draw them and compare texels. The old-buggy result is noise or wrong mips.

ContextCreate: never refuse for a lost engine. Accept the context and answer lost from DP2/Clear2/Present, which is G11's contract. Settle open questions 1 and 2 (the D3D8 and DX5-7 runtime reaction, and whether a Reset makes mode sets) on the 86Box bed with G11's PhaseLog accounting. Never provoke a post-mode-set refusal on .124's CRT.

Split the switch: bit 2 = recover (part B) only; a new bit (5 or 6 are unclaimed by the sibling designs) = report (part C), kept off on daily-use boots until both the D3D8 and DX5-7 (G75) reactions are measured; record (part A) either gets its own opt-in bit armed for G04's boot, or its record-only arm is proven on .124 with a D3DSafe=0x80 boot running lost_recover before it goes default-on. Delete 'boot A proves it'.
Limit resets to one per DDI entry (a per-call flag), in addition to the 2 s gap and the 3-per-60 s window. Express the latency bound in spins per call, not in wall-clock time.

Make ARM_ROOM count only VcrDdRoom calls made inside a DP2/Clear2 walk (a flag set by D3d_DrawPrimitives2). Treat lost_midframe as the first reset of a rasterising engine on silicon: 86Box first, attended on .124, or drain the engine first, as SOFT already does.

Keep loss and policy state device-wide: one record for the chip, as a DLL global next to g_vcr_eng_resets or in the miniport (exposed through vcr_info). Tie fog validity to the generation rather than to per-PDEV fog_valid alone. Read every test verdict from the device-wide counters.

Cite 3dfx's own idle-timeout reset (GPL h5 minihwc.c, ours :2781-2810) as the vendor precedent. Decide explicitly whether FBI_FIFO_RESET belongs in a mid-session reset (the vendor's mid-session reset omits it; only init-time h3InitResetAll uses it), and keep the multi-chip SLI/AA refusal that the SLIAA-GUARD applies to it.

On boot B, read chip 0's 3D registers (0x200104, 0x200110, 0x200208-0x200214, 0x2001ec-0x2001f8, fog) before and after lost_recover outside any game. They are readable, as the 11-12 dump shows, and this answers open question 8 by measurement. If anything the HAL relies on changes, re-send G03's baseline after a reset before re-arming.
On a generation change, also force a texture flush for the bound surfaces (make tex_writes_seen mismatch), not only target/state/TMU/fog.

Make VcrDdEngineRetry try the read-only re-arm first (the chip may already be idle) and request a reset only if that fails. Run the GetDriverInfo retry only after confirming on the bed that dxg holds the devlock there.

Apply the same SLI, live-Glide and exclusive_pid refusals to the existing IOCTL_VCR_RESET_ENGINE / VCR_ESC_RESET_ENGINE path. When amending the README Safety section, keep the phrase 'turns acceleration OFF' that test_vcr_kmd_2d.py:158 pins.

Re-rate G02 as P1 and make G01 a hard dependency for the games_unblocked list, since the realistic post-Glide failure never gives up. Record the stale-exclusive_pid silent no-draw (vcrdd_d3d.c:1859, :1887) as a separate gap.

problems: (Paths are relative to the v56k-bench worktree unless absolute.) The flip changes nothing on .124 today, so it is neither P0 nor P1. Both switches have been set explicitly since 2026-09-28 (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:570 and :620; scripts/fleet/fleet-roster.txt:23), and the 11-12 ring confirms them with 513/16 and 513/18 (voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dplan_1112/reports/onbox.md:71-72). The design concedes this (designs/G20.md:38). Nothing writes these values on its own: miniport/*.c has no VcrDiagSet for D3D32 or D3DBigTex, and the 3dfx panel refuses to write them (scripts/3dfx/3dfxctl/ctl_logic.h:162-166). Every P0 item (G05, G06/G07, G10, G04) is measured and fixed on the armed configuration, and none of them waits for G20.

The claim that 'seven titles cannot run' on a fresh install is overstated, and the design's own table (designs/G20.md:126-130) shows it. Rainbow Six needs neither switch and runs. Thief II runs, on its DX6 path at 640x480 (/mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Thief2/Play Thief 2.bat:13-26). Three entries are inferred, not measured: UT2003 ('CreateTexture failure (inferred)'), Max Payne ('unknown (inferred)') and Halo's need for D3D32. Only two failures are measured without the switches: H&D Deluxe's 'Unable to initialize graphics' (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md:730-736) and UT2004's 'Critical Error' (evidence/silicon/d3d32_step16/step16_run.log:54, d3d32_titles_sweep.json). Halo's white menu (FINDINGS.md:440) was seen with BigTex armed but DXT2/4 not yet listed, so a fully unarmed Halo has never been measured. The failures are not silent either: two raise dialogs, and a boot without the switches lacks 513/16 and 513/18.

The scenarios G20 guards against are remote, and each already has a cheaper hook. A re-image removes vcr-kmd completely, because 3dfx drivers are never installed automatically. Any reinstall therefore goes through tools/deploy_box.py install, which already writes Diag values at install (voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/tools/deploy_box.py:279-281; it writes MaxBootAttempts=2, not the compiled 3), or through the INF, which already sets NOCLOBBER Diag defaults ([vcr.Service] AddReg=vcr.Diag, voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/inf/vcrkmd.inf:73, 78-83). The '.143 V5 5500' case: that card is the second adapter, on AmigaMerlin 3.1-R11 (docs/fleet-inventory.md:168-172; fleet-roster.txt:25), and nothing plans to move it to vcr-kmd. A REGDELETE of Diag is a documented trap (vcr-kmd/README.md:129-131, CLAUDE.md). It would also wipe MaxBootAttempts, LogLevel and the kill switches, and a compiled default restores only two of those values.

The design's rejection of alternative (a) is partly wrong (designs/G20.md:635). It says 'a manual install loses the values', but every install of vcrkmd.inf runs the [vcr.Diag] AddReg, whether through DRVUPDATE or Device Manager. Only deleting the Diag key loses them. Its 'two sources of truth' objection already holds today: deploy_box.py writes MaxBootAttempts=2 against a compiled default of 3.

The design's own end state recreates the risk it guards against. Boots B and C delete .124's explicit values, and the design recommends leaving them absent (designs/G20.md:522, open question 5). The rollback binary it keeps, vcrmp_fda1b8c9.sys (G20.md:497, :519), reads an absent value as off, so a later rollback would silently disarm H&D, UT2004, Halo and Thief II's D3D9 display on the one box that matters. Parts 1-2 (a kernel InForce record, a rewritten library launcher and a fleet push) exist only because those values get deleted.

Part 1 lands new kernel behaviour default-ON (designs/G20.md:361): a registry create and write in VcrFindAdapter on every boot. That conflicts with the lane rule that new kernel behaviour lands default-OFF until proven on silicon, and its only consumer that cannot already see the in-force state is one .bat. Host tools can read the in-force flags today through `vcrctl info` (the flags field, voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/tools/vcrctl.c:193) outside D3D runs.

Scope overlaps two other designs. Part 0 is already owned by G80 Part B, rated P2 there (designs/G80.md:242-243: "G20's 'Part 0' is done here, and G20 keeps only its default flip"). The new d3dprobe caps fields and DXT2/4 tests overlap G74 (designs/G74.md:320 adds DXT2/DXT4), and none of them depends on the flip.

Dependencies are missing. G30 requires G20's D3D32 flip to come after G30 (designs/G30.md:291, :506). G07 wants its chain fix defaulted together with G20's BigTex decision (designs/G07.md:182), because the confetti path (DXT and A8R8G8B8 chains) exists only with D3DBigTex. G20's depends_on lists only G10, G01, G11 and G04.

Boot B's Halo check cannot pass as written. It asks for 'Halo's menu textured, not white' from `halo.exe -timedemo`, but -timedemo goes straight into the cutscene benchmark: the 11-12 frames show space, the canyon and the escape pod, never the menu, and the run did not finish in 485 s (reports/onbox.md:200-209). UT2004's botmatch runs at 4-6 fps and ignores WM_CLOSE (onbox.md:238, :274).

The game runs in boots B and C cost a lot and prove nothing new about G20. They re-run the configuration that has been armed daily since 09-28, at the price of three supervised boots and about 50 CRT mode switches (designs/G20.md:509-511). That is the campaign's scarcest resource, and the P0 items need it. The 'never run' 16 bpp-target texture matrix is new only to d3dprobe: UT2004 and UT2003 drew BigTex DXT at 16 bpp + D16 on 11-12 (onbox.md:162, :237-238), and the 16-bit titles have run on the BigTex path since 09-28.

The P1 rationale (designs/G20.md:599-606) does not meet the definitions. 'A prerequisite for reliability across a re-image' is not 'a prerequisite for P0 work'. The G21 side effect does not apply on .124, and G21 itself is rated P2 for exactly that reason: 'No staged .124 title is known to hit it in the deployed configuration' (designs/G21.md:682-683; also :87, 'Defaulting D3DBigTex on (G20) is not a substitute'). G73 lists the fresh-install control for G20/G21 as an optional boot (designs/G73.md:535), and history §9 puts the drift fix last (reports/history.md:643-662).
corrections: Re-rate G20 from P1 to P2, for a reduced fix only. Rate the compiled-default flip, the InForce record and the Thief II launcher rewrite P3, and defer them until a second vcr-kmd VSA-100 install actually exists.

Replace steps 1-2 and parts 1-2 with an install-time profile: no kernel change and no dedicated .124 boot. Commit .124's chosen Diag profile (D3D32=1, D3DBigTex=7, citing the 09-28 step 16 run and the 11-12 evidence). Make tools/deploy_box.py install REGWRITE those two values and read them back for the V56K HWID, beside its existing MaxBootAttempts, LogLevel and BootAttempts writes (deploy_box.py:279-281).
