That covers a re-arm forgotten after a supervised disarm (README.md:127-131 tells operators to disarm) and a wiped Diag key.

Answer open question 5 the other way: keep .124's values explicit for good. If the compiled flip ever proceeds, its proof boot deletes a value for that boot only and writes it back afterwards, so a rollback to vcrmp_fda1b8c9.sys never disarms the box.

Drop Part 0, which G80 Part B owns (designs/G80.md:243). Move the probe additions into G74; they can run today on the armed configuration. Those additions are dxt2, dxt4, dxt4_decode1, tex8888_2048x1024, the texDXT2/4 caps fields and the texture matrix behind a 16 bpp target.

Correct the gap text. Measured failures without the switches: H&D Deluxe (D3D32) and UT2004 (BigTex). Halo's white menu means DXT2/4 were missing; a fully unarmed Halo has never been measured. Thief II runs, degraded, on DX6 at 640x480. UT2003 and Max Payne are inferred. Rainbow Six is unaffected.

If the P3 flip goes ahead later, change the plan in five ways. Add G30 and G07 to depends_on. Replace the Halo -timedemo check with the staged launcher to the textured main menu, or with dxt4_decode1. Cut the game lists in boots B and C to: the Thief II launcher check, caps --expect, the ring 513/16 and 513/18, and an H&D start (boot C only). Keep InForce default-off behind its own Diag value until proven, or drop it in favour of the install-time values. Count the effort of the Thief II library change at its full fix-loop cost: purge, GAMESYNC, a fullscreen screenshot, and a push to every box that carries the title.

problems: The gap is real only as a fresh-install default, and its size is overstated (KMD = voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd). In code, KMD/miniport/vcrmp.c:238 and :244 default both switches to 0. The HAL then offers DDBD_16 only (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:2079), three texture formats (:2085-2099) and a 256 maximum (:2158). On .124 nothing manifests: the ring shows vcr_info.flags 0x00000f90, i.e. D3D32, BIGTEX, TEXDXT and TEX32 armed (KMD/evidence/d3dplan_1112/onbox/ring_start.txt:69-70). caps_124.txt reports MaxTexture 2048, tex8888 and DXT available, and hal_fullscreen X8R8G8B8 = 1. Of the 'seven titles': Rainbow Six is unblocked by neither switch. Thief II only degrades to DX6 at 640x480 (shipped Play Thief 2.bat:13-24). UT2003 and Max Payne are inferred. Three fresh-install failures are confirmed: H&D, UT2004 ('Critical Error' with D3D32 alone, step16_run.log:54) and Halo (white menu without DXT2/4, FINDINGS.md:439-441).

The design overstates how proven the defaulted configuration is ('proven on .124 and used daily since 2026-09-28', G20.md §5 and §9). The switches have been armed since 09-28, but the behaviour step 1 makes default arrived only on 11-08 with vcrdd 95678704 (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:139-170): every texture placed by mipchain_ext (vcrdd_d3d.c:381-391), and the 16/16-in-32 pair (vcr_rtfmt.h:70-84). JK, MotS, Shogo, SS2, Thief Gold and R6 were seen only at menus or intros. The only in-game frames on this configuration (onbox.md §4, 11-12) show confetti noise, dark lightmaps and white areas. G20 §1 also says every BigTex run on record was at a 32 bpp target. That is wrong: UT2003 at 640x480x16 and UT2004 at 1280x960x16 with D16 ran BigTex behind 16 bpp targets on 11-12.

Step 2 does change the 16 bpp lane, contrary to §4.5 and §9 ('A 16 bpp target's register writes are identical whatever the switch says'). With rt32, dwZBufferBitDepths gains DDBD_32 and GUID_ZPixelFormats gains D24X8 and D24S8 at every desktop (vcrdd_d3d.c:2055-2057, :2188; vcr_rtfmt.h:195-197). A DX5-7 title that takes the deepest Z (the Rainbow Six pattern, vcr_rtfmt.h:70-77) then draws 16/16-in-32. It writes the same registers, but with auxBufferStride = BS_LINEAR_STRIDE(4*w) (vcr_3dseq.h:74), and its Z uses twice the memory. A fresh install today gives those titles D16 only. The 16/16-in-32 path is proven on one title, on one image (be58b7d).

'Step 1 also fixes G21 on the VSA-100' is only half true, and it conflicts with G21's own design. G21 finds two defects that exist on both paths: a 16 bpp texture whose top level is 1x1 is sampled 8 bytes early, and render-target textures keep DirectDraw's 4-byte placement (G21.md §1 items 1 and 3; vcrdd_d3d.c:387-391). G21 explicitly rejects 'default D3DBigTex on (G20)' as a substitute (G21.md:87, :170) and proposes its own Diag\D3DTexPlace. The plan now has two designs claiming the same fix.

The VRAM figures are stale, and one address bit is unprobed. .124 runs its 256 MB VBIOS mode: chip 0's DirectDraw heap is 0-0x3ed3000 (64332 KB), and 0-0x3aff000 at 1280x1024x32 (onbox/ring_after_probe_i_decoded.txt:53; ring_after_modeseq_decoded.txt:89), not 27 MB (KMD/README.md:111, :496). So G20's rationale for tex8888_2048x1024 ('fill 23 of the 27 MB heap') and its risk line ('1600x1200x32 ~23 of 27 MB') are wrong for .124; they hold only for a VSA-100 with 32 MB per chip. More important: half of .124's heap needs address bit 25. The munge carries it in register bit 1 (common/vcr_texlod.c:79-82, which matches H3DEFS.H SST_TEXTURE_ADDRESS), but no probe has exercised it, because texhigh fills only 20 MB (tools/d3dprobe.c:861-866). Step 1 makes that munged base the default for every texture.

The design contradicts itself on gating. §4.4 (G20.md:306-317) lists G11's zpair contract and G04's attended E0 Max Payne run as 'Preconditions' of step 2, while §10 (G20.md:584-585) calls both 'soft'. The Max Payne hard freeze happened in exactly the armed 1/7 configuration that step 2 would ship (history.md §4.1). The 11-11 readiness rounds mark 13 .124 D3D titles 'blk' because of it (history.md:410-413). Step 2 also needs G10's Diag\D3DSafe bit 3, which is default 0 (G10.md §0), to become default-on first. Proving that change needs its own boot, which G20's one-change-per-boot schedule does not include.

Proof boots B and C change nothing behaviourally: a deleted value means the same 1/7 that boot A sets explicitly. Yet they schedule about 22 and 20 CRT mode switches (G20.md:507-511): UT2004, UT2003, Halo and JK in boot B; H&D, Halo, R6 and an attended Max Payne in boot C. Those runs re-test G05, G06 and G04, not G20's 'absent means on'. Putting Max Payne in boot C would turn a G04 freeze into a failed G20 proof.

InForce records what the miniport hands over, not what the HAL offers. It ignores three cases: Diag\D3D = 0 (VCR_INFO_F_NO_D3D, vcrmp.c:444); a 2D give-up, where g2d_ok = 0 withdraws the whole HAL (vcrdd_d3d.c:2058, :2136; onbox-02); and an older vcrdd.dll. The proposed launcher lines read only InForce\D3D32 and InForce\D3DBigTex (G20.md:243-245), although the key also carries D3D. This is no regression against the current Diag-reading block. It does fall short of the design's own FINDINGS lesson: read the effect, not the switch.

The 804 d=2 'hand-made key' rule needs a driver-static once-per-boot flag. FindAdapter can run more than once in a boot: the INF binds PCI\VEN_121A&DEV_0009 generically with MaximumNumberOfDevices = 4 (inf/vcrkmd.inf:35, :62), so a PnP stop/start or another VSA-100 devnode (a V5 5500's second chip, unconfirmed) calls it again. That call opens the volatile key the same boot created and logs a false WARN. A real hand-made non-volatile key stays non-volatile, because ZwCreateKey only opens it, and the WARN lives only in the ring, which is lost at reboot.

Tooling and test details. d3dprobe_run.py has no --pace option; the 11-12 run used evidence/d3dplan_1112/onbox/d3dprobe_paced.py. The @bigtex alias collides in name with the existing default-list test 'bigtex', a 256x256 checker (tools/d3dprobe.c:955-956). The README header 'Every switch here is off when absent' (README.md:90) is already false today: rows 102, 116 and 117 say default ON. For MOVED_DIAG, D3DBigTex must leave NEW_DIAG, or dict(BASE_DIAG, **NEW_DIAG, ..., **MOVED_DIAG) raises TypeError (test_vcr_kmd_integration.py:104; verified). problems: The code gap is real: KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1905-1910 answers 1 pass / DD_OK to every set, and it is registered at :2143. The claimed impact is not. Halo (G15.md:81, :475, :459). The only ValidateDevice call in halo.exe (0x5adef0) is inside the statically linked ID3DXEffect::ValidateTechnique (vtable slot 61 = 0x5add56). Halo's fx.bin loader (0x52fa35-0x52fa66, 122 effects) calls 0x52f780 for each effect. On a device without pixel shaders, that routine looks up the technique 'TDefault_no_ps' by name (0x52f84c) and validates it (0x52f8a5). A failure returns 0 (0x52f8c8). The loader then releases every effect (0x52fa6a-0x52fa8f) and raises the 'shaders\fx.bin' error (0x52fb26-0x52fb3b, routine 0x57ea70). FindNextValidTechnique (0x52f88d) runs only when that technique is absent. So a single refusal means Halo cannot load its shaders. The plan expects 'D3DX falls back' or 'may lose an effect'; neither happens. G17.md:22-36 attributes the glow square to X8R8G8B8, so the link to G17 does not hold. Halo already runs its timedemo on today's answer (onbox/session_log.md:21).

problems: The gap is confirmed in the source and in the deployed binary. vcrdd_d3d.c:1905-1910 never reads the context. In the deployed vcrdd.dll (md5 95678704, equal to out/vcrdd.dll), _D3d_ValidateTextureStageState@4 at 0x1ac40 is just `movl $1,0xc(%eax); movl $0,0x10(%eax); mov $1,%eax`. Nothing else covers for it: d3d8.dll's DX7-DDI ValidateDevice (0x6d9e0f70) runs the texture update at 0x6d9dab70, flushes via *0x2c, calls the thunk via *0x174, copies dwNumPasses, and throws any negative ddrval straight back to the app.

The design's open question 1 is settled by disassembly, and the answer undercuts its stage-2 work: D3D8 and D3D9 never send stage >= wMaxTextureBlendStages (2) to our DX7 DDI.
- d3d8 SetTextureStageStateI: 0x6d9d4b28 `cmp 0x37c(%esi),%edi; jae` skips the DDI SetTSS. 0x37c is caps.MaxTextureBlendStages (set at 0x6d9dbf07; device+0x40 is a D3DCAPS8, copied by 0x6d9ad9b0 with `rep movsl` of 0x35 dwords).
- The d3d8 texture-bind loop (0x6d9dabbf) uses the same bound.
- Every d3d9 DDI SetTSS (0x4fe73070, 0x4fe74140, 0x4fe5c760, 0x4fe784e0) starts with `cmp 0x20a0(%eax),%ecx; jae`. 0x20a0 holds MaxTextureBlendStages unless the device has PS 2.0 (0x4fe5bf57-77).
- Consequence: TOOMANYOPERATIONS can never reach Max Payne, Halo, NewDark-D3D9, BF1942 or H&D. The tss2 walker record, the stage-2 default, the stage-2 counters and the probe's 3-stage cell only matter to DX6/DX7 apps. No staged caller on .124 uses more than 2 stages: Thief Gold's 5 modes and NewDark's 8 are all 1-2 stages. UE1's D3DDrv (the PRS 12099 3-stage app) makes 0 Device7 +0x98 calls, against 70-75 SetTSS calls in UT436, Deus Ex and Unreal Gold.
- Also: d3d8's DX7 SetTSS 0x6d9e11c0 drops any TSS index >= 24 (the limit getter 0x6d9e2120 returns 0x18), so ARG0 and RESULTARG never arrive from D3D8. D3D9's limit is 0x21 (0x4fe5dad0), so they can arrive from D3D9.

The walker change has a trap that would break the proven path. vcrdd_d3d.c:1597 is `DWORD *th = stage == 0 ? &c->tex_handle : &c->tex_handle1;`, so every stage other than 0 points at tex_handle1. Stage 2 is safe today only because the `!ts` check at :1598 skips it. The obvious way to do §5.3 (`ts = ... stage == 2 ? c->tss2`) would let a stage-2 TEXTUREMAP overwrite stage 1's handle and set dirty, which changes drawing for any DX6/DX7 app that binds a stage-2 texture. The specified Python test only checks for 'no c->dirty = 1', so it would not catch this.

Max Payne has a FATAL validation path that the design leaves out; §3 says a refusal only 'splits the material into passes'.
- In e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll at 0x10005650, when the count of layers already in the pass is 0, the code jumps to 0x100056e4. It logs ' FATAL ERROR: failed to validate even one layer' (0x10072a94), then calls _CxxThrowException (stub 0x10055910 jumps through the import at 0x1008996c). The throw carries P_DriverException_Failed with 'Failed to validate material' (catchable types at 0x10069ad8).
- Part A cannot predict this. Under today's lenient answer Max Payne never searches its alternatives ('trying DIFFUSE_MUL', 'no more alternatives'), so the would-refuse log shows only first choices.

Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe is a confirmed caller with textures bound, but §3 lists it as 'none found / undetermined'. The design scanned igraph2.dll only; G31.md:173 already flagged this. The real calls are in Bin/i3d2.dll:
- 0x1005f320: stage-0 COLOROP=MODULATE2X with SetTexture(0), then ValidateDevice; on OK with 1 pass it sets flag 0x40.
- 0x10060388: stage 0 SELECTARG1 and stage 1 MODULATE, both textures bound; sets flag 0x10000000.
- 0x100603e6: stage-1 MODULATE2X; sets flag 0x20000000.
- The other 4 raw +0x100 hits are other interfaces: 0x10004f83 passes 2 args, 0x1009c1c7 and 0x1009c1e5 pass 0, and 0x10074c9a tests %al.
This is a staged .124 title and the clearest Part B case: today it is told MODULATE2X works, and the HAL draws it as MODULATE.

NewDark's legacy DX6 display has fatal validations that cannot be overridden, and the design's contingency does not reach them. In Thief2.exe (md5 1109955d) the IDirect3DDevice3 at 0x9d80f0 is validated through +0xa4 at:
- 0x5eb6e6 (error 0x10), 0x5eb760 (0x11) and 0x5ee07c (0x12): each sets 0x9d81a0 and returns 0;
- 0x5ee1ac: on failure jumps to the 0x5ee09b `return 0` epilogue.
None of these checks d3d_disp_forcevalid. The D3D9 sites do (0x606b45-4d calls 0x6a4ea0 with 0x72f9c8). The DX6 display is what newdark_display_swap picks on every vcr-kmd box without D3D32=1 and D3DBigTex bits 0+2, which is the default install. Step 2 only ever runs the D3D9 path, so this path is never measured.

System Shock 2 is filed as 'undetermined', but the reason is known. shock2.exe is the SafeDisc v1 loader and the game itself is the encrypted SHOCK2.ICD, so no D3D calls can be seen statically. It is the 1999 Dark engine, so Thief Gold's fatal Device3 validations with no override are likely (inferred). The rollout gate leaves out both SS2 and H&D.

The Diag plumbing and the deploy step are incomplete.
- D3DFeat is read by the miniport, but §8 only swaps vcrdd.dll. Part B can never arm without the new vcrmp.sys.
- vcrdd_2d.c:436 declares `vcr_info info;` without zeroing it, and vcrmp.c:794-797 copies only min(OutputBufferLength, the old sizeof). With an older miniport the appended d3dfeat is stack garbage and could arm bit 0. 'Size checked by the reader' is stated but no test covers it.

The 5.2 DISABLE row contradicts the soundness test in 7.1. color_path handles colour (:690) and alpha (:725-742) separately. With stage-0 COLOROP=DISABLE, a texture bound, and ALPHAOP=SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) (D3D's stage-0 default), it selects CP_ASEL_TMU and sets CP_TEXTURE, so texture alpha is drawn. D3D (refrast) stops at a disabled stage 0 and outputs diffuse, alpha included. The vendor's count is 0, so the answer is OK, and 'OK implies drawn as D3D defines' fails. This is a drawing bug the validator cannot refuse its way out of.

The verdict field added to log_combo is unreliable. Its dedupe hash covers only tss1 COLOROP/ALPHAOP (vcrdd_d3d.c:890), and stage1_combine gives TM_TC_MULT for both MODULATE(T,C) (exact) and MODULATE(T,D) (refused). Two such sets are logged once, under the first set's verdict.

The design differs from the vendor in two cases and leaves one case undefined.
- D6MT.C:3245-3249 also stops the count on an unbound stage whose ALPHA op is BLENDTEXTUREALPHA(PM); §5.1 counts colour ops only.
- D6MT.C:3672-3751 returns WRONGTEXTUREFORMAT when a counted stage's alpha arguments sample TEXTURE with no valid handle. §5.2 defines no verdict for that case, and our HAL draws iterated alpha there (:725).

The d3dprobe method is weak in four places.
- 'SRCALPHA/ZERO over black to read alpha as colour' actually yields rgb×a; with a ZERO dest factor the background is irrelevant. Alpha errors get scaled down by the texel colour and lost in 565 quantisation.
- Its expected answers come from vcr_tssval fed the app-side stages, so the 3-stage cell will 'fail' armed by construction.
- It reads D3DFeat from the registry, which can differ from the value the driver read at boot.
- ±10 at 16 bpp is tighter than the existing tex2* tolerance of 14.

'Chip-independent' holds for Voodoo3 and VSA-100 (2 TMUs) but not for Banshee (1 TMU). The caps always advertise 2 stages (vcrdd_d3d.c:2169-2170) and compute_regs programs TMU1, so on a Banshee every counted textured stage 1 cannot be drawn. This is minor: no Banshee runs the D3D lane.

Part A does not leave the proven path untouched. Moving color_path and stage1_combine into vcr_cmb_legacy.h changes the binary. 'Safe to land default-on' therefore has to wait for the silicon re-run of the default d3dprobe matrix.

problems: CONFIRMED GAP: the gap is real in our code as deployed (out/vcrdd.dll md5 95678704 = the source at 481acfd/be58b7d). set_rs special-cases only TEXTUREHANDLE (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1393-1406). tex_view and tex_view_ext read only TSS 13/14/16/17/18 (:779, :788-795, :814, :826-833). ctx_defaults leaves stage 0 at POINT/POINT, WRAP, MODULATE with alpha SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) (:1138-1146). TSS 12 is stored but never read (:1591-1611). The legacy caps are 0xcb/0x17 (:2036-2043; caps_124 TextureFilterCaps 03010317). A case-insensitive grep finds no legacy mapping anywhere in display/, include/ or common/. The runtime does not do the mapping either: XP d3dim.dll's app-facing SetRenderState is Device2 vtable slot 23 = 0x6d921737, and Device3 slot 22 is a thunk at 0x6d9161cd that jumps to it. It forwards states 17/18/21/3/44/45 as raw op-8 tokens through 0x6d91a6d8. Its cache store 0x6d921556 maps nothing; only WRAPU/V get special handling.

CONFIRMED HW AND VENDOR: H5 INCLUDE/H3DEFS.H:253-260 defines TMINFILTER BIT(1), TMAGFILTER BIT(2), TCLAMPS BIT(6) and TCLAMPT BIT(7), which equal include/vcr_3dregs.h TM_*. h5 Glide gtex.c:2405-2406 writes the same bits. vcrdd_3d.c:116/124 write tDetail = 0 on every textured draw, so a stale SST_TFILTER_SEPARATE (H3DEFS.H:707) cannot override them. I recomputed every fbzColorPath/textureMode value in design §4.6 (0x0c002401, 0x0c482405, 0x0c000005, 0x0c007201, 0x0c004001, 0x08241a0f, 0x08241ac9) and all are correct. The vendor and Microsoft tables match the design: VH5/D3RSTATE.C:2177-2196, 2263-2296, 2674-2720, 2860-2945; D7DP2.C:1602-1605; MSP2 d3dstate.c:62-66, 583-650, 1836. The legacy_blend RGB expectations also check out.

CONFIRMED VISUAL: MotS is point-sampled. My crop of FBS/mots_game.png at x 940-1100, y 200-320 shows hard texel blocks. Neither MotS nor JK has a filtering option in its Display menu (FBS/mots_display.png, jkdf2_display.png), so visual-06 is right and games-20/21 are wrong. Whether JK/MotS actually request LINEAR is still unproven; Phase 0 decides that.

WRONG RUNTIME PREMISE (design §2 item 2, finding 1, §4.2 'every receipt' rationale, open question 4). The cited RS 1-135 + TSS re-send loop (d3dim 0x6d922344-0x6d92239c) is inside Device3::SetRenderTarget (vtable slot 14 = 0x6d921fb5). It sits in the branch taken only when the DDI level [this+0xf58] is below 3 (`cmpl $0x3,0xf4c(%esi); jl` at 0x6d922178). Our HAL advertises D3DDEVCAPS_DRAWPRIMITIVES2EX (vcrdd_d3d.c:2066-2070), which makes d3dim set DDI 3 (0x6d91642f / 0x6d916455). SetRenderTarget then emits only a DP2 SETRENDERTARGET token (0x6d91b14f, op 0x29). That loop never runs on our HAL.

ACTUAL DEVICE-CREATION ORDER: device creation does ContextCreate (0x6d915e9c -> 0x6d91834c -> 0x6d91816a), then the default-state init 0x6d913654 (called at 0x6d9160de), which runs in this order:
- It invalidates the RS cache (rep stos -1 at 0x6d9136d8-e6) and the TSS cache (0x6d913ade-e9).
- It sends the RS defaults through Device2::SetRenderState. States 17, 18 and 21 are skipped.
- It sends the TSS defaults for every stage through SetTextureStageState (0x6d91b516). For stage 0 that is ALPHAOP = SELECTARG1(TEXTURE).
- LAST it sends RS 17 = NEAREST, 18 = NEAREST and 21 = MODULATE (0x6d913c57-72).

Both writers append to one DP2 buffer (op 8 at 0x6d91a6d8, op 0x19 at 0x6d91ac84, cursor +0x1e24). So with the bit on, every d3dim (DX3/5/6) context ends creation with ALPHAOP = 0x7ffffffe. Open question 4's prediction, 'alpha 1.0 as today', is the opposite of what the binary does.

REDUNDANCY FILTERS: d3dim drops a SetRenderState whose value equals its cache when DDI >= 2 (0x6d92188b-0x6d9218a6). SetTextureStageState drops redundant values the same way (0x6d91b548-4c). The two caches are independent: the legacy-to-TSS mapping exists only in the driver. Consequences:
- (a) A DX6 title's explicit SetTextureStageState(0, ALPHAOP, SELECTARG1) never reaches us, so the sentinel installed at creation persists in every Device3 title: Thief Gold, SS2, Shogo, AvP and Thief II DX6. That holds whether or not the title itself sends legacy states.
- (b) Open question 1 is answered: redundant app SetRenderState calls are filtered. Execute-buffer STATERENDER is not filtered (0x6d91d325 drops only override-locked states).
- (c) legacy_order (MODULATE, then TSS ALPHAOP SELECTARG1, then MODULATE) reads (32,0,0) three times on a CORRECT driver; the design expects (128,0,0) then (32,0,0).
- (d) legacy_addr's 'ADDRESSV = WRAP' step is filtered, because d3dim's cache store does not mirror RS 3 into 44/45. V stays CLAMP on a correct driver.
- (e) The NEAREST control in legacy_mag, and the tss_address last-writer steps, break if they reset state through the other API.

The 86Box step 0 and boot B would then report correct drivers as failing.

REGRESSION RISK NOT ACKNOWLEDGED: 3dfx enabled the legacy-MODULATE alpha override on Win9x only on 11/09/99 (VH5/D6MT.C:136-137, rev 1.19). That is after Thief (1998) and SS2 (Aug 1999) shipped, so DX6 titles were validated on 3dfx drivers without the rule. Installing the rule in every DX6 context, through the runtime's own creation-time MODULATE, can make an alpha-less texture translucent or invisible wherever blending or alpha test is on and vertex alpha is below 255. The design classifies DX6 titles as affected only 'if Phase 0 shows legacy states', and every d3dim context will show them.

NOT A FAITHFUL VENDOR MIRROR: 3dfx clears the legacy flag on ANY COLOROP/COLORARG1/COLORARG2/ALPHAOP/ALPHAARG1/ALPHAARG2 TSS write, on any stage (VH5/D7DP2.C:1608-1616, 1737-1746; D6DP2.C:1496-1505). The design replaces the sentinel only on a stage-0 ALPHAOP write. Because d3dim drops redundant ALPHAOP writes, a DX6 title that drives COLOROP or the arguments through TSS leaves legacy mode under 3dfx but stays in it under G08.

OPEN QUESTION 3 IS ANSWERABLE NOW:
- d3dim's CreateContext passes dwhContext = [obj+4] - 1. That is 0, 1 or 2 for IDirect3DDevice, Device2 and Device3 (0x6d918204-19). [obj+4] is the interface version; compare the TEXTUREPERSPECTIVE default branch at 0x6d913733.
- d3dim700 passes 3 (0x7394e965).
- Together these are 3dfx's documented numbering '0=DX3, 1=DX5, 2=DX6, 3=DX7, 4=DX8' (VH5/D3CONTXT.C:356-357).

Still unverified: whether ddraw and dxg carry the value to the kernel driver. 3dfx's NT build computes it but stores it only in the non-WINNT branch (D3CONTXT.C:436-443). So scoping by interface version should be the primary scope, not the fallback.

GRADUATION CONDITION 3 IS UNSOUND:
- lgc_misc 0x100 is set by the runtime at creation in every DX5/6 context, so it says nothing about an application mixing APIs.
- For D3D7/8/9 contexts it misses a legacy token that no TSS token follows, which would install the mapping silently. d3dim700 has a re-send loop over render states 2-135 (0x7394f28c, reached by pointer from a vtable, trigger unknown).
- 'Inert by construction' therefore does not follow.
SCOPING TRAP: D3DTSS_ADDRESS (12) is a valid DX7 texture-stage state, removed only in DX8. If the RS mapping is scoped to legacy contexts, the 12 -> 13/14 copy must stay universal.

MIXED-API HAZARD (vendor-consistent but untested): after a legacy TEXTUREMAG = LINEAR, a Device3 title's SetTextureStageState(0, MAGFILTER, POINT) for its HUD is dropped by d3dim, whose TSS cache still holds POINT. The HUD then stays bilinear. ADDRESS against ADDRESSU/V diverges the same way. Nothing in the boot-B checks looks for blurred HUD or text, or for clamp/wrap edges.

CAPS EXPOSURE UNDERSTATED: the two added bits (DECALALPHA, MIPLINEAR) are visible to IDirect3DDevice7 apps as well, because the DX7 headers still define them. They are harmless, since both are drawn correctly, but 'D3D8/9 cannot see it' is the wrong boundary. Advertising MIPLINEAR can also change a DX5 title's code path (for example creating mip chains, about +33% texture memory), not only its filtering.

MINOR:
- set_rs returns before any work for st >= 256 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1396-1397). The 0x40 override counter must sit before that return.
- d3dim already converts WRAPU/V into D3DRENDERSTATE_WRAP0 (RS 128) and sends both on DP2 drivers (0x6d9217b7-0x6d921811). That is relevant to G86, not a G08 defect.
- Unverified: whether XP's d3d8 or d3d9 init sends RS 17/18/21. No `push 0x2; push 0x15` pair was found in d3d8.dll. The d3dprobe gate in boot B still covers it.

- Give it its own D3DFeat sub-bit, or install it only in DX3/DX5 contexts (hctx_in 0 or 1), where the application has no TSS API.
- In DX6 contexts, map MODULATE's alpha to plain SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) until in-game evidence on .124 says otherwise.
- Cite VH5/D6MT.C:136-137 (rule enabled on Win9x 11/09/99) as the reason.

Either mirror 3dfx's exit rule (any COLOROP/COLORARG1/COLORARG2/ALPHAOP/ALPHAARG1/ALPHAARG2 TSS token on stage 0 or 1 ends legacy-MODULATE mode), or state why the narrower DDK wording (stage-0 ALPHAOP only) was kept. Add the case to test_vcr_kmd_legacy.c, asserting both values.

Make scoping by interface version the primary scope:
- Phase 0 first proves that ContextCreate's incoming dwhContext reaches the kernel. Expect 0, 1 or 2 from d3dim, 3 from d3dim700 and 4 or more from d3d8/9.
- Then apply the legacy RS mapping only when hctx_in is 2 or less.
- Keep the TSS 12 -> 13/14 copy universal.
- Use EXECUTEBUFFER-flag scoping only if the value does not arrive.

Replace graduation condition 3 with 'zero legacy texture tokens (lgc_n of rs 3/17/18/21/44/45) in every context with hctx_in of 3 or more'. Delete the '0x100 => inert by construction' argument, and note that d3dim sets 0x100 at creation in every DX5/6 context.

Fix the DX5/DX6 probe for d3dim's per-API redundancy caches:
- Every step must change the value as that API's cache sees it:
  - legacy_order: MAPBLEND DECAL -> MODULATE; TSS ALPHAOP MODULATE -> SELECTARG1; MAPBLEND DECAL -> MODULATE.
  - legacy_addr: set ADDRESSV to CLAMP before setting it to WRAP.
  - Return to NEAREST through TEXTUREMAG, not through TSS.
- Record that with the bit on, the untouched default already reads (32,0,0) for a T565 + vertex-alpha-64 + blend draw.
- Add a 'DX6 TSS-only, no legacy calls' case that measures this effect at creation.
Correct the caps statement: DECALALPHA and MIPLINEAR are visible to DX5-7 applications, including Device7. Add the code-path risk (a DX5 title may now create mip chains) to the risk table.
In the design document, answer open questions 1, 3 and 4 with the addresses above. Leave two unknowns open: d3dim700's 0x7394f28c re-send trigger, and whether dwhContext passes through to the kernel.

Minor:
- Count rs >= 256 override tokens before set_rs's early return at vcrdd_d3d.c:1396.
- Tell G86 that the runtime already sends WRAP0 (RS 128) for WRAPU/V on DP2 drivers. Raw 5/6 matter only for execute-buffer pass-through.

problems: The games list is overstated: four of the named DX6 titles never send the legacy texture states. Thief Gold sets MAG/MIN through SetTextureStageState (THIEF.EXE: edi=2 at 0x5738bc, TSS 16/17 at 0x573ac0/0x573adb). Per texture it switches to POINT only for colour-keyed textures (0x574ee6-0x574f30), and no SetRenderState call passes an immediate 3/17/18/21/44/45. NewDark's DX6 display does the same (Thief2.exe 0x5ea060-0x5ea0cb; globals 0x78a258/0x78a25c = 2 in .data; setter 0x5ea140), and so does Shogo's d3d.ren (TSS 16/17/18 at 0x10015e7f-0x10015f8b). SS2 runs the same lgd3d (inferred: its ICD is encrypted). G08 cannot change any of them, yet G08.md:535-542 and visual.md V-06 'Affected' list them.

visual-06's Thief II DX6 frame is not G08 evidence, and it may count against G08's destination path. NewDark DX6 asks for LINEAR through TSS by default (mode global 0x78a268 = 1). Yet FBS/thief2_c2.png (640x480x16; the DX6 path per docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:628) shows hard texel blocks on the ground. The moon is a keyed sprite, which lgd3d point-samples on purpose. The only silicon proof that TSS LINEAR reaches the TMU is the 32 bpp D3D9 frame, and no d3dprobe test checks bilinear: tools/d3dprobe.c sets POINT everywhere, and only perf (:1511) uses LINEAR, unchecked.

Open question 8 and boot-A Outcome A2 (G08.md:484-485) are already answered by the binaries, and the answer is A1. JK.EXE sets its render flags to 0x19b3 (0x42961c). It clears the 0x180 LINEAR bits only when the chosen device is not a HAL (0x401abd-0x401ad2; record field 0 = hal->dcmColorModel != 0, set at 0x42bddc-0x42bdf5), and writes TEXTUREMAG/MIN = D3DFILTER_LINEAR (0x42b7e9/0x42b801). MotS is identical (0x42c7dc, 0x401bed-0x401c02, 0x42e9a9/0x42e9c1). Neither binary has a filtering option ('bilin'/'filter' strings absent; neither Display menu has one). With set_rs ignoring 17/18 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1393-1406) and the point-sampled frames, the JK/MotS filtering defect is proven, not inferred. games.md:397-400's 'JK's own option' is refuted.

The translucency impact is understated as 'possibly'. JK gives translucent faces vertex alpha 0x5a and flag 0x200 (0x43b6d8-0x43b6ec), and adds 0x400 when the device reports TEXTURECAPS_ALPHA (0x43b831-0x43b849). Its per-batch emitter (0x429fd8-0x42a08b) then sends SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, ALPHABLENDENABLE and TEXTUREMAPBLEND MODULATEALPHA or MODULATE. MotS is identical (0x43f69d, 0x43f82b). Today stage-0 alpha is SELECTARG1(TEXTURE) (vcrdd_d3d.c:1141), so these faces draw opaque wherever the texture has no alpha. Opaque faces carry alpha 0xff (0x43b6f1), so the fix cannot trip JK's always-on ALPHATEST NOTEQUAL (0x42b8dc-0x42b8f7).

Rainbow Six is not an execute-buffer title (G08.md:102, :537). RainbowSix.exe writes no execute-buffer STATERENDER instructions; it sends the legacy states through vtable+0x5c, i.e. IDirect3DDevice2::SetRenderState. Wrappers: 0x47ad90 (MAG/MIN 1-6) and 0x47ae90 (MAPBLEND 1-8). Constant callers: LINEAR at 0x405084/0x48c916, MIPLINEAR at 0x48c84e (objects flagged at +0x84), NEAREST at 0x471564, MODULATE at 0x47156d. So whether its states arrive depends on open question 1 (runtime forwarding), its MIPLINEAR objects depend on G07, and it has never been seen in game on .124.

The legacy-MODULATE sentinel kept in tss[ALPHAOP] (G08.md:151, :243-249) is overwritten by the runtime's TSS init, which the design itself shows follows the device-creation render-state stream (G08.md:111-113). Any title that relies on the default MODULATE therefore never gets the rule. AvP is such a title: its execute buffers write states 1,4,8,9,14,17,18,19,20,23,26,27 and never 21 (filter switch at 0x4cfbfc-0x4cfc82). 3dfx avoids this: it keeps the flag in pRc->texMapBlend, which only TEXTUREMAPBLEND writes (VH5/D3RSTATE.C:2898-2905), and applies it regardless of TS[0].alphaOp (VH5/D6MT.C:4816).

About half of the scope has no staged .124 consumer:
- TEXTUREADDRESS/U/V: none of JK, MotS, R6 or AvP sends 3/44/45.
- D3DTSS_ADDRESS 12: no DX6 TSS title sends it; Thief sends ADDRESSU 13 instead.
- DECAL/COPY/ADD/DECALALPHA/MASK: JK/MotS use only MODULATE/MODULATEALPHA, R6's only constant is MODULATE, and AvP sends none.
- The inert mirrors.
- The DECALALPHA/MIPLINEAR caps bits: JK never reads filter caps, R6 picks MIPLINEAR with no caps check, and AvP uses only NEAREST/LINEAR.
These parts are P3 yet carry roughly half the probe and test effort. The MIPLINEAR cap can also steer a DX5/6 title that reads caps onto mip chains (G07 exposure) for no measured gain.

The in-game register proof does not survive in the ring. log_combo is an INFO event (vcrdd_d3d.c:905), but at the default LogLevel 3 the 1024-entry ring fills with DEBUG CreateSurfaceEx events. The ring_decoded.txt of onbox/games/UT2004_botmatch, UT2003_flyby and Halo_timedemo each hold 0 combine events and 1008-1013 DEBUG D3D events; only the final 'context gone' line survives. 'The ring's cp/tm match section 4.6' therefore works for a short probe run and fails for a game.

The Dark-engine titles get the wrong pass criterion and the wrong role. Boot-B step 5 expects Thief Gold/SS2's 'moon and walls bilinear' (G08.md:499-500), but lgd3d point-samples keyed textures by design and takes its filters from TSS. These titles are regression controls for the mapping, and default-ON condition 3 (G08.md:351-352) covers only D3D7/8/9 contexts. If d3dim.dll re-sends its render-state defaults after an app's TSS, an unconditional mapping would clobber Thief's filters. That is exactly the risk the controls should catch.

JK/MotS get no positive in-game translucency check: boot B only asks that translucent surfaces be 'not worse' (G08.md:497). The Phase 0 counters record token values, not whether the fix changes pixels. MODULATE (2) is also the opaque-face value, so the counters cannot show the translucent cases.

Making G75 a hard dependency (G08.md:75, :523-524) puts a new DX5/DX6 probe on the critical path of a CPU-only state mapping. The destination path can be proven with d3dprobe controls that need no driver change. The mapping can be proven with host tests plus a JK/MotS in-game run.

Minor: 'D3D8/9 titles cannot see the change' (G08.md:57-58) is inaccurate. The D3D8 runtime passes the legacy low byte through (caps_124.txt: TextureFilterCaps 03010317, which would become 0x1f). The bits are only undefined in d3d8caps.h, so the risk is negligible.
corrections:
Re-grade games_unblocked by evidence:
- Certain: Jedi Knight DF2 and Mysteries of the Sith, which run D3D at 1280x960x16 on .124 (filtering in every scene, plus translucent faces).
- Likely: Rainbow Six (Device2; pending open question 1 and a first in-game run; G07 for its MIPLINEAR objects).
- Filter-only, after G71: AvP.
- Remove Thief Gold, System Shock 2, Shogo, Thief II DX6 and H&D; they become regression controls.
- Half-Life, Descent 3 and Turok 2's D3D renderers are unused on .124 (P3).

Split the item:
- Core (P1, Diag\D3DFeat bit 1): TEXTUREMAG/MIN mapped to MAG/MIN(/MIP)FILTER, and TEXTUREMAPBLEND with the legacy MODULATE alpha rule. Keep the full eight-mode table (cheap, host-tested), but give probe coverage only to MODULATE and MODULATEALPHA.
- Follow-up (P3, its own bit or later): TEXTUREADDRESS/U/V, D3DTSS_ADDRESS, the inert mirrors, and the DECALALPHA/MIPLINEAR caps bits.

Keep the legacy-MODULATE state in a per-context flag with 3dfx semantics: set by rs21 = MODULATE, cleared only by another rs21 value. Resolve it in color_path whenever stage-0 alpha selects TEXTURE from an alpha-less texture. Do not store it in tss[ALPHAOP], where the runtime's TSS init erases it before AvP-style titles draw. Add a native test for that ordering: render-state MODULATE, then the runtime's TSS init (ALPHAOP SELECTARG1(TEXTURE)), then a draw, must give iterated alpha.

Before any driver change, add the d3dprobe bilinear and clamp controls and run them on the deployed 95678704 at 640x480x16 and 1280x960x16, on a clean engine per G01 (no reboot needed). Treat the result as the go/no-go for G08's destination path; it also explains or refutes the Thief II DX6 texel blocks.
Close open question 8 with the JK/MotS addresses and drop Outcome A2 for those two titles. Keep Phase 0 for Rainbow Six (open question 1) and for the DX6/D3D8 controls.

Make the in-game proof objective. Either set LogLevel=2 in the verification boot (boot A, together with the deploy), or add two values to the context-end Phase 0 events: the OR of textureMode filter bits drawn, and a count of draws where the legacy MODULATE resolved to iterated alpha with alpha blending on. The JK/MotS pass is then: tm filter bits 0x6 set, that count above 0, and the screenshots.

Add an in-game translucent-face check for JK and MotS (a window, force field or water face): translucent with the bit on, opaque with it off. Bilinear filtering on their alpha-tested 1555 cutouts gives the usual edge fringes; record that as expected, not as a regression. JK/MotS never send COLORKEYENABLE (their cutouts use ALPHATEST NOTEQUAL, JK 0x42b8dc-0x42b8f7), so G09 does not gate this check.

Treat Thief Gold, SS2, Shogo and the NewDark DX6 path as must-not-change controls: with the bit on they must show the same tm/cp and the same frames, and lgc_misc 0x100 must never be set. Extend default-ON condition 3 to DX6 Device3 contexts, and delete the 'moon and walls bilinear' criterion.

Make G75 a soft dependency for the core. Prove the core with tests/native on vcr_legacy.h, the d3dprobe controls, and the JK/MotS ring and frames; add G75's legacy_* cases when that probe exists. Re-estimate the core as S-M. G07 matters only for R6's MIPLINEAR objects: JK and MotS send TEXTUREMIN = LINEAR, never a MIP* value, so they never walk a chain.

Keep P1, scheduled first among the Phase 2 quality items once the stability work (G01/G03) has landed. Escalate to P0 only if an in-game frame shows a gameplay-relevant translucent surface (for example a force field) drawn opaque. Fix the 'D3D8 cannot see the change' wording.

problems: (KMD = voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd.) DEFAULT-PATH HAZARD. KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:926 declares `tmu_view v0, v1;` as uninitialised stack structs, and tex_view (:754-803) writes only the fields that exist today. Design §4.3 says alpha_one is 'always 0 in tex_view', but §7's Python check asserts 'tex_view (the default path) never sets it'. Built that way, v0.alpha_one is stack garbage on the 16 bpp default path, so :962 could emit TM_TCA_ONE instead of TM_TCA_REPLACE for A1R5G5B5/A4R4G4B4 textures on every fresh install. That breaks the claim that the registers are byte-for-byte unchanged with the switch off, and the planned test would pin the bug.

d3dprobe coverage gap. The design says cells 1-4 of texx8888_alpha 'cover the three TCA sites'. They do not. Cells 1-2 are single-texture and exercise TMU0 at vcrdd_d3d.c:962. Cells 3-4 put the X8 texture at stage 1, which is TMU0 through stage1_combine at :954. No cell puts an X8 texture at stage 0 with a second stage, so the TMU1 site (:951, textureMode1) is never exercised on silicon.

The format list has two sources. §4.1 appends the X8 entry inside VcrDdD3dHalInfo (vcrdd_d3d.c:2081-2097). §4.2 and §7 pin vcr_texfmt_list() in the new header. Unless HalInfo builds g_texfmt from that function, the native test checks a copy, not the code the HAL runs. Existing literal source assertions also break: tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_dxt24.py:32 (`g_texfmt[9]`), test_vcr_kmd_bigtex.py:62 (the reset chain), :75-77 (HalInfo order) and :120-121 (pf_kind body). The design lists only additions to these tests.

Refactor nuance. Today pf_kind (vcrdd_d3d.c:293-310) returns ARGB32 for ANY 32-bit RGB surface when tex_32 is set; only pf_tmfmt (:320-321) refuses alpha mask 0. mipchain_ext uses kind alone (:403-406). If the refactor merges kind and tmfmt into one classify that refuses X8 at armed 7, mipchain_ext stops packing a DirectDraw-created 32-bit no-alpha texture. DX5-7 titles can create one, because Dd_CanCreateSurface (vcrdd_ddraw.c:610-631) refuses only Z. Rendering is unaffected (such a surface is unsampleable either way), but placement changes, which contradicts §4.5's byte-for-byte claim. §4.5's 'no X8 surface can exist' is true only for D3D8/9.

Flag-bit collision. VCR_INFO_F 0x8000 (the next bit after NO_GDIGAMMA 0x4000, include/vcr_ioctl.h:143) is also claimed by G01 (FIFOGUARD), G07 (MIPGUARD), G08 (D3DLEGACY), G09 (D3DCKEY), G16/G24 (D3DLINES) and G39 (MODECLEAR). G34 already proposes an appended vcr_info.d3d_texfmt word instead (designs/G34.md:260).

Plan inconsistency with G20. G17 says bit 3 'joins the D3DBigTex default-on decision (G20)'. But G20's InForce record hands over `x->d3dbigtex & 7` and defaults an absent value to 7 (designs/G20.md:190, 218, 289), and G34 says 'G20's default deliberately stays below bit 3' (designs/G34.md:402). As planned, bit 3 is masked out of InForce, and a fresh VSA-100 install keeps Halo's flares broken even after G20 lands.

Priority is understated: the affected-bitmap inventory (§2.4) covers only ui and a30. A host parse of the multiplayer maps, read-only from the share, finds 2D X8R8G8B8 non-bump bitmaps that fail CreateTexture today. bloodgulch has 11 tags, including scenery\teleporter_base\bitmaps\teleporter_dust, teleporter_shield\...\teleporter_shield_dust, weapons\flamethrower\bitmaps\flamethrower_numbers, 'flares weapon lens'/'lens1', 'flares pr overcharge', the scorpion headlight_lens_flare and rasterizer\default 2d. sidewinder has 12, including sky\dusk\bitmaps\sky dusk. b30 has sky\bitmaps\crap water0/1, and hangemhigh has 9. Halo is .124's LAN-party title, so these are common multiplayer scenes, which is P0 by the design's own 'raise to P0' criterion. Inferred, not yet seen on screen: 'default 2d' black/white used as fallbacks in additive passes would draw in the vertex colour, which could explain the over-exposed object.

The boot C regression set is narrower than the risk the design itself names. §9 names Red Faction, Max Payne and the DX6 enumerators as likely X8 choosers, but boot C tests only UT2004, UT2003, Thief II and H&D. It omits Red Faction and BF1942 LAN (D3D8), a DX6/7 enumerator (Shogo, JK/MotS) and Rainbow Six, which scripts/fleet/fleet-roster.txt:23 says 'fails with them'. Max Payne is excluded for stability, so its X8 behaviour stays untested before any default-on. There is also no Halo multiplayer-map frame.

§9's 'no interaction with Glide/OpenGL ... D3D state is rewritten per flush' is inaccurate. The TMU combineMode is written only by the Reset3D sequence (include/vcr_3dseq.h:193; Reset3D is off on .124), never per flush (display/vcrdd_3d.c:107-126). MesaFX on Napalm uses the combine extension (build/retro3dfx-gl/src/mesa/drivers/glide/fxsetup.c:1465), which sets SST_CM_USE_COMBINE_MODE (build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/h5/glide3/src/gtex.c:1902, 2274). h5 Glide notes that some combineMode bits act even with that bit cleared (gtex.c:1205-1212). After a GL session, TCA_ONE, like every legacy TCA the HAL writes, may not be what executes. This hazard predates G17 (G01/G03), but the risk text should say so.

Forward hazard for later gaps. alpha_one is complete today only because no TMU colour combine reads the raw local texel alpha: stage1_combine (vcrdd_d3d.c:849-873) emits only TC REPLACE/PASS/MULT/ADD (include/vcr_3dregs.h:181-188), and color_path reads texture alpha only through CC_M_ATMU and ASEL_TMU (:709, :728, :735). A G12 or G13 fix that adds SST_TC_MALOCAL or ADD_ALOCAL (BLENDTEXTUREALPHA at stage 1, ALPHAREPLICATE) would read the X byte. 3dfx remaps exactly those muxes for textures without alpha (retro-3dfx H5 W2K D6MT.C:4836-4850).

vcr_tca_alpha_one is specified on bare TCA values (0x08200000 -> 0x24000000, and so on). The :954 site ORs TC and TCA together (stage1_combine returns `tc | tca`, :873). The function must rewrite only the SST_TACOMBINE field (0x1FF<<21), and the native test as written never feeds it a word with TC bits set.

Minor accuracy. The design says 'not found' on whether 3dfx read an X8 texel's alpha as 1. The vendor source settles it: its D3TXTR.C:2035-2039 sets TEXFMTFLG_ALPHA for every RGB8888_RMASK surface, so the X8R8G8B8 it listed for DX8 (D3INIT.C:2496-2507) was sampled with the X byte as alpha. Also, Appendix A gives the mip count at '+0x12'; it is at +0x14 (halo.exe 0x523fff, 0x524094).
corrections: Record the evidence verified for this review. (1) The XP SP3 runtimes map a DX7 entry to D3DFMT_X8R8G8B8 only when dwFlags is EXACTLY DDPF_RGB (0x40): d3d9.dll 0x4fe059d2 `cmp $0x40,%ecx`, 32-bit jump-table case to 0x16 at 0x4fe05aeb; d3d8.dll 0x6d9b6872 and 0x6d9b698b. (2) In halo.exe 1.10, the table at file 0x25e040 has index 10 = 0x16, and its single consumer is at 0x523fc0. (3) Creation is mostly lazy, through the texture cache 0x444550 (37 call sites), plus an eager tag-load path at 0x43f030. The binder 0x518680 calls SetTexture(stage, bitmap+0x28), so a failed create reaches our HAL as TEXTUREMAP 0. (4) The X byte is 255 in every 2D X8 bitmap in ui.map. (5) SST_TCA_ONE = MZERO|INVERT_OUTPUT = 0x24000000 (h5 h3defs.h:351, :374; the vendor's H3DEFS.H:383). (6) caps_124.txt shows tex565=1 alongside hal_fullscreen R5G6B5=1. That suggests the runtime handles a format that is both a display mode and a texture, but it is not proof. Pin the exact-flags requirement in the native test.

In compute_regs, zero-initialise the views (`tmu_view v0 = {0}, v1 = {0};`) or make both tex_view and tex_view_ext write alpha_one. Replace §7's 'tex_view never sets it' with a check that the default path reads alpha_one = 0.

Have VcrDdD3dHalInfo build g_texfmt from vcr_texfmt_list() through texfmt()/texfmt_fcc(), so the native test runs the HAL's own list, or add a Python cross-check. Return kind and tmfmt separately from vcr_texfmt_classify. At armed 7, X8 stays kind ARGB32 with tmfmt NONE (today's values), so mipchain_ext placement is unchanged. Pin both values in the native test.

Have vcr_tca_alpha_one take the whole textureMode word and rewrite only bits 21-29. Test it with TC bits present, e.g. TM_TC_MULT|TM_TCA_MULT -> TM_TC_MULT|0, and TM_TC_REPLACE|TM_TCA_REPLACE -> TM_TC_REPLACE|TM_TCA_ONE.

Add texx8888_alpha cell 5 for the TMU1 site (:951). Stage 0: X8 red with X byte 0x00, ALPHAOP and COLOROP SELECTARG1(TEXTURE). Stage 1: an A8R8G8B8 texture bound, COLOROP and ALPHAOP SELECTARG2(CURRENT), which gives TMU0 PASS/PASS. Blend SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA over blue. Want (255,0,0); old-buggy (0,0,255).
Do not take VCR_INFO_F 0x8000. Carry the X8 bit in an appended vcr_info word guarded by info.size (G34's d3d_texfmt, or the raw d3dbigtex value), so all the D3DBigTex/D3DTexFmt bits share one field.

The same holds in 10 of 19 MP maps: damnation, gephyrophobia, icefields, longest, sidewinder and timberland (dusk/night); carousel and boardingaction (space/stars); dangercanyon and deathisland (ocean). Each sky's sun lens flare (sky -> lens 'sun' -> flares_generic, X8) is used in a10, a30, b30, d40, ui and 17 of 19 MP maps; only putput and ratrace have none. In bloodgulch, 80 bullet-impact effects (AR, pistol, ... on dirt, stone, metal, glass) spawn particle 'flare h stealth cannon', whose bitmap 'flares weapon lens' is X8 (that it draws as a square is inferred). THE a30 SKY IS NOW PROVEN STATICALLY, NOT 'inferred link' (G17.md:148). The 2-stage map list of scex 'sky\sky_a30\skydusk0\shaders\sky dusk' is [stars DXT1, sky dusk X8]. Halo picking the 2-stage list on a 2-stage device is inferred; the frames match it. With stage 1's handle 0, compute_regs sets two = tex && ... && c->tex_handle1 && view_of(...) (vcrdd_d3d.c:926-927) and drops stage 1 silently, leaving stars only. The sky regions of the a30 frames are about 91% pure (0,0,0): the 180 s frame's mean is (1.4,1.6,1.4), while the missing gradient's mean is (63,68,90). MENU EVIDENCE SUPPORTS THE ROOT CAUSE. The three flat squares in the 09-28 menu frame lie on one line through the screen centre: from (619,614) and (690,143) the line crosses y=480 at x=639.2 and predicts x=710 at y=10, where the third square sits. That is the reflection axis of a lens flare (ui sky 'sun in space' -> flares_generic X8). An unaligned DXT read would give noise, not flat squares on a flare axis. visual.md V-12's alignment reading is refuted, and onbox.md:207's '180 s largely right' misses the black sky.

THE COUNTERS MISS THE DOMINANT CASE. The §3.3 reasons (G17.md:219-224) count four cases: stage 0 with handle 0, a refused texture, a missing texcoord set, and stage 1 'with a handle' dropped. The a30 sky (and b30's water) is a fifth case: stage 1 whose op reads TEXTURE with handle 0, dropped at vcrdd_d3d.c:926-927. It increments nothing, so boot B cannot show the biggest consumer. d3dprobe (D3D8) also cannot prove that D3D9 exposes X8. Only a HAL-side count of X8 surfaces Halo creates in boot C proves the consumer.

THE VERIFICATION PLAN LACKS SKY CRITERIA. The pass criterion covers only the flat flare rectangle (G17.md:443); the a30 sky and the starfield are 'predictions' to note. The reference frame is 'optional' (G17.md:447), yet sky correctness cannot be judged without one; .240 (Radeon 9800 XT) has Halo 'verified' in the compat DB. At about 1.7 fps the timedemo's scene at a given wall-clock second drifts with any frame-rate change, so the '2 s burst over 54-66 s' may catch a different shot. Halo's own fps and memory are not compared between boot B and boot C.

THE REGRESSION SET IS MIS-TARGETED (G17.md:444, :456). UE2 cannot pick X8R8G8B8: UT2004's D3DDrv.dll calls CheckDeviceFormat only for DXT1/3/5, A8R8G8B8 and R5G6B5 (G34.md:190). The two long UT2003/UT2004 sessions therefore prove nothing about bit 3. The titles at risk are:
- the D3DX users: Max Payne (D3DXCreateTextureFromFileInMemoryEx) and Thief II (d3dx9_43), G34.md:191-194;
- the DX6/7 enumerators: H&D's igraph2 converter, AvP's first-fit walker, Shogo, JK/MotS and R6.
Max Payne is excluded (G17.md:436) but is the most likely to switch to X8. Arming bit 3 on .124's party configuration would expose it untested.

THE DEPENDENCIES ARE WRONG FOR A P0.

THE MEMORY RISK IS FRAMED AS VIDEO MEMORY (G17.md:457-460). With D3DPOOL_MANAGED the runtime uploads a texture to VRAM on first use (inferred), so bump maps that are never drawn cost their system-memory copies, not heap. Up to 26 MB of X8 per map (mostly bump maps) matters on .124's 256 MB of RAM if Halo creates them eagerly. That is measured with halo.exe's commit and working set, not with 513/10.

Combine 20 is a plain single-level A8R8G8B8, not only the FOURCC case. (d) The heap is 0-0x3ed3000 (ONBOX ring seq 24681), so the README's 27 MB is stale. (e) There are exactly four readers of tex_ext (d3d.c:532, 842, 1301; 3d.c:255). (f) I recompiled vcr_texlod.c and reproduced every row of the design's §2 table, the 273 shapes with exactly one non-zero pad (RGB16 1x1, pad 8), and the 408 identical NAPALM vs NAPALM|BIG cases. (g) The vendor rounds the base up and puts 1x1 at +8 (VH5/D3TXTR.C:880-889, 3734-3765); Glide rounds the sum down (G5/glide3/src/ditex.c:1781-1787).

Bit 0 alone breaks a path the design calls 'benign or a fix' (§4.2). Today the default branch (d3d.c:537-539) driver-packs TEXTURE|MIPMAP|3DDEVICE surfaces 16-byte aligned. mipchain_ext excludes 3DDEVICE (d3d.c:389-391; the exclusion was added in 481acfd). So bit 0 sends mipmapped render-target textures back to dxg's 4-byte placement until bit 1 is armed.

Graduation moves allocation from a two-pass allocator to a single-pass one. mipchain_ext calls HeapVidMemAllocAligned once and turns a 0 return into DDERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY (d3d.c:441-446). The runtime survives the lost block at offset 0 with a second pass; our single call does not (KMD/include/vcr_ddheap.h:14-24; .124's heap starts at 0). Defaulting bit 0 on moves every single-level texture on a fresh install onto the single-pass path, while DdHeapFloor stays default-off. The design names the risk (G63) but graduates after one boot anyway.

rtt_align's FAIL baseline on the BigTex path (boots A0/C) is not guaranteed. On that path the 2x1 spacers are driver-placed with {16,16} alignment (d3d.c:438-441; the vendor uses the same, VH5/DDMEMMGR.C:349-360). If the linear heap rounds a 4-byte request up to the 16-byte pitch, the spacers leave the heap on the grid, the dxg-placed render-target texture lands aligned, and the test PASSES. §1's 'likely trigger' (per-level 2x2/1x1 blocks de-phasing the heap) rests on the same unanswered rounding question, so it contradicts itself.

The default-path tex1x1 expectation conflicts with the design's own pitch assumption. §4.7 infers that dxg's texture pitch is DWORD ('the value 4 is inferred to be today's pitch rule'). A 1-wide 16 bpp texture would then get pitch 4 != w*2, which tex_view REFUSES (vcr_texlod.c:18-20): the quad draws untextured (513/7), not misaddressed. Part 0 never counts a refused texture. Bit 0 also makes every 1-wide 16 bpp texture (1xN ramps) samplable, a behaviour change missing from §4.2. This is unconfirmed: dxg's pitch for a 2-byte row is unmeasured, and no evidence file records it.

Part 0's counters do not measure what §9 and §11 use them for. target_of runs on every DP2 and every Clear2 (d3d.c:1852, 1884; also 1189, 1737), so 'rt_offgrid++' counts calls, not targets. The texture check in compute_regs (d3d.c:921-966) sees only the bound top level, so it is blind to G07's per-level scatter and to refused textures. A zero count in UT2004 or Halo therefore does not show their textures read right. Also, the existing game rings (onbox/games/*/ring_decoded.txt) hold no 513/21-23 combine lines, so no title has yet been observed binding a 1x1 or a 3DDEVICE texture. UT2003's 26 logged combines have neither.

A misplaced render-target texture is self-consistent for a 3D round trip. colBufferAddr[3:0] are unused (SPEC §8.40), and texBaseAddr drops the same 4/8/12 bytes (absent levels are 0 mod 16 for sizes of 8 and up). So render, then sample, reads back exactly what was drawn. What is actually wrong is the up-to-12-byte overwrite of the previous heap block, and CPU Lock or 2D Blt (byte-exact base_of, KMD/display/vcrdd_2d.c:164-169) disagreeing by the phase. Bit 1's games list (Halo, UT2003/UT2004, Max Payne) overstates any visible gain.

The '+16 MB below zero' read is VSA-100-only (a Voodoo3's 24-bit wrap is correct).

D04 0x10011785 and 0x10011c26-0x10011c5d pick D16 only when Use16bit is set, else D24X8 (D24S8 with UseStencil). The fallback at 0x1001230e-0x1001234d tries D32, then D24S8, then fails fatally. (2) Field layout. UT2003 Engine.dll 0x1038dd16-0x1038de5d registers Use16bit at +0x58 and nothing at +0x60/+0x64. (3) WinDrv 0x11104bda-0x11104be7 passes ColorBytes=0. (4) UT2003.exe 0x1090d80d-0x1090d842 runs AutoConfigure when GIsClient && FirstRun==0. 0x10906fcb-0x1090703e writes 640/480, Projectors=False and NoDynamicLights=True for 0x121a. 0x10908e95-0x10908ebe raises FirstRun to 2225. (5) UT2004.exe has the same code (0x1090f11c, 0x10907f40, 0x1090930a = 3369). The gap is real but it is NOT in vcr-kmd: 640x480 is a staged-library defect (FirstRun=0), and 16 bpp is Epic's intended vendor policy.

(B) BREAKS THE JOIN LAUNCHER. G19.md:422 replaces 'start "" "UT2004.exe"' with 'start "" "UT2004.exe" %UE2_DEVID%'. LIB/UT2004/'Join fleet UT2004 server.bat' would then read 'start "" "UT2004.exe" -nodeviceid "192.168.1.132:7777"'. UE2 treats the FIRST command-line token as the URL: UT2004 Engine.dll 0x104258c7-0x1042593d runs ParseToken, then appStricmp 'SERVER', then cmp word [Parm],0x2d. If that token starts with '-', it loads FURL::DefaultLocalMap. So the box would sit at the menu and never join the server. That is the 'reported success' failure shape.

The list of flag effects is incomplete. G19.md:237-242 names three effects, all in D3DDrv, but WinDrv also reads the flag as a fullscreen-only lock. In UT2003 WinDrv.dll, 0x11104bc2-0x11104be0 sets the SetRes Fullscreen arg to flag|requested, and 0x11104d62 makes EndFullscreen refuse to go windowed. UT2004 WinDrv.dll 0x11112092 does the same with RenDev+0x70. So -nodeviceid also unlocks windowed mode and ALT+ENTER. Engine.dll was never scanned for other readers.

problems: GATING: Part A is not 'byte-for-byte unchanged'. It rewrites alphaMode for 65 of the 225 factor pairs (55 of them inside D3D's 1..13; I checked this with a host model of the proposed header). That applies on the default 16 bpp lane and on every D3D32 X8R8G8B8 back buffer (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:995-998, replaced by vcr_blend_alphamode). Unless the plan adopts D3DFeatOff it gets NO off switch (G28.md §4.1). The words are 'unchanged' only for inputs that have been measured. d3dprobe names only SRCALPHA/ZERO and SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA (KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c:739-740, 1125-1126). The only logged combines are UT2003's MENU and the probes: am 0x44119/0x45110/0x45119/0x46410 (KMD/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt; d3dplan_1112/onbox/ring_*_decoded.txt).

MEASUREMENT: the in-game baseline and the boot-1 A/B (G28.md §7.1, §7.2) list only Halo, UT2003, UT2004, Thief II, Red Faction, H&D and Max Payne. None of the 16 bpp DX5/DX6 titles is on it (JK DF2, MotS, Shogo, AvP, SS2, Thief Gold, Rainbow Six), although Part A changes their path too. Two further limits: the 513/21 combine log stops at 64 combines per context (vcrdd_d3d.c:73, 897-898), and the ring holds 1024 entries, which game sessions overran at LogLevel 3 (onbox/README.md:49-51). The baseline can therefore miss a dest-alpha pair completely.

VENDOR FACT WRONG: '3dfx shipped no real destination alpha / never did real destination alpha' (G28.md §2, §11 Findings text; the gap text) is half wrong. srcBlend/dstBlend write the application's ALPHA-CHANNEL factors (DSTA, 1-DSTA, SRCA, 1-SRCA) into SST_ASRCFACT/SST_ADSTFACT (VH5/D3RSTATE.C:3109-3151, 3222-3245). setDX6state clamps those factors only when ulBpp != 32 (VH5/D6DP2.C:6271-6313). Only the RGB factors are substituted at every depth (6240-6269). So at 32 bpp 3dfx shipped Part B's alpha-channel words by default, on EVERY target, X8R8G8B8 back buffers included. That is precedent for Part B's register values, and the Findings text should not record the opposite.

MISSED IN-REPO PRECEDENT: our own MesaFX ICD on this silicon already does both halves (build/retro3dfx-gl/src/mesa/drivers/glide/fxsetup.c:1540-1683). DST_ALPHA becomes ONE and ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA becomes ZERO when the visual has no hardware alpha (:1568, 1571, 1642, 1645). The alpha-channel DSTA codes are used only at 32 bpp with alpha (:1608, 1612, 1679, 1683). SRCA codes 1 and 5 are used at any 32 bpp (:1600, 1604, 1671, 1675), so OpenGL titles on .124 drive the 0x51 alpha byte through Glide (inferred from code, not traced). MesaFX keeps SATURATE without hardware alpha (:1574). The design's SATURATE -> ZERO is the more correct choice.

TRANSPORT RATIONALE FALSE: 'vcr_info.flags is full: 0x7fff pinned' (G28.md §4.3) is not true. flags is a vcr_u32 (KMD/include/vcr_ioctl.h:86), so 17 bits are free. tests/native/test_vcr_kmd_abi.c:118-138 pins only the current list of flags and would simply be extended; G05.md:336 itself offers a 0x8000 flag.

OVERSTATED PROOF: 'Part A uses only BF_ONE/BF_ZERO, the RGB values the proven path writes on every opaque draw' (G28.md §3.5, §4.1) is inaccurate. An opaque draw writes alphaMode with AM_BLEND clear and every factor field 0 (vcrdd_d3d.c:991-994). The new words, such as 0x00044010 (ZERO/ONE with blend on) and 0x00040010, have never been written by this HAL. The codes are legal (SPEC L2958-2969), so there is no hardware risk, but they are not 'proven'.

PROBE TABLE ERROR: destalpha_rt r6 (INVDESTALPHA/DESTALPHA, red ff over blue, Ad c0) comes to 3f00c0 by D3D's formula, not 4000bf (G28.md §5.2; host model: R=3f, B=c0). The difference is inside the 8-count tolerance, and ref_blend computes the real value, but the table misleads anyone reading the logs.

PREMISE UNCONFIRMED (1): that a target without alpha reads destination alpha as 1 is marked inferred (G28.md §2), and I found no source that states it. The DX DDK alpha-blend pseudo-code (dxddk dd3ddk_4eg4) leaves da undefined for formats without alpha. The only support is indirect: the PRS 8373 values, and the GL/MesaFX rule. §5.4's NVIDIA cross-check is written as 'stop and decide', but it appears in neither §4.1's gating nor §7.2's pass criteria.

PREMISE UNCONFIRMED (2): 'every 32 bpp flip-chain back buffer is X8R8G8B8, so never rt_alpha' (G28.md §3.2) is unverified for a D3D8/9 app that asks for an A8R8G8B8 back buffer. It holds only if the runtime refuses that buffer on 121a:0009 (runtime.md §4.3 flag 0x4000: OFFSCREEN_RENDERTARGET instead of SAME_FORMAT_UP_TO_ALPHA; inferred) or labels the surface with an alpha mask (has_pixfmt reads lpGbl->ddpfSurface, vcrdd_d3d.c:166-169). Suppose the runtime grants the buffer while it carries fill_pixfmt's display format, which has no alpha mask (vcrdd_ddraw.c:30-43). Then Part A turns a DESTALPHA-over-stored-alpha technique that works today into 'alpha = 1'. bb_a8r8g8b8 is measured, but Part A is not gated on the result.

problems: CONFIRMED, not refuted: compute_regs sets FZ_DITHER (bit 8) whenever DITHERENABLE != 0 at every target depth (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:978-980). git blame dates these lines to 56e0bc15 (2026-09-26), so they are in deployed build 95678704. Nothing masks the bit downstream: VcrDd3dState writes r->fbzMode as computed (KMD/display/vcrdd_3d.c:79), FZ_DITHER has no other user in vcr-kmd, and clears write their own fbzMode with no dither (vcrdd_3d.c:158). D3DPRASTERCAPS_DITHER is advertised (vcrdd_d3d.c:2019; RasterCaps 0x00100191, bit 0).

Hardware facts check out. The spec text is quoted correctly: fbzMode[8] 'must be cleared' at renderMode[1:0]=2 (SPEC L3254), and bit 19 is 'ignored' there (L3268). Bit positions match the GPL h3defs.h (SST_ENDITHER=BIT(8), SST_DITHER2x2=BIT(11), SST_ENDITHERSUBTRACT=BIT(19), SST_RM_32BPP=2). h5 Glide clears 8/11/19 at 32 bpp (G5/gglide.c:3904-3907). CSIM skips the whole dither/truncate stage at 32 bpp (CSIM/FBI.C:1455). 3dfx's HAL sets ENDITHER with no depth check (VH5/D3RSTATE.C:3500-3530, :3761), and every hardware write passes pRc->sst.fbzMode through unmasked (D6DP2.C:6092-6152, D6TRI2I.C:1623). The fix is the exact state our Glide/OpenGL already uses at 32 bpp on this silicon. It changes no other register and nothing on the 16 bpp, Voodoo3, SLI or flip paths. I independently re-ran the reference model against CSIM's _sstDit5/_sstDit6 (RGBFMT.C:252-264): 0 mismatches, and the 0x868281 off/4x4/2x2 table is reproduced exactly.

Every §8 command passes '--pace 5000', but d3dprobe_run.py has no --pace option and parses strictly (KMD/tools/d3dprobe_run.py:226-258, 'a = ap.parse_args()'), so each run stops with 'unrecognized arguments' before upload. Pacing is already built in: vcr_pace.h is called at tools/d3dprobe.c:196 and :1464, and the EXECW budget is set at d3dprobe_run.py:119.

Event code clash. 'Event 513 what 24' is also claimed by G01 (designs/G01.md:170,328), G03:247, G05:268, G10:180-240, G11:137, G13:177-194, G15:266 and G16:106-109,390. Whichever item lands first gets 24, and step C's 'read the log for 513 / what 24' would then count another item's events. Also, the 513 description in vcr_events.h:75 already omits codes 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 21-23.

The dither32 verdict can escalate to P1 by mistake. §6.1 says PASS = all four checks, and §8 says FAIL means the chip dithers at 32 bpp, so raise to P1. But the 'dither off' check is a control, and it is an exact (tolerance 0) colour-path claim that has never been measured: every existing 32 bpp check uses tolerance 8-24 (tools/d3dprobe.c:926-953; evidence/silicon/d3d32_step16/d3d32_render___bpp_32_.txt). A failed control, or a G01 stale-FIFO run (reports/onbox.md:127: 7 pass / 35 fail), shows up as a FAIL of dither32, not as 'void'.

The dither32 A/B never tests a blended draw. The only 32 bpp dither trace in 3dfx's C model is in the 32 bpp alpha-blend branch: the commented-out 'Why dither in 32bpp?' error at CSIM/FBI.C:1385-1387. UE2, Halo and Thief II draw much of each frame blended. A PASS on an unblended flat quad and ramp does not show that the blend path ignores bit 8.

dither16 makes an unrelated model a gate for G30. §6.2 passes only on an exact match to the CSIM-derived 4x4/2x2 model. If the silicon differs ('other'), run 2 fails on both the old and the new build, d3dprobe_run exits 1 (d3dprobe_run.py exit_code), and step B's 'all must hold' cannot be met until the model is fixed. The G30 criterion (old block == new block) does not need the model at all.

Step B always spends a dedicated driver build, deploy and reboot. If step A passes, which is the expected result (CSIM skips the stage, and the retail HAL shipped the bit at 32 bpp on every V5), G30 changes no pixel, and the reboot buys only spec hygiene on a box whose reboots carry activation and safe-reboot overhead.

Step C launches Max Payne only to count an event. Max Payne froze the box once (2026-10-04) and is run only with a person watching. Its dither choice is a single compare that the event would merely confirm (e2driver/e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll 0x1002875a: 'cmpl $0x3,0x10(%esi)'; dither 1 if below 3, else 0).

The static scan is overstated for Halo. 'FALSE, at its only site' is true only for direct calls: halo.exe has one SetRenderState(0x1a) call through vtbl+0xE4, setting FALSE (0x516456-0x51645b), and the other 25 'push 0x1a' sites are other methods. But halo.exe statically links the D3DX effect compiler (its strings include 'DITHERENABLE' and ID3DXEffectCompiler messages) and loads SHADERS/fx.bin, which is encrypted (no plaintext strings). Effect-state dithering is invisible to the scan. The other title claims verified: UT2004 D3DDrv 0x10011f43-48 and UT2003 0x1001082f-34 set TRUE unconditionally, and Thief2.exe 0x605cc4-0x605cfa is the flag-conditional site.

The 16 bpp matrix change has two owners. G30 §4.5 step 2 (Diag\D3DDither, keep 4x4 by default) and G19 §4.5 item D (designs/G19.md:447-452: 'set FZ_DITHER2X2 with FZ_DITHER on 16 bpp targets ... behind a Diag switch') are the same change, with opposite recommendations and different switch names.

Reason 3 in G30 §4.5 is half wrong. It says 3dfx's 2x2 matrix 'belonged with the overlay's 2x2 box filter'. With OVERLAYMODE Optimal (the default), modes at 1024x768 and above (every .124 game mode) used the '4x4 dither subtract + 4x1 tap' filter (VH5/REGKEYS.H:153-156; VH5/DDFXNT.C:2653-2670), while D3D still rendered with DITHER2x2 always. 2x2 was a fixed choice ('D3D won't let you chose the dither matrix size so hardcode something', D3RSTATE.C:3502), not a pairing with the filter. Reasons 1, 2 and 4 still support keeping 4x4.

Scope creep in a kernel header. vcr_fbz_dither_rows (a hook for G51) and the 16 bpp reference model (vcr_dm0 / vcr_dith_ch / vcr_dither_565) would ship in KMD/include/vcr_dither.h with no caller in the driver. G30's fix needs only vcr_fbz_dither and an FZ_DITHERSUB define.

Gating is acceptable. The change is reachable only with Diag\D3D32=1 (default OFF), so a fresh install's register stream is byte-identical (vcr_rt_rendermode is 16 for VCR_RT_16 and VCR_RT_REFUSED). On .124 it goes live without its own switch, but it only removes a bit the spec forbids, and Glide already runs this silicon at 32 bpp with the bit clear.
corrections: Remove '--pace 5000' from every d3dprobe_run.py command in §8. Pacing is compiled into d3dprobe (vcr_pace.h), and d3dprobe_run adds the pace worst case to its EXECW budget.

Do not hard-code what=24. Allocate 513 what-codes at landing time from one plan-level registry (or the order of landing), name the code in vcr_events.h, and backfill the missing 513 codes in the description. Step C should match the event's message text ('DITHERENABLE ... not dithered'), not the number. Alternatively, fold a per-context 'dither dropped' count into the existing 'context N gone' summary (what 2) and drop the new code altogether.

Give dither32 a three-valued RESULT: pass / fail / void. It is void when either dither-off control (flat block, off ramp) is not exact, or the control shows a dead colour path (G01). Raise to P1 only when the controls are exact AND dither-on differs from dither-off.

Add a blended on/off pair to dither32: the existing 'blend' scene (0x80ff0000 SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA over a known clear) plus a blended ramp, each drawn with DITHERENABLE TRUE and FALSE. The decisive check is on == off pixel for pixel. This covers the blend branch, where CSIM's only 32 bpp dither remnant sits.

Make dither16 informational for G30. The G30 checks are: the dither-off block equals the truncation value 0x848284, and the dither-on block hash is identical on the old and new builds. Report the 4x4/2x2/other classification as data, not as pass/fail, so a CSIM-versus-silicon difference cannot block G30.

Make step B conditional. If step A's dither32 passes on 95678704, land G30 in the next batched D3D build and verify dither32 in that build's normal supervised boot. Give G30 its own build and reboot only if step A fails, and in that case before G19's 32 bpp A/B.

Drop Max Payne from step C, or count it only during a supervised G04 session that runs it anyway. Keep Halo, Thief II NewDark and H&D in step C. For Halo specifically, its effect collection (SHADERS/fx.bin) can set DitherEnable outside the static scan.

Give the 16 bpp matrix/subtraction change one owner: either G30 step 2 or G19 item D, with one Diag switch name. Rewrite §4.5 reason 3: at 1024x768 and above the vendor used the 4x4-subtract/4x1 filter while rendering 2x2. The case for keeping the 4x4 default stands on 'no correctness reason / proven lane / subtraction was opt-in'.

Keep KMD/include/vcr_dither.h minimal: vcr_fbz_dither plus FZ_DITHERSUB in vcr_3dregs.h. Put the 16 bpp reference model on the probe and test side (tools/ or tests/native), and land vcr_fbz_dither_rows with G51.

Extend the GPL-header cross-check (tests/python/test_vcr_kmd_d3d.py test_the_register_offsets_are_computed_from_the_gpl_header) with RM_32BPP == SST_RM_32BPP, since the new helper keys on it, alongside the FZ_DITHER / FZ_DITHER2X2 / FZ_DITHERSUB == SST_* checks.

State in the plan that the gap's title list ('Halo, Thief II, H&D, Max Payne') lists the 32 bpp titles, not the titles that dither. Halo's only direct call sets FALSE, Max Payne dithers only when [+0x10] < 3, UE2 dithers unconditionally but renders 16 bpp today (V-08), and Thief II NewDark and H&D stay unknown until the on-box count.

problems: CONFIRMED GAP (source matches the deployed vcrdd.dll: out/vcrdd.dll md5 95678704 = deployed). In voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/display/vcrdd_d3d.c, set_rs (:1393-1406) stores state 47 and compute_regs (:921-1029) never reads it. The only depth bits set are FZ_DEPTH|FZ_ZFUNC|FZ_ZAWRITE (:986-990). FZ_ZBIAS (include/vcr_3dregs.h:115) is never set. zaColor is written only by the clear (display/vcrdd_3d.c:160). prim_caps builds RasterCaps 0x1001b1 (:2019-2020), so there is no 0x4000. A case-insensitive grep finds no other zbias/zaColor use in display/, include/ or miniport/.

INSTRUMENTATION DOES NOT WORK AS WRITTEN (design §3.6, §7.2, §7.3). It appends ', ZBIAS max %d over %u changes' to the ctx_free 'context %u gone' text (display/vcrdd_d3d.c:1212-1215). A ring message is capped at 95 characters (include/vcr_log.h:32), and that line is ALREADY cut off in every game session captured on 11-12: games/UT2004_botmatch/ring_decoded.txt:1020 '...63 texture ', Halo_timedemo:1018 '...77 texture f', UT2004_statfps:1013 '...22 texture flu', UT2003_flyby:1015 '...42 texture ' (all under evidence/d3dplan_1112/onbox/). The ZBIAS max N that boot A and boot B rely on would therefore never appear. G27.md:299 already notes the line is full, and G76.md:271 already plans a 'zbias' counter slot in its own event. A count of state changes also says nothing about exposure (triangles drawn biased).

UE2 CLAIM OVERSTATED. Verified by disassembly: in both D3DDrv.dll builds, SetZBias clamps ZBias*5 to 0..15 and the deferred commit calls IDirect3DDevice8::SetRenderState (vtable +0xc8, index 50) with 0x2f, unconditionally. UT2004 (md5 b6bb4d87): VA 0x100167e0 and 0x1001a809. UT2003 (md5 04c412ca): VA 0x10014470 and 0x10017aa9. But D3DDrv also stores RasterCaps&0x4000 into the render device at +0x50 (UT2004 VA 0x10010ba0-0x10010bab), and the Engine.dll callers of SetZBias were not traced. Whether UE2 sends ZBIAS when the cap is absent is therefore UNCONFIRMED. The design's own 'Who reads +0x50' question already admits this.

TITLE LIST INCOMPLETE OR WRONG (heuristic scan: push 0x2f, then a call through a SetRenderState vtable slot). (1) Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe, a .124 D3D title, is missing. Its D3D8 engine HiddenAndDangerous/Bin/i3d2.dll (d3d8 loaded dynamically by igraph2.dll) calls SetRenderState(ZBIAS,1) at VA 0x10098f64 when material flag bit 14 is set, and SetRenderState(ZBIAS,0) at 0x1009909b. (2) The UE1 D3DDrv.dll of UnrealTournament436, UnrealTournament, UnrealGold and DeusEx sends ZBIAS 15 through IDirect3DDevice7::SetRenderState (+0x50): UT436 VA 0x10004ab9, reset to 0 at 0x10004d98. (3) SeriousSamSecondEncounter/Bin/Engine.dll (D3D8) has 2 sites, and Tribes2/GameData/OpenGL2D3D.dll (D3D7) has 2. Items 2 and 3 matter only if those titles are switched to D3D on .124. (4) No immediate ZBIAS site was found in MaxPayne, RedFaction, Shogo, SystemShock2, ThiefGold, RainbowSix, AliensVsPredator, JediKnightDF2 or JediKnightMotS. This supports the design's 'not Red Faction', so the gap's own games list (which includes Red Faction) is wrong.

BF1942 IS TESTABLE NOW. The design (§9, games_unblocked) says it can be checked 'only after G72's SafeDisc block'. But the library ships 'Host Battlefield 1942 - LAN.bat' and 'Join ... - LAN.bat', which skip the disc mount (BF1942/launch.txt). BF1942.exe (md5 a56d63e8) calls SetRenderState(0x2f) at VA 0x603bd9 and 0x604a3b, which I confirmed. A LAN host run can be in boots A and B today.

CAPS-GATED USERS CANNOT BE SEEN IN BOOT A. A title that sends ZBIAS only when D3DPRASTERCAPS_ZBIAS is reported shows N=0 in boot A by construction. Boot B then changes two things at once: bias drawing and caps-driven path switches. Yet boot B's game list covers only UE2, Halo, Thief II, Jedi Knight and StarCraft, and leaves out H&D, BF1942 and the rest of the 15 D3D titles. A regression in boot B could not be pinned on the bias value or on a path switch.

zbias_clear MAY PASS VACUOUSLY ON THE BOX. Every DP2 starts with memset(&w,0) and prepared=0 (vcrdd_d3d.c:1835), and Clear2 (:1882-1898) is a separate call. If the D3D8 runtime sends the Clear through Clear2, or ends the DP2 batch at the clear, the state is re-sent anyway, and the test passes even when clear_rects' dirty=1/prepared=0 (:1419-1420) is removed. Only a D3DDP2OP_CLEAR in the same batch as the next draw (:1754-1757) exercises the restore. The planned source pin is the real guard, and which clear path the runtime takes is not recorded.

zbias_scale CLAIM NOT REACHABLE (§5.1). The design says a scale keyed to the desktop 'paints every strip red'. With --full 640x480x16 the fullscreen PDEV is itself 16 bpp, so pd->bpp equals the target format; windowed runs are 32/32. None of the planned runs produces a target whose depth differs from the PDEV's, so only the --zfmt d24x8 (Z-keyed) variant can be caught on the box. A pd->bpp key is caught only by the source pin.

HARDWARE: SOUND, WITH THE 32 BPP ADDER INFERRED. Confirmed: SST_ENZBIAS is BIT(16) (glide3x/h5/incsrc/h3defs.h:765) and SST_ZACOLOR_DEPTH is 0xFFFFFF (:979). The SPEC strings (avenger_spec.doc) say bit 16 adds zaColor's depth field to Z or 1/W; zaColor[23:0] is used at 32 bpp and [15:0] otherwise; and the biased Z/W is what gets written (strings L4566, L4571, L4800). In the register table zaColor is 'Yes / Yes' like fbzMode, so a write between triangles is ordered with the pipeline. The depth-unit diagram (strings L12838-12874: 'iterated Z[27:12]', 'Sign extend 16-bit zaColor', 'Clamp to 0-FFFF') is the 16-bit-era picture, so the 24-bit sign extension AND the 24-bit clamp are both inferred. A nuance the design misses: for |bias| <= 8192 the low 16 bits of its 24-bit values are the same int16, so they work whether the hardware sign-extends from bit 23 or bit 15. They fail only if the hardware treats [23:0] as unsigned (decals vanish) or clamps at 0xFFFF (every biased pixel lands in front). Both show up in the 32 bpp zbias_scale run.

PROVEN PATHS: UNCHANGED, CONFIRMED. VcrDd3dState reserves 12 slots, which hold 8 state writes plus 4 TMU0 writes with no further room check (vcrdd_3d.c:76-122). The fog block and the compressed block reserve their own room. With one zaColor write the count is exactly 13, which matches the design. vcr3d_regs is never compared with memcmp (vcrdd_3d.h:36-44). No DDraw or 2D path writes a 3D register; the only zaColor writer is the clear. The reset sequence (include/vcr_3dseq.h) does not touch zaColor. Glide writes grDepthBiasLevel(0) at open (glide3/src/gsst.c:972,976), so a bias that D3D leaves behind cannot leak into Glide or OpenGL. The vendor's packet-1 macro ignores its chip argument (VH5/FIFOMGR.H:70-72), so its zaColor is also a chip-field-0 broadcast, the same as the design's.

MAGNITUDE AND SIGN ARE UNPROVEN. UE1 sends ZBIAS 15 and UE2 up to 15; at 3dfx's 2 LSB16 per step that is 30 LSB16 at 16-bit Z, which can show decals through nearby geometry far from the camera. The EQUAL/ALWAYS sign departs from 3dfx's rule, and there is no hardware or refrast evidence either way. The design rightly asks for a reference NVIDIA zbias_step and zbias_func run before graduation. Note that 86Box's support for fbzMode bit 16 was not verified here.
corrections: Do not append the counters to ctx_free's 513/2 line. Either use G76's VCR_EV_DD_D3DUSE 'zbias' slot (G76.md:271), counting triangles drawn while ZBIAS != 0 and FZ_DEPTH is set, or emit a separate INFO record with zbias_max, zbias_sets and biased_tris in the numeric a/b/c fields, which the 95-character text limit cannot cut. Add a source pin that the new record is not part of the 513/2 format string.

Restate fact 1 as: UE2's D3DDrv forwards SetZBias as SetRenderState(ZBIAS) whatever the caps say (UT2004 VA 0x100167e0/0x1001a809, UT2003 VA 0x10014470/0x10017aa9), but it stores the cap at render-device +0x50 (VA 0x10010ba0), and whether Engine.dll calls SetZBias without the cap is unmeasured until boot A's counter (fixed as above) reports it.

Fix the title list. Add Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe as a measured sender: D3D8, Bin/i3d2.dll VA 0x10098f64 (ZBIAS 1 on flag-bit-14 materials) and 0x1009909b (ZBIAS 0). List the UE1 D3DDrv renderers (UT436, UT, Unreal Gold, Deus Ex: ZBIAS 15 via IDirect3DDevice7, UT436 VA 0x10004ab9), Serious Sam TSE's Engine.dll and Tribes 2's OpenGL2D3D.dll as senders that matter only if those titles are switched to D3D. Drop Red Faction (no call site; this agrees with the design). Mark Halo and Thief II NewDark (Thief2.exe is D3D9) as 'only if the D3D9 runtime maps DEPTHBIAS'.

Run BF1942 in boots A and B now, through 'Host Battlefield 1942 - LAN.bat', which needs no disc; its SetRenderState(ZBIAS) sites are at VA 0x603bd9 and 0x604a3b. Remove the 'only after G72' condition. Add H&D Deluxe in-game to both boots.

Split the cap from the drawing: D3DFeat bit 2 honours ZBIAS with no caps change, and a separate bit reports D3DPRASTERCAPS_ZBIAS. Arm them on separate clean boots (one Diag change per boot). Then the bit-2 boot changes only draws that titles already ask to bias. The cap boot is the only one that can expose caps-gated senders, which boot A cannot see by construction, so run every .124 D3D title once in that boot with the counters on (Max Payne supervised, or left out: it has no static ZBIAS site).

Make zbias_clear meaningful on the box. Record in the probe log and the ring whether the clear arrived as D3DDP2OP_CLEAR inside the same DP2 as the following draw, or as Clear2 or a batch boundary: count DP2-CLEAR ops separately from Clear2 calls. Treat a pass as evidence for the restore chain only in the first case, and keep test_every_clear_forces_the_bias_back as the primary guard.

In §5.1, drop the claim that a desktop-keyed scale 'paints every strip red' in the planned runs, or say it is caught only by the source pin.
