Fullscreen 16 bpp runs on a 16 bpp PDEV, so pd->bpp equals the target format in every planned case. Keep the --zfmt d24x8 run, which does catch a Z-keyed scale.

In §2 and §3.8, record that the 24-bit values are also valid int16s for |bias| <= 8192, so bit-23 versus bit-15 sign extension does not matter. Plan B is needed only if zbias_scale at 32 bpp shows every biased strip missing (unsigned field) or every strip red up to k=2048 (a 16-bit clamp). Name both signatures in the boot B pass/fail table.

Keep the reference-card zbias_step and zbias_func runs as a gate before graduation, and add UE1's ZBIAS 15 (30 LSB16) to the bleed-through check in the boot B frames. 86Box's emulation of the bias is unverified (it would cover only 16-bit Z), so treat the 86Box bed as optional evidence for the 16 bpp path.

problems: CONFIRMED (no change needed): the gap is real as deployed. Nothing in KMD sets TRILINEAR, TLODDITHER, LOD_ODD or LODBIAS (grep). tex_view/tex_view_ext widen LODMAX identically for POINT and LINEAR (KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:779-786, 814-824). prim_caps has no MIPFLINEAR/LINEARMIPLINEAR (vcrdd_d3d.c:2036-2040), and .124 reports TextureFilterCaps 03010317 (caps_124.txt). UE2 tests exactly MIPFLINEAR: UT2003 D3DDrv.dll 0x1000f5d5-0x1000f639 checks TextureFilterCaps & 0x30000, then & 0x20000, logs 'Supports trilinear' or clears its trilinear flag; UT2003.log:42 has no such line. The hardware words check out: they are 3dfx's HOME_BOTH LINEAR row, VH5/D6MT.C:5453-5526, used for every texture on this chip (VH5/D3TXTR.C:2178-2193; D6MT.C:5660-5690). The bit values match GL5 h3defs.h:248, 307-378, 719-733. The ST0/W0 broadcast to TMU1 is in SPEC L2367-2369 ('TREX0 & TREX1') and Glide relies on it (h3 gglide.c:2538). The odd-LOD reverse flip is corroborated by the SPEC combine-unit diagram labels tc_reverse_blend / trilinear_enable / LODB[0], and by the vendor Glide note that UMA trilinear 'only works if GR_COMBINE_FACTOR_LOD_FRACTION is used on TMU 0' (H5/GLIDE3/SRC/GTEX.C:1383-1395). That note is #ifdef Q3D in the vendor tree; only our fork has it unconditionally.

Legacy filter caps are named wrong and conflict with G08 (part 1 of 2: the naming). designs/G26.md:110 calls D3DPTFILTERCAPS_MIPLINEAR 'point within a level, linear between levels'. That is the definition of LINEARMIPNEAREST (0x10). In the DDK, MIPLINEAR (0x08) is 'nearest mipmapping, with bilinear filtering applied'. 3dfx's own legacy table agrees: VH5/D3RSTATE.C:1858-1866 gives D3DFILTER_MIPLINEAR as TREX0 = REPLACE|TMINFILTER with no TRILINEAR, and :1867-1874 gives LINEARMIPNEAREST as TLODDITHER or TRILINEAR. FORCE_TRILINEAR maps MIPLINEAR to LINEARMIPLINEAR (:2252-2257). 0x08 is a mode today's HAL already draws (MIN LINEAR + MIP POINT).

Legacy filter caps conflict with G08 (part 2 of 2: the overlap). G26.md:235 and :378 gate 0x08 behind TRILIN and pin it to the tri branch. designs/G08.md:271 adds the same bit under G08's own Diag bit, and G08.md:390 pins it 'only under the bit'. The two python tests contradict each other. G08.md:273 and :581 hand LINEARMIPNEAREST (0x10) to G26, and G26 never addresses it; 0x10 is advertised today (vcrdd_d3d.c:2037) but drawn as truncated nearest-mip. The G08 contract row (G26.md:291) maps TEXTUREMIN MIPLINEAR onto MIPFILTER LINEAR. That is wrong: MIPLINEAR maps to MIN LINEAR + MIP POINT, which G08.md:163-170 has right.

Diag\D3DFeat bit collision. TRILIN = 0x400 (G26.md:259, :266 'd3dfeat >> 10') is also G27's LODCTRL (designs/G27.md:41, :331) and G31's FOGZ (G31.md:39, :375). G27 is a declared G26 dependency and will be armed in the same campaign. 'Settled by the first to land' (G26.md:488) leaves three designs' tests, README Diag rows and REGWRITE steps pointing at one bit.

tLOD[17:12] gets two owners. G26 adds vcr_tf_lodbias in a new vcr_texfilt.h and says G27 uses it (G26.md:201, :288). G27 adds vcr_tlod_lodctl with a round_q seam and says 'G26 depends on this item's round_q seam, not the reverse' (G27.md:311, :547; test :463). G27 section 5.4 (G27.md:307-311) also gives LINEAR the +0.5 nearest rounding whenever LODCTRL is armed and TRILIN is not. G26's 'NEAREST = today's words' (G26.md section 4.5; native test 1, tl0 = 0x808) therefore holds only with LODCTRL off.

levels is computed too early. G26.md:223 stores levels = lodmax - lod + 1 in tex_view/tex_view_ext, from the chain count. G26.md:230 then lets G27 (MAXMIPLEVEL raises LODMIN) and G07 (the contiguity guard lowers LODMAX) change tLOD before vcr_tf_single runs. The plumbed levels can then disagree with the tLOD actually written. Two outcomes: TRI armed on a one-level range (harmless at weight 0, but TMU1 fetches for nothing), or TRI skipped on a valid range.

The risk is understated: single-stage draws gain a new exposure to Glide residue. G26.md:444 says 'trilinear adds no new kind of exposure' and :284 says 'exactly as both already break the two-stage path'. Today a one-texture draw writes only TMU0 with REPLACE (KMD/display/vcrdd_3d.c:113-118), so stale TMU1/2PPC state cannot touch it. A TRI draw depends on TMU0's other-select and on TMU1's whole combine, because TMU other/local always come from combineMode (SPEC L2836). MesaFX's ordinary single-texture path sets TMU1's combine to GR_CMBX_ZERO (MESA/fxsetup.h:636-659), and a CLEAN Glide close does not undo the extended combine (designs/G03.md residue table).

Stale 2PPC (the same exposure). Glide enables 2PPC by default (FX_GLIDE_2PPC=1, GL5/glide3/src/gpci.c:1875), and a killed client leaves it on (G03.md:111). VcrDd3dState writes TMU0 then TMU1, and with 2PPC both writes reach both TMUs (SPEC L2838). Both TMUs end with TMU1's REPLACE|LOD_ODD word, which gives odd-levels-only mipmapping on draws that are correct today. Boot B step 5 (a clean Quake III quit) covers only the clean-close case.

Evidence correction: the bits have already run on VSA-100. G26.md:47 and :301 say no stack of ours ever set TRILINEAR/LOD_ODD/LOD_frac on this silicon. The vintage lane's d3dlab 'miplinear' mode (retro-3dfx/tests/d3dlab/d3dlab.c:177-184: single stage, MIPFILTER LINEAR) has a golden measured on .143's VSA-100 (retro-3dfx/tests/golden/d3dlab_golden.json:45-49). It goes through 3dfx's setupSingleStage HOME_BOTH row (VH5/D6MT.C:5689-5690), so these exact words have run on VSA-100 silicon without a hang. At LOD≈0 it only shows level 0 (it equals mippoint): it lowers the stability risk, but does not prove the blend.

Red Faction is overstated as a consumer. rf.exe's 'Trilinear filtering enabled.' (0x5aa788) comes from an off-by-default console toggle (rf.exe 0x54f250-0x54f2af). The toggle flips byte 0x1e65600 and calls SetTextureStageState(0, D3DTSS_MIPFILTER=0x12, LINEAR/POINT) through vtable+0xfc. It sets stage 0 only and reads no caps. RF requests nothing in a default session, and its lightmapped world is two-stage (NEAREST/DITHER, never TRI). UE2 is the real caps-driven consumer; Thief II remains inferred.

The perf A/B will measure leftover TMU1 state. Once tmu1_tri drops back to 0, VcrDd3dState skips TMU1 (G26.md section 4.4), so after a TRI draw TMU1 keeps TRILINEAR|LOD_ODD and the chain and keeps fetching through later single-stage draws. 3dfx parks an unused TMU at LODMIN=LODMAX=8 'for performance reasons' (VH5/D6MT.C:5663-5669, 0x820). Glide forces an idle TMU to 1x1 (GL5 distate.c:1596-1601; gsst.c:445 'to increase single texturing tri fillrate'). perf --fill --mip point/linear will therefore mix TMU1 leftover state into the trilinear cost. The same leftover exists today after any two-stage draw.

Minor: the arm rule includes devices 0x0004/0x0005 (G26.md:266) for an 86Box smoke test. G26 itself says that test proves only 'no hang', because 86Box samples level 0 (KMD/tools/d3dprobe.c:47-50). The rule also ignores Glide's one-TMU rule for 4 MB H4 boards (GL5 gpci.c:1189).

Unconfirmed, and already an open question: f = 0 at the LODMIN/LODMAX clamp rests on 86Box (voodoo_render.c:414-418). The SPEC says only that the LOD is 'clamped to the range [lodmin, min(8.0, lodmax)]'. If silicon keeps a nonzero fraction, then at an even LODMAX the TMU1 level past the chain is blended in. That matters most for DXT chains, which vcr_tex_chain_usable cuts short (vcrdd_d3d.c:819). trilinear_end must pass before any title, not only before graduation.
corrections: Caps: TRILIN adds only LINEARMIPLINEAR (0x20) and MIPFLINEAR (0x20000). That gives 0x03030337 with TRILIN alone, and 0x0303033F (3dfx's value) only together with G08's MIPLINEAR (0x08). G26 owns LINEARMIPNEAREST (0x10). TRI makes it true (MIN POINT with the same words), and LODDITHER makes it approximately true (3dfx's TREX0 row, VH5/D3RSTATE.C:1867-1868). Decide with G08 whether 0x10 stays unconditional until G08 lands. Fix G26.md:110, :235, :291 and :378: the python test pins 0x20 and 0x20000 to the tri branch and leaves 0x08 to G08's test.

Allocate every Diag\D3DFeat bit (and every event 513 'what' number) in one table in the plan, in the shared vcr_d3dfeat.h, before any item lands. TRILIN and LODDITHER must not reuse 0x400, which G27 and G31 both claim. Tests, the armed event and the README rows take their values from that header.

Keep one writer of tLOD[17:12]: G27's vcr_tlod_lodctl(round_q), or vcr_tf_lodbias renamed and adopted by G27 if G26 lands first, but not both. TRI passes round_q 0. DITHER passes its quarter-LOD compensation. NEAREST passes whatever G27 decides. Scope G26's native test 1 to LODCTRL off and add a row with LODCTRL armed.

Derive the trilinear eligibility inside vcr_tf_single from TMU0's final tLOD word: TRI only when (LODMAX field - LODMIN field) >= 4, one whole LOD in 4.2. This drops the tmu_view.levels plumbing and its ordering hazard against G27/G07. Add native cases where a raised LODMIN (MAXMIPLEVEL) or a lowered LODMAX turns the decision to NONE.

Make G03's baseline a precondition for arming TRILIN in any game session, not only for graduation: TMU combineMode = 0 after the SPEC's 12-NOP 2PPC exit, and TMU chromaRange cleared. The alternative is for the armed path to write TMU combineMode = 0 itself (after the NOPs) at a context's first TRI state. Rewrite the risk rows G26.md:284 and :444: single-stage TRI draws newly depend on TMU1/2PPC residue, and after an ordinary clean MesaFX session TMU1 sits at GR_CMBX_ZERO. Run G03's 'tmu1 two-stage' residue probe alongside step B5.

Use the vintage lane as the vendor reference before Boot B. Run the new trilinear, trilinear_odd, trilinear_end and trilinear_ramp probes (or a minified/ramp d3dlab mode) under 3dfx's own HAL on .143's VSA-100. It drives the same HOME_BOTH words and answers open questions 1-3 (the UMA mechanism, LOD-fraction accuracy, the far-end weight) with 3dfx's configuration. Restate G26.md:47 and :301 as 'run on VSA-100 by the vintage HAL at LOD≈0 only (.143 d3dlab miplinear)'.

Run trilinear_end (16-bit, odd and even LODMAX) before any in-game TRI session. Until it shows f = 0 at LODMAX, also keep TRI off chains truncated by vcr_tex_chain_usable (DXT): a nonzero fraction there would blend foreign bytes into distant surfaces.

Fix the games list. UE2 is the primary consumer (it checks the cap and stages UseTrilinear=True), and its gain is limited to single-stage meshes: BSP and terrain get DITHER or NEAREST. Thief II is inferred. Red Faction gains only when the player types its console toggle, and only on stage 0. Max Payne starts sending LINEAR once the cap appears (G15 notes it degrades on its own today), so its armed run stays supervised. Priority stays P2.

Armed path only: when tmu1_tri goes from 1 to 0, park TMU1 the vendor way (tLOD low 12 bits = 0x820, LODMIN=LODMAX=8), so leftover TMU1 fetches do not cost fill rate. At minimum, have perf --fill set a known TMU1 state before each mode, so the point/linear A/B measures trilinear and not TMU1 leftovers. With both bits clear the default write sequence stays byte-identical.
Restrict arming to the VSA-100 (device 0x0009). If the Voodoo3 smoke test is kept, mirror Glide's 4 MB one-TMU rule; it proves nothing about filtering in any case.

Citation hygiene: cite the vendor Glide UMA hack as #ifdef Q3D (H5/GLIDE3/SRC/GTEX.C:1383-1395). Its value is 3dfx stating that TMU0 must use LOD_FRACTION (MLODFRAC|REVERSE), which is the design's TMU0 word, not 'what Glide does'. Cite the SPEC combine-unit diagram labels (tc_reverse_blend / trilinear_enable / LODB[0]) beside 86Box for the odd-LOD reverse flip.

understand:history.summary:
History of Direct3D on the V5 6000 (.124, vcr-kmd), from the docs, git, sweep evidence and tests (read-only; no box contacted).
1. The HAL is a DX7-level NT DDI rasterizer on ONE VSA-100 (chip 0). It never touches SLI, sends PCI-FIFO register writes with a status poll per vertex, and has no CMDFIFO.
2. A fresh install gets 16 bpp targets and 256x256 16-bit textures. D3D32 and D3DBigTex add 32 bpp and 2048/DXT/8888; both have been armed on .124 since 2026-09-28.
3. Proven on silicon: the d3dprobe matrix 40/40 fullscreen and 42/42 windowed at 16 and 32 bpp; the big-texture/DXT/decode matrices (09-28, 11-08); every swept title reaches its menu or intro.
4. Correction to the brief: in-game frames DO exist for JK DF2, MotS and Thief II (D3D9 and DX6). They date from 09-28, before the 11-08 fixes, and none was compared to a reference.
5. Fixed so far: renderMode, PARMADJUST, attach-list walk, mip chains, TMU flush, D3DOP_EXIT, DXT2/4, half-pixel centre, 16-byte texture placement, and 16-over-32 Z.
6. NEW (concurrent on-box session today): X8R8G8B8+D16 is confirmed refused. The runtime says 'match', ContextCreate refuses, and CreateDevice returns 8876086c. Vendor HAL: D16 ARBITRARY_COLOR_DEPTH, 32-bit Z allocated.
7. NEW: at 32 bpp, triangles draw nothing (9/31 fullscreen, 7/35 windowed; 36 triangles sent). This came after a 4-chip Glide session ended by display reset with no HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE and Reset3D off: the documented, unproven hazard.
8. HAL gaps:
   - MODULATE2X/4X and op 16 are drawn as MODULATE; UT2003 uses MODULATE2X in 7 of 26 logged set-ups.
   - ALPHAREPLICATE and COMPLEMENT are dropped; alpha always blends ONE/ZERO.
   - Lines and points are skipped while line caps are advertised; flat shade and colour key are advertised but not done.
   - No specular, trilinear, LOD bias, ZBIAS, stencil, mirror or DESTALPHA; render-to-texture is untested.
   - ValidateTextureStageState says yes to everything.
9. Latent default-path bugs: the 16-byte placement and the 26-bit texBaseAddr exist only on the D3DBigTex path.
10. Max Payne, 10-04: the game froze; the box did not, and normal-priority work starved. No ring was taken. The frozen frame lacks the menu text the 09-29 frame shows. The cause is unknown, and .124 is 'blk' for every D3D title in the 11-11 readiness rounds.
11. Performance: there is no D3D game frame rate on our HAL. Only synthetic numbers exist (151 fps, ~30k triangles/s). AmigaMerlin's UT99 D3DDrv at 69 fps is the only reference, and the vendor's D3D ran 4-chip SLI.
12. Tests: nothing executes the state→register mapping. d3dprobe has no check for alpha test, the blend matrix, culling, indexed or fan primitives, clamp/filter, TFACTOR or RT textures, and reads only the top-left 256x256.
13. DdHeapFloor, FlipDeadline and Reset3D have never run on silicon. D3D32 and D3DBigTex are proven; their docs and tests still say 'not on silicon'.

items.title: 32 bpp D3D draws no triangles after an unreleased 4-chip Glide session (found today, Reset3D off)
items.detail: The concurrent on-box session (11-12, uncommitted) ran two d3dprobe renders on the current build. Fullscreen 1024x768x32 with D24X8: 9 pass / 31 fail. Windowed on the 32 bpp desktop: 7 pass / 35 fail. Clears pass, but every flat, gouraud, tex, blend and ztest check reads the clear colour. The ring shows a valid ContextCreate (target 0x300000 32 bpp, Z 0x600000) and 'context gone: 28 DP2, 36 triangles, 14 clears, 0 unparsed': the HAL sent triangles and none appeared. The same configuration was 40/40 on 09-28, and windowed 32 bpp was 42/42 on 11-08. Earlier in this boot, pid 0x764 took HWCSETEXCLUSIVE and 4-chip SLI (75244 s). The session ended through DrvAssertMode with 'SLI/AA off: display reset' (75345.6 s), and no HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE was logged. Reset3D is off. Even when armed it runs only at the owner's own release, never at DrvAssertMode. This is the README's 'killed Glide client needs a cold boot before 32 bpp D3D' hazard. Not proven: a cold boot with no Glide session, then the same run, separates leftover state from a code regression.

items.title: X8R8G8B8 + D16: the runtime promises the pair, ContextCreate refuses it (CreateDevice 8876086c)
items.detail: d3dprobe caps reported CheckDepthStencilMatch(X8R8G8B8, D16) = match on 09-28 and again today. vcr_rt_format(rt32,32,16) returns REFUSED, and the source comments expected the runtime to answer 'no'. Today's concurrent run of render --full 640x480x32 --zfmt d16 failed CreateDevice with 8876086c, and the ring shows 513/12 'ContextCreate refused: 32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z'. Any D3D8/9 title that picks D16 for a 32 bpp back buffer fails to start. The vendor H5 HAL publishes D16 with D3DFORMAT_OP_ZSTENCIL_WITH_ARBITRARY_COLOR_DEPTH. It states that Napalm cannot mix Z and colour depths, so it allocates a 16-bit Z request as 32-bit at a 32 bpp primary and substitutes or reallocates at attach time.
games: any D3D8/D3D9 title choosing D16 at 32 bpp (which staged titles do is unknown)

items.title: Max Payne 10-04: the game froze (not the box), normal-priority work starved, cause not established, no ring captured
The frozen Max Payne frame has no menu text; the 09-29 menu frame does
items.detail: This is my own observation; it is not in any write-up. The 09-29 capture of Max Payne's menu shows the items (Resume Game ... Quit) and a status line. Both 10-04 probe frames, and the GDI screenshot after them, show the background art and the cursor but no menu text. The two probe frames are identical (difference bbox None), and the GDI shot differs only in a box around the cursor (640,480-925,664). So the last presented frame was not a complete menu frame. That suggests the game had stopped presenting before or during its text pass, i.e. before the second capture. It argues against 'the probe caused it'. A menu fade-in is the alternative explanation (inferred).

items.title: The experiment that separates the Max Payne hypotheses
items.detail:
All runs are attended, on vcrdd 95678704, from a cold boot with no Glide session.
- Setup: Diag LogLevel=2 and a larger LogEntries, both read at boot. At the default (DEBUG, 1024 entries) the per-DP2 events wrap the ring in seconds.
- E0: no capture at all. Only agent PING/PROCLIST/WINLIST for 10 minutes, plus one early wmic to record the game's Priority and threads. Then WM_CLOSE, then vcrctl log. Look for 512 a=9 (engine give-up), the 513 a=2 counters, and 511 a=12/13 (flips, by retrace or deadline, longest read and wait).
- E1: fbshot --probe at start /high only.
- E2: the default fbshot escape, last, at normal and then high priority.
Reading the results:
- A freeze in E0 acquits the tools.
- A freeze only in E2 convicts the lock wait; E2 completing at high priority shows a priority inversion rather than a deadlock.
- Repeat E0 three times: the freeze was seen once in about four sessions.

items.title: .124 is 'blk' for every Direct3D title in the 11-11 whole-fleet readiness rounds because of the Max Payne freeze
items.detail: The readiness matrix marks .124 'blk' for 12 titles: Halo, UT2003, UT2004, Shogo, MotS, Rainbow Six, Red Faction, Thief Gold, Thief II, System Shock 2, Max Payne, AvP and H&D. The stated reason: 'The vcr-kmd README says no D3D title in an unattended sweep (Max Payne froze it on 2026-10-04). It needs a supervised session.' Resolving the freeze unblocks every D3D multiplayer round for .124.
games: Jedi Knight Mysteries of the Sith

items.title: In-game D3D frames exist (JK DF2, MotS, Thief II), but all predate the 11-08 fixes and none was checked against a reference
games: Jedi Knight Mysteries of the Sith

items.title: No Direct3D game frame rate exists on our HAL; the only numbers are synthetic
items.detail: d3dprobe perf at 640x480x16 with --novsync (300 frames of 200 textured triangles plus a clear) gave 151.2 / 151.1 / 150.9 fps, about 30k triangles/s. With vsync it held 85.0, and 84.2 at 32 bpp. The only D3D game numbers on .124 are AmigaMerlin 3.1-R11's UT99 436 D3DDrv on UTbench: 69.11 fps at 1024x768x16, 69.5 at 800x600x16, 68.1 at 800x600x32; it exits at 1280x960 and above. The bench runner already has a ut:d3d lane.

items.title: Direct3D runs on one VSA-100 (chip 0); the vendor's D3D defaulted to 4-chip SLI
items.detail: Nothing in vcrdd_d3d.c or vcrdd_3d.c touches SLI, chipMask or the SLI escape. All 3D writes go to the master's register window. On a 6000 the vendor's 3dfx Tools default is D3D SSTH3_SLI_AA_CONFIGURATION="5" ('Fastest', 4-chip SLI). The vendor reaches SLI from D3D at 3D-surface creation (Compute_SLIAA_Config, called from DDSURF.C:452) through the same miniport IOCTL Glide uses. Our D3D therefore uses one quarter of the board's fill rate.

items.title: Every vertex is register writes through the PCI FIFO with a status poll; no CMDFIFO
items.detail: vertex() calls VcrDdRoom (an uncached status read loop) and then writes up to 15 float registers. A triangle is three vertices plus BEGIN/DRAW commands, about 50 MMIO writes. State is another 12+ writes per change. Roadmap item 6 still lists 'The CMDFIFO instead of PCI-FIFO writes'. There is no CPU-cost measurement on the Athlon XP. All of this is unmeasured against games.

items.title: Texture streaming is a CPU write plus a TMU flush per draw; Halo's Bink movies run ~10x slow
items.detail: Unlock and TEXBLT mark a texture dirty. The next draw that samples it runs Glide's download-coherency sequence (2D NOP, texBaseAddr away and back, nopCMD, and an optional texture-port write-back). Halo's Bink intros played ~10x slow on vcr-kmd with halo.exe at ~100 % CPU; 'texture Lock path is the first suspect'. The staged launcher passes -novideo wherever vcrmp runs, so the cause is masked, not fixed.

items.title: MODULATE2X/4X and BLENDCURRENTALPHA are drawn as MODULATE, and UT2003 uses them
items.detail: color_path's default branch draws 'MODULATE, MODULATE2X/4X and the rest' as MODULATE. stage1_combine maps everything unknown to TM_TC_MULT. TextureOpCaps (0x184f) does not advertise them, but ValidateTextureStageState accepts them. The UT2003 log_combo capture (11-08) shows stage-0 op 5 (MODULATE2X) in 4 of 26 logged set-ups, stage-1 op 5 in 3, and stage-1 op 16 (BLENDCURRENTALPHA) in 1. Those surfaces come out at half brightness, and op 16 is wrong (inferred effect). The VSA-100 combine extension has an output shift, per grColorCombineExt's 'shift' argument.

items.title: D3DTA_ALPHAREPLICATE and D3DTA_COMPLEMENT are silently dropped
items.detail: ARG_KIND(a) = a & D3DTA_SELECTMASK removes the argument modifiers before the mapping. This is a documented gap ('rare in games'). d3dprobe's DXT alpha pass was rewritten to go through the blender so it would not depend on it. No title's set-up log has yet been checked for these modifiers.

items.title: Separate alpha blend factors are ignored; alpha always blends ONE/ZERO
items.detail: compute_regs writes AM_ASRC(BF_ONE)|AM_ADST(BF_ZERO) whatever the source and destination blend states are. At 32 bpp, where the target has an alpha channel, destination alpha receives unblended source alpha. The alphaMode register has separate alpha-factor fields.

items.title: Lines and points are parsed and skipped while line caps are advertised
items.detail: LINELIST(_IMM), LINESTRIP, the indexed line ops and POINTS are skipped by size ('not drawn yet'). D3DDD_LINECAPS is set and dpcLineCaps is filled with the triangle caps. Geometry drawn as lines (HUDs, maps, debug overlays) vanishes silently. A thin-triangle emulation is possible (inferred).

items.title: Flat shading (SHADEMODE) is never read, though COLORFLATRGB is advertised
items.detail: vcrdd_d3d.c has 0 references to SHADEMODE. Every triangle is gouraud-interpolated from its per-vertex colours. The DX7 caps advertise D3DPSHADECAPS_COLORFLATRGB. The vendor implements a shadeMode render-state handler.

items.title: Colour-keyed textures are not implemented, though TRANSPARENCY is advertised
items.detail: COLORKEYENABLE has 0 references; D3DPTEXTURECAPS_TRANSPARENCY is in the DX5-7 texture caps. 3dfx's own revision history says 'Napalm doesn't support texture chroma key'; they later re-enabled the cap 'for WHQL' and implemented colorKeyEnable in software state. DX5/6 titles that key out texels would draw them opaque (inferred).
games: DX5/DX6-era titles (inferred: Jedi Knight, Thief Gold, System Shock 2, Shogo)

items.title: Specular highlights are not drawn
items.detail: vertex() reads the specular colour only to carry the vertex-fog factor in its alpha. No specular RGB is added anywhere, and ShadeCaps carry no SPECULAR bits (D3D8 reports 00004008). The vendor advertises SPECULARGOURAUDRGB and handles render state 29.

items.title: No trilinear, no LOD bias, no MAXMIPLEVEL, anisotropy 1
items.detail: tex_view only sets the LOD range of a chain. MIPFILTER LINEAR is treated as nearest-level, and the filter caps lack MIPFLINEAR. D3DTSS_MIPMAPLODBIAS and MAXMIPLEVEL are never read, and dwMaxAnisotropy is 1. The vendor advertises MIPFLINEAR.

items.title: Not offered: ZBIAS, stencil, MIRROR/BORDER, DESTALPHA blends, P8 textures
items.detail:
Details per feature:
- ZBIAS: not in the raster caps. The vendor biases through zaColor.
- Stencil: D24S8 is listed on D24X8's storage and its stencil is never written or tested; dwStencilCaps is 0. The vendor advertises 8 stencil ops on Napalm.
- Address modes: WRAP and CLAMP only. The vendor has MIRROR.
- DESTALPHA/INVDESTALPHA: not in DestBlendCaps 0x3f, although blend_src/dst map them. The vendor advertises them.
- P8: SETPALETTE and UPDATEPALETTE are skipped.

items.title: ValidateTextureStageState always answers '1 pass, DD_OK'
items.detail: Applications that validate stage set-ups (D3D7/8 ValidateDevice) are told every combination works. MODULATE2X, op 16, ALPHAREPLICATE and the rest then degrade silently instead of letting the engine choose a fallback path. Nothing tests it.

items.title: Render-to-texture is untested; Halo runs with DisableRenderTargets
items.detail: Halo's FATAL dialog 105 (0x52cb57) is render-target creation failing. The staged config.txt sets DisableRenderTargets for 0x121a:0x0009, so the effects that need render targets are off. Render-target textures (DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE) keep DirectDraw's 4-byte placement. No d3dprobe test renders into a texture and samples it.

items.title: 16-byte texture placement exists only on the D3DBigTex path; the default path still uses DirectDraw's 4-byte placement
items.detail: The 11-08 fix (481acfd) is in mipchain_ext, which runs only when tex_ext is set. VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain's default path takes MIPMAP chains only, so a single-level texture on a fresh install (switch off) can still land at ...4 and be sampled 4 bytes early: the UT2003 bug class. The regression test pins only mipchain_ext.

items.title: The default path's 24-bit texBaseAddr samples textures above 16 MB 16 MB lower
items.detail: Without D3DBigTex the HAL writes the Voodoo3's texBaseAddr field. On a 64 MB VSA-100 whose heap reaches 27 MB, a texture placed above 16 MB is sampled from the wrong address. Any D3DBigTex bit writes all 26 bits, and d3dprobe texhigh shows the difference. This is latent on every VSA-100 install with the switch off.
games: any default-path title with >16 MB of textures

items.title: DdHeapFloor has never run on silicon; every D3DBigTex texture now goes through the single-pass allocator
items.detail: The DirectDraw heap starts at offset 0. HeapVidMemAllocAligned returns 0 for 'no memory', so the block at 0 is handed out, read as a failure and lost. ddlab vidmem showed 120 of 121 blocks. Since 481acfd every texture on the BigTex path is allocated through HeapVidMemAllocAligned, and a 0 return there becomes DDERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY. DdHeapFloor, the cure, is host- and 86Box-tested only. No 'on' run (ddlab vidmem, sdlddraw) is on record for .124.

items.title: Reset3D has never run on silicon and cannot cover a killed or display-reset Glide end
items.detail: Reset3D runs only at the exclusive owner's own HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE after a good RESTORE_MODE. When armed, it clears chip 0's chipMask, sliCtrl, combineMode, aaCtrl and stencil state. DrvAssertMode deliberately never resets, and exclusive_pid is PDEV-scoped, so a stale owner is not even reported across a mode change. No 604 a=3 event appears in any committed evidence; step 16 skipped it. Today's 32 bpp failure followed exactly such an unreleased end (history-01).
games: all Direct3D titles run after a Glide/OpenGL game in the same boot

items.title: The 16 bpp stale-stencil premise is unproven
items.detail: Only 32 bpp targets write stencilMode=stencilOp=0. The chip is ASSUMED to ignore a stale stencil enable left by a Glide/OpenGL session at 16 bpp. The planned check is a 32 bpp GL session with stencil, then d3dprobe at 16 bpp. It was never run.
games: 16 bpp D3D titles after a GL title

items.title: FlipDeadline is 86Box-only; .124's 16 bpp DirectDraw flip half rate is unresolved
items.detail: The achieved-refresh deadline is off until 'counters from real titles justify it'. Its 0.889x → 0.95x A/B cannot be shown on 86Box. ddlab measured 46.9 and 42.1 flips/s at 85 Hz on .124 at 16 bpp, against 87.4 at 32 bpp; the run is confounded and not the completion rule. d3dprobe perf at 16 bpp with vsync held 85.0 fps. No game's 511 a=12/13 flip counters are on record.
games: 16 bpp Direct3D titles (JK, MotS, SS2, Thief Gold, R6, Red Faction)

items.title: D3D32: proven and in daily use, but four blockers remain before default-on
items.detail:
Verified on 09-28 (step 16: 40/40, 42/42, perf 84.2; H&D starts) and armed since. Remaining:
1. Today's 'no triangles after an unreleased Glide session' (history-01).
2. The X8R8G8B8+D16 refusal, which a default-on D3D32 exposes to every 32 bpp D3D8/9 client (history-02).
3. The 16 bpp stencil premise and Reset3D.
4. The README's LAN-party caution.
The README's other two blockers are gone: Rainbow Six is fixed by be58b7d and Thief II works. Flipping the default needs a MOVED_DIAG entry with evidence and a change to test_d3d32_is_a_default_off_switch.

items.title: D3DBigTex: verified on silicon and armed for six weeks, but the docs still say 'not on silicon' and the raw outputs are not committed
items.detail:
Evidence that it works: commit 4ef226e (09-28) records tex512..2048, mip2048, texhigh, dxt1/3/5 and tex8888 passing; 481acfd (11-08) records the big/DXT matrix at 100/0 including dxt5_big_*.
Where the docs still say 'NOT yet on silicon': the README row and Status paragraph, tests/README.md:239 and the bigtex test docstring. Roadmap item 6 still says UT2004 dies at 256x256.
Case for at least partly defaulting it: the default path's alignment and 26-bit address bugs (history-23, history-24).

items.title: The Rainbow Six fix rests on one image; 95678704 has never had a full sweep
items.detail: The 11-08 'fixed driver' re-sweep ran at 02:08 on 13256e46, and Rainbow Six still errored in it. The 16-over-32 Z fix (be58b7d, vcrdd 95678704) was committed at 02:41 and is evidenced only by RainbowSix_intro_then_menu_z16in32.png. The fix applies only with rt32 (D3D32 armed). The compat DB still says 'untested'.

items.title: UT2003: menu text fixed, in-game unseen, combine ops still degraded
items.detail: The coloured-noise fonts were DXT5 512xN pages DirectDraw had placed at ...d6b4; they were fixed by 16-byte placement (13256e46). The 11-08 sweep had also dropped UT2003 to 640x480. Its menu combos include MODULATE2X and BLENDCURRENTALPHA, which are drawn as MODULATE (history-12). The compat DB says 'untested', and the game is blk in readiness.

items.title: The AvP library fix (11-12) was never run on .124
items.detail: AvP asserted before creating any D3D device because 154 disc files were still InstallShield-obfuscated. They were decoded in place (3f3d1bd) and deployed fleet-wide (9bcb565). The proof lists .110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240 reaching the menu, but not .124. AvP has therefore never created a D3D device on vcr-kmd. Earlier, its stall showed the old desktop at 640x480x16.

items.title: Red Faction: the 09-29 black frame came from an unfocused run; its cause was never established
items.detail: On 09-29 the scanned-out frame was black (extrema 0/0), and the sweep recorded 'close keys withheld - game not focused'. On 11-08, with the game focused, a 3D object appeared at 30 s and the menu at 60 s, apparently on the same vcrdd build (b63ea6a5). The plan lists it as 'now renders its menu' without a cause. In-game was never seen.

items.title: Shogo's main menu is not clearly evidenced on vcr-kmd
items.detail: The 11-08 30 s frame shows the SHOGO intro logo. The 60 s frame is near-black (mean 2.0, max blue 82) inside a warped light-blue border, and the 09-29 frames were mean 1.6 at both samples. The plan groups Shogo with titles that 'render their menus or intros correctly'. The compat note 'client menu renders intermittently' dates from the GeForce2 era.

items.title: Halo: only the menu is verified, behind three workarounds
items.detail: The textured menu renders at 1280x960 after DXT2/DXT4 were aliased to the DXT3/5 hardware formats (4ef226e). It runs with DisableRenderTargets and -novideo (Bink ~10x slow). 'Gameplay needs a person' because the menu ignores synthetic input. The game is withheld from readiness rounds on .124. The SSE2 floor in its requires.json is 'at least partly wrong'.

items.title: Thief II's D3D9 display depends on D3D32 plus D3DBigTex bits 0 and 2
items.detail: NewDark 1.26's D3D9 display is 32 bpp only and needs a pow2(screen) X8R8G8B8 texture. The staged launcher keeps cam_ext.cfg only when vcrmp runs AND D3D32=1 AND D3DBigTex has bits 0 and 2 set; otherwise it falls back to the 640x480 DX6 display. It ran in mission on 09-28. It ignores WM_CLOSE (force-closed in sweeps).

items.title: Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe requires 32 bpp Direct3D
items.detail: Its launcher forces 'Display bitdepth' 32. With D3D32 off the game says 'Unable to initialize graphics ... requires DirectX 8'. With D3D32 on, the menu renders over a 3D scene (11-08). The compat DB says it 'stops at profile creation'. In-game was never seen.

items.title: Jedi Knight DF2 / MotS: the D3DOP_EXIT fix; legacy DX5 paths are exercised only by games
items.detail: The DP2 walker had answered COMMAND_UNPARSED at a DX5 execute buffer's EXIT (opcode 11), 47 times in one run, and D3DIM's fallback crashed JK.EXE. EXIT now ends the walk with DD_OK. JK then rendered its first level at 1280x960x16, and MotS ran 7,014 DP2 calls and 342k triangles with 0 unparsed. d3dprobe is D3D8-only, so execute-buffer, DX5/6 texture-handle and colour-key paths have no lab test.
games: Jedi Knight Mysteries of the Sith

items.title: Battlefield 1942 single player is blocked by SafeDisc 2.80 (not our driver)
items.detail: SafeDisc 2.80.010 in Mods\bf1942\Mod.dll raises 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM'. The LAN host launcher runs the dedicated server, and the join needs a partner. The game never reaches the HAL in single player.

items.title: The compat DB's Direct3D rows for .124 are mostly GeForce2-era
items.detail: The H&D, Thief Gold, Thief II, UT2004, Shogo, JK, MotS, AvP and Red Faction rows were measured on 2026-08-31, when .124 had a GeForce2 GTS; the V5 was first reported 09-01. All are flagged stale. Only the Max Payne and SS2 rows (09-29) are vcr-kmd results. The 11-08 results were never recorded, so Rainbow Six and UT2003 still read 'untested'.
evidence: CLAUDE.md Driver Stack Map (.124 V5 reported 2026-09-01)

items.title: Large parts of the HAL have no d3dprobe check
No host test executes the state→register translation
items.detail: The python D3D tests are source-text assertions on particular lines (PARMADJUST, opcode cases and the like). color_path, blend_src/dst, cmp, stage1_combine, fvf_layout and compute_regs sit in the DDI file, whose Microsoft DDK headers are not committed, so they are never run on the host. vcr_rtfmt.h, vcr_3dseq.h and vcr_texlod.h show the Win32-free-header pattern that would make them testable.

items.title: The recorder wraps within seconds of D3D play; no ring per title or for the freeze
items.detail: LogLevel defaults to 3 (DEBUG) and LogEntries to 1024, both read at boot. Per-DP2 DEBUG events (513 what 8, target changes; what 14, stage textures) fill the ring quickly: today's two probe runs used ~400 entries. No sweep saved a ring per title, and none was taken after the Max Payne freeze. log_combo (INFO 513/21-23) has been captured only for UT2003.

items.title: Capture tooling under D3D exclusive mode: fbshot is blocked, --probe is slow, sweeps rely on GDI
items.detail: The default vcrctl fbshot waits on win32k's display lock under a D3D exclusive app. --probe works but crawls when the game holds the CPU. The rule is no vcrctl or ExtEscape while a D3D game runs. lan_sweep's verdict frames are the agent's GDI SCREENSHOT; for a flip-chain game that may return either buffer (inferred). Sweep verdicts are therefore menu-level 'alive, no error window'.

items.title: A failed CreateDevice makes the D3D8 runtime switch modes twice in 156 ms
items.detail: Today's D16 refusal test: the runtime set 640x480x32 and reverted to 1280x1024x32 156 ms later during its own cleanup. d3dprobe's paced exit hold never got a chance. Any probe of a refusal case (or a game whose CreateDevice we refuse) re-syncs the 1998 CRT twice almost at once, which breaks the pace rule. The on-box agent did not repeat it.

items.title: Documentation drift and undocumented switches
Several verification claims exist only as prose
No soak and no checked in-game scene for any D3D title since the 11-08 fixes
items.detail: The longest Direct3D runs on record are JK DF2's ~1 minute and the 30/60 s sweep samples. GL and Glide titles got 20-30 minute multiplayer soaks on the fleet servers. Since 11-08 no gameplay scene exists for any title. Gameplay has never been seen on vcr-kmd for Halo, UT2003/UT2004, H&D, Red Faction, Shogo, SS2, Thief Gold, R6, Max Payne, AvP or BF1942.

items.title: DirectDraw items the D3D and 2D titles depend on
items.detail:
What works:
- The DDraw HAL reports BLT, BLTCOLORFILL, READSCANLINE and FLIPNOVSYNC; there is no stretch blit and no overlay.
- Flips latch at retrace (WASSTILLDRAWING until then).
- The 2D titles render their menus: RA2/YR, TS, StarCraft, and WC2, whose 8 bpp surface is black to GDI and visible only via fbshot.
Open: Descent's DOSBox output=ddraw falls back to 640x400 for an unknown reason. ddlab sdlddraw was built to name the failing step and has never run on silicon.

understand:games.summary:
Per-title Direct3D requirement table for .124 (V5 6000, vcr-kmd), built read-only from staged configs and binaries, the KMD code, the evidence trees and the vendor H5 HAL.
1. Fifteen titles are routed to our D3D HAL: UT2003 and UT2004 (D3D8 D3DDrv); Halo and Thief II NewDark (D3D9); Max Payne, H&D Deluxe, Red Faction and BF1942 (D3D8); Shogo, System Shock 2, Thief Gold and Rainbow Six (DX6-era IM); Jedi Knight, Mysteries of the Sith and AvP (DX5 execute buffers).
   - Two have never reached a device on .124: BF1942 (SafeDisc 2.80) and AvP (game data until the 11-12 library fix; .124 was not in the 7-box proof).
2. The rest of the library on .124:
   - DirectDraw-only 2D: RA2/Yuri, Tiberian Sun, StarCraft, Warcraft II, Descent II Win95.
   - DirectDraw output: DOSBox (Descent 1/2 output=ddraw still show a black 640x400) and the software renderers.
   - Seven titles have dormant D3D renderers: UE1 x3, Turok 2, Carma 2, Descent 3, GoldSrc, Serious Sam, Tribes 2. .124 routes them to Glide/OpenGL.
   - WCP, Rogue Squadron and DBTS are not on .124 (max_os win9x).
3. Measured defect: UT2003's logged stage set uses D3DTOP_MODULATE2X in stage 0 and stage 1 (sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt). The HAL draws it as MODULATE (vcrdd_d3d.c:714, :862), so UE2's lit world is half-bright once in game. The VSA-100 has combineMode OUTSHIFT_2X and 3dfx used it (D6MT.C:649-652).
4. Hard requirements: seven titles need D3D32 and/or D3DBigTex, both default OFF.
   - H&D: "Unable to initialize graphics" without D3D32.
   - UT2004: CreateTexture fails without D3DBigTex.
   - Halo: white menu without DXT2/4, and a FATAL dialog unless config.txt carries DisableRenderTargets.
   - Thief II: drops to the DX6 path at 640x480.
5. Advertised but not done:
   - lines/points are dropped;
   - texture colour key (TRANSPARENCY cap) is ignored;
   - ValidateTextureStageState says OK to everything;
   - the D3D8 runtime reports X8R8G8B8+D16 as matching, but ContextCreate refuses 32/16.
6. Missing but hardware-capable: Z bias, W-buffer (USEW currently disables depth), trilinear/LOD bias, MIRROR, specular, SRCCOLOR source blend, dest alpha, P8/A8/L8/A8L8/X8R8G8B8 textures (Halo's format names), stencil at 32 bpp. Cube maps and T&L are hardware limits.
7. Stability: Max Payne froze the box 2026-10-04, cause unknown, and nothing in game has been checked since the 11-08 fixes.
   - In-game frames exist only for JK, MotS and Thief II (09-28).
   - The compat DB's .124 rows are mostly GeForce2-era (08-31).
8. Performance: D3D runs on one of four chips (vendor promoted 3D to SLI). Registers go through the PCI FIFO per vertex, every Lock drains the engine (suspected cause of Halo's 10x-slow Bink), and the 16 bpp flip half-rate is unexplained.
9. Config fixes for the user's choices:
   - UT2003/2004 stage UseVSync=False; Red Faction stages Vsync=0, and its FLEETRES resolution goes to HKLM while it runs 640x480x16 (likely reads HKCU).
   - Thief II stages 8x MSAA against "no AA".

items.title: UT2003: MODULATE2X in stage 0 and stage 1 drawn as MODULATE (half-bright lightmaps and lit meshes)
items.detail:
The HAL's own log_combo dump of UT2003's texture stages shows:
- stage 1 COLOROP 5 (D3DTOP_MODULATE2X) on combines 1, 5 and 6;
- stage 0 COLOROP 5 (MODULATE2X of texture and diffuse) on combines 3, 10 and 12.

color_path maps every unhandled op, MODULATE2X included, to MODULATE. stage1_combine maps it to TM_TC_MULT; the logged textureMode 0x800242cf carries 0x24000 = MULT. The world lightmap pass and vertex-lit actors therefore come out at half intensity in game. Only menus have been seen, and they use SELECTARG1/MODULATE.

Fix: the VSA-100 combineMode has SST_CM_CC_OUTSHIFT_2X/4X (FBI) and SST_CM_TC_OUTSHIFT_2X/4X (TMU), and 3dfx's HAL uses them for D3DTOP_MODULATE2X/4X. Needs a d3dprobe check (stage-0 and stage-1 MODULATE2X cells) and a host test.
evidence: KMD/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108/UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt (combine 1 'ops: s0 2 2 1 a 2 2 1 s1 5 a 2'; combine 3 'ops: s0 5 2 0 a 4 2 0')
KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:714 (default: MODULATE, MODULATE2X/4X, and the rest)
KMD/display/vcrdd_d3d.c:862 (tc = TM_TC_MULT; MODULATE(2X/4X) and the rest)

items.title: UT2004: same MODULATE2X stage sets on the same D3DDrv code path
items.detail: UT2004's D3DDrv.dll is the same Unreal Engine 2 renderer as UT2003, and its ini carries the same D3DDrv settings. The MODULATE2X stage sets measured on UT2003 are expected here too, so the lit world will be half-bright in game. Only UT2004's menu has been seen (11-08 PASS). Confirm with the same log_combo harvest during a supervised in-game run.

items.title: UT2003/UT2004 need D3DBigTex (2048, DXT1/3/5, A8R8G8B8) and D3D32, both default OFF
UE2 asks for trilinear, LOD bias -0.5, cube maps, detail textures, Z bias and projectors; none is advertised
items.detail:
What the staged ini and D3DDrv ask for, and what our caps give:
- Staged: UseTrilinear=True, DefaultTexMipBias=-0.5, UseCubemaps=True, DetailTextures=True. D3DDrv also probes 'Supports Z biasing' and has SetZBias/SetProjectorMaterial.
- Our caps: no MIPFLINEAR, no MIPMAPLODBIAS, no CUBEMAP, no ZBIAS, 2 stages.
- UE2 falls back: multipass ('No stages left for ...'), 'not using cubemaps', no bias. Decals and projectors may z-fight or misproject (inferred).
- Our vertex path drops the q coordinate (vcrdd_3d.c:211-222), so projected texture coordinates would be wrong (inferred).

Hardware status:
- Z bias: zaColor + SST_ENZBIAS.
- LOD bias: tLOD SST_LODBIAS.
- Trilinear: SST_TRILINEAR / LOD_ODD+TSPLIT, partial.
- Projected texture coordinates: per-TMU 1/W (inferred).
- Cube maps: not possible on this chip.
evidence: UT2004/System/D3DDrv.dll UTF-16 strings 'D3D Driver: Supports Z biasing', 'Supports LOD biasing', 'Supports trilinear', 'D3D Device: not using cubemaps', 'No stages left for lightmap'

items.title: UT2003/UT2004 staged UseVSync=False contradicts the user's vsync-on choice
items.detail: Both staged inis set UseVSync=False, and the DirectDraw HAL advertises DDCAPS2_FLIPNOVSYNC and honours DDFLIP_NOVSYNC. The UE2 titles therefore present without vsync and tear. Fix in the library (per 3dfx box via FLEETRES), or with a driver-side force-vsync switch.

items.title: Halo depends on D3DBigTex=7 + D3D32 and on its config.txt DisableRenderTargets for 0x121a:0x0009
evidence: REPO/../retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md:435-442 (Halo 2026-09-28: armed switches, FATAL 105, white menu without DXT2/4)
docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:627 (textured main menu, gameplay needs a person)

items.title: Halo names A8/Y8/AY8/A8Y8/P8-bump/X8R8G8B8 bitmap formats that the HAL does not offer
items.detail:
halo.exe carries the bitmap format names a8, y8, ay8, a8y8, p8, p8-bump and x8r8g8b8. Our texture list is 565/1555/4444, plus A8R8G8B8 and DXT1-5 with BigTex; there is no L8, A8, A8L8, P8 or X8R8G8B8.

Halo's reaction to the missing DXT2/4 was to draw white rather than convert. HUD, effect or detail bitmaps in these formats may therefore render white or missing in gameplay (inferred).

The VSA-100 samples A8, I8 (=L8/Y8), AI44 and AI88 (=A8L8) natively, P8/AP88 with a palette, and ARGB8888 (usable as X8R8G8B8 with the alpha ignored) (Glide base formats, inferred).
evidence: LIB/Halo/halo.exe strings: a8 y8 ay8 a8y8 p8 p8-bump x8r8g8b8 a8r8g8b8 dxt1 dxt3 dxt5

items.title: Halo's Bink video runs ~10x slow on vcr-kmd; every DirectDraw Lock drains the engine
items.detail:
Halo's Bink intros were still playing 13 minutes after launch at ~100% CPU, so the launcher now passes -novideo whenever vcrmp runs. FINDINGS names the texture Lock path as the first suspect.

Dd_Lock calls VcrDd2dSync on every lock: a full engine drain, regardless of whether the surface is in use. Every Unlock also marks the texture for a TMU cache flush. A movie that updates a texture per frame serialises CPU and chip. Whether Bink also reads VRAM back is unverified.
evidence: FINDINGS.md:446-450 (Bink ~10x slow, -novideo, Lock path first suspect)

items.title: Halo gameplay never seen: decal depth bias, stencil, specular, cube maps, fog; SSE2 floor unproven
evidence: LIB/Halo/halo.exe strings: DEPTHBIAS, CCW_STENCILFAIL, cube map, DisableSpecular, environment_fog, -useff, -use00, -timedemo

items.title: Max Payne froze the box on 2026-10-04, cause not established; default fbshot cannot see it
items.detail:
Max Payne (D3D8 via e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll, 1280x960x32) stopped responding during the fbshot --probe session. The user saw it frozen with Num Lock alive, and a forced close restored the desktop.

Because of this, no D3D title runs in an unattended sweep. The default vcrctl fbshot parks in win32k under its exclusive mode; fbshot --probe works.

Next step: a supervised run with the flight-recorder ring (LogLevel 2) and fbshot --probe.
evidence: docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:553-556 (Max Payne stopped responding, cause not established)
KMD/README.md:156 (fbshot parks under a D3D game; --probe finished)

items.title: Max Payne renderer needs: 32 bpp (D3D32), DXT, render targets, optional cube maps and bump
evidence: LIB/MaxPayne/e2driver/e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll strings (D3DTEXOPCAPS_*, cube maps, DRV_setRenderTarget, DXT1-5, CreateVertexShader (software))

items.title: Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe forces 32 bpp: hard D3D32 dependency; in game unchecked on our HAL
evidence: KMD/README.md:788 (H&D forces 32 bpp, failed 'Unable to initialize graphics', starts with D3D32)
Bin/i3d2.dll strings: 'cannot build lightmap with compressed textures', 'cannot find bumpmap texture format', 'A220 - Reflection map'

items.title: Red Faction: staged resolution/depth never applied (HKLM vs HKCU) and Vsync=0 staged
items.detail:
The launcher writes Resolution Width/Height/Bit Depth (1280x960x32) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction. The game's per-user state lives in HKCU: install.reg puts UpdateRate and Vsync there, and the card detection writes 'Video Card 0' there.

Both 11-08 sweeps measured 640x480, and the 09-29 scan-out was 640x480x16@85. So rf.exe very likely reads HKCU and FLEETRES's values never land (inferred).

The staged Vsync=0 also contradicts the user's vsync-on choice.
evidence: LIB/RedFaction/README-FLEET.txt:78-82 (Video Card 0 values written to the same HKCU key)

items.title: Red Faction: the 09-29 black frame was never explained; in game never seen; D16@32 risk once 32 bpp lands
items.detail:
On 09-29 the scanned-out frame was black: 'the game draws nothing visible through our D3D HAL'. By 11-08 the menu rendered, with no recorded cause, so a regression could hide here.

RF's hard requirements are met (MODULATE, SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, 8 MB). It also uses detail textures, trilinear (lost), fog and GeoMod dynamic textures (the Lock path, inferred).

If its 32 bpp setting starts to apply, its D3D8 Z choice may hit the X8R8G8B8+D16 refusal ('Device creation failed!'). Timedemo switches (-timedemo, -frameratetest) exist for measuring it.
evidence: rf.exe strings: 'Your video card is missing the following features required by Red Faction', 'Texture blending mode = Modulate', 'Trilinear filtering enabled.', 'Unable to initialize DirectX 8.0 -- Device creation failed!'

items.title: Rainbow Six: fixed to its menu by the 16/16 Z rule; in game unchecked; colour-keyed surfaces and palettized textures
evidence: RainbowSix.exe strings: 'Surface::SetTransparentValue', 'CheckForPalettized() : CreatePalette()', 'Create palette failed while loading surface (loadtex)'

items.title: Shogo (LithTech 1.0 d3d.ren): prefers 8-bit palettized textures, checks the SRCCOLOR source blend and 1-pass lightmaps
evidence: Shogo/d3d.ren strings: 'Couldn't find suitable 8 bit texture format.', 'Src blend SRCCOLOR: %s, Dest blend SRCALPHA: %s', 'Using 1 pass lightmapping!', 'Z-test: %s, Table fog: %s, Palette alpha: %s'

items.title: System Shock 2 (Dark DX6): menu only, default 640x480, nothing in game ever checked
items.detail:
SS2's game binary is inside the SafeDisc-v1 SHOCK2.ICD, and it runs under DAEMON Tools. It reaches its menu (09-29, 11-08) at the engine default of 640x480, since no game_screen_size is staged.

The Dark engine's lgd3d is DX6: 16-bit textures, alpha, lightmaps (2 stages or 2 passes) and fog (inferred). It also checks the texture memory the driver reports, and our dwVidMemFree is a constant (inferred effect). It ignores WM_CLOSE.

items.title: Thief Gold (Dark DX6 lgd3d): menu/intro only; checks the driver's texture-memory report
items.detail:
THIEF.EXE uses lgd3d d6Render/d6Prim_s/d6Frame (DX6) and carries 'Direct3d device driver does not accurately report texture memory usage'. Our DirectDraw HAL sets dwVidMemTotal/Free once at heap creation; how the runtime reports free texture memory from it is inferred.

No resolution is staged, so it runs at 640x480. Only intro and menu have been seen; in game, never.
evidence: LIB/ThiefGold/THIEF.EXE strings: x:\prj\tech\libsrc\lgd3d\d6Render.cpp, 'Direct3d device driver does not accurately report texture memory usage.', 'Using D3D device: %s'
LIB/ThiefGold/Play Thief Gold.bat (start thief.exe, no FLEETRES)

items.title: Thief II NewDark: needs D3D32 + D3DBigTex bits 0+2; staged 8x MSAA, 16x aniso, trilinear and distortion FX
Jedi Knight DF2 (DX5 execute buffers): played after the D3DOP_EXIT fix, but before the 11-08 fixes; re-verify
items.detail:
JK crashed in D3DIM until the DP2 walk accepted the execute-buffer EXIT opcode (11). It then played at 1280x960x16 on 09-28.

The frame shows point-sampled textures. MotS, the same engine, is filtered, so this is probably JK's own option (inferred).

Not yet checked: whether its colour-keyed textures and automap lines draw (both inferred needs: COLORKEYENABLE is ignored and lines are skipped). Menus are 8 bpp DirectDraw.

items.title: Mysteries of the Sith: PASS in D3D 1280x960 (7,014 DP2, 342k tris, 0 unparsed) before the 11-08 fixes
items.detail: MotS is the best-proven execute-buffer title: in game, bilinear-filtered, with a clean quit, on 09-28. It needs re-verification after the half-pixel, alignment and 16/16 changes. Watch colour-keyed textures and lines (inferred needs).

items.title: Aliens vs Predator has never reached a D3D device on .124; library fixed 11-12 but .124 untested
items.detail:
Every .124 run of AvP died on game data (alt_tab.cpp:198) before creating a D3D device. 154 obfuscated files were decoded in the library on 2026-11-12, and 7 boxes reached the menu; .124 was not one of them.

AvP is Direct3D-only (DX5/6 IM via DirectDraw 6, execute-buffer error table). It picks palettized or 16-bit RGB texture formats; we offer no P8, so it uses 16-bit. It is the next execute-buffer title to meet the HAL (needs the D3DOP_EXIT handling) and may use colour keys (inferred).
evidence: avp.exe strings: 'chosen %u-bit palettized texture format', 'AwSetD3DDevice() OK', D3DERR_EXECUTE_*

items.title: Battlefield 1942: blocked by SafeDisc 2.80 before D3D; then an HTL warning, cube maps, stencil and DXT
evidence: BF1942.exe strings: 'does not support Hardware Transform and Lighting (HTL)', 'makeNormalizedHalfVectorCubeMap() Failed to create cubemap', 'SStencilEnable', '32bit depth buffer'

items.title: X8R8G8B8 + D16: the D3D8 runtime reports a match, ContextCreate refuses the pair
items.detail:
The live caps say zmatch X8R8G8B8/D16 = 1, but vcr_rt_format refuses a 32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z (DDERR_INVALIDPIXELFORMAT). A D3D8/9 title that picks D16 at 32 bpp gets a failed CreateDevice.

None of the titles run so far hits it. At risk: Red Faction once its 32 bpp setting applies, BF1942 (depth choice), and fresh installs.

The chip has no 32-colour/16-Z mode. A driver-side fix could back D16 with 32-bit storage while rt32 is on, the reverse of the Rainbow Six 16/16 fix (inferred design).
evidence: KMD/include/vcr_rtfmt.h vcr_rt_format (32 bpp needs z_bits 0 or 32)

items.title: Lines and points are parsed and skipped while line caps are advertised
items.detail:
VcrDdD3dHalInfo sets D3DDD_LINECAPS and fills dpcLineCaps with the triangle caps. The DP2 walk skips LINELIST(_IMM), LINESTRIP, INDEXEDLINE* and POINTS. HUD, automap or tracer lines simply vanish.

Likely users (all inferred): JK/MotS automap, Rainbow Six planning overlays, Halo, UE2. Thief II already stages pixel_parts_as_disks / square_parts_as_disks.

Which titles really send lines is unmeasured. A per-context skip counter in the 'context gone' log line would show it. 3dfx's HAL has D6LINE.C/D6POINT.C.

items.title: Texture colour key: TRANSPARENCY is advertised but D3DRENDERSTATE_COLORKEYENABLE is never read
items.detail:
prim_caps advertises D3DPTEXTURECAPS_TRANSPARENCY, but compute_regs has no colour-key handling (no COLORKEY/CHROMA anywhere in vcrdd_d3d.c). DX5/6 titles that colour-key textures will show the key colour.

Likely affected (inferred): JK and MotS, which carry DDERR colour-key handling; Rainbow Six (SetTransparentValue); AvP.

3dfx's HAL maps a texture's CKSRCBLT key into the chromaKey register when COLORKEYENABLE is set. The hardware tests it after the bilinear filter, a known 3dfx limit.

items.title: Depth: ZENABLE=D3DZB_USEW turns depth OFF; no W-buffer and no Z bias although fbzMode has both
items.detail:
compute_regs enables depth only when ZENABLE == D3DZB_TRUE, so a title that sets D3DZB_USEW (2) without checking caps loses depth testing entirely. WBUFFER and ZBIAS are not advertised; caps-checking titles therefore fall back (UE2 and Halo decals lose their bias).

The register header defines FZ_WBUFFER and FZ_ZBIAS, and 3dfx implements both (zaColor bias, SST_WBUFFER for USEW).

Which titles set USEW or ZBIAS is unmeasured (inferred: Dark engine, DX6 titles, UE2, Halo).

items.title: ValidateTextureStageState always answers 1 pass/OK; stage-1 ops and argument modifiers are approximated
Specular RGB, flat shading, separate alpha blend and destination alpha are ignored
items.detail:
Four render-state gaps:
- Specular: vertex() feeds only the diffuse colour; the specular alpha is used solely as vertex fog.
- Shading: SHADEMODE is never read, so everything is gouraud.
- Alpha blend: always ONE/ZERO on the alpha channel.
- Destination alpha: DESTALPHA is not offered.

Caps are honest for specular and dest alpha (ShadeCaps 0x4008, DestBlendCaps 0x3f), so titles fall back. Specular highlights (Halo, UE2, Max Payne; inferred) are lost. 3dfx advertised specular gouraud, and dest alpha on Napalm at 32 bpp.
evidence: KMD/display/vcrdd_3d.c:187 (argb = diffuse only), :202-208 (specular alpha as fog)

items.title: Direct3D renders on one VSA-100 of four (no SLI); fill-bound titles at 1280x960x32 get a quarter of the board
items.detail:
Neither vcrdd_d3d.c nor vcrdd_3d.c programs sliCtrl or chipMask, and the Reset3D release writes sliCtrl=0. 3dfx's display driver runs Compute_SLIAA_Config at 3D-surface creation and promotes the device to SLI (Promote_DeviceToSLIAA).

The user chose no AA, so the non-AA 4-chip SLI shape is the target.

Most affected (inferred): UT2003/4, Halo, Max Payne, H&D and Thief II at 1280x960x32.
evidence: docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md:1534-1549 (vendor D3D path ends in IOCTL_3DFX_SLI_AA_ENABLE)

items.title: Triangle traffic goes register by register through the PCI FIFO (9-15 MMIO writes per vertex), not the command FIFO
items.detail:
vertex() writes sVx, sVy, the four colour floats, sVz and sOOWFBI, plus 3 per texture set, each behind VcrDdRoom. The KMD roadmap names the CMDFIFO as the next step, and 3dfx's HAL uses CFIFO.C packets.

High-polygon titles on software T&L (UE2, Halo, Max Payne) pay this cost on every triangle.
evidence: KMD/README.md:796 (The CMDFIFO instead of PCI-FIFO writes)

items.title: 16 bpp flips on .124 measured at about half the refresh (42-47 flips/s at 85 Hz), unexplained
items.detail:
ddlab's 16 bpp flip runs on .124 measured 46.9 and 42.1 flips/s; 32 bpp ran 87.4 and 86.3. The completion rule is not the cause, and the 16 bpp run was confounded.

If this is real, every 16-bit D3D title may be capped near half refresh: Shogo, JK, MotS, Rainbow Six, Red Faction as staged, SS2, Thief Gold, AvP. Needs the plan step-16 per-frame counters (511/12-13) from a real title.

items.title: No hardware T&L or shaders: every D3D8/9 title uses software vertex processing on the Athlon XP
items.detail:
VertexShaderVersion is 0 and FVFCaps 2; the HAL accepts only D3DFVF_XYZRHW. Consequences:
- UE2's UseHardwareTL=True falls back to software.
- Halo runs a fixed-function or 0.0 path.
- BF1942 warns about HTL.
- Max Payne creates vertex shaders in software.

The CPU has SSE but no SSE2. Halo's requires.json floors on SSE2 and is overridden for .124.

items.title: DirectDraw 2D titles work; the HAL has no colour-key or stretch caps, so those blits run in the HEL
items.detail:
RA2/Yuri and Tiberian Sun (16 bpp, FR resolution, TS with VideoBackBuffer=yes), StarCraft/BW and Warcraft II (640x480x8 via Storm.dll) all rendered in the 09-29 sweep. 8 bpp palettes go through DrvSetPalette.

The HAL advertises only BLT, BLTCOLORFILL and READSCANLINE: no DDCKEYCAPS, no stretch, no overlay. Keyed or stretched blits fall to the runtime's software emulation, although Dd_Blt itself can do keyed copies.

Low risk. Mainly CPU cost and capture limits: GDI cannot photograph the 8 bpp DirectDraw surfaces.

items.title: DOSBox output=ddraw (Descent 1/2) shows a black 640x400: one DirectDraw setup call fails; overlay output has no overlay caps
items.detail:
The Descent DOSBox confs use output=ddraw with fullresolution=original. The 09-29 frame mean was 0.0 at 640x400, which is DOSBox's surface fallback after one SDL DirectX5 DirectDraw call failed; which call is unknown. ddlab sdlddraw replays the sequence, and Diag\DdHeapFloor (heap block at offset 0) is the one hypothesis.

Four titles use output=overlay; we advertise no overlay, so SDL uses software YUV (inferred; they PASS).
evidence: KMD/README.md:592-611 (Descent's black 640x400 is a DOSBox fallback)

items.title: Glide/OpenGL titles keep dormant D3D renderers that .124 does not use
items.detail:
The dormant D3D paths and what .124 routes instead:
- UE1 D3DDrv (Unreal Gold, UT 436, Deus Ex; staged GameRenderDevice=D3DDrv): FLEETRES writes GlideDrv because GlideRender=1.
- Turok 2 Video_D3D.dll: Glide.
- Carmageddon 2 BRender d3d.bdd: Glide.
- Descent 3: OpenGL.
- GoldSrc hw.dll: OpenGL.
- Serious Sam (D3D8, inferred): OpenGL.
- Tribes 2 OpenGL2D3D.dll: OpenGL.

These are fallbacks only. UE1 D3DDrv was the 32-bit route under AmigaMerlin's HAL. Low priority unless a title's Glide/GL path breaks.

items.title: Library titles not on .124 with D3D paths: WC Prophecy, Rogue Squadron, Die by the Sword (Win9x-only)
items.detail: WCProphecy (GL_00005/GL_00006.DLL import DDRAW), Rogue Squadron (Rogue Squadron.EXE imports DDRAW) and Die by the Sword (rld3d.dll) are all max_os win9x and staged for the Voodoo 2 box. compat shows them absent on .124. Their DX5/6 D3D paths matter only if one is re-staged for XP. They would then need the same execute-buffer, colour-key and 16-bit texture handling as Jedi Knight (inferred).

items.title: In-game evidence gap: no D3D title seen in game since the 11-08 fixes; compat .124 rows are GeForce2-era
items.detail:
Only Jedi Knight, MotS and Thief II were ever seen in game on our HAL, all on 09-28 and before the half-pixel, alignment and 16/16 fixes. Everything else is menus or intros at most. The LAN matrix marks .124 'blk' for every D3D title.

The compat DB's .124 rows are mostly 2026-08-31 measurements on the GeForce2 GTS.

A supervised in-game pass per title, with LogLevel 2 harvesting log_combo (event 513 what 21-23) and a proposed unsupported-state log, would replace the inferred requirements here with measured ones.

items.title: Palettized (P8) textures not offered; DP2 SETPALETTE/UPDATEPALETTE are parsed and dropped

understand:hal.summary:
I audited our vcr-kmd Direct3D HAL (vcrdd_d3d.c and vcrdd_3d.c in full, plus the DirectDraw, 2D, escape and miniport paths it touches) against 3dfx's own V5 HAL, read-only. The full report has path:line evidence, opcode, state and caps tables, and a phased plan.
1. The worst gap is stability. A killed Glide client leaves its command FIFO 0 enabled. The on-box agent measured today that every D3D triangle then silently disappears while clears still work. A windowed run then made the 2D idle check time out, acceleration went off, and the D3D HAL was gone until a mode set. Nothing in our code turns off an idle-but-enabled FIFO: the miniport only resets a busy chip, and Diag\Reset3D refuses to run while the FIFO is on. D3D surfaces were placed inside the stale FIFO window, which makes this a credible freeze mechanism.
2. A dead engine is silent to Direct3D. After a give-up, DrawPrimitives2 and Clear2 still answer DD_OK and draw nothing, so the picture freezes while the game runs. That matches Max Payne's 2026-10-04 symptom. The HAL also never writes combineMode, 2-pixels-per-clock exit, clip rect 1, chroma, stipple or aaCtrl, so it relies on state Glide left behind.
3. A 32 bpp target with a D16 Z is refused although the runtime says the pair matches. Confirmed on silicon today: CreateDevice failed and the runtime made two mode switches 156 ms apart on the CRT. 3dfx allocated such a Z as 32-bit.
4. Over-promises: lines and points are advertised but skipped; texture colour key (TRANSPARENCY) and flat shading are advertised but ignored; ValidateTextureStageState says yes to everything; D24S8 is listed with no stencil; DRAWPRIMITIVES2EX is reported while state blocks (STATESET) are skipped.
5. The combine path is a small fraction of Direct3D. Argument modifiers are dropped, TFACTOR next to a texture becomes diffuse, MODULATE2X/4X become MODULATE, and stage 1 is applied before stage 0's diffuse. The first in-game frame on this HAL (UT2004 botmatch) is very dark and has block-noise textures. Mipmapped DXT and A8R8G8B8 chains have never been tested.
6. Gaps the hardware can close (3dfx's own V5 HAL shipped them): ZBIAS, W-buffer (USEW currently turns depth off), specular, texture colour key, trilinear and LOD bias, MIRROR, stencil at 32 bpp, more texture formats, and the legacy DX5 texture states, which are ignored. The default path (no D3DBigTex) still has the 11-08 texture-alignment bug.
7. Performance is bounded by the transport: PCI PIO with a status read per vertex, strips sent as separate triangles, a CPU idle wait at every flip, all under the display lock, on one chip of four.
Plan: phase 0 adds log-only counters and runs each D3D title in-game once to measure which gaps it hits. Phase 1 is the stability fixes behind a new Diag\D3DSafe bit field. Phases 2-3 are correctness and feature parity behind Diag\D3DFeat, using the VSA-100 extended combine. Phase 4 is performance (strip/fan setup mode, then the command FIFO). Every step comes with the d3dprobe tests and a new DX7 probe named in the report.

items.title: Killed Glide client's command FIFO 0 left enabled: D3D triangles vanish, then the 2D give-up removes the HAL
items.detail: Measured today on .124 with the deployed vcrdd.dll. cmdFifo0.baseSize = 0x1fe (enable bit set) with readPtr stuck. Fullscreen 1024x768x32 then scored 9 pass / 31 fail: clears worked, no triangle drew. A windowed run timed out on SST_CMD0_BUSY, acceleration went off for the desktop PDEV, and GetDeviceCaps failed (8876086a) until a mode set; after the mode-set engine reset the same probe was 40/40. Nothing stops an idle-but-enabled FIFO: the miniport resets only a BUSY chip at a mode set, and Diag\Reset3D refuses to write while the FIFO is on. D3D surfaces (including a texture at 0xc0000) sat inside the stale FIFO window 0x18000-0x117000, a credible freeze mechanism (inferred). Fix: stop cmdFifo0/1 at every mode set with no exclusive owner, and refuse plus request a reset at ContextCreate/DP2 when the FIFO is on with no owner. Proposed Diag\D3DSafe bit 0, default off until proven.
games: all Direct3D titles run after an OpenGL/Glide game was killed

items.title: HAL does not own all 3D state: combineMode, 2PPC exit, clip rect 1, chroma, stipple, aaCtrl never written
items.detail: VcrDd3dTarget and VcrDd3dState write only the legacy set. They never write combineMode on FBI/TMU0/TMU1 (nor the 12-NOP exit from 2-pixels-per-clock), clipLeftRight1/BottomTop1 (SST_ENRECTCLIP1), chromaKey/chromaRange, stipple, aaCtrl or chipMask. Glide notes that combineMode bits act even with USE_COMBINE_MODE clear, and 3dfx's V5 HAL writes all three combineModes first at every state flush. Glide's extended combine and stencil outlive even a clean close, and Reset3D (default off, owner release only) does not cover clip1, chroma or stipple. Today's register dump shows these at 0, so this was not today's cause; it is a latent fault of the same class as hal-01. Fix: a D3D baseline written once per DP2 (Diag\D3DSafe bit 1), pinned in test_vcr_kmd_d3dseq.c.
games: all Direct3D titles after an OpenGL/Glide session on the same boot

items.title: Engine give-up is silent: DP2/Clear2 return DD_OK and draw nothing, ContextCreate never checks
items.detail: give_up() sets g2d_ok=0 after 2,000,000 status reads, and VcrDdRoom then fails at once. prepare() fails, tri() returns, and DrawPrimitives2 still answers DD_OK. D3d_ContextCreate does not check g2d_ok, and flips continue, so the game keeps running behind a frozen picture until the next mode set. This matches Max Payne's 'frozen, Num Lock alive, pixel-identical frames'. Fix (Diag\D3DSafe bit 2): return a loss code from DP2/Clear2/Flip, fail ContextCreate, log once, and optionally recover through the miniport's VcrHwResetEngine.
games: any title after a FIFO or idle timeout

items.title: D3D contexts cache a PDEV pointer that a mode change frees (use-after-free risk)
items.detail: ContextCreate stores pd = lpGbl->dhpdev, and DrvDisablePDEV frees the PDEV. ctx_free calls VcrDd2dSync(c->pd), DP2 and Clear2 dereference c->pd, and a mip chain is freed with the heap pointer saved at allocation. If dxg delivers a call on an old context, or frees a chain, after a dynamic mode change or alt-tab, kernel memory is used after free (inferred: whether dxg tears contexts down first is unverified, and alt-tab was never tested). Fix: scrub g_ctx entries in DrvDisablePDEV/DrvDisableDirectDraw, re-derive pd per call, and add an 86Box alt-tab test.
games: any D3D game alt-tabbed or switching modes

items.title: Fog-table cache never invalidated after a Glide session or display reset
items.detail: pd->fog_valid/fog_loaded is reset only when a new PDEV is allocated. An exclusive Glide/OpenGL release, a set, and DrvAssertMode's device reset leave it claiming D3D's table is loaded, so table or vertex fog on the same PDEV uses a stale table. Fix: clear fog_valid in HWCSET/HWCRLSEXCLUSIVE and DrvAssertMode. This is CPU-only.
games: windowed or same-mode D3D titles with fog after an OpenGL/Glide game

items.title: 32 bpp target + D16 refused although D3D8 CheckDepthStencilMatch says yes: CreateDevice fails, two mode sets 156 ms apart
items.detail: vcr_rt_format refuses a 32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z, yet the D3D8 runtime reports X8R8G8B8+D16 as a match. Confirmed on .124 today: CreateDevice returned D3DERR_INVALIDCALL, ContextCreate logged 513/12, and the runtime's cleanup switched the CRT twice 156 ms apart. 3dfx's V5 driver allocated a requested 16-bit Z as 32-bit on a 32 bpp primary. Fix: place Z surfaces in Dd_CreateSurface with 32-bit storage when rt32 is on (Diag\D3DSafe bit 3); d3dprobe --bpp 32 --zfmt d16 must pass.
games: any D3D8 title choosing D16 at 32 bpp

items.title: STATESET skipped while DRAWPRIMITIVES2EX is reported: state blocks may record-as-apply and never execute
items.detail: The walker skips D3DDP2OP_STATESET by size. 3dfx's DX7 HAL records RS/TSS between STATESETBEGIN and END without applying them, and executes, captures and deletes blocks itself. If the XP runtime sends STATESET to a DP2EX driver (inferred), recorded states are applied at record time and ApplyStateBlock does nothing. Settle it by measurement first (a phase 0 counter), then implement.
games: DX7/DX8 titles using state blocks (Halo, UT2003, UT2004 likely)

items.title: Legacy DX5 texture render states and D3DTSS_ADDRESS ignored
items.detail: set_rs maps only TEXTUREHANDLE. TEXTUREMAPBLEND, TEXTUREMAG/MIN, TEXTUREADDRESS/U/V, WRAPU/V, BORDERCOLOR, MIPMAPLODBIAS and D3DTSS_ADDRESS (12) are stored but never read. DX5 titles therefore draw point-sampled with MODULATE only (stage-0 defaults POINT/MODULATE). DX5 MODULATE's 'vertex alpha when the texture has no alpha' rule is also lost. TextureBlendCaps advertises DECAL/MODULATEALPHA/COPY/ADD. 3dfx's NT HAL maps all of these onto stage 0, which suggests the runtime forwards them (inferred). Testing needs a DX7 probe; d3dprobe is D3D8.

items.title: Texture combine: modifiers dropped, TFACTOR mis-mapped, 2X/4X and most ops drawn as MODULATE, stage 1 applied before diffuse
items.detail:
These are the combine-path errors:
- ARG_KIND masks COMPLEMENT and ALPHAREPLICATE.
- TFACTOR paired with a texture becomes diffuse, so a TFACTOR alpha fade does not fade.
- BLENDTEXTUREALPHA/BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA are right only with TEXTURE as arg1.
- MODULATE2X/4X, SUBTRACT, ADDSIGNED and all other ops are drawn as MODULATE; alpha ops other than ADD/SELECT are drawn as MODULATE.
- Two stages compute (tex0 OP1 tex1) OP0 diffuse, which is wrong for a stage-1 ADD, SELECT, BLEND* or MODULATE2X (a lightmap at half brightness).
- Stage 1 is ignored when stage 0 has no texture, or when stage 1 only uses CURRENT/TFACTOR.
- Blending's alpha channel is always ONE/ZERO.
The VSA-100 extended combineMode (OUTSHIFT, inverts, alpha selects) and the TMU chroma registers as TFACTOR implement all of these, as 3dfx's HAL did with 19 ops.

items.title: ValidateTextureStageState always answers 1 pass / DD_OK
items.detail: Every combination is validated, including those color_path and stage1_combine approximate and more than 2 stages, so games never fall back to a path the HAL draws right. 3dfx validated: TOOMANYOPERATIONS for more than 2 stages, and specular as an argument refused. Fix: answer UNSUPPORTEDCOLOROPERATION/ALPHAOPERATION/ARGUMENT exactly where the mapping approximates, with a d3dprobe 'validate' matrix.

items.title: ZBIAS ignored and not reported
items.detail: D3DRENDERSTATE_ZBIAS is never read and RasterCaps lacks ZBIAS. The VSA-100 has fbzMode bit 16 plus zaColor, which 3dfx used: zaColor = minus (bias shifted by 1 at 16 bpp, by 9 at 24 bit) for LESS/LESSEQUAL. VcrDd3dClear rewrites zaColor, so the bias must be re-sent after every clear. Decals and bullet holes z-fight today. d3dprobe 'zbias' test.

items.title: D3DZB_USEW turns depth testing OFF; W-buffer not implemented, WINFO skipped
items.detail: Depth is enabled only for ZENABLE == D3DZB_TRUE, so an app asking for a W-buffer draws with no depth at all. The VSA-100 has fbzMode W-buffering. 3dfx reported WBUFFER, scaled rhw from WINFO, and moved vertex fog to the Z iterator when W-buffering. Fix: map USEW to FZ_WBUFFER, use WINFO, report the cap; d3dprobe 'wbuffer' test.

items.title: Table fog is always W-based (a Z-based table fogs the whole screen); vertex fog is a synthetic-W approximation
items.detail: vcr_fog_table indexes by W only, so FOGSTART/END of 1.0 or less (Z units) give every pixel full fog. 3dfx zeroed such tables (PXLFOGLIN, PRS 13517, Centipede). Vertex fog rides a synthetic 1/W through an identity ramp, interpolating 1/W rather than the factor, and is disabled when the FVF has no specular. 3dfx used an iterated fog source (FOG_Z|FOG_ALPHA; semantics inferred). d3dprobe tests 'fogtable_z' and 'fogvertex_grad'.
games: DX5-DX7 titles using table fog with Z-unit start/end

items.title: SPECULARENABLE ignored
items.detail: The vertex specular colour is read only for fog alpha, and highlights are never added. 3dfx pre-added specular to diffuse per vertex with a saturating add (CLAMP888), a cheap approximation that fits vertex() directly. Report SPECULARGOURAUDRGB afterwards; d3dprobe 'specular' test.
games: DX6-DX8 titles with lit specular materials

items.title: Texture colour key: TRANSPARENCY advertised, COLORKEYENABLE ignored
items.detail: DX5-7 caps promise D3DPTEXTURECAPS_TRANSPARENCY, but the surface's DDRAWISURF_HASCKEYSRCBLT key is never read, so keyed textures draw their key colour. The hardware has the FBI chroma key (fbzMode bit 1 + chromaKey 0x134); 3dfx expanded the key to xRGB888 by texture format, noting that the FBI tests after bilinear filtering. D3D8 has no colour key, so a DX7 probe is needed.

items.title: Lines and points advertised (LineCaps = TriCaps) but parsed and skipped
items.detail: POINTS, LINELIST, LINESTRIP, INDEXEDLINELIST(2), INDEXEDLINESTRIP and LINELIST_IMM are all skipped. HUD lines, map overlays, beams and point particles vanish. Fix: draw them as two-triangle quads through the existing setup unit; d3dprobe 'lines' and 'points' tests.
games: DX5-DX8 titles with line HUDs or point particles

items.title: SHADEMODE FLAT and FILLMODE wireframe/point ignored
items.detail: ShadeCaps advertise COLORFLATRGB/ALPHAFLATBLEND, but flat geometry is gouraud-interpolated, and DX5 execute-buffer flat flags in INDEXEDTRIANGLELIST wFlags are ignored. 3dfx handled both. Fix: send the provoking vertex's colour for all three vertices; wireframe via the line path. d3dprobe 'flatshade' test.

items.title: No trilinear, LOD dither, LOD bias or nearest-LOD rounding; MIPMAPLODBIAS and MAXMIPLEVEL ignored
items.detail: MIPFILTER LINEAR behaves as POINT. The hardware truncates the LOD where 3dfx added a +0.5 bias to round to the nearest. MIPMAPLODBIAS and MAXMIPLEVEL are never read. The VSA-100 has SST_TRILINEAR, SST_TLODDITHER, the tLOD LODBIAS field and a two-TMU LOD split; 3dfx reported MIPLINEAR/LINEARMIPLINEAR/MIPFLINEAR. d3dprobe 'trilinear' and 'lodbias' tests.
games: all mipmapped D3D titles (visible mip bands)

items.title: MIRROR addressing falls back to WRAP
items.detail: Only CLAMP sets the TM_CLAMPS/T bits; MIRROR and BORDER fall through to WRAP. The VSA-100 tLOD has SST_TMIRRORS/T (bits 28-29) and 3dfx reported MIRROR. d3dprobe 'mirror' test.

items.title: Stencil not implemented although D24S8 is listed
items.detail: dwStencilCaps is 0, the stencil states are ignored and D3DCLEAR_STENCIL is dropped, yet D24S8 is in the Z list. Apps that pick D24S8 and use stencil masks or shadows without reading StencilCaps draw unmasked effects (inferred). The VSA-100 has stencilMode/stencilOp at 32 bpp, and 3dfx reported full stencil ops. d3dprobe 'stencil' test.
games: D3D8 titles that use stencil at 32 bpp

items.title: Texture formats: no L8, A8, A8L8, A4L4, R3G3B2, A8R3G3B2 (or P8)
items.detail: The default list is 565/1555/4444; D3DBigTex adds 8888 and DXT1-5. 3dfx listed the luminance, alpha and 332/8332 formats on Napalm. P8 is disabled in the vintage tree because the palette path sampled white. Titles must convert or fail (inferred). Add the formats with d3dprobe decode tests.

items.title: Default path (no D3DBigTex) still has the 11-08 texture-alignment bug
items.detail: Without D3DBigTex, VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain places only DDSCAPS_MIPMAP chains, so every single-level texture keeps DirectDraw's 4-byte placement. texBaseAddr drops bits 3:0, and such textures are sampled up to 12 bytes early. The 11-08 fix exists only in mipchain_ext. Render-target textures keep DirectDraw's placement on both paths. This affects a fresh install, or any box without the switch.
evidence: docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md (resume point 2026-11-08: the UT2003 alignment fix)
games: all textured D3D titles on a box without Diag\D3DBigTex

items.title: Mipmapped DXT and A8R8G8B8 chains never tested; one fallback places them unaligned with no mip levels
items.detail: Every d3dprobe DXT and 8888 test uses Levels=1; only R5G6B5 chains are tested. mipchain_ext leaves a chain to DirectDraw when any level's own FOURCC differs. VcrDdD3dCreateTexSurface then sizes each level and DirectDraw places it 4-byte aligned, so the top level is sampled misaligned with no mips. This is a candidate for UT2004's in-game block noise. Add d3dprobe mipdxt1/mipdxt5/mip8888, and read events 513/19 vs 513/20 during a UT2004 run.

items.title: TMU texture cache not flushed after a 2D-engine Blt into a texture or after rendering into a texture
items.detail: VcrDdD3dTexWritten runs only on Unlock and TEXBLT. Dd_Blt and clipped_blt copying into a video-memory texture with the 2D engine, and the 3D engine rendering into a texture (SETRENDERTARGET), never mark it dirty, so the TMU can sample stale texels. Render-target textures also keep DirectDraw's possibly 4-byte placement. d3dprobe 'blt2tex' and 'rtt' tests.
games: titles using render-to-texture or DirectDraw texture updates

items.title: PCI PIO with a status read per vertex, strips/fans as separate triangles, a CPU idle wait at every flip, all under the display lock
