items.detail: vertex() calls VcrDdRoom before each vertex, writing 8-14 registers including colour as 4 floats. TRIANGLESTRIP/FAN (and the indexed forms) resend 3 vertices per triangle. Dd_Flip waits for the engine to go idle. 3dfx streamed packet-3 fans through the command FIFO. The display-lock holds fit 'everything crawled while Max Payne ran' (inferred link). Plan: setup-unit strip/fan mode and packed sARGB, then the command FIFO with a swap command, measured with a heavy d3dprobe perf scene and a UT2004 botmatch.

items.title: Minor caps: no guard band, MaxTextureRepeat 0, SRCALPHASAT advertised unverified
items.detail: Guard band 0, so the runtime clips every edge triangle on the CPU; 3dfx used -200..2048 x -200..1536. dwMaxTextureRepeat is never set; 3dfx reported 32768. SrcBlend SRCALPHASAT maps to BF_SATURATE, but 3dfx did not advertise it and 16 bpp targets have no destination alpha. Decide it with a probe.

items.title: UPDATEPALETTE parsed wStateCount times; the DDK sends exactly one record
items.detail: The walker loops n = wStateCount over header plus entries. 3dfx documents and asserts a single record regardless of wStateCount, so any other count would mis-step the stream. Low risk while P8 stays unlisted.

items.title: Smaller ignored states: WRAP0-7, STIPPLEDALPHA, BORDERCOLOR, TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS/projected coords, SETTEXLOD, MAXMIPLEVEL
items.detail: These are stored and never read. vertex() uses u,v only, so projected coordinates are wrong. SETTEXLOD (the managed-texture LOD clamp) is skipped. Mostly low impact; cylindrical WRAP has no hardware support (inferred).

items.title: 4096-entry handle table naming every mip level can fill; lookups degrade near capacity
items.detail: One open-addressing table serves all processes, and name_surface enters every attached surface. Large UE2-style texture sets can hit 'surface handle table full', after which textures draw untextured. Absent-key lookups scan to an empty slot, and handle_forget rebuilds the whole table per DestroySurface. Fix: do not name mip sub-levels, grow the table, log a high-water mark.

items.title: Max Payne freeze: cause still open, candidates now concrete
items.detail: The candidates are: (a) a stale command FIFO with D3D surfaces inside its window (hal-01); (b) a silent engine give-up (hal-03), which fits the frozen picture with Num Lock alive; (c) display-lock starvation from PIO (hal-25); (d) the game or SafeDisc 2.51. Plan: apply hal-01 and hal-03, cold boot, confirm cmdFifo0 is off, then run Max Payne attended and read the ring and registers afterwards.

items.title: DirectDraw caps under-report what the 2D engine does: no colour-key or stretch caps; DEPTHFILL to the HEL
items.detail: The 2D engine performs source colour-keyed blits, but DDCAPS_COLORKEY/DDCKEYCAPS_SRCBLT are not reported, so the runtime emulates keyed blits (inferred). No stretch cap is reported, and DDBLT_DEPTHFILL is not accepted, so both run in software.

items.title: Direct3D renders on chip 0 only; the other three VSA-100s are idle
items.detail: The HAL never enables SLI for D3D targets, and the AA/SLI work is Glide-only. 3dfx's V5 D3D used multi-chip configurations (inferred from its SLI/AA config at surface creation). This is a long-term item after the command FIFO.

items.title: First in-game D3D frames on this HAL (UT2004 botmatch): very dark, coloured block noise, striped surfaces
items.detail: Every earlier sweep checked menus only. Today's UT2004 botmatch reached gameplay, but frames show a very dark scene (luma 28), multicolour block noise on several meshes and the terrain, and horizontal stripes. Candidates: MODULATE2X loss (hal-09), DXT chain placement (hal-23), combine and format gaps. Diagnose with a LogLevel 2 run (log_combo 513/21-23, refused textures 513/7).

items.title: Per-channel colour write enables exist in renderMode but COLORWRITEENABLE is not offered
items.detail: VSA-100 renderMode bits 17-20 are per-channel write enables, written only at target setup as all-on. The DX8 COLORWRITEENABLE state could be honoured, and its misc cap reported (inferred: the D3D8 runtime reads it from DX7 misc caps). Low priority.

items.title: Hardware limits, correctly not claimed
items.detail: The VSA-100 has no hardware T&L, cube or volume textures, pixel or vertex shaders, anisotropic filtering, DOTPRODUCT3/BUMPENVMAP, BLENDOP or separate alpha blend. The caps correctly omit them (3dfx omitted bump and dot3 too), and the runtime does vertex processing in software.

items.title: Tooling: d3dprobe misses most gaps; a DX7 probe and per-context gap counters are needed
items.detail:
d3dprobe (D3D8) has no tests for the gaps above, and D3D8 cannot send legacy states or colour keys at all. Needed:
- d3dprobe additions: mipdxt1/5, mip8888, zbias, wbuffer, specular, flatshade, lines, points, validate, tfactor_tex, mod2x, areplicate, stage1_add, mirror, lodbias, trilinear, stencil, blt2tex, rtt, stateblock, d16_32, and an after-Glide-kill scenario.
- a DX7 probe for legacy states, colour keys and DX7 state blocks.
- log-only counters in the 'context gone' event recording which gaps each title hits.
Also: README still calls D3DBigTex 'NOT yet on silicon', although it passed 83/0 today.

understand:perf.summary:
I couldn't measure triangle throughput or any game frame rate: no D3D game number exists on vcr-kmd, and the one silicon test is fill-bound. The code-level findings are firm; all bus and fill timings are estimates (marked inferred) until a new triangle-rate test replaces them.
1. **The biggest structural limit is that there is no command FIFO.** Every 3D register write is an uncached store into chip 0's 31-entry PCI FIFO, and the driver reads `status` before every vertex. The CPU can only get about one triangle ahead of the chip, so the game's CPU work and the chip's drawing run one after the other instead of overlapping.
2. **Each triangle costs 27/36/45 uncached writes (untextured / 1 texture / 2 textures) plus at least 3 status reads**, roughly 5-8 µs (inferred), or about 120-220K triangles/s with the CPU doing nothing else.
3. **Strips, fans and indexed primitives are sent as independent triangles**, so strip/fan content costs up to 3x more than needed.
4. **Single-texture fill probably runs at about 1 pixel per clock.** The driver never enables the chip's two-pixels-per-clock mode, its band setting, column band or hardware guard band; 3dfx's driver and our Glide enable these by default. Today's on-box register read confirms they are off. The 151 fps `d3dprobe perf` result fits a 1 px/clk model (6.9 ms predicted, 6.6 ms measured) and not 2 px/clk (3.9 ms). This is cheap to fix and could double single-texture fill.
5. **Direct3D uses one of the four chips:** Glide measured 330 Mpix/s on one chip against 1,125 on four. At the staged 1280x960, one chip cannot hold 85 fps on overdraw-heavy scenes even at 2 px/clk (inferred).
6. **Cheaper costs:**
   - every log call formats a message and makes an IOCTL whatever the log level, including one per texture bind;
   - the full state and render target are re-sent at every DrawPrimitives2 call and every change;
   - every flip, Lock and texture upload waits for the chip to go idle.
7. **Possible bug (unverified):** frames may be drawn into the buffer still on screen while a vsync'd flip is pending, which would show as tearing.
8. **Plan:**
   - P0: add in-driver counters first; with vsync on (your choice), success is measured as the share of frames on time and the per-frame headroom, not average fps.
   - P1-P5: logging gate, 2PPC/band/column band, a lighter direct-write path, register shadows, guard band.
   - P6-P9: the command FIFO (reusable tested code exists in `scripts/3dfx/driver/nt/gbk`), a queued hardware flip modelled on our Glide, texture upload through the FIFO, then SLI last and supervised.
   - Each step sits behind its own Diag switch and gets a regression test.
9. **The command-FIFO work depends on another agent's on-box finding today:** a killed Glide client's FIFO left switched on silently stops every D3D triangle. Every baseline must start from a clean state.

Path abbreviations in the evidence below (`KMD`, `VH5`, `GL5`, `GBK`, `EV`, `PLAN`) are defined at the top of the report.

items.title: No command FIFO: every 3D write is an uncached store into chip 0's 31-entry PCI FIFO, so the CPU and the chip run one after the other
items.detail: `w3()`/`vertex()` write the setup registers straight to the PCI FIFO, and `VcrDdRoom` polls `status` before every vertex. The FIFO holds 31 entries (measured), about 2.5 vertices, so the CPU spins through each triangle's rasterisation and the chip idles while the CPU does software T&L. Frame time is roughly CPU work plus GPU work instead of the larger of the two (inferred). The register window is mapped uncached; the LFB is write-combined. 3dfx's HAL and our h5 Glide both use a CMDFIFO in frame-buffer memory with hole counting and read the read pointer only when room runs out. Fix: P6 (Diag `D3DCmdFifo`: ring at 96 KB, packet 3, fenced write-combined writes); interim P3.

items.title: 27/36/45 uncached writes plus at least 3 status reads per triangle (about 5-8 µs, inferred)
items.detail: Per vertex: one `VcrDdRoom` (one status read, plus one per spin), `sVx`, `sVy`, four float colours, `sVz`, `sOowfbi`, three writes per texture stage, and one `sBeginTriCMD`/`sDrawTriCMD`. That is 27 writes per untextured, 36 per single-textured and 45 per dual-textured triangle, with 3 or more reads, for every primitive type. The model below is inferred: a write costs 45-150 ns, and a read about 1 µs (the vendor comment says so) and also waits for every posted write ahead of it. On that model a textured triangle costs about 4.6-8.4 µs, or 120-220K triangles/s with the CPU fully in the HAL — about 700-1,300 textured triangles per 85 Hz frame at 50% CPU. Interim fix without a CMDFIFO: count FIFO credit from one status read, as the text path's `VCR_MONO.credit` does.

items.title: Two-pixels-per-clock, its band height and the column band are never programmed, so D3D fill is probably about 1 textured pixel per clock
items.detail: Nothing in the HAL writes `combineMode` (only Reset3D writes 0). `renderMode[24:22]` = 0 and `fbzColorPath[31:30]` = 0, and today's on-box register read shows `combineMode` 0, `renderMode` 0x001e0002 and `fbzColorPath` 0x0c002401. 3dfx's HAL enables 2PPC by default on Napalm, with band log2 2 and column band 2 (its comment: '6 MTexels/s' in 3DMark2000); our Glide enables 2PPC when one TMU suffices. The `d3dprobe perf` scene, computed from its own formula, draws about 0.99 Mpix of textured triangles plus a 0.31 Mpix clear per frame. Its 6.6 ms frame (151 fps) fits a 1 px/clk model (6.9 ms) and not 2 px/clk (3.9 ms). Fix: P2 (Diag `D3D2ppc`): set bit 29 in `combineMode` on FBI, TMU0 and TMU1, clone TMU0's state into TMU1, send 12 `nopCMD` on the switch to 1 px/clk, band 2, column 32. Expected up to about 2x single-texture fill (inferred).

items.title: Direct3D renders on one VSA-100 of four; Glide measured 330 Mpix/s on one chip against 1,124.6 on four
items.detail: Target and state writes go to chip 0 only, with snooping off, and SLI is enabled only at Glide's request. At the staged 1280x960 with overdraw 2.5 (inferred), fill takes 18.4 ms at 1 px/clk, 9.2 ms with 2PPC, and 2.7 ms on four chips with SLI. So a locked 85 fps at 1280x960 on one chip is marginal even with 2PPC and a CMDFIFO. SLI for D3D (P9) needs an SLI enable for the life of a fullscreen device, snooped FIFO and texture writes, room checks per chip and an SLI flip. It is the highest-risk step (SLI/AA wedge history), and SLI does not help frames limited by the CPU or the setup unit. Interim option for the operator: stage the heavy titles at 1024x768.

items.title: Strips, fans, indexed and immediate-fan primitives are sent as independent triangles, three full vertices each
items.detail: `walk()` turns TRIANGLESTRIP, TRIANGLEFAN, INDEXEDTRIANGLELIST(2), INDEXEDTRIANGLESTRIP/FAN and TRIANGLEFAN_IMM into `tri()`/`imm_tri()` calls, each sending three complete vertices. Nothing uses the setup unit's own strip/fan continuation (`SM_FAN` and `SM_NO_PINGPONG` in `sSetupMode`; one vertex plus `sDrawTriCMD`), packet-3 strips, or the vendor's autostrip (shared-edge detection, then 1-vertex continuation packets). Up to 3x fewer vertex writes are available on strip and fan content. Fix: P3 in the direct path, carried over as packet 3 in P6. Keep the odd-triangle winding equivalent.

items.title: Each vertex sends its colour as four floats and repeats sOow1, where 3dfx's HAL sends one packed sARGB and no sOow1
items.detail: `vertex()` writes `sRed`/`sGreen`/`sBlue`/`sAlpha` as floats, and for two stages an `sOow1` equal to `sOow0`. The vendor packs the colour into `sARGB` and never writes `sOow1` (case-insensitive check: no hits in `D6TRI2I.C`, `D6STRIPI.C` or `D6FANI.C`). That would take 12 to 9 writes per single-textured vertex and 15 to 11 per dual-textured vertex. A test pins the float colour (`V3D_SARGB` never written), so the change needs a Diag switch, with the default path kept floats. Dropping W1 depends on the setup unit taking TMU1's W from W0 when `SM_W1` is clear (inferred); verify with `d3dprobe tex2mod`/`tex2add`.

items.title: Logging on the drawing path: every VcrDd() call formats a message and makes an IOCTL whatever the level, and every texture bind logs a DEBUG event
items.detail: `VcrDd()` always runs `vsnprintf` and `EngDeviceIoControl`; the level is filtered only in the miniport after the round trip, and the default `LogLevel` is DEBUG, so DEBUG events are also stored. DP2 logs a DEBUG event on every `D3DTSS_TEXTUREMAP`, and on each TEXBLT and render-target change. Flip, Lock and Blt each log a TRACE event, paid for and then dropped. At about 5-15 µs per event (inferred), a title binding hundreds of textures per frame could lose several ms per frame, and the events also flood the flight-recorder ring. Fix: P1 — cache the miniport's level in the PDEV, return early, and count texture binds instead of logging them. No register traffic changes.

items.title: The full state and render target are re-sent at the first triangle of every DrawPrimitives2 call and on every change; nothing is shadowed
items.detail: `dp2walk` is zeroed per DP2 call (`prepared` = 0), so `prepare()` reruns `compute_regs()` and re-sends the target (7-9 writes) plus all state (8 FBI, 4 TMU0, 4 TMU1, maybe a NOP): about 19-30 uncached writes and 2-4 status reads. `compute_regs` also does two handle lookups, texture LOD maths and a 64-entry `log_combo` scan. TEXTUREHANDLE and TEXTUREMAP mark the context dirty even when unchanged; Clear and SETRENDERTARGET force a re-send; `Clear2` re-sends the target per rectangle. Only the fog table is shadowed. The vendor uses per-group dirty flags and writes state only if it changed. Fix: P4 (Diag `D3DShadow`, register shadows with invalidation).

items.title: A flip makes the CPU wait for the whole engine to go idle, then writes vidDesktopStartAddr by IOCTL; there is no hardware swap queue
items.detail: `Dd_Flip` returns WASSTILLDRAWING (one IOCTL per retry) until the previous flip latches, then calls `VcrDd2dSync`, a full drain, then makes the flip IOCTL plus vblank and TRACE IOCTLs; completion is polled. Today the drain costs only about one triangle because the FIFO is tiny; with a CMDFIFO it would stall the CPU for the whole tail of each frame. The vendor and our own h5 Glide (which runs on this box) queue `leftOverlayBuf` + `swapbufferCMD` in the FIFO, throttle pending swaps, and scan out through the overlay. Fix: P7 (Diag `D3DHwSwap`, after P6). Preferred route: the overlay swap, as our Glide does it. Fallback: `leftDesktopBuf` + `SST_SWAP_DESKTOP_EN`, which both existing users apply only in AA.

items.title: Render-after-flip hazard (unverified): DP2 and Clear2 draw immediately into the buffer a pending vsync'd flip is still scanning out
items.detail: `Dd_Lock` and `Dd_Blt` refuse the pending `flip_from` buffer, but DP2 and Clear2 never check it, and the HAL advertises `D3DDEVCAPS_CANRENDERAFTERFLIP` while executing writes immediately. If the D3D8 runtime does not wait (`vcr_flip.h` itself calls this 'the D3D pattern'), frame N+1's clear and first draws land in the buffer still on the CRT for up to 11.8 ms at 85 Hz. That would show as tearing or a flash, never in a GDI capture. Measure first with a P0 counter of draws into a pending `flip_from`. The real fix is the in-order hardware swap (P7); the vendor answers GetFlipStatus OK for 3D because its swap is queued.

items.title: Texture uploads and Locks make the CPU wait for the engine to go idle; each uploaded texture adds a 7-write cache flush and an uncached video-memory read
items.detail: The D3D8 runtime uploads managed textures by Lock plus CPU writes: `Dd_Lock` calls `VcrDd2dSync`, a full idle wait. TEXBLT also drains, then copies with `memcpy` into the write-combined LFB. The next draw runs `VcrDd3dTexFlush`: two 2D NOPs, `texBaseAddr` pointed away and back with a `nopCMD`, and one texel read uncached from video memory and written back through the texture port. The vendor downloads with packet 5 through the CMDFIFO, in order with draws and with no idle wait, and flushes the texture cache in the FIFO. Fix: P8 (packet-5 TEXBLT; per-surface last-use fences for Lock), after P6.
games: all Direct3D titles at level load

items.title: No guard band is reported (dvGuardBand* = 0), so the D3D runtime clips every screen-edge triangle in software
items.detail: The extended caps compute -2048/2048 guard values and then discard them (`(void)guard`). The vendor reports -200/-200/2048/1536 on Napalm with guard-band clipping on by default, and Glide sets `renderMode` bit 21 (`SST_RM_ENGUARDBAND`) by default. Without a guard band, the runtime's software clipper does work the hardware could skip — CPU time in the runtime, estimated at a few % (inferred). Fix: P5 (Diag `D3DGuardBand`: report the vendor's values and set `renderMode` bit 21), gated on a pixel-exact guard-band `d3dprobe` test.

items.title: Minor per-call overheads: FPU save and target_of per DrawPrimitives2 call, and an IOCTL for every vblank or flip-completion poll
items.detail: Each DrawPrimitives2 call does `EngSaveFloatingPointState`/`EngRestoreFloatingPointState`, a `memset`, `target_of` and `fvf_layout`. Each vblank or flip-completion poll is an IOCTL to the miniport, although the DLL already maps the register window and could read `status[6]` itself. Each costs a few µs; worth trimming only once P0 shows them.

items.title: No Direct3D game frame rate exists on vcr-kmd, and the only silicon perf number is fill-bound, not a triangle-rate measurement
items.detail: Every D3D number on the V5 6000 is `d3dprobe perf`, with 200 triangles per frame: 85.0 fps before `DDCAPS2_FLIPNOVSYNC`; then about 151 fps with novsync at 640x480x16; 84.2 fps with vsync at 640x480x32; and today 85.1 and 84.4 fps with vsync. Only 67 of the 200 triangles have area (about 0.99 Mpix), so the result is fill-dominated and its `tris_s` field is not triangle throughput. The 2026-11-08 game sweeps recorded frame statistics only. The only D3D game number on this card is the vendor stack's UT99 D3DDrv: 69.1 fps at 1024x768, 4 chips. A UT2004 `-benchmark` run started today by the on-box agent may give the first one.

items.title: D3D benchmark tooling: one game benchmark is ready, others need launch work or staging, and the synthetic tests need new modes
items.detail: Ready: `utbench_sweep.py` runs UT 436 UTbench through D3DDrv and parses `fps.txt`; UT 436 is deployed on `.124`, and the vendor-HAL reference is 69.1/69.5 fps. UT2004 and UT2003 have `-benchmark` botmatches (the on-box agent's exact command line is in evidence); Halo has `-timedemo` (inferred). 3DMark2000 and 3DMark2001 SE are on the share but not installed or staged; batch flags are unconfirmed, and 3DMark99 needs DX6.1. Unreal Gold's UE1 `-benchmark` never exits. Needed: `d3dprobe perf` modes for setup, fill, state, upload and flip (separating triangle cost from fill) and a `glidelab` triangle-rate mode as the CMDFIFO target. Titles without a timedemo use the P0 driver counters over a fixed scripted segment.

items.title: Measuring with vsync on: the driver records flip timing, per-frame headroom and the chip's pixel counters itself
items.detail: With vsync on, average fps saturates at the refresh, so the primary numbers come from the driver: per-frame work time (from the successful flip of frame N-1 to the first flip call of frame N) and the vsync wait (the WASSTILLDRAWING retries); headroom = 1 - work/period (median and 95th percentile); the on-time rate and a histogram of 1, 2 and 3+ refreshes per frame; HAL time split into FIFO-room spins, idle syncs and logging IOCTLs. The chip's own counters, sampled at flips, give pixels per frame, overdraw and an estimated GPU time (`fbiPixelsOut` 0x15c, `fbiTrianglesOut` 0x25c; offsets computed from field order). Everything is logged per session, as the flip counters already are, so no `vcrctl` runs during a game. Vsync-off runs are diagnostics only, via the game's setting or a `D3DNoVsync` switch (the vendor had the same registry override). Always record the refresh actually used: today a run planned for 120 Hz ran at 85.

items.title: Host-tested CMDFIFO logic already exists in fxD3D's gbk, but two parts of its kernel half must not be copied
items.detail: `gbk_fifo.c` (room, wrap and jump packet; the 10-store init with hole counting) and `gbk_packet.c` (packet 1/3/4/5/0 headers, masked against overflow) are pure-logic and have host tests, ready to port into a KMD header for P6. Do not copy from `gbkernel.c`: (1) `gbk_fifo_make_room` reads `readPtrL` on every reserve, which would recreate perf-02 — read it only when room runs short, as the vendor and Glide do; (2) its fence macro is a no-op that is only correct on an uncached ring, while vcr-kmd's LFB is write-combined, so a real store fence is needed. Its 10M-iteration wait budget is also about 10 s of reads; use the 2M `SPIN_CAP` bound.

items.title: Command-FIFO hazards: a killed Glide client's FIFO left on silently stops every D3D triangle; direct and FIFO writes must never mix
items.detail: Today's on-box run found a killed Glide session's `cmdFifo0` left enabled (`baseSize` 0x1fe, read pointer stuck): D3D clears worked but every triangle failed, until a mode set's engine reset turned the FIFO off; 40/40 passed after. Our own FIFO must therefore detect a foreign FIFO and refuse to arm (or idle-check and reset it, as Reset3D does), and must drain and disarm before any direct 2D, GDI, mode-set or Glide access. Write-combined FIFO writes need a fence every 64K dwords (a hole-counting quirk) and around the wrap jump. Every wait must be bounded and fall back to the direct path, and no request may exceed one ring lap (the vendor's 3DMark2000 TDR hypothesis). A perf baseline must start from a cold boot or clean mode set with `cmdFifo0` off and `d3dprobe render` at 40/40.

understand:visual.summary:
I looked at all 68 requested PNGs and 157 other .124 frames of the same titles. Only three Direct3D titles have any in-game frame: Jedi Knight, Mysteries of the Sith and Thief II. All three are fbshots from 2026-09-28, taken before the three 11-08 HAL fixes. The build deployed now, vcrdd 95678704, has never had a full sweep: the 02:08 re-sweep ran on 13256e46, and Rainbow Six's fix is shown only by a 320x240 strip.
- Fixed, with before and after frames: the half-pixel defect, which left the right column and bottom row unrendered in Red Faction, Thief II, UT2003, UT2004 and Max Payne, and is now fixed in all of them except Max Payne, which was never recaptured; and the unaligned DXT textures, which put colour noise in UT2003's menu text and NVIDIA logo.
- Rainbow Six: every sweep with D3D32 armed failed CreateDevice (black frame plus error); the 95678704 fix is shown only by that strip.
- Still open, shown in frames:
  - A mode set never clears video memory. AvP showed the old desktop as 640x480x16 garbage for its whole session, and UT2004 showed it before its first frame.
  - D3D titles that run after a Glide/OpenGL title in the same boot went black (Red Faction) or lost their menu backdrop (Shogo, H&D). The HAL never resets the Glide combine and stencil state, and Diag\Reset3D is off and has never run on silicon. This is a correlation only and needs an A/B.
  - DX5/DX6 titles draw point-sampled (JK, MotS, the old DX6 Thief II engine) while NewDark D3D9 Thief II on the same card is bilinear. The HAL ignores the legacy TEXTUREMAG/MIN/MAPBLEND/ADDRESS states and D3DTSS_ADDRESS although its DX5/6 caps advertise them; the vendor HAL maps all of them.
  - The old DX6 Dark engine draws foliage as flat key-colour silhouettes. The caps advertise TRANSPARENCY but the 3D path has no colour key. This is the engine Thief Gold 1.37 and System Shock 2 still run.
  - UT2003 and UT2004 render at 16 bpp although the staged configs set Use16bit=False and D3D32 is armed; the ring log shows UT2004's only context at 16 bpp.
- Minor or unconfirmed: a 1-pixel bright line at the bottom of UT2004's menu; Halo's flat squares on 09-28, probably the old alignment bug; transient single-colour GDI frames (Halo all-white at 60 s, Shogo black mesh, UT2003 thin band); H&D full-screen noise on 09-28, which the sweep scored PASS.
- Ruled out: JK and MotS's top-aligned 3D view is the game's own layout; the software renderer draws it the same way.
- Not testable from these frames: lines and points, MODULATE2X, ALPHAREPLICATE and separate alpha blend factors. No HUD, particle or lightmap frames exist.
- Many frames show no Direct3D rendering at all: 8 bpp DirectDraw menus, intro videos, 2D menus, dialogs, OpenGL titles and downscaled copies.

items.title: Half-pixel defect: right column and bottom row left unrendered in pre-11-08 frames (fixed on 13256e46; Max Payne never recaptured)
items.detail:
Before the fix, the last column and row of full-screen D3D quads were not drawn:
- Red Faction menu: column 639 white in 480/480 rows, row 479 white across 640/640 pixels.
- Thief II NewDark menu: column 1279 black in 679/960 rows; row 959 one flat colour (10,14,10).
- UT2003 menu: column 639 black 478/480, row 479 black.
- UT2004 menu: column 1279 black 816/960, row 959 black 754/1280.
- Thief II in-mission D3D9 frame: column 1279 and row 959 entirely black.
- Max Payne (10-04 full-size probe): column 1279 mean luma 4.2, against 12.4 in column 1278.
The 13256e46 re-sweep shows Red Faction at 0/480 and 0/640, and Thief II and UT2004 edges with content. The fix is xy_bias = 0.5 (vcrdd_3d.c:190-191, 304), the vendor's pixelOffset. A quad drawn from -0.5 to W-0.5 by the D3D convention missed the last pixel centre on the Voodoo (inferred geometry). Max Payne has no frame on a fixed build.

items.title: Textures off the 16-byte boundary drew colour noise in UT2003's menu text and NVIDIA logo (fixed on 13256e46)
items.detail:
Before the fix:
- UT2003 menu text was colour noise (the before_align_fix frame and the 00:48 60 s frame).
- Multicoloured speckles filled the NVIDIA logo's background disc (00:48 30 s frame, x 215-355, y 160-300).
The after_align_fix frame is clean. The cause was textures that DirectDraw placed at addresses ending in 4 (UT2003_combos_unaligned.txt, combines 20/22/24). mipchain_ext now places every texture 16-byte aligned (vcrdd_d3d.c:367, 441). The 09-28 Halo squares (visual-12) are probably the same bug.

items.title: Rainbow Six failed CreateDevice (black frame plus RAINBOW SIX ERROR) in every sweep with D3D32 armed; the fix on 95678704 is shown only by a 320x240 strip
items.detail:
Every armed sweep frame of Rainbow Six is black with the RAINBOW SIX ERROR dialog: 09-28 07:05, 09-29, 10-01, 11-08 00:48 and 11-08 02:08. The ring logged "ContextCreate refused: 16 bpp target with a 32-bit Z". The 16/16 fix landed on 95678704 at 02:41, after the 02:08 re-sweep, so the re-sweep frames still show the failure. Its only proof is a 960x240 strip of three thumbnails.
Needed: a full-resolution menu frame and an in-game frame on 95678704.

items.title: A mode set never clears video memory: the old 32 bpp desktop is shown as garbage at the new depth
items.detail:
- AvP's 640x480x16 screen showed the old 1280x1024x32 desktop, misread, for its whole session. AvP never made a device.
- UT2004 showed the same garbled desktop at 1280x960x16 before its first frame (09-29, 30 s).
IOCTL_VIDEO_SET_CURRENT_MODE masks off VIDEO_MODE_NO_ZERO_MEMORY (vcrmp.c:674), and VcrHwSetMode (vcrmp_hw.c:652-718) never clears the framebuffer. The NT contract is to zero video memory when that bit is clear (inferred, DDK). Any title that stalls or redraws only part of the screen shows garbage. The fix candidate is a 2D fill at mode set; the fill exists at vcrdd_ddraw.c:450.

items.title: D3D titles go black or lose their menu backdrop when a Glide/OpenGL title ran earlier in the same boot (correlation)
items.detail:
Seen:
- Red Faction drew nothing, not even in the scanned-out frame, right after GLQuake (09-29).
- Shogo showed its menu text on black with no cloth backdrop: on 09-29 after RTCW and Serious Sam, and on 10-01 after Serious Sam.
- H&D on 10-01, after Hexen II GL, showed its frame on black at 30 s and all black at 60 s.
All three render fully in the Glide-free 11-08 sweeps, where the board check is glideprobe --noopen.
Why this fits the code:
- The D3D path never writes combineMode, chipMask or aaCtrl, and writes stencilMode/stencilOp only for 32 bpp targets (vcr_3dseq.h:66-69).
- That 16 bpp ignores stencil is UNPROVEN (vcr_3dseq.h:44-46).
- Stencil state and an extended colour combine outlive even a clean Glide close (vcr_3dseq.h:84-85).
- The reset, Diag\Reset3D, is off by default and has never run on silicon (vcrdd_2d.c:384-386, 405; README.md:112).
Counter-cases:
- On 09-29 H&D, the first title of sweep part 2, rendered fine, but a person used the box between the parts.
- On 09-28 23:46 H&D showed only its frame without its text, which looks like load timing.
Needed: an A/B (cold boot, RF/Shogo, then GLQuake with a clean quit, then RF/Shogo again; repeat with Reset3D=1). If it is confirmed, the D3D context should write combineMode=0 and stencilMode=0 itself for every target (inferred).

items.title: DX5/DX6 titles draw point-sampled textures: the HAL ignores the legacy texture render states its DX5/6 caps advertise
items.detail:
Seen in the in-game frames:
- JK and MotS (1280x960x16) and Thief II on its original DX6 engine show hard texel blocks with no bilinear blending.
- The same Thief II scene through NewDark D3D9 on the same card is bilinear (compare the moon).
Code:
- The DX5/6 device description advertises the legacy filter and blend caps (vcrdd_d3d.c:2036-2043).
- set_rs only stores a render state (:1393-1405); filtering comes only from D3DTSS_MAG/MINFILTER (:788-791), which default to POINT (:1145-1146).
- D3DRENDERSTATE_TEXTUREMAG/TEXTUREMIN/TEXTUREMAPBLEND/TEXTUREADDRESS and D3DTSS_ADDRESS (12) are stored and never read (:1591-1611).
Vendor: maps texMag/texMin to TS[0] (D3RSTATE.C:2168-2297), texMapBlend to stage ops (:2851-2910), TEXTUREADDRESS (:2645) and D3DTSS_ADDRESS (D7DP2.C:1602-1605), and notes TextureMapBlend is still used for WINNT (D3INIT.C:124-126).
The same engine runs Thief Gold 1.37 and System Shock 2 (no NewDark files in their trees).
Risks beyond what the frames show: MODULATEALPHA/DECALALPHA translucency and CLAMP requests (inferred). That these engines request bilinear filtering is also inferred.
Verify by logging rs[17,18,21,3] and tss[12] during JK.
games: Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith

items.title: Old Dark engine (DX6) foliage draws as flat key-colour silhouettes: TRANSPARENCY is advertised but the 3D path has no colour key
items.detail:
Seen: in the DX6 Thief II frame, trees and bushes are solid (0,0,8) dark blue: 3638 px in the tree region, 2027 and 2016 px in two bushes. Their outlines are tree- or bush-shaped with no texture inside. The NewDark D3D9 frame textures the same objects green.
Code:
- The DX5/6 caps advertise D3DPTEXTURECAPS_TRANSPARENCY (vcrdd_d3d.c:2034-2035).
- The 3D path never uses V3D_CHROMAKEY or FZ_CHROMAKEY (vcr_3dregs.h:32, 107); colour keys exist only for DirectDraw blits (vcrdd_ddraw.c:434-456, 539-542).
- The vendor defaults colorKeyEnable to TRUE (D3RSTATE.C:3029-3036, 3709) and uses the chroma path (D6MT.C:269, 603).
Reading: a leaf model's key-coloured texels drawn opaque and then darkened by the night lighting (inferred).
Ruled out:
- Vertex fog: the HAL disables it when there is no specular (vcrdd_d3d.c:1358-1360).
- Overall brightness: mean luma is 6.9 against 8.4 for the D3D9 frame.
This engine still runs Thief Gold 1.37 and System Shock 2, whose gameplay has never been captured.
Two ways out: stop advertising TRANSPARENCY, or implement the chroma key.

items.title: UT2003 and UT2004 render at 16 bpp although they ask for 32 (Use16bit=False, D3D32 armed)
items.detail:
Every UT2003 and UT2004 frame is 565-quantised, with an ordered-dither pattern on the menu backdrop gradients. The staged configs set Use16bit=False (UT2004.ini:329, UT2003.ini:259). The ring shows UT2004's only context as "1280x960 pitch 2560, 16 bpp 3D" (d3d32_end_vcrlog.txt:906), with no refused 32 bpp attempt before it, so the choice was made above the driver.
The cause is not established; candidates are the D16-at-32 bpp CheckDepthStencilMatch lead and a UE2 colour-depth default. UT2004's log would show which.
The other 32-bit titles do get 32 bpp: Halo, H&D and Thief II D3D9 frames are 32 bpp.
With D3D32 off (the default for a fresh install), every D3D title is 16 bpp.

items.title: UT2004 menu: a one-pixel bright line on the screen's bottom row
items.detail: After the fix, row 959 has mean 232.5 with 725 px of (231,231,231); rows 958 and 957 are 93.9 and 18.2. Before the fix the line sat on row 958 (132.7), with row 959 uncovered. Because it moved with the half-pixel fix, it is a texture edge that is actually drawn, consistent with bilinear sampling across a WRAP edge (inferred). UT2004 is D3D8, so it sends ADDRESSU/V, which the HAL honours (vcrdd_d3d.c:792-795). It may also appear on reference hardware; compare before acting.

items.title: Transient single-colour or half-drawn GDI frames (Halo all-white, Shogo black mesh) are not proof either way
items.detail:
Halo's 60 s frame on 13256e46 is exactly one colour, (255,255,255), with no logo, text or cursor. The plan calls it the animated menu (PLAN:177-178), but the menu's white phase keeps its logo, text and cursor (halo_libdeploy_15.png, halo_novideo_1.png). Shogo's 60 s frame on 13256e46 shows the backdrop mesh drawn black with no text, in a boot with no Glide session.
GDI reads the flip-chain buffer at the desktop offset (vcrmp_hw.c:708), which can be the back buffer mid-frame (inferred).
Recapture with fbshot --probe, several frames a second apart.

items.title: UT2003 at 60 s on 13256e46: a thin horizontal band across a black frame
items.detail: The frame is black except for a yellow-green band at y 485-492 spanning the full width. It could be an intro or menu opening transition (inferred) or a collapsed full-screen quad. The same title at 60 s on b63ea6a5 showed its menu, and at 30 s on 13256e46 its logos rendered correctly. It needs a recapture.

items.title: Halo menu (09-28): flat opaque squares where soft sprites belong
items.detail: A 52x52 square at x 593-646, y 588-641 holds only 4 dithered colours near (38,53,36); two more hard-edged squares sit near (690,140) and (710,10) in the nebula. The frame predates the 11-08 alignment fix, so a misread small DXT3/5 glow texture, alpha included, is the most likely explanation; a missing texture or alpha is another (inferred). The 11-08 menu frames catch a different animation moment, so they neither confirm nor refute it. Recapture the planet-phase menu on 95678704.

items.title: H&D full-screen colour noise with D3D32 armed (09-28 07:05), which the sweep scored PASS
items.detail: At 1280x960 the whole screen is noise with a periodic structure (luma mean 111), and lan_sweep still called it PASS. The frames are clean on later builds (09-29 armed, 11-08). This is historical, but it shows that the luma-statistics verdict cannot catch a garbage frame. The same goes for the stale desktop in visual-04. A frame check belongs in the sweep.

items.title: Not a driver defect: Jedi Knight's and MotS's 3D view sits top-aligned
items.detail: The JK and MotS in-game frames draw the 3D view at x 180-1100, y 0-690: centred horizontally, at the top, with the gauges in the bottom corners. The 8 bpp software path draws the identical layout (jkdf2_game.png), and the view-size slider is mid-range. The HAL only adds xy_bias to pre-transformed vertices (vcrdd_3d.c:190-191). Do not chase this.
games: Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith

items.title: No frame shows or rules out the known HAL gaps (lines/points skipped, MODULATE2X, ALPHAREPLICATE, separate alpha blend)
Direct3D titles with NO in-game frame at all on .124
items.detail:
No in-game frame exists for: Aliens vs Predator, Battlefield 1942 (single player, Host LAN and Join LAN), Halo, Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe, Red Faction, Shogo, System Shock 2, Thief Gold, Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six, Unreal Tournament 2003, Unreal Tournament 2004 and Max Payne.
- What exists instead: menus, in-engine menu backdrops (H&D, UT2004), intro videos, dialogs and desktops.
- In-game frames exist only for:
  - Jedi Knight DF2: jkdf2_d3d2/3, 1280x960x16;
  - Mysteries of the Sith: mots_game;
  - Thief II: thief2_c2 (DX6) and thief2_d3d9_armed_4 (NewDark D3D9).
  All are 09-28 fbshots, before the half-pixel, alignment and Rainbow Six fixes.
- Nothing at all has been captured on the deployed vcrdd 95678704 except the 320x240 Rainbow Six strip.
- Never captured in D3D mode on .124: the D3D renderers of the Glide/OpenGL titles (Unreal Gold, UT 436, Deus Ex, Descent 3, Turok 2, Carmageddon 2, Half-Life). The D3D frames that do exist are from the 86Box Voodoo3 bed and from .123.

items.title: Frames that show no Direct3D rendering at all
items.detail:
These frames cannot show a HAL defect:
- JK and MotS sweep frames: 640x480 8 bpp DirectDraw crawls; JK's palette is lost in the GDI capture (README-FLEET:42-47).
- Thief Gold sweep frames and Red Faction 30 s: intro videos.
- System Shock 2 menus: 2D DirectDraw. The 11-08 13256e46 frame is pixel-identical to the 09-29 fbshot, across a change of xy_bias.
- BF1942 (all three shortcuts): SafeDisc dialog, server console, empty desktop.
- UT2004 30 s frames: black loading screen or splash.
- LAN Jedi Academy, SoF2 and Serious Sam frames: OpenGL titles.
- The four LAN PNGs that are 640x480 copies of 1280x960 frames: downscaled, so one-pixel defects are invisible.
- RES/day/fbshots/mots_new.png: fbshot follows flips line by line, so a moving cut-scene comes out as a mix of several frames (README.md:156).
games: Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith

understand:runtime.summary:
I read our HAL, the 3dfx NT driver, the DX8 and W2K DDKs (including Microsoft's NT Permedia2 sample) and the XP SP3 runtime DLLs themselves, disassembled. Today's on-box evidence settled several open points.
1. D3D8 and D3D9 treat vcrdd as a DX7 (DP2EX, non-T&L) driver. It never sets DDHALINFO_GETDRIVERINFO2, and GetDriverInfo2 (f828169c) appears in no ring dump. That path works: d3dprobe passes 40/40, and UT2003, Halo and NewDark create devices. The vintage lane's 2026-08-12 claim that a DX7 build means no D3D8 hardware is wrong; 3dfx's own NT driver was DX7.
2. For a DX7 driver, d3d8.dll and d3d9.dll take render-target textures and depth pairing from a built-in PCI-id table. We inherit 3dfx's entry 121a:0009 = 0x4580: R5G6B5 and A8R8G8B8 render-target textures, a lockable D16, and no "Z with any colour depth". X8R8G8B8 render-target textures can never be granted, because the registry can only switch these flags off.
3. X8R8G8B8 + D16 is confirmed broken on silicon. The runtime says the pair matches, our ContextCreate refuses it, CreateDevice returns 8876086c, and the runtime switched the CRT twice 156 ms apart while cleaning up. The fix is 3dfx's: give a 16-bit Z 32-bit storage. R5G6B5 + D24 is already correct: D3D8 refuses it, and DX6/7 titles draw 16/16.
4. The runtime's DDPIXELFORMAT converter has no DDPF_ALPHA case, so A8 can never reach a D3D8/9 game. X8R8G8B8, X1R5G5B5, X4R4G4B4, L8, A8L8, A4L4, R3G3B2, A8R3G3B2 and P8 can be added to our DX7 list, and the TMU samples all of them.
5. Execute-buffer titles (JK, MotS, Rainbow Six) send their raw DX5 render states (TEXTUREMAPBLEND, MAG/MIN filters, ADDRESS, SHADEMODE, COLORKEYENABLE) straight into our DP2, and DX6 SetRenderState titles probably do too. The HAL handles only TEXTUREHANDLE. The DX6 titles affected are AvP, Thief Gold, System Shock 2 and Shogo.
6. XP sends each mip level as its own CreateSurface, because we do not answer GUID_NTPrivateDriverCaps. Our allocator never sees a whole chain. The blocky noise on distant surfaces in today's UT2003, UT2004 and Halo frames fits this, unproven. XP also asks for GetHeapAlignment and we decline it.
7. The runtime passes texture ops the caps do not list: UT2003 uses MODULATE2X, which is drawn as MODULATE, so its world is half-bright. ValidateTextureStageState always answers OK. Lines and points are advertised but skipped.
8. D3D8/9 emulate state blocks for our DDI type, games fall back to software vertex processing (none insists on hardware T&L), and the MIPFILTER values are translated for us.
9. A DX8-level DDI would add little (A8, X8R8G8B8 render targets, Caps2) at a high cost. Stay on DX7.
10. Our caps are mode-independent and must stay so. With Diag D3D32 off (the default) there is no 32 bpp D3D8/9 at all, including windowed on the 32 bpp desktop.

items.title: D3D8/D3D9 run vcrdd as a DX7-DDI driver (no GetDriverInfo2); this works and contradicts the vintage 'DX=7 means no D3D8 hardware' finding
items.detail:
DrvGetDirectDrawInfo sets only DDHALINFO_GETDRIVERINFOSET, never DDHALINFO_GETDRIVERINFO2 (0x8). XP's GetDriverInfo queries today include no GUID_DDStereoMode/GetDriverInfo2 (f828169c).

The runtimes therefore synthesize D3DCAPS8/9, the format list and the Z ops from the DX7 data. That works: D3D8 d3dprobe passes 40/40, UT2003 creates a software-vertex-processing device, and Halo and NewDark (D3D9) run.

The vintage lane's section 16 conclusion, 'D3D8 has no hardware because the driver is built DX=7', is wrong in general. 3dfx's shipped NT driver was DX7 (SOURCES DX=7), and its NT DX8 path was never compiled.
evidence: ONBOX/ring_after_probe_ii_decoded.txt seq 24824-24836 (GetDriverInfo GUIDs; no f828169c in any ring)

items.title: X8R8G8B8 + D16: the runtime reports a match, ContextCreate refuses it, and CreateDevice fails 8876086c (confirmed on silicon)
games: any D3D8/D3D9 title that picks D16 at 32 bpp (none measured yet among deployed titles)

items.title: A CreateDevice failed after the runtime set the mode costs two CRT mode switches about 150 ms apart
items.detail:
For a fullscreen device the D3D8 runtime sets the display mode before it creates the buffers and calls ContextCreate. When ContextCreate refuses, the runtime restores the desktop mode at once: 640x480x32 at 83009.862 s, back to 1280x1024x32 at 83010.002 s.

Any game that retries other Z formats or modes after a failure turns this into rapid mode flapping on the 1998 CRT. The project rule is at least 5 s between switches.

Remove the refusals that games can reach (runtime-02). Keep the 513/12, 15 and 17 logs loud.
games: any D3D8/D3D9 title whose CreateDevice is refused at ContextCreate

items.title: R5G6B5 + D24X8/D24S8: D3D8 refuses the pair itself; DX6/7 titles draw it 16/16 (correct, keep the tests)
items.detail:
CheckDepthStencilMatch(R5G6B5, D24X8 or D24S8) returns no, and CreateDevice returns 8876086a before the driver is asked.

DX5/6/7 titles never ask the runtime. Rainbow Six picks its Z at the 32 bpp desktop and reaches the driver, where be58b7d draws a 16 bpp target over a 32-bit Z as 16/16. No action needed; keep the tests pinning both answers.

items.title: D24S8 is listed and reaches applications, but stencil is never honoured (StencilCaps 0)
items.detail:
The Z list includes D24S8 (Z mask 0x00ffffff, stencil mask 0xff000000), and D3D8 exposes it as D3DFMT_D24S8 (format and match = 1). D3DNTHAL_D3DEXTENDEDCAPS.dwStencilCaps is never set, so it is 0.

The HAL writes stencilMode = stencilOp = 0 at every 32 bpp setup, drops D3DCLEAR_STENCIL, and compute_regs reads no stencil state. Apps that check StencilCaps see nothing; apps that only check the format silently get no stencil test.

The VSA-100 does 8-bit stencil at 32 bpp, and 3dfx listed KEEP through DECR. Count STENCILENABLE per context before investing; UT2003/2004 are staged with UseStencil=False.

items.title: Render-target textures and Z ops come from a PCI-id table built into d3d8/d3d9; we inherit 3dfx's 121a:0009 entry, so no X8R8G8B8 render target is ever possible
evidence: XPRT/d3d9.dll same entries at file 0x13f0/0x1400/0x1410; per-format code 0x4fdfbe19-0x4fdfbe4b

items.title: The runtime's DDPIXELFORMAT converter has no DDPF_ALPHA case, so A8 is impossible via the DX7 DDI; other formats can be added
items.detail:
d3d8.dll 0x6d9b6850-0x6d9b6d48, with the same cases in d3d9.dll, recognises RGB, RGB+alpha, PAL8, ZBUFFER(+STENCIL), LUMINANCE(+ALPHAPIXELS) and BUMPDUDV. It has no DDPF_ALPHA case.

Today's list offers only R5G6B5, A1R5G5B5 and A4R4G4B4, plus A8R8G8B8 and DXT1-5 when D3DBigTex is armed. The following can be added as DX7 entries, and the TMU samples all of them:
- X8R8G8B8, X1R5G5B5, X4R4G4B4 (alpha forced to 1)
- R3G3B2, A8R3G3B2
- L8, A8L8, A4L4

A8 (TMU format 2) needs a DX8 GETFORMAT. Bump formats are impossible: the hardware has none. Halo's format names include a8, y8, ay8, a8y8, x8r8g8b8 and p8-bump (usage inferred). Today Halo drew a glow sprite as a translucent square, which fits a missing alpha/luminance format (inferred). UE2 adapts through SupportsTextureFormat and ConvertDXT.

items.title: No paletted textures: P8/A8P8 are not listed, and DP2 SETPALETTE/UPDATEPALETTE are skipped
items.detail:
The probe measured texP8 = 0. The walker skips SETPALETTE by record size and UPDATEPALETTE by its counts.

The converter maps PALETTEINDEXED8|RGB to P8/A8P8, and the TMU has P8, P8_ARGB6666 and AP88 formats. Supporting them needs list entries, palette handling in DP2, and a palette download.

Shogo's renderer looks for 'Palette alpha'. Halo has p8-bump (inferred).

items.title: Legacy DX5/DX6 render states reach DP2 raw, and the HAL handles only TEXTUREHANDLE
items.detail:
Execute buffers are handed to DP2 as they are (D3DNTHALDP2_EXECUTEBUFFER): JK's streams end in D3DOP_EXIT, and MotS had 0 unparsed commands. STATERENDER=8 is RENDERSTATE, carrying the application's own values.

Microsoft's NT sample maps TEXTUREHANDLE, TEXTUREMAPBLEND, BORDERCOLOR, MIPMAPLODBIAS, ANISOTROPY, TEXTUREADDRESS(U/V) and TEXTUREMAG/MIN into TSS0 for every render state it receives. 3dfx kept TEXTUREMAPBLEND 'for WINNT'.

Our set_rs stores every state but uses only TEXTUREHANDLE:
- TEXTUREMAPBLEND is ignored: TSS stay at MODULATE with texture alpha, so MODULATEALPHA translucency is lost and DECAL/COPY/ADD/DECALALPHA are wrong.
- MAG/MIN are ignored, so everything is point-sampled.
- ADDRESS and WRAP are ignored, so everything wraps.
- SHADEMODE FLAT is ignored.

Fix: a mapping table, including the DDK's legacy MODULATE alpha rule. Testing needs a DX5/DX6 probe, because d3dprobe is D3D8 only.
evidence: JK.EXE/JKM.EXE/RainbowSix.exe GUID scan: IDirect3D2 + ExecuteBuffer, no IDirect3D3

items.title: COLORKEYENABLE is ignored while D3DPTEXTURECAPS_TRANSPARENCY is advertised
items.detail:
The DDK: colour key is the AND of the render state and DDRAWISURF_HASCKEYSRCBLT on the texture, and 'it is up to the driver'. We advertise TRANSPARENCY but never set FZ_CHROMAKEY or the chromaKey register, so key-coloured texels draw opaque in DX5-7 titles.

3dfx used the FBI chroma key, converting the key per texture format. It notes the key is tested after the bilinear filter, so the result is approximate; hardware support is partial. Rainbow Six's exe carries colour-key code.

items.title: D3DTSS_ADDRESS (stage state 12) is stored but never applied
items.detail:
tex_view and tex_view_ext read only ADDRESSU and ADDRESSV. Both Microsoft's NT sample and 3dfx copy TSS 12 into U and V.

A DX6/7 title that clamps through D3DTSS_ADDRESS therefore gets wrap: seams on sky boxes and UI. Who uses it is unknown; count it.

items.title: XP creates each mip level in its own CreateSurface, so the TMU's packed chain holds only if the heap places the levels back to back
items.detail:
The DDK: dwSCnt is usually 1 on NT unless the driver answers GUID_NTPrivateDriverCaps with ATOMICSURFACECREATION. XP asked and we declined. The repo itself measured seven calls for a 64x64 D3D8 texture.

VcrDdD3dCreateMipChain and mipchain_ext size a block from the levels in one call and mark each call's surface MIP_TOP. The TMU reads level k at base + chain offset(k).

A fresh heap passes (mip and mip2048 on silicon). Today's UT2003, UT2004 and Halo frames show blocky noise on minified or distant surfaces while the same surfaces close up are clean. That is consistent, but unproven: the DXT small-level layout and cache flushes are the alternatives.

3dfx reserved the whole chain from lpSurfMore->dwMipMapCount at the top level's call. Fix (default off): that reservation, or ATOMICSURFACECREATION. Test with a fragmented-heap chain test.

items.title: XP asks for GUID_GetHeapAlignment and we decline, so DirectDraw places surfaces on 4-byte boundaries with no 16-byte pitch
The runtime passes texture ops the caps do not list: UT2003 uses MODULATE2X, which is drawn as MODULATE, so the world is half-bright
items.detail:
TextureOpCaps is 0x184f, but UT2003 set COLOROP 5 (MODULATE2X) on stage 0 (TEXTURE x DIFFUSE) and stage 1, and op 16 (BLENDCURRENTALPHA) on stage 1. color_path and stage1_combine draw 2X/4X as MODULATE.

Today's UT2003 and UT2004 frames show 'the whole world very dark'. 3dfx listed MODULATE2X/4X on Napalm, through the combine output shift (route inferred).

items.title: ValidateTextureStageState always answers '1 pass, DD_OK'
items.detail:
Any ValidateDevice probe (D3D7/8/9) reaches this callback (inferred) and is told every combination works. Titles therefore never take their fallback paths, and then degrade silently (see runtime-14).

3dfx validated op by op and argument by argument. Make it answer exactly what compute_regs implements.
games: Thief II NewDark (any title that calls ValidateDevice)

items.title: Lines and points: the line caps are copied from the triangle caps, but every line and point opcode is skipped
items.detail:
prim_caps fills dpcLineCaps from the triangle caps, so the runtime believes lines draw with texture, blend and Z, and sends DP2 LINELIST, LINESTRIP and indexed lines. The walker skips them, and skips POINTS as well.

Which titles use them is unknown. Count them per context, then draw them as triangle quads.

items.title: Caps are under-reported against the hardware, and some states are silently dropped (ZENABLE=USEW disables depth)
items.detail:
Missing from what the runtime publishes, though the hardware or 3dfx's caps have them:
- ZBIAS, WBUFFER, MIPMAPLODBIAS
- trilinear (MIPFLINEAR), MIRROR
- specular and FOGGOURAUD
- DESTALPHA blends (blend_src/blend_dst already map them)
- COLORWRITEENABLE
- guard band (computed but unused), MaxTextureRepeat

The runtime still forwards the states. Depth is enabled only for D3DZB_TRUE, so D3DZB_USEW turns depth off. ZBIAS, SPECULARENABLE and MIPMAPLODBIAS are ignored.

items.title: Hardware/mixed vertex processing is refused (no HWTRANSFORMANDLIGHT); no deployed title insists on it
items.detail:
DevCaps 0x8ae50 has no HWTRANSFORMANDLIGHT; the VSA-100 has no T&L. UE2 logs 'will use software transform and lighting / software vertex processing' although the ini says UseHardwareTL=True.

Every D3D8/9 title in the sweeps created a device. The runtime supplies MaxStreams 16 and MaxActiveLights 8, and translates the D3D8 MIPFILTER values to DX7 (the silicon mip tests pass).

items.title: State blocks: D3D8/9 emulate them for our DDI type (no work); DX7-interface state blocks (STATESET) are skipped by the walker
items.detail:
d3d8 and d3d9 device init set 'emulate state blocks' when the DDI type is <= 5, and read the registry knob EmulateStateBlocks only above that. The odd values 5, 7, 9 and 11 are the T&L types (the mapping is inferred). So D3D8/9 never send STATESET to vcrdd.

The DX7 runtime expects drivers to record and replay state blocks: the DDK's 'Accelerated State Management', Microsoft's sample, and 3dfx's D7DP2.C. Our walker skips STATESET by size and applies the recorded states immediately. DX7-interface titles that use state blocks would mis-render. Count them.
evidence: W2KDDK help d_grafx.chm 4.7.4 Accelerated State Management

items.title: Managed-texture uploads go through Lock + CPU writes, and every Lock drains the engine
items.detail:
D3D8 on this HAL fills managed textures by Lock + CPU writes, not TEXBLT. Dd_Lock calls VcrDd2dSync, a full drain, on every lock. Each texture Unlock forces a TMU flush before the next use.

Per-frame uploads therefore serialise the CPU and the chip. Halo's Bink intros play about 10x slow, which may be this (inferred). Fix: drain only when the surface may still be in use.

items.title: With Diag\D3D32 off (the default) there is no 32 bpp D3D8/9: no X8R8G8B8 device, and no windowed device on the 32 bpp desktop
games: all windowed D3D on the 32 bpp desktop

items.title: The runtimes read caps and the Z list at the desktop mode and re-read them at every mode change, so our answers must stay mode-independent
items.detail:
D3DExtendedCaps and ZPixelFormats are re-queried at every DirectDraw enable (29 and 25 times this morning). D3D8 answers fullscreen-format questions from desktop-mode data. DX6 titles pick their Z at the desktop depth (Rainbow Six).

Our render depths and Z list do not depend on pd->bpp. 4a9793b proved what goes wrong if they do: it removed D16 at the 32 bpp desktop and broke the proven 16 bpp device. Any new format or Z entry must keep this property.

items.title: A DX8-level DDI gains little for these games at a high cost; stay on DX7
evidence: XPRT/d3d9.dll strings 'Cannot convert vertex declaration for dx8 driver'

items.title: Throughput: the runtime's strips, fans and indexed lists become independent triangles, with a status-register read for every vertex (UT2003 flyby 9.41 fps at 640x480x16)
items.detail:
walk() emits tri() for every triangle of every list, strip and fan. VcrDd3dTriangle writes 3 vertices of up to 15 MMIO floats each. VcrDdRoom reads the status register before every vertex.

The UT2003 flyby averaged 9.41 fps at 640x480x16: 59,589 DP2 calls and 37.0M triangles, with 116.7 ms of each 123 ms frame spent in 'Hardware DrawPrimitive'.

This is HAL-side: use the setup unit's strip/fan mode and track FIFO room instead of polling. Attributing the bottleneck to submission rather than CPU vertex processing is inferred.

items.title: A killed Glide/OpenGL client's cmdFifo0, left enabled, silently stops every D3D triangle (cross-reference: finding of the on-box session)
items.detail:
Status 0xa1f with cmdFifo0 enabled and its read pointer stuck: clears worked, every triangle failed, and the 2D engine was given up. After vcrctl modeseq's engine reset, the probe passed 40/40.

D3D context creation should clear stale CMDFIFO/3D state. This is a precondition for validating every 32 bpp item above.
games: every D3D title run after a Glide/OpenGL title

items.title: UE2 picks 16 bpp + D16 on this PCI id despite Use16bit=False; the staged UT inis disable vsync and pin 60 Hz
items.detail:
UT2003.log shows 'D3D Detected: 3dfx video card', then back buffer 23 (R5G6B5), depth 80 (D16) at 640x480x16@120, while the ini says Use16bit=False. That this is UE2's own 3dfx path keyed on vendor 0x121a is inferred.

The staged UT2003/UT2004 inis set UseVSync=False and DesiredRefreshRate=60, which conflicts with the 'vsync on' campaign choice and with the CRT's 85-120 Hz. This is a library fix, not a driver one.

items.title: d3dprobe caps does not measure several runtime answers this plan depends on
items.detail:
d3dprobe caps reports the DevCaps-to-FVFCaps fields and 11 formats.

It does not report: StencilCaps, LineCaps, Caps2, PresentationIntervals, MaxStreams, MaxPointSize, guard band, MaxTextureRepeat; the formats X8R8G8B8, X1R5G5B5, X4R4G4B4, L8, A8, A8L8, A4L4, R3G3B2, A8P8, D16_LOCKABLE; D3DUSAGE_RENDERTARGET on R5G6B5, A8R8G8B8 and X8R8G8B8 textures (expected yes/yes/no); D3DUSAGE_DYNAMIC; or ValidateDevice of MODULATE2X.

The HAL also lacks per-context counters for skipped lines/points, STATESET, legacy states, COLORKEYENABLE, STENCILENABLE and unsupported TSS ops. Those counters would settle the inferred items in the report.

items.title: 3dfx's NT D3D HAL is a DX7 DDI; no DX8 caps or format ops on XP
items.detail: The W2K/XP driver builds with DX=7 and DXDDKVERSION=7. GetDriverInfo2, BuildDX8TextureFormats and BuildD3DCaps8 compile only for DX >= 8, which 3dfx never built on NT; retro3dfx first built it in commit c34d62f. On XP the D3D8 runtime builds D3DCAPS8 from the DX7 caps for 3dfx's driver exactly as it does for vcr-kmd (inferred). So 3dfx's DX7 caps are the yardstick, and matching 3dfx needs no DX8 DDI.

items.title: 3dfx resizes a mismatched Z instead of refusing it (fixes X8R8G8B8 + D16)
items.detail:
Napalm needs the Z depth to match the colour depth.
- A D16 requested on a 32 bpp primary is allocated as 32-bit (24-bit depth).
- At attach time the Z is relabelled or reallocated to match the target.
- Depth fills on a resized Z are adjusted.
- ContextCreate has no depth check (removed in D3CONTXT revision 12).
Our vcr_rt_format/ContextCreate refuses 32 bpp + D16. That is today's CreateDevice 8876086c on .124, although the D3D8 runtime reports zmatch X8R8G8B8/D16 = 1. Copy the pattern behind a Diag switch, but convert depth fills by MSB replication ((d<<8)|(d>>8), the spec's LFB rule). 3dfx's high-word copy is right only for 0 and 0xFFFF. A locked promoted D16 returns 24-bit values; 3dfx accepted that, since DdLock never reads the FX_ORIGINALLY flags.

items.title: All Napalm texture-stage ops come from combineMode bit 31; ours writes combineMode = 0
D3DTA_COMPLEMENT and D3DTA_ALPHAREPLICATE are combineMode field tricks
items.detail: COMPLEMENT XORs the op's invert field (e.g. INVERT_OTHER_ONE_MINUS_X) into combineMode. ALPHAREPLICATE adds 1 to the select field, because each select lists the RGB source and then its alpha; alternatively it swaps fbzColorPath MSELECT from MRGBTMU to MATMU. ValidateTextureStageState refuses a complement that the op's table entry does not allow. Our HAL has neither modifier.

items.title: TFACTOR goes to TMU chromaKey/chromaRange (chip 6) and FBI c0/c1; ours only c1
items.detail:
On a TEXTUREFACTOR change, 3dfx writes the factor to:
- both TMUs' chromaKey and chromaRange; the constant alpha sits in chromaRange[31:24] because combineMode bit 30 is set;
- the FBI's c0 and c1.
It re-sends the factor after FastFill. The TMU chroma registers are reserved for TFACTOR, and the texture colour key uses only the FBI chromaKey. Ours loads c1 only. That serves an FBI-side stage but not a TMU stage: stage 1, or BLENDFACTORALPHA inside a TMU.
evidence: SPEC chromaRange: 'When combineMode[30]=1, then the chromaRange register is used to store constant color values in the texture units'

items.title: Stage mapping, 2ppc and the 12-NOP exit rule
items.detail: Stage 0 runs on TMU1 and stage 1 on TMU0, as in ours. 3dfx enables 2ppc (combineMode bit 29) for single-stage and untextured draws at 15/16 bpp in non-high modes, and turns it off for two stages and for trilinear. Before leaving 2ppc it sends 12 nopCMDs to chip field 0x6 (TMUs only) and writes combineMode before any other 3D register. The spec says 2ppc helps only at 15/16 bpp and broadcasts TMU writes to both units. Ours never enables 2ppc, though our sequence already knows the NOP rule from Glide. The 16-bit D3D titles would benefit (inferred).
evidence: SPEC combineMode: 'send down at least 12 NOP commands with the chip field set to select both TMUs'

items.title: Single-pass trilinear on one texture; multitexture + trilinear refused
LOD bias, registry bias and MAXMIPLEVEL (with a stage-0 bug)
items.detail:
- D3DTSS_MIPMAPLODBIAS goes into tLOD LODBIAS (4.2 format) through CalcBias42.
- With no app bias, two-stage draws get +0.5, and so do point-mip single-stage draws.
- The registry LOD_BIAS is added on top.
- MAXMIPLEVEL raises LODMIN, but stage 0's value is used for both TMUs. The code comment admits this bug; F-22 Lightning 3 drove the clamp.
- 3dfx never advertises MIPMAPLODBIAS.
Ours handles neither LOD bias nor MAXMIPLEVEL.

items.title: MIRROR via tLOD bits 28/29; BORDER never supported
items.detail: CLAMP is textureMode bits 6/7. MIRROR is tLOD TMIRRORS/TMIRRORT (bits 28/29), per stage. WRAP is the default. BORDER is commented out of the caps and has no register. Our address caps are 0x15, with no MIRROR.

items.title: No anisotropic filtering
items.detail: dwMaxAnisotropy is 1 and the ANISOTROPY render state is a dummy handler. textureMode and tLOD have no anisotropy field (inferred from the field list). Ours is the same; nothing to do.

items.title: Texture formats: palettized and luminance formats are the gap; P8 is suspect
items.detail: 3dfx exports 565, 1555, 4444, 332, 8332, L8, A8, A4L4 and A8L8, plus 8888, DXT1-5 and FXT1 on Napalm. It exported P8 as well, until retro3dfx turned it off because P8 sampled white through this driver. A8P8 was always off. The hardware mapping is L8A8->AI88, A4L4->AI44, L8->I8 and A8->A8, and the palette goes to nccTable0[4..11]. Ours exports 565, 1555, 4444, 8888 and DXT1/3/5, with no P8, L8, A8 or A8L8. Glide's own Napalm palette path suggests the white P8 is a driver bug (inferred); prove P8 on silicon first.

items.title: Texture size, aspect, alignment and TBIG rules
items.detail:
- Napalm textures are 1..2048, with tLOD TBIG for large ones.
- DXT dimensions must be multiples of 4, and non-power-of-two sizes are refused.
- Aspect ratios above 8:1 are stored as 8:1.
- texBaseAddr is 16-byte granular: base = start - sum of LOD sizes, rounded up to 16.
- With PIXELCENTER=1, each texture adds textureCenter[log2 size] to S and T.
Ours offers 2048 only with Diag D3DBigTex. The >8:1 handling and the texel-centre offset are worth matching, with host tests.

items.title: Stencil: 32 bpp only, all 8 ops, the disabled state must be written as 0
items.detail: 3dfx advertises all eight stencil ops on Napalm and strips STENCIL_ENABLE below 32 bpp. Whenever stencil is off it writes stencilMode = SST_STENCIL_MODE_DISABLE (0) and stencilOp = 0, because the chip otherwise treats a disabled stencil as ALWAYS + REPLACE. FASTFILL clears stencil from stencilMode. We list D24S8 but have no stencil caps and no stencil state handling.
evidence: SPEC stencilMode: 'only capable of being used when 32 BPP rendering is enabled'

items.title: W-buffer: ours turns depth OFF when an app asks for USEW
items.detail: 3dfx maps ZENABLE=USEW to WBUFFER + ENDEPTHBUFFER and remaps W from WINFO into [1, 65520] (aW/bW). The spec describes a 4.12 floating-point W depth. 3dfx advertises WBUFFER and WFOG. Our compute_regs enables depth only for D3DZB_TRUE, so a W-buffered title draws with no depth test at all. Once W-buffering is added, vertex fog must move from W to the Z iterator, as 3dfx does.
evidence: SPEC fbzMode: 'a floating-point w-buffering scheme utilizing a 4-bit exponent and a 12-bit mantissa'

items.title: Z bias through zaColor, with ENZBIAS always on
items.detail: 3dfx scales ZBIAS (0..16) by 2 at 16 bpp and by 512 for a 24-bit Z. It negates the value for LESS/LESSEQUAL, masks it to the Z width and loads it into zaColor. ENZBIAS is always set. FASTFILL also uses zaColor, so zaColor is restored after clears. The scale follows the primary's depth, not the Z's; do not copy that. Ours has no Z bias and no ZBIAS cap.

items.title: Fog: 64-entry W table; vertex fog via W, or via Z when W-buffering
items.detail:
- Table fog uses a 64-entry W-indexed table packed as (e1<<24)|(d1<<16)|(e0<<8)|d0, with ENFOGGING|FOG_DITHER.
- Vertex fog takes the specular alpha. With no Z or a Z-buffer it rides in W(fbi) with FOG_Z|FOG_ALPHA. With a W-buffer it moves to Z with FOG_Z.
- RANGEFOG is a dummy.
- A Centipede-specific linear fog fix exists.
Ours carries vertex fog by placing 1/W on a ramp table. That is proven on silicon, but it occupies W and must move to Z once W-buffering exists.

items.title: fogMode FOG_Z|FOG_ALPHA: the spec and the shipped driver disagree
items.detail: The spec says bit 4 takes precedence when both bits are set, which would mean fog by depth. Yet 3dfx's Z-buffered vertex fog sets both and sends the fog value in W(fbi). The spec also says W is clamped to [0,0xff] for the fog unit, so the likely reading is that bits[4:3]=3 selects iterated W on Napalm (inferred). Test it with d3dprobe before anyone adopts it. Our ramp-table method does not depend on it.
evidence: SPEC fogMode: 'If both bit(3) and bit(4) are set, then bit(4) takes precedence'
SPEC fbzColorPath bit 28: 'clamped to [0,0xff] inclusive for use in the Alpha Combine Unit and the fog unit'

items.title: Specular: textured triangles get an additive second pass
Destination alpha: 3dfx advertises it, then substitutes ONE/ZERO on every draw
items.detail: 3dfx advertises DESTALPHA, INVDESTALPHA and SRCALPHASAT and maps them to the hardware factors. setDX6state then rewrites the RGB factors on every Napalm draw (PRS 8373): DSTALPHA becomes ONE, and 1-DSTALPHA, SATURATE and COLORBEFOREFOG become ZERO. Below 32 bpp it also clamps the alpha-channel factors. Those values are D3D's answer for a target without alpha (inferred), so 3dfx never did real destination alpha. The spec says the silicon supports RGB ADST_ALPHA and ASATURATE. Ours passes DSTALPHA to the hardware and advertises SRCALPHASAT, so on X8R8G8B8 it reads stale alpha. Use the hardware factor only for targets with alpha, and substitute otherwise.
evidence: SPEC alpha blending factor table (ADST_ALPHA, ASATURATE)

items.title: SAMECOLOR factors: SRCCOLOR as source and DESTCOLOR as destination are real on VSA-100
items.detail: Napalm added A_SAMECOLOR/AOM_SAMECOLOR (codes 8/9). As a source factor it is the source colour; as a destination factor it is the destination colour. 3dfx maps SRCCOLOR/INVSRCCOLOR (source) and DESTCOLOR/INVDESTCOLOR (destination) to them. Our blend_src/blend_dst map those to ONE with the comment 'the chip cannot', which is true only of Voodoo3. The fix is two lines plus the caps.
evidence: SPEC: 'Added new alpha blending functions A_SAMECOLOR and AOM_SAMECOLOR to allow src*src and dst*dst blending calculations'

items.title: BLENDOP subtract and per-channel write masks exist in silicon but not through a DX7 DDI
items.detail: fogMode bits 8-11 hold RGB/alpha blend reverse and subtract; MIN and MAX are not listed. renderMode bits 17-20 are R/G/B/A write masks at 32 bpp only, and fbzMode bit 9 is all-or-nothing at every depth. 3dfx's DX8 caps leave BLENDOP and COLORWRITEENABLE commented out, and DX7 has no such states. Neither is reachable unless we implement a DX8 DDI (inferred). Low priority.
evidence: SPEC renderMode: 'Only used when 32BPP rendering is enabled'

items.title: Lines and points as quads through the setup unit; ours drops them
items.detail: dp2Line draws each line as a 1-pixel quad, with specular clamp and fog. On NT a line spans y-1..y; Win9x moved it to -0.5..+0.5 for WHQL. dp2Point draws a 1x1 quad +/-0.5 around the centre. There is no point size (MaxPointSize 1), so no point sprites. FILLMODE wireframe and point route strip and fan edges or vertices through these routines. Our DP2 walk skips every line op ('not drawn yet'). Copy the Win9x geometry, not the NT one.

items.title: Texture colour key via the FBI chromaKey, on by default, tested after filtering
items.detail: With COLORKEYENABLE set and a source colour key on the texture, 3dfx loads the FBI chromaKey and sets fbzMode ENCHROMAKEY; paletted textures go through the palette. The TMU chroma registers stay reserved for TFACTOR. A new 3dfx context starts with colorKeyEnable TRUE, which is DX5 behaviour (inferred). The chip compares the output colour after the bilinear filter, which 3dfx's own comment calls incorrect for D3D. Our caps claim TRANSPARENCY, but nothing handles COLORKEYENABLE.

items.title: Guard band: renderMode bit 21 + clip1, caps -200..2048 x -200..1536
items.detail: With GUARDBAND_CLIPPING=1 (the default), 3dfx sets renderMode ENGUARDBAND, programs clipLeftRight1/clipTopBottom1 from the viewport, and advertises a -200..2048 by -200..1536 guard band. The runtime then need not clip triangles that cross the screen edge (inferred). The spec requires even left and right edges. Ours advertises no guard band. Hidden & Dangerous needed clip initialisation (PRS 12728).
evidence: SPEC clipLeftRight1: 'must be aligned on even pixel boundries'

items.title: Pixel centre +0.5 and texel centre offset confirm our xy_bias
items.detail: PIXELCENTER defaults to 1. Every vertex x,y gets +0.5, and every texture gets textureCenter[log2 size] on S/T. Our vertex path adds xy_bias 0.5, matching the vertex half. The texel-centre half is worth a d3dprobe check (inferred).

items.title: Clears via FASTFILL, with depth from zaColor and stencil from stencilMode
evidence: SPEC FASTFILL: 'the depth value taken from zaColor[23:0] and the stencil value taken from stencilMode'

items.title: At most 6 queued swaps, because more hangs the chip
items.detail: MAXPENDINGBUFFERS_TOAVOIDHANG is 6. With vsync, 3dfx queues WaitOnVsync+1 swaps, capped at 6; without vsync it queues 6, 'to avoid hardware hang'. The registry MAX_PENDING_BUFFERS is capped at 6 too. retro3dfx bounded the swap spin that was a hard-freeze vector. This pass did not check our flip path's queue depth; it should enforce the same ceiling (inferred).

items.title: 3dfx runs D3D in SLI by default: overlay promotion + 4-way on a 4-chip board
items.detail: Creating a 3D flip chain calls Enter_3DApplication. That promotes the primary to the overlay, because desktop flips cannot be pipelined and Napalm SLI needs the overlay. It also promotes the device to SLI/AA. Compute_SLIAA_Config defaults to maximum performance: SLI_AA_CONFIGURATION 5 (4-way SLI, AA off) on a quad-chip board, 2-way on a dual-chip board. Multitexture with trilinear then gets per-chip LOD bias offsets (0/0.25/0.5/0.75). Our D3D runs on one chip, although our kernel driver already runs 4-chip SLI for Glide.

items.title: Frame-buffer CMDFIFO with packet-3 vertices vs our per-register PCI writes
Texture-cache flush on every texture state send; tLOD 0x820 when untextured
items.detail: 3dfx flushes each TMU's texture cache whenever it sends texture state: it writes the inverted base address, then the real one. Untextured draws write tLOD 0x820 and, on Napalm, both TMUs' textureMode, because the CCU can take iterated data through the TCUs. Ours flushes only when a bound texture was written. That is the same mechanism with a narrower trigger, which is fine unless a texture changes by another route (inferred).

items.title: Vendor bug: TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS overwrites ADDRESSU/V in the NT DP2 parsers
items.detail: All three NT DP2 texture-stage parsers store D3DTSS_TEXTURETRANSFORMFLAGS into ADDRESSU and ADDRESSV. A DX7 title that sets transform flags therefore loses its wrap and clamp modes on 3dfx's NT driver. Win9x revision 100 fixed it. Do not copy it. If a title's texture addressing differs between the vendor NT driver and ours, this is a candidate cause.

items.title: Do not copy Z_ACCESS_OPT (guessing at depth-clear patterns)
items.detail: W2K defines Z_ACCESS_OPT. The driver counts flips without a Z clear and changes its behaviour in DdLock and HandleSLIAA based on that count; Z bias and depth fills reset it, and Z_CLEAR_OPTIMIZATION defaults to 1. It guesses at the application's clear pattern, which can break any title that clears differently (inferred).

items.title: Vendor caps omissions and DX8-path caps bugs
Per-application workarounds in the vendor HAL
The Win9x HAL holds later fixes the NT tree lacks
No hardware T&L: the vendor's T&L HAL is CPU code and not built on NT
items.detail: TLCLIP, LIGHT, SOALIGHT, PROCPRIM, SOAPRIM, TNLDP2, TNLINIT and XFORM are an SSE/3DNow software T&L HAL. It is not built on NT (SW_TNL=0) and is optional and off by default on Win9x. It sets HWTRANSFORMANDLIGHT only on Win9x with SSE or extended 3DNow. The VSA-100 has no geometry engine, so D3D8/9 titles run software vertex processing on both drivers.

items.title: Legacy TEXTUREMAPBLEND is ignored by our HAL
items.detail: 3dfx maps each legacy TEXTUREMAPBLEND mode onto stage-0 texture stage states: DECALALPHA, MODULATEALPHA, DECAL/COPY, MODULATE (with an internal marker), DECALMASK/MODULATEMASK (with ENALPHAMASK) and ADD. Our HAL advertises DECAL, MODULATE, MODULATEALPHA, COPY and ADD but only stores the state. Stage 0 then comes from the TSS defaults: MODULATE, with texture alpha. A DX5-interface title using MODULATEALPHA, DECAL or COPY would render with the wrong alpha or lighting. This assumes the runtime passes the state through, which 3dfx's handler suggests (inferred). A d3dprobe log of a DX5 title's render states would settle it.

items.title: ValidateTextureStageState: 3dfx refuses what it cannot draw; ours always says OK
ShadeCaps: 3dfx advertises SPECULARGOURAUDRGB and FOGGOURAUD
items.detail: 3dfx's ShadeCaps are 0x000c53ca, including specular flat/gouraud in mono and RGB, and fog flat/gouraud. Ours are 0x500a (0x4008 as D3D8 reports them), with neither specular nor fog bits, although we do vertex fog. Add FOGGOURAUD now, since we fog per vertex, and SPECULARGOURAUDRGB once specular is drawn (inferred).

items.title: Render-to-texture and tiled-heap placement (not compared with ours)
AA caps: ANTIALIASSORTINDEPENDENT is SLI/AA full-scene AA; do not advertise it (user: no AA)
items.detail: On Napalm, 3dfx advertises ANTIALIASSORTINDEPENDENT. It is delivered as full-scene AA through the SLI/AA buffer configuration, when an app sets DDSCAPS2_HINTANTIALIASING or the registry asks for it. EDGEANTIALIAS is a no-op, and stippled alpha is a dummy. The user chose no AA, so our caps should keep these bits off (inferred).

items.title: Trilinear: one pass for a single texture stage (uses both TMUs, drops 2ppc); impossible in one pass with two textures
items.detail:
Trilinear is native for a single texture stage, using textureMode[30] trilinear with tc_mselect=5 (LOD fraction). TMU1 fetches the odd LODs and TMU0 the even LODs and blends them (tLOD[18] lod_odd, [19] lod_tsplit; [23] lod_zerofrac for split bilinear). One copy of the texture serves both TMUs: texBaseAddr is a full 26-bit address, which Glide's single-pass UMA path relies on.

Cost and limits:
- It takes both TMUs, and 2ppc must be off.
- Trilinear plus a second texture stage does not fit in one pass. 3dfx's driver fails ValidateTextureStageState with D3DERR_TOOMANYOPERATIONS 'because V5 doesn't support it'.
- The substitutes are LOD dither (textureMode[4], about +0.375 LOD on average, offset with lodbias) or two passes.
- SPEC section 3.3 says trilinear is two-pass, but that section is self-declared stale; section 3.5 and textureMode say single cycle.

Today our caps offer no MIPFLINEAR or LINEARMIPLINEAR (TextureFilterCaps 03010317).

Plan: map D3DTFP_LINEAR on a single active stage to 3dfx's TMU0/TMU1 split tables. With two stages, fall back to LOD dither.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3852 (txt line, 8.76 textureMode bit 30 trilinear)

items.title: Extended combine (combineMode[31]) gives MODULATE2X/4X, ADDSIGNED(2X), SUBTRACT, ADDSMOOTH, BLEND*ALPHA, MODULATE*_ADD*, COMPLEMENT and per-TMU TFACTOR natively
items.detail:
Each of the three combine stages (TMU1, TMU0, FBI) computes ((A'+B')*C'+D') << outshift.
- A and B each take one of four invert modes: x, -x, 1-x or x-1/2. The fields are combineMode[10:9] and [12:11], with alpha at [22:21] and [24:23].
- outshift is x1, x2 or x4: combineMode[15:14], with alpha at [27:26].

3dfx's Napalm driver advertised, in 2 stages: MODULATE2X/4X, ADDSIGNED(2X), SUBTRACT, ADDSMOOTH, BLEND{DIFFUSE,TEXTURE,FACTOR,CURRENT}ALPHA, BLENDTEXTUREALPHAPM and the MODULATE*_ADD* ops.

TFACTOR inside a TMU stage comes from that TMU's chromaKey/chromaRange registers, used as a constant colour once combineMode[30]=1. That setting also disables texture chroma substitution, and section 21.8 requires it for the new combine functionality.

Limits:
- Complement on arg2 is not available for ADDSIGNED, SUBTRACT and BLEND*ALPHA.
- ALPHAREPLICATE works except as a TMU's M input.
- D3D8 LERP and MULTIPLYADD fit only some argument sets (inferred).
- A third, texture-less stage in the FBI unit may be possible (inferred); 3dfx offered 3 stages only on Voodoo3.

Today:
- Our driver writes combineMode = 0.
- TexOpCaps is 0x184f, with no 2X/4X, ADDSIGNED or SUBTRACT.
- An application that uses MODULATE2X/4X anyway gets MODULATE.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2825 (combineMode[30]: chromaRange = TMU constant colour)
/home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:6248 (21.8: combineMode[30] must be set)
/home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/SW Architecture Spec.doc:753 (txt line, complement arg2 unsupported)

items.title: Cube maps, volume textures, DOT3, BUMPENVMAP(LUMINANCE) and PREMODULATE are impossible
items.detail:
Why each one cannot be built:
- Cube and volume maps: each TMU iterates only S/W, T/W and 1/W. There is no R or Q coordinate, no face select and no depth slice, and textureMode/tLOD describe a single 2D mip chain.
- DOT3: the combine units work per channel, (a+/-b)*c+d in each R, G and B lane, so no cross-channel sum exists.
- EMBM: a TMU's output enters the next TMU only as a combine input, never its address generation. The only TMU-to-TMU link is the interface named by trexInit1 tt_FIFO_sil and rg_ttcii_inh.

3dfx commented out CUBEMAP, VOLUMEMAP and DOTPRODUCT3, and set PreModulate, BumpEnvMap and DotProduct3 to FALSE. Keep all of these out of the caps.

The 'bump mapping' in SPEC's overview means emboss-style bumps done with the two TMUs (inferred).
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3905 (txt line, per-channel combine units)
/home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3993 (expect data from upstream TREX)

items.title: Destination alpha: native at 32 bpp alongside depth and stencil; 1-bit at 15 bpp; at 16 bpp only with depth off
items.detail:
What each render depth gives:
- 32 bpp (renderMode[1:0]=2): the alpha planes are always enabled, and fbzMode[18] must be clear. renderMode[20] gates alpha writes. DESTALPHA and INVDESTALPHA are blend factors 3 and 7.
- 15 bpp: the 1-bit alpha shares the fbzMode[9] write enable with RGB.
- 16 bpp: the aux buffer can serve as an alpha buffer only with depth disabled.

Alpha-channel blend factors are zero, srcA, dstA, one, 1-srcA and 1-dstA at 32 bpp, but only ZERO and ONE at 15 and 16 bpp.

Today:
- The blend caps lack DESTALPHA and INVDESTALPHA (SrcBlend 1f33, DestBlend 3f).
