- The alpha channel always blends with ONE/ZERO, so a 32 bpp target's alpha never blends.

Plan: offer DESTALPHA on 32 bpp targets only, and map it to ONE/ZERO elsewhere (inferred convention).
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3266 (txt line, fbzMode bit 18 / automatic dest alpha)

items.title: Stencil: native 8-bit with all eight D3D ops and every compare function, at 32 bpp only
items.detail:
Registers:
- stencilMode holds the reference [7:0], mask [15:8], write mask [23:16], enable [24] and function [27:25].
- stencilOp holds fail, zfail and zpass in [3:0], [7:4] and [11:8].
- The eight ops are keep, zero, replace, incr-sat, decr-sat, invert, incr-wrap and decr-wrap: exactly D3DSTENCILOP 1-8.

Stencil works only with renderMode[1:0]=2, whose aux word is 24-bit Z plus 8-bit stencil. That is the only configuration where D24S8 exists anyway.

With the enable bit clear, the chip behaves as ALWAYS/REPLACE, so the write mask must be cleared too. Our 32 bpp setup already does this.

Clears:
- FASTFILL clears all 8 stencil bits.
- A masked clear needs the 2D engine with a byte mask, which is what Glide does.

Two-sided stencil is impossible: there is a single stencilOp register (inferred).

Today the stencil caps are 0. D24S8 is listed, but its stencil is never written or tested. 3dfx offered all 8 ops.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3358 (txt line, stencil only at 32 BPP)

items.title: Colour and Z depth must match; our driver refuses a 32 bpp target with D16 though the runtime reports the pair as matching (CreateDevice fails on .124)
items.detail:
renderMode[1:0] sets the pixel size of the colour and aux buffers together:
- 16-bit Z (20.12 iterator) pairs with 565 or 1555.
- 24-bit Z plus 8-bit stencil (28.4 iterator) pairs with 8888.
- zaColor's depth field is [15:0] versus [23:0].
3dfx's own comment: 'Napalm cannot handle a different depth zbuffer and rendering surface!'

3dfx fixed both directions by allocation:
- 16 bpp target with a 32-bit Z: use a 16-bit aux buffer inside the 32-bit Z surface. We already do this; it is the Rainbow Six fix.
- 32 bpp target with a requested D16: allocate the Z at 32 bits, at create time on a 32 bpp desktop or by reallocating at attach. DX8 advertises this as D16 with D3DFORMAT_OP_ZSTENCIL_WITH_ARBITRARY_COLOR_DEPTH.
- A locked D16 then holds 24-bit Z in 32-bit words; 3dfx patched DepthFill values for that.

On .124 the runtime reports CheckDepthStencilMatch(X8R8G8B8, D16) = 1, but vcr_rt_format refuses the 32/16 pair. The on-box run measured the result: CreateDevice failed with 0x8876086c (D3DERR_INVALIDCALL), and the log said 'ContextCreate refused: 32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z'.

items.title: Mirror addressing is native per axis (tLOD[28]/[29]) but not offered
items.detail:
tLOD[28] (tmirrors) and [29] (tmirrort) mirror each axis independently. Glide's GR_TEXTURECLAMP_MIRROR_EXT and 3dfx's driver both use them; 3dfx sets TMIRRORS per stage and advertises D3DPTADDRESSCAPS_MIRROR.

MIRRORONCE has no single bit (inferred).

Today TextureAddressCaps is 0x15: WRAP, CLAMP and INDEPENDENTUV, without MIRROR.

items.title: Border-colour addressing is impossible: clamp is clamp-to-edge and there is no border register
items.detail:
textureMode's clamp forces S into [0, width) and T into [0, height), which samples the edge texel.

The TMU register set (textureMode, tLOD, tDetail, texBaseAddr*, nccTable, chromaKey, chromaRange) has no border colour. 3dfx's feature matrix and architecture spec both say Border Color: No.

Padding a border ring into the texture is only an approximation (inferred). Keep D3DPTADDRESSCAPS_BORDER off.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3865 (txt line, clamp to [0, width))

items.title: P8, A8P8 and alpha palettes exist in the register spec but have never been shown to draw correctly on this silicon
items.detail:
What the spec defines:
- textureMode format 5 (P8), format 6 (P8 expanded to ARGB 6666, the only alpha palette, at 6 bits a channel) and format 14 (AP88 = A8P8).
- A 256-entry palette, written through the nccTable0 I/Q registers with bit 31 set.
- Four texels are looked up at once, so bilinear filtering works on P8.
Glide writes the palette that way (0x80000000 | ((i & 0xFE) << 23) | rgb into nccTable0[4..11]) and broadcasts one palette to both TMUs.

Why it is still unproven:
- The vintage driver lane found P8 textures sampling white under 3dfx's D3D driver on Napalm. The symptom was GoldSrc in D3D: a white world under a textured RGB sky.
- That lane turned on 3dfx's own DISABLE_PAL8_ON_NAPALM switch, which compiles P8 and A8P8 out.
- 3dfx itself disabled and re-enabled palettized textures (revs 24/25), and left its DX7 A8P8 entry permanently off.
- Our OpenGL driver runs Counter-Strike with FX_NO_PALETTED_TEXTURE=1.
- The cause is unknown: the palette write path, the chip field, or the driver.

Do not offer P8 until a d3dprobe P8 quad (or Glide grTexDownloadTable with a GR_TEXFMT_P_8 texture) draws correctly on .124. Today texP8 is 0.
games: GoldSrc titles in the Direct3D renderer (Half-Life, Counter-Strike)

items.title: No line or point primitive: draw them as triangles; our driver advertises line caps but skips every LINE and POINT opcode
items.detail:
The 3D engine's only drawing commands are triangleCMD/ftriangleCMD, the setup unit's sBeginTriCMD/sDrawTriCMD, NOP, FASTFILL and SWAPBUFFER. The spec itself says lines are 'special case triangles'.

How others draw them:
- Glide draws a line as a 4-vertex strip offset by +/-0.5 in the minor axis, and a point as a small triangle pair.
- 3dfx's D3D driver draws lines as two triangles with a sub-pixel adjustment table, and points as a +/-0.5 quad (MaxPointSize 1; its DX8 LineCaps are 0).
- The 2D engine's Bresenham lines have no Z, texture or blending, so they are no use for D3D.

Today dpcLineCaps is filled by the triangle prim_caps, while D3DNTDP2OP_LINELIST, LINESTRIP, POINTS and the indexed variants are skipped as 'not drawn yet'. HUD lines, particles and wireframe draw nothing.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:550 (txt line, lines as special-case triangles)

items.title: Z-bias is native as a constant (fbzMode[16] adds zaColor); there is no slope-scaled bias
items.detail:
fbzMode[16] adds zaColor[15:0] (16 bpp) or zaColor[23:0] (32 bpp) to the computed Z or 1/W.

3dfx's mapping of D3DRENDERSTATE_ZBIAS 0..16:
- state << 1 with a 16-bit Z, state << 9 with a 24-bit Z;
- negated for LESS and LESSEQUAL;
- ZBIAS was advertised.

zaColor is also the FASTFILL clear depth and the constant depth for fbzMode[20], so the bias must be restored after every clear. Glide saves and restores it; our Clear2 writes zaColor.

D3D9 SLOPESCALEDEPTHBIAS has no register (inferred).

Today RasterCaps 00100191 lacks ZBIAS.

items.title: W-buffer is native (fbzMode[3]): 4.12 float at 16 bpp, 24-bit at 32 bpp, sharing the FBI 1/W with the fog table
items.detail:
fbzMode[3] compares the inverse of the normalized W, stored as a float with a 4-bit exponent and 12-bit mantissa. fbzMode[21] chooses W or Z as the source of that float.

At 32 bpp, Glide's farthest W value is 0xFFFFFF, and 3dfx's matrix lists a 24-bit W with 8-bit stencil.

The W used is the FBI's Wb, which also indexes the fog table. So:
- A W-buffer and table fog combine naturally (3dfx's FnZTable case 8).
- Vertex fog with a W-buffer moves the fog factor into Z (case 5).

3dfx offered WBUFFER and WFOG. Today WBUFFER is not offered and D3DZB_USEW is not handled.

items.title: Render-to-texture works for linear 565/1555/8888 textures with pitch = width x bytes and a 16-byte-aligned base, but not with SLI on
items.detail:
Requirements:
- colBufferAddr must be 16-byte aligned, and colBufferStride[13:0] is a linear stride that must also be 16-byte aligned.
- A linear texture's rows are packed (base + lod_offset + s + t*lod_width), so the target's pitch must equal width x bytes.
- Glide's TEXTUREBUFFER extension works exactly this way and refuses a format that does not match the render mode.
- After rendering, flush the texture caches: write texBaseAddr inverted and then rewrite it, between NOP pixel flushes.

Limits:
- Under SLI a target is split across the chips' memories by y' packing, so a render-target texture needs SLI off for that target (inferred).
- 3dfx marked 4444, 332, 8332, L8, A8, A4L4 and A8L8 as OFFSCREEN_RENDERTARGET, but the 3D engine cannot draw those formats. They would need render-then-2D-convert.

Today render-target textures keep DirectDraw's placement and pitch.

items.title: AGP (non-local) texturing is impossible: the texture base is a local 26-bit address, and the 6000's chips sit on PCI-66 behind a bridge
items.detail:
texBaseAddr forms a 26-bit local-memory address with no AGP or non-local bit.

AGP serves only two purposes:
- a command-FIFO location;
- a DMA source into local memory (agpMoveCMD, CMDFIFO packet 6). The spec itself calls packet 6 'pretty much broken with AGP command fifos'.

PSEXT: the SLI boards attach 'using a universal slot and the PCI 66 protocol', and 'the 4-way SLI board uses a bridge chip'. On this board even the AGP DMA path is out of reach (inferred).

3dfx's own word:
- SWARCH: 'lack of support for AGP execute mode'; AGP Texture Memory: No.
- TEXTURENONLOCALVIDMEM is commented out.
- D3D.XLS row 147 says Yes; that is an API-level line (the runtime places the texture and the driver copies it) and contradicts the register spec.

Every texture must fit in a chip's 32 MB beside its buffers, replicated per chip in SLI.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:6253 (packet 6 broken with AGP CMDFIFOs)

items.title: Anisotropic filtering is impossible (one bilinear footprint per TMU per pixel)
items.detail:
textureMode[1] and [2] choose only point or bilinear for minification and magnification. tDetail adds only separate RGB and alpha filter selects.

3dfx reported MaxAnisotropy 1, and its matrix and spec say No.

A negative LOD bias is the only substitute: sharper, but aliased (inferred). Our MaxAnisotropy 1 is correct.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3828-3829 (txt line, min/mag filter bits)

items.title: Vertex fog can be exact: the fog unit takes iterated alpha, Z or W directly (fogMode[4:3]); our driver approximates it through a synthetic 1/W
items.detail:
Table fog is per-pixel: 64 entries indexed by a float of the FBI's 1/W, with the 8 low bits interpolating between entries.

The fog source mux:
- fogMode bit 3 selects iterated alpha; bit 4 selects the top 8 bits of iterated Z.
- 3dfx's shipping driver sets both bits to feed iterated W, clamped to [0,0xff] when fbzColorPath[28]=1 (with that bit clear, W wraps).
- With a Z-buffer, 3dfx uses FOG_Z|FOG_ALPHA and writes sOowfbi = 255 - specular alpha.
- With a W-buffer, it uses FOG_Z and carries the factor in Z (sVz = factor << 8).
Either way the D3D vertex fog factor is interpolated exactly per pixel (FOGGOURAUD).

Our driver instead sends a synthetic 1/W chosen to land on a ramp table, which is only approximate across a triangle. vcr_fog.h justifies this with 'a fog unit that only knows W', a premise the spec contradicts.

FOGRANGE is a vertex-processing matter (inferred), and 3dfx did not offer it. Today ShadeCaps lacks FOGGOURAUD.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2867 (txt line, table fog from 1/W)
/home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2791 (fbzColorPath bit 28 W clamp for fog unit)

items.title: Fog source with fogMode bits 3 and 4 both set: the spec says bit 4 (Z) wins, but 3dfx's code relies on it meaning W
items.detail:
The conflict:
- SPEC section 8.22 says 'If both bit(3) and bit(4) are set, then bit(4) takes precedence', which would mean Z.
- 3dfx's driver sets FOG_Z|FOG_ALPHA and puts the fog value in Wfbi.
- SPEC section 8.20 says the clamped W feeds 'the Alpha Combine Unit and the fog unit'.
The 8.22 sentence looks inherited from SST-1 (inferred).

One d3dprobe run settles it: run fogvertex with the factor in Wb and fogMode[4:3]=3, and compare pixel-exact against D3D linear fog.

If W does not reach the fog unit, fall back to FOG_Z with the factor in the top byte of Z, as 3dfx does under a W-buffer.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2885 (txt line, bit 4 takes precedence)

items.title: Specular has no second colour iterator: add it on the host when untextured, draw a second additive pass when textured
items.detail:
There is only one ARGB iterator set per triangle (startR..startA, sARGB).

3dfx's method:
- Untextured: CLAMP888(diffuse + specular) per vertex on the host.
- Textured: draw the same triangle again, with the specular colour as the iterated colour, blend ONE/ONE (or keep the source factor under alpha blending), ZFUNC EQUAL when Z writes are on, FOGADD-only fog, and auto-strip off.
- Its matrix says 'Napalm: single texture scenario only, 2-pass', and 'Specular into texture stage(s): No' (just a second iterated colour).

The two-pass method is exact for opaque surfaces and approximate under alpha blending (inferred).

A single-pass variant is untested (inferred, low confidence): load a TMU's colour iterator separately through a chip-field sARGB write, have a free TMU compute texture x diffuse, and let the FBI add specular.

Today ShadeCaps has no SPECULARGOURAUDRGB.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2239-2243 (txt line, startR..startA FBI only)

items.title: COLORWRITEENABLE: per channel at 32 bpp (renderMode[20:17] under fbzMode[9]), all-or-nothing at 15/16 bpp; PLANEMASK impossible
items.detail:
By render depth:
- 32 bpp: renderMode[17], [18], [19] and [20] enable R, G, B and A writes, and are 'only used when 32 BPP rendering is enabled'. fbzMode[9] is the master enable.
- 15 bpp: fbzMode[9] gates RGB and the 1-bit alpha together.
- 16 bpp: only the masks 0x0 and 0xF can be honoured, through fbzMode[9].

3dfx never offered COLORWRITEENABLE. Its matrix says plane masking 'can only mask individual color channels', so PLANEMASK is impossible.

Today PrimitiveMiscCaps is 0x72, without COLORWRITEENABLE. Offering it on 32 bpp targets, and 0/0xF elsewhere, is a register write.

Whether 16 bpp really ignores renderMode[19:17] has not been measured.

items.title: Our driver leaves dithering on for 32 bpp targets; the spec requires fbzMode[8] clear at 32 bpp
items.detail:
The spec says: 'fbzMode bit(8) must be cleared when 32-bit color rendering is selected (renderMode[1:0]=0x2)'. Glide clears it at 32 bpp and forces 2x2 dither plus dither subtraction (fbzMode[11], [19]) at 16 bpp; 3dfx's D3D driver sets DITHER2x2.

vcrdd_d3d.c sets FZ_DITHER whenever D3DRENDERSTATE_DITHERENABLE is TRUE, at every target depth, and nothing clears it. Every D3D32 draw from an application that enables dither therefore violates the spec; the effect on silicon has not been measured.

Also:
- We use the 4x4 matrix with no dither subtraction.
- Under SLI, dithering breaks at a band height of 1.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3254 (txt line, bit 8 must be cleared at 32 bpp)

items.title: SRCCOLOR as source factor and DESTCOLOR as destination factor are native (A_SAMECOLOR 0x8/0x9); our driver maps both to ONE
items.detail:
The alphaMode factor codes:
- 0x2 means the OTHER pixel's colour: destination colour as a source factor, source colour as a destination factor.
- 0x8 (A_SAMECOLOR) means the SAME pixel's colour; 0x6 and 0x9 are the inverses.
- 0xF is SRCALPHASAT (min(As, 1-Ad)) as a source factor, and colour-before-fog as a destination factor.
So all 13 D3D blend factors map.

3dfx's Napalm caps add SRCCOLOR, INVSRCCOLOR, DESTALPHA, INVDESTALPHA and SRCALPHASAT as source factors, and DESTALPHA and DESTCOLOR as destination factors.

Our vcrdd_d3d.c blend_src and blend_dst return BF_ONE for these, commented 'SRCCOLOR the chip cannot' and 'DESTCOLOR the chip cannot'. Both comments are wrong for the VSA-100. The caps hide the factors too: SrcBlend 1f33 lacks SRCCOLOR and INVSRCCOLOR, and DestBlend 3f lacks DESTCOLOR and INVDESTCOLOR.

items.title: Blend ops ADD, SUBTRACT and REVSUBTRACT are native (fogMode[11:8]) with separate alpha factors at 32 bpp; MIN and MAX are impossible
items.detail:
Blend operations:
- fogMode[8] and [9] set the order and add/subtract for RGB; [10] and [11] do the same for alpha.
- That gives (S*a)+(D*b), (S*a)-(D*b) and (D*b)-(S*a).

alphaMode[23:16] gives the alpha channel its own factors: at 32 bpp, zero, srcA, dstA, one, 1-srcA and 1-dstA.

There is no MIN or MAX, which is why 3dfx left D3DPMISCCAPS_BLENDOP off (inferred reason).

Today the alpha channel always blends with ONE/ZERO, and no blend op is exposed.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2853-2856 (txt line, fogMode blend order/op)

items.title: Alpha test is native; Glide's skip-transparent-pixels trick is a free fill-rate win
items.detail:
alphaMode has the enable at [0], eight compare functions at [3:1] and the reference at [31:24]. Our driver already uses it.

Glide forces alpha test GT 0 when blending with SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA and Z writes off, so pixels with alpha 0 skip their read-modify-write.

The same applies to our driver when the application has not enabled alpha test (inferred benefit). It must not change results.

items.title: Colour key: the FBI chroma compare runs after texture lookup and before the combine; TMU chroma substitution cannot coexist with TFACTOR or the extended combine
items.detail:
Two places can key on colour:
- The FBI: fbzMode[1] compares the texel against chromaKey 'immediately after texture mapping lookup, but before the color combine unit and fog'. A keyed texel is dropped even when it is later modulated. chromaRange adds per-channel inclusive or exclusive ranges.
- The TMU: its own chroma substitution replaces the texel with black before filtering. It works only while combineMode[30]=0.

The conflict: combineMode[30]=1 is required both for the new combine functionality and for using chromaKey/chromaRange as the per-TMU constant colour (TFACTOR). 3dfx's D3D driver therefore keys in the FBI only, and keeps the TMU chromaKey for the texture factor.

Plan: use FBI keying for D3D colour key. Bilinear fringes remain (inferred).
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3224 (txt line, chroma compare after texture lookup)

items.title: Stipple: 4x8 pattern or rotate mode only; D3D's 32x32 STIPPLEPATTERN cannot be expressed
items.detail:
fbzMode[2] enables stipple masking. fbzMode[12] chooses either a rotating 32-bit register or a 4x8 monochrome pattern indexed by x[2:0] and y[1:0].

STIPPLEDALPHA could be approximated (inferred). These titles rarely use stipple (inferred).

items.title: The chip samples many more texture formats (332, 8332, A8, L8, A4L4, A8L8, P8, A8P8, FXT1, DXT1-5) than the 565/1555/4444/8888/DXT1/3/5 we offer
items.detail:
textureMode[11:8] selects formats 0-15, plus the compressed set under textureMode[31].

D3D formats these can serve:
- R3G3B2, A8R3G3B2, L8, A4L4, A8L8 and A8.
- DXT2 and DXT4, which use the same hardware formats as DXT3 and DXT5.
- The X variants, with alpha forced to one (inferred).
- A8 needs care: the hardware also returns RGB = alpha where D3D expects 0, so its colour must not be used (inferred).

Not native: R8G8B8 (convert on upload), the bump formats, and YUY2/UYVY as textures.

3dfx's DX7 list carried 332, P8, 8332, L8, A8, A4L4, A8L8, AP88, 8888, DXT1-5 and FXT1. P8 and A8P8 have since been compiled out (see hw-09).

Today the caps list 565, 1555, 4444, 8888, DXT1, DXT3 and DXT5.

items.title: Textures: 2048x2048 maximum (tLOD[30] tbig), aspect up to 8:1, power of two only, base 16-byte aligned
items.detail:
Limits:
- tLOD[30] counts LODs from 2048.
- lod_aspect [22:21] with s_is_wider [20] allows at most 8:1.
- Glide reports no non-power-of-2 support.
- texBaseAddr holds address bits [25:4] (bit 1 supplies the 26th), so a base on a 4-byte boundary samples from the wrong address.

That last rule is exactly what produced UT2003's noise on .124 (2026-11-08). It is fixed by aligning every texture our driver places.

Other notes:
- Multi-base mode (tLOD[24] with texBaseAddr1/2/38) could sample per-level DirectDraw allocations without repacking (inferred).
- Non-power-of-2 textures, or aspect ratios above 8:1, need padding with scaled coordinates (clamp, no mips) (inferred).

items.title: Texture repeat range is bounded by the 14.18 S/T iterators (about +/-32 repeats at 256-texel scaling, inferred)
items.detail:
S/W and T/W iterate as 14.18 fixed point, and our VcrDd3dTexScale scales the wide side to 256 texels. That leaves roughly +/-32 repeats before the integer part wraps (inferred arithmetic).

3dfx reported dwMaxTextureRepeat 256 with TEXREPEATNOTSCALEDBYSIZE.

Large tiled floors that repeat further would swim. The standard remedy is to re-base each triangle's integer texture offset on the host (inferred).

items.title: LOD bias is native (tLOD[17:12], 4.2 signed, -8..+7.75) with lodmin/lodmax clamps; our caps lack MIPMAPLODBIAS
items.detail:
The fields:
- tLOD[17:12] holds lodbias, 4.2 signed.
- tLOD[5:0] and [11:6] hold lodmin and lodmax, which serve D3DTSS_MAXMIPLEVEL.

3dfx converted D3D's float bias with CalcBias42 and offered MIPMAPLODBIAS. The planning-era architecture spec said No; the shipped driver had it.

The LOD dither offset (+0.375) must be subtracted from the bias when dither is on. Glide clamps the bias to -0x20..0x1f.

Today RasterCaps lacks MIPMAPLODBIAS.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/SW Architecture Spec.doc:972 (txt line, planning-era No)

items.title: Two pixels per clock (combineMode[29]) is unused by our D3D: about 1.7x fill per chip for single-textured 15/16 bpp draws
items.detail:
How it works:
- combineMode[29] turns it on, and renderMode[24:22] sets the band height.
- It applies only to single-textured triangles, and both TMUs must hold identical state.
- Leaving 2ppc needs 12 NOPs addressed to the TMUs only (chip field 0x6); this is a hardware bug.
- The spec recommends it for 15/16 bpp only; at 32 bpp only at very low resolutions. It may need disabling at very high resolutions or refresh rates.

It works on this silicon: our Glide's 4-chip fill of 1124.6 Mpix/s at 166.8 MHz is about 281 Mpix/s per chip, above what 1 pixel per clock allows (inferred arithmetic).

3dfx enables it by default, writes it into all three combineModes and drops it for trilinear. Ours writes combineMode = 0, so it always runs at 1 pixel per clock.

Plan: land it default-OFF behind a Diag switch, with a d3dprobe perf A/B.

items.title: Four-chip SLI is native, but our Direct3D renders on chip 0 only
items.detail:
How SLI works:
- sliCtrl assigns line y to the chip whose (y & renderMask) == compareMask, and each chip packs its lines as y'.
- chipMask steers register writes, and commands can go to all chips at once.
- Linear memory (textures) overlaps the master chip's memory; tiled memory (buffers) is split across chips.

Caveats:
- FASTFILL in SLI runs at single-chip speed; use 2D blits for clears.
- Dithering breaks at a band height of 1.
- Y-origin flips need care.
- Render-target textures need SLI off (inferred).

Our D3D writes sliCtrl = 0 in its reset, and IOCTL_VCR_SLI is reached only through Glide's SLI_AA_REQUEST. The miniport already drives 4-chip SLI for Glide (miniport/vcrmp_sli.c).

Ceiling: 4 chips x 2 pixels/clock x 166.8 MHz is about 1.33 Gpix/s single-textured, against 0.167 Gpix/s today (inferred estimate). The CPU's software T&L limits the real gain.
games: every Direct3D title on .124 (all render on chip 0)

items.title: A frame-buffer CMDFIFO with packet-3 strips and fans could replace our PCI-FIFO register writes and independent triangles
items.detail:
Today our driver writes 3D registers through the 32-entry PCI FIFO with room polling: one sBeginTriCMD plus two sDrawTriCMD per triangle, and 8-14 words per vertex.

What the CMDFIFO offers:
- It lives in frame-buffer memory (the lower 16 MB only) and counts holes, so CPU writes may land out of order.
- Packet 3 carries up to 16 vertices of an independent, strip or fan stream per header.
- Packet 5 streams texture-port data in order with rendering.
- There are two independent streams.

3dfx's driver emits packet 3. Strips and fans send one vertex per triangle instead of three (inferred).

The packet 6 and AGP paths are unusable on this board (see hw-14).
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:4832-4836 (13.1.6 packet 3, max 16 vertices, strip codes)

items.title: Guard-band clipping is native (renderMode[21], coordinates to +/-4k); our caps report a zero guard band
items.detail:
renderMode[21] clips against clipLeftRight1/clipTopBottom1 while the rasterizer accepts coordinates in [-4k, 4k]. The left and right edges must be even.

3dfx reported a guard band of -200..2048 x -200..1536 and set SST_RM_ENGUARDBAND.

With a zero guard band, the runtime clips every primitive that crosses the viewport on the CPU (inferred cost).

items.title: Only packed sARGB reaches the TMUs; our driver's separate sRed..sAlpha floats reach the FBI only
items.detail:
The spec's register table lists sARGB as FBI+TREX* and sRed..sAlpha as FBI only. The TMU combine inputs for iterated RGB and alpha (SST_CM_TC_*SELECT_IRGB/IA) are therefore fed only by sARGB. 3dfx sends packed sARGB and uses diffuse inside TMU stages.

Ours writes sRed, sGreen, sBlue and sAlpha, and vcr_3dregs.h marks SARGB 'NOT used'.

This is harmless while no TMU stage selects diffuse. Once the extended combine lands, it would break diffuse-in-stage ops such as BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA in stage 0, or MODULATE with D3DTA_DIFFUSE in a TMU (inferred from the chip column). Verify with d3dprobe.

items.title: 1555 render targets (A1R5G5B5/X1R5G5B5) are native (renderMode[1:0]=1) but not offered
items.detail:
renderMode=1 renders ARGB1555. renderMode[16:15] chooses the stored alpha bit: always 0, always 1, or the MSB of the blended alpha.

The 1-bit alpha shares the RGB write enable and FASTFILL with the colour planes, and destination alpha is automatic.

Our vcr_rt_format accepts only 16 and 32 bpp targets (565 and 8888).

items.title: Projected textures (D3DTTFF_PROJECTED) look possible per TMU but are unverified
items.detail:
Each TMU divides by its own 1/W: sWtmu0, and sWtmu1 for TMU1. textureMode's tclampw exists 'when projecting textures to avoid projecting behind the source of the projection'.

Sending q*rhw as a TMU's W, and s*rhw and t*rhw as S and T, would give per-pixel s/q and t/q (inferred).

3dfx did not offer PROJECTED. Verify with a d3dprobe quad where q != 1, compared against a CPU reference.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:3859 (txt line, tclampw for projected textures)

items.title: No flat-shade mode: replicate the provoking vertex's colour on the host, which loses strip reuse
items.detail: Colour is always iterated from three vertices. 3dfx replicated the provoking vertex's colour on the host, and noted 'HW cannot support FLAT_SHADE and Auto Strip/Fan'.
evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/DOCS/avenger_spec.doc:2239-2243 (txt line, iterated colour registers)

items.title: FASTFILL clears colour, depth and stencil in one command, but has no per-bit stencil mask and runs at single-chip speed in SLI
items.detail:
At 32 bpp, FASTFILL writes:
- the color1 ARGB value to the colour buffer;
- zaColor[23:0] as depth;
- stencilMode[7:0] as stencil, when the stencil write mask is set.

Limits:
- Per-bit stencil masks are not honoured.
- In SLI, a hardware bug limits FASTFILL to single-chip fill. SGRAM tiled surfaces also corrupt, but the 6000 uses SDRAM. 3dfx recommends the 2D BLT engine in SLI.
- At 15 bpp the 1-bit alpha cannot be cleared separately.

items.title: Whether a stale STENCIL_ENABLE is ignored at 16 bpp is unproven
items.detail:
The spec says stencil functions are usable only at 32 bpp. That supports vcr_rtfmt.h's assumption that the chip ignores stencilMode at 16 bpp, but nobody has measured it, and Glide programs stencilMode with no pixel-size check.

If the assumption is wrong, a 16 bpp D3D session that follows a 32 bpp Glide/OpenGL session that used stencil would fail or rewrite its pixels. The remedy named in vcr_3dseq.h is the Diag Reset3D switch.

items.title: Source caveat: SPEC section 3.3 is self-declared out of date and contradicts the register chapters
items.detail:
Section 3.3 opens with 'This section is horribly out-of-date and inaccurate ... Please ignore this section'. Its stale claims:
- trilinear is two-pass (L554); section 3.5 and textureMode[30] say single cycle;
- destination alpha works only without depth (L573); section 21.4 says it is automatic at 32 bpp;
- a palette offset register exists (L567); section 8.82 describes register writes only.

Other conflicts between sources:
- Section 8.22's 'bit(4) takes precedence' conflicts with 3dfx's fog code (see hw-17).
- SWARCH's DX7 table is from the planning stage; it says no LOD bias, which the shipped driver had.
- D3D.XLS says AGP texture memory: Yes, which the register spec contradicts (see hw-14).

From chapter 12 on, the body's chapter numbers are one higher than the table of contents.

items.title: Silicon checks the documents cannot settle, each sized as a d3dprobe test
items.detail:
The checks:
1. Does fogMode[4:3]=3 use iterated W? (fogvertex already exists.)
2. Is a stale STENCIL_ENABLE ignored at 16 bpp?
3. Can a chip-field sARGB write load a TMU's colour iterator separately? (This would allow single-pass specular.)
4. What does 2ppc gain at 1024x768 and 1280x1024, at 16 and 32 bpp? (perf mode, behind a default-OFF Diag switch)
5. Is renderMode[19:17] ignored at 16 bpp?
6. Do projected textures work through the TMU W?
7. How does D3D fill scale on 1, 2 and 4 chips in SLI?
8. Does a P8 quad draw correctly? (see hw-09)

Each needs a new d3dprobe mode with a golden. Rules for running them:
- Never run vcrctl or ExtEscape tools while a D3D game runs.
- Change one Diag setting per clean boot.
- Space mode switches at least 5 s apart.

understand:onbox.summary:
The on-box pass on .124 is done: 47 min of box time (09:59-10:46), 13 d3dprobe runs and 4 in-game D3D sessions. The box stayed healthy throughout and ended at 1280x1024x32@85 with nothing of the run left running. Max Payne was not launched, and nothing was rebooted or changed in the registry, driver or Diag.

**Headline: Glide's command FIFO left switched on stops every D3D triangle.** An OpenGL/Glide 4-chip SLI session about 2 h earlier closed on h5 Glide's not-idle path. Its SLI went off through the kernel's display reset rather than Glide's own request. That path skips `cmdFifo0.baseSize = 0` (minihwc.c hwcRestoreVideo), so cmdFifo0 stayed ON: baseSize 0x1fe, window 0x18000-0x117000, readPtr stuck.
- **What broke.** D3D devices still created and cleared, but drew no triangles: 9/40 fullscreen 1024x768x32, 7/42 windowed.
- **How it got worse.** A windowed texture placed inside the FIFO window made the chip busy (status 0xa1f). The desktop's 2D engine then gave up, and after that the D3D HAL was not offered at all (8876086a).
- **Recovery.** One paced mode switch (`vcrctl modeseq`) set off the miniport's busy-at-mode-set engine reset, which turns cmdFifo0 off. With nothing else changed, the same tests passed: 40/40, 42/42 and 40/40 (640x480x16).

**The X8R8G8B8 + D16 lead is confirmed.** The runtime reports the pair as matching, but CreateDevice returns 8876086c and the ring logs 513/12 "32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z". The runtime's own revert then made two CRT mode switches 156 ms apart.

**On a clean engine, every d3dprobe texture and decode check passes:** 83/0 and 37/3. The 3 failures are the `*_def` locks, which the D3D8 runtime refuses. Every decode had 0 wrong texels, the 1:1 case included, so the half-pixel fix holds on silicon.

**First in-game D3D captures** (UT2004 twice, UT2003 flyby, Halo timedemo):
- The sky, weapons, HUD, text, trees and smoke are right.
- Terrain and rock meshes are covered in blocky multi-coloured noise.
- Lightmapped surfaces in UT2003/UT2004 are very dark.
- Large solid-white sky/horizon areas appear in UT2003/UT2004.
- A Halo glow is drawn as a visible square.
- UT2003's grass is blue.

**Performance is very low.**
- UT2003 flyby, 640x480x16: 9.41 fps average, 2.07 minimum. Frames take 123 ms, 116.7 ms of that inside DrawPrimitive.
- UT2004 at 1280x960x16: 4-6 fps.
- Halo's timedemo had not finished after 485 s.
- d3dprobe perf only shows the 85 Hz vsync.

**Not reached:**
- Red Faction has `-level`/`-timedemo` switches but needs its disc mounted, which would change registry state.
- Shogo, Thief II and Hidden & Dangerous: no documented switch found.
- The remaining D3D titles (Jedi Knight/MotS, SS2, Thief Gold, Rainbow Six, BF1942, AvP) were not tried in-game.

**Committed and pushed to master as e3056d1** (evidence only). `tests/run_all.sh` has 3 failures, none in these files: gameres apply-saves, version tags not on origin, and a pxe DevicePath check. retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md and the v56k plan were not updated; that is left for the synthesis step.

items.title: Glide's command FIFO left on after a not-idle Glide close silently stops every D3D triangle (clears still work)
items.detail:
An OpenGL/Glide 4-chip SLI session (pid 1892, 75242-75345 s, ~2 h before) did not close cleanly. Its SLI went off through IOCTL_VIDEO_RESET_DEVICE ('SLI/AA off: display reset'), not 'Glide asked'. pid 1892 itself issued a hwcext 16 escape afterwards, so the process was alive and running its close. Our h5 Glide's hwcRestoreVideo skips the whole register restore when the board is not idle at close, including '/* disable the CMD fifo */ cmdFifo0.baseSize = 0'.

Resulting state, read with vcrctl reg (read-only): cmdFifo0 baseSize 0x1fe (enabled), base 0x18000, 255 pages, readPtr 0x2f624 unchanged on two reads, aMin 0x2f630, holeCount 0x22177.

In that state, d3dprobe fullscreen 1024x768x32 + D24X8 created the device and context and logged 'ContextCreate 1 ... 36 triangles, 14 clears, 0 unparsed'. Every clear read back right, but every triangle check read the clear colour: 9 pass / 31 fail. Windowed 32 bpp: 7/42.

After the miniport's busy-at-mode-set engine reset (VcrHwResetEngine writes cmdFifo0.baseSize=0), with no driver or setting changed: 40/40, 42/42 windowed, 40/40 at 640x480x16.

Why nothing caught it: the miniport resets only a BUSY chip, and an enabled-but-idle FIFO passes the 2D idle test (10 M desktop 2D ops after the session). Diag\Reset3D (off) refuses whenever SST_CMDFIFOEN is set.

Fix direction:
- stop the FIFO fetch at the display reset that ends a not-idle Glide close (VcrSliOff 'display reset' already runs there);
- check cmdFifo0 at D3D ContextCreate;
- never place surfaces inside an enabled FIFO window.

The 16 bpp path was not tested while the FIFO was on. Why an idle-but-enabled FIFO blocks PIO triangles but not fastfill is not measured.
games: every D3D title run after any OpenGL/Glide title on the same boot

items.title: Stale FIFO + a D3D surface inside its window -> CMD0 busy -> desktop 2D give-up -> no D3D HAL at all until a mode set
items.detail:
In the windowed probe, the D3D surfaces were placed at 0x40000 (target), 0x80000 (Z) and 0xc0000 (texture), all inside the stale cmdFifo0 window 0x18000-0x117000. About 1.3 s after the texture was written, the chip read 0xa1f (SST_BUSY + SST_CMD0_BUSY; FBI/TMU/2D idle; PCI FIFO empty). The ring logged 'ERR DD_2D 2D engine never went idle (status 00000a1f) - acceleration off for this PDEV' for the desktop PDEV.

After that, d3dprobe fullscreen got GetDeviceCaps(HAL) 8876086a and CreateDevice 8876086a with no mode switch: any D3D game started then would have failed. One paced switch (vcrctl modeseq 6000 1024 768 32 85) set off 'chip 0 not idle (0xa5f)' -> 'engine reset (busy at mode set): idle again (0x5f)' and restored everything.

A 2D give-up currently removes acceleration and the D3D HAL for the life of the PDEV; it could try the engine reset first. The run itself caused this escalation, by probing windowed while the stale FIFO was on; the underlying state is onbox-01.

items.title: X8R8G8B8 + D16 is reported as matching but CreateDevice fails (INVALIDCALL), and the runtime's revert double-switches the CRT
items.detail:
The caps (caps_124.txt) report zmatch X8R8G8B8/D16 format 1, match 1 and hal_fullscreen X8R8G8B8 1. But d3dprobe render --full 640x480x32 --zfmt d16 gets CreateDevice 8876086c (D3DERR_INVALIDCALL). Ring 24713: 'WRN DD_D3D 513/12 ContextCreate refused: 32 bpp target with a 16-bit Z on a VSA-100 (16/16 or 32/32 only)' (b=0x20, c=0x10).

The D3D8 runtime set mode 144 (640x480x32@85) at 83009.846 s and restored mode 159 at 83010.002 s on its own: two CRT re-syncs 156 ms apart, which the probe's exit hold cannot cover. A D3D8/9 game that takes the advertised pair will fail and flash the 1998 tube the same way. The probe was not repeated.

Fix options: make D16 not match a 32 bpp target (vcr_rtfmt.h warns D16 must stay listed at a 32 bpp desktop for 16 bpp devices), or draw 32/16 through a hidden 32-bit aux buffer.
games: any D3D8/D3D9 title that picks D16 at 32 bpp

items.title: In-game blocky multi-coloured texture noise on terrain and rock meshes (UT2004, UT2003, Halo)
items.detail:
Every in-game frame shows 4x4-block-like multi-coloured 'confetti' over the terrain and many static rock meshes. Other surfaces in the same frames are correctly textured: near rock faces, weapons, UT2004 grass, trees, HUD and text.
- UT2004 run 1 (90 s, zoomed crops) and run 2 (80/100 s).
- UT2003 flyby (60/90/120 s).
- Halo timedemo: patches on canyon rock faces (90/120 s).

d3dprobe passes every texture test on the same driver: mip chains to 2048 in R5G6B5, A8R8G8B8, single-level DXT1/3/5 up to 1024x512, decode texel-exact. So the noise comes from a path the probe does not exercise.

Unverified hypothesis: both Unreal titles have UseCompressedLightmaps=True, so the lightmaps are DXT1 and drawn in texture STAGE 1. The probe never puts a DXT texture in stage 1, never builds a multi-level DXT chain (sub-4x4 levels), and never does terrain alpha-layer passes. These are the first probe tests to add. All captures were made after the engine reset (cmdFifo0 off).

items.title: Lightmapped world very dark in UT2003/UT2004 (consistent with no MODULATE2X)
items.detail:
All lightmapped world geometry in UT2004 (both runs) and the UT2003 flyby renders at roughly half brightness or less. Unlit items look right: the weapon model, HUD and grass.

The HAL's TextureOpCaps 0x184f do not offer MODULATE2X, and the HAL draws MODULATE2X as MODULATE (known gap). UE2 lightmaps are authored for a 2x modulate, so the dark result is consistent with this. It is not verified that UE2 takes that path here, and the gamma ramp (Brightness/Gamma 0.8 in UT2004.ini) is a second candidate.

VSA-100 has the hardware for it: Glide's grTexColorCombineExt takes a shift (x2/x4).

items.title: Solid-white sky/horizon regions and white polygons in the Unreal Engine 2 titles
items.detail:
Where sky or distant horizon should be, large areas render pure white.
- UT2004 run 2: the sky seen through a cave opening is white (80 s); a white band covers most of the horizon under a correct orange sky strip (100 s).
- UT2003 flyby: terrain solid white with a cyan triangle and a striped floor (30 s); a white wedge in the sky (120 s).
- UT2004 run 1, 65 s: a similar striped/white early frame.

UT2003.log reports 'Using w- pixel fog'. d3dprobe's fogtable test covers only w 1..8 with a blue fog colour.

Candidates, unverified: W table fog over large world-unit ranges or the fog colour; TFACTOR; a blend mode the HAL maps to white. Halo's sky is right.

items.title: Halo: a glow sprite is drawn as a visible translucent square
items.detail:
In the Halo timedemo at 60 s (canyon cutscene), the glow around a blue crystal is a sharp-edged translucent teal rectangle instead of a soft glow: the texture's alpha shape is not applied.

This is consistent with the known gap that the HAL ignores D3DTA_ALPHAREPLICATE (color_path masks the modifier off). A glow texture usually carries its shape in alpha. A stage alpha-source or blend-mode mapping is the other candidate.

The rest of Halo's cutscenes render largely right: ring and planet at 30 s, the escape pod with smoke over trees at 180 s, crisp subtitle text.

items.title: UT2003: deco-layer grass rendered blue, and a grey checkerboard patch
items.detail:
In the UT2003 flyby (60/90/120 s), the grass decorations are vivid blue; on Antalus they should be green-yellow. At 120 s a grey checkerboard texture also appears.

UT2004's grass on the same map renders the right colour (UT2004_statfps_080s.png), so this is a UT2003-specific texture or vertex-colour path: possibly a red/blue swap in one format, or a material the engine could not create.

items.title: D3D in-game performance is very low; frame time is spent inside DrawPrimitive
items.detail:
- **UT2003 flyby** (staged Benchmark script, -benchmark), 640x480x16@120: Results avgfps '2.067308 / 9.411991 / 1.#INF00 fps', Score 9.419. Stats CSV: 1998 frames in 245.7 s (8.1 fps), 122.99 ms mean frame, of which Hardware DrawPrimitive 116.73 ms, at 29,362 primitives and 33,846 software-processed vertices per frame (about 240k triangles/s end to end). Present 0.76 ms; locks, state and texture changes negligible.
- **UT2004 botmatch**, 8 bots, 1280x960x16: stat fps '4 cur FPS / 6 avg FPS'.
- **Halo -timedemo**, 1280x960: not finished in 485 s; 26.1 M triangles and 764 clears in the session.
- **d3dprobe perf** (200 tris/frame), vsync on: 85.1 fps at 640x480x16 and 84.4 fps at 1024x768x32, i.e. bound by the 85 Hz refresh. Ring at 1024x768: flips 300, retrace 284, deadline 15.

The cost is runtime software T&L plus the HAL's DP2 walk and register writes, roughly 4 us per triangle; this split is not separated. Likely, but unmeasured: per-triangle PIO through the PCI FIFO with status reads. A heavy d3dprobe perf scene (thousands of tris/frame, --novsync) is needed to profile the HAL alone.

items.title: d3dprobe on a clean engine: render, texture and decode checks all pass on silicon
Tooling gaps met during the run
items.detail:
- **d3dprobe_run.py has no --pace.** d3dprobe_paced.py wraps it to pass --pace 5000.
- **d3dprobe *_def tests always fail under D3D8:** a DEFAULT-pool texture cannot be locked.
- **d3dprobe perf (200 tris/frame) only measures vsync.**
- **The monitor gate's refresh assumption is wrong:** it assumes the highest listed refresh (100/120 Hz), and the runtime picked 85 Hz every time.
- **The flight-recorder ring is too small for a game session:** 1024 entries at LogLevel 3 wrap within seconds of a game starting (UT2004 about 67,000 events, UT2003 110,000, mostly dbg CreateSurfaceEx). A game's D3D record survives only in a fetch right after it ends.
- **UT2004's own end paths fail:** -benchmark -seconds=60 never ends at these frame rates, and UT2004 ignores WM_CLOSE (run 1 was forced by pid and its log is 0 bytes). Use stat fps via -exec plus the console exit, which worked.
- **Halo -timedemo** does not finish within 8 minutes here.
- **The 10-minute screensaver** was running at the start and must be dismissed before fullscreen tests.
- **agentcall.py first read DOWNLOAD's status 1 (binary OK) as an error**; fixed.

items.title: Stability record: no hang, crash or dialog across 13 probe runs and 4 game sessions
items.detail:
Every program returned the desktop to 1280x1024x32@85, and no Dr. Watson entry or error dialog appeared. Agent PING never failed.

How each game closed:
- UT2004 run 1 ignored WM_CLOSE and was forced by pid; the desktop came back.
- UT2003 and UT2004 run 2 closed cleanly via console exit with the game focused.
- Halo closed cleanly on WM_CLOSE.

At the end: status 0x1f (idle), cmdFifo0 off, nothing of this run left running.

The only unpaced event was the runtime's own double mode switch on the refused 32/16 device (onbox-03).

items.title: A game's new mode shows stale desktop VRAM until its first frame
items.detail: In UT2004 run 1 at 45 s, the frame at the new 1280x960x16 mode shows the old 32 bpp desktop pixels reinterpreted at 16 bpp: doubled icons, green/purple tint. The visible primary is not cleared at the mode set or at primary creation. AvP showed the same on 2026-10-14. This is cosmetic, but it reads as corruption to a player during loading.

items.title: The Unreal titles run 16 bpp on this HAL; UT2003 drops to 640x480
items.detail:
- UT2004.log: 'Enter SetRes: 1280x960 / Using back-buffer format 23 (16-bit) / depth-buffer format 80 (16-bit)', although UT2004.ini has Use16bit=False.
- UT2003.log: 'Enter SetRes: 640x480 / Best-match display mode: 640x480x16@120', although its ini asks for 1280x960. It also logs 'software transform and lighting' and 'Device doesn't support D3DVTXPCAPS_MATERIALSOURCE7'.

So the 32 bpp D3D path is not what these titles use, and UT2003's resolution drop (seen on 11-08 too) persists. Cause not determined.

items.title: Not reached in this run
items.detail:
- **Red Faction:** rf.exe's switch table has -level, -timedemo and -frameratetest (README-FLEET lines 56-58), but the title needs its disc mounted. D: currently holds the SoF image, and a Daemon Tools mount is registry state, which this run was not allowed to change.
- **No switch found:** a strings look found no documented direct-to-3D switch for Shogo (Client.exe), Thief II NewDark or Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe.
- **Not attempted in-game:** Jedi Knight/MotS, System Shock 2, Thief Gold, Rainbow Six, BF1942 and AvP. Max Payne was excluded by rule.
- **No numbers:** Halo fps is unknown (timedemo unfinished); no --novsync perf was run.
- **Untested in the stale-FIFO state:** the 16 bpp path. No fresh-boot control exists for the in-game defects; all were captured after the engine reset.
